selectionNote: Replay-verified worlds from the three supplied discovery exports, subject to the explicit website exclusions. Featured worlds lead; remaining worlds are interleaved across experiments, profiles, and coding agents. Automated agreement does not establish human validity.
samplePolicy: First three file-distinct, nonexcluded replay images in the first eligible prompt family; no model inference is performed.

worlds.title: Count the guitar strings
worlds.question: How many dark strings visibly run from the guitar's headstock, along the neck, and across its body? Count each continuous thin path once. Answer 4, 5, 6, 7, or 8.

worlds.title: Water after a wall is removed
worlds.question: The dark blocks make a landscape of columns standing on the ground, and the pale blue blocks are the rain water trapped in that landscape as it is drawn. Water is only held where taller columns stand on both sides of it; water that can reach either open end of the landscape runs off. Exactly one column is red. Take that whole red column away, down to the ground, leave every other column exactly as it is, and let the water settle again. How many blocks deep is the water standing directly above the column the black arrow points at? Answer with the number of blocks alone: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Find the connecting cell
worlds.question: Four colored cell islands are shown, each with one gold pin. Which color's island would split into separate pieces if the single cell holding its gold pin were removed? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Trace the winding cable
worlds.question: Starting at each ring, follow its dark cable to the colored square. Which cable makes exactly one complete clockwise turn around the black hub? Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Rotate, then reflect
worlds.question: A reference 5-by-5 glyph is drawn inside the magenta-bordered frame at the top.  Four framed squares below each hold another 5-by-5 glyph, and each square carries a coloured tag just above it: one crimson, one teal, one amber, one violet.  Transform the reference glyph as follows: first turn it a quarter turn clockwise, then flip it over like a mirror across the horizontal midline so that the top edge swaps with the bottom edge.  Exactly one of the four tagged glyphs equals the reference after this two-step transformation.  Which colour tag belongs to that matching glyph?  Answer with exactly one of: crimson, teal, amber, violet.

worlds.title: Count checkpoints inside a band
worlds.question: At how many of checkpoints T1 through T6 is the center of the black trace marker strictly inside the blue band? Answer with an integer from 0 to 6.

worlds.title: Find the remaining loops
worlds.question: Gray links meet only at cyan round stations; a crossing without a station is not a connection. A bridge is a gray link whose removal disconnects its panel. Imagine removing every bridge link at once. A loop group is a remaining connected group of stations that contains a loop. Which panel has exactly two loop groups? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Match the dash pattern
worlds.question: The gray dashed bar at the top is a pattern of solid dashes separated by empty gaps. Below it are three colored dashed bars: one is red, one is green, and one is blue, and each has a different dash-to-gap ratio (how long each solid dash is compared to the empty gap to its right). Which colored bar has exactly the same dash-to-gap ratio as the gray bar? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Find the interlocked rings
worlds.question: This image shows five framed square panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel holds exactly two rings of the same thickness, drawn in two different flat colours, and in every panel the two rings cross each other at exactly two places, so ring count, ring size, colour, position and the amount of ink carry no information. The rings are opaque, so at each crossing one ring passes in front and hides a short piece of the other one, leaving a plain break in the ring behind. Two rings are interlocked when neither ring stays in front the whole way round: one ring passes in front at one crossing and behind at the other, so each of the two rings carries exactly one break and each is still a single connected curve. Two rings are merely stacked when the same ring passes in front at both crossings, so that front ring carries no break at all while the ring behind it is broken twice and falls into two separate pieces. Exactly one panel holds a pair of interlocked rings. In each of the other four panels the pair is merely stacked, and the piece of the ring behind that lies between its two breaks is at least 26 pixels long, so both of its breaks are plainly visible. Which ring is drawn in which colour, which ring is in front at a given crossing, and where the pair sits inside its panel are all free to vary. Which numbered panel holds the two interlocked rings, that is the panel in which each of the two rings carries exactly one break? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Track colors and shapes
worlds.question: The three fixed slots start with the shown colored shapes. Read the five cards from left to right. The dot counts name two slots. A BLUE card swaps only the colors in those slots; an ORANGE card swaps only the shapes. The other attribute stays. What color and shape finish in the magenta-ringed slot?

worlds.title: Follow the negative space
worlds.question: Which two colored gates are connected by one continuous white path through the charcoal maze? Paths may bend; corner-only touching does not connect. Answer as color-color, for example red-blue.

worlds.title: Reveal a hidden shape
worlds.question: The picture shows two square plates side by side, each enclosed by a coloured frame and each printed with a fine black-and-white speckle. Both plates cover the same 7 rows and 7 columns of equal square cells, and the two plates are the same size, so every cell of the right plate has one matching cell of the left plate. The right plate repeats the left plate's speckle cell by cell, in one of two ways. In a plain cell the speckle is copied straight across, so that cell of the right plate is exactly the matching cell of the left plate. In a slid cell the speckle is copied from further to the right: what the right plate shows at a point of a slid cell is what the left plate shows the slide distance further right of the matching point, in the same row. The slide distance is the same in every slid cell and is printed above the plates as the distance between the two small coloured tick marks. Each row of the left plate is a loop, so a strip that runs past its right edge continues from its left edge. Neither plate on its own shows anything but speckle; only comparing them tells the slid cells from the plain ones. On the 7 by 7 grid the slid cells form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: crescent, funnel, pinwheel, spiral, staircase. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Compare two routes
worlds.question: Trace each navy network from its green ring to its red ring, ignoring dead-end branches. Which green-to-red route is longer along the network: top or bottom?

worlds.title: Remove a plug
worlds.question: Ignore pale gray marks. The amber plug is solid now. If only the amber plug were erased to white, would the enclosed white pocket become connected to the outside white background? White areas connect through shared edges, not diagonal corner contact. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Match the disc colors
worlds.question: Near the middle of the image sits a small cluster made of exactly two separate coloured discs, with empty white space between them. Do the two disconnected discs carry the SAME colour? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Track the grid state
worlds.question: The 4x4 grid has one red-ringed starting cell. Read the marker in its row of the ROW LEDGER, then the marker in its column of the COLUMN LEDGER. A filled diamond toggles ON/OFF and an outlined diamond holds the state. What is the ringed cell's final state? Answer ON or OFF.

worlds.title: Read the overall trend
worlds.question: Fit one straight trend line to the entire cyan trace. Compared with the dashed horizontal reference, does that fitted line go upward or downward from left to right? Answer upward or downward.

worlds.title: Locate the steering wheel
worlds.question: Which half of the centered dashboard visibly contains the steering wheel? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Compare distant directions
worlds.question: Two distant corner strokes are drawn (dark indigo) on a white canvas, one in the upper-left area and one in the lower-right area. Each stroke points in one of the four directions: right, down-right diagonal, down, or down-left diagonal. The two strokes either share the SAME direction (reading as two continuing parallel rails) or diverge at a RIGHT ANGLE to each other. Do the two distant strokes point in the same direction?

worlds.title: Reveal a pattern by subtraction
worlds.question: Exactly two of the small square chips in this picture are drawn with a black border; all the other chips are drawn with a gray border. Each chip is divided into a 5 by 5 grid of 25 equal square cells, and every cell is filled with one of just two tones, a darker tone and a lighter tone. The three-square key near the bottom left shows those two tones with their exact midpoint tone between them. Carry out this operation on the two black-bordered chips: lay one chip exactly on top of the other so their borders coincide, and mark every one of the 25 grid positions whose tone differs between the two black-bordered chips. Marked positions are exactly the positions where one chip is darker and the other is lighter; positions where both chips agree stay unmarked. The marked positions form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the full centre row together with the full centre column, 'ex' is the two full diagonals, 'tee' is the full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. Neither black-bordered chip shows the symbol on its own, and the gray-bordered chips and the key are decoration. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, ex, tee, ell.

worlds.title: Repair the ball’s route
worlds.question: A ball enters at the black dot on top and runs down the wiring: at every black wedge it goes off to the side the wedge points, meets the next wedge below, and finally drops into one of the colored cups. The square at the top left shows a goal color. Turning a wedge means making it point the opposite way and changing nothing else. Exactly one of the four ringed wedges can be turned so that the ball ends in a cup of the goal color. Which ring is it? Answer blue, crimson, green, or violet.

worlds.title: Update the grid
worlds.question: A 5 by 5 square grid of cells stands on a white card.  Each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Below the grid a small key holds one, two, or three teal dots; the number of dots is the number of rounds R to apply.  A round transforms the whole grid by this rule: for every cell, count how many of its eight surrounding neighbours (the cells that touch it along an edge or at a corner) are dark; in the next round that cell is dark if and only if the count is exactly two, otherwise it is pale.  Note that a dark cell may turn pale and a pale cell may turn dark.  Apply the round rule R times, using each round's result as the starting grid of the next round.  After the last round, count how many cells in the 5 by 5 grid are dark.  Is that count odd?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Follow the lamp logic
worlds.question: Begin with the two-lamp state shown in START. Read the eight colored gate glyphs from left to right: a red circular arrow around the left lamp flips left; a blue circular arrow around the right lamp flips right; a violet double arrow exchanges the lamps. Apply each gate to the current state. What is the final state: both-dark, left-lit, right-lit, or both-lit?

worlds.title: Track the rotating registers
worlds.question: The front badge moves that token. On its current tile: turn RIGHT on GOLD or LEFT on BLUE and flip the color. Then rotate badges CARD to HERE, old HERE to the other tile with the same LINK letter, and old LINK to queue BACK. Step and repeat. Which exits first? Answer token-red or token-violet.

worlds.title: Trace bead interior match
worlds.question: Near the middle of the image sits one short, thin, connected coloured trace. Threaded onto that trace, at two interior points (not its ends), are exactly two small coloured beads. Do the two beads carried by the same connected trace carry the SAME colour? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Notch triplet correspondence
worlds.question: Oppose each candidate tile's opening direction and reverse its three-tile order. Which candidate reproduces all three directions in R: A or B?

worlds.title: Stencil union tile bind
worlds.question: The cream board carries small decorative coloured squares lying on the bare board; none of them touches a grid and none of them means anything. There are exactly six GRIDS on the board. Every grid is a 4-by-4 arrangement of sixteen square cells inside a solid frame, and each cell is either black (filled) or cream (empty). Two of the grids are STENCILS: a stencil is the grid whose frame is dark slate, and the two stencils sit at two opposite corners of the board. The KEY pattern is the cell-by-cell OVERLAY of the two stencils: a cell of the key is filled when that same cell is filled in either stencil or in both, and empty only when that cell is empty in both stencils. Neither stencil on its own gives the key. The other four grids are TILES: a tile is a grid whose frame is red, blue, green or purple, and the four tiles carry those four different frame colours. Exactly one tile's sixteen cells match the key pattern exactly, cell for cell; each of the other three tiles differs from the key in at least one cell. Grid positions, which corner holds which stencil, how many cells are filled, and the board clutter carry no other information. What is the frame colour of the tile whose pattern matches the key exactly? Answer red, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Switchyard permutation rail
worlds.question: Read the three shapes nearest the gold dock along its navy run: circle, square, triangle. Continue along that run through all six short gate bars. A bar above the rail swaps the first and second shapes; a bar below swaps the second and third. Apply the gates in traversal order. Then read each colored-dock run away from its dock. Which dock shows the resulting shape order? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Shuffle echo correspondence
worlds.question: The upper-left card is BEFORE and the upper-right card is AFTER: the same three black shapes have been shuffled. The lower-left card binds colors to the BEFORE slots. Match by shape. Which color follows the black shape now in the left slot of the AFTER card? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Dual offset compare
worlds.question: Consider the black marker in the red track and the black marker in the blue track, each expressed as a fraction of its own track's width from the left edge. Which marker has the larger normalized offset? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Paired crossing offset
worlds.question: Does the trace in the left plot cross its dashed horizontal baseline before the trace in the right plot? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Plate cut balance
worlds.question: The figure shows one solid grey plate on white paper, cut all the way across by a single dark curve that has exactly one height at every horizontal position and runs past both ends of the plate. Only grey plate area counts: the dark curve's own pixels belong to neither side, and the small saturated coloured marks are decoration lying outside the plate. Grey plate area above the curve means grey lying higher than the curve at the same horizontal position; below means lower. Is there more grey plate area above the dark curve or below it? Answer with one word: above or below.

worlds.title: Cross panel rank hold
worlds.question: Which colored sample keeps the same horizontal rank—leftmost, middle, or rightmost—in both panels? Answer coral, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Trace halfway chord side
worlds.question: Follow the colored trace from its left endpoint and locate the point halfway along its total traveled length (not halfway across the image). Imagine the straight chord joining the two endpoints. Is that halfway point ABOVE or BELOW the chord? Answer ABOVE or BELOW.

worlds.title: Serpentine row count
worlds.question: A single connected winding blue route is drawn on the page. A normal single stroke might look like one line, but here the one connected route meanders up and down across several distinct horizontal rows. How many distinct horizontal rows does the route sweep through? Answer 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Shield balance centroid
worlds.question: Is the visible shield's colored area centered left-to-right? Answer yes only if its area centroid is within the middle 1.5% of the shield width; otherwise answer no.

worlds.title: Stitch face alternation
worlds.question: This picture shows a mending board on a plain white background. Exactly one flat tape strip has a thin thread stitched through it: that thread crosses the tape exactly five times, and one end of that thread carries a small crimson square tag. At each crossing the thread either passes in FRONT of the tape, staying visible right across it, or BEHIND the tape, hidden where the tape covers it and leaving a visible gap. Loose thread scraps and bare tape pieces elsewhere in the picture are not stitched through any tape and must be ignored. Walk the thread from its tagged end and take the five crossings in the order the thread meets them. The stitch alternates if front and behind strictly take turns along that walk, never twice in a row. Does this stitch alternate? Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Visible wave alternation
worlds.question: Following the single blue waveform from left to right, does each lobe lie on the opposite side of the gray centerline from the lobe before it? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Dice two pip alignment
worlds.question: On the die face, are the two large colored pips diagonally aligned rather than sharing a row or column? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Twin seal xor
worlds.question: The image shows two separate dot-grid seals: a left seal made of amber and gray dots and a right seal made of amber and gray dots. Each seal is a 3-by-3 grid. Superimpose the two seals cell by cell (the XOR or difference of the two grids, the declared transform): a grid position counts as marked exactly when the left seal and the right seal disagree in colour at that cell (one amber, the other gray). The set of marked cells forms a symbol. Which symbol does the marked grid form?

worlds.title: Chromatic delta route
worlds.question: Follow the one connected route from the red start cap to the green end cap. It has 33 solid-colored sections, each using one of the two visible route colors. For each of the 32 adjacent section pairs, write # when their colors differ and . when they match. Read those 32 marks in route order as a 4-by-8 bitmap and compare it with A) LOOM = 10011001/01100110/01100110/10011001 or B) KNOT = 00011100/00011000/11111011/00111100. Which symbol appears? Answer A or B. Ignore the caps, quiet route window, distractors, and background.

worlds.title: Chain reflow reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one tape in this picture is teal; every other tape is pale lavender. The teal tape is a single unbranching chain of 25 equal square tiles joined edge to edge, so it has exactly two ends and every other tile has exactly two neighbours along the chain. Each tile of the teal tape carries one round dot filled with one of just two grays, a darker gray and a lighter gray; the three-square key in one corner shows those two grays with their exact midpoint gray between them. Exactly one end tile of the teal tape has small black brackets drawn at its four corners. Carry out this operation: start at that bracketed end tile and walk along the teal tape tile by tile to its other end, collecting the 25 dots in the order you meet them; then write that sequence into a 5 by 5 grid, filling the first row left to right with the first five dots, the second row with the next five, and so on to the fifth row; then mark every grid position whose dot was the darker gray. Exactly 9 of the 25 positions are marked. The marked positions form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the full centre row together with the full centre column, 'ex' is the two full diagonals, 'tee' is the full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. The tape's own path across the picture is not the symbol, the lavender tapes and the key are decoration, and only the walking order along the teal tape decides which grid position each dot occupies. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tee.

worlds.title: Tensor tile expansion
worlds.question: Use the teal-or-blue 2 by 2 chip as a layout. Replace each of its dark squares with an upright copy of the coral-or-magenta 2 by 2 chip, and each pale square with a blank 2 by 2 block, preserving row and column order. Which 4 by 4 symbol appears: one falling diagonal, one rising diagonal, two falling dashes, or two rising dashes?

worlds.title: Two peel core reveal
worlds.question: Inside the cyan-framed 15 by 15 mosaic, peel the dark shape twice. In each simultaneous peel, a dark cell remains dark only if all four edge-sharing neighbors are dark; every other cell becomes light, and beyond the mosaic counts as light. After exactly two peels, which shape remains: cross, tee, or elbow? Ignore rotation and reflection; answer ambiguous if the two best shapes tie.

worlds.title: Twin ball consensus
worlds.question: Two gauges show a coloured ball in either the upper or lower zone, each channel marked by a green midline tick. Do the two balls occupy the same zone (both on the same side of their green midline)?

worlds.title: Paired void agreement
worlds.question: Do the two separated seals have the same enclosure status: either both enclose one empty chamber or both leave their chamber open to the outside? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Illusory edge cycle
worlds.question: The picture shows exactly seven equal dark discs on a light page, together with pale grey marks that are background clutter and must be ignored. One wedge is cut out of every disc, and the tip of every cut wedge sits exactly at the centre of its own disc, so each disc shows two straight cut edges that start at that centre. Call two discs linked when one straight cut edge of each disc runs along the straight line joining the two disc centres, so that the two edges together spell out one unbroken invisible segment whose two ends are pinned by those two centres; treat an edge as running along that line when it is within ten degrees of it. In this picture the linked pairs form one single closed chain: each disc of the chain is linked to exactly two other discs, the chain closes into one loop, and every disc outside the chain is linked to no disc at all. The loop itself is never painted; the discs are the only ink. All seven discs share one size and one colour, and the seven cut wedges always remove the same total amount of disc area, so disc count, disc size, disc position, colour and total ink say nothing about the answer. Report how many discs the closed chain runs through, which is the number of sides of the invisible loop: three, four or five. Answer unclear if the picture does not show exactly one such closed chain, for instance if some disc is linked to three or more discs or if the linked discs do not close into a single loop. Answer unclear as well if the reading is too close to call, that is if the nearest pair of discs that is not linked comes within fourteen degrees of being as well aligned as the worst aligned linked pair. How many sides does the invisible loop have: three, four, five, or unclear?

worlds.title: Orthogonal mirror thread
worlds.question: The blue thread is one closed curve. Considering the whole curve, does its mirror axis rise / or fall \ from left to right? Answer rising or falling.

worlds.title: Implied line concurrence
worlds.question: Three separated colored bars stop before reaching one another. Imagine extending each bar as a straight line. Do all three extended lines meet at one point, or do their three pairwise intersections form a small triangle? Answer one point or triangle.

worlds.title: Conjunctive bar reference
worlds.question: A coloured reference bar on the left has a colour and a tilt. In the 2-by-2 grid of coloured bars on the right, exactly one bar matches the reference in BOTH colour AND tilt. Which grid position is that bar? Answer top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right.

worlds.title: Concave bite search
worlds.question: Each sector contains one filled tile. Which sector contains the only tile whose outside border has a single inward bite? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Triad tally consensus search
worlds.question: The picture shows three separate blocks of dot tallies on a plain background: one near the top-left corner, one near the top-right corner and one near the bottom centre of the page. Nothing joins the three blocks and the space between them is empty. Each block holds exactly four tallies arranged as two rows of two, so every block has an upper-left, an upper-right, a lower-left and a lower-right position, and the same four position names are used in all three blocks. A tally is a single horizontal row of small solid squares; every square in the picture has the same size and the squares of a tally are evenly spaced, so the only thing that distinguishes one tally from another is how many squares it holds. Every tally holds between two and eight squares. Exactly one of the four positions holds the same number of squares in all three blocks. Each of the other three positions holds the same number of squares in exactly two of the three blocks and a clearly different number in the remaining one, and the three wrong positions are shared out over the three different pairs of blocks, so whichever two blocks you compare you will find a second position that also seems to agree. All three blocks must therefore be read: no two of them can single out the answer, and no block on its own carries any information about it. The answer is not revealed by ink colour, by exactly where the blocks sit, by which block holds the odd tally of a position, or by amount of ink: inside any single block the answer position is never the one with the most squares nor the one with the fewest, and its total over the three blocks is equally often the largest, the second, the third and the smallest of the four positions. Which block position holds the same number of squares in all three blocks? Answer with one of: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right.

worlds.title: Enclosed courtyard search
worlds.question: The cyan shape is one connected plate with four white courtyards, each marked by a colored dot. Three courtyards have a white opening to the outside. Which colored dot marks the only courtyard completely enclosed by cyan? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Reverse skyline search
worlds.question: Each color has one four-bar skyline on the left and one on the right. Every skyline contains one bar at each of the same four heights. Reading bars left to right within each skyline, which color's right-hand height sequence is exactly the reverse of its left-hand sequence? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Arena field flips
worlds.question: A light-grey arena spans the entire canvas as a single connected region. Its coloured border carries the initial state of the tracked field: blue border means the field is OFF and orange border means it is ON. Inside the arena, each red toggle dot inverts the field; red dots outside the arena on the white margin are ignorable decoys. Count all interior red toggles over the full arena and flip the initial state once per such toggle. Is the field's final state ON? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: State route dwell
worlds.question: Trace the one connected route in increasing station-number order. The token starts in state A, B, or C as shown by its colored start badge (red=A, green=B, blue=C). At each station, a right triangle advances the state one step A-B-C-A, a left triangle moves it one step backward, and an outlined square leaves it unchanged. Record the state after every station. Which state has the longest uninterrupted run in that record? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Pipchain hop ribbon
worlds.question: This picture contains one ribbon: a chain of coloured square cells joined end to end by short dark bridges, so the whole chain is a single connected strip that wanders from one side of the ribbon to the other. Each cell holds some dark pips, between one and four of them. Read the ribbon in order starting from its left-hand end cell and following the bridges to its right-hand end cell. A solid dark triangular tab is welded to the top edge of exactly one cell: that is the cell where the token starts. The token then makes exactly three hops. For each hop, count the pips in the cell the token is on now and move the token that many cells forward along the ribbon, counting every cell it passes over. The cell's colour never affects anything, and every grey mark outside the ribbon is inert decoration. After the three hops, how many pips are in the cell the token ends on? Answer with one of 1, 2, 3 or 4.

worlds.title: Parity pulse patch
worlds.question: The gold ring marks the tracked cell. Dark cells are ON and light cells are OFF. Apply exactly two synchronous pulses. On each pulse, every cell flips its state if exactly two of its orthogonal neighbors were ON just before that pulse; otherwise it keeps its state. Neighbors beyond the board do not count. Is the tracked cell ON after both pulses?

worlds.title: Cube roll stamp
worlds.question: The six colored squares form a cube net: the junction square starts FRONT, the square above it starts TOP, and the squares left, right, below, and far-right start LEFT, RIGHT, BOTTOM, and BACK. Read the six arrows in the attached rail from top to bottom. Each arrow rolls the cube one quarter-turn in that screen direction: up brings the current FRONT face to TOP, down brings BACK to TOP, left brings RIGHT to TOP, and right brings LEFT to TOP. Colors stay attached to their faces. After all six rolls, which color is on TOP?

worlds.title: Duo island hole agree
worlds.question: The image shows two separate black rings, one near the upper-left and one near the lower-right. Are the two distant rings in the SAME enclosure state (both fully closed loops, or both broken open)? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Closed trace cycle
worlds.question: Does the one dark track contain a closed route? Ignore the colored dots. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Slotted slab piece count
worlds.question: This page shows one near-black slab together with coloured rings, frames, blocks and bars as decoration. Only the near-black slab decides the answer; every coloured or grey mark is decoration, never touches the slab, and never counts. The slab was cut from one square block built of small equal square cells, and four white slots have been cut out of it. Each slot is one cell wide, runs along a single straight line of cells, and starts at a border of the block. A slot that reaches the opposite border cuts right through the block there; a slot that stops short leaves a bridge of slab cells at its far end, and the shortest such bridge is one cell wide. Two patches of slab belong to the same piece when you can travel from one to the other over slab only, always stepping between cells that share a whole edge; stepping between two cells that meet at a single corner is not travelling, and no scene requires it. A slot that stops short can still leave its line joined to a neighbouring line only where the two lines still share slab, so slots that stop short on neighbouring lines and start from opposite borders can separate the slab even though neither slot cuts right through. How much dark ink the slab holds, how many slots are cut, how long the slots are, which border each slot starts from, whether the slots run across or down, how large the cells are, where the slab sits on the page, and how many coloured decorations appear never decide the answer. Into how many separate pieces is the slab divided? Answer 1, 2 or 3.

worlds.title: Nested pocket order
worlds.question: The black ink is one connected thin drawing that encloses exactly two white pockets. Is one white pocket nested inside the other? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Articulation tile mosaic
worlds.question: The teal mosaic is made of equal square tiles. Tiles are connected only when they share a full side, not when they meet at a corner. Is there any one teal tile whose removal would split the remaining teal tiles into two or more groups? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route first waypoint
worlds.question: A dark connected route has an orange ring around its start. Three colored disks (red, green, blue) sit on the route in some order. Starting at the orange ring and walking along the route, which colored disk is met FIRST?

worlds.title: Forked route terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green start, follow the dark connected route through its fork. Which terminal—amber or violet—is farther along the route? Use route distance, not straight-line distance. Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Bay record climb
worlds.question: The image shows one thick dark corridor on a plain background. The corridor is a single connected shape built from six long horizontal bays; each bay is a solid rectangle, the six bays sit at six different heights, no two bays overlap in height, and every bay has its own uniform thickness, measured as its height. No two bays are equally thick. Bays are stitched together by short vertical connectors that all share one common narrow width, much narrower than any bay is thick and much shorter than any bay is long; a connector may run past a bay it does not join, and where it does it stays clear of that bay. The bays and connectors form one single unbranched chain: exactly two bays are the ends of the chain and each of the other four bays is joined by connectors to exactly two bays. A hollow green frame stands in clear background just beyond one free end of one of the two end bays, and that bay is the start bay. Walk the chain from the start bay, stepping through connectors from bay to bay until the far end bay is reached, and read off the thickness of each bay in the order the walk meets it. This walking order is the only order that counts; it is not the top-to-bottom order of the bays. Light gray squares are decoration and mean nothing. Counting only bays after the start bay, how many bays on this walk are thicker than every bay met earlier on the same walk? Answer 1, 2 or 3.

worlds.title: Route chord crossing count
worlds.question: Trace the navy centerline from the green START to the red FINISH. Count only interior crossings of the imaginary straight line joining the centers of START and FINISH; do not count the endpoints. Does the route cross it 2 or 3 times? Answer 2 or 3.

worlds.title: Route interval compare
worlds.question: Follow the dark centerline between the three colored rings; gold is the middle ring. Is the longer along-route section red-gold or gold-green? Use the route length rather than the equal straight-line gaps, and ignore pale gray dashes.

worlds.title: Trajectory flip parity
worlds.question: A 5 by 5 square grid of cells stands on a white card.  Each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Below the grid a small key holds one, two, or three teal dots; the number of dots is the number of rounds R.  A round transforms the whole grid by this rule: for every cell, count how many of its eight surrounding neighbours (the cells that touch it along an edge or at a corner) are dark; in the next round that cell is dark if and only if the count is exactly two, otherwise it is pale.  A dark cell may turn pale and a pale cell may turn dark.  Apply the round rule R times, using each round's result as the starting grid of the next.  Between each pair of consecutive grids, count how many of the twenty-five cells changed state (dark to pale or pale to dark).  Add those per-round change counts over all R rounds into one total of cell flips.  Is that accumulated total of cell flips odd?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Lifo stack rewrite
worlds.question: The START stack is shown bottom to top from left to right. For each numbered card, compare its color with the current top tile. If they match, pop and remove the top tile; if they do not match, push a new tile of the card color on top. After card 9, read the top two tiles from top downward. Which two-letter code is shown in the key?

worlds.title: Culprit column tally
worlds.question: The dark blocks make a landscape of columns standing on the ground, drawn as it stood before any rain. Rain water is held only where taller columns stand on both sides of it, and water that can reach either open end of the landscape runs off; one block of water fills one empty cell. Exactly one of the four columns carrying a black tag below the ground was taken away, down to the ground, before the rain fell; every other column stayed exactly as it is drawn, and the tags are numbered 1 to 4 from the left. The pale blue squares along the top count all the water the landscape holds after that column was taken away, one square for one block. Which tagged column was taken away? Answer with the tag number alone: 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Coupled recipe frontier
worlds.question: Each colored workshop has shared stocks A and B. One X batch and one Y batch use the A and B amounts shown in their recipe columns. Split the stocks between any whole numbers of X and Y batches without exceeding either stock. Which workshop can make the most total batches: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Mirror copy closure
worlds.question: START is a 7 by 7 stamp grid. Read the three MIRROR cards left to right. At each card, copy every current dark cell across its blue line and keep the originals. Which option is the final stamp pattern? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Correspondence anchor distance
worlds.question: The top reference panel shows one gray anchor dot and one colored dot. The colored dot is placed either very close to the gray anchor (near) or far away from it (far). Below, three candidate panels A, B, C each show one gray anchor dot and one colored dot. Which candidate reproduces the same near/far distance relationship as the reference: its colored dot near or far from its own anchor matching the reference?

worlds.title: Convex hull membership correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate panel, A or B, has exactly the same set of colored points on the outside convex hull as the REFERENCE panel? A point is on the hull when it is a vertex of the smallest convex polygon containing all five points. Panels may be translated, rotated, or uniformly scaled; A is left and B is right. Ignore panel position, marker size, and line thickness. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Stencil cell color binding
worlds.question: The panel labeled KEY at the top of this image is a 4x4 grid of sixteen cells in which exactly four cells are filled dark gray; the other twelve are blank. Below it are three more 4x4 grids, labeled A, B and C from left to right, whose cells are painted red, blue, green or orange. A cell of the KEY card corresponds to the cell in the same row and the same column of a colour grid, counting rows from the top and columns from the left. The grids are drawn at a different cell size and in a different place than the KEY card, so this row-and-column correspondence is the only alignment that matters and pixel positions never line up. Every colour grid paints each of the four colours in exactly four of its cells, so no colour is rarer or more common than another. In exactly one of the three colour grids, all four cells that the KEY card marks carry one and the same colour; in the other two grids the four marked positions carry at least two different colours. What is that single colour? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Ribbon seam completion
worlds.question: Three colored ribbons cross a missing window. A ribbon continues only when its color meets the same-height endpoint at both vertical seams. Which labeled patch completes all three ribbons? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Punched tape registration
worlds.question: Find the five-column punch sequence from the REFERENCE tape inside the longer TARGET tape without reversing it. Which color tag is attached to the target column aligned with the magenta-marked reference column: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Nearest square aspect
worlds.question: A light panel holds three coloured rectangles: one red, one blue, one green. Which colour's rectangle is CLOSEST to being a perfect square, meaning the smallest relative gap between its own width and its own height? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Enclosed void compare
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Each colored silhouette contains enclosed background holes. Which panel has more holes? Answer A, B, or tie.

worlds.title: Unit cut remainder
worlds.question: The picture shows one solid black measuring stick near the top and five horizontal rods below it. The rods all begin on the same left edge and have the same thickness. Four rods are coloured red, green, blue and orange; the fifth rod is grey. The grey rod is a distractor and carries no information; ignore it completely. Imagine cutting each coloured rod from its left end into pieces exactly as long as the black stick, taking as many whole stick lengths as will fit. What is left over at the right end of that rod, a piece shorter than the black stick, is that rod's LEFTOVER. A rod that is a little longer than three sticks has a short leftover; a rod that is a little shorter than three sticks has a long leftover, so a longer rod does not mean a longer leftover. Nothing is drawn to mark where the cuts would fall; the stick length and the rod lengths are the only measurements needed. In every picture each coloured rod is longer than the black stick, no two coloured leftovers are equal, and no coloured rod is close to an exact whole number of stick lengths. The colours, the vertical order of the rods, the position of the black stick and the number of whole cuts carry no information; the answer need not be the longest rod, need not be the rod that reaches furthest right, and is never the grey rod. Which coloured rod has the longest leftover? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Probe reference match
worlds.question: At the gray dashed vertical probe, which colored horizontal reference is closest to the blue trace? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Widest checkpoint spread
worlds.question: At which checkpoint is the vertical distance between the highest and lowest colored marker greatest? Answer T1, T2, T3, or T4.

worlds.title: Prior fork tines
worlds.question: This is a table fork. An ordinary table fork typically has four tines (prongs), but report exactly what is drawn here. Count the tines actually drawn on this fork and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Tricolor flag bands
worlds.question: How many horizontal stripes are in the flag? Count each visible solid-color band once; ignore the pole, outline, and label. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Compass needle heading
worlds.question: This image shows a compass dial. The rim circle, the four long tick marks, the four short diagonal marks and the letter N are fixed decoration: they are drawn in exactly the same place in every image of this set, so they never indicate the answer. The needle is the two-triangle arrow through the centre of the dial. Exactly one of its two triangles is filled with a solid colour; the mirror-image triangle on the other side is only a grey outline. Report the direction that the SOLID coloured triangle points, using the image itself and not what a compass normally does. If it points between two of the four long ticks, round to the nearer one; the four short diagonal marks show the exact halfway lines. Answer with exactly one word: up, right, down, or left.

worlds.title: Padlock shackle connection
worlds.question: At the padlock body's top edge, which end of the black U-shaped shackle is visibly separated from the body? Answer left, neither, or right.

worlds.title: Recycling flow consistency conflict
worlds.question: Do all three two-tone arrows point around the red center in the same circular direction? Use each dark triangular head to judge its arrow, ignore the corner marks, and answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Chroma difference reveal
worlds.question: The image is a uniform colored-noise field. Take the red-minus-green channel difference at every pixel. A coarse diagonal-band letter appears where the difference is large. Which letter is revealed, A or B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Spiral scan reveal
worlds.question: After placing the row-major stream back through the marked spiral and averaging, which broad symbol appears?

worlds.title: Slice sort reassembly
worlds.question: The image shows eight separate vertical slices standing side by side. Each slice is a stack of 8 square cells and some cells are filled dark. Under every slice a coloured key bar is printed, and all eight bars have different heights. The slices were cut from one 8x8 sheet and then shuffled; a slice's bar height gives its place in that sheet, shortest bar leftmost and tallest bar rightmost. Put the eight slices back in that order, keeping every slice upright and unchanged. The dark cells of the rebuilt 8x8 sheet then match one of these symbols: ex, frame, tee, ell, diamond. Which symbol do they most closely match? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Neighborhood majority reveal
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 12 by 12 grid, replace each cell by a dark cell exactly when at least five cells in its centered 3 by 3 neighborhood are dark; cells beyond the frame count as light. Which symbol appears: ring, tee, chevron, or cup?

worlds.title: Keyed block average glyph
worlds.question: The cyan frame contains a 9-by-9 field of tiny dark squares. The gold square shows one averaging window, exactly one faint grid cell. Replace every cell by its average darkness (a uniform two-dimensional box average), treat the darker of the two resulting levels as ink and the lighter as blank, and do not rotate or reflect. Which glyph appears: tee, corner, chevron, or fork?

worlds.title: Contour closure
worlds.question: A set of short dark line segments is drawn as a ring on a white canvas, placed end to end with small gaps between neighbours. Wherever two neighbouring segments nearly meet they count as connected; if every consecutive pair nearly meets all the way around, the whole ring closes into ONE single loop. An 'open' drawing, by contrast, has one place where the chain is broken by a much larger, clearly visible gap, so the segments do NOT form a loop. Does the drawing form a single closed loop? Choose: closed or open.

worlds.title: Vanishing point convergence
worlds.question: Which colored field has short strokes whose imagined supporting lines meet at one common point? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Dashed loop enclosure
worlds.question: The picture shows four closed curves and one black dot on a plain background. Each curve is painted as a ring of short dashes of one colour, so its outline is broken by small gaps; the gaps are openings in the drawing only, and every curve is still one closed loop that comes back to where it started. No curve crosses or touches another curve, no region is filled, and the colours, the sizes, the positions of the curves, the number of dashes and the total amount of ink carry no information. A curve encloses the black dot when the dot lies in the region shut in by that closed loop. How many of the four curves enclose the black dot? Answer 0, 1, 2 or 3.

worlds.title: Convex layer survivor
worlds.question: Imagine stretching the tightest convex rubber band around all the dots. Remove every dot the band touches, then repeat on the remaining dots. Which colored dot is removed later? Answer red, blue, or tie.

worlds.title: Rotational orbit completion
worlds.question: The hollow gray ring marks the center. Ignore the four colored dots when judging the existing dark constellation. Under a 120-degree turn about the ring, the dark dots form complete three-dot orbits except for one missing position. Which colored candidate dot fills that position? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Convexity search
worlds.question: Four filled polygons are drawn, one in each quadrant of the image (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). Exactly one polygon is convex: it bulges outward everywhere and has no inward notch. The other three polygons are concave: each has one clearly visible inward notch. Which quadrant contains the only convex polygon?

worlds.title: Concyclic marker panel search
worlds.question: The image shows four equal panels labeled A, B, C, and D. Each panel contains exactly four identical dark disks. The centers of four disks are concyclic when one circle passes through all four centers. Which labeled panel contains the only concyclic quartet? Ignore labels and locations, inspect every panel, and answer A, B, C, or D. A unique residual gap separates the correct panel from the runner-up.

worlds.title: Pipe path panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Each panel contains a network of straight dark pipes laid on the same square lattice of nodes: every pipe runs either horizontally or vertically between two neighbouring lattice nodes, and pipes touch one another only end to end at a shared node, so no pipe ever crosses over or under another. Every panel contains exactly the same number of pipes and the same total length of gap, so the amount of ink, the number of pipes and the general clutter carry no information. In every panel exactly three of the pipes are broken: a broken pipe is drawn with a plainly visible empty gap in its middle, and no connection passes across that gap. Each panel also carries exactly two round terminal dots in a warm colour, each sitting on a lattice node where unbroken pipe ink meets, and in every panel the two terminals stand the same lattice distance apart, so their spacing and their placement inside the panel carry no information. Two terminals count as joined only if you can travel from one to the other along a continuous unbroken chain of pipe ink, following the pipes, never jumping across a gap and never crossing empty background. In exactly one panel the two terminals are joined. In each of the other four panels every possible route between the two terminals is interrupted by at least one visible gap, and the narrowest gap that would have to be bridged there is at least twice the width of a pipe. Which numbered panel has its two terminal dots joined by a continuous unbroken chain of pipe? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Two closed loops search
worlds.question: Which panel contains exactly two completely closed dark loops? A loop is closed only when its dark stroke has no gap. The short detached dashes are not loops. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Equal pip pairs search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has the same number of navy pips in its left and right compartments? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State first revisit
worlds.question: Five panels are stacked vertically and read TOP TO BOTTOM as panel 1, panel 2, panel 3, panel 4, panel 5. Every panel shows the same horizontal track divided into five equal slots, with slot 1 leftmost and slot 5 rightmost. One red token sits in exactly one slot of each panel. The red token is the SAME token in every panel, and between any two consecutive panels it always moves to a DIFFERENT slot. A REVISIT means the token returns, in some panel, to a slot it already occupied in an EARLIER panel (higher in the stack). Reading the panels in order, in which panel does the token FIRST revisit a previous slot? If the token NEVER returns to a slot it used earlier, answer 'never'. Answer 'panel 3', 'panel 4', 'panel 5', or 'never'.

worlds.title: State motion concordance
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 from left to right. Each identity keeps its glyph and shows a keyed state LOW, MID, or HIGH. Between adjacent panels, a transition agrees when state and horizontal slot move in the same direction, including stay/stay. Which label has the most agreeing transitions? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Pour transfer replay
worlds.question: The picture shows four vessels standing side by side. A vessel is drawn as a vertical stack of square unit cells: the number of cells in a stack is that vessel's capacity, that is, the largest number of units it can hold, and it never holds more. The dark blue cells, which always sit at the bottom of a stack, are the units the vessel holds to begin with, and the light grey cells above them are its free space. Different vessels may have different capacities and different starting amounts. Under each vessel there is one coloured disc, and the four disc colours, green, orange, purple and yellow, are all different, so a vessel is named by the colour of its own disc. Below the vessels there is a row of five cream cards, and each card is one pour. A card carries two small discs coloured like two of the vessel discs and one black arrow drawn between them: the card pours from the vessel named by the disc at the arrow's tail, the plain end, into the vessel named by the disc the arrowhead points at. A pour moves as many whole units as it can, which is the smaller of two amounts: the number of units the source vessel is holding at that moment, and the free space still left in the target vessel at that moment. So the pour stops as soon as the source is empty or the target is full, whichever happens first, and any units it could not move stay in the source vessel. Nothing is spilled or created: the units a pour moves leave the source and arrive in the target. The cards act one at a time, in order from the leftmost card to the rightmost card, as the grey arrow below the row shows, and the amounts the vessels hold keep changing as later cards act. A red ring marks one of the vessel discs: the marked vessel is the one whose disc centre is nearest to the centre of that red ring. The amounts the vessels hold after the cards have acted are not drawn anywhere; only the starting stacks are drawn. After all five cards have acted in order from left to right, how many units does the marked vessel hold? Answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Turn flip walker
worlds.question: The magenta arrow shows the walker's starting cell and direction. The board wraps at every edge. Perform the seven STEP cards from left to right. For each step: if the current tile is LIGHT, turn right; if it is DARK, turn left. Then flip that tile and move forward one cell. Which direction does the walker face after all seven steps? Answer up, right, down, or left.

worlds.title: Bulk color rewrite
worlds.question: The top row shows six beads. Read the cards from left to right. On each card, every bead whose color matches the left dot changes at the same time to the right dot; all other beads stay unchanged. After all cards, how many blue beads are there? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Curve loop crossings
worlds.question: The image shows one closed black loop (a ring) on a white background and a thick red thread that starts at a green dot and ends at a blue dot. The thread is an open curve: it begins at the green dot, travels across the picture, and stops at the blue dot. The thread CROSSES the black loop each time it passes from the inside of the loop to the outside (or from the outside to the inside). A crossing happens exactly where the red thread overlaps the black ring. How many times does the red thread cross the black loop? Count each passage through the ring as one crossing. Answer with a single number from 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Articulation junction
worlds.question: Which colored junction is an articulation point? Remove that junction and every line segment touching it; which removal increases the number of disconnected pieces of the visible network? Answer red, blue, or green; ignore the frame and text.

worlds.title: Loop depth duel
worlds.question: The picture shows black closed loops on white paper, plus one red dot and one blue dot. Every black curve is a complete closed loop with no opening. Loops never touch or cross each other, and no dot touches a loop. A loop surrounds a dot when the dot lies inside that loop; loops that do not contain the dot do not count, no matter how near they are. Which dot is surrounded by more loops? Answer red, blue, or same.

worlds.title: Euler trail panel
worlds.question: Links meet only at cyan round stations; a crossing without a station is not a connection. Which network can be traced in one stroke using every link exactly once, without lifting or repeating a link? The stroke may start and finish at different stations. Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Marked link distance three
worlds.question: Does the shortest route from the green junction to the purple junction use exactly three dark links? Follow links only between visible circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Fork branch marker count
worlds.question: A blue line starts at an orange ring, runs along a shared trunk to a junction, then splits into two branches. Each branch ends in a coloured terminal dot (red or green), and several black waypoint dots are drawn along each branch. Starting at the ring, walk along the blue line to the junction and then follow both branches to their ends. Which coloured terminal, red or green, is on the branch that has MORE black waypoints along it? Answer red or green.

worlds.title: Cycle route terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green source, follow dark links without reusing a link. Which colored node, red or blue, can be reached by two different routes? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Wall pass first dot
worlds.question: The grey line in this picture is one single cable. It never branches and it never touches or crosses itself, so it has exactly two loose ends. One of those ends lies inside the orange ring. The short black bar is a wall. The cable is drawn on top of the wall, so wherever the cable runs over the bar the bar is interrupted, and each such place counts as one crossing of the wall. Three dots - one red, one green and one blue - sit on the cable. Start at the end inside the orange ring and walk along the cable, following every bend, towards the other end. Ignore every dot you meet before your first crossing of the wall. Which dot is the first one you meet after you have crossed the wall for the first time? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: First repeat checkpoint
worlds.question: Start at the green ring and follow the one continuous dark cable to the red square. Which checkpoint color is the first to appear for a second time: orange, purple, or blue? Count checkpoints in travel order along the cable.

worlds.title: Longest alternating checkpoint run
worlds.question: Each panel has one unbranched black route from a green START disk to a colored terminal. Follow each route and read its six cyan and yellow checkpoints in travel order. Which terminal has the longest contiguous run in which checkpoint colors alternate cyan, yellow, cyan, yellow (or yellow, cyan, yellow, cyan)? A run stops when two consecutive checkpoints have the same color. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Band attribute correspondence
worlds.question: A single large connected plaque fills most of the image. At its far left and far right sit two coloured blocks. Do the two blocks at the two distant ends carry the SAME colour? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Pulse flip correspondence
worlds.question: The navy trace has three labeled lanes: R is the reference and A and B are candidates. Each lane has four interior pulses. Flip each candidate lane vertically, read all four pulses from left to right, and choose the candidate whose up/down pulse sequence exactly matches R.

worlds.title: Triroster pip consensus bind
worlds.question: The sandy board is scattered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly three pale ROSTER panels sit on it, each in a different far corner of the board. Only what is drawn inside the three rosters decides the answer; every square lying on the bare board is decoration and means nothing. Each roster carries six large square TOKENS, and each roster carries exactly one token of every colour: red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. Inside every token sit between one and four small dark square PIPS, and that number is the token's pip count. The tokens are arranged in a different order inside each roster, so a token's position tells you nothing about its colour and matching tokens by position does not work: you must match them by colour. Because every colour appears exactly once on every roster, and because every pip count from one to four appears on every roster, no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink singles out the answer. Exactly one colour is given the SAME pip count on all three rosters. Every other colour is given the same pip count on at most two of the three rosters, and each pair of rosters agrees on at least one further colour besides the answer, so reading only two rosters can never decide the answer: all three distant rosters must be compared. Which colour has the same pip count on all three rosters? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Room neighbor atlas
worlds.question: The four mosaics share one navy atlas. The gold-tagged mosaic is the reference. Two room colors are neighbors when their square cells share a side; corner contact does not count. Which red, green, or blue tag marks the mosaic with exactly the same set of neighboring color pairs as the reference?

worlds.title: Chord gap correspondence
worlds.question: The upper strip has the same circle, square, and triangle on both sides of a missing center. Each lower colored frame is a candidate insert. In a candidate, follow each colored route from its left port to its right port; route colors only help tracing. Without rotating or flipping, which frame reconnects every left shape to the identical right shape? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Paired trace crossing parity
worlds.question: Across the two separated mini-plots, is the combined number of trace crossings of the dashed baselines odd or even? Answer odd or even.

worlds.title: Nearest tick lean count
worlds.question: The picture is a white measurement sheet carrying two separate horizontal rows of short vertical ticks that never touch each other. One row is drawn in pure black: those six or more black ticks are evenly spaced and form the reference lattice. The other row is drawn in red and holds exactly six red gauge ticks; each red tick stands a little way to the left or to the right of one black lattice tick, and no red tick is exactly aligned with a black one. The red row may be drawn above or below the black row; the colours, not the positions, say which row is which. Every pale grey, blue and green mark elsewhere on the sheet is decoration and carries no information. For each red gauge tick, look at the one black lattice tick whose centre is closest to that red tick's centre; the red tick leans left if its centre is to the left of that black tick's centre, and leans right otherwise. How many of the six red gauge ticks lean left? Answer with a single whole number: 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Slope sign agreement
worlds.question: Do the coral and blue needles lean in the same horizontal direction as they rise? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Paired delta comparison
worlds.question: The left column is PRE and the right column is POST. For each color, define change as POST height minus PRE height (higher on the chart is positive). Which sample has the larger change? Answer CYAN or ORANGE.

worlds.title: Racecourse loop closure
worlds.question: Is the visible racecourse a closed loop? Treat the saturated route as the racecourse: answer yes only when it joins continuously back to itself, and no when the route has two visible ends.

worlds.title: Button eyelet holes
worlds.question: This picture shows a scattered sewing kit on a plain white background. Exactly one item is drawn in a strong colour: a single round button, drawn as one filled coloured disc. Every other mark is plain grey - including grey discs that also have holes - and every grey mark is decoration that must be ignored; no grey mark touches or overlaps the coloured button. A hole is a background-coloured opening lying completely inside the coloured disc; the holes never touch one another and never reach the rim of the disc. A button in this picture may have any number of holes. How many holes does the coloured button have? Answer with exactly one of: 2, 3, 4, 5.

worlds.title: Split medallion area balance
worlds.question: Inside the outlined circular medallion, do the dark and light colored regions cover the same area? Ignore the outline. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Color grid latin validity
worlds.question: Does every row and every column of the visible 4-by-4 color grid contain four different dot colors? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Paired register difference
worlds.question: There are two far-separated square registers, each marked by a gold corner notch. Turn both registers until the notch is upper-left. For every corresponding cell of the aligned 8-by-8 rasters, write # when the mean RGB colors differ and . when they match. Read the resulting 8-by-8 difference bitmap and compare it with A) RING = 00111100/01100110/11000011/11000011/11000011/11000011/01100110/00111100 or B) CROSS = 10011001/00011000/00011000/11111111/11111111/00011000/00011000/10011001. Which symbol appears? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Halfturn shade rank reveal
worlds.question: This picture shows one large square panel with a solid dark border. Inside the border the panel is a lattice of 12 rows and 12 columns of equal square cells, separated by thin coloured rules; number the rows 1 to 12 from the top and the columns 1 to 12 from the left. Every cell is filled with a single flat shade, and exactly three shades are used in the whole panel: a light one, a middle one and a dark one. All three shades appear many times, so 'darker' always means darker than another cell of the same panel and never darker than some fixed outside standard. Four coloured notches on the border, one on each side, mark the panel's horizontal and vertical centre lines; they cross at the panel's centre point, which is the corner where the four middle cells meet. Carry out this operation. Turn the panel a half turn, 180 degrees, about that centre point, so that the cell in row r and column c lands on the cell in row 13 minus r and column 13 minus c. Now look only at the upper half of the panel, its rows 1 to 6, and mark every cell there that is strictly darker in shade than the cell it lands on, that is the cell in row 13 minus r and column 13 minus c. Leave a cell unmarked when the two shades are equal and when the landing cell is the darker one. The marks form a pattern on a lattice 12 cells wide and 6 cells tall, and that pattern is always exactly one of six figures. 'cross' is a wide horizontal bar two rows thick across the middle with a two-cell wide vertical bar through the middle running the full height. 'tee' is a solid two-row bar along the top with a two-cell wide vertical bar hanging from its middle. 'ell' is a three-cell wide vertical bar down the left side with a solid two-row bar along the bottom. 'ring' is a hollow rectangle: solid top and bottom rows and single-cell left and right sides. 'ex' is two full diagonals crossing. 'arrow' is a chevron whose two arms meet at the bottom middle and continue as a short two-cell wide stem. The figure is drawn nowhere in the picture. Each pair of compared cells straddles both centre lines, so no half of the panel contains a single complete pair and neither half alone rules out any figure. The three shades are used exactly 48 times each in the panel and exactly 24 times each in the upper half, so shade area, cell counts, colours, sizes and positions are the same for every answer. Which figure do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: arrow, cross, ell, ex, ring, tee.

worlds.title: Toothline rasterize
worlds.question: Follow the connected route from the amber triangle to the teal circle. It has nine V-shaped teeth. In route order, write a dark cell for a tooth pointing up and a light cell for a tooth pointing down, filling a 3 by 3 tile left-to-right and top-to-bottom. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Paired bar average reveal
worlds.question: Starting at each triangular notch, match the seven bar rows in order. For each pair, average the two dark bar lengths (all averages are whole cells), then center a bar of that average length in a nine-cell row. Which symbol do the seven centered rows form: arrow, diamond, or funnel? If the two closest symbols tie, answer ambiguous.

worlds.title: Ordered wire waypoints
worlds.question: A black arrow marks the start of one continuous colored wire. Follow the wire from the arrow through its three circular tags. Which tag color is encountered second: amber, teal, or violet? Answer with the color name.

worlds.title: Through thread edges
worlds.question: The page carries several thin dark threads. All threads have exactly the same dark colour and the same thickness, so colour and thickness say nothing about which thread matters; every pale grey blob is background clutter and must be ignored. Exactly two thread ends touch each of the four sides of the page -- two on the top side, two on the bottom side, two on the left side and two on the right side -- so counting ends on a side cannot settle the question. Threads never touch or cross each other. Exactly one thread runs all the way from one side of the page to a different side; every other thread starts on a side and dead-ends deep inside the page, far from any side. Some dead-ending threads are longer than the thread that gets across, so length does not settle it either: the only way to tell is to follow a thread along its whole length from one end to the other. Report the two sides linked by the single thread that runs from one side to another. Answer ambiguous if more than one thread links two different sides. Which two sides of the page does that one through-thread join?

worlds.title: Thread symmetry mode
worlds.question: Can the entire connected blue network be traced in one continuous stroke without lifting and without retracing any segment? Answer possible or impossible.

worlds.title: Detached seam interlock
worlds.question: The two separated colored pieces have equally tall jagged facing edges. Without turning either piece, slide them straight horizontally together. Would the two entire jagged edges meet exactly, or would bumps collide and leave gaps? Answer fit or clash.

worlds.title: Solid medallion sector
worlds.question: A set of dark discs is scattered on a white canvas split into four quadrants by a gray cross at the center. Exactly one disc is the solid badge: a fully filled (solid) disc of standard size. The others are hollow rings, too-small solid discs, or too-large solid discs. Which quadrant contains the unique solid badge? Answer top_left, top_right, bottom_left, or bottom_right.

worlds.title: Inward crescent pair search
worlds.question: Each quadrant contains one badge made of two separate crescent-shaped marks. A crescent's opening is its concave side. Which quadrant contains the only badge whose two openings face toward one another across their gap? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Weak link pair search
worlds.question: The picture shows eight upright coloured bars on a plain background: two red bars, two blue bars, two green bars and two purple bars. The two bars that share a colour form one pair, and colour alone says which two bars belong together; the two bars of one pair are always drawn near each other with plain background between them, and each pair keeps to its own part of the page. All bars are drawn with the same width; only their lengths differ. The bars float freely, so they do not stand on any shared baseline and the length of a bar is how long the bar itself is, not how high or how low it sits on the page. Score a pair by the length of its shorter bar: the pair's score is the length of whichever of its two bars is the shorter one, so a pair with one very long bar and one short bar scores badly. Exactly one pair has a strictly greater score than every other pair. The single longest bar in the whole picture always belongs to one of the losing pairs, so the answer is never the colour of the longest bar. Which pair holds more coloured ink in total, where each pair sits on the page, which bar of a pair is drawn on the upper left and which on the lower right, how far apart the two bars of a pair are, and the small grey specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which coloured pair has the longest shorter bar? Answer with one of: red, blue, green, purple.

worlds.title: Overlapping density search
worlds.question: Each colored dot marks a cyan mosaic cell. For each dot, count the cyan cells in the 5-by-5 square of cells centered on its marked cell; the marked cell counts as cyan. Which color has the largest count? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Paired angle sum search
worlds.question: Each color appears once in the left set and once in the right set. Which color's two angle openings add up exactly to the gold reference angle? Exactly one matches. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Focal toggle register
worlds.question: Find the single round state-register disk: its colour declares the initial state (blue = OFF, orange = ON). A cluster of red dots rests tightly on and around this disk; every one of those red dots is a toggle that flips the state (OFF to ON, or ON to OFF). Red dots placed far away elsewhere on the canvas are decoys and do nothing. Apply every toggle in the disk's cluster to the initial state and read the final state. Does the tracked state finish ON? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route toggle accumulator
worlds.question: Starting at the green square, trace the one connected dark route to the purple finish marker. The token starts OFF; a diamond gate toggles its state and a circular gate leaves it unchanged. Is the token ON at the finish? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Gapshift tray replay
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small cassette drawn with a thick black frame, and every pale grey mark lying outside that frame is inert decoration that means nothing. Inside the frame there are two pale beds. The upper bed is a tray of nine equal square cells in three rows of three. Eight of those cells are filled with a solid colour: exactly two red, two green, two blue and two yellow. The ninth cell is left as bare pale bed, and that cell is the gap. One tray cell also carries a thick black ring drawn just inside its own border; the ring is only a marking and the cell it rings holds a colour like any other cell. The lower bed is a strip of four equal slots, each holding one solid black arrow, and the four arrows are carried out in order from the leftmost slot to the rightmost slot. Each arrow points up, down, left or right, and it says which way the gap moves for that step: the gap exchanges places with the single coloured cell immediately next to it in the direction the arrow points, so that cell's colour slides into the square the gap has just left and the gap takes over that cell. Every one of the four arrows shown is a move the gap can actually make, so the gap never runs off the tray, and nothing else in the tray changes during a step. The ring never moves: it stays on the same tray cell from the first step to the last, and only the colours slide. After all four arrows have been carried out, which colour stands in the ringed cell? Answer with one of red, green, blue or yellow.

worlds.title: Second collection wire
worlds.question: Begin with an empty collection at the round START. Follow the connected wire to the arrow and read each bead in order. Add its letter to the collection; repeated letters add nothing. Whenever A, B, and C have all been collected, note the letter on that completing bead and immediately empty the collection. Which letter completes the second collection: A, B, or C?

worlds.title: Twin vessel transfer ledger
worlds.question: The two bowls start with the shown bead counts. Read the four separate cards by their purple dot counts: one, then two, three, and four. Each teal arrow moves exactly one bead from the bowl at its tail to the bowl at its head; no source bowl is empty when used. After all four transfers, which bowl has more beads: left, same, or right?

worlds.title: Compact cavity parity
worlds.question: The solid dark blob encloses exactly one or two white cavities (holes). Is the number of enclosed white cavities ODD or EVEN? Answer odd or even.

worlds.title: Focal face degree
worlds.question: Which colored chamber has the most full-wall neighbors? Count only chambers sharing a straight wall segment; answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Sealed pool area verdict
worlds.question: This page shows one solid dark reef of blocky outline, together with grey, blue, orange, red and green decorations that lie on the open page away from the reef. Only the dark reef ink and the white paper decide the answer; the coloured decorations never count and never block anything. White paper cut into the reef forms pools. A pool is shut when dark reef ink encloses it completely, so that no white route leads from that pool out to the open page around the reef; a pool that reaches the open page through a white gap in the reef is an open notch, and an open notch never counts, no matter how large it looks or how deep it cuts. Take the shut pools only. Compare the white area of the single largest shut pool with the summed white area of every other shut pool. Areas are compared as they are drawn, and the reef is drawn on a coarse block grid, so no shut pool is a borderline sliver.
