How much dark ink the reef carries, how many shut pools there are, how large the reef is, where the reef sits on the page, how deep the open notches cut, and which colours appear never decide the answer by themselves. Is the largest shut pool larger in white area than all the other shut pools put together? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Common neighbor rooms
worlds.question: Black walls divide the white floor into rooms. Two different rooms are neighbors when they share a black wall segment; meeting only at a corner does not count. Which color's two marked rooms have at least one common neighboring room: cyan or orange? Exactly one color does.

worlds.title: Common cycle station
worlds.question: The navy links form an undirected station graph: eight stations are arranged in two rows and exactly one nearest-neighbor link is missing. Is the red station on every simple cycle? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Detached trace checkpoint
worlds.question: Following each detached trace from its green start toward red, which ringed checkpoint is encountered first: amber or violet? Compare order along each drawn trace, not straight-line position.

worlds.title: Husk merge node
worlds.question: The image shows one opaque light-gray square chip on a plain white background, together with scattered gray bars that all lie outside the chip. Inside the chip, one network of thick dark corridors of constant width joins six small square markers. Three markers sit inside the chip and are coloured, one orange, one purple and one blue; each of those three sits where exactly three corridors meet. Two markers are green and one marker is yellow, and all three of those sit on the chip's border. Every corridor either joins two markers or runs from one marker to the chip's border and stops there; no two corridors cross or touch except at a marker, and between any two markers there is exactly one route along corridors that never reuses a corridor. From each green marker take that one route to the yellow marker. The two routes begin apart and then run together, and the first marker that both routes pass through is always one of the three coloured markers. The gray bars outside the chip are decoration and mean nothing. Which coloured marker is the first marker that both routes pass through? Answer orange, purple or blue.

worlds.title: Directed divider area
worlds.question: Trace the navy divider from the green START to the red FINISH. Which side of your travel contains more cream floor: left or right? Ignore the divider and the colored endpoint markers.

worlds.title: Ribbon midpoint checkpoint
worlds.question: Follow the dark centerline from the blue start to the orange finish along the broad folded ribbon. Which checkpoint ring, red or green, is closer to the halfway point of the entire route measured along the centerline?

worlds.title: Riffle rank binding
worlds.question: The KEY row shows six coloured tokens, each with a rank ruler beneath it: the number of filled cells in that ruler is the token's rank, from 1 to 6. Below, candidate rows A and B show the same six colours without rulers. Split the ranks into a low half (1,2,3) and a high half (4,5,6). A row is riffled when, reading left to right, it alternates low, high, low, high, low, high, with the low ranks ascending and the high ranks ascending, giving 1,4,2,5,3,6. In each candidate row, translate every token to its KEY rank, reading left to right. Which single row, A or B, is the riffled one? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Conditional nose reversal
worlds.question: Each panel shows a blue puck with a gold nose, a green arrow showing its movement, a violet gate line, and a red bullseye. Imagine sliding the puck to the arrowhead. If the moved center is to the right of the gate line, turn the puck 180 degrees around its center; otherwise keep its facing. Which panel would put the gold nose inside the bullseye? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Two hop attribute relay
worlds.question: One tile in the left column is ringed in black. Find the middle-column tile holding that same black shape, and count the dots in that middle tile. Then find the right-column tile with that same number of dots. What color is its bar? Answer blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Cross splice tilewalk
worlds.question: Move both tokens for 8 rounds. RED reads the red arrow on BLUE's card; BLUE reads the blue arrow on RED's card. Move together using the start-of-round board. Then rebuild RED's vacated card from RED-landing red + BLUE-landing blue; rebuild BLUE's vacated card from BLUE-landing red + RED-landing blue. Read both landing cards before rebuilding; landing cards stay. Which goal contains RED: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Forced bijection matrix
worlds.question: A dot means that a row may pair with a column. Pair all eight rows with different columns. There is exactly one complete assignment. Which column must the red-ringed TARGET row take? Answer A, B, C, D, E, F, G, or H.

worlds.title: Correspondence arrow heading
worlds.question: The top reference panel shows one gray arrow. Below, three candidate panels A, B, C each show one colored arrow. Each arrow points in one of eight compass directions (east, northeast, north, northwest, west, southwest, south, southeast). Which candidate's arrow points in the same compass direction as the reference arrow?

worlds.title: Colored gap direction correspondence
worlds.question: The image has a REFERENCE panel and candidates A and B. Each panel contains five isolated, uniquely colored open boxes. The gap direction is the side of a square outline that is missing: UP, RIGHT, DOWN, or LEFT. Which candidate has exactly the same mapping from color to gap direction as the REFERENCE? Boxes may be rearranged and resized; ignore panel position, box position, box size, and box order. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Flip stack shade binding
worlds.question: This image shows four tokens. Each token is a vertical stack of four flat gray tiles with a solid black tab touching exactly one end of the stack. The tab marks where the token's shade sequence starts, so a token is read tile by tile starting at its tab end: top to bottom when the tab is above the stack, bottom to top when the tab is below it. Each tile counts as one of three shades - dark, medium or light - and every token in the image uses the same four shades in some order, so only the order of the shades read from the tab end distinguishes the tokens. The token labeled REF at the top is the reference. The three lower tokens, labeled A, B and C from left to right, are each surrounded by a colored halo, and exactly one of them reads out the same shade sequence as REF. What is the halo color of that matching token? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Threaded checkpoint order
worlds.question: Trace the single dark route from the green START dot to the red FINISH dot. Record the colors of the four square checkpoints in the order the route passes through them. Routes may bend differently. Which option has exactly the same checkpoint-color order as the REFERENCE? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Cube net opposite correspondence
worlds.question: Fold the six connected squares of the NET into a cube. Which colored face is opposite the face with the magenta ring: red, green, or blue? Squares joined by an edge stay joined; colors and the ring stay on their faces.

worlds.title: Under curve area
worlds.question: Three colored hills stand on three gray baselines, each colored region filled solidly beneath its flat hilltop. Which colored hill has the largest filled area (the most colored ink under its curve)? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Baseline crossing compare
worlds.question: Which panel, A or B, has more strict crossings of its colored trace with its horizontal baseline? Count a crossing only when adjacent marked checkpoints lie on opposite sides. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Rise chain reference
worlds.question: The picture shows nine gray bars of equal width, evenly spaced and standing on one black baseline; only their heights differ. A single black bar stands on the same baseline to the left of the vertical black divider: that is the reference bar, and only its height matters. Read the nine gray bars from left to right. A pair of neighbouring gray bars is a RISE when the right bar of the pair is taller than the left bar by strictly more than the height of the reference bar; every other neighbouring pair is not a rise. A CHAIN is a group of consecutive gray bars in which every neighbouring pair inside the group is a rise, and the longest chain never contains more than five bars. A single gray bar with no rise on either side of it is a chain of one bar. The pale horizontal guide rows are decorative and carry no information. How many gray bars does the longest chain contain? Answer 1, 2, 3, 4 or 5.

worlds.title: Step plateau leader
worlds.question: Which colored step curve contains the longest uninterrupted horizontal plateau? Measure each plateau from one vertical step to the next, or from a plot edge to the nearest step. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Donut entropy leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order. In each donut, treat the four colored sector areas as proportions p. Compute -sum(p log2 p). Which panel has the largest value? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior table legs
worlds.question: This is a table. How many legs does it have? Count only the visible legs and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Checkerboard columns
worlds.question: How many columns are in the checkerboard? Count each vertical column of visible squares once; ignore the CHECKERBOARD label and the outer border. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Mirror twin chirality
worlds.question: This image shows a grey vertical bar with one coloured step-block shape on each side of it. The bar, the small grey squares on the bar, the grey baseline and the white background are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. Both shapes are drawn in the same colour, stand on the same baseline, are built from the same five columns of the same width, cover the same total area, and are placed symmetrically about the bar. The only thing that can differ is the left-to-right order of their five column heights. Read that order off each shape and compare the two, using the image itself and not what a mirror normally does. The right-hand shape is 'mirrored' if its column heights run in the reversed order of the left-hand shape's, and 'copied' if they run in the same order. Answer with exactly one word: mirrored or copied.

worlds.title: Bias traffic lamps
worlds.question: How many colored circular lamps are visible inside the traffic signal? Count each separate colored circle once.

worlds.title: Fork prong conflict
worlds.question: How many separate upward prongs are visible above the fork's solid shoulder? Count each separated tip once and answer with a number.

worlds.title: Skewness letter reveal
worlds.question: The image is a 16x16 field of gray-noise blocks. Every block has the same mean brightness and the same variance, so no level, range, or spread cue can hide or reveal anything. But a coarse letter is encoded in the local SHAPE of the luminance distribution: a glyph-stroke block is lopsided (most pixels slightly dark, a minority quite bright, so it has a strong positive third central moment), while a background block is symmetric gray noise (zero skewness). Compute the local luminance SKEWNESS of every block so the lopsided stroke blocks light up and the letter appears. Which letter is revealed, T or L? Answer T or L.

worlds.title: Interleaved column symbol
worlds.question: Four colored corner marks enclose a grayscale square. Its columns were recorded in the order 0, S/2, 1, S/2+1, 2, S/2+2, and so on, where S is the square width. Undo that column interleave, apply a 5x5 mean filter with edge replication, and ignore the colored marks and fine texture. Which broad symbol appears: bell, leaf, ladder, or hook?

worlds.title: Arrow aim stencil reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows a sheet of white paper carrying one solid red dot and a 5 by 5 square grid of 25 dark solid triangular arrowheads, one arrowhead in every cell of the grid. Four small blue squares printed at the four corners of the grid mark its extent: each blue square sits at the outer corner of a corner cell, so the four blue squares are the corners of the square block of 25 cells. Every arrowhead is the same size and shape, and each one sits at the centre of its own cell; only the direction it points differs from cell to cell. Apply this rule to the grid: shade a cell if, and only if, that cell's arrowhead points straight at the red dot, that is, if the ray leaving the arrowhead's blunt back through its sharp tip would run into the red dot. Every other arrowhead is turned well away from the red dot, by at least 55 degrees. The shaded cells then draw one of these five symbols on the 5 by 5 grid: plus (the whole middle row and the whole middle column shaded, making an upright cross), ex (both full diagonals shaded, making a diagonal cross), tee (the whole top row plus the rest of the middle column shaded), ell (the whole left column plus the rest of the bottom row shaded), cee (the whole left column plus the rest of the top row shaded). One or two cells may be shaded wrongly; take the symbol that the shaded cells match most closely. Which symbol do the shaded cells form? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Vertical difference reveal
worlds.question: The magenta frame contains the reference row. For every cell in the cyan grid, compare it with the cell directly above, using the reference-row cell above the first row. Make the result black if the two cells differ and white if they match. Which symbol appears: flag, hook, stair, or fork?

worlds.title: Diagonal parity projection
worlds.question: The cyan frame contains a 13-by-13 source mosaic. Read its 25 northwest-to-southeast diagonals in order, starting with the single bottom-left cell and ending with the single top-right cell. For each diagonal, write dark if it contains an odd number of dark source tiles and light if it contains an even number. Pack the 25 results left-to-right across five rows of a 5-by-5 result, without rotating or reflecting it; ignore gray grid lines and gold guide marks. Which reference card matches? Cards A, B, C, and D are in reading order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

worlds.title: Negative space cavity
worlds.question: A field of colored square tiles covers the canvas except for one empty white region at its center. Which shape does that empty region form? Choose from: circle, square, diamond, triangle.

worlds.title: Circular flow coherence
worlds.question: Which colored field has dash directions that follow one smooth circular flow around its center? Compare the whole field; ignore color, count, position, and isolated dashes. Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Proximity group count
worlds.question: The picture shows identical coloured dots and one black reference bar. Two dots are linked when the straight-line distance between their centres is shorter than the length of the black bar. Linking is transitive: dots joined through other dots belong to the same group. How many groups do the dots form? Answer 2, 3, 4 or 5.

worlds.title: Dotfield symmetry axis
worlds.question: Which colored dashed line is the mirror-symmetry axis of the complete black dot constellation? Answer orange or blue.

worlds.title: Constellation total tether
worlds.question: Imagine one straight tether from each colored ring's center to every dark-dot center. Add the tether lengths separately for each ring. Which ring has the smallest total length? Use center-to-center distances; the rings are candidates, not dots, and ring size does not count. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Reference bar thickness match
worlds.question: A dark horizontal reference bar is drawn inside the grey box at the top of the image. The thickness of a bar is how tall it is: the vertical extent between its top edge and its bottom edge. Below the box the image is split by thin lines into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), each containing one dark horizontal bar. Exactly one quadrant's bar has the SAME thickness as the reference bar; the other three bars each have a clearly different thickness. Which quadrant contains the bar whose thickness matches the reference bar? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Cyclic gap alternation search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only four-point arrangement whose two shortest consecutive center-to-center gaps alternate with its two longest gaps when the four disk centers are read clockwise, including the wraparound gap? Each panel contains exactly four identical dark disks; ignore labels and panel position, and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Nested span panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side, numbered panel-1 to panel-5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly five horizontal coloured bars drawn one above another at five fixed heights. Read every bar as the horizontal stretch it covers between its left end and its right end; the height, thickness, colour and vertical position of a bar never carry information, and bars in different panels are never compared. Two bars of the same panel are separate when their stretches do not touch at all, nested when one stretch lies entirely inside the other, and crossing when the stretches overlap while neither one lies entirely inside the other. In exactly one panel every pair of bars is separate or nested, so that panel holds no crossing pair; each of the other four panels holds at least one crossing pair, and every overlap, gap and nesting margin in the image is at least sixteen pixels wide, so no pair is a close call. Every panel holds five bars and nearly the same total bar length, and bar colours are dealt at random, so bar count, colour, size and total ink can never identify the panel. Which numbered panel contains no crossing pair of bars? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Inscribed circle search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has an amber circle that touches all three sides of the outlined triangle without crossing any side? Panels A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Balanced brackets search
worlds.question: Reading left to right, which labeled row is a balanced bracket sequence? Add one for each opening bracket and subtract one for each closing bracket: the running total must never go below zero and must finish at zero. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State rendezvous
worlds.question: Four ordered panels are shown left to right. Each panel draws the same horizontal track divided into six slots by thin divider lines. A red token and a green token each occupy exactly one slot in every panel, and each token keeps its own fixed color as it moves between slots. In the first (leftmost) panel the two tokens are in different slots. Read the panels left to right and report the earliest panel (P2, P3, or P4) at which the red token and the green token occupy the same slot. Answer 'panel 2', 'panel 3', or 'panel 4'.

worlds.title: First state reentry
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 from left to right. Each labeled tile has one of three visible states. After a tile changes away from its P1 state, which tile is the first to return to its own P1 state? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Shelf insert shift
worlds.question: At the top of the picture is a shelf of six square slots in a row, numbered by their drawn left-to-right position. A slot either holds one coloured disc or is empty. A thick black rectangle is drawn around exactly one slot: that is the queried slot, and the ring marks a place on the shelf, never a particular disc. Below the shelf is a row of cream cards, applied one at a time in drawn left-to-right order, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries a small strip of six white boxes standing for the six shelf slots in the same left-to-right order, and a black triangle drawn just under that strip; the card acts on the slot whose white box is nearest to the triangle. Above the strip each card carries either a coloured disc or a plain grey square. A card with a coloured disc is an insert: the disc in the named slot and every disc to its right each move one slot to the right, whatever was in the sixth slot falls off the end of the shelf and is gone, and a new disc of the card's colour is placed in the named slot. A card with a grey square is a remove: whatever the named slot holds is taken away, everything to its right moves one slot to the left, and the sixth slot ends empty. Empty slots shift in exactly the same way as discs do, and a card's named slot always refers to the shelf as it stands when that card acts, not to the shelf as first drawn. The shelf is drawn only in its starting state: no later shelf, and not the final shelf, is drawn anywhere in the picture. The queried slot is guaranteed to hold a disc once every card has acted, and its colour is one of red, orange, blue or green. After every card has acted in order, what colour is the disc in the ringed slot? Answer with one word: red, orange, blue or green.

worlds.title: Gated corridor replay
worlds.question: The pawn starts in the colored-ringed room. Rooms are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right by black-dot count. Each gate is OPEN when its two colored bars lie along the corridor and CLOSED when they cross it. Read the six cards from left to right. A colored-background card flips the gate named by its black-dot count. A white arrow card tries to move the pawn one room in its direction; it moves only when the gate between the rooms is OPEN, and otherwise stays. The pawn also stays if an arrow points beyond the corridor. Which room contains the pawn at the end? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Vacancy slide replay
worlds.question: The six board cells are A-F in row-major order (A-C on top, D-F below). Five pip-labeled tiles and one empty cell start as shown; the red outline marks the tile to track. Read the eight cards from left to right. On each card, the named tile slides into the empty cell only if it shares a side with the empty cell; otherwise nothing moves. Which cell contains the marked tile after all cards? Answer A, B, C, D, E, or F.

worlds.title: Nesting depth match
worlds.question: The image shows several closed black loops and three colored dots. A dot is said to lie at nesting depth N when exactly N of the closed black loops go around it (N is the number of loops that enclose the dot). The green dot is the reference. Count, for the green, red, and blue dots, how many black loops enclose each. The green dot is the reference. Which of the red or blue dots has the same loop-count as green? Answer with exactly red or blue.

worlds.title: Euler trail selection
worlds.question: Each colored network has five colored nodes and six gray links. Which network can be traced in one continuous stroke using every link exactly once, without lifting or retracing: red, blue, or green? A link is one gray segment between two nodes; the network must be connected; ignore the canvas.

worlds.title: One stroke trace
worlds.question: Three separate networks are drawn on white paper, one in each third of the picture: left, centre and right, kept apart by two pale vertical rules. In every network the grey wires meet only at the round dark hubs, and each wire joins exactly two hubs. A network can be DRAWN IN ONE STROKE when a pen can start at some hub of that network, travel only along its wires, draw every one of its wires exactly once and never lift off the paper; the pen may pass through a hub as often as it likes, may never run along the same wire twice, and may never jump from one hub to another without a wire. Exactly one of the three networks can be drawn in one stroke. Which network is it - left, centre or right?

worlds.title: Three way cut station
worlds.question: Gray links join round stations. Imagine removing one colored station and every link touching it. Which removal splits the network into exactly three separate parts? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Common loop junctions
worlds.question: Is there a simple loop of dark links that passes through both the green and purple junctions? A simple loop follows links and visits no junction more than once, except for returning to its start. Links connect only at visible circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Dot on colored route
worlds.question: A single winding route is drawn in orange. Two colored dots, one red and one blue, are shown nearby. Exactly one of the two colored dots lies ON the orange route (its color ink sits on top of the route stroke). Which colored dot -- red or blue -- lies on the route? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Trace island winding
worlds.question: Starting at the green port, follow the dark path around the gray island to the red terminal. Does it wind clockwise or counterclockwise around the island? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Wire halfway dot
worlds.question: The grey stroke in this picture is one single wire. It never branches and never crosses or touches itself, so it has exactly two loose ends and you can follow it from one end to the other. One red dot, one green dot and one blue dot sit on this wire. The halfway point of the wire is the point on the wire that has the same length of wire to one loose end as to the other. Measure every distance only as length along the wire, following each of its turns; straight-line distance across the picture does not count, and neither does the middle of the page. Which dot is nearest to the halfway point of the wire, measured along the wire? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: Barred edge terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green ring, follow the dark-line network. If the segment marked by two red bars is closed, which colored square becomes unreachable? Gray dots are junctions; lines meet only at those dots.

worlds.title: Between gates checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green START ring, follow the single black route to the purple FINISH ring. Which colored checkpoint is encountered after the yellow diamond gate but before the cyan diamond gate? The route never branches or crosses itself. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Focal twin arrow match
worlds.question: Near the middle of the image sits a small cluster made of exactly two separate solid triangle glyphs, with empty white space between them. Each triangle points toward one of the four cardinal directions (right, down, left, up). Do the two disconnected triangles point in the SAME direction? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cyclic bead order correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate has the same complete clockwise bead-color order as R after its left-right reflection?

worlds.title: Rulepair turn transfer
worlds.question: The cream board carries seven square tiles that never touch each other, plus small pale decorative squares lying on the bare board that mean nothing. Every tile is a 5 by 5 grid of cells inside a thick coloured frame, and every cell is either FILLED, showing a small dark square, or EMPTY, showing plain white. Exactly one tile has a navy frame and exactly one tile has a brown frame: together they are the RULE PAIR and they sit at opposite corners of the board, far apart. The brown tile shows the very same pattern as the navy tile after one single hidden CHANGE has been applied to the whole 5 by 5 grid. The hidden change is one of exactly four possibilities: a quarter turn clockwise, a half turn, a mirror flip left for right, or a mirror flip top for bottom. Exactly one of those four changes turns the navy pattern into the brown pattern, so comparing the two distant tiles cell by cell tells you which change is in force. Exactly one tile has a dark graphite frame: it is the QUERY, it sits at a further corner, and its pattern is unrelated to the rule pair. The remaining four tiles are the CANDIDATES; each wears a frame in a different colour taken from red, orange, green, teal, blue and purple. The four candidates are exactly the four results of applying the four possible changes to the query pattern, one candidate per change, so exactly one candidate shows the query pattern after the change that the rule pair fixes. Because all four candidates are turns or flips of the same query pattern, every candidate has exactly the same number of filled cells and the same amount of dark ink, and the frame colour, the tile size and the tile position tell you nothing about which one is right. The rule pair on its own cannot pick a candidate and the query on its own cannot pick a candidate: you must read the change off the two distant rule-pair tiles and then apply that same change to the distant query pattern. Which candidate shows the query pattern after the same change the rule pair shows? Give the colour of that candidate's frame. Answer red, orange, green, teal, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Singleton neighbor tapestry
worlds.question: The four rows are stitched into one navy tapestry. In the gold-tagged source row, cyan squares are ON and cream squares are OFF. For each of the seven positions, the transformed square is ON exactly when exactly one of the left, current, and right source squares is ON; the two ends wrap around and are neighbors. Which colored-tag row is exactly the transformed row? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Stepvector correspondence
worlds.question: The left grid is BEFORE and the right grid is AFTER. Match the circle, square, and triangle across the two grids. Exactly one shape moved one cell to the right and stayed in the same row. What color tab marks that shape in the AFTER grid? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Heatmap reversal binding
worlds.question: Which colored row is hottest in panel P but coldest in panel Q? Each panel has one heat square for each row; darker squares are hotter. Answer amber, teal, or violet.

worlds.title: Treemap quarter share
worlds.question: Which coloured block covers an area closest to exactly one quarter of the panel's total coloured area? The framed panel is tiled by exactly four solid coloured blocks separated by thin pale gutters: one red, one blue, one green and one orange. The small colour swatches printed above the panel, the grey rings and the grey ticks are decoration and are never measured. Take the panel's total coloured area to be the sum of the areas of those four blocks. Answer with one colour: red, blue, green or orange.

worlds.title: Chain median orientation
worlds.question: The dark-blue chain has five straight legs. Rank the legs by visible centerline length, shortest to longest. Is the middle (third) leg horizontal or vertical? Answer horizontal or vertical.

worlds.title: Checkpoint route distance
worlds.question: A gold ring marks a checkpoint on the teal route. Following the route itself, not a straight line, which endpoint is closer to the checkpoint? Answer LEFT or RIGHT.

worlds.title: Jigsaw edge complement
worlds.question: Do the two visible jigsaw pieces fit? Compare their facing vertical edges as six equal-height bands; answer yes only when every pair of facing bands has complementary inward/outward offsets, and no otherwise. Ignore color and the gap between pieces. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Signal lamp crate match
worlds.question: This picture shows a signal depot on a plain white background. Exactly two things are drawn, and they sit far apart at opposite corners. One is a single signal plate: a grey rectangle with a dark grey frame, holding one vertical stack of dark round lamps. The other is a block of exactly four crates, each drawn as one filled coloured rectangle: one red, one amber, one green and one blue, in any arrangement. Each crate holds a row of dark upright bars. The signal plate may hold any number of lamps from 2 to 5, and the four crates hold 2, 3, 4 and 5 bars in some order, so exactly one crate holds as many bars as the plate holds lamps. Call that crate the twin crate. The bars are wider when a crate holds fewer of them, so no crate is bigger or inkier than another. What colour is the twin crate? Answer with exactly one of: red, amber, green, blue.

worlds.title: Bowling ball hole count
worlds.question: How many separate dark circular finger holes are visible inside the colored bowling ball? Count only circles fully inside the ball.

worlds.title: Heartbeat guide excursions
worlds.question: How many upward excursions of the single dark heartbeat trace visibly rise above the red horizontal guide? Count each connected above-guide excursion once; ignore all downward excursions. Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Path stencil trace
worlds.question: Inside the small pale inset is one connected navy trace with a red start cap and eight station dots. Follow the trace from the red cap in its connected order. At each station, lift its attached short tick and project the tick into the next column of one common vertical stencil, preserving whether it lies on the clockwise or counterclockwise side of the directed trace. Read the eight projected columns as the declared code: A) WAVE = ++--++--; B) FORK = +--++---. Which symbol appears? Ignore the pale frame and every mark outside the inset. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Shadow offset reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one square plate in this picture is drawn with a black border; every other plate is drawn with a pale lavender border. The black-bordered plate is divided into an 11 by 11 grid of 121 equal square cells, and every cell is filled with one of just two tones, a darker tone and a lighter tone. The three-square key near the bottom left shows those two tones with their exact midpoint tone between them. Nearby, separated from the plate by plain background, are exactly two small black marks: one hollow black ring and one solid black square. They are the gauge. The distance between the centres of the two black marks is a whole number of plate cell widths, either horizontally, or vertically, or the same whole number of cell widths in both directions at once; that whole number is the slide length in cells, and the slide runs in the direction that leads from the hollow ring to the solid square. Carry out this operation. Take a copy of the black-bordered plate's own pattern of darker cells. Slide the whole copy across the plate by the gauge's slide, that many cells in that direction. Lay the slid copy back over the plate and mark every cell of the plate that is darker in the plate and is also covered by a darker cell of the slid copy; any part of the copy pushed off the edge of the plate is discarded. The marked cells form exactly one symbol inside the middle 5 by 5 block of the plate: 'plus' is that block's full centre row together with its full centre column, 'ex' is that block's two full diagonals, 'tee' is that block's full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is that block's full left column together with its full bottom row. The plate on its own shows no symbol, the two black marks carry no pattern of their own, and the lavender plates, the lavender marks and the key are decoration. Which symbol do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, ex, tee, ell.

worlds.title: Odd stamp convolution
worlds.question: Use the coral 2 by 2 stamp at every dark square of the teal 5 by 5 placement board, without rotating it. Align the stamp's top-left square with each placement square. A result square is dark exactly when it is covered an odd number of times. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Odd sum constellation
worlds.question: Rotate each framed card until its magenta corner is upper left. On each 5 by 5 wraparound grid, the center is zero. Add every marked offset on one card to every marked offset on the other, wrapping across opposite edges. Keep a result cell dark only when it is reached an odd number of times. Which pattern needs the fewest cell changes: plus, x, or box-dot? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Remote notch duet
worlds.question: Each separated medallion has one triangular notch. Imagine a ray from each medallion's center to its notch. Are the two notch rays more than a right angle apart? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Trail facing bead
worlds.question: The picture contains exactly one thin dark outline. That outline is a single closed loop: it never branches and never crosses itself, so it can be walked like a circular track. Exactly four small filled circles (red, green, blue, amber) sit on the loop; the loop passes through each of them. Walking around the loop visits the four circles in a cyclic order. Straight-line nearness in the picture is not relevant: two circles can look close yet be far apart along the loop. Starting at the red circle and walking along the loop, the second circle you meet is the same one in both directions. Which colour is that second circle? Answer with one of: green, blue, amber.

worlds.title: Alternating fork terminal
worlds.question: Start at the red dot. At the first fork take the upper outgoing branch, at the next fork take the lower, then upper, then lower. What shape is at that endpoint? Answer circle or square.

worlds.title: Invisible aperture aspect
worlds.question: The inward tips of the four detached pointers mark the four corners of an invisible rectangle. Is that rectangle wider or taller? Answer wider or taller.

worlds.title: Paired signature match
worlds.question: The top panel is the reference signature: a pair of colored dots in a left slot and a right slot. Which candidate panel below reproduces the reference on BOTH slots in the same left/right order? Answer top_left, top_right, bottom_left, or bottom_right.

worlds.title: Diagonal balance plate search
worlds.question: Each quadrant contains one connected square-cell plate. Ignore cells lying on either plate diagonal. Which quadrant has equal filled-cell area on both sides of the first diagonal and equal filled-cell area on both sides of the second diagonal? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Twin comb ledger search
worlds.question: The picture shows eight combs on a plain background. A comb is a group of three solid vertical teeth of equal width standing side by side on one common baseline, so within a comb only the heights of the teeth differ. Four combs are pressed against the left edge of the page in one column and form the left ledger; the other four are pressed against the right edge in one column and form the right ledger. The wide middle of the page is empty, and nothing joins the two ledgers. Counting downwards from the top of the left ledger its combs are the first, second, third and fourth. The signature of a comb is its three tooth heights read from left to right, where the height of a tooth is how far it rises above its comb's baseline. Exactly one comb in the left ledger has the same signature as one comb in the right ledger: all three of its teeth match that far comb's three teeth in the same left-to-right order. Every other pairing of a left comb with a right comb differs by a clearly visible amount in at least one of the three teeth, and the picture always contains decoy pairs that agree on two of their three teeth and disagree on the third, so a comb that only half matches is not the answer. Both ledgers must be read: the left ledger alone never reveals which of its combs is repeated, and the right ledger alone never names a row. Which row of the right ledger holds the repeat, the ink colour, how far each ledger sits from its edge, the small up and down shifts of the baselines, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which comb of the left ledger has its signature repeated by a comb of the right ledger? Answer with one of: first, second, third, fourth.

worlds.title: Ascending run route search
worlds.question: Start at each cyan dot and follow its black route to the colored dot. Which colored route has every straight run strictly longer than the run before it? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Dual field bullseye search
worlds.question: Each color has one detached straight bar on the left and one on the right. Imagine extending each bar's centerline in both directions. Which color has both centerlines pass through the gold disk? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State bilateral change
worlds.question: A tracked signal is recorded at two ordered time steps shown side by side: the LEFT marker is the INITIAL state (time step 1) and the RIGHT marker is the FINAL state (time step 2). A blue marker means state OFF and an orange marker means state ON. Did the signal's state CHANGE between the initial and final records? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: State temporal majority
worlds.question: Read the five numbered snapshots in temporal order. Each snapshot has four labeled rows A, B, C, and D. The ring in snapshot 1 marks one tracked row; follow that same row through all five snapshots. Which state shape does the tracked row show in more snapshots: circle or diamond?

worlds.title: Pairwipe bead pan
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one row of equal solid coloured squares, evenly spaced and standing side by side, and exactly one further solid coloured square of the same size standing on its own well above that row. Every pale grey mark anywhere in the picture is inert decoration that means nothing. Each coloured square is a bead, and every bead is red, green, blue or yellow. The lone bead above the row is the one bead that is already lying in the pan. The pan itself is not drawn, and the beads that collect in it are never drawn, so you must keep track of the pile in your head. The beads of the row are the queue, and they are tipped into the pan one at a time in order, starting with the leftmost bead of the row and finishing with the rightmost. Tipping one bead in works like this: if the bead now showing on top of the pan is the same colour as the arriving bead, the two wipe each other out and both are removed from the pan, uncovering whatever lay beneath; otherwise the arriving bead simply comes to rest on top of the pan and covers what was there. The pan never becomes empty at any point, and no bead ever enters the pan except by being tipped in from the row, in that left-to-right order. After the whole row has been tipped in, which colour is showing on top of the pan? Answer with one of red, green, blue or yellow.

worlds.title: Alternating triplet patch
worlds.question: Start with the two MEMORY beads from top to bottom, then read the four NEW beads in row order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. The lamp starts OFF. After each NEW bead, flip the lamp exactly when the newest three beads alternate colors (cyan-coral-cyan or coral-cyan-coral). Is the lamp ON after all four NEW beads?

worlds.title: Paired vector homecoming
worlds.question: A token starts at the gray HOME ring. Apply the left colored arrow, then the right colored arrow, moving one grid step per arrow. Ignore the pale corner symbols. Does the token finish somewhere other than HOME? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Loop enclosure
worlds.question: Is the black ring a fully closed loop that encloses exactly one white region? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cycle link selection
worlds.question: Which colored link lies on a loop? A link lies on a loop when another visible route still connects its two endpoints after that link is removed. Choose red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Clasp cut pocket survival
worlds.question: This page carries one black line figure and several coloured decorations. Only the black figure and the red stretch drawn inside it matter; blue, green, grey, purple and orange marks are decoration and never count. The black figure is a single thread: every black stroke in it is joined to the rest, and one short stretch of that thread is painted red instead of black, so the red stretch is a piece of the thread and not a separate object. Exactly one white pocket is fully enclosed by the thread as drawn. Now imagine cutting the red stretch out of the thread and leaving nothing behind in its place, while every black stroke stays exactly where it is. A white pocket counts as enclosed only when you cannot leave it and reach the outside of the page without crossing a black stroke. After that cut, is at least one white pocket still fully enclosed by the black strokes? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Island lake nesting
worlds.question: The black wall surrounds the yellow island. Using edge-sharing (corner touching does not connect regions), is the white water immediately around the yellow island cut off from the outer white background? Answer yes if it is enclosed, or no if a visible channel connects it outside.

worlds.title: Single pocket seal
worlds.question: Ignore the pale gray decorations. Does the connected teal seal contain exactly one enclosed white pocket? A pocket is a white area fully surrounded by teal; white areas connect only through shared edges, not diagonal corners. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Dual loop terminal
worlds.question: Two disconnected green-to-terminal route networks are shown. Follow each dark route and choose the terminal—amber or violet—whose route contains a closed loop. Use the route topology, not the terminal's position or color alone. Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Moat loop enclave
worlds.question: The picture shows one dark wall of constant thickness on a plain white background. The wall is a single closed loop: it never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself, and it never reaches the edge of the picture. Because it is one closed loop it cuts the white background into exactly two parts, an enclosed part sealed off by the wall and an outside part that reaches the edge of the picture. The loop is long and winding, so the enclosed part is a narrow lane rather than a plain blob, and narrow white lanes also occur outside the loop. There are exactly two dots, one orange and one purple, both the same size and both clear of the wall. Exactly one of the two dots is in the enclosed part; the other is in the outside part. A dot is in the outside part when you can travel from it over white background to the edge of the picture without ever crossing the wall. Which dot is the one sealed inside the loop? Answer orange or purple.

worlds.title: Paired checkpoint order
worlds.question: Trace each separate navy route from its green START to its red FINISH. Do the blue and orange checkpoints appear in the same order on both routes, or in reversed order? Answer same or reversed.

worlds.title: Red corridor bypass
worlds.question: If the red corridor segment is blocked, can the green port still reach the gold port through the remaining dark corridors? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Rank slot binding
worlds.question: The KEY row shows six coloured tokens; the number of filled cells in the ruler beneath each token gives that colour's rank from 1 to 6. Below, candidate panels A and B each place the same six colours into six labelled boxes. A panel is matched when every coloured token sits inside the box printed with its rank. In which panel, A or B, does every colour sit in the box labelled with its rank? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Additive span balance
worlds.question: In which panel is the gold span exactly as long as the red span plus the blue span? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Midturn stance recovery
worlds.question: One single turn about one point carries the green shape exactly onto the orange shape. Exactly one of the four blue shapes stands halfway along that motion: one and the same turn carries the green shape onto it, and that very same turn carries it onto the orange shape. All four blue shapes are the same shape in the same orientation, so only their positions differ. The four blue shapes are numbered 1 to 4 from the left. Which one is it? Answer with exactly one of: blue-1, blue-2, blue-3, blue-4.

worlds.title: Converted bottleneck capacity
worlds.question: Each machine can handle at most its shown units. An arrow p:q converts p input units into q output units. Convert every machine limit to FINISH units; a line is limited by the smallest result. Which line can deliver most: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Counterfactual unmasking switch
worlds.question: The triangle is the factual run; dark means ON. Each lower cell applies its row rule to the touching pair above. The red-ringed TOP flip alone leaves the bottom unchanged. Test one numbered switch at a time in two fresh trials. In both trials, force that cell to the opposite of its shown value and rebuild below it. Trial A keeps TOP as shown; Trial B also flips the red-ringed TOP cell. Which switch makes A and B end with different bottom rows? Answer switch-1, switch-2, switch-3, or switch-4.

worlds.title: Halo correspondence
worlds.question: A solid disk is shown at the top (the reference). Below, a row of objects, each a colored disk with a colored halo ring. Find the object whose disk color matches the reference disk, then report the color of that object's halo.

worlds.title: Nested shell order correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate ring, A or B, has the same outside-to-inside color nesting order as the REFERENCE ring? A match requires the full sequence of four colored shells; candidate rings may be translated or uniformly scaled. Ignore panel position, ring thickness, and the arbitrary starting angle. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Skyline motif window binding
worlds.question: The image has two panels separated by a horizontal black rule. The upper panel shows a TEMPLATE of 3 gray bars. The lower panel shows a TRACK of 9 gray bars. All bars have the same width and spacing and are drawn at the same vertical scale, each panel's bars standing on that panel's baseline. Directly above every track bar there is one colored flag (a small square). Exactly one run of 3 consecutive track bars has heights equal, bar for bar in left-to-right order, to the 3 template bars. Report the color of the flag above the track bar immediately to the RIGHT of that matching run (the 4th bar counting from the start of the run). Answer with exactly one of: crimson, amber, teal, violet.

worlds.title: Rigid landmark plate
worlds.question: The REFERENCE and each option show four colored bolts on a rigid plate. A plate may be moved and rotated, but not reflected, resized, or bent. Colors must correspond. Which option is exactly the same plate? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Transpose xor correspondence
worlds.question: Transpose the RIGHT 4x4 grid across its main diagonal. XOR it with the LEFT grid: a result cell is filled exactly when one, but not both, corresponding cells is filled. Which result card is correct: A, B, or C?

worlds.title: Errorbar center offset argmax
worlds.question: Three colored error bars are shown: one red, one blue, one green. Each error bar has three short horizontal ticks at three distinct heights: a low tick and a high tick (the two outermost ticks) and one middle tick between them. The middle tick of a bar may sit off the vertical midpoint between that bar's own low and high ticks. Which colored bar's middle tick is FARTHEST from the vertical midpoint between its low and high ticks (the most asymmetric error bar)? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green. (selection by largest center offset).

worlds.title: Adjacent heat contrast
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Each panel is a heatmap with four labeled rows and six equal-width columns, using one shared blue-to-yellow scale. For each panel, horizontal contrast is the mean absolute heat difference between neighboring columns, averaged over all rows. Which panel has the greater horizontal contrast? Choose A or B; ties and near ties are quarantined.

worlds.title: Pair sum reference
worlds.question: The chart shows five colored bars standing on one common baseline: red, orange, green, blue and purple, in some left-to-right order. The horizontal gray gridlines are exactly one unit apart, so a bar's value is its height measured in gridline units above the baseline. Bar widths, bar positions and the left-to-right order carry no information. The dashed black rule marks a target level, measured in those same gridline units above the baseline. Exactly one pair of bars has values that add up exactly to the target level, and every other pair of bars misses it. Which two colors are that pair? Answer with the two color names joined by " and ", in alphabetical order, for example "blue and red".

worlds.title: Boxplot whisker ratio
worlds.question: Which colored box plot has the longest upper whisker relative to its box height?

worlds.title: Paired interval iou
worlds.question: Rows A-D run from top to bottom. Each row contains one blue and one orange horizontal interval on the same scale. For each row, divide their overlap length by their union length (the length covered by at least one interval). Which row has the largest fraction? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior rainbow bands
worlds.question: A rainbow classically shows seven color bands (red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet), but report exactly what is drawn here. This is a rainbow painted across the sky. How many color bands are drawn on it? Count only the visible bands and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Traffic lamp count
worlds.question: How many circular lamp lenses are inside the traffic-signal housing? Count each visible lens once; ignore the housing, bracket, and SIGNAL label. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Bicycle wheel size
worlds.question: This image shows one side view of a two-wheeled machine standing on a drawn ground line. The two wheels are the black rings with black spokes and a black hub; the frame, saddle and handlebar are coloured, the ground line is coloured, and the grey page border, the four grey corner ticks and the loose coloured spots near the top are fixed decoration that never indicates the answer. THE LEFT WHEEL is the wheel whose centre is further to the left of the page and THE RIGHT WHEEL is the other one, whichever end the handlebar happens to be drawn on; the machine faces left in some images and right in others, and that has nothing to do with the answer. A wheel's SIZE is the diameter of its black ring, measured across the ring from outer edge to outer edge. Compare the two diameters using this rule: if they differ by LESS than a tenth of the larger diameter, the wheels count as the same size; otherwise the wheel with the larger diameter is the larger one. No image in this set is a borderline case: the difference is always either well inside or well outside that tenth. The two wheels may be equal or one may be larger, the wheels change scale from image to image, and so do the frame colour, the spoke count, the number of spots and the facing direction. Judge the wheels drawn in this image, and do not answer from how the wheels of a bicycle usually compare. Which wheel is larger? Answer exactly one of: left, right, same.

worlds.title: Positive terminal wire color
worlds.question: Which colored wire is connected to the terminal marked with a plus sign? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Rainbow between band conflict
worlds.question: Along the visible five-band rainbow, compare bands from the outside toward the inside. Which color band lies directly between the blue and yellow bands? Answer red, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Checker phase reveal
worlds.question: The image is a field of grey noise. Deinterlace the checkerboard by keeping only the even-parity cells (cells whose row plus column index is even) and averaging within each kept cell. Which glyph, the rising band A or the falling band B, does the deinterlaced checkerboard reveal? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Chromatic register reveal
worlds.question: Align the three marked color separations by their four corner marks, average the aligned squares, and name the broad symbol.

worlds.title: Interleaved sheet extract
worlds.question: The picture shows one framed lattice of 14 rows and 7 columns of square cells; each cell is either dark (filled) or blank. Beside every lattice row, just outside the frame on its left, exactly one marker is printed: either a filled dot or a hollow ring. Exactly 7 rows carry a filled dot and exactly 7 rows carry a hollow ring. Discard every row whose marker is a hollow ring, keep the rows whose marker is a filled dot in their original top-to-bottom order, and push those 7 kept rows together into a single block of 7 rows and 7 columns. The dark cells of that block form one of these five symbols: ring (a closed square outline with a hollow centre), wedge (a solid triangle pointing down, widest across its top row), zigzag (a bar along the top, a staircase running down to the left, and a bar along the bottom), arrow (a broad arrowhead pointing down with a short stem below it), slash (a thick diagonal band running from the top left corner to the bottom right corner). Which of the five symbols do the dark cells of that block form? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Row prefix parity
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 12 by 12 grid, first invert the top-left cell and every other cell in both directions, making a checkerboard pattern of inverted cells. Then form a new grid: in each row, make a cell black exactly when the number of black cells from the left edge through that cell is odd; otherwise make it white. Which symbol appears: diamond, hourglass, left fan, or right fan?

worlds.title: Paired mosaic change symbol
worlds.question: On the two 12-by-12 mosaic cards, align matching gold, orange, and purple corner dots. Keep a cell exactly when its two colors differ. Which shape does the change map form: plus, X, diamond, or dashed square?

worlds.title: Concentric ring count
worlds.question: A field of dark dots is arranged on nested circles that all share one common center. Every dot on a single circle forms one ring, and a much bigger radial gap separates each circle from the next than the gap between neighbouring dots along any one circle. How many rings of dots are there? Choose: 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Convex position constellation
worlds.question: For each color, take the centers of its visible dots and imagine their convex hull. Which color has no dot strictly inside the convex hull of its other dots? Ignore color, lane, dot size, count, and placement; choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Pattern period tick
worlds.question: The picture shows a wide horizontal band of small dark grey rectangles on a plain pale background, and below the band five upright bars of equal size and shape: one black bar on the left and four coloured bars, one red, one green, one blue and one orange. Inside the band one arrangement of rectangles is repeated over and over from left to right, always shifted by the same fixed horizontal distance, so the whole band maps exactly onto itself when it is slid sideways by that distance; that repeat distance is drawn nowhere as a line, a gap or a mark, and no rectangle, no edge and no local patch of the band is marked out. Exactly one of the four coloured bars stands to the right of the black bar by exactly that repeat distance. Each of the other three coloured bars stands at a distance that differs from every whole number of repeats by at least 18 pixels, so no other bar is one repeat, two repeats or any whole number of repeats away. The colours of the bars, their left-to-right order, which bar is nearest or farthest, the number of rectangles, the size of the rectangles, the amount of ink and the position of the band carry no information about the answer. Which coloured bar stands exactly one repeat distance to the right of the black bar? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Rotational constellation order
worlds.question: Considering the complete set of black dots, which rotation about their shared center maps the constellation onto itself: 180 degrees or 120 degrees? Answer 180 or 120.

worlds.title: Rotational symmetry order
worlds.question: The hollow gray ring marks the center. Ignore the ring and judge all 60 dark dots together. What is the smallest positive turn that makes the whole dark-dot pattern coincide with itself: 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, or 1/6 of a full turn? Answer 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, or 1/6.

worlds.title: Reference height order search
worlds.question: A reference group of three black bars is shown in the top box. The bars sit on a shared baseline and each has a different height, so they form a left-to-right arrangement ordered by height. The image below is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right); each quadrant contains its own group of three black bars on a shared baseline. Exactly one quadrant's three bars are arranged in the SAME left-to-right height order as the reference group (the same pattern of shortest, middle, and tallest reading left to right). The other three quadrants each have a different arrangement. Which quadrant contains the group whose three-bar height order matches the reference group? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Interior marker panel search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only group with one marker strictly inside the triangle made by the other three markers? Inspect all four equal panels, ignore labels and position, and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Complement tile grid
worlds.question: This image shows six four-by-four grids, each drawn as an outlined box with thin internal grid lines. The single grid in the upper row is the reference grid. The five grids in the lower row are the candidates, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. In every one of the six grids exactly eight of the sixteen cells are filled solid, so all six grids carry the same number of filled cells and the same amount of ink. The reference grid is drawn slightly larger than the candidates, so only the pattern of filled cells matters, never a grid's size or its position on the canvas. Every grid is drawn upright in the same orientation, and no candidate is rotated or flipped. Exactly one candidate is the exact complement of the reference: comparing the two grids cell by cell at matching row and column positions, that candidate fills every cell the reference leaves empty and leaves empty every cell the reference fills, so laying it over the reference would cover the whole four-by-four square with no gap and no doubly covered cell. One of the other four candidates is an exact copy of the reference pattern, and each of the remaining three disagrees with the exact complement in at least two cells. Which numbered candidate is the exact complement of the reference grid? Answer with exactly one of: grid-1, grid-2, grid-3, grid-4, grid-5.

worlds.title: Directed cycle search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has arrows forming one directed loop that visits all four colored circles exactly once before returning to the start? Follow the orange arrowheads; A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Repeated block search
worlds.question: Each row contains two blocks of four colored tiles. Which labeled row has the second block in exactly the same left-to-right color order as the first block? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State peak distance
worlds.question: Five panels sit side by side and are read left to right. The leftmost panel is the START panel: it shows a horizontal rail divided into five slots, slot 0 at the left up to slot 4 at the right, with a single magenta marker on one slot. An orange ring around the marker marks the START slot index of a register. The four panels to the right are OPERATOR panels, read left to right; each holds one coloured triangle. A green right-pointing triangle advances the register's value by one (+1) and a red left-pointing triangle retreats it by one (-1). Apply the four operators in order from the ringed start; the register's value after each step is start plus the running sum of the steps. What is the MAXIMUM distance from the start value the register ever reaches across the whole replay (counting the start as distance 0)? Answer with the integer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Finite state replay
worlds.question: Start at the ringed state in the START row. The table gives the destination state for each current state (rows A, B, C) and input symbol (alpha or beta). Apply the numbered input sequence from left to right. Which state is reached after the last input? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Slide blank replay
worlds.question: On the left is a board of 3 by 3 square cells. Number the cells 1 to 9 in reading order: 1, 2, 3 across the top row, 4, 5, 6 across the middle row, and 7, 8, 9 across the bottom row. Eight of the cells hold a coloured tile and the colours are blue, brown, green, orange, pink, purple, teal and yellow, each used exactly once. The ninth cell is plain light grey: that is the gap, and it holds no tile. One cell is marked by a red ring: the marked cell is the cell whose centre is nearest to the centre of that red ring, and the ring is only a marker, so it neither is a tile nor changes the colour of the cell it is drawn on. On the right is a row of cream cards, each carrying one solid black triangle that points up, down, left or right. The cards are applied to the board one at a time, in order from left to right, as the grey arrow below the row shows. A card's triangle points the way the gap moves: the gap and the neighbouring cell in that direction exchange contents, so the tile in that neighbouring cell slides into the gap and the cell it came from becomes the new gap. Up means towards the top of the board, down towards the bottom, left towards the left edge and right towards the right edge. Every card drawn is a legal move: the gap always has a neighbouring cell in the direction its card points. Nothing else moves, tiles never change colour, and the cells keep their numbers throughout. The board after the cards have been applied is not drawn anywhere. After every card has been applied in order, what does the marked cell hold? Answer with one word: the colour of the tile that is in it, or empty if the gap is in it.

worlds.title: Conditional transfer replay
worlds.question: The parcel starts at the symbol in the START box. Read the route cards from left to right. On each card, move the parcel from the left symbol to the right symbol only if it is currently at the left symbol; otherwise it stays where it is. At which symbol does it finish?

worlds.title: Rotor switch walk
worlds.question: Four pip-labeled stations form the clockwise cycle A→B→C→D→A (A has 1 pip, B 2, C 3, D 4). The red ring marks the starting station. Repeat once for each orange STEP card: first read the station you are on; if its symbol is filled, move one station clockwise, and if its symbol is a ring, move one station counterclockwise; then flip the filled/ring state of the station you just left. Which station do you occupy after all STEP cards? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Piece count
worlds.question: Ignore the white background and look only at the dark linework. Pieces that touch (an endpoint on a segment, or a crossing) are part of one connected cluster; pieces separated by white are different clusters. How many distinct connected clusters of linework are drawn in total? Answer with exactly 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Region adjacency hub
worlds.question: Which colored region shares a straight boundary segment with both of the other two? Choose red, green, or blue; ignore the frame.

worlds.title: Chain interlock pick
worlds.question: The picture shows four rings drawn as flat bands on white paper: one black, one red, one green and one blue. Wherever two bands cross, one of them runs through the crossing unbroken and the other is interrupted by a white gap; the unbroken band is the one passing in FRONT there and the interrupted band passes BEHIND. Every coloured ring crosses the black ring at exactly two places. Call a coloured ring INTERLOCKED with the black ring when the ring in front is different at those two places, that is, the coloured ring is in front at one crossing and behind at the other; if the same ring is in front at both crossings the two rings are NOT interlocked. Crossings between two coloured rings do not matter for this question. Exactly one coloured ring is interlocked with the black ring. Which coloured ring is interlocked with the black ring? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: Cycle hitting station
worlds.question: A loop is a closed route following links that repeats no station except its start/end. Imagine removing one colored station and every link touching it. Which removal leaves no loop anywhere? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Single stroke network
worlds.question: Can every dark link be traced exactly once in one continuous stroke, starting and ending at any junction? Junctions may be revisited, links may not, and links meet only at visible colored circles. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Last colored marker on route
worlds.question: A winding grey route runs from a small orange ring toward a dark terminal dot. Three coloured rings -- blue, green and red -- are centred on the route. Tracing the route from the orange ring toward the terminal, which colour ring is encountered LAST? Answer blue, green or red.

worlds.title: Colored route intermediate
worlds.question: Follow the dark connected network from the green node to the red node. Which colored node lies on that route: blue or gold? Answer blue or gold.

worlds.title: Chain free ring
worlds.question: This picture shows five coloured rings arranged in a closed chain; each ring overlaps its two neighbours, and every overlapping pair meets at exactly two crossings. At each crossing one of the two rings is drawn with a short break: the broken ring passes BEHIND, and the unbroken ring passes IN FRONT. Two rings are interlocked only when the order alternates between their two crossings, that is when each of them is in front at one crossing and behind at the other. If the same ring is in front at both of their crossings, that pair is not interlocked and the two rings could be pulled apart. Exactly one ring in the picture is not interlocked with either of its neighbours, so it could be lifted away from the chain. Which ring is that? Answer with its colour, one of: blue, brown, green, orange, purple, red.

worlds.title: Network route farthest
worlds.question: Starting at the green circle, which colored terminal has the greatest shortest-route distance along the dark lines? Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Every link terminal
worlds.question: Each box is a separate network. Starting at green START, which colored terminal can end a route that uses every black link exactly once? You may revisit circles, but must not reuse a link. Links meet only at circles and never cross. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Crosscanvas route terminal
worlds.question: One thin connected dark trace begins at the black source dot on the far left, winds continuously across nearly the whole image, and ends at exactly one of the three coloured dots on the far right. Which colour is the dot that this single trace connects to? Answer coral, teal, or violet.

worlds.title: Route turn handshake correspondence
worlds.question: One navy route is a single connected trace through fields R, A, and B. R is the reference; A and B are candidates. In each field, walk the route left to right and record the handedness of its five interior bends. Walk each candidate right to left before comparing; which candidate has the same complete turn-handshake as R?

worlds.title: Pivot tape mirror break
worlds.question: The picture shows one narrow tape lying somewhere on a decorated board. Only the marks on the tape decide the answer; every mark off the tape is decoration and means nothing. The tape carries a black diamond at its exact middle, and one of its two ends is drawn as a solid pointed arrow tip while the other end is square. On each side of the diamond there is the same number of small coloured square marks, evenly spaced along the tape. Counting outwards from the diamond, the mark at step 1 on one side is paired with the mark at step 1 on the other side, step 2 with step 2, and so on to the last step. Every pair is made of two marks of the same colour, except for exactly one pair whose two marks have different colours. Colours repeat across pairs, and on every tape the two colours of the odd pair each occur three times in total, so counting how often a colour occurs cannot tell you which side of the diamond the answer is on. Find the one pair whose two marks differ, and look at the mark of that pair lying on the side of the diamond that has the arrow tip. What colour is it? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Rank echo tags
worlds.question: The five navy dots at left are the reference. Dot sizes may all change. Which colored tag marks the row at right whose left-to-right size ranking exactly matches the reference? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Split seal correspondence
worlds.question: The two gray cards at the top are the LEFT and RIGHT reference sets. Black four-square glyphs count as the same when one can be quarter-turned to match the other; mirror images do not count. Each tagged card below has a left column and a right column, with order within a column irrelevant. Which color tags the only card whose left column contains exactly the LEFT set and whose right column contains exactly the RIGHT set? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Badge notch orientation
worlds.question: In the highlighted filled badge, is the notch cut into its upper edge or lower edge? Answer upper or lower.

worlds.title: Window area unit tally
worlds.question: The sheet carries exactly one solid slate-grey patch, and exactly one square window of sheet colour is cut out of the interior of that patch. Every other mark on the sheet, in any other colour, is decorative and must be ignored. Take the area of that square window as one unit of area, and take the slate ink still present after the window is cut as the measured area. How many whole units of area does the slate ink cover, that is, the largest whole number of window-areas that fits inside the slate ink area? Answer with a single integer.

worlds.title: Sampling window density
worlds.question: Which outlined sampling window has the greater blue-point density? Divide the number of blue points inside each window by that window's interior area. Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Local slope sign agreement
worlds.question: In the local inset, read each colored segment from left to right. A segment RISES when its right end is higher on the page and FALLS when its right end is lower. Do the CYAN and ORANGE segments have the same trend—both RISE or both FALL? Answer YES or NO.

worlds.title: Woven crossing parity
worlds.question: Do the two visible ribbon badges use the same over-under crossing? At each badge's central crossing, identify the uninterrupted diagonal; answer yes only when the two uninterrupted diagonals have the same slant, and no otherwise.

worlds.title: Mitten rack overlap
worlds.question: This picture shows a mitten-drying room on a plain white background. Two identical dark grey wooden racks, drawn as open rectangular frames, stand far apart: one near the left edge and one near the right edge. Each rack hangs between two and five mittens, all drawn as the same shape at the same size, so mittens differ only in their single flat colour; the thumb of a mitten may point either way, and that never matters. No rack ever hangs two mittens of the same colour. Some mittens may also lie loose on the floor in the empty space between the two racks; a loose mitten is not on a rack and must be ignored completely. Call a colour shared when at least one mitten of that colour hangs on the left rack and at least one mitten of that colour hangs on the right rack. The two racks need not hang the same number of mittens, and the two racks need not be at the same height. How many colours are shared between the two racks? Answer with exactly one of: 0, 1, 2, 3.

worlds.title: Week grid column count
worlds.question: How many columns are in the WEEK grid? Count each separate outlined vertical box once, including boxes on both sides of the wide center break.

worlds.title: Rainbow badge bands
worlds.question: How many colored bands are visible inside the dark-outlined rainbow disk? Count each uninterrupted band once; ignore the pale gray dots outside the disk. Answer 5, 6, 7, or 8.

worlds.title: Route turncode reveal
worlds.question: One red cap marks the start of one connected navy route and a green cap marks its end. Follow the route from red to green. It has 32 successive teeth, each with an apex between two baseline joins. Unroll the route in traversal order. For every tooth write # when its apex is above its two joins and . when it is below. Place the 32 marks row-major into a 4-row by 8-column bitmap and compare it with A) LOOP = 11110000/10011001/10011001/11110000 or B) LACE = 00001111/01100110/01100110/00001111. If the distances tie, choose A; tie cases are quarantined. Which symbol appears? Answer A or B. Ignore the caps and background.

worlds.title: Ribbon stack reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one ribbon in this picture is orange; every other ribbon is pale green-gray. The orange ribbon is a single unbranching chain of six equal square panels joined edge to edge by narrower necks, so it has exactly two ends and every other panel has exactly two neighbours along the ribbon. A solid black triangle outside one end panel points at the end where the ribbon starts. Each panel carries a 5 by 5 field of small dark square dots and empty cells, but that field is printed in the ribbon's own travel frame, not in the frame of the page: within a panel, a row runs in the direction the ribbon leaves that panel toward the next panel along the chain, from the panel's first column to its fifth, and the rows are numbered in the quarter-turn clockwise from that direction. The final panel uses the direction by which the ribbon arrived at it. Carry out this operation: read every panel's 5 by 5 field in that panel's own travel frame, lay all six fields on top of one another so that cell (row, column) meets cell (row, column), and keep exactly the cells that carry a dot in every one of the six panels. Exactly 9 of the 25 cells survive. The surviving cells form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the full centre row together with the full centre column, 'ex' is the two full diagonals, 'tee' is the full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. No single panel shows the symbol, the ribbon's path across the page is not the symbol, the pale ribbons are decoration, and stacking the panels in page orientation instead of each panel's own travel frame does not give the symbol. Which symbol do the surviving cells form? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tee.

worlds.title: Finite difference arrow
