worlds.question: Inside the purple frame, compare every square with the square immediately to its left (treat the first square in each row as unchanged). Mark a cell dark exactly when the pair differs. Which arrow appears: up, down, left, or right?

worlds.title: Ribbon route reassembly
worlds.question: Follow the connected ribbon from the red ring to the gold triangle. Read its 25 panels in travel order and place them left-to-right in five rows of five. Which dark-panel pattern needs the fewest panel changes: corner (a full edge row plus an end column), tee (a full edge row plus the center column), or chevron (two diagonal arms meeting at a tip)? Rotations and reflections keep the same name; answer ambiguous for a tie.

worlds.title: Constellation handedness
worlds.question: Ignoring position, scale, color, and rotation, do the two separated dot constellations have the same handedness? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cocircular arc pair
worlds.question: The page shows exactly four thin dark arcs: one near the top edge, one near the bottom edge, one near the left edge and one near the right edge. Every pale grey blob is background clutter and must be ignored. All four arcs are drawn in the same dark colour with the same thickness, the same length and the same curvature, so colour, thickness, length, curvature and the amount of ink say nothing about the answer. Because the four arcs share one curvature, each arc is a piece of a circle of one common size, and the only thing that tells those circles apart is where the centre of each circle lies. Exactly two of the four arcs are pieces of one and the same circle, that is, the two arcs whose circles have the same centre; each of the other two arcs belongs to a circle with a different centre. Continue each arc into its whole circle and report which two arcs share a circle, naming each of the two by the page edge it lies near. No single arc can settle this: only the agreement between two of them can. Answer unclear if no two arcs share a circle, or if two different pairs of arcs come so close to sharing a circle that the sharing pair cannot be told apart. Which two arcs lie on the same circle: top and bottom, left and right, top and left, top and right, bottom and left, bottom and right, or unclear?

worlds.title: Half turn tile patch
worlds.question: The colored patch contains exactly 36 equal square tiles joined edge-to-edge. Around the red center pin, would the whole patch look unchanged after a 180-degree half-turn? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Negative space waist
worlds.question: The two detached colored banks bound one pale corridor. Does the corridor stay evenly wide as it bends, or does its width clearly change at the middle? Answer even or changing.

worlds.title: Route reach color
worlds.question: Follow the single dark route from the orange start marker. Which colored destination marker does the route connect to? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Dual signature seal search
worlds.question: Each quadrant contains one compact filled medallion. A medallion has a hole when a background region is completely enclosed by its ink, and it has a notch when its outside border has one inward bite. Which quadrant contains the only medallion with both a hole and a notch? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Patch pair parallel search
worlds.question: The picture is a plain page divided, from top to bottom, into four horizontal bands of exactly equal height; no line is drawn between them. Counting downwards the bands are the first, second, third and fourth. Each band holds one station. A station is made of two separate square-ish clusters of twelve short straight strokes each: the two clusters of a station are drawn in the same ink colour, they stand side by side in that band with a wide band of empty background between them, and no mark joins them. Every stroke inside one cluster has the same tilt, so a cluster shows a single stroke direction twelve times over. A tilt has no arrowhead: a stroke and the same stroke turned by a half turn point the same way. Exactly one station has both of its clusters tilted the same way, so that the strokes of its left cluster are parallel to the strokes of its right cluster. In every other station the two clusters are tilted clearly differently. Both clusters of a station must be read: one cluster alone never decides anything. Clusters that belong to different bands are never a match, and the page always contains a cluster in some other band whose tilt copies the winning tilt exactly, so a tilt that appears again elsewhere on the page does not name a band. The ink colours, which is only there to show which two clusters belong to the same station, how far the stations sit from the left edge, the small up and down shifts of the stations, and the tiny isolated specks dotted about the background all carry no information. Which band holds the station whose two clusters of strokes are parallel to each other? Answer with one of: first, second, third, fourth.

worlds.title: Radial order badge search
worlds.question: Which labeled badge has, from its center outward, cyan, amber, violet, then green? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Cocircular arc pair search
worlds.question: Each color draws two detached curved strokes. Imagine extending each stroke along its own circle. Which color's two strokes lie on one and the same circle, with the same center and radius? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Corner state match
worlds.question: Two small tracking registers are far apart, one at the top-left corner and one at the bottom-right corner of the canvas, and the white space between them is empty. Each register has one coloured start dot (blue = tracked state OFF, orange = tracked state ON) plus a cluster of red toggle dots that invert that register's own tracked state, once per red dot. Track each register's state independently, then bind the two distant registers together by comparing them. Do both tracked states end up equal? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: State first return route
worlds.question: Start at the ringed badge and follow the one connected route through stations 1 to 11 in increasing number order. The token has four states A, B, C, and D. The badge colors mean red=A, green=B, blue=C, and purple=D. At each station, a filled right-pointing triangle advances one state cyclically A-B-C-D-A, a filled left-pointing triangle retreats one state, and an outlined square leaves the state unchanged. Ignore the starting position when looking for a return. After the token has first left its starting state, which numbered station is the first station at which the token has the starting state again? Answer 1 through 11.

worlds.title: Reflect track replay
worlds.question: The board is a grid of square cells with five rows and six columns, read left to right. In the leftmost column a black disk marks the row where the token starts. The next four columns are four moves applied in that order. In a move column the teal cells mean up and the amber cells mean down, and the number of coloured cells in that column is how many rows the token moves; grey cells are inert filler. If a move would carry the token past the top row or past the bottom row, it bounces off that edge and spends its remaining steps in the opposite direction. The rightmost column shows one coloured cap per row: red, blue, green, purple and pink in some order. After all four moves have been applied, which cap colour is in the token's row? Answer with one colour name.

worlds.title: Ticket queue replay
worlds.question: FRONT is the left end. Read badges 1 then 2: cyan swaps the two front tickets; coral serves (removes) the front ticket. Which color is at the front afterward?

worlds.title: Serpentine heading mirror
worlds.question: Begin with the direction shown by the white arrow in the purple tile. Follow the touching tiles in alternating row order: left-to-right, then right-to-left, then left-to-right, then right-to-left. Gold means turn clockwise by one quarter turn; teal means reflect the direction across a vertical mirror, swapping east with west while keeping north and south. What is the final compass direction?

worlds.title: Focal face adjacency
worlds.question: Do the red and blue chamber marks share a full wall? The dark glyph contains enclosed white chambers; a corner touch does not count. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Twin seal depth duel
worlds.question: This page shows black ink together with coloured decorations in red, blue, orange, purple, green and grey. Only black ink counts as a wall; coloured and grey marks never count, even when a decoration is drawn as a closed ring with its own hole. A white area is shut in when you cannot travel from it to the edge of the page without crossing black ink, and its depth is the number of separate black rings you must cross to get out. A black ring that carries a visible gap is not a wall around anything: you may walk through the gap, however narrow it looks and however far it lies from the area you started in. Exactly two clusters of black rings on this page shut in a white core; each of those clusters is a stack of two or three black square rings drawn one inside the other around its own core, and the two clusters stand apart with plain white page between them. Every other black mark on the page shuts in nothing. The two cores never have the same depth: one is shut in by exactly one more unbroken ring than the other. How large a cluster is, how many rings are drawn in it, how much black ink it holds, where on the page the pair sits, and how many coloured marks are drawn never decide the answer. Taking the two clusters in left-to-right order, which cluster's core is shut in by more unbroken black rings? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Alternating station cycle
worlds.question: The black railway is one closed loop. Count only yellow stations centered on the railway; ignore identical yellow stations away from it. Could the on-railway stations be colored alternately cyan and orange all the way around so that every neighboring pair has different colors? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Boundary incidence badge
worlds.question: The amber tile is solid. Does it touch two different connected white regions? White areas connect through shared edges, not diagonal corners; a region may be enclosed or connected to the outside. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Ribbon midpoint checkpoint
worlds.question: Which ringed checkpoint—amber or violet—is closer to the halfway point of the thick green-to-red ribbon?

worlds.title: Rank fix duet
worlds.question: The picture contains exactly two dark cords in two far-apart parts of the image, and the two cords never touch each other. Each cord is a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness with two free ends. On each cord one end is covered by a black square, which marks that cord's start; the other end is bare. Each cord carries exactly three disks sitting on it, one red, one green and one blue, so every colour appears once on each cord. On a given cord, walk along the stroke from that cord's black start square towards its bare end and number the disks 1, 2 and 3 in the order you meet them; that number is the disk's position on that cord. The two cords may have very different total lengths and different disk spacings, and only the order of meeting counts, not any distance. Exactly one colour has the same position number on both cords, and the other two colours have their two position numbers exchanged. Which colour has the same position number on both cords? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Bicolor belt distance
worlds.question: Trace the uniformly wide belt from the green ring to the red ring. Is the total centerline distance traveled on cyan pavement or on orange pavement longer? Answer cyan or orange.

worlds.title: Sliding tile exit
worlds.question: The blue square is a sliding tile. Without rotating it, keep the whole tile on the dark floor and trace from its blue start. Which exit can it reach, red or gold? Answer red or gold.

worlds.title: Gateway ladder reach
worlds.question: A pale sheet is split by four thick dark walls into five vertical strips. A blue dot sits in the far-left strip, and one coloured dot sits in each of the other four strips: cyan, then magenta, then lime, then gold. An open wall has a tall pale gap at its top, so the route can pass; a sealed wall runs top to bottom and blocks everything to its right. The blue dot reaches a coloured dot exactly when every wall to that dot's left is open. How many of the four coloured dots can the blue dot reach? Answer with exactly one of: zero, one, two, three, four.

worlds.title: Fractional pin alignment
worlds.question: Each panel has a red row and a blue row of three pins. For each row, divide the left gap by the right gap. Which panel has the same ratio in red and blue? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Sole passage gateway
worlds.question: This picture is a 6 by 6 block of square rooms. Walls are solid ink, and you may walk between two rooms only through a doorway gap in the wall between them. Two rooms hold a black dot, and four other rooms have a coloured floor: orange, green, blue and pink. Exactly one of those four coloured rooms lies on every walking route between the two black dots; each of the other three can be left out by some route. Which coloured room is it? Answer with exactly one of: orange, green, blue, pink.

worlds.title: Merged load feasibility
worlds.question: Each line starts with the first ADD load. At each arrow p:q, convert p current units into q units, then merge the next ADD load. At every stage the current load must be at most MAX. Which line stays within all three limits: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Unavoidable portal gate
worlds.question: Move through touching corridor cells (white or marked) up, down, left, or right. Matching letter portals also connect directly. Which colored gate must every route from START to EXIT cross? Answer amber, cyan, violet, or lime.

worlds.title: Seam patch completion
worlds.question: The top band shows colored contour lines broken by a blank window in the middle. Below, three framed patches A, B, C each propose a way to fill the window. Which patch completes the window so that every colored contour continues continuously across the seam?

worlds.title: Colored arc curvature correspondence
worlds.question: The image shows a REFERENCE panel and candidates A and B. Each panel has four uniquely colored curved strokes. Rank the strokes from 1 (least bowed) to 4 (most bowed) by normalized bow from the straight endpoint chord. Which candidate has the same color-to-curvature-rank assignment as the REFERENCE? Ignore panel position, stroke position, rotation, reflection, and line width. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Nested frame depth glyph binding
worlds.question: The upper part of this image shows four rectangular frames drawn in red, blue, green and purple. The frames are strictly nested: each frame lies completely inside the next larger one, but they are not concentric, so a frame can sit off-centre inside its neighbour. The bottom row of the image shows four grey tiles, and each tile carries exactly one black glyph - a filled disk, a filled square, a filled triangle, or an open ring. The tiles stand for the four frames in nesting order: the leftmost tile stands for the innermost frame, the next tile for the frame that encloses it, and so on, with the rightmost tile standing for the outermost frame. Tile position carries no other meaning, and glyphs are assigned to tiles independently of frame colour. Which glyph is on the tile that stands for the red frame? Answer disk, square, triangle, or ring.

worlds.title: Interval endpoint order
worlds.question: Each card contains four colored horizontal intervals, one per row. Rows may be rearranged, and a whole card may be shifted or stretched horizontally. Read all eight interval endpoints from left to right, recording both color and whether each endpoint starts or ends its interval. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same endpoint order as the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Hole incidence correspondence
worlds.question: The magenta frame marks the REFERENCE emblem. Match it to the TARGET emblem with the same topology: compare the sorted numbers of enclosed white holes in each separate black piece. Every emblem has three pieces and four holes in total; shapes, piece order, positions, and sizes do not matter. Which target frame color is it: red, green, blue, or orange?

worlds.title: Runlength color compare
worlds.question: Which color covers the greater total horizontal length along the bar? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Fraction ratio layout
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Each panel shows a fraction as two rows of repeated colored terms separated by a horizontal rule. The numerator is the number of terms above the rule and the denominator is the number below it. Which displayed fraction is larger? Choose A or B.

worlds.title: Uneven scale readout
worlds.question: The picture shows four horizontal SCALES drawn one above the other. Each scale is a dark grey horizontal line carrying short dark grey TICKS that hang below it; the leftmost tick of a scale sits at the left end of its line and the rightmost tick at the right end. The ticks of a scale are NOT evenly spaced, and every scale has its own tick pattern and its own number of ticks. Above each scale stands one solid triangular POINTER; the four pointers are red, green, blue and orange, one to a scale, and each pointer marks the position directly under the middle of its triangle. On every scale, stepping from one tick to the next tick on its right always adds exactly ONE UNIT of value, however wide or narrow that gap looks, and the leftmost tick of a scale reads zero. The VALUE a pointer reads is therefore the number of ticks strictly to its left, plus the fraction of the way it stands across the gap it is in, that fraction being its distance from the tick on its left divided by the whole width of that same gap. Distance in the picture is not value: a pointer standing further to the right, or further from the tick on its left, need not read more. No pointer ever stands on a tick, and no two pointers read the same value. The number of ticks on a scale, the width of the gap a pointer stands in, the pointer's distance from the left end of its scale, its distance from the tick on its left, and how high up the picture its scale is drawn are each the answer no more often than chance allows. Which pointer reads the largest value? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Checkpoint trace gap
worlds.question: At which labeled checkpoint is the vertical gap between the cyan and magenta markers largest?

worlds.title: Difference in differences leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order and share the same vertical scale. In each panel, subtract the blue marker from the orange marker at BEFORE and again at AFTER, then subtract the BEFORE gap from the AFTER gap. Which panel has the largest result? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior stove burners
worlds.question: This is a stovetop range. How many burners are on it? Count only the visible burners and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Paperclip loop state
worlds.question: Is the paperclip's large loop open or closed? Answer open or closed.

worlds.title: Door handle hinge side
worlds.question: This image shows one door leaf lying flat on a page. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks just inside it are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The door leaf is the large solid coloured rectangle. The small dark slate blocks that sit astride one single edge of the leaf, half on the leaf and half off it, are the hinges, and the edge they straddle is the hinged edge; every hinge block in an image is on that one edge. The one solid black disc painted inside the leaf is the handle. Any white bars crossing the leaf are panel grooves and never mark the answer. Now imagine the straight line drawn across the middle of the leaf parallel to the hinged edge: it splits the leaf into a half that touches the hinged edge and a half that does not. The handle belongs to the half that contains the centre of the black disc. Which edge carries the hinges, the leaf's size and shape, where it sits on the page, its colour, the number and size of the hinge blocks, the size of the handle and the number of panel grooves all change from image to image, and the handle need not be placed where a door handle is normally placed. Read only what is painted in this image and do not answer from where handles usually go. Is the handle in the same half of the leaf as the hinged edge, or in the opposite half? Answer with exactly one of: same, opposite.

worlds.title: Bias radiation blades
worlds.question: How many large dark wedge-shaped blades are visible in the radiation warning sign, around the center disk? Count each detached large blade once; ignore the center disk, border, and small square markers. Answer 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Usb left terminal shape conflict
worlds.question: At the end of the branch that extends left from the central stem of the large USB-like symbol, which colored endpoint shape is visible: circle, square, or triangle? Ignore the two small corner diamonds and answer with the shape name.

worlds.title: Value modulo band
worlds.question: The image is a 32x32 lattice of flat gray blocks, each painted a single random gray level, so the field looks like uniform flat noise. A hidden vertical band was encoded in the VALUE of the gray levels: inside the band every block's level is an exact multiple of 7 (residue 0), outside it the levels are arbitrary. Take each block's gray level MODULO 7 and light up the residue-0 blocks; the band appears. Which vertical band is revealed, the left band L or the right band R? Answer L or R.

worlds.title: Adjacent difference emblem
worlds.question: Find the grayscale square just inside four colored 16x16 corner marks, with an 8-pixel gap. For every pixel, take the absolute difference from the pixel immediately to its right, reusing the rightmost pixel at the right edge, then replace each result by the centered 5x5 mean with edge replication. Ignore the marks and canvas and choose the broad symbol: wave, ring, hook, or crown.

worlds.title: Swatch band stencil reveal
worlds.question: The image shows one square panel enclosed by a coloured frame and ruled into a 9 by 9 grid of equal square cells. Every cell is printed in one flat shade of grey taken from six evenly spaced greys. Above the panel two key squares are printed in the same coloured outline, and each carries one of those six greys. Keep a cell when its grey lies in the closed band between the two key greys, that is when it is no darker than the darker key square and no lighter than the lighter key square; discard every other cell, whether it is darker than the darker key or lighter than the lighter key. The kept cells form one of these symbols: plus, square, chevron, ladder, arrow. Each symbol is drawn on a 7 by 7 block of cells that may sit anywhere inside the 9 by 9 panel. Match by sliding each symbol over the panel to the placement disagreeing with the kept cells in the fewest of the 81 cells, and take the symbol with the smallest such count. Which symbol do the kept cells form? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Halftone blur reveal
worlds.question: Blur the cyan-framed halftone field until its tiny checks blend together. Which symbol appears: circle, triangle, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Phase keyed decimation glyph
worlds.question: The cyan mosaic is divided into 2-by-2 blocks. In every block, keep only the cell in the same corner as the gold dot in the small cyan key. Close the gaps without rotating or reflecting. Which symbol appears: cup, arch, bolt, or crown?

worlds.title: Enclosed region marker
worlds.question: Thick black line-work on a white canvas separates the picture into white regions. Every white region that is part of the outer background reaches the edge of the picture; exactly one white region is completely sealed off by black line on every side and never touches the picture edge. Four small coloured dots (red, green, blue, orange) each sit in one of the white regions. Which coloured dot lies inside the completely sealed-off white region? Choose: red, green, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Smooth path constellation
worlds.question: Which color's dots lie on one smooth bowed path? Compare the complete dot set; ignore color, lane position, dot count, and dot size. Choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Stroke axis convergence
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain background covered with many short grey strokes and four coloured dots: one red, one green, one blue and one orange. Every grey stroke has the same length, the same thickness and the same colour, and the strokes never touch each other or the dots. The strokes are aimed: if a stroke is extended into a full straight line in both directions, that line passes through one single hidden spot, apart from a small wobble of at most twenty-four degrees that is added to each stroke on its own. All the strokes are aimed at the same hidden spot. Exactly one of the four coloured dots is sitting on that spot; the other three dots are far away from it, and they lie on the same circle as it does. Because of the wobble a single stroke is not enough: the spot is the place that fits all of the strokes together best. The colours of the dots, where the dots and strokes are placed, how many strokes there are and how much ink the picture contains carry no information about the answer. Which coloured dot are the grey strokes aimed at? Answer with one of red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Hull lamina balance
worlds.question: Imagine the tightest convex rubber band around every black dot, then uniformly fill the region inside it. Which colored marker is closer to the balance point of that filled region: red or blue? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Occluded curve continuation
worlds.question: The gray band hides the middle of the curves. Each color marks one left fragment and one right fragment. Extend every fragment through the band without changing its direction or bend. Which color's two fragments form one smooth curve? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Proximity quadrant search
worlds.question: The image is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) by two light-grey lines that cross at the image centre, where a small mid-grey diamond marker is drawn. Each quadrant contains one dark filled dot. Exactly one dot is closer to the central marker than every other dot. Which quadrant contains the dot that is nearest to the central marker? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Equidistant hub panel search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only four-marker arrangement with one marker equally distant from each of the other three? Inspect all four equal panels, ignore labels, color, position, and size, and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Escape gap panel
worlds.question: Thin gray lines split this image into four square panels side by side, counted from the left. Each panel contains one ring drawn as a circle outline with a single opening cut out of it, and one small filled dot lying outside that ring. A dot faces its ring's opening when the straight direction from the centre of that ring to that dot passes through the opening rather than through the drawn part of the ring. Exactly one panel has its dot facing its own opening; in every other panel the direction to the dot misses the opening by more than fourteen degrees. Every ring has the same radius, and opening width, dot distance, dot colour, ring colour, panel position and the amount of ink in a panel carry no information about the answer: the facing panel is not systematically the one with the widest or the narrowest opening, nor the one with the nearest or the farthest dot. Compare each dot only with the ring in its own panel. Which half of the image contains the panel whose dot faces its ring's opening, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: One stroke link search
worlds.question: Which labeled network can be traced in one stroke using every dark link exactly once? Start at any circle; do not lift your pencil or retrace a link. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Closed domino chain search
worlds.question: Which labeled row can use every domino exactly once in a closed chain? Dominoes may be reordered and flipped; every pair of touching ends, including last-to-first, must have the same color. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State lifo stack
worlds.question: A leftmost panel shows the initial stack: a vertical column of coloured discs sitting on a base line, read bottom to top, with the top (highest) disc marked by an orange ring. To the right are four operator panels, read left to right. A PUSH panel shows a coloured disc above a matching upward arrow and places that colour onto the top of the stack; a POP panel shows a dark downward arrow over an empty slot and removes the current top disc, revealing the colour below it. The final stack is not drawn anywhere; replay the operators in order from the initial stack. What colour is on top of the final stack? Answer 'red', 'green', 'blue', or 'empty' (if every disc was popped).

worlds.title: State pattern match
worlds.question: Read P1 through P5 from left to right. Each labeled tile keeps its identity. Which label's five states exactly match the TARGET row? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Undo history replay
worlds.question: The picture is a single row of cream panels, acted on from left to right as the arrow beneath the row shows. The leftmost panel, the one drawn inside a dark ring, holds a coloured square: that is the colour the paint pot holds before anything happens. Every panel to its right is a card, and the cards act on the pot one at a time in drawn left-to-right order. A card holding a coloured circle is a paint card: it paints the pot that colour. A card holding a dark grey left-pointing triangle is an undo card: it cancels the most recent paint card that has already acted and has not itself already been cancelled, so the pot goes back to the colour it held just before that paint card acted; if every paint card that has acted has already been cancelled, the undo card changes nothing. A paint card counts as still in effect once it has acted and has not been cancelled. The colour the pot holds at the end is not drawn anywhere in the picture. What colour does the paint pot hold after the last card has acted? Answer with one word: red, blue, green, amber or violet.

worlds.title: Majority vote replay
worlds.question: The four lamps start as shown. Read the five VOTE cards from left to right. Each card's blue-dot count names one lamp, and its green CHECK strip repeats that count. Replace the named lamp's state with the majority state of the other three lamps: it becomes ON when at least two of them are ON, and OFF otherwise. The other lamps stay unchanged. Is the magenta-ringed lamp ON or OFF at the end?

worlds.title: Checkpoint lamp replay
worlds.question: Four pip-labeled lamps start as shown (filled = ON, ring = OFF). Read cards 1 through 8 from left to right. A triangular FLIP card toggles the lamp named by its 1-4 pips. A square SAVE card replaces the saved snapshot with the current four-lamp pattern. A circular RESTORE card replaces the current pattern with the most recently saved snapshot; before card 1, that snapshot equals the starting pattern. After all cards, how many lamps are ON? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Cut point selection
worlds.question: The image shows a network of black connection points (filled dots) joined by black links. A point is a cut point if removing it and all of its links would split the network into more separate pieces than before. Exactly one of the red and blue highlighted dots is a cut point. Consider removing the red dot (and its links) and then removing the blue dot (and its links). For only one of those two dots does the network split into more pieces. Which dot is it: red or blue? Answer with exactly red or blue.

worlds.title: Face separation pair
worlds.question: Do the red and blue markers lie in the same open region when the dark closed contours are treated as walls? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cut link partition
worlds.question: The picture shows a wiring diagram on white paper. Grey wires of equal thickness join only where they meet at a junction, and no two wires cross anywhere in the picture, so wires that merely pass near each other are not joined. Exactly one wire is drawn in violet instead of grey. A red, a blue and a green dot each sit on a junction of the wiring, and no dot sits on an end of the violet wire. Now imagine erasing the violet wire completely while leaving every grey wire and both of its end junctions in place. After that erasure, two dots count as connected only if you can travel from one to the other along grey wire the whole way, never jumping a gap. Once the violet wire is erased, which dots are still connected to each other? Answer 'red and blue', 'red and green', 'blue and green', or 'all three'.

worlds.title: Topology signature panels
worlds.question: The blue-framed panel on the left is the reference. A black connected component is one black piece, and a hole is a white region fully enclosed by black. Which panel to the right has the same ordered pair (number of black connected components, number of holes) as the reference? Answer first, second, or third.

worlds.title: One hole per island
worlds.question: The picture contains three separate dark islands and three white holes in total. A hole is a white region fully enclosed by one side-connected dark island; dark parts touching only at a corner do not connect. Does every dark island enclose exactly one hole? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Fork branch length
worlds.question: A blue line starts at an orange ring, runs along a shared trunk to a junction, then splits into two branches. Each branch ends in a coloured terminal dot (red or green). Following the blue line from the ring, which coloured terminal, red or green, is at the far end of the LONGER branch (the branch with the greater length along the stroke)? Answer red or green.

worlds.title: Ringed trace checkpoint order
worlds.question: Starting at the ringed port, follow the solid navy trace. Which labeled checkpoint, A or B, do you encounter first? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Pipe fewer corners
worlds.question: This picture contains exactly two gray pipes. The two pipes never touch each other, and no pipe ever touches or crosses itself. Each pipe runs from one end sitting inside a black ring to its other end, which is covered by a colored square: one pipe ends at the orange square and the other pipe ends at the purple square. Every pipe is built only from horizontal and vertical straight sections, so every bend in a pipe is a right-angle turn. Follow each pipe from its black ring to its colored square and count the right-angle turns you pass along that pipe. How long the pipes are, how much of the picture they cover, and where they sit do not matter; only the number of right-angle turns counts. Which colored square is at the end of the pipe with fewer right-angle turns? Answer orange or purple.

worlds.title: Dual wave last checkpoint
worlds.question: Green and red waves start together at the end circles of each separate chain and move one dark link per round. Which colored checkpoint is reached latest by its nearer wave? A link is one dark segment between adjacent circles. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Unique visit terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green circle, follow black links from circle to circle without visiting any circle more than once. Which colored terminal can be reached on a route that visits all three purple checkpoints? Links meet only at circles and never cross. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Distal parity twins
worlds.question: Two disconnected light-grey pin-badges sit far apart on the blank canvas: one near the top-left corner, one near the bottom-right corner. Each badge carries a small number of dark navy pins on its light field. Do the two far-apart badges carry the SAME parity of pin count (both an odd number or both an even number of pins)? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Board contour attribute correspondence
worlds.question: The board has three labeled cards: R is the reference and A and B are candidates. Rotate each candidate contour 90 degrees clockwise, compare its complete filled-cell contour with R, and answer with the halo color on the matching candidate.

worlds.title: Patchbay hop trace bind
worlds.question: The picture is one patch bay. On the left there are five square coloured pads, one per row; on the right there are five identical dark square sockets. Five grey cables of identical colour and thickness each join exactly one pad to exactly one socket, and every socket is used exactly once. Each cable runs as a staircase of horizontal and vertical straight runs. Where two cables meet, one passes over and the other passes under: the cable underneath is drawn with a small white break, and it continues on the far side of the crossing cable in the same straight run, in the same row or column. A break is therefore never the end of a cable; a cable ends only at a pad or at a socket. Exactly one socket is outlined by a magenta frame. The rows are not wired straight across: the pad in the framed socket's own row is never the answer, and the cables carry no colour, thickness, or style information about which pad they come from. Follow the cable that leaves the framed socket, turning at every corner and continuing straight through every break, back to the pad it comes from. What is the colour of that pad? Answer red, orange, purple, blue, green or teal.

worlds.title: Cavity fill badge
worlds.question: The gold-framed mosaic is the source. Cyan cells are walls and cream cells are empty. Starting from a cream cell, you may move up, down, left, or right through cream cells; diagonal moves do not count. The result keeps every source cyan cell cyan and changes to cyan exactly those cream cells that cannot reach any outer edge of the source. Which red, green, or blue frame marks the exact result?

worlds.title: Column drift correspondence
worlds.question: The upper-left mosaic is the SOURCE. The blue pip stacks above its columns are drift counts. In every source column, move all tiles downward by that column's pip count, wrapping tiles that pass the bottom back to the top. Exactly one of the other three mosaics is the result. Which color labels it: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Trace direction alternation
worlds.question: In the boxed trace, as x increases, do the seven straight pieces alternate rising and falling at every interior bend? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cable knot side length
worlds.question: The sheet is off-white. Exactly one mark on it is pure black: a single thin cable that runs continuously from its left end to its right end and has exactly one height at every horizontal position it covers. One small red ring is drawn centred on a point of that cable; the cable passes straight through the middle of the ring. The ring splits the cable into two parts: the left part runs from the cable's left end to the ring centre, and the right part runs from the ring centre to the cable's right end. The length of a part means the distance travelled along the cable itself, following all of its rises and falls from one end of the part to the other; it is not the horizontal distance between the part's ends, so a part that covers less width can still be the longer one when it climbs and falls more steeply. The two parts are never equally long: their cable lengths always differ by at least thirty pixels. The pale coloured polylines, the grey border and the short grey tick marks are decoration and carry no information. Which part of the cable is longer? Answer with one word: left or right.

worlds.title: Paired aperture ratio
worlds.question: Which colored U-shaped gauge has the larger clear opening-width to inner-depth ratio? For each U, divide the clear horizontal distance between its inner side walls by the clear vertical distance from the open mouth to the inner base. Ignore the pale gray marks. Answer coral or blue.

worlds.title: Lamina centroid band
worlds.question: The two gold horizontal guides divide the frame into UPPER, MIDDLE, and LOWER bands. Treat the filled lamina as uniformly dense. In which band lies its center of area? Answer UPPER, MIDDLE, or LOWER.

worlds.title: Week grid trace columns
worlds.question: How many columns are in the visible WEEK grid? Count each vertical lane traced from the top rail to the bottom rail, including the two outer lanes. Answer with a whole number.

worlds.title: Domino seam twin
worlds.question: This picture shows a row of domino-like tiles on a plain background. Each tile is split into two halves and every half is printed with one compact cluster of small dark grey dots. Exactly one small red arrow is drawn well below the row, clear of the tiles, pointing up at the butt seam where two neighbouring tiles meet. Look only at the two dot clusters nearest that arrow, one on its left and one on its right; every other cluster in the row and every mark of any other colour is decoration and must be ignored. Do those two clusters contain the same number of dark dots? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Clock frame hour tab count
worlds.question: How many inward hour tabs are visibly fused to the single colored clock frame? Count every colored tab protruding from the inner edge toward the center. Do not count the gray hands or center pin.

worlds.title: Tail lamp color match
worlds.question: Do the two circular tail lamps on the rear of the car visibly have the same solid fill color? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route gap delta
worlds.question: Inside the pale route window is one connected navy route with a red start cap, a green end cap, and 31 amber station rings. Follow the route from red to green and straighten it by station order. Measure the 32 successive center-to-center station gaps; call the shorter gap 0 and the longer gap 1. Apply the binary first difference: keep gap 1 as the first output bit, then write 1 whenever a gap class differs from the preceding class. Lay the 32 output bits row-major into a 4-by-8 bitmap. Which displayed template is closer by Hamming distance: A) CREST = 00111100/01100110/11000011/11111111 or B) VAULT = 11111111/11000011/01100110/00111100? Choose A on a tie; quarantine a gap of at most 2. Ignore the caps, window, and marks outside it.

worlds.title: Rail hop reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one stroke in this picture is a long unbroken wire: it runs straight across, turns at its end, comes back the other way, and does this until it has made five horizontal passes, one under the next. Five short vertical rails, drawn in a different colour, stand across those passes, so the wire meets a rail at twenty-five crossings, five on every pass. At each crossing the wire does one of exactly two things: it arches up over the rail in a small raised hop, or it cuts straight across at the level of the pass. One end of the wire carries a small filled round bead just inside the wire's tip; the other end has no bead. Carry out this operation: start at the beaded end and walk along the wire to its far end, so you travel the five passes one after another; write the first pass you travel into row 1 of a 5 by 5 grid, the second into row 2, and so on to row 5; within each pass, fill that row's five columns left to right in the order you meet its five crossings as you travel, so a pass walked from right to left fills its row starting from the crossing you reach first; then mark every grid position whose crossing was a raised hop. Exactly 9 of the 25 positions are marked. The marked positions form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'ell' is the whole left column together with the whole bottom row; 'tee' is the whole top row together with the centre column below it; 'eff' is the top row's first four positions, the left column down to row 4, and the middle row's first three positions; 'zed' is the top row's first three positions, then a step down and left through row 2 column 4, row 3 column 3 and row 4 column 2, then the bottom row's last three positions. The rails, the scattered marks elsewhere in the picture and the wire's own position on the page are decoration; only which crossings are hopped, taken in walking order from the beaded end, decides the symbol. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: eff, ell, tee, zed.

worlds.title: Cyclic ternary difference
worlds.question: Treat pale, mid, and dark as 0, 1, and 2. For each matching square, subtract the two-dot panel from the one-dot panel, wrapping modulo 3. Mark a result square only when the remainder is 1. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Bent strip rectification
worlds.question: A cyan strip was bent by shifting its narrow crossbars sideways. Starting at the red ring and ending at the gold triangle, slide each crossbar perpendicular to travel until both cyan edges are straight; do not reorder or flip crossbars. Which dark symbol appears: arch, cup, or tee? Answer ambiguous for a tie.

worlds.title: Textured energy silhouette
worlds.question: Which symbol is hidden by the texture: a circle or a diamond?

worlds.title: Lattice row drift
worlds.question: The picture shows exactly one solid dark plate on a pale background; every pale grey blob is background clutter and must be ignored. The plate is pierced by holes: equal rectangular patches of background, each one completely surrounded by plate. The holes form several rows, every row holding the same number of holes, evenly spaced within each row and evenly spaced from row to row. Reading the rows from top to bottom, either the holes line up in exactly straight vertical columns, or every row is shifted sideways from the row above by the same step in the same direction, and in that case the step is at least a quarter of the width of one hole. The colours, the plate's size, the hole size, the number of rows and columns, the total amount of dark ink and the thickness of the plate's outer border are all varied independently of the answer, and the rows are shifted about the middle row, so no single row, corner or border tells you the answer: only the whole lattice, top row against bottom row, does. Answer unclear if the plate or a hole is broken open, if any hole is not completely surrounded by plate, if the rows do not all hold the same evenly spaced number of holes, or if a sideways step is present but smaller than a quarter of a hole's width. Going down the plate, which way do the columns of holes lean: left, right, in line, or unclear?

worlds.title: Nested contour phase
worlds.question: The small colored cog-ring has eight outer tips and eight inner notches. Around the whole ring, do the inner notches point toward the outer tips or toward the gaps between neighboring tips? Answer aligned or staggered.

worlds.title: Center orbit texture
worlds.question: Inside the single colored tile, are the eight pale dashes collectively more nearly pointing toward the tile center or running around it? Answer toward or around.

worlds.title: Spanning route target
worlds.question: A single thin route starts at the orange marker on the left and crosses the whole image to one far destination on the right. Which colored destination does the route connect to? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Complementary tile pair search
worlds.question: Each quadrant contains two detached filled tiles made of five-by-five square cells. Overlay each pair on the same grid without rotating either tile. Which quadrant contains the only pair whose cells fill every grid cell exactly once, with no overlap? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Sum reach ruler search
worlds.question: The picture shows six separate solid horizontal bars on a plain background. Two of them are drawn in one colour and are the reference bars: one of these sits alone near the top-left corner of the page and the other sits alone near the bottom-right corner. The remaining four bars are drawn in a second colour and are stacked one above another in a single column near the middle of the page; counting downwards from the top of that column they are the first, second, third and fourth candidate bars. The length of a bar is how far it reaches from its left end to its right end. Every bar is horizontal and every bar has the same thickness, so lengths can be compared directly and thickness carries no information. Exactly one candidate bar is exactly as long as the two reference bars laid end to end, that is, as long as the length of the top-left reference bar plus the length of the bottom-right reference bar. Both reference bars are needed: each of the other three candidate bars differs from that combined length by a clearly visible amount, and one of them is built to match a single reference bar on its own, or that same single reference bar counted twice, so looking at only one corner of the page will point at the wrong bar. The colours used, which corner holds which reference bar, how long the winning bar is, where the column sits on the page, the order of the three losing bars and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which candidate bar in the column is exactly as long as the two reference bars added together? Answer with one of: first, second, third, fourth.

worlds.title: Solid window search
worlds.question: Which labeled tile contains a completely filled 2-by-2 cyan square? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Bisected area balance search
worlds.question: Panels A, B, C, and D run top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. Each contains one connected blue tile island and a gold vertical center rule. Which island has exactly the same total blue area on the left and right of its own gold rule? Count every blue part equally. Exactly one balances. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State ring parity
worlds.question: Find the small round state ring on the canvas. Its top tick dot declares the initial state (blue = OFF, orange = ON). Going clockwise from the tick, each of the ring's four sectors is a step: an orange sector flips the tracked state, a blue sector leaves it unchanged. Apply every sector in order and report whether the tracked state finishes ON. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Dual register concordance
worlds.question: The image shows two separate state registers, left and right. In each register, start at the ringed phase and read operation cards 1 through 5 from top to bottom. A right arrow advances one step through phases 1, 2, 3, then back to 1; a left arrow moves one step backward; a diamond swaps phases 2 and 3 while leaving phase 1 fixed. Apply every operation in order. Do the two registers finish at the same phase? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Rotor window dial
worlds.question: This canvas carries a single rotor. The rotor is a ring of exactly eight small coloured squares, evenly spaced around a common centre, one square each in red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple and pink. These eight positions are the stations of the ring. Just outside the ring, opposite exactly one station, there is a solid black curved bracket: that bracket is the read window and it never moves. Inside the ring, at the hub, there is a stack of solid black turn glyphs, one turn per line. A line consists of a black triangle followed by one, two or three small black square pips. The pips say how many stations that turn advances the ring. The triangle says which way: a triangle whose point aims to the right turns the whole ring of coloured squares one station at a time in the clockwise direction, and a triangle whose point aims to the left turns it in the anticlockwise direction. The turns are applied in order from the top line of the hub stack to the bottom line, starting from the ring exactly as it is printed. The ring is a closed loop, so a square that passes the last station carries on round to the next one. The whole ring turns together, so the eight colours keep their cyclic order; only the window is fixed. Placement and tilt of the rotor vary freely from picture to picture; every faint grey mark beyond it belongs to the backdrop and means nothing. After all of the turns in the hub stack have been carried out, which coloured square is standing at the read window? Answer with one of red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue, purple or pink.

worlds.title: Courtyard entry chronicle
worlds.question: Read the four snapshots in row order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right. The gold square is the courtyard. Which colored bead makes the first outside-to-inside transition? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Skipstep badge trail
worlds.question: Start on the first of the 12 colored badges after the green START ring and follow the single purple track toward the red END ring. At a round badge, jump forward one badge. At a diamond badge, jump forward two badges, skipping the badge between. Read and obey only badges you land on. If a jump would go beyond the final badge, stop on your current badge. What color is that badge: cyan, amber, or rose?

worlds.title: Remote maze triptych
worlds.question: Is the reachable marker pair in the left, center, or right panel? A route may pass through a doorway but not through dark ink.

worlds.title: Geode core wall depth
worlds.question: This page shows one black figure and several coloured decorations. Only the black ink and the green patch decide the answer; blue, orange, grey and purple marks are decoration and never count, even when they are drawn one inside another. Black ink is a solid wall that you cannot pass through. Exactly one small green patch is painted on the page. Imagine walking from the green patch to the edge of the page. You may walk freely over white space, over the green patch and over any decoration colour, and you may never step on black ink. Count how many separate black walls you must pass through on the way out, choosing the route that passes through as few walls as possible. A wall that has a visible gap cut through it does not have to be passed through at all, because you can walk out through that gap instead. How big the black figure is, where it sits on the page, how much black ink it holds, how many chambers it has, and how many nested outlines you can see anywhere on the page never decide the answer. How many separate black walls must you pass through to get from the green patch to the edge of the page? Answer 1 or 2.

worlds.title: Same room pair
worlds.question: The black walls divide the white floor into rooms. Movement is through edge-sharing white space; walls cannot be crossed. Which color's two dots are in the same room: cyan or orange?

worlds.title: Courtyard pair connectivity
worlds.question: Which color pair lies in one and the same enclosed white chamber of the teal sheet: orange with purple, or green with pink? White areas connect only through shared edges; each dot counts as part of its surrounding white chamber, and diagonal corner contact does not connect chambers. Answer orange-purple or green-pink.

worlds.title: Local loop port order
worlds.question: Starting at the green port, follow the centerline of the compact closed loop clockwise. Which colored port—amber or violet—is encountered first? Use the loop order, not straight-line distance.

worlds.title: Ply span duel
worlds.question: The image shows two separate cords of the same dark teal ink, one in each of two far-apart corners of the picture, with clear background between them. Each cord is a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness folded into flat back-and-forth switchbacks: it never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself or the other cord. Exactly two small square beads are printed on each cord. One cord carries both orange beads and the other cord carries both purple beads; no cord carries beads of two colours. For each cord, measure the separation between its two beads by travelling along that cord's own ink from one bead to the other, following every fold; a straight jump across background, or across a neighbouring fold, is never a legal step. The two straight-line bead separations are deliberately built to be almost equal, so the straight-line gap tells you nothing: only the distances measured along the cords differ. Both cords must be inspected, since the answer is a comparison between them. All gray shapes anywhere in the image are decoration and mean nothing. Which bead pair is farther apart measured along its own cord? Answer orange or purple.

worlds.title: Dual trace terminal match
worlds.question: Trace the navy trail touching each green start. Do the two trails end at the same terminal color? Answer same or different.

worlds.title: Sandwiched checkpoint trace
worlds.question: Starting at the blue ring, follow the single dark route to the orange ring. Among the eight checkpoint dots, exactly one interior checkpoint is sandwiched between two checkpoints that match each other and have the opposite color. What color is that sandwiched checkpoint: red or green?

worlds.title: S curve port link
worlds.question: A pale field is split by three thick vertical walls into bands. A blue dot sits in the left band and a red dot in the right band. The band walls form an S-corridor in the pale field: the left wall and right wall leave a gap at the bottom, and the middle wall leaves a gap at the top if it is open. Trace the pale background and decide whether the blue dot can reach the red dot without crossing any dark wall. Are the two dots connected by the pale field? Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Counterfactual queue insertion
worlds.question: Move the gold-ringed card along the gold arrow into the gold INSERT gap, shifting later cards right. After the move, which color is in the cyan-bracketed slot? Answer red, blue, green, or violet.

worlds.title: Barred holder binding
worlds.question: The five cards on the left are badges, each carrying two coloured pips. The five cards on the right are holders, each carrying four coloured pips; count the holders 1 to 5 from the top. A badge fits a holder only if both of the badge's colours appear on that holder, and the order of the pips means nothing. A full arrangement puts every badge into a holder it fits, one badge in each holder, and several different full arrangements are possible here. One badge is marked by a black tag. The tagged badge fits three or more holders, and it really is placed in some of them by some full arrangement, but exactly one holder it fits is never given to it by any full arrangement. Which holder is that? Answer with exactly one of: holder-1, holder-2, holder-3, holder-4, holder-5.

worlds.title: Entailed balance invariant
worlds.question: The two top balances are exact, but they do not fix every symbol's weight. Which colored bottom equation must balance for every set of positive weights that fits both top rows? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Flip cancel stacks
worlds.question: Each stack reads TOP downward. Follow cards 1-8 in order. For A to B, move A's top tile onto B and flip it (dark to light or light to dark). If B's new top two tiles match, remove only that pair. Which final stack matches TARGET? Answer stack-A, stack-B, stack-C, or stack-D.

worlds.title: Track fraction correspondence
worlds.question: The top reference panel shows a gray horizontal track with one dark marker sitting on it at some position along the track. Below, three candidate panels A, B, C each show a gray horizontal track (of a possibly different length) with a colored marker. Compare each marker's position relative to its own track: one-quarter, one-half, or three-quarters of the way along. Which candidate's marker is at the same fractional position along its own track as the reference marker?

worlds.title: Cyclic landmark correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate ring, A or B, preserves the same clockwise cyclic order of the five colored landmarks as the REFERENCE ring? Rotation of a whole ring is allowed; reflection and swapping landmark identities are not. A is the left candidate and B is the right candidate. Ignore panel position and dot size. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Zoom window pointer binding
worlds.question: The wide horizontal strip is a tape of colored cells. The framed panel below it shows exactly three neighboring tape cells, in their original left-to-right order, reproduced at twice their size on the tape; nothing else was changed. Four triangles above the tape each point down at one cell. Every one of those four pointed cells has the same color as the middle cell of the framed panel, so the middle color alone cannot tell them apart; only one of the four pointed cells also has the framed panel's left color on its left and its right color on its right. Which triangle points at the middle cell of the framed panel? Answer with that triangle's color: orange, brown, teal, or navy.

worlds.title: Tagged polyomino rotation
worlds.question: The top row shows three pieces made from seven equal square tiles. Each piece has a colored tag directly below it. The bottom piece is exactly one top piece after rotation by a quarter-turn (90, 180, or 270 degrees); it is not reflected. Which tag color belongs to the matching top piece? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Network station correspondence
worlds.question: Both panels show the same seven-station network, but the station positions are rearranged. What fill color in the right panel belongs to the magenta-centered station in the left panel? Match stations using all connections. Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Steeper than reference
worlds.question: Three colored diagonal segments (red, blue, green) and one gray reference segment sit on a light panel, each in its own column. Count how many of the colored segments are STEEPER than the gray reference segment, where a segment is steeper if its tilt away from horizontal is greater than the gray segment's tilt (treating rising and falling tilts equally). Answer with only the number: 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Bubble threshold marker
worlds.question: Each bubble contains one visible marker shape: circle, square, triangle, or diamond. A bubble qualifies only when its center is strictly right of the vertical dashed threshold and strictly above the horizontal dashed threshold. Which marker shape belongs to the largest qualifying bubble? Answer circle, square, triangle, or diamond.

worlds.title: Earliest qualified peak
worlds.question: The picture is one chart panel crossed by nine pale vertical gridlines and by one black dashed horizontal line. Five traces run across the panel: one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one grey. The grey trace is a distractor and carries no information; ignore it completely. Every trace is a straight path from one gridline vertex to the next, so a trace's highest point is always one of its nine vertices. A coloured trace QUALIFIES when its highest vertex lies above the black dashed line; a coloured trace whose highest vertex lies below the dashed line does not qualify, no matter how far left or how high its other vertices are. Among the qualifying coloured traces only, take the one whose highest vertex sits furthest to the LEFT. In every picture at least two coloured traces qualify, no two coloured traces have their highest vertex on the same gridline, each coloured trace has exactly one highest vertex, and no vertex touches the dashed line. The colours, the drawing order and the left-hand starting heights carry no information; the answer need not be the tallest trace, need not be the trace whose highest vertex is furthest left overall, and the grey trace is never the answer. Which coloured trace has the leftmost highest vertex among the traces that qualify? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Paired composition gain
worlds.question: From composition A to composition B, which category gains the most percentage points? Each strip totals 100%. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Vector cross area leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order and share the same scale. Treat each colored segment from the gray origin to its endpoint dot as a vector. Compute the absolute 2D cross product |blue_x orange_y - blue_y orange_x|. Which panel's two vectors span the largest parallelogram area? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior bowling holes
worlds.question: This is a bowling ball seen from directly above. How many finger holes are punched in it? Count only the visible holes in the ball and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Arrow target alignment
worlds.question: Does the arrowhead point into the bullseye? Say yes when the bullseye's marked center lies between the two straight side edges of the arrowhead extended forward; otherwise say no.

worlds.title: Die center pip
worlds.question: This image shows one die face: a large rounded square with round pips on it. Four short grey ticks are drawn inward from the middle of each of the four edges of the square; they are fixed decoration and are drawn the same way in every image of this set. The centre point of the face is where the line joining the top and bottom ticks crosses the line joining the left and right ticks. Round pips of the same colour may also appear on the background outside the square; those never count. Judge only what is drawn inside the square, and do not use how many pips a real die shows or where a real die puts them. The centre point counts as covered when it lies inside one of the pips on the face, and uncovered when it lies on bare face colour. Is the centre point of the face covered by a pip? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Clock rim ticks
worlds.question: How many black tick marks are visible around the clock's rim? Count every black rim mark once; ignore the hands.

worlds.title: Sim cut corner conflict
worlds.question: Which corner of the visible SIM-card body is diagonally cut away? Judge the outer blue-green body, ignore the gold contacts, and answer top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right.

worlds.title: Separable backplane reveal
worlds.question: A separable brightness backplane runs across the field: each row and each column carries its own independent brightness offset, and these offsets swamp a coarse diagonal-band glyph. Remove that separable backplane by subtracting every row's mean and every column's mean. Which diagonal band is then revealed, the rising band A or the falling band B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Second difference triptych
worlds.question: Find the red, green, and blue corner-marked panels and order them by color. Compute (red plus blue) divided by two, minus green, at each corresponding grayscale pixel; add back the neutral gray level and ignore borders, colored marks, and fine carrier. Which broad symbol appears: ring, cross, arrow, or wave?

worlds.title: Legend expand reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows two framed panels. The blue-framed panel on the left is the legend: it has four rows, and each row prints one coloured square beside one small black stroke drawn inside a square area. The four strokes are always these four and no others: a bar (a horizontal stroke across the middle), a post (a vertical stroke down the middle), a back-slash (a diagonal stroke from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner) and a fore-slash (a diagonal stroke from the top-right corner to the bottom-left corner). The green-framed panel on the right is the plan: a grid of 4 rows and 4 columns of coloured squares, each square printed in one of the four legend colours. Build a board by replacing every plan square with the stroke that the legend pairs with that square's colour, keeping the plan's row and column positions, so the board is 4 rows by 4 columns of strokes. The board agrees with one of these five symbols in at least 13 of its 16 tiles. cross: the four tiles running from the top-left corner to the bottom-right corner are back-slashes and the four running from the top-right corner to the bottom-left corner are fore-slashes, so the strokes draw a large X, and the other eight tiles are bars. ladder: every tile of the leftmost column and of the rightmost column is a post and the eight tiles between them are bars, so the strokes draw two tall rails with rungs between them. pillar: every tile of the two middle columns is a post and the eight tiles of the outer columns are bars, so the strokes draw one broad upright column down the centre. chevron: the top row and the bottom row are all bars; in the second row the first tile is a back-slash and the fourth is a fore-slash, and in the third row the second tile is a back-slash and the third is a fore-slash, so the strokes draw a shallow V pointing down at the centre; the remaining tiles are bars. zigzag: the first and third rows have back-slashes in their two left tiles, the second and fourth rows have fore-slashes in their two right tiles, and the other eight tiles are bars, so the lean alternates from row to row. Which of the five symbols does the board match in the most tiles? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Edge code strip chain
worlds.question: Without rotating the seven green-framed strips, arrange them left to right so the cyan end-cap is on the outside left, the magenta end-cap is on the outside right, and every pair of touching inner edges has identical four-dot codes (filled dot = 1, hollow dot = 0, read top to bottom). Which symbol appears in the dark cells: plus, X, V, or T?

worlds.title: Half turn subtraction glyph
worlds.question: Inside the cyan frame, rotate a copy of the 11-by-11 tile mosaic by half a turn (180 degrees) about the gold center dot. Keep a result cell dark only when that cell is dark in the original and light in the rotated copy. Keep the original orientation. Which glyph appears: fork, hook, stair, or rake?

worlds.title: Border breach direction
worlds.question: A dark connected region fills part of the canvas and reaches out to run into exactly one border of the square canvas. It does not reach any of the other three borders. Which border does the region run into and break? Choose top, bottom, left, or right.

worlds.title: Barred path continuation
worlds.question: The same colored stroke appears on both sides of the opaque striped panel. Which color forms one smooth continuation behind the panel? Compare the whole path and answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Unpaired mirror dot
worlds.question: The picture shows seventeen identical dots on a plain background: thirteen are grey and exactly four are coloured red, orange, green and blue. Ignore the colours and look only at where the dots are. Exactly one straight line, which is not drawn anywhere in the picture, acts as a mirror for the whole arrangement: reflecting every dot across that line lands it on another dot, with a single exception. That one exception dot has no mirror partner, and it is always one of the four coloured dots. Which colour is the dot without a mirror partner? Answer red, orange, green or blue.

worlds.title: Constellation cycle count
worlds.question: Treat two black dots as linked when the distance between their centers is shorter than the gray scale bar. Every dot has exactly two links. Does the complete constellation form one closed ring or two separate closed rings? Answer one or two.

worlds.title: Affine lattice vacancy
worlds.question: The dark disks occupy 24 of the 25 intersections of one invisible 5-by-5 grid with straight, evenly spaced rows and columns. The grid may be rotated and slanted. Which colored hollow ring is centered at the one missing grid intersection? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Orientation match count
worlds.question: The reference bar in the box at the top of the image shows an orientation. The image is divided into a left and a right half, and each half holds several identical thin bars, each drawn at one of several orientations. A bar matches the reference when it leans in the same direction as (is parallel to) the reference bar. Which half, left or right, contains MORE bars matching the reference orientation? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Orientation consensus search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only bar whose centerline orientation differs from the other three bars in that panel? Treat bars as undirected lines and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Collinear dot lane
worlds.question: This image shows six framed rectangular panels of identical size, numbered 1 to 6 in reading order: panels 1, 2 and 3 are the top row from left to right, and panels 4, 5 and 6 are the bottom row from left to right. Every panel contains exactly five solid dots of the same single colour and the same size, so all six panels carry the same number of dots and the same amount of ink. In each panel the five dots form a lane running from one side of the panel towards the other at that panel's own arbitrary tilt, with irregular spacing between neighbouring dots, so neither the tilt of a lane, the gaps along it, its length, nor its place inside the panel carries any information. Exactly one panel is perfectly straight: the centres of all five of its dots lie on one single straight line. In each of the other five panels the lane is bent, because exactly one of its three inner dots is pushed sideways off the line of the rest, far enough that its centre misses the straight line through the rest of that lane by at least a third of a dot's width. No line is drawn in the image; only the dots and the panel frames are drawn, and straightness must be judged from the dot centres alone. Which numbered panel holds the perfectly straight lane of five dots? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5, panel-6.

worlds.title: Interior point search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has one teal dot strictly INSIDE the triangle formed by its other three teal dots? A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Colored adjacency match search
worlds.question: The reference and each card show five joined color pairs. Which labeled card has exactly the same five unordered color pairs as the reference? Pair order and left-to-right order within a pair do not matter. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State first region entry
worlds.question: Four panels read top to bottom. Every panel shows the same five slot columns and a shaded vertical band (the region) that always covers the middle column. Four tokens - one red, one green, one blue, one orange - sit in the slots, with exactly one token per occupied slot, and each token keeps its fixed color as it may move between panels. A token is inside the region when it is in the middle shaded column. Reading the panels top to bottom, which token is the FIRST to move from outside the region into the region? Answer 'red', 'green', 'blue', or 'orange'.

worlds.title: State transition echo
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P5 in order. Follow each labeled tile and count every directed state change between adjacent panels; ignore a tile when its state stays the same. Which directed state change occurs most often? Exactly one wins. Answer LOW->MID, LOW->HIGH, MID->LOW, MID->HIGH, HIGH->LOW, or HIGH->MID.

worlds.title: Ladder swap descent
worlds.question: The picture is a row of four square panels showing the same scene at four successive moments. Read the panels in order from left to right, as the grey arrow below them shows. Each panel contains five discs, and the five discs are the same five objects in every panel: an object moves only a short way from one panel to the next. Positions are read inside each panel, that is, relative to that panel's own frame, because every panel frames the same square scene. To follow an object from one panel to the next, take the disc in the next panel whose place inside its panel is nearest to the place the object had inside the previous panel; the picture is always drawn so that this nearest-place matching is unambiguous and pairs the five discs one to one. Colour does not follow an object: the five colours blue, green, orange, purple and yellow are dealt out afresh in every panel, so each panel shows each colour exactly once but an object may wear a different colour in every panel. A black ring is drawn in the first panel only, and it marks one object: the marked object is the one whose disc centre is nearest to the centre of that ring. The ring is drawn only in the first panel and never moves with the object. Which colour is the marked object wearing in the fourth panel, the rightmost one? Answer with one of blue, green, orange, purple or yellow.

worlds.title: Checkpoint lamp replay
worlds.question: The three lamps start as shown. Read the six cards from left to right. A SET card replaces the pictured lamp's state (solid means ON; hollow means OFF). SAVE remembers all three current states. RESTORE returns all three lamps to the most recently saved states. Is the ringed lamp ON or OFF at the end?

worlds.title: Dial program replay
worlds.question: The marked dial starts at one labeled position. Read the operation cards from left to right: an orange triangle advances one position clockwise, and a purple vertical bar reflects the position across the dial's vertical axis. Where does the marker finish? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Separating count
worlds.question: The image shows three closed black loops and two small colored dots: one green and one red. A loop is said to SEPARATE the two dots when exactly one of them lies inside the loop (the green dot is on one side and the red dot on the other). A loop does not separate them when both dots lie on the same side of it (both inside or both outside). Count how many of the closed black loops separate the green and red dots. Answer with a single number from 0, 1, or 2.

worlds.title: Maze reachability panels
worlds.question: Each of three black-framed maze panels has white walkable corridors and red and green markers. Moving only up, down, left, or right through non-black pixels, which panel lets green reach red: left, center, or right? Ignore frames and walls.

worlds.title: Wall neighbor duel
worlds.question: The picture shows one rectangular plate on white paper. Black walls divide the plate into regions; each region is a single connected area of one flat colour, and every wall inside the plate separates two different regions. Exactly one region is filled red and exactly one other region is filled blue; all remaining regions are white. Two regions count as NEIGHBOURS only if they are separated by a wall along a whole stretch of their border; regions that meet only where walls cross, at a single corner point, are NOT neighbours. The white paper outside the plate and the black walls themselves are not regions. Which shaded region has more neighbours: the red region, the blue region, or do they have the same number? Answer red, blue, or same.

worlds.title: Tile topology completion
