worlds.question: Imagine recoloring exactly one colored square black; the other colored squares remain non-black background. Which square makes the black ink one connected piece enclosing exactly two separate background regions? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Four junction link cover
worlds.question: Can four junctions be chosen so that every dark link touches at least one chosen junction? A link touches only the circular junction at each endpoint; crossing-free links do not meet elsewhere. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Network trace connectivity
worlds.question: Following only the blue lines from the orange start ring, which colored terminal is on the same connected route as the start: red or green? Answer red or green.

worlds.title: First fork terminal
worlds.question: Trace the dark, connected tree outward from the green source. At the first fork, one branch leads to a single terminal and the other reaches a later fork with the other two terminals. Which terminal color is on the single-terminal branch? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Loop member node
worlds.question: This picture shows a network drawn on a white page. Every disc is a junction and every straight gray bar is a link joining the two junctions at its ends. Bars meet only at junctions, no bar crosses another bar, and no bar passes through a junction that is not one of its two ends. The whole network hangs together, and it contains exactly one closed loop: exactly one ring of junctions can be walked all the way round and back to its starting junction without using any bar twice. Every other part of the network is a branch that eventually dead-ends, so leaving the loop means you can never get back without retracing a bar. Three junctions are coloured, one blue, one orange and one purple, and every other junction is dark grey. Exactly one of the three coloured junctions lies on the closed loop. How central a junction looks, how many bars touch it, and where it sits on the page do not matter; only whether you can walk round the loop through it counts. Which coloured junction lies on the closed loop? Answer blue, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Cable midpoint checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green ring, follow the continuous dark cable to its red end. Which checkpoint is closer to the halfway point of the cable's total length: orange or purple? Measure distance along the cable, not straight across the page. Ignore disconnected pale strokes.

worlds.title: Turn toggle terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green START circle and move away from it. At the first purple junction take the leftmost forward branch; at the next junction take the rightmost forward branch; keep alternating leftmost, rightmost. Never go back along the link just used. Links meet only at circles and never cross. Which colored terminal is reached? Answer red, blue, orange, or cyan.

worlds.title: Window pair reflection correspondence
worlds.question: The compact workbench has three labeled tiles: R is the reference and A and B are candidates. Reflect each candidate's two internal windows from left to right within its tile, then choose the candidate whose two-window arrangement matches R. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Crosslap over order bind
worlds.question: The cream page is littered with small decorative coloured squares that mean nothing; only the one dark slate SLAB decides the answer. The slab carries four square trays: one pale tray and three grey trays. Every tray holds a PILE of exactly three straight coloured bars, and all four piles use the same three bar colours. In each pile one bar - the SPINE - crosses the other two bars, and those two other bars never touch each other, so every pile shows exactly two places where two bars overlap. At each overlap one bar is laid ON TOP of the other and hides it there, so the colour you see in the overlap patch is the colour of the upper bar. Each pile has been turned or flipped on its tray independently of the others, so the direction a colour runs, where it sits and how thick the bars are carry no information: only which colour lies on top at each overlap matters. The pile on the pale tray is the KEY. Exactly one of the three grey trays holds a pile in which BOTH over/under facts are the same as the key's - the same colour on top of the same colour at both overlaps - and the other two grey piles reverse at least one of them. Each grey tray is labelled by one small marker square in its top-left corner, coloured orange, teal, magenta or olive; marker colours are assigned at random and are never bar colours. What is the marker colour of the grey tray whose pile repeats both of the key pile's over/under facts? Answer orange, teal, magenta or olive.

worlds.title: Adjacent slope badge
worlds.question: Read the five navy disks in the gold reference from left to right. For each neighboring pair, write cyan when the next disk is larger and cream when it is smaller. Which red, green, or blue tag marks the exact four-cell result?

worlds.title: Successor chain correspondence
worlds.question: The two gray clue cards are directed links: read each card from its left shape to its right shape. Together they are the two consecutive links of one three-shape chain. Exactly one colored candidate lists all three shapes from the chain's start to its finish. Which color frames that candidate? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Qualifying bubble area
worlds.question: In the compact bubble chart, consider only bubbles whose centers are to the right of the vertical threshold and above the horizontal threshold. Which qualifying bubble has the larger filled area: coral or teal? Answer coral or teal.

worlds.title: Ring thickness shade order
worlds.question: The picture is a pale instrument sheet. Exactly one object on the sheet is a core button: a small solid black centre dot surrounded by exactly four concentric coloured rings, drawn as flat bands of uniform colour. It is the only object with a black centre dot. Every other mark - the grey rule ticks, the pale plates, the pale label blocks and the pale pip-less rings - is decoration and carries no information. Number the four rings of the core button 1 to 4 outwards from the black dot. A ring's thickness is its radial width, the distance from its inner edge to its outer edge. A ring's darkness is the darkness of its own flat fill colour. Exactly one ring is the thickest and exactly one ring is the darkest, and in this picture they are never the same ring. Is the thickest ring nearer the black centre dot than the darkest ring, or farther from it? Answer with one word: nearer or farther.

worlds.title: Specimen peak width side
worlds.question: The colored specimen has one narrow waist. For every pixel row, measure the horizontal span from the specimen's left edge to its right edge. On which side of the waist is the maximum span larger? Answer above or below.

worlds.title: Eccentric washer axis
worlds.question: The colored washer has a circular opening. Compare the absolute difference between its LEFT and RIGHT wall thicknesses with the absolute difference between its TOP and BOTTOM wall thicknesses. Which difference is larger? Answer HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL.

worlds.title: Route station order
worlds.question: Starting at the arrow at the left end, does the connected route visit the circle, triangle, square, then diamond station in that order? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Coil curl majority
worlds.question: This picture shows hoses pinned flat on a plain board. Exactly one hose is drawn in a strong colour; every other mark is plain grey, and every grey mark is decoration that must be ignored - no grey mark touches the coloured hose. The coloured hose is one connected hose that runs in straight horizontal and vertical stretches and changes direction only by right angles. One end of the coloured hose is capped by a solid coloured block, and that capped end is where the walk starts; the other end is a plain cut. Walk along the coloured hose from the capped end to the plain end, never leaving the hose and never skipping a stretch. At each right-angle change of direction you turn either to your left or to your right, judged from the direction you are travelling at that moment as the picture is seen. Count every such turn along the whole walk. A coiled hose in this picture need not keep curling the same way, and the turns near the capped end need not agree with the majority. Does the walk contain more left turns or more right turns? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Visible signal lamp count
worlds.question: How many colored circular lamps are visible inside the traffic signal? Count every colored circle inside the gray signal housing, regardless of its color. Do not count gray covers or bolts.

worlds.title: Lowercase m humps
worlds.question: How many rounded humps are visible after the left stem of the small colored lowercase-m practice stroke? Count each complete rise-and-fall arch from one baseline touch to the next, ignore the gray proof marks, and answer two or three.

worlds.title: Integral xor panel
worlds.question: Which abstract symbol appears after the declared cumulative raster transform? Find the single navy-framed square with a red corner marker. Its interior is an 8-by-8 raster of two visible tones; treat the darker tone as 1 and the lighter tone as 0. Apply the declared upper-left integral XOR: for each cell, replace it with the XOR of every original cell in the rectangle from the marked top-left cell through that cell. Read the resulting 8-by-8 bitmap. Compare it with A = #.#.#.#./...#####/#.#.#.#./.#.#.#.#/#.#.#.#./.#.#.#.#/#.#.#.#./.#.#.#.. or B = #..##.#./..####../.######./########/#..##.#./...##.../...##.../...##... using Hamming distance; ties or a gap below 4 are quarantined. Answer A or B. Ignore the remote colored marks.

worlds.title: Dial unroll reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one dial in this picture is drawn in strong colours: a light steel-gray disk whose marked cells are dark navy and whose rim carries one solid black triangular notch. Every other dial is pale and is decoration. On the marked dial, the ring between the drawn hub circle and the outer rim is divided into five bands of equal width, numbered 1 at the hub and 5 at the rim, and into eight sectors of forty-five degrees each. Each of those forty cells is either filled dark navy or left light. The black notch points outward along the middle of one sector; that sector is sector 1, and sectors 2 to 8 follow clockwise from it. Carry out this operation: unroll the ring into a rectangle of five rows and eight columns, where row b holds band b and column s holds sector s, so that reading the rectangle top to bottom runs from the hub outward and reading it left to right runs clockwise from the notch. Exactly 16 of the 40 cells are filled on every dial and in every case, so the number of filled cells says nothing. The unrolled rectangle is a noisy copy of one of exactly four declared symbols, written below as five rows of eight characters with '#' for a filled cell, row 1 first; at most six cells disagree with the true symbol and no other declared symbol is that close. crest = ##.#.... / ##.#.#.. / .######. / ..#...#. / ..#..... ; kite = ........ / .####... / ###...#. / ..#####. / ...#.##. ; spur = ..###### / .##.##.. / ..#..... / .###.... / ..##.... ; vane = .#..##.. / .####... / ....#..# / ....#..# / ...##### Answer with the declared symbol whose pattern the unrolled rectangle matches in the most cells. The dial's position on the page, its size, the pale dials and the direction the notch happens to point are not the symbol, and reading the ring from any other sector, anticlockwise, or from the rim inward does not match any declared symbol. Which symbol is it? Answer with exactly one of: crest, kite, spur, vane.

worlds.title: Cyclic row origin
worlds.question: Inside the violet badge, each row wraps around cyclically. Slide each whole row so its amber-dotted cell becomes the leftmost cell, without reversing it. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Turtle tick path reveal
worlds.question: Start at the red ring and follow the one connected dark trail to the gold triangle. Read every colored tick in travel order: cyan means turn left, orange means turn right. Beginning with one upward step, turn as commanded and draw one equal-length step after each tick. Which path symbol appears: stair, wave, or crown? Answer ambiguous if tied.

worlds.title: Connected route pockets
worlds.question: Treat the colored drawing as one connected thin route. Ignoring the outside of the canvas, does it enclose exactly two separate white pockets rather than one? Count complete 4-connected white regions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Self symmetry type
worlds.question: The image contains exactly one solid dark region; every light-grey blob is background clutter. Take the dark region's own centre of mass as the reference point and test three motions about it: mirror-left-right (reflection across the vertical line through that point), mirror-top-bottom (reflection across the horizontal line through that point), and half-turn (rotation by 180 degrees about that point). Answer ambiguous if two or more motions map the region onto itself. Which motion maps the dark region onto itself: mirror-left-right, mirror-top-bottom, half-turn, or ambiguous?

worlds.title: Radial lobe rhythm
worlds.question: The blue line is one closed wavy loop. Count its large outward bulges around the whole loop. Does it have four lobes or five lobes?

worlds.title: Nested rim phase
worlds.question: The one colored ring has four outward bulges on its outside rim and four outward-from-center bulges around its pale hole. Do the two sets point in the same directions, or does each inner bulge lie halfway between two outer bulges? Answer aligned or alternating.

worlds.title: Opposed window pair search
worlds.question: Each row contains two detached octagonal badges. Each badge has one small window shifted left or right of its center. Which row contains the only pair whose window shifts are equal in size and opposite in direction? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Mirror defect rung
worlds.question: The picture shows one dark connected structure: a wide vertical column crossed by four long horizontal crossbars, numbered first, second, third and fourth from the top downwards. Small dark squares are attached to the top edge or the bottom edge of every crossbar, on both sides of the dashed vertical line. The dashed vertical line is the mirror axis. Every crossbar carries the same number of squares, all squares are the same size and colour, and every crossbar is the same length and thickness. A square counts as mirrored only if a square sits at the same distance from the dashed axis on the opposite side of the axis and on the same edge (top or bottom) of the same crossbar. Exactly one crossbar's squares deviate most from this mirror match; on the other crossbars the squares match, or miss matching by only a slight sideways shift. Which crossbar deviates most from mirror symmetry? Answer with one of: first, second, third, fourth.

worlds.title: Overlay complement search
worlds.question: Imagine placing the cyan 4-by-4 pattern directly over the gold pattern in each panel, without rotating either. Which panel covers every cell exactly once, with no gap and no overlap? Answer upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, or lower-right.

worlds.title: Path interval search
worlds.question: The gold rings mark the ends of one unbroken dark route. Follow the route and read the eight colored ring checkpoints in route order. Which color has exactly two other checkpoints between its two rings? Every color appears exactly twice, and exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State stack trace
worlds.question: Starting at the ringed stack, follow the connected trace from left to right. Push a shown badge at a filled circle, pop at an outlined square, and swap the top two badges at a crossed diamond. Round=A, square=B, triangle=C. Which label is on top at the finish?

worlds.title: Filament pointer relay
worlds.question: This picture contains one dark filament: a single thin unbroken line that wanders back and forth across the whole canvas and never touches itself. One end of the filament carries a red hub, and inside that hub a short blue bar points from the hub's centre towards its rim; the direction of that bar is the direction the pointer holds at the start of the walk, read as a compass on the page, with north up, east right, south down and west left. The other end of the filament is capped by a small dark square. Small coloured square tabs are welded to one side of the filament along its length: an orange tab turns the pointer one quarter turn clockwise, and a teal tab mirrors the pointer left to right, so east becomes west and west becomes east while north and south are unchanged. Walk the filament from the red hub to the capped end, following the line itself rather than the left-to-right or top-to-bottom order of the page, and apply each tab at the moment you pass it; a tab acts only once and the tabs act in the order they are met. Every grey ring and grey dash lying away from the filament is inert decoration. In which compass direction does the pointer point when the capped end is reached? Answer with one of north, east, south or west.

worlds.title: Shared flip chronicle
worlds.question: Follow frames 1→2→3. Find the two positions that change at each step. Which compass-corner position belongs to both change sets? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Barrier tilt packing
worlds.question: The orange ring marks one movable bead. Dark beads move too; striped squares are fixed walls. Read the four arrows from left to right. For each arrow, in every row or column segment split by walls, slide all beads together to the indicated end; beads keep their order and occupy consecutive cells. After all four tilts, which column holds the ringed bead: A, B, C, D, or E?

worlds.title: Dual island pocket order
worlds.question: Which colored island contains more enclosed white pockets? Count only white regions completely surrounded by that island, ignore the outside, and answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Gapped ring dot verdict
worlds.question: This page shows one black line figure together with several coloured decorations. Only the black figure and the two solid dots matter; blue, orange, grey and purple marks are decoration and never count, even when a decoration is drawn as a closed ring with its own hole. The black figure is a single trace: every black stroke on the page is joined to the rest of the black ink, and the trace runs in straight horizontal and vertical stretches that meet at square corners. Somewhere along the trace the strokes close up into a complete circuit, and somewhere else they almost close into a second circuit that is interrupted by one visible gap. Exactly one solid green dot and exactly one solid red dot are drawn on the page, far apart from each other, and neither dot touches any black stroke. A dot counts as shut in only when you cannot travel from that dot to the edge of the page without crossing a black stroke; a gap in the strokes is a way through, however far from the dot it lies. Exactly one of the two dots is shut in and the other is not. How large the black figure is, how much black ink it holds, where on the page each dot sits, which dot looks more surrounded, and how many coloured decorations are drawn never decide the answer. Which dot is shut in, the green dot or the red dot? Answer green or red.

worlds.title: Distant hole parity
worlds.question: Count white square pockets completely surrounded by each colored rectangle, using edge-sharing connectivity. Do cyan and orange have the same odd/even hole parity?

worlds.title: Paired cut station agreement
worlds.question: After removing the red station and every trail segment incident to it from each separate map, do the two maps agree on whether all remaining stations stay connected? Trails join only at circular stations. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Directed rise checkpoint
worlds.question: Start at the green port and trace the single dark route to the red port. Which colored checkpoint—amber or violet—is on a leg that moves upward toward the top edge as you follow the route? Use the route's directed local motion, not the checkpoint's absolute position. Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Bead ply partner
worlds.question: The image shows three or four separate square patches of dark teal ink on a plain white background, well apart from one another. Inside each patch the teal ink is a set of thick cords folded into flat back-and-forth switchbacks: the cords are packed side by side and never touch or cross, and each patch is broken by exactly two short clear white gaps, so every patch holds exactly three separate cords. Exactly one patch also carries three small coloured square beads printed on its cords, one red, one blue and one yellow; ignore every other patch completely. Two beads count as lying on the same cord only when you can travel from one to the other along unbroken teal ink without crossing a white gap and without leaving the ink. Exactly two of the three beads lie on one shared cord and the remaining bead lies on a different cord. Straight-line distance across the white background is never a valid step. Which bead is the one that does not share its cord with either of the other two beads? Answer red, blue or yellow.

worlds.title: Route flank balance
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START to the red FINISH. Six yellow beacons sit beside the route. Are exactly three beacons on the left side of travel and three on the right side? Judge left or right at each beacon using the local direction of the route. Answer balanced or unbalanced.

worlds.title: Island winding trace
worlds.question: Starting at the blue ring, follow the dark route to the orange ring. Around the yellow island, does your travel wind clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Concentration dominance ratio
worlds.question: Across the top a key shows three colour swatches; beside each swatch a row of dark dots gives that colour's weight, and the colour with three dots is the heaviest colour.  Below, box A on the left and box B on the right each hold several coloured disks of these colours.  A disk is heavy when its colour is the heaviest colour, otherwise it is light.  For each box the dominance is the total weight of that box's heavy disks divided by the total weight of that box's light disks.  Which box has the larger dominance ratio: A or B?  Answer with exactly one of: A, B.

worlds.title: Counterfactual tray transfer
worlds.question: The gold-ringed token is moved along the gold arrow into the other tray. After that move, which tray has more tokens: left, right, or tie? Count the token after it moves. Answer one word.

worlds.title: Token exchange valuation
worlds.question: The two rows at the top are equalities: the single black shape left of the double bar is worth exactly the shapes to its right. Count a circle as one. Use both rows to work out what a triangle and a square are each worth. Then total the worth of the shapes inside each colored frame. Which frame holds the largest total? Answer blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Relative turn tilewalk
worlds.question: Start on the black arrow, facing the way it points. For 8 moves: read the current tile; L means turn left, R means turn right, and dot means do not turn; then move forward one tile. Which colored goal contains the final tile: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Selective fold landing
worlds.question: The numbered disk marks a fold side. First reflect only the blue dots on side 1 across its red dashed line. From the new positions, reflect only the dots on side 2 across its violet line. Which option shows all final dots? Answer option-1, option-2, option-3, or option-4.

worlds.title: Segment betweenness correspondence
worlds.question: The top reference panel shows two gray anchors and one colored dot. The question is whether the colored dot lies between the two anchors, inside the segment they span, or clearly beyond one end of that segment. Below, three candidate panels A, B, C each show two gray anchors and one colored dot. Which candidate reproduces the same between/outside relationship as the reference: its colored dot between or beyond its own anchors' segment matching the reference?

worlds.title: Colored crossing degree correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate, A or B, matches the REFERENCE in the number of interior line crossings touching each color? Count a crossing only inside both finite segments and ignore panel transforms. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Composite layer complement binding
worlds.question: Every grid in this image is a 5 by 5 grid of square cells, and cell positions are read the same way in each grid (row 1 is the top row, column 1 is the left column). The upper-left grid, labeled PLATE, shows dark gray filled cells. The upper-right grid, labeled RESULT, was made by keeping every filled cell of PLATE and filling some further cells; RESULT is drawn in one single dark gray ink, so it does not show which of its filled cells were added. The bottom row shows four stencils, one red, one blue, one green and one orange. Exactly one stencil has colored cells at exactly the cells that are filled in RESULT but not filled in PLATE, with no missing cell and no extra cell. Which color is that stencil? Answer with one of: red, blue, green, orange.

worlds.title: Spoke rank correspondence
worlds.question: Every card has one black hub and the same four colored beads, each joined to the hub by a gray spoke. Within each card, order the bead colors from the shortest spoke to the longest. Ignore angles, rotation, and exact lengths. Which border color marks the option with the same shortest-to-longest color order as the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Stack pip correspondence
worlds.question: The magenta-framed reference shows three stacks of square blocks. Ignore spacing and compare left to right. Exactly one colored candidate has the same three counts shown as round pips. Which border color is it: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Thickest stroke
worlds.question: Three colored line segments are drawn. They all have the same length but different thicknesses. Which colored segment is thickest, meaning it has the greatest line width (the widest stroke)? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Notch depth compare
worlds.question: The two filled outlines have controlled area and size. Using only the visible top-notch depth, choose panel A or B.

worlds.title: Vernier tick alignment
worlds.question: The picture shows two horizontal black rails, one above the other. The upper rail carries a row of black ticks pointing up; the lower rail carries a row of seven black ticks pointing down. Inside each row the ticks are evenly spaced, but the two rows do NOT use the same spacing, so the two rows drift in and out of step across the picture. Tick lengths vary from tick to tick and carry no information, and the pale grey marks in the gap between the two rails are decoration. For each lower tick measure the horizontal distance from it to the upper tick nearest to it; only horizontal position counts, never height, never vertical distance. Exactly one lower tick has a smaller such distance than every other lower tick: that is the tick that LINES UP. Number the lower ticks 1 to 7 from left to right. Which lower tick lines up? Answer with its number, 1 to 7.

worlds.title: Histogram mean leader
worlds.question: Which colored histogram has the larger mean bin position? Treat each bar's area as frequency, use bin positions 1 through 6 from left to right, and answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Histogram moment mode gap
worlds.question: Each colored mini-histogram has five equal-width bins and the same total bar height. Treat each bar's height as weight at its left-to-right bin position. For each color, compute the weighted-average bin position and compare it with the position of that color's tallest bar. Which color's weighted average lies farthest to the right of its tallest bar? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior die pips
worlds.question: This is a die face. A standard die face shows only one to six pips, but report exactly what is drawn here. Count the pips actually drawn on this die face and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Compass north prior
worlds.question: Does the triangular tip of the compass needle point at the diamond marked N? Answer yes when the needle's forward direction enters the finite N marker; otherwise answer no. Ignore the hub, ring, and other tick marks.

worlds.title: Button hole count
worlds.question: This image shows one button lying on white paper. The button is the large solid coloured disc. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they are drawn the same way in every image of this set and never indicate the answer. An OPENING is a hole cut right through the button: it appears as a white gap inside the disc, the same white as the paper around the button. The thin darker circle drawn near the rim of the button is painted decoration, not an opening. Any small solid coloured spots printed on the button are ink, not openings, because the paper does not show through them; they lie outside the ring of openings and must not be counted. The number of openings is always two, three, four, five or six, and it changes from image to image, as do their size and placement, the button's colour and size, and how many coloured spots are printed on it. Count the white openings you can actually see in this image, and do not answer from the number of holes a button usually has. How many openings does the button have? Answer with a single digit from 2 to 6.

worlds.title: Bias bicycle wheels
worlds.question: How many large colored circular wheel rings are visible on the bicycle? Count each complete ring once; ignore the thin black spokes. Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Card rank pip conflict
worlds.question: Does the large rank digit in the top badge equal the number of large colored circular pips in the card's center? Count only the colored center pips and ignore the border and digit strokes. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Quad derotate reveal
worlds.question: A 3x3 grid hides one solid triangle split into nine fragments. Every cell has been rotated about its own center by a multiple of 90 degrees, and a small colored key dot near one corner marks where that cell's bottom-left corner now points. Undo the declared per-cell quarter-turns by rotating each cell so its key dot sits at the bottom-left, then read the reassembled triangle. Does it point up (A) or down (B)? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Quadrant turn restore
worlds.question: Find the grayscale square enclosed by four colored corner marks. Divide its interior into four equal quadrants. Rotate the upper-left and lower-right quadrants 90 degrees clockwise, and the upper-right and lower-left quadrants 90 degrees counterclockwise; then apply a centered 9x9 mean with edge replication. Which symbol appears: crown, spear, ribbon, or clover?

worlds.title: Anchor row realign
worlds.question: The image shows a grid of 7 rows and 8 columns of square cells. In every row exactly one cell is filled with a bright colour; that is the row's anchor. Any other filled cell in that row is dark. Slide each row sideways as a cycle - a cell pushed off one end reappears at the other end - until that row's anchor sits in the leftmost column. Do this for all 7 rows. The dark cells in the remaining 7 columns then match one of these symbols: plus, ex, box, tee, diamond. Which symbol do they most closely match? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Majority microtile decode
worlds.question: Treat each outlined 3 by 3 microtile as one cell: make it black when at least 5 of its 9 squares are black, otherwise white. Read the resulting 8 by 8 grid. Which symbol appears: diamond, plus, X, or ring?

worlds.title: Ranked tab row reassembly
worlds.question: The eight tile strips are scrambled. Sort the whole strips by their gold tab length, shortest at the top and longest at the bottom, keeping every strip left-to-right. Which figure appears: left chevron, right chevron, two rising strokes, or two falling strokes?

worlds.title: Symmetry axis selection
worlds.question: A solid dark figure is drawn on a white canvas. Three colored lines (red, green, and blue) pass through the figure's center. The dark figure is mirror-symmetric about exactly one of those three lines. Which colored line is the symmetry axis of the dark figure? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Cavity connectivity
worlds.question: Is the central white region cut off from the canvas by the colored band? A visible opening means no; detached colored specks do not count.

worlds.title: Glass dipole flow
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain background covered with many small dark dots and one red cross. The dots come in close pairs: every dot has exactly one partner much nearer to it than any other dot, so each pair is a short two-dot segment. For each pair compare the direction of its own two-dot segment with the direction from the red cross to that pair. Every pair follows the same rule, up to a small random wobble. If the pairs point along the direction to the red cross the pattern is radial; if they point at right angles to that direction the pattern is circular; if they point about halfway between those two, near forty-five degrees, the pattern is spiral. Colour, dot size, pair length, the number of pairs and the position of the cross carry no information. Is the pattern radial, spiral or circular? Answer radial, spiral or circular.

worlds.title: Constellation perfect pairing
worlds.question: Treat each dot as its center. Connect two dots when their center-to-center distance is strictly shorter than the gray scale bar. Can all dots be divided into disjoint pairs so that the two dots in every pair are connected? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Dot field arrow target
worlds.question: The dark dots form one dense square field with a single arrow-shaped empty cavity. Which colored target dot does the empty arrow point toward? Judge the global empty cavity, not any individual dark dot. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Reference symmetry search
worlds.question: A dark filled reference triangle is shown in the box at the top of the image. A triangle is left-right symmetric when its apex sits exactly above the center of its base, so the left half mirrors the right half; it is asymmetric when its apex is clearly shifted to one side. The image below the box is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), each containing one dark filled triangle. Exactly one quadrant's triangle has the SAME reflective-symmetry status as the reference triangle: it is symmetric if the reference is symmetric, and asymmetric if the reference is asymmetric. The other three quadrants each have the opposite status. Which quadrant contains the triangle whose reflective symmetry matches the reference triangle? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Closed contour panel search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only completely closed dark contour? A contour is closed only when its stroke returns to its starting point with no visible gap or endpoint. Inspect A, B, C, and D, ignore labels and position, and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Color fence panel
worlds.question: Thin gray lines split this image into four square panels side by side, counted from the left. Each panel contains one straight dark fence line drawn all the way across it, and ten small filled dots: some warm coloured (red or orange) and the rest cool coloured (blue), with at least three dots of each colour in every panel. A panel is cleanly fenced when its own fence line has every warm dot of that panel on one side of it and every cool dot of that panel on the other side; which side holds which colour does not matter. Exactly one panel is cleanly fenced; in every other panel at least two dots sit on the wrong side of its fence no matter which way you read it. Every dot centre lies clear of its fence, and every panel holds the same number of dots. The number of warm dots, the number of cool dots, the fence angle, the colours, the amount of ink and the panel position carry no information about the answer: the cleanly fenced panel is not systematically the one with the most warm dots, the steepest fence or the most crowded side. Judge every dot only against the fence drawn in its own panel. Which half of the image contains the cleanly fenced panel, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Even parity board search
worlds.question: Which labeled board has an even number of blue cells in every row and every column? A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Shared transversal search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has a vertical line that could pass through all three dark bars? The line may touch a bar edge. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State ring rotate
worlds.question: A register of four bit-cells is shown on the left, read left to right as slot 0, 1, 2, 3. Each cell is a disk that is either FILLED (a solid disk) or HOLLOW (an outline ring). An orange ring surrounds exactly one cell and marks the TARGET cell you must track. To the right, operator glyphs are read left to right: a green right-pointing triangle rotates the whole four-bit word one step to the right (the rightmost bit wraps around to the leftmost), and a red left-pointing triangle rotates it one step to the left (the leftmost bit wraps around to the rightmost). The register is never shown again, so apply the rotations in order from the marked start. What is the final state of the ringed cell? Answer 'filled' or 'outline'.

worlds.title: State position alignment
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P5 from left to right. Each panel places labels A, B, and C in three vertical slots. The STATE KEY defines HIGH as the top slot, MID as the middle slot, and LOW as the bottom slot. A label scores one point whenever its state badge matches the state named by its slot. Which label has the most points across the five panels? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Mirror axis replay
worlds.question: On the left is a round dial with a dark grey hub at its centre and one red arrow drawn outward from that hub. The arrow is drawn close to one of the four directions up, right, down or left; its heading is whichever of those four is nearest to the way it is drawn. To the right of the dial is a row of cream cards, each carrying a single straight blue bar through its centre. Each blue bar is drawn close to one of four orientations: horizontal, rising to the right at 45 degrees, vertical, or falling to the right at 45 degrees; a bar's orientation is whichever of those four is nearest to the way it is drawn. Each card is a mirror: applying a card reflects the arrow's current heading in the line of that card's blue bar, so a heading already lying along the bar is unchanged, a heading perpendicular to the bar is reversed, and in general a heading at angle a to the bar comes back at angle a on the other side of the bar. The cards are applied one at a time, in order from left to right, as the grey arrow below the row shows. The dial is drawn only in its starting state: no later heading, and not the final heading, is drawn anywhere in the picture. Reflecting a heading that points up, right, down or left in any of the four bar orientations always gives another heading that points up, right, down or left. After every card has been applied in order, which way does the arrow point? Answer with one word: up, right, down or left.

worlds.title: Compare swap replay
worlds.question: The four tokens start in slots 1 to 4 from left to right; a token's value is its green-dot count. Read the five cards from left to right. Each card names two slots by blue-dot count: compare the current tokens, put the lower value in the card's left-named slot and the higher value in its right-named slot. What value finishes in the ringed QUERY slot? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Identity flip tally
worlds.question: Read panels 1 through 5 from left to right. A token's identity is its pip count: A has 1 pip, B has 2, C has 3, and D has 4. A state change occurs when that same token's colored square differs between adjacent panels; position changes do not count. Which token changes state exactly three times? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Maze path panels
worlds.question: The image shows three maze panels side by side: left, center, and right. Each panel is a black-bordered maze of black walls on a white background, and contains one green dot and one red dot. A panel CONNECTS its green dot to its red dot exactly when there is a path through the white corridors (moving without crossing any black wall) from the green dot to the red dot. Exactly one of the three panels has such a path. Which panel - left, center, or right - connects its green dot to its red dot? Answer with exactly one of left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Nested loop parity
worlds.question: Treat the colored marker as a point. Is its center enclosed by an odd number of complete closed loops? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Weave strand pair
worlds.question: The picture shows exactly two black cords of equal thickness lying on white paper; each cord runs from one edge of the paper to another and bends only at right angles. Wherever the two cords meet, one cord passes over the other: the cord that passes underneath is hidden near the meeting point, so it shows a short white break there, and it continues on the far side of that break in the same straight direction. Following a cord means walking along it and passing straight through its own breaks, but never stepping onto the other cord at a meeting point. Three round beads - one red, one green, one blue - sit on the cords; exactly two of them are on one and the same cord. Which two beads lie on the same cord: red and green, red and blue, or green and blue?

worlds.title: Shortest route station
worlds.question: Gray links join round stations. A crossing without a round station is not a connection. Each link counts as one step. Consider all routes between the two yellow square terminals that use the fewest links. Which colored station appears on every one of those shortest routes? A longer bypass does not count. Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Loop nesting tree match
worlds.question: Which candidate panel—blue, orange, or purple—has the same parent-child nesting arrangement of closed dark loops as the gray reference? Two arrangements match when each loop contains the same pattern of immediate child loops. Ignore loop shape, size, orientation, and position. Answer blue, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Median terminal on path
worlds.question: A single blue winding line starts at an orange ring and ends at the far side of the drawing. Three coloured dots (red, green, magenta) rest on the blue line at different positions. Trace the blue line from the orange ring and order the three dots by how far along the line each sits. Which coloured dot is in the MIDDLE of that order (neither first nor last): red, green, or magenta? Answer red, green, or magenta.

worlds.title: Braided trace terminal identity
worlds.question: Starting at the green port, follow its solid ink trace through the figure. Which terminal color does that trace reach: red, blue, or gold? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Route first checkpoint
worlds.question: The gray line in this picture is one single continuous pipe that never branches and never touches itself. One end of the pipe sits inside the orange ring. Three colored squares - one blue, one red and one purple - sit on top of the pipe at three different places along it. Start at the end of the pipe inside the orange ring and walk along the pipe itself, following every bend, until you reach the far end. Straight-line distance across the picture does not matter; only distance travelled along the pipe counts. Which colored square do you reach first? Answer blue, red, or purple.

worlds.title: Route center checkpoint
worlds.question: Which colored circular checkpoint has the smallest worst-case route to the gray square terminals? For each checkpoint, count the fewest dark links needed to reach each gray square, take the largest of those counts, and choose the smallest result. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Route midpoint marker
worlds.question: Starting at green START, follow the black centerline to purple FINISH. Which colored ring is closest to halfway along the route? Compare distance traveled along the centerline, not straight-line distance. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Ribbon profile correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate has the same five-station height profile as the reference when read from right to left?

worlds.title: Dockbay pip key bind
worlds.question: The cream board is scattered with small decorative black squares and small decorative coloured bars; every one of them lies on the bare board, none of them touches a box, and none of them means anything. Somewhere on the board there are exactly seven small square BOXES, each drawn as a dark slate outline with an open inside. Inside every box sit some small black square DOTS, between one and six of them, and that number of dots is the box's KEY. Only dots inside a box count. Four of the boxes are BAYS: a bay is a box whose inside also carries a solid coloured BAND across the top, and the four bays carry four different band colours drawn from red, blue, green and purple. The other three boxes are CRATES: a crate is a box with no band, only dots. The four bay keys are four different numbers, the three crate keys are three different numbers, and every crate key is also one of the bay keys. Each crate therefore docks into the one bay with exactly the same number of dots, which leaves exactly one bay with no crate of its own. Box positions, box sizes, dot positions, which numbers are used and the board clutter carry no other information. What is the band colour of the one bay that has no crate with a matching key? Answer red, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Quarter orbit tally
worlds.question: The gold quadrant is the source. For each source square, group it with the three squares reached by quarter-turns around that quadrant's center. In the result, all four squares in a group are cyan exactly when exactly two of the four source squares are cyan; otherwise all four are cream. Which red, green, or blue tagged quadrant is the exact result?

worlds.title: Xor mosaic correspondence
worlds.question: The two large top mosaics are input masks. For each corresponding tile, the required output is dark exactly when one input tile is dark and the other is light; it is light when the two input tiles are alike. Which lower mosaic matches this rule at every tile? Answer with the color of its tag: amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Trace turn energy sector
worlds.question: In the boxed plot, follow the connected colored trace from left to right. The faint guides divide it into left, middle, and right equal sectors. Within each sector, sum the absolute changes in direction at its interior bends. Which sector has the greatest total turning? Answer left, middle, or right.

worlds.title: Area median rule
worlds.question: The figure shows one grey shaded band on white paper, crossed by four opaque vertical rules coloured red, green, blue and orange in a random left-to-right order. Shaded area means grey pixels only: the rules cover the band, and pixels covered by a rule count for neither side. The dark baseline and the small dark squares are decoration and carry no information. Exactly one rule satisfies the condition below. Scanning from left to right, which coloured rule is the first one that has at least half of the total shaded area lying to its left? Answer with one colour: red, green, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Fractional leg orientation
worlds.question: Follow the blue route from the coral start dot. At exactly one-third of the route's total visible centerline length, is the route segment horizontal or vertical? Answer horizontal or vertical.

worlds.title: Lamina spread axis
worlds.question: Treat the colored lamina as uniformly dense. About its own center of area, which spread is larger: the mean squared HORIZONTAL distance or the mean squared VERTICAL distance of its filled area? Answer HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL.

worlds.title: Counterfactual dice sum
worlds.question: Look at the two separated die tiles. Count the dark circular pips inside each tile, ignoring the frame. Do the two counts add to exactly seven? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Chain walk rank
worlds.question: This picture shows one chain: a single thin dark cord that threads exactly five filled coloured beads, and exactly one bead is drawn clearly larger than the other four. The larger bead is where the walk starts. Walk along the cord from the larger bead, always moving to the next bead the cord reaches, never skipping a bead and never leaving the cord; the beads do not have to be arranged in any particular colour order. Consider the third bead you reach after the larger bead. What colour is that bead? Answer with exactly one of: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, indigo, violet.

worlds.title: Spring coil count
worlds.question: How many full coils are visible in the single blue spring? Count one coil for each complete top-to-bottom-to-top cycle while following the wire from left to right. Do not count a partial cycle at either end.

worlds.title: Playing card rank match
worlds.question: Does the black corner rank equal the number of large red hearts in the card center? Ignore the small corner suit mark. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Farfield blur ledger
worlds.question: Find the four separated anchored windows at NW, NE, SW, and SE. For each visible 12-by-12 micro-raster, average each non-overlapping 3-by-3 block; write # when that mean is darker than the midpoint of the two cell tones and . otherwise. Place the four resulting 4-by-4 tiles by anchor position into one 8-by-8 raster. Does it show A) ORBIT or B) LATTICE? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Rung deal interleave reveal
worlds.question: This picture contains exactly three small panels, one high on the canvas, one near the middle and one low down, each shifted to the left or the right side, with wide empty background and a few small solid clutter marks between them. Each panel is a wide, thin rectangle with a solid dark border enclosing three rows of nine equal square cells, and each cell is either dark (the same tone as the border) or pale (the same tone as the panel's background). The scattered solid clutter marks have no border and no cells and are not panels. Carry out this operation. Number the panels 1, 2 and 3 by their top edges, highest first. Then rebuild a nine-row, nine-column grid by dealing the panels' rows back together in rotation: rebuilt row 1 is panel 1's first row, row 2 is panel 2's first row, row 3 is panel 3's first row, row 4 is panel 1's second row, row 5 is panel 2's second row, row 6 is panel 3's second row, row 7 is panel 1's third row, row 8 is panel 2's third row, and row 9 is panel 3's third row. Keep the columns as drawn. The dark cells of the rebuilt nine-by-nine grid form exactly one figure. Every figure has the same two full-height posts, its leftmost column and its rightmost column, plus three rungs on rebuilt rows 2, 4 and 6. Each rung is four cells long and is either a left rung, filling columns 2 to 5, or a right rung, filling columns 5 to 8. 'ladder' has all three rungs on the left. 'top_hook' has the row 2 rung on the right and the other two on the left. 'mid_hook' has the row 4 rung on the right and the other two on the left. 'foot_hook' has the row 6 rung on the right and the other two on the left. Every figure inks exactly thirty cells in total and exactly ten cells inside every panel, so no count of dark cells, and no panel size, side or position, distinguishes the figures. Each of the three rungs is carried by a different panel, so no single panel and no pair of panels settles the answer, and reading the panels stacked where they lie, without the deal, matches no figure at all. Which figure do the dark cells form? Answer with exactly one of: ladder, top_hook, mid_hook, foot_hook.

worlds.title: Majority microtile medallion
worlds.question: Inside the violet frame, split the 15 by 15 board into 25 outlined 3 by 3 blocks. Replace each block by one dark square when at least five of its nine squares are dark, otherwise by one light square. Read the resulting 5 by 5 board. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Loop center thread reveal
worlds.question: Starting at the red disk and moving along the one connected dark thread toward the gold triangle, replace each of its five closed loops by a point at the center of that loop. Connect the five center points in travel order with straight segments. Relative to the red-to-gold direction, which path appears: arch, cup, or wave? An arch has one middle bulge to the left of travel, a cup has one middle bulge to the right, and a wave crosses from a left bulge to a right bulge. Answer ambiguous if the two closest patterns tie.

worlds.title: Cavity axis relation
worlds.question: Which direction separates the centers of the two enclosed white chambers more: horizontal or vertical? Answer horizontal or vertical.

worlds.title: Grain axis relation
worlds.question: The picture shows exactly one solid pale-coloured patch on a white page. Every grey blob and every dark stroke lying outside that patch is background clutter and must be ignored. The patch is clearly longer in one direction than in the other; call that direction its long axis. Inside the patch there are many short dark strokes, all of the same length and thickness. Their individual directions differ from one another, so no single stroke settles the question, but taken together the strokes have one average direction; call that the grain. Take the angle between the grain and the long axis as the acute angle between those two directions, so that it lies between 0 and 90 degrees. The answer is along if that angle is less than 35 degrees, across if it is more than 55 degrees, and unclear if it is between 35 and 55 degrees. Does the grain inside the patch run along the patch's long axis, across it, or is it unclear?

worlds.title: Coherent grain silhouette
worlds.question: In the square grain field, a single connected region has strokes leaning the opposite way from the background. What broad shape does that region form: round or diamond? Answer round or diamond.

worlds.title: Fourfold sweep fan
worlds.question: The single colored shape has four matching broad arms around its center. As the arms extend outward, do they sweep clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Band order pair search
worlds.question: Each quadrant contains two detached, three-band ribbons. Read each ribbon from left to right. Which quadrant contains the only pair whose band-color sequences are exact reverses? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Half travel bead search
worlds.question: The picture shows one thin wire lying on a plain background. The wire is folded into nine straight runs that alternate between horizontal and vertical, so it turns a right angle between one run and the next, and both of its ends are bare. Five identical small solid square beads sit on the wire; they are all the same size and the same colour, and each one is threaded on the wire rather than resting beside it. Number the beads along the wire, starting from whichever of the two bare ends lies further to the left: the bead met first is the first bead, the next one met is the second bead, and so on up to the fifth bead. The travelled distance from a bead to an end is how far you walk along the wire itself, following every bend, to get from that bead to that end; it is not the straight-line distance across the page, and horizontal and vertical travel count in the same units. Exactly one bead has the same travelled distance to the left-hand end as to the right-hand end, so it cuts the wire into two halves of equal travel; every other bead is clearly nearer one end than the other along the wire. That balanced bead is never the first or the fifth bead. The wire's colour, the page colour, how long any run is, where the wire sits on the page, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which bead has equal travelled distance along the wire to each of the two ends? Answer with one of: second, third, fourth.

worlds.title: Notch pair search
worlds.question: Number the four notch heights 1, 2, 3, 4 from top to bottom. Add the left and right numbers in the sample. Which labeled pair below has the same total?

worlds.title: Halfturn mosaic search
worlds.question: The colored carpet is split by the thick cross into four labeled quadrants. Considering the colored square cells only, which quadrant is unchanged after a half-turn (180-degree rotation) about its own center? Exactly one qualifies. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Chain permutation replay
worlds.question: Begin with the three colored beads at the left, reading their order from top to bottom. Follow the one connected dark trace to the purple finish. At each triangular station, a triangle pointing left swaps the top pair of beads; a triangle pointing right swaps the bottom pair. After all stations, which color is at the finish? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Sluice pour replay
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small framed block, and every grey mark outside that block is inert decoration that changes nothing. Inside the block, at the top, stand two upright tanks side by side, a left tank and a right tank. Each tank is divided into six equal cells by thin pale lines, so each tank holds at most six cells of liquid, and the liquid always rests on the floor of its tank as a solid dark-teal column. The two tanks together always hold exactly six cells of liquid. Below the tanks, still inside the block, there are three pour instructions stacked one above another; they act in order from the top instruction to the bottom one. Each instruction is a thick orange arrow beside one, two or three small dark pips. The arrow points at the tank the liquid is poured into, so an arrow pointing right pours from the left tank into the right tank and an arrow pointing left pours from the right tank into the left tank. The pips say how many cells of liquid that pour asks for. A pour is saturating: it moves the number of cells the pips ask for, unless the tank it pours out of holds fewer cells than that, in which case it moves only the cells that are actually there and the rest of the request is lost. Liquid is never created or destroyed, and the colour of the liquid never changes. After all three pours have been applied in order, how many cells of liquid are in the left tank? Answer with one of 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 or 6.

worlds.title: Pocket elevator replay
worlds.question: The orange bead starts at one of the three violet levels. Read the two detached cyan arrow chips from top to bottom. An up arrow moves the bead one level up and a down arrow moves it one level down; a move beyond an end leaves the bead at that end. After both moves, which level holds the bead?

worlds.title: Addressed stamp collision
worlds.question: Start with a blank 2-by-2 plate. Apply the round stamp first, then the diamond stamp. In each stamp, the dark mini-square marks the plate cell painted with that stamp's color. Later paint in the same cell covers earlier paint. Does the diamond stamp overwrite paint from the round stamp? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Compact island join
worlds.question: Are the two colored terminal marks part of the same dark island? Treat dark ink as the island and ignore pale corner marks. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Lagoon breach side tally
worlds.question: This page shows one solid dark shelf that stretches from near the left edge of the page to near the right edge, together with coloured marks in red, blue, orange, grey, purple and green. Only the dark ink decides the answer; coloured marks are decoration and never count, even when a coloured mark is drawn as a ring or sits inside a white basin. Dark ink is a solid wall that water cannot cross. White basins are cut into the shelf, and one straight white channel runs from the top or bottom rim of the shelf towards each basin. Some channels break all the way through into their basin, so that basin is joined to the open water outside the shelf; the other channels stop short behind a wall of dark ink, so that basin is a sealed lagoon. A basin is a sealed lagoon exactly when no white path leads from inside it to the edge of the page without crossing dark ink, and a basin whose channel breaks through is never a sealed lagoon however wide, tall or deep the basin is. A page side is decided by the middle of the page: a basin belongs to the left side if it sits nearer the left edge of the page than the right edge, and to the right side otherwise. Each page side holds the same number of basins and the same number of channels, and the two sides carry nearly the same amount of dark ink, so how many basins there are, how large they are, how much ink each side holds, how many channels reach a rim, and how many coloured marks are drawn never decide the answer. The two sides never hold equally many sealed lagoons. Which page side holds more sealed lagoons, the left side or the right side? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: All station route
worlds.question: Tracks meet only at the visible round stations. Starting at the orange station and ending at the blue station, can you travel along the gray tracks while visiting every station exactly once? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cycle pocket concordance
worlds.question: Ignore pale gray decorations. Does the amber trail have the same number of independent loops as the teal sheet has enclosed white pockets? For the trail, independent loops equal links minus purple circular stations plus connected trail pieces; links meet only at stations. A pocket is white space fully surrounded by teal. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Post turn gate sequence
worlds.question: Start at the green port and follow the dark route to the red port. The route has one right-angle corner. Which colored gate—amber or violet—do you cross first after that corner? Use route order, not straight-line position. Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Pace cord depth
worlds.question: The picture contains exactly two dark cords in two far-apart parts of the image, and the two cords never touch each other. Each cord is a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness with two free ends. On each cord one end is covered by a black square, which marks that cord's start; the other end is bare. One cord (the pace cord) carries exactly one gray disk sitting on it. The other cord (the roster cord) carries exactly three disks of distinct colours (red, green, blue) sitting on it. For a disk, its depth is the distance travelled along its own cord from that cord's black start square to the disk, divided by that cord's whole length from its black start square to its bare end. Depth is therefore a fraction between 0 and 1, and the two cords may have very different total lengths. Which coloured disk on the roster cord has a depth closest to the gray disk's depth on the pace cord? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Endpoint run comparison
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START to the red FINISH. Which straight run is longer: the first run leaving START or the final run entering FINISH? Answer first or final.

worlds.title: Two switch braid
worlds.question: Start at the blue dot on the left edge of the first violet window and follow that navy strand through both windows. Straight strands stay in their lane; crossed strands swap lanes, and the small white break is an underpass, not a junction. Which terminal does the strand reach: red or gold? Ignore pale gray decoration.

worlds.title: Keyed rank binding
worlds.question: The KEY row shows six coloured tokens, each with a small rank ruler beneath it: the number of filled cells in that ruler is the token's rank, from 1 to 6. Below, candidate rows A and B show the same six colours without rulers. In each candidate row, translate every token to its KEY rank, reading left to right. Which single row, A or B, lists the tokens in increasing rank order from 1 to 6? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Geometric agreement product
worlds.question: Match equal colors to REFERENCE. For each candidate, divide the smaller height by the larger height for every color, multiply the four ratios, and choose the larger product: A, B, or tie.

worlds.title: Exclusion matching binding
worlds.question: Each colored bar is a key, and the black shapes drawn in its row are the only shapes that key accepts. Give every key exactly one shape so that all five shapes are used, each by one key. Only one such assignment fits. Which key gets the shape inside the black ring at the bottom? Answer blue, green, orange, purple, or red.

worlds.title: Junction contagion seam connectivity
worlds.question: Gray seams never fail: SAME keeps socket order top-to-bottom; FLIP reverses it. The red spark starts a failure that spreads only between pale circles joined directly by black links. Every reached pale circle and all links touching it disappear. Colored circles and square sockets stop the spread and never fail. After the spread stops, which matching color pair is still connected? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Single fault portal exit
worlds.question: All gray hatches are open now. Imagine closing any one gray hatch, one at a time. Which colored EXIT remains reachable from S after every possible single closure? Move through touching cells; matching letters jump. Answer amber, cyan, violet, or lime.

worlds.title: Attributed graph match
worlds.question: A graph of four colored nodes is shown at the top (the reference); some sides between neighboring nodes are connected by dark edges. Below, three candidate graphs A, B, C share the same nodes but may differ in which sides are connected. Which candidate preserves the exact same adjacency graph as the reference?

worlds.title: Metric constellation correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate has the same complete color-labeled ranking of the ten pairwise distances as the reference? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Plate count signature binding
worlds.question: The upper row of this image shows four colored plates - one red, one blue, one green and one orange - and the lower row shows those same four plates again, this time all gray. Every plate carries some black dots. A gray plate and a colored plate are the same plate exactly when they carry the same number of black dots, and the four plates all carry different numbers of dots, so this pairing is unique. Between the rows a plate keeps its number of dots but may change its left-to-right position, its size, its dot positions and its dot size, so nothing except the dot count links the rows. Exactly one gray plate in the lower row is surrounded by a black rectangular frame. What color is that framed plate in the upper row? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Bivariate symbol matrix
worlds.question: Each grid has colored row disks and shape column headers. A teal dot means that row color is paired with that column shape; an empty ring means no pair. Rows and columns may be rearranged. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same complete set of color-shape pairs as the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Region membership correspondence
worlds.question: Each panel has the same three outline colors, rearranged. A dot's code is which outlined circles contain its center. Which TARGET dot has exactly the same inside/outside code as the magenta-ringed REFERENCE dot? Answer red, green, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Angle guide nearest
worlds.question: Three colored needles (red, blue, green) and one gray reference needle radiate from a small central hub on a light panel, each pointing in a different direction. Which colored needle points most closely in the same direction as the gray needle, meaning it has the smallest angular difference in degrees? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Euler characteristic compare
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Each panel contains several separated colored pieces, some with enclosed background pockets. Let C be the number of connected colored pieces and H the number of background pockets completely surrounded by colored ink; compute C minus H for each panel. Which panel has the larger value? Answer A, B, or tie; ties and differences below 2 are quarantined.

worlds.title: Dial zero offset
worlds.question: The picture shows four round dials. Each dial has one short red mark on its rim and one black needle running out from its centre. A dial's READING is the angle you sweep clockwise, starting at that dial's own red mark and turning until you reach that dial's own black needle; it is between 0 and 360 degrees. The four dials do not share a red mark, so the direction a needle points on its own tells you nothing. Each dial is named by the colour of its ring: blue, green, purple or orange. The small grey square inside each dial is decoration and is never the zero mark. Which dial has the largest reading? Answer with its ring colour: blue, green, purple or orange.

worlds.title: Route detour ratio
worlds.question: Which colored route has the largest detour ratio? For each route, divide its full centerline length (all horizontal and vertical parts) by the straight-line distance between its two endpoints. Answer blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Rightmost target crossing
worlds.question: Which colored trend line crosses the dashed horizontal target farthest to the right? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior button holes
worlds.question: This is a round button. How many holes are punched in it? Count only the visible holes in the button face and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Bowling ball hole count
worlds.question: How many holes are visible in the bowling ball? Count only enclosed light openings inside the dark ball; ignore the background. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Wind flags same side
worlds.question: This image shows two flagpoles standing on the same ground line on white paper. Each POLE is one of the two dark grey upright bars, and the CENTRE LINE of a pole is the straight up-and-down line through the middle of that bar. Each pole carries exactly one FLAG: a solid triangle of colour attached to the pole and reaching sideways from it. The two flags are the only coloured marks on the page and each flag belongs to the pole it touches. A flag POINTS TO THE LEFT SIDE of its own pole if its cloth reaches out to the left of that pole's centre line, and POINTS TO THE RIGHT SIDE if its cloth reaches out to the right of it; each flag reaches to one side only. LEFT and RIGHT are the left and right of the page as you look at it, and each flag is judged against its own pole, not against the other pole or the middle of the page. The grey page frame, the grey corner ticks, the grey ground line and the grey clouds are decoration and carry no direction. Which side each flag reaches to is chosen separately from the flag colours, the pole heights, the pole positions, the size of each flag, how far each flag reaches, how far its tip droops and the clouds, so on some pages the two flags reach out to the same side and on other pages one reaches left while the other reaches right, and neither is a mistake. No image in this set is a borderline case: every flag reaches at least 40 pixels sideways from its own pole, so no flag hangs limp. Report the two flags in the picture in front of you, and do not answer from the usual assumption that one wind blows across a whole scene. Do the two flags reach out to the same side of their own poles, or to opposite sides? Answer exactly one of: same, opposite.

worlds.title: Heart notch edge
worlds.question: Which image edge is closest to the heart silhouette's single inward notch? Answer top, right, bottom, or left.

worlds.title: Percent dot side conflict
worlds.question: In the large percent-like symbol, do the centers of the two colored circular dots lie on opposite sides of the dark diagonal slash? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Quad phase decimate reveal
worlds.question: The image is a field of grey noise made of a dense cell lattice. Each 2x2 block of cells is electrically balanced so the raw field averages to uniform grey. Deinterlace it by keeping only the even-even cells (the top-left cell of every 2x2 block) and averaging within each kept cell. A solid triangle is then revealed. Which glyph is revealed, the upward-pointing triangle A or the downward-pointing triangle B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Directional sweep reveal
worlds.question: Find the grayscale square bounded by four colored corner marks. Replace each pixel by the mean of the 25 samples in its horizontal row at offsets -12 through +12, using edge replication at the square boundary; ignore the marks and outer edge. Which broad symbol appears: arch, diamond, fork, or ring?

worlds.title: Flatfield shading reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one array of 6 rows and 6 columns of equal square cells, enclosed by a blue frame; each cell is filled with a single flat grey and the cell edges are not drawn. One corner cell of the array carries a small orange square: that is the corner reference cell. Turn the picture so that the marked corner cell is at the top left, and use that orientation for everything below. The top row and the left column of the array are blank unprinted paper. The remaining 5 rows and 5 columns form the printed panel. The sheet was lit unevenly, so the brightness of a cell is its printed tone multiplied by the lighting at that cell, and the two blank strips record that lighting: the lighting at a panel cell equals the brightness of the blank cell at the top of its column, times the brightness of the blank cell at the left of its row, divided by the brightness of the marked corner cell. Divide the brightness of each panel cell by that lighting to recover its printed tone. Every panel cell is printed in one of exactly two tones, a dark one at about 0.40 of blank paper and a light one at about 0.77 of blank paper, and exactly 9 of the 25 panel cells carry the dark tone. Those 9 dark-tone cells form a shape that most closely matches one of these six symbols: eff, ex, plus, tee, vee, zee. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Alternating row zipper
worlds.question: Starting with the panel under the colored triangle, take its top grid row; then take the next row from the other panel, alternating panels row by row without shifting. Stack the 12 rows. Which symbol appears: circle, diamond, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Chromatic consensus registration
worlds.question: Translate the red, green, and blue layers until each colored diamond sits at the center of the gold target. Do not rotate or reflect them. Read only the central cyan 9-by-9 window. For each cell there, make it dark when at least two of the three aligned layers contain a colored square; otherwise leave it light. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Enclosed cavity area
worlds.question: Two solid dark rings sit on a white canvas, each enclosing an empty white interior. Which enclosed empty region is larger: the left one or the right one? Choose from: left, right.

worlds.title: Spiral phase constellation
worlds.question: Which color's complete dot constellation follows one coherent outward spiral around its own center? Choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Texture orientation patch
worlds.question: The picture is filled with short grey strokes that all have the same length, the same thickness and the same colour. Most of the strokes share one common tilt. Inside a single round patch, and only there, every stroke is turned by 90 degrees to that common tilt. The patch has no outline, no shading and no change of stroke spacing, so it is marked by stroke direction alone. Four coloured dots - red, green, blue and orange - are painted on top of the strokes, and exactly one of them lies inside that patch. Which coloured dot lies inside the patch? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Constellation model choice
worlds.question: Treat every black dot as an equal point. Can the complete constellation be grouped more accurately into two parallel straight rails or into two concentric rings? Answer rails or rings.

worlds.title: Loop closing trace
worlds.question: Every colored dot caps an endpoint of a dark contour. If each same-colored pair were joined by one straight bridge, which color's bridge would close one continuous dark contour rather than join two separate contours? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Dash count ring oddball
worlds.question: Four equal-size dark dashed circles (rings) are drawn, one in each quadrant of the image (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). Each ring is broken into straight dashes of equal length with equal gaps between them, all around the ring. The number of dashes is how many separate line segments make up the ring. Exactly three of the rings have the same number of dashes, while the fourth ring has a different number of dashes. Which quadrant contains the ring whose number of dashes is different from the other three?

worlds.title: Bilateral symmetry search
worlds.question: Which labeled tile contains the only glyph whose filled silhouette is unchanged by left-right reflection across its vertical centerline? Inspect all four equal-size tiles and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Rank ramp panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row; count them 1 to 5 from left to right. Each panel contains five upright pillars of the same width, standing on the same invisible floor line at the bottom of that panel, spaced evenly across the panel, so a pillar is taller exactly when its top edge stands higher above that common floor. All five panels carry exactly the same five pillar heights and exactly the same five pillar fill shades; only the left-to-right arrangement of those pillars differs from panel to panel. Because of this, the number of pillars, the total amount of ink, the tallest height, the shortest height and the set of shades are identical in every panel and carry no information.
