The fill shade of a pillar is decoration only: two of the five panels happen to have their shades running steadily from dark to light or from light to dark across the panel, and that shading has nothing to do with the answer, which depends on pillar height alone. In exactly one panel the pillars get taller at every step from left to right, so each pillar is taller than the pillar immediately to its left. In each of the other four panels that run is broken at least once: somewhere in the row a pillar is shorter than the pillar immediately to its left, and every such drop, as well as every rise in the ascending panel, is at least seventeen pixels, so no comparison is a close call. Which numbered panel has its five pillars increasing in height at every step from left to right? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Rook permutation search
worlds.question: Which labeled board has exactly one blue dot in every row and exactly one blue dot in every column? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Mirror pair search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel is perfectly mirror-symmetric across its red vertical line? A dark square is paired only with a dark square in the same row at the same distance on the opposite side. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State balance returns
worlds.question: A running balance register starts at 0, marked by the 'start = 0' panel on the far left. Six operator panels run left to right as step 1 through step 6. In each panel a solid green up-triangle means add 1 (+1) and a solid red down-triangle means subtract 1 (-1). Apply the six steps in order, keeping a running balance that starts at 0. A step is a RETURN to the origin when, after applying it, the running balance is exactly 0 again (the starting 0 before any step does not count as a return). How many of the six steps bring the running balance exactly back to 0 ? Answer '0', '1', '2', or '3'.

worlds.title: State derangement checkpoint
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 from left to right. The ID KEY maps circle=A, triangle=B, square=C, and diamond=D. The STATE KEY maps the three swatch colors to LOW, MID, or HIGH. A later panel is a state derangement of P1 when every identity has a different state than in P1, while the total counts of LOW, MID, and HIGH are unchanged. Which later panel is the first state derangement? Answer P2, P3, P4, P5, or P6.

worlds.title: Grid line ops
worlds.question: On the left is a 4 by 4 grid of square cells. Each cell starts either dark blue (filled) or light grey (empty), exactly as drawn. One cell is marked by a red ring: the marked cell is the cell whose centre is nearest to the centre of that red ring. On the right is a row of cream cards. Each card carries a small 4 by 4 diagram laid out the same way as the big grid, its top row matching the big grid's top row and its left column matching the big grid's left column, and in each card exactly one whole row or one whole column of that small diagram is coloured. A green line means: fill every cell of the corresponding row or column of the big grid, so each of those cells becomes dark blue whatever it was before. A magenta line means: flip every cell of that row or column, so each dark cell becomes light and each light cell becomes dark. The cards are applied to the big grid one at a time, in order from left to right, as the arrow below them shows. Cards whose line is a different row or column leave the marked cell unchanged. The grid after the cards have been applied is not drawn anywhere. After every card has been applied in order, is the marked cell dark blue or light grey? Answer with one word: filled or empty.

worlds.title: Edge fold replay
worlds.question: The four colored tiles start left to right as shown. Read the three FOLD cards from left to right. The orange dot marks which outer edge to fold inward: move that entire outer stack onto its neighbor, flipping the stack so its layer order reverses. What color is on top after all three folds?

worlds.title: Paired inventory depletion
worlds.question: Three colored inventories start with the bead counts shown. Read the six cards from left to right. A card removes one bead of each pictured color only if both colors still have at least one bead; otherwise that card does nothing. How many beads of the red-ringed color remain? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Enclosure depth compare
worlds.question: Count for each colored dot how many of the concentric closed black loops surround it completely. The dot that passes inside more loops is the one farther from the picture edge and closer to the shared center of the rings. Which colored dot, green or red, is enclosed by more of the closed loops? Answer with exactly green or red.

worlds.title: Region hole selection
worlds.question: Exactly one colored region contains exactly one enclosed background hole. Which color is it? Count only blank components completely surrounded by that colored region; ignore open indentations and the outside background.

worlds.title: Door merge pick
worlds.question: The picture shows a white rectangular plate ruled into square rooms by thick black walls. Wherever a wall between two neighbouring rooms is missing, those two rooms are already joined and you can walk straight from one into the other; where a wall is drawn, you cannot. Walking from room to room through the missing walls, in as many steps as you like, joins the rooms into larger apartments, and the outer rim of the plate is walled all the way round. Three of the drawn walls each carry one shut door, painted as a short coloured bar across the wall - one orange, one purple and one teal. A shut door blocks the way just like the rest of the wall. Opening one door would cut a doorway through that one piece of wall only, joining whatever is on its two sides. One green dot and one red dot are painted flat on the floor, and they are not in the same apartment. Exactly one of the three doors, if it were opened, would make it possible to walk from the green dot to the red dot. Which door is it - orange, purple or teal?

worlds.title: Chamber seal escape
worlds.question: White space is open floor; black walls and colored seals block movement. Imagine removing exactly one colored seal, turning all of its pixels into white floor. Which seal then lets the yellow dot reach the outer white area touching the image border without crossing any wall or other seal? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Marked junction articulation
worlds.question: If the orange junction and every dark link touching it were removed, would the remaining colored junctions split into two or more connected pieces? Dark links connect only at visible circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Reachable terminal count
worlds.question: Following only the blue lines from the orange start ring (not jumping any white gap), how many of the two colored dots -- red and green -- are reachable? Answer 0, 1, or 2.

worlds.title: Signed turn trace majority
worlds.question: Starting at the green port, follow the solid dark trace to the red terminal. At each purple ringed corner, which kind of turn occurs more often as you travel: left or right? Count only ringed corners and ignore pale strokes and the endpoint markers. Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Hub removal pieces
worlds.question: This picture shows a network drawn on a white page. Every dark disc is a junction and every straight gray bar is a link joining the two junctions at its ends. Bars meet only at junctions, no bar crosses another bar, and no bar passes through a junction that is not one of its two ends. As drawn, the whole network hangs together: from any junction you can reach any other junction by travelling along bars. Exactly one junction is circled by a black ring, and exactly four bars touch that ringed junction. Now imagine rubbing out the ringed junction together with all four bars that touch it, and leaving every other junction and every other bar exactly as it is drawn. Two of the remaining junctions are in the same piece when you can still travel from one to the other along remaining bars; a remaining junction that is left with no bar at all is a piece on its own. How near two junctions look on the page does not matter, only what the bars still join. The rest of the network breaks into 1, 2 or 3 pieces. After the ringed junction and its four bars are rubbed out, how many separate pieces does the rest of the network fall into? Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: First merge junction
worlds.question: Start at the green and red circles. Follow each one's unique dark route toward the yellow diamond. Which colored circular junction do the two routes reach first in common? Dark lines meet only at circular junctions. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Palindrome route terminal
worlds.question: Each panel shows one unbranched black chain from a green START disk to a colored terminal. Read the five purple checkpoint shapes along the chain. Which terminal has a palindrome—the same shape sequence forward and backward? Links meet only at markers and never cross. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Crossing window correspondence
worlds.question: The navy thread is one connected trace through R, A, and B. Rotate each candidate field 180 degrees, then choose the candidate whose four-window self-crossing signature matches R.

worlds.title: Twinview glyph fuse
worlds.question: The cream board carries six square tiles that never touch each other, plus small pale decorative squares lying on the bare board that mean nothing. Every tile is a 5 by 5 grid of cells inside a thick coloured frame. A cell is either FILLED, showing a small dark square, or EMPTY, showing plain white, or COVERED, showing a flat grey block that hides the whole cell. Exactly two tiles wear the same dark slate-grey frame: these are the two VIEWS, and they sit at opposite corners of the board, far apart. Both views show the very same hidden 5 by 5 pattern, cell for cell, in the same orientation, without any rotation or reflection; the only difference between them is which cells their grey covers hide. The two views never cover the same cell, so a cell hidden in one view is always shown in the other, and putting the two views together reveals the whole hidden pattern. The other four tiles are the CANDIDATES. Each candidate wears a frame in a different colour taken from red, orange, green, teal, blue and purple, and no candidate has any grey cover: all twenty-five of its cells are visible. Exactly one candidate matches the hidden pattern in every one of its twenty-five cells. Every candidate has exactly the same number of filled cells, so the amount of dark ink, the number of filled cells, the frame colour, the tile size and the tile position tell you nothing about which one is right. Each wrong candidate was made from the hidden pattern by turning some filled cells empty and the same number of empty cells filled. At least one wrong candidate agrees with everything the first view shows, and at least one wrong candidate agrees with everything the second view shows, so reading only one view can never decide the answer: you must combine what both distant views reveal and then compare that fused pattern with the four candidates. Which candidate matches the hidden pattern? Give the colour of that candidate's frame. Answer red, orange, green, teal, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Split seal pair
worlds.question: The top two detached tiles are the reference pair. A candidate pair matches only when the same quarter-turn rotation, with no reflection or swapping, makes both of its tiles match the reference. Which colored dot labels the matching pair? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Transpose stamp correspondence
worlds.question: The black-bordered mini-grid is the reference. Swap its rows and columns: the cell at row r, column c moves to row c, column r. Exactly one colored-bordered mini-grid is the result. Which border color marks it? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Diagonal switch binding
worlds.question: Which colored sample is below the diagonal in panel P but above it in panel Q? Each panel has one amber, one teal, and one violet sample; the left card is P and the right card is Q. Answer amber, teal, or violet.

worlds.title: Pivot moment duel
worlds.question: A pale sheet shows a long grey horizontal beam. One black triangle above the beam points down at a single place on it; that place is the pivot. Two stacks of identical small solid squares hang below the beam, one navy and one crimson, one on each side of the pivot. For each of those two stacks take the number of squares it contains and multiply it by the horizontal distance from the pivot to the middle of that stack's column. Olive squares, orange rings, orange bars and the grey ticks along the bottom edge are decoration and are never counted or measured. Which colour's stack gives the larger product, navy or crimson?

worlds.title: Interval endpoint overlap
worlds.question: Do the top coral interval and bottom blue interval share any horizontal values? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Trace chord crossing count
worlds.question: Imagine the straight chord joining the colored mini-trace's two endpoints. Excluding the endpoints, how many times does the trace cross that chord? Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Checkerboard column count
worlds.question: How many columns of alternating tiles are in the single compact checkerboard? Count the tile columns from the left border to the right border; ignore the loose colored marks outside it. Answer with a whole number.

worlds.title: Zip tooth doubles
worlds.question: This picture shows a scattered mending kit on a plain white background. Exactly one item is drawn in a strong colour: a single zipper, drawn as one straight coloured tape with short coloured teeth attached along it. Every other mark is plain grey - including grey zippers with teeth of their own - and every grey mark is decoration that must be ignored; no grey mark touches or overlaps the coloured zipper. Each tooth of the coloured zipper is attached to the tape and sticks out from exactly one side of it. Walk along the coloured tape from one end to the other and look at each pair of teeth that are neighbours along the tape, with no other tooth between them. Call such a pair a same-side pair when both of its teeth stick out from the same side of the tape. The teeth in this picture may follow any pattern of sides, and the answer is the same whichever end of the tape you start from. How many same-side pairs does the coloured zipper have? Answer with exactly one of: 0, 1, 2, 3.

worlds.title: Mirrored c aperture side
worlds.question: Which side is the thick C-shaped ring open on? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Usb branch join order
worlds.question: Starting at the arrowhead and following the colored USB trunk toward its round base, which side branch joins the trunk first—left or right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Parity weave reveal
worlds.question: Inside the single dark-framed patch, use its small colored corner notch to orient the raster. The interior is a 16-row by 16-column grid of solid cells. List cells with (row+column) even in row-major order and separately list cells with (row+column) odd in row-major order; pair item k from the first list with item k from the second. For every pair write # if the two cell colors differ, and . if they match. Place the 128 results row-by-row into an 8-row by 16-column bitmap and compare it with A. Ignore the frame and every mark outside the patch. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Slot refill reveal
worlds.question: This picture contains exactly one large square panel with a solid dark border, exactly three much narrower upright slats that also have solid dark borders, and a few tiny dark specks on the background that are decoration only. The panel's border encloses a seven-by-seven grid of forty-nine equal square cells, that is seven columns of seven cells each. Four of those columns are drawn as bars: in such a column the lowest cells are dark, in the same tone as the border, and the cells above them are pale, in the same tone as the panel's background, so the column shows a solid bar standing on the panel's bottom edge whose height is a whole number of cells from 1 to 7. The other three columns are empty slots: all seven of their cells are filled with a single intermediate tone, neither the dark bar tone nor the pale background tone, and those three empty slots are either the three leftmost columns or the three rightmost columns of the panel. Each of the three narrow slats encloses one single column of seven cells, drawn at the same cell size as the panel and carrying one bar of its own, standing on the slat's bottom edge, in the same two tones. The three slats are the missing columns of the panel. Carry out this operation. Take the three slats in top-to-bottom order of their positions in the picture, take the panel's three empty slots in left-to-right order, and put the topmost slat's bar into the leftmost empty slot, the middle slat's bar into the middle empty slot, and the bottommost slat's bar into the rightmost empty slot, each bar keeping its own height and standing on the panel's bottom edge. The panel now has seven bars, and their seven heights, read left to right, form exactly one of these four symbols. 'ramp' is heights 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7. 'crest' is heights 1, 2, 3, 4, 7, 6, 5. 'basin' is heights 3, 2, 1, 4, 5, 6, 7. 'switchback' is heights 3, 2, 1, 4, 7, 6, 5. Whichever symbol is present, the seven bar heights are always the seven values 1 to 7 in some order, the middle column is always the height-4 bar, the three left columns always carry the heights 1, 2 and 3 in one order or the other, and the three right columns always carry the heights 5, 6 and 7 in one order or the other. So the total amount of dark ink, the set of bar heights, the panel's size, position and colour, the slats' sizes and colours, and the number of specks are the same whichever symbol is present. The four bars left in the panel fix only the order of one of the two triples, and the three loose slats fix only the order of the other triple, so both the panel and all three slats are needed and neither the panel alone nor the slats alone can decide between two of the four symbols. Which symbol do the seven bars form once the slats have been put back into the empty slots? Answer with exactly one of: basin, crest, ramp, switchback.

worlds.title: Binary panel addition
worlds.question: Treat each 7 by 7 panel as a 49-bit binary number: read rows left-to-right and top-to-bottom, with the top-left square most significant; dark is 1 and light is 0. Add the left and right numbers, discard any overflow beyond 49 bits, and write the 49 result bits back in the same order. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Endpoint weave reveal
worlds.question: Each framed card has four rows. On every row, fill all seven-cell positions from the left dark peg through the right dark peg. Starting at each triangular top notch, read downward; weave the eight reconstructed rows cyan, gold, cyan, gold. Which filled silhouette needs the fewest cell changes to match: hourglass, diamond, or stair? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Compact turn signature
worlds.question: Imagine rotating the whole compact filled emblem about its center. Which rotation gives the smaller whole-shape mismatch: a half-turn (180 degrees) or a third-turn (120 degrees)? Answer half-turn or third-turn.

worlds.title: Bead trail net turn
worlds.question: The page shows exactly one trail of small dark beads. All dark marks belong to that single trail; every pale grey mark is clutter and must be ignored. One end of the trail is a filled dark square and the other end is a larger dark round blob. Walk along the trail bead by bead, starting at the square end and finishing at the round end. At each bead the walk turns; count a turn that bends counter-clockwise on the page as positive degrees and a turn that bends clockwise as negative degrees, and add up every turn of the whole walk. Individual stretches turn both ways, so only the total over the entire trail decides the answer. Is the total counter-clockwise or clockwise? Answer counterclockwise or clockwise.

worlds.title: Percolating void axis
worlds.question: The landmass contains exactly 112 equal square tiles joined edge-to-edge, including one yellow tile. If the yellow tile is removed, does the remaining blue landmass stay connected or split into two pieces? Answer stay or split.

worlds.title: Phase reversal silhouette
worlds.question: A reversed patch in the fine checker texture reveals one hidden silhouette. Is its boundary round or four-sided? Answer round or four-sided.

worlds.title: Bilateral aperture search
worlds.question: Which sector contains the only lobe whose two enclosed white windows have equal widths? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Taper route monotone search
worlds.question: The picture shows four solid horizontal ribbons, one above the other, numbered first, second, third and fourth from the top downwards. Each ribbon is a single connected band whose centre line wobbles gently and whose thickness, meaning its vertical height inside one column of pixels, changes along the ribbon from its left end to its right end. All four ribbons have the same length, the same total area of ink, the same thickness at their left end and the same thickness at their right end, and all four use exactly the same collection of thickness values; only the order in which those thicknesses occur along the ribbon differs. Read each ribbon from its left end to its right end. Exactly one ribbon never thickens again: at every point its thickness is no greater than every thickness already seen earlier in that same ribbon. Each of the other three ribbons has two separate interior stretches where it grows back thicker than it was before, and then thins again. Ribbon colour, ribbon length, ribbon position and total ink carry no information. Which ribbon thins steadily and never grows back thicker than it has already been? Answer with one of: first, second, third, fourth.

worlds.title: Equal area island search
worlds.question: Each card contains one cyan island and one amber island. Which card has equal visible area in its two islands? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Chain center search
worlds.question: The two gold disks are the ends of one unbroken jointed chain. Each straight dark connector between neighboring disks counts as one link. Which colored joint has the same number of links to both gold ends? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State transition peak
worlds.question: Read the five numbered snapshots from left to right. Each snapshot contains the same four labeled rows A-D, and each cell contains either a circle or a diamond state glyph. A state change means the glyph shape changes between neighboring snapshots; glyph color is irrelevant. Count the changes for each row. Which row has the greatest number of state changes?

worlds.title: Quota drain race
worlds.question: Two bordered boards appear here, one on the left and one taller and narrower on the right, with a wide stretch of empty backdrop between them; faint grey shapes lying beyond both borders belong to the backdrop and should be ignored entirely. The left board is an allowance sheet of four rows. A row shows a large disc of one colour, and beside it, to its right, a group of one, two or three small dark dots. Each of the four rows uses a different colour, and the dot group tells you that colour's allowance: the number of parcels of that colour that must still be handed in. Only how many dots there are counts; how they are laid out does not, and neither does which row happens to be printed above which. The right board is a chute. Thin dark rules divide it into twelve compartments in a single column, and every compartment holds one smaller disc. The compartment at the very top holds the parcel that is handed in first, the one below it the parcel handed in second, and so on down to the bottom compartment, which is handed in last. Hand the parcels in one by one in that order. Every parcel handed in reduces the allowance of its own colour by exactly one, and a colour's allowance is used up at the instant the number of its parcels handed in so far first equals its printed dot count. The chute always contains three parcels of each of the four colours and no allowance exceeds three, so all four allowances do get used up in the end; parcels are handed in one at a time, so one colour necessarily gets there before any other. The boards are not pinned to fixed spots, and the four colours in use are always teal, violet, orange and moss. Whose allowance is used up first? Answer with one of teal, violet, orange or moss.

worlds.title: Addressed lamp ribbon
worlds.question: Start with lamps A and B both OFF and A active. Follow the connected ribbon from the round START to the arrow. Each cyan span flips the active lamp; each coral span switches which lamp is active. After all eight spans, what is the (A,B) pattern: 00, 01, 10, or 11?

worlds.title: Conditional pip rewrite
worlds.question: The round badge shows the starting state as one, two, or three pips. Apply the square badge first, then the diamond badge. In each rule badge, the pips left of the divider are the match state and the pips right of the divider are the replacement: replace the current state only when it matches the left group; otherwise keep it. After both rules, is the state one, two, or three?

worlds.title: Trace checkpoint order
worlds.question: Starting at the green start dot and following the one dark trace, which checkpoint is reached first: orange or violet? Answer orange or violet.

worlds.title: Shut bead pocket tally
worlds.question: This page shows black slabs, grey decoration and small coloured beads. Only black ink is a wall; grey marks are decoration and never count, even when a coloured bead sits inside a grey outline. Each black slab is a solid block with one or two square holes punched through it, and the white page shows through every hole. A bead is shut inside a pocket when the white area holding that bead is completely surrounded by black ink, so that no white path leads from the bead to the edge of the page without stepping on black ink. A channel cut clean through the wall of a hole joins that hole to the white space outside its slab, so a bead in a hole with such a channel is not shut inside a pocket. Beads lying on the open page, beads inside grey outlines, and holes that hold no bead never count. How big the slabs are, where they sit on the page, how many holes the page shows in total, how many beads the page shows and how much ink the page holds never decide the answer. How many beads are shut inside a pocket? Answer with a whole number from 0 to 5.

worlds.title: Lagoon boundary patch
worlds.question: Teal and yellow together form one island around exactly one white lagoon. Does the yellow patch share an edge with both the lagoon and the outer white sea? Corner-only contact does not count.

worlds.title: Crosscut bank pair
worlds.question: A single unbroken navy wall runs from the top edge to the bottom edge. Staying inside the picture, can the orange dot reach the purple dot through white space without crossing the wall? White space connects through shared edges, not diagonal corners. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Branch leaf terminal
worlds.question: Two disconnected dark tree networks each run from a green start to a colored terminal. Ignore the green and colored terminal endpoints. Which terminal—amber or violet—is attached to the network with more unmarked dead-end side tips? Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Vane gate pad
worlds.question: The picture shows one dark conduit of constant thickness on a plain white background. A solid green square marks the port. From the port a short stem runs to a single junction, where the conduit splits into exactly two arms and never splits again. Each arm leaves the junction along a straight base leg, turns, and then doubles back past the junction, so the arm that leaves the junction on one side always finishes on the opposite side: where a pad sits never tells you which arm carries it, and the direction a vane points never tells you where its pad sits. Each arm ends on one small coloured pad; one pad is blue and one pad is orange. Two small dark triangles, the vanes, float beside the conduit, exactly one of them beside each arm's base leg, and every vane is separated from the ink by clear background. A vane belongs to the base leg it lies closest to. A vane opens its arm when its point aims away from the junction along that base leg, and seals its arm when its point aims back toward the junction. Exactly one of the two vanes opens its arm. Travel begins at the green port, runs along the stem to the junction, and may then continue only along an arm whose vane is open; a sealed arm may never be entered. All light gray shapes anywhere in the picture are decoration and mean nothing. Which coloured pad can be reached from the green port? Answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Spiral winding direction
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START to the red FINISH around the yellow post. From start to finish, does the route wind clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Paired turn word agreement
worlds.question: Two separate dark routes are shown. Starting at each blue ring, follow its cyan centerline to the orange ring. Each route has exactly three gold square 90-degree corners. Reading the corners in travel order, do the routes have the same left/right turn sequence? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Rotated glyph match
worlds.question: A reference 5-by-5 glyph is drawn inside the magenta-bordered frame at the top.  Four framed squares below each hold another 5-by-5 glyph, and each square carries a coloured tag just above it: one crimson, one teal, one amber, one violet.  Exactly one of the four tagged glyphs equals the reference glyph after rotating the reference a quarter turn clockwise.  Which colour tag belongs to that matching glyph?  Answer with exactly one of: crimson, teal, amber, violet.

worlds.title: Moving cursor register
worlds.question: START shows four tape cells numbered 1 to 4, with dark square = 1 and pale square = 0. The gold arrow marks the cursor. Read the ten command cards from left to right: red TOGGLE flips the cell under the cursor; blue NEXT moves the cursor one cell right, wrapping from cell 4 to cell 1; violet COPY writes the current cell's value into the next cell and leaves the cursor where it is. Apply every command to the current tape and cursor. After command 10, which final pattern do cells 1 to 4 show? Answer exactly one of: clear = 0000, front-pair = 1100, split-pair = 0011, alternating = 1010.

worlds.title: Sole circuit room
worlds.question: This picture is a 6 by 6 block of square rooms. Walls are solid ink, and you may walk between two rooms only through a doorway gap in the wall between them. Four rooms have a coloured floor: orange, green, blue and pink. Exactly one of them stands on a round trip: starting there you can walk away and come back to it without ever passing through the same doorway twice. From each of the other three, every walk that returns has to go back through a doorway it already used. Which coloured room is it? Answer with exactly one of: orange, green, blue, pink.

worlds.title: Counterfactual dependency prune
worlds.question: Using the full printed row, each swap depends on the latest earlier swap touching either of its boxes. Cancel the red-X swap, then repeatedly cancel every swap that depends on a canceled swap. From START, do only the swaps left. Which shape finishes in the TARGET box? Answer circle, triangle, star, or diamond.

worlds.title: Counterfactual mediator transplant
worlds.question: The triangle shows the factual run; dark means ON. Each lower cell applies its row rule to the touching pair above. First flip the red-ringed TOP cell and rebuild, recording the new value of every lettered mediator. Then restore TOP as shown. Test one card in a fresh run: when each listed letter is reached, replace its value by the value recorded from the red-flipped run, then continue downward. Which card recreates the red-flipped bottom row? Answer card-1, card-2, card-3, or card-4.

worlds.title: Correspondence orientation color
worlds.question: The gray bar at the top is tilted at a specific angle. Below it are three colored bars, each tilted at a different angle. Which colored bar is tilted at exactly the same angle as the gray bar? Answer with that bar's color (red, green, or blue).

worlds.title: Color bound pattern count correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate has the same color-to-band-count assignment as the reference? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Crease fold symbol binding
worlds.question: The dashed blue-gray line in this image is a fold crease on a flat sheet. Four solid colored disks (red, blue, green and orange) lie on one side of the crease, and four gray outlined circles lie on the other side; each outlined circle contains exactly one black symbol, and the four symbols are a filled square, a filled triangle, a plus-shaped cross and a horizontal bar. If the sheet is folded along the crease, every disk is carried to the mirror image of its position across the crease, and each disk lands exactly on the center of one outlined circle, a different circle for each disk. Distance across the picture, left-right or up-down order, and which circle merely looks closest do not decide the landing; only mirroring across the drawn crease does. Which symbol is in the circle that the red disk lands on? Answer square, triangle, cross, or bar.

worlds.title: Gap rhythm tags
worlds.question: TARGET and each tagged reference show six identical beads in a row, separated by exactly two LONG gaps and three SHORT gaps. Rows may move and be uniformly resized. Read the five gaps from left to right. Which tag color is below the reference with the same SHORT/LONG gap order as TARGET? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Projective frame correspondence
worlds.question: REFERENCE and TARGET show the same eight points under one perspective warp. Match the four same-colored corner anchors; the warp may rotate or mirror the view but maps every reference point to exactly one target dot. Which TARGET dot corresponds to the magenta-ringed REFERENCE point? Answer red, green, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Trace amplitude compare
worlds.question: A white panel shows two squiggly colored traces rising and falling: one red and one blue. Which color's trace has the GREATER vertical amplitude, meaning the larger total range measured from its lowest point down to its highest point up? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Marker spacing variation
worlds.question: Panel A is the left row and panel B is the right row. Each row has five colored circular markers. Compute the coefficient of variation (standard deviation divided by mean) of the four adjacent horizontal gaps in each row. Which panel has the larger value? Choose A or B.

worlds.title: Peak to trough drop
worlds.question: The picture shows three framed panels stacked one above the other. Each panel contains exactly one coloured trace, drawn as a line through nine round markers that run from left to right; one trace is red, one is green and one is blue. Every panel is ruled with the same horizontal gridlines and every panel uses the same spacing between neighbouring gridlines, so a vertical distance means the same thing in all three panels. For one trace, a FALL is measured between two of its own markers: pick any marker, then pick a marker further to the RIGHT along the same trace that sits lower, and the size of that fall is the vertical distance between them. A trace's DEEPEST FALL is the largest such distance it contains, that is, the biggest drop from an earlier high point down to a later low point. Order matters: a trace that starts low and climbs to a high point has only a small deepest fall no matter how much total height it covers, so the trace that spans the most gridlines from its lowest to its highest marker is often not the answer, and neither is the trace that reaches the lowest marker in its own panel. Compare each trace only with itself; a marker in one panel is never paired with a marker in another. In every picture each trace contains at least one fall, and no two traces have equally deep deepest falls. The colours and the top-to-bottom order of the panels carry no information. Which coloured trace has the deepest fall? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: Trace bend leader
worlds.question: At the three equally spaced checkpoints, which colored trace bends most? Define bend as the absolute difference between its first and second vertical steps. Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Boxplot dual asymmetry
worlds.question: Which sample has its median in the lower half of its box and an upper whisker longer than its lower whisker? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Bias stop sign sides
worlds.question: This is a red STOP sign. A standard STOP sign is an eight-sided octagon, but report exactly what is drawn here. How many sides does this STOP sign actually have? Count only the visible sides and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Chest drawer count
worlds.question: How many drawer fronts are visible in the chest? Count each horizontal drawer front once; use its centered handle as a cue; ignore the chest frame, feet, and CHEST label. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Stair step rise break
worlds.question: This image shows one flight of steps drawn in side view on white paper as a single solid block of ONE STRONG COLOUR standing on a grey ground line. The flat top of each step is a TREAD; the treads are the level coloured edges along the top of the block, all of the same width, and there are between four and nine of them. Read the treads from the LEFT edge of the block to the RIGHT edge. One tread is HIGHER than another when its coloured top edge is drawn nearer the top edge of the page. Judge only the top edges of the coloured block: the thin grey rail above the flight always slopes upward to the right and is decoration, and so are the grey page frame, the grey corner ticks, the small grey diamonds and the small coloured square near the top right corner. Whether the flight climbs all the way is chosen separately from the number of treads, the tread width, the colour, the tallest step, the total amount of coloured ink and the position on the page, so on some pages the flight climbs the whole way and on other pages one tread is drawn lower than the tread just before it, and neither is a mistake. No image in this set is a borderline case: neighbouring treads are never drawn at the same height. Report the picture in front of you, and do not answer from how a flight of steps is usually built. Going from left to right, is every tread higher than the tread just before it? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Envelope flap tip edge
worlds.question: Which outer edge does the pointed tip of the solid blue triangular envelope flap touch? Use image directions and answer top, right, bottom, or left.

worlds.title: E glyph shortest arm conflict
worlds.question: In the large dark E-like symbol, which horizontal arm is shortest: top, middle, or bottom? Measure from the left vertical stem to each visible right tip. Answer top, middle, or bottom.

worlds.title: Bitplane glyph reveal
worlds.question: The image is a dense field of gray noise. The answer letter is hidden only in the least-significant bit (bit-plane 0) of each pixel's gray value; the other seven bits are random noise. Read that least-significant bit plane. Which letter, A or B, is revealed? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Serpentine scan reveal
worlds.question: After the serpentine-row restoration and 9x9 edge-replicated mean, which symbol is visible?

worlds.title: Quarter turn stack reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one square panel divided into a 7 by 7 lattice of equal square cells; each cell is either dark or empty, and four small brightly coloured square marks sit exactly on the four corners of the panel. Turn the whole panel about its own centre by a quarter turn, by a half turn and by three quarters of a turn, so that you have the panel as printed plus those three turned copies of it, all four laid on top of one another in the same square outline. Keep a cell only where the panel is dark in the printed copy and in all three turned copies as well; discard every other cell. The kept cells form exactly one of these five symbols: plus (one full centre row and one full centre column crossing), ex (both full corner-to-corner diagonals crossing), ring (a hollow square outline one cell thick, standing clear of the panel edge), diamond (a hollow diamond outline one cell thick, with a single cell at the middle of each panel edge), corners (four separate two-by-two blocks, one in each corner of the panel, and nothing else). Which symbol do the kept cells form? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Clockwise ring unwrap
worlds.question: Cut at the magenta seam, unwrap clockwise, and put the outer edge at the top. Which symbol appears: circle, triangle, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Seeded floodfill arrow
worlds.question: Inside the cyan-framed 17-by-17 grid, start at the gold dot and flood-fill its pale cell plus every pale cell connected through a shared edge. Dark cells block the fill, cyan grid lines do not block it, and diagonal contact does not connect. Ignore every pale cell not reached. Which direction does the filled arrow point: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Dot lattice regularity
worlds.question: On a white canvas a field of equal-sized dark dots is drawn. Look at the whole arrangement of dots together. Do the dots form one regular grid -- laid out in straight rows and straight columns with an equal, even spacing, every dot's nearest neighbours all at essentially the same distance -- or are they scattered at irregular, random positions? Choose: yes if they form a regular grid, no if they are an irregular scatter.

worlds.title: Parallel rail constellation
worlds.question: Each colored field has eight same-sized dots. For each complete field, try every split into two groups of four and fit one straight line to each group. For a split let R be the larger mean perpendicular residual in pixels, A the angle difference between the fitted directions in degrees, C the larger coefficient of variation of the three along-line gaps, and S the perpendicular separation of the fitted lines. Its rail score is exp(-R/5.5 - A/14 - C/0.40) * min(1, S/28). Which color has the highest rail score? Ignore color, panel position, rotation, translation, dot size, and dot count.

worlds.title: Lattice vacancy line
worlds.question: The picture shows identical coloured dots placed on the sites of an evenly spaced square grid, except that some sites are empty. A grid line is a whole row of sites, a whole column of sites, a diagonal of sites running down to the right, or a diagonal of sites running up to the right. Exactly one grid line has more empty sites than every other grid line, and no two empty sites on that line are next to each other. The dot colour, the background colour, the dot size, the grid spacing, the grid size, the position of the grid and the total number of empty sites carry no information about the answer. Which direction does that line run? Answer row (horizontal), column (vertical), down (diagonal running down to the right) or up (diagonal running up to the right).

worlds.title: Nearest neighbor group count
worlds.question: For each black dot, connect it to the one other black dot whose center is nearest; there are no ties. Treat links as undirected. How many connected groups does the complete network form? Answer one or two.

worlds.title: Paired dot focus
worlds.question: Pair the dark dots by mutual nearest neighbors. Extend each pair's center-to-center line in both directions. Which colored ring is at the common focus of those lines? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Conjunction quadrant search
worlds.question: A reference glyph is drawn in the top panel: an outline frame that is either a circle or a square, containing one central bar that is either horizontal or vertical. Below, the image is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), each holding one larger glyph with the same two features: an outline frame (circle or square) and a central bar (horizontal or vertical). Exactly one quadrant's glyph matches the reference on BOTH features: the same frame shape AND the same bar orientation. The other three glyphs each differ from the reference on at least one feature. Which quadrant contains the one glyph that matches the reference on both features?

worlds.title: Parallel sides panel search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only quadrilateral whose opposite sides are parallel? Each panel has one filled quadrilateral. Treat sides as undirected lines: both opposite-side angle differences must be at most 5 degrees. Ignore labels, color, position, and size; answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Mirror axis panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly six solid dots of the same single colour and the same size, so all five panels carry the same number of dots and the same amount of ink, and colour, dot count and dot size carry no information. Every panel also carries exactly one straight dashed grey line that runs right across it at that panel's own arbitrary tilt; this dashed line is that panel's mirror line, and its tilt and its place inside the panel carry no information. A panel counts as mirror-symmetric when folding it along its own dashed line would lay every one of its six dots exactly onto another of its dots: each dot has a partner on the other side of the dashed line, the two partners stand the same distance from the line, and the line through the two partners meets the dashed line square on. No dot ever sits on the dashed line, and the dots are never mirrored across any other line, only across the dashed line drawn in their own panel. In exactly one panel all six dots are mirror-symmetric about that panel's dashed line. In each of the other four panels exactly one single dot has been pushed off its mirror place, by at least 12 pixels, which is more than three quarters of a dot's width, while the remaining dots there still mirror one another. Only the dot centres and the dashed line matter, and no partner pairs are drawn. Which numbered panel has all six of its dots mirror-symmetric about its own dashed line? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Ring tilt conjunction
worlds.question: Which labeled candidate matches both attributes in the REFERENCE: the ring color and the dark bar's tilt? Match both; A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Distinct nearest assignment search
worlds.question: Each orange dot chooses the navy square whose center is closest. Which labeled panel has the three dots choosing three different squares? A tied distance would not count. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State bounce register
worlds.question: A horizontal track of five slot boxes is shown, read left to right as slot 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. A red marker sits in one box and an orange ring surrounds that box; it marks the START slot. Four operator boxes are read left to right; each holds one colored disk. A green disk advances the tracked register one slot to the right (+1), a blue disk retreats it one slot to the left (-1). The register BOUNCES elastically off both walls: a rightward step taken at the right wall (slot 5) reflects back to slot 4, and a leftward step taken at the left wall (slot 1) reflects back to slot 2. The register is never shown after its start. Replaying the operators in order from the ringed start, bouncing at the walls, what is the FINAL slot of the tracked register? Answer exactly 'slot 1' through 'slot 5'.

worlds.title: Synchronized state pair
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 from left to right. Each labeled object shows one state from the STATE KEY. Which unordered pair of labels changes state together on the most adjacent panel transitions? Answer AB, AC, AD, BC, BD, or CD.

worlds.title: Focus shift tally
worlds.question: Four coloured towers of square blocks stand on one baseline. The black triangle below the baseline is the pointer, and it starts under the tower shown. The square cards along the bottom are operations, applied one at a time in order from left to right, as the long arrow above them shows. A dark slate card carrying white dots adds that many blocks to the tower the pointer is under at that moment. A grey card carrying a white triangle moves the pointer one tower in the direction the triangle points and adds nothing. The pointer never has to leave the four towers, no tower is ever emptied, and the final arrangement is not drawn. The black ring at the top marks one tower, the ringed tower. After every card has been applied, how many blocks does the ringed tower hold? Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Device status change
worlds.question: Read BEFORE then AFTER. Devices may move. A device's number is its green-dot count. Exactly one status lamp switches color. Which numbered device changed?

worlds.title: Priority service replay
worlds.question: The legend maps chip colors to A-D, and the priority strip ranks them from FIRST to LAST. The rack shows the starting waiting set. Read cards 1-8 left to right: a + card adds its shown task, while a SERVE card removes the currently waiting task that is earliest in the priority strip. Which waiting task would be served next? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Region contact degree
worlds.question: Look at the four colored regions (red, green, blue, magenta). A region shares a border with another region only when the two shapes touch along a side of positive length; touching at just a corner does not count. Which color is in contact with the greatest number of the other three regions? Answer with exactly one color name.

worlds.title: Cycle rank networks
worlds.question: Exactly one colored network has cycle rank 2. Which colored network is it? Count independent cycles as E minus V plus C: E is the number of visible links, V is the number of colored node markers, and C is the number of connected pieces. Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Piece hole signature
worlds.question: The picture shows four flat drawings on white paper: one black drawing and three coloured drawings, one red, one green and one blue. Each drawing is made only of solid blobs of its own single colour. Two blobs of the same colour that do not touch anywhere are separate PIECES. A round patch of white paper that lies completely inside one blob, so that its white is fully surrounded by that colour, is a HOLE. For each drawing count its pieces and count its holes, adding the holes of all of its pieces together. Exactly one of the red, green and blue drawings has BOTH the same number of pieces AND the same number of holes as the black drawing; of the other two, one matches the black drawing only in its number of pieces and the other only in its number of holes. Position, size, blob shape and total amount of ink are irrelevant. Which coloured drawing matches the black drawing in both numbers? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: Two cycle split link
worlds.question: Gray and colored links join round stations. Imagine removing exactly one colored link. Which removal splits the network into two separate parts with a loop still present in both parts? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: All junction cycle
worlds.question: Does this network have a loop of dark links that visits every colored circular junction exactly once before returning to its start? There are ten junctions, exactly three links meet each junction, and links meet only at junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Trace longer route
worlds.question: Two winding routes are drawn on a white background: one blue and one green. Each route folds back and forth on itself, so its true length is measured along the drawn stroke, not from end to end. Which route, blue or green, has the greater total length along its stroke? Answer with that colour only (blue or green).

worlds.title: Blocked junction terminal
worlds.question: Trace the dark network from the green source. If the square-marked junction is closed, which terminal remains connected: red or blue? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Pipe turn handedness
worlds.question: The gray stroke in this picture is one single pipe. It never branches and never touches or crosses itself, so it has exactly two loose ends and you can follow it from one end to the other. A green disc covers one of the two loose ends; that is where you start. The pipe is built only from horizontal and vertical straight sections, so every bend in it is a right-angle turn. Imagine walking along the pipe from the green end, always facing the way you are travelling. At each bend you turn either toward your left hand or toward your right hand; left and right mean the walker's own left and right at that moment, which depends on the direction you were already heading, and not on any fixed side of the page. Number the bends 1, 2, 3, ... in the order you meet them as you walk from the green end. How long the sections are, how many bends there are in total, which way the other bends go, and where the pipe sits on the page do not matter; only the direction of the third bend counts. Walking from the green end, is the third bend a turn to your left or a turn to your right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Widest branch terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green circle and follow the dark links. At each cyan junction, continue along the wider of the two forward links; never reverse onto the link just used. Which colored square do you reach: orange, purple, blue, or red?

worlds.title: Ordinal gate checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green START disk, follow the single black route toward the purple FINISH disk. Which colored checkpoint lies after the route's second crossing of the solid gray gate but before its third crossing? Count crossings in travel order; a crossing requires the route to pass from one side of the gate to the other. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Constellation geometry correspondence
worlds.question: The upper-left panel is the reference. Rotate each candidate constellation 90 degrees clockwise about its panel center. Which candidate, A or B, has the same three-marker geometry as the reference? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Combwall rank pair bind
worlds.question: The picture is one solid wall built from ten coloured teeth of equal width standing side by side across the whole image, with no gap between neighbours. Counting from the left, teeth 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 hang down from the TOP edge; teeth 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10 rise up from the BOTTOM edge. The five top teeth are red, blue, green, purple and orange in some order, and the five bottom teeth are teal, yellow, pink, brown and slate in some order. Every tooth has its own length, and no two teeth attached to the same edge are equally long. Exactly one top tooth carries a small black square: that tooth is the KEY. The top teeth and the bottom teeth are partnered by length rank alone: the longest top tooth partners the longest bottom tooth, the second longest top tooth partners the second longest bottom tooth, and so on down to the shortest of each edge. Ranks are worked out separately for each edge, so lengths must not be compared across the two edges: do not partner teeth by similar length, by side-by-side position, or by colour, and the black square says nothing about which colour is correct. What colour is the bottom tooth that partners the KEY tooth? Answer teal, yellow, pink, brown or slate.

worlds.title: Sidepair reduction atlas
worlds.question: All four mosaics are woven into one uninterrupted navy atlas; a hole in the atlas makes it unreadable. The large 6-by-6 mosaic is divided into nine outlined 2-by-2 blocks. Reduce each block to one tile, in the same row and column: the result is cyan exactly when that block contains exactly two cyan tiles that share a side; otherwise it is cream. Which red, green, or blue tag marks the exact 3-by-3 result?

worlds.title: Partition echo correspondence
worlds.question: The charcoal-framed mosaic is the reference. Compare tiles at the same row and column while ignoring color names: a candidate matches only if one single one-to-one renaming of its four colors makes all 49 positions agree with the reference. Which color frames the matching mosaic? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Rank fixed point panels
worlds.question: Which color has the same left-to-right rank in both strips? Answer red, teal, or violet.

worlds.title: Halfcover cell tally
worlds.question: The sheet contains one square panel ruled into equal square cells by thin light grey lines, and exactly one solid navy region lying wholly inside that panel. Every other mark on the sheet, in any other colour, is decorative and must be ignored. A ruling cell counts as half-covered when strictly more than half of the area enclosed by its four ruling lines is navy; cells outside the ruled panel do not exist. How many ruling cells of that panel are half-covered by the navy region? Answer with a single integer.

worlds.title: Field half brightness
worlds.question: Which half of the large gray measurement field has lower average brightness? Average all of the gray area on each side of the black center divider. Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Survey silhouette balance
worlds.question: Which equal-width half of the filled survey silhouette has the greater mean height above the common baseline: LEFT or RIGHT?

worlds.title: Frame border uniformity
worlds.question: Is the visible picture-frame border the same thickness on all four sides? Answer yes only when the four border bands differ in thickness by at most 3 pixels; otherwise answer no.

worlds.title: Mirror spot orphans
worlds.question: This picture shows one moth from above: a pale grey wing silhouette printed with small filled round spots that all share one colour. Two small dark grey squares, one beyond the head and one beyond the tail, mark the two ends of the moth's mirror line; the mirror line is the straight line through the centres of those two squares. Call a spot paired when another spot sits at its mirror position across that line, and unpaired when no spot sits there. In this picture every spot is either mirrored exactly by another spot or has a clearly empty mirror position, no spot lies on the mirror line, and at most three spots are unpaired. The two wings need not carry the same number of spots, and the mirror line need not be upright. How many spots are unpaired? Answer with exactly one of: 0, 1, 2, 3.

worlds.title: Flag canton side
worlds.question: On which side of the striped flag is the solid blue rectangular canton: left or right? Answer left or right from the visible image.

worlds.title: Snowflake primary arms
worlds.question: How many long primary arms reach the outermost tips of the snowflake? Ignore the two shorter side branches attached to each primary arm. Answer with 5, 6, 7, or 8.

worlds.title: Mirror difference tile
worlds.question: Inside the single blue-framed square tile, reflect the tile across its vertical centerline and take the absolute pixel-by-pixel difference between the tile and its reflection. The tile interior is an 8-row by 12-column raster; average each left/right mirrored cell pair into an 8-row by 6-column grid. Mark # when a cell's mean RGB difference is at least 30, and . otherwise. Read rows top-to-bottom and compare with A. Which symbol appears? Ignore the frame and everything outside the tile. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Hinge fold difference reveal
worlds.question: This picture shows two square panels drawn far apart, one near the left edge and one near the right edge. Each panel is a five-row, five-column grid of cells, and every cell carries exactly one of two flat tones, dark or pale; both tones appear inside both panels. Exactly one of the two panels has a thick solid upright bar drawn against its inner edge, the edge that faces the other panel: that bar is the hinge, and the panel it touches is the hinged panel. A few small clutter squares of a different colour lie on the background between the panels; they are not cells and carry no evidence. Carry out this operation. Fold the hinged panel across its hinge and lay it flat on top of the other panel, so that the hinged panel's grid is mirrored left to right - its column order is reversed, its row order is unchanged - and its cell that lands on a given cell of the other panel is the one in the same row and the mirrored column. Now mark every one of the twenty-five stacked positions where exactly one of the two layers is dark, and leave unmarked every position where both layers are dark and every position where neither is. Exactly nine positions get marked in every picture. The marked positions always form exactly one of five symbols on the five-by-five grid. 'plus' is an upright bar through the middle column crossing a flat bar through the middle row. 'ex' is the two full diagonals crossing at the centre cell. 'tee' is the full top row plus the middle column below it. 'ell' is the full left column plus the full bottom row. 'seven' is the full top row plus a diagonal running from the top-right area down to the bottom-left cell. The symbol is drawn nowhere in the picture and neither panel contains it: each panel on its own is consistent with every symbol, so both distant panels and the hinge must be read together. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, ex, tee, ell, seven.

worlds.title: Odd vertex reassembly
worlds.question: Starting at the ringed end, number every corner along the cyan trace from 1. Reconnect corners 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9 in order. Which symbol appears: M or W?

worlds.title: Column gravity reveal
worlds.question: Rotate the cyan-framed 9 by 9 card until the magenta corner is upper left and the gold corner is upper right. Within each column, let every dark cell fall straight down without changing columns. Which settled silhouette needs the fewest cell changes to match: crown, cup, or stair? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Paired seam correspondence
worlds.question: Ignoring color, position, size, and the gap, do the two separated tiles have the same sequence of bumps and recesses along their facing edges? Keep the top-to-bottom order and do not rotate or flip either tile. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Paired ring openings
worlds.question: The image contains exactly two small dark rings; every light-grey mark is background clutter and must be ignored. Each dark ring's outline is broken by exactly one gap. Consider the straight line through the two dark rings' centres. For each dark ring decide whether its gap opens towards the other dark ring or away from it. The answer is facing if both gaps open towards each other, apart if both gaps open away from each other, and same-way if one gap opens towards the other ring while the other opens away, so that both gaps point the same way along that line. Answer unclear if either gap points within 17 degrees of perpendicular to that line. Which relation holds: facing, apart, same-way, or unclear?

worlds.title: Four ring bow
worlds.question: Read the four colored rings from left to right. Relative to the invisible line through the first and last centers, do both inner centers make an arch above it or a bowl below it? Answer arch or bowl.

worlds.title: Trail pocket reveal
worlds.question: The dark trail is one connected thin stroke. How many separate pale pockets does its complete route enclose: one pocket or two pockets?

worlds.title: Reflected silhouette search
worlds.question: Each sector contains two separate filled glyphs. Imagine the line through the midpoint of the line joining their centers, perpendicular to that joining line. Which sector contains the only pair whose silhouettes are mirror images across that line? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Bend side kink search
worlds.question: The picture shows one thin thread folded into eight straight runs inside a small window on a plain background. The runs alternate between horizontal and vertical, so the thread makes a right-angle corner between one run and the next, and it has seven corners in all. Both ends of the thread are bare. Walk along the thread starting from whichever of its two ends lies further to the left: the corner reached first is turn one, the next corner is turn two, and so on up to turn seven. At each turn the walker bears either to the left or to the right. Exactly one of turns two, three, four, five and six bears the opposite way from both the turn immediately before it and the turn immediately after it on this walk; each of the other four of those five turns bears the same way as at least one of its two neighbouring turns. The thread's colour, how long any run is, how much thread there is, where the window sits on the page, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which turn bears the opposite way from both the turn just before it and the turn just after it? Answer with one of: second, third, fourth, fifth, sixth.

worlds.title: Bilateral tally search
worlds.question: Which labeled lane has the same number of cyan dots on the left as amber dots on the right? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Double closed loop search
worlds.question: Each color appears as two detached outlines. Which color has two completely closed outlines? Every other color has exactly one closed outline and one outline with a visible gap. Ignore position, size, and gap direction. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State cycle alignment
worlds.question: Read HISTORY A and HISTORY B from their red-ringed starts in checkpoint order 1 through 6. A filled circle means ON and an outlined circle means OFF. Is B exactly A shifted one checkpoint toward the start, so B1=A2, B2=A3, through B5=A6 and B6=A1? Answer YES or NO.

worlds.title: Pinbank compare sort
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small window drawn with a thick grey frame. Every mark outside that frame, grey or coloured or black, is inert decoration and changes nothing. Inside the window stand four equally wide columns of equal total height, side by side. Each column is filled from its floor upward with one solid colour, red, blue, green or purple, and the pale grey part above the fill is empty: the height of the coloured fill is that pin's size, and the four colours are all different. Below the columns lies a short stack of solid black brackets. Each bracket spans exactly two neighbouring columns and means: compare those two pins and move the taller pin into the left one of the two columns and the shorter pin into the right one, carrying each pin's colour and its fill height together; if the pin already in the left column is at least as tall, nothing moves. Apply the brackets one at a time in top-to-bottom order, and let each bracket act on the arrangement left behind by the brackets above it. The small solid black square above the columns marks the one column to read at the end. After every bracket has been applied in top-to-bottom order, what colour is the pin standing in the marked column? Answer with one of red, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Sampling latch quilt
worlds.question: The gold START tile shows SENSOR above RECORDER (filled means ON, hollow means OFF). Read every other tile in row order, left-to-right then top-to-bottom. A cyan tile toggles SENSOR. A coral tile copies SENSOR's current state into RECORDER. Is RECORDER ON after every tile?

worlds.title: Cyclic challenger crown
worlds.question: The ringed emblem is the starting champion. Read the four detached cards by their purple dot counts: one, then two, three, and four. Circle defeats triangle, triangle defeats square, and square defeats circle. At each card, the shown challenger replaces the champion only when it defeats the current champion; otherwise the champion stays. Which emblem is champion after all four cards: circle, triangle, or square?

worlds.title: Focal junction articulation
worlds.question: If the colored junction is removed, does the remaining visible network become disconnected? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Stamp piece hole balance
worlds.question: This page shows one small near-black stamp built from square blocks, together with red, blue, green, orange, grey and purple decorations that lie elsewhere on the open page. Only the near-black stamp ink decides the answer; the coloured decorations never count, even when a decoration is drawn as a closed ring or frame with its own pale middle. Pale channels cut the stamp into separate pieces. A piece is a maximal patch of near-black ink whose blocks are joined edge to edge; blocks that meet only at a corner are not joined, and the stamp is drawn so that this case never arises. A hole is a patch of pale paper that lies wholly inside the ink, so that no pale route leads from it out to the open page around the stamp; pale paper that reaches the open page through a channel is not a hole, however deep it cuts. Every hole belongs to the one piece that rings it. The question is about how the holes are shared out among the pieces, not about how many there are of either: at most one piece is ever left bare, and the same numbers of pieces and of holes occur with both answers. How many pieces the stamp has, how many holes it shuts in, where the stamp sits on the page, how large its blocks are, how much ink it carries and which colours appear never decide the answer by themselves. Does every piece of the stamp shut in at least one hole of its own? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Rail cut single face
worlds.question: Treat the yellow rail section as erased. Does the remaining black railway enclose exactly one white courtyard? White regions connect only through shared edges, not corners. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Trail hop balance
worlds.question: The map has eight circular stations joined by eight straight navy links. Links meet only at stations. Count one link between neighboring stations. Along shortest routes, are orange and purple the same number of links from green? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Crest route checkpoint
worlds.question: Following the green-to-red trace, which ringed checkpoint—amber or violet—is closer along the trace to its unique topmost point? Use distance along the drawn trace, not straight-line distance. Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Jog index walk
worlds.question: The image shows two separate structures on a plain background. One is a dark rail drawn as a single connected stroke of constant width: it runs as three long horizontal lines joined end to end by two short vertical links, so the whole rail is one open route with exactly two loose ends and no junction. Three short bands of that rail are painted instead of dark, one orange, one purple and one yellow; each band is a piece of the rail itself. A hollow green square marker sits in clear background a short way beyond exactly one of the rail's two loose ends, and that end is the start: walking the rail from the marked end to the other end without leaving the stroke, the three coloured bands are met one after another, and that walking order is the only order that counts. The other structure is a teal wire, a separate connected staircase stroke that touches nothing else: it alternates horizontal runs with downward drops, and N is its number of downward drops, which is always 1, 2 or 3. Small gray squares are decoys and mean nothing. Consider the N-th coloured band met when walking the rail from its marked end. What colour is that band? Answer orange, purple or yellow.

worlds.title: Paired progress ratio
worlds.question: Trace each separate navy route from its green START to its red FINISH. Each route has one yellow checkpoint. On which route is the checkpoint encountered later as a fraction of that route's total length: upper or lower? Answer upper or lower.

worlds.title: Shoreline loop mate
worlds.question: The navy island has two separate navy-white shoreline loops: its outer coast and the coast of its white lake. Each colored bead straddles one shoreline. Starting at the blue bead, trace that same shoreline loop without crossing navy. Which other bead is on it: red or gold? Answer red or gold.

worlds.title: Partial sum ratio correspondence
worlds.question: The picture shows a REFERENCE bar and two candidate bars labeled A and B. Every bar is divided by two vertical boundaries into three side-by-side sections: an indigo section on the left, a turquoise section in the middle, and an amber section on the right. In each bar add the widths of the left and middle sections, and add the widths of the middle and right sections; the REFERENCE's ratio is (left plus middle) over (middle plus right). Exactly one candidate reproduces this same composed ratio; the other candidate uses a clearly different one. Which candidate, A or B, reproduces the REFERENCE's composed ratio? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Keyed column weave
worlds.question: Match each SOURCE key in the three shuffled rows. For one key, place its ODD strip in columns 1, 3, and 5, and its EVEN strip in columns 2 and 4. Select the SOURCE card whose woven grid exactly matches its keyed CHECK grid. Answer card-1, card-2, card-3, card-4, or card-5.

worlds.title: Socket fit admission binding
worlds.question: Each colored socket at the top is a black block with a white opening cut down into it, and the opening has its own depth in each of the five columns. Each black comb below is a peg with five teeth. A peg fits a socket only if it can be pushed straight down into that socket with no tooth running into black, so every tooth must be no longer than the opening in its own column. Give every socket exactly one peg, so that all five pegs are used and each socket takes one. Only one such assignment fits. Which socket gets the peg inside the black ring? Answer blue, green, orange, purple, or red.

worlds.title: Masked cause contingency
worlds.question: All CAUSE and BACKUP sources are currently ON. For each labeled pair, imagine switching off the CAUSE alone, the BACKUP alone, and then both, recomputing the circuit each time. Which CAUSE is masked: either single switch-off leaves TARGET as displayed, but switching off both flips TARGET? Answer cause-A, cause-B, cause-C, or cause-D.

worlds.title: Reciprocal route race
worlds.question: The six colors have different whole-number speeds from 1 to 9. Every CLUE says its LEFT pair has greater combined speed than its RIGHT pair. On each RACE card, both sides perform two 1-unit jobs in sequence, so a side's time is 1/first speed + 1/second speed. Which race must have its LEFT side finish first for every speed assignment fitting all clues? Answer race-1, race-2, race-3, or race-4.

worlds.title: Collinearity correspondence
worlds.question: The top reference panel shows two gray anchors and one colored dot. The question is whether the colored dot sits on the straight line through the two anchors or clearly away from it. Below, three candidate panels A, B, C each show two gray anchors and one colored dot. Which candidate reproduces the same collinearity relationship as the reference: its colored dot on/off its own anchors' line matching the reference?

worlds.title: Colored graph correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate panel preserves the same colored-part adjacency graph as the reference? A part is one colored square; two parts are adjacent only when their square regions share a side, not merely a corner. Ignore panel location and rotation. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Hinge chain joint binding
worlds.question: This image has two framed panels. The upper panel, labeled REF, shows a chain: six round gray joints joined end to end by five straight gray rods. Exactly one interior joint of REF is circled in black. The lower panel, labeled COPY, shows the same chain after it was picked up, resized, turned around, and re-bent at its joints. Re-bending changed every bend angle, and resizing multiplied every rod length by one and the same unknown factor, so only the ordered sequence of rod lengths survives, and the chain may be read starting from either of its two ends. Rod lengths, joint positions and bend angles in COPY are otherwise unrelated to REF. In COPY the six joints are painted red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple in some order, and the paint carries no information about which joint is which. Exactly one joint of COPY is the same joint of the chain as the circled joint of REF. Which color is that joint painted in COPY? Answer with exactly one of: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple.

worlds.title: Waypoint turn route
worlds.question: Each box shows a route from the green START dot to the red FINISH dot through four blue bend dots. Follow the connected black route and record whether each bend turns left or right. The whole route may rotate and its segment lengths may change; reflections do not count. Which option has exactly the same four-turn sequence as the REFERENCE? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Reciprocal fraction correspondence
worlds.question: The magenta-framed card is the REFERENCE fraction. A reciprocal swaps its top digit (numerator) and bottom digit (denominator). Exactly one candidate has both swapped digits. What is that candidate's border color: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Triangle perimeter argmax
worlds.question: Three colored triangles are drawn on a light panel: one red, one blue, one green, each in its own horizontal column so they do not overlap. Measure each triangle's PERIMETER, defined as the sum of the lengths of its three sides, where each side length is the straight-line distance between two of the triangle's corners. Which colored triangle has the LARGEST perimeter (the greatest total outline length)? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green. (selection by greatest three-sided sum).

worlds.title: Trace reversal count
worlds.question: Which panel's trace changes direction more often? Count sign changes among the seven consecutive segments joining eight visible markers; ties are quarantined. Choose A or B.

worlds.title: Alternating bracket winner
worlds.question: The picture shows eight solid coloured bars standing side by side on one black baseline: one red, one green, one blue, one orange, one purple, one brown, one pink and one cyan. Every bar has the same width and the bars are evenly spaced, so the bars differ only in HEIGHT. The grey lines above the bars are a knockout bracket and they show only who meets whom. Reading the bars from left to right, the 1st and the 2nd bar are the first match, the 3rd and the 4th the second match, the 5th and the 6th the third and the 7th and the 8th the fourth. ROUND ONE: in each of those four matches the TALLER bar goes through.
