ROUND TWO: the four bars that went through keep their left-to-right order and meet in two matches, the 1st against the 2nd and the 3rd against the 4th, and now the SHORTER bar goes through. FINAL: the two bars that are left meet and the TALLER of them wins. The answer is the colour of the bar that wins the final. Because the rule alternates, the winner is never the tallest bar in the picture and never the shortest one; in every picture it is also never the second tallest, never the second shortest, and never the bar that would win if the two rules were exchanged so that the shorter bar went through in round one, the taller in round two and the shorter in the final. No two bars that meet in a match are within fifteen pixels of each other in height. Colour is handed out to the eight positions at random and means nothing, and the amount of coloured ink, how far left or right a bar stands and which bars a bar stands beside mean nothing beyond fixing the matches above. Nothing marks the winner: the bracket lines, the pale grey horizontal rules, the dark frame and the black baseline are decoration. Which colour wins the final? Answer red, green, blue, orange, purple, brown, pink or cyan.

worlds.title: Stacked benchmark segment
worlds.question: Which colored segment of the stacked bar contains the vertical black dashed benchmark? Answer with the color name. A benchmark exactly on a segment boundary is excluded.

worlds.title: Stacked share gain
worlds.question: Treat each bar's colored area as its own whole, ignoring the white dividers. Which color's share increases the most from the left bar (A) to the right bar (B)? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior snowman balls
worlds.question: This is a snowman. A typical snowman is made of three stacked snowballs, but report exactly what is drawn here. How many snowballs make up this snowman? Count the visible snowballs and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Mug handle side
worlds.question: Which side of the mug is the handle attached to? Treat the image as a front view; answer left or right.

worlds.title: Lane gap leader
worlds.question: This image shows three running lanes drawn on white paper, one above the other, separated by pale grey lane lines. Each lane holds exactly one RUNNER, a solid coloured disc, and exactly one FINISH POST, the short upright dark grey bar drawn in that same lane. The three runners are red, green and blue, and every finish post belongs only to the lane it is drawn in, so each runner is judged against the post in its own lane and never against a post in another lane. The GAP of a runner is the distance from the centre of that disc rightwards to the centre of the post in its own lane, measured across the page; every runner in this set is drawn to the left of its own post. The finish posts do not stand in a line: each post is placed in its own lane independently of the others, so the runner that is farthest to the right on the page need not be the runner with the smallest gap. Which runner has the smallest gap, which colour that runner is, how far to the right each runner sits, and the size of each disc are all chosen independently of each other, so no colour, position or disc size predicts the answer. The pale grey page frame, the two grey corner ticks and the grey lane lines are decoration and mark no finishing position. No image in this set is a borderline case: the smallest gap is at least 26 pixels smaller than the next smallest, and the rightmost runner sits at least 26 pixels right of the next one. Report what this picture in front of you actually shows, and do not answer from the usual assumption that the runner farthest ahead on the page must be the one closest to finishing. Which runner has the smallest gap to the finish post in its own lane? Answer exactly one of: red, green, blue.

worlds.title: Mug handle side conflict
worlds.question: The blue loop is the mug handle. On which side of the cup body is it attached? Use image directions and answer left or right.

worlds.title: Qr finder corner conflict
worlds.question: On the visible QR-like square, which corner does not contain a large three-layer finder target? A finder target has a colored outer square, a pale square gap, and a colored center. Ignore the small dark modules. Answer top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right.

worlds.title: Mirror xor reveal
worlds.question: The image is a random lattice that is the mirror of itself except in one place. Take the left-right mirror difference (XOR) of the two halves. Which letter, A or B, does the difference reveal? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Concentric ring restore
worlds.question: Find the gray square bounded by four colored corner marks. Its pixels were recorded one square perimeter at a time, from the outside ring inward, starting at each ring's upper-left corner and walking clockwise; every second ring was recorded in reverse. Restore the square, replace each pixel by the mean of its 9x9 edge-replicated neighborhood, ignore the marks and fine carrier, and read the broad symbol: crescent, lattice, plume, or arrow?

worlds.title: Clamp span intersect reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows a grid of 5 rows and 7 columns of blank cells. Above the grid there are three coloured bars, one bar per colour, each drawn in its own lane and covering a run of whole columns. To the left of the grid there are three more coloured bars, the same three colours again, each in its own lane and covering a run of whole rows. Take each colour in turn and shade every cell that lies both in a column covered by that colour's bar above the grid and in a row covered by that colour's bar to the left of the grid. A cell is shaded if at least one colour shades it; the small grey squares outside the grid shade nothing. The shaded cells form a shape that most closely matches exactly one of these five symbols: corner, cross, flag, goalpost, tee. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Stair step deshear
worlds.question: Inside the cyan frame, cyclically shift the top grid row 0 cells left, the next row 1 cell left, the next row 2 cells left, and so on, wrapping cells around each row. Which symbol appears: arrow, cup, bolt, or key?

worlds.title: Column gravity skyline
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 9-by-9 grid, let gravity pull every dark tile straight down within its own column. Tiles may pass through empty cells but never move sideways; pack them against the bottom with no gaps, preserving the column order and image orientation. Which skyline appears: rising stairs, falling stairs, peak, or valley?

worlds.title: Dashed contour shape
worlds.question: A set of short, separated dark bars is laid tip-to-tail around the perimeter of a single shape on a white canvas. Each bar lies along the outline, and by continuing each bar to its next collinear neighbour across the small gaps the whole closed outline reads as that one shape. Which shape does the dashed outline trace? Choose from: circle, square, diamond, triangle.

worlds.title: Constellation outline
worlds.question: Look at the one large group in which every dot is joined into a closed outline. Disregard separate specks. Is its global shape a circle, a triangle, or a diamond?

worlds.title: Broken ring completion
worlds.question: The picture shows several separate dark arcs. Every arc is a piece of one and the same circle, and the remaining parts of that circle are not drawn. Four coloured dots are also drawn: one red, one blue, one green and one orange. Exactly one of those dots lies on the completed circle; the other three lie clearly inside or clearly outside it. No dot touches an arc. The background shade, the arc shade, the arc thickness, the number of arcs, the lengths of the arcs and of the gaps between them, the size and position of the circle, the dot size, the total amount of ink, and how close a dot happens to be to the nearest arc all carry no information about the answer. Which coloured dot lies on the completed circle? Answer red, blue, green or orange.

worlds.title: Spiral constellation winding
worlds.question: Starting at the gray center, follow the black dots from nearest to farthest. Does the chain wind clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Constellation reflection axis
worlds.question: The dark dots—not the colored guide lines—form an exact mirror pattern. Which colored guide line is its reflection axis? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Reference disk radius match
worlds.question: A dark reference disk is shown in the box at the top of the image. Below it, the image is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), each containing one dark filled disk. Exactly one quadrant's disk has the SAME size (the same radius) as the reference disk; the other three disks each have a clearly different radius. Which quadrant contains the disk whose radius matches the reference disk?

worlds.title: Collinear triple search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only trio of identical dark markers whose centers are collinear? A trio counts when its three centers are no more than 3 pixels from their best-fit straight line. Inspect every triple in A, B, C, and D; answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Aperture match strip
worlds.question: The top of this image holds a thin gray key box containing two horizontal plates, one above the other; the vertical empty space between them is the reference aperture. Thin gray lines split the area below the key box into four panels side by side, counted from the left. Each panel contains two vertical posts, and the horizontal empty space between that panel's two posts is that panel's aperture. Every plate and post in the image is drawn with the same thickness. Exactly one panel has an aperture exactly as wide as the reference aperture is tall; every other panel's aperture differs from the reference by more than one bar thickness. Bar colour, post height, post placement, plate length, panel position and the amount of ink in a panel carry no information about the answer, and the matching aperture is not systematically the widest or the narrowest one. Which half of the panel strip contains the matching aperture, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Polyomino clutter match
worlds.question: Which panel contains a solid block-shape exactly matching the REFERENCE? A shifted copy counts as the same; rotated or mirrored shapes do not. Panels A-D are in reading order (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).

worlds.title: Latin color grid search
worlds.question: Which labeled grid has all four colors exactly once in every row and exactly once in every column? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State machine register
worlds.question: A colour state machine is shown. On the left is the start token: a coloured disk (red, green, or blue) marked by an orange ring; that colour is the machine's starting state. To its right, four operator boxes are read left to right, and each box holds one dark shape -- a filled circle, square, or triangle -- standing for an operator. Below them is the transition table: its left column lists the three current states as coloured disks (red, green, blue from top to bottom), and its top row lists the three operators as the same dark shapes (circle, square, triangle). For a current state and an operator, the table cell below shows the coloured disk of the next state. Apply the operators in order from the start state: for each operator find its shape in the table's top row, go down that column to the row of the current state, and read the next state colour from that cell. What colour is the machine in after all four operators? Answer 'red', 'green', or 'blue'.

worlds.title: State alternation track
worlds.question: Which labeled tile changes state at every step? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Copy wire relay
worlds.question: The picture shows five vertical lanes, drawn as five grey vertical lines side by side. At the top of each lane there is one coloured disc: that colour is the colour the lane holds to begin with, and the five starting colours are blue, green, orange, purple and yellow, each used exactly once. Between the lanes there are five black arrows, each drawn horizontally at its own height, each joining two different lanes. An arrow is a one-way copy: the lane at the arrow's tail, the plain end, keeps the colour it is holding, and the lane the arrowhead points at throws away whatever colour it was holding and takes a copy of the colour the tail lane is holding at that moment. Nothing is exchanged: this is a copy and not a swap, so after a copy two lanes hold the same colour and the colour that was overwritten is gone unless some other lane still holds it. The arrows act one at a time, from the topmost arrow down to the bottommost arrow, as the grey arrow in the left margin shows, and a lane's colour keeps changing as later arrows act on it. At the bottom of every lane there is a grey socket, and a red ring marks one of them: the marked lane is the lane whose bottom socket centre is nearest to the centre of that red ring. The colours the lanes hold after the arrows have acted are not drawn anywhere; only the starting discs at the top are drawn. After all five arrows have acted in order from top to bottom, which colour does the marked lane hold? Answer with one of blue, green, orange, purple or yellow.

worlds.title: Synchronous neighbor replay
worlds.question: The five lamps start as shown. For each visible STEP card, update every lamp simultaneously: a lamp becomes ON exactly when its immediate left and right neighbors had different states before that step; a missing neighbor beyond an end counts as OFF. Is the ringed lamp ON or OFF after all steps?

worlds.title: Nested carrier exchange
worlds.question: Three colored carts begin in three docks arranged LEFT, MIDDLE, and RIGHT. Each beige parcel is identified by its pip count; the red outline marks the parcel to track. Read the seven cards from left to right. On an orange card, the two pictured colored carts exchange docks and carry their parcels with them. On a purple card, the two pip-coded docks exchange only the parcels currently there while their carts stay put: one pip means LEFT, two MIDDLE, and three RIGHT. Cart colors always name the carts themselves, wherever they currently are. Which dock contains the red-outlined parcel after all seven cards? Answer LEFT, MIDDLE, or RIGHT.

worlds.title: Enclosed holes
worlds.question: Ignoring the outside white background, look only at white gaps fully enclosed by the colored shape (each one is a separate closed pocket with no path out to the picture edge). How many enclosed white pockets are there inside the shape? Answer with exactly 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Face incidence junction
worlds.question: Which colored junction touches exactly two bounded faces: red, green, or blue? Treat every visible link as a wall and every visible junction as a vertex. A bounded face is a distinct blank region enclosed by links; count each face when its boundary includes the colored junction, and do not count the unbounded outside region.

worlds.title: Dead end wall rooms
worlds.question: The picture shows a white rectangular plate with a solid black border, and exactly five straight black walls drawn inside it. A wall splits a room in two only if it runs the whole way across that room, meeting black ink at both of its ends. A wall that stops short of the far side and leaves a white gap at one or both ends splits nothing, however long it is. The rooms are the separate white areas inside the border: two spots lie in the same room when you can walk from one to the other without crossing any black ink. How many rooms is the plate divided into? Answer 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Chamber adjacency degree
worlds.question: Black lines are walls. White areas connected without crossing black form chambers. Two chambers are neighbors only when they share a black wall segment; touching at a corner does not count. Which colored dot is in a chamber with exactly three neighboring chambers? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Universal room junction
worlds.question: The dark wall network encloses exactly three white rooms. Is the green circular junction on the boundary of all three rooms? A room is a side-connected white region completely cut off from the outer white area; corner-only contact does not join rooms. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Count markers before terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the orange ring and walking only along the blue path toward the green dot, how many black dots do you pass before reaching the green dot? Answer with the number of black dots only (0, 1, 2, or 3).

worlds.title: Directed route reachability
worlds.question: Begin at the green source and follow dark lines only in the direction shown by their orange arrowheads. Which terminal—red, blue, or gold—is reachable? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Loop shortcut dot
worlds.question: The grey stroke in this picture is one single closed loop: it never branches, never crosses or touches itself, and it comes back to where it started. Four dots sit on this loop - one green, one red, one blue and one orange. Starting at the green dot and walking along the loop, there are exactly two ways to reach the red dot: one way round and the other way round. Exactly one of the two coloured dots, blue or orange, lies on each of those two ways. Length is measured only as distance travelled along the loop itself, following every bend; straight-line distance across the picture does not count. Take the shorter of the two ways from the green dot to the red dot. Which coloured dot do you pass on it? Answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Route checkpoint signature
worlds.question: Starting at each gray ring, follow its dark cable toward the colored square. Which colored square ends the cable whose checkpoints occur in the order orange, blue, then purple?

worlds.title: Four link terminal
worlds.question: From the green START node, which colored terminal is exactly four links away? Count each black line between neighboring circular nodes as one link. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Branching trace correspondence
worlds.question: Read each connected trace as a four-symbol code: at the up, right, down, and left arms, record whether the interior excursion is on the arm's left or right. Rotate candidate A and candidate B clockwise, compare their codes with reference R, and answer A or B for the exact match.

worlds.title: Riffle track source bind
worlds.question: The dark board is littered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly one cream CARD sits somewhere on it. Only what is drawn on the card decides the answer; every mark off the card is decoration and means nothing. The card carries six small square BEADS lying in two feed rows of three: an UPPER row and a LOWER row. The six beads all have different colours, one each of red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple. Below the two rows lies the TRACK: six equally spaced square slots in a single horizontal line. Five slots are drawn as empty outlines and exactly one slot is filled solid dark - that filled slot is the MARKED slot. The beads are combed into the track by one vertical sweep line travelling across the card from left to right: the bead whose centre the sweep reaches first drops into the leftmost track slot, the bead reached next drops into the second slot, and so on, so the six beads fill the six slots from left to right in the order of their horizontal centres, no matter which feed row each bead came from. The two rows are staggered, so the sweep order alternates between the rows irregularly and cannot be read off either row on its own; a bead's own row never tells you its sweep position. The track slots are equally spaced, and a slot's position tells you nothing about the beads except its rank in the track. What colour is the bead that lands in the marked slot? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Address transpose tags
worlds.question: The gold tag marks a 2-row by 3-column dot card. Swap every dot's row and column address, making a 3-row by 2-column card. Which colored tag marks the exact result? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Quarterturn atlas correspondence
worlds.question: The gray-tagged cluster is the reference. Exactly one colored-tagged cluster places the same four landmark shapes in the same relative layout after rotating the map by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees. Reflections and swapping shape identities are not allowed; treat each upright symbol as a landmark marker, not an arrow. Which color tags the matching cluster? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Ribbon checkpoint width
worlds.question: In the boxed ribbon inset, which marked checkpoint cuts through the wider filled blue ribbon: amber or violet? Compare the horizontal span at each marker's center; answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Dip recovery count
worlds.question: The sheet is off-white and carries one small framed inset. Exactly one mark in the whole figure is pure black: a single thin black trace inside that inset which runs continuously from its left end to its right end and has exactly one height at every horizontal position it covers. The guide height is the height of the trace's own left end, and the dotted grey line inside the inset is drawn at exactly that height. Follow the black trace from its left end rightwards. It first drops below the guide height. A return is a place where the trace comes back up and passes from below the guide height to above it; a dip that stays below the guide height is not a return, and passing from above back down to below is not a return either. Every turning point of the trace is at least sixteen pixels clear of the guide height, so the trace never merely touches that height and every return is a full crossing. Count every return along the whole trace, including the ones in its middle. The pale coloured curves, the other grey frames on the sheet and the short grey tick marks are decoration and carry no information. How many returns does the black trace make? Answer with one number: 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Waist edge proximity
worlds.question: Is the narrow waist of the colored sample closer to its top edge or its bottom edge? Answer top or bottom.

worlds.title: Aperture capture balance
worlds.question: The gold circle is a sampling aperture. Of the visible teal specimen area (gold boundary ink does not count), is more inside or outside the aperture? Answer INSIDE or OUTSIDE.

worlds.title: Button hole count
worlds.question: How many holes are punched through the visible button face? Count only fully enclosed holes in the large face; ignore its outer border. Answer with a whole number.

worlds.title: Rose frame bearing
worlds.question: This picture contains exactly one navy compass rose and exactly one crimson arrow, drawn far apart on a plain background. The rose is the navy figure made of four separate solid tips placed at right angles around a common centre: exactly one tip is a triangle and the other three tips are squares. The navy triangular tip marks NORTH; going clockwise around the rose from the triangular tip, the three square tips mark EAST, then SOUTH, then WEST. The crimson arrow points along its own length, towards its wide triangular head and away from its narrow flat tail. Grey marks are decoration and must be ignored. Screen-up is not necessarily north: the rose is the only thing that fixes the compass directions. Assign the arrow to whichever of the four rose directions is closest in angle to the arrow's pointing direction. Which compass direction is the crimson arrow pointing? Answer north, east, south or west.

worlds.title: Visible flag stripe count
worlds.question: How many horizontal stripes are visible on the flag? Count every full-width or canton-shortened horizontal stripe once.

worlds.title: Fuse wire continuity
worlds.question: Inside the glass fuse, is the colored wire one unbroken path from the left metal cap to the right metal cap? Follow its raised bypass; any visible background-colored gap means broken. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route width blur
worlds.question: One connected navy ribbon runs inside the pale route window from a red start cap to a green end cap. Follow it from red to green and treat each of its 32 successive sections as one width sample. Apply a three-sample box blur to the width sequence, then read the 32 blurred samples row-major as a 4-by-8 bitmap. Which displayed template is closer: A) BOW = 10011001/01100110/01100110/10011001 or B) HARP = 11100111/10000001/10000001/11100111? Use Hamming distance, choose A on a tie, and quarantine ties. Ignore the caps, window, and background.

worlds.title: Speckle majority reveal
worlds.question: The dark-bordered square panel is divided into a 7 by 7 grid of equal square cells. Every cell is packed edge to edge with a fine speckle of exactly two inks, warm orange and cool blue, and different cells use different orange-to-blue area ratios. Carry out this operation on the panel: for each of the 49 cells, compare the total area of warm orange ink inside that cell with the total area of cool blue ink inside the same cell, and mark the cell if warm orange covers more than half of it. The small speckled square below the panel is an exactly half-and-half reference mixture. The marked cells form one symbol on the 7 by 7 grid: 'plus' is a full centre row plus a full centre column, 'ex' is both full diagonals, and 'tee_up', 'tee_right', 'tee_down' and 'tee_left' are a full edge line plus a full centre stem running away from that edge towards the opposite side. Gray blocks outside the panel are decoration. Which symbol do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, ex, tee_up, tee_right, tee_down, tee_left.

worlds.title: Bilateral halfstamp fold
worlds.question: Inside the dashed badge, flip the cyan stamp left-to-right and flip the coral stamp top-to-bottom. Superimpose the flipped 4x4 stamps, treating each lighter square as blank and keeping a dark square exactly where one stamp, but not both, is dark. Which symbol appears: X, ring, H, or U?

worlds.title: Scanline phase reveal
worlds.question: Circularly slide each horizontal band until its cyan square is leftmost. Ignore the cyan column. Which symbol do the dark squares form?

worlds.title: Hollow chamber balance
worlds.question: Imagine a horizontal line through the center of the colored shell. Does the upper half of the enclosed white chamber contain more pixels than the lower half? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Traced wire port
worlds.question: The picture shows a pale panel crossed by several dark wires. Every wire has the same dark colour and the same thickness, and each wire ends at one of the four coloured squares (red, green, blue, orange) on the rim of the panel; those squares are the ports. Exactly one wire carries a filled dark dot, clearly fatter than any wire, at its other end. Follow the wire that carries that dot, along its whole length, and report the colour of the port it ends at. Wires never cross one another. Answer unclear if the dotted wire reaches no port or more than one port, and also answer unclear if anywhere along its length the dotted wire touches, or leaves a gap narrower than two wire widths to, any other wire or any port other than the one at its own end. Which port does the dotted wire reach: red, green, blue, orange, or unclear?

worlds.title: Compact bend majority
worlds.question: Follow the blue trail from its red start to its green finish. The trail has exactly seven visible interior corners; count every corner as a left or right turn. Are there more left turns or more right turns? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Diagonal bisector patch
worlds.question: Imagine the two corner-to-corner diagonals of the square image. Which diagonal divides the colored patch into two more nearly equal areas: the rising diagonal (bottom-left to top-right) or the falling diagonal (top-left to bottom-right)? Answer rising or falling.

worlds.title: Route alternation search
worlds.question: Each sector contains one continuous five-segment route. Which sector contains the only route whose four successive turns alternate left, right, left, right (or the mirror-reversed equivalent) at every interior bend? Answer NW, NE, SW, or SE.

worlds.title: Halved patch balance search
worlds.question: The picture shows four solid dark patches arranged in one tight two-by-two cluster on a plain background: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right of that cluster. Each patch is a blocky shape built from small square tiles of one fixed size, and every patch is built from exactly the same number of tiles, so all four patches hold the same total dark area. A short straight coloured bar lies across each patch and cuts it into two parts, one part on each side of the bar; some bars are upright and some are flat. The dark area of a part is how much dark tile area lies on that side of the bar, which is not the same thing as how wide or how tall that side reaches. Exactly one patch is cut into two parts of equal dark area; the two equal parts of that patch have clearly different outlines, so equal area does not mean the patch looks mirrored or evenly spread about its bar. In each of the other three patches one part clearly holds more dark area than the other. The colours used, the outline shape of each patch, where the bar sits inside the patch outline, where the cluster sits on the page, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which patch of the cluster is cut by its bar into two parts of equal dark area? Answer with one of: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right.

worlds.title: Alternating badge search
worlds.question: Which labeled badge has different colors on every pair of squares that share an edge?

worlds.title: Balanced plate centroid search
worlds.question: Each panel shows one connected blue plate and a gold balance pin at the center of its square frame. Treat every visible blue part as equally heavy. Which plate has its center of area inside the gold pin? Exactly one does. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State route coverage
worlds.question: Start at the ringed badge and trace the one connected route in increasing station-number order. The token has four states A, B, C, and D. The badge colors mean red=A, green=B, blue=C, and purple=D. At each station, a filled right triangle advances one state cyclically A-B-C-D-A, a filled left triangle retreats one state, and an outlined square leaves the state unchanged. Include the starting state and every state after stations 1 through 9 in the visited history. Which state is never visited? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Relay jump pip tally
worlds.question: This picture contains six separated grey-framed cards, spread far apart across the canvas. Each card carries three things: a coloured square in its top-left corner, which is that card's own address colour; a coloured square in its top-right corner, which is the address colour of the card this card forwards to; and a row of one, two or three small dark squares along its bottom, which is that card's pip tally. The six address colours are all different and are drawn from red, green, blue, purple, orange and teal. A solid dark triangle floats just above exactly one card, and that card is where the relay starts. The relay lands on four cards in total: it lands first on the card under the triangle, and then makes exactly three jumps, each jump going from the card it is on to the card whose top-left address colour matches that card's top-right forwarding colour. Count the pips on every card the relay lands on and add them up; pips on cards the relay never lands on do not count, and every plain mid-grey square or circle outside the cards is inert decoration that counts for nothing. What is the total number of pips on the four cards the relay lands on?

worlds.title: Overdraft alarm wire
worlds.question: Begin with balance 0 and the alarm OFF. Follow the connected wire from its round gold START to the arrow. Each cyan bead deposits 1. Each coral bead withdraws 1 when the balance is above 0; if the balance is 0, that withdrawal leaves it at 0 and locks the alarm ON. Is the alarm ON at the arrow? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Quadrant rotor carpet
worlds.question: The colored disk marks the token's starting cell in the large 3-by-3 grid. Read the four small command grids from top to bottom. In each command, the bright 2-by-2 block identifies four cells whose contents rotate one corner clockwise: top-left to top-right to bottom-right to bottom-left to top-left. All other cells stay fixed. After all four commands, which cell holds the token: top-left, top, top-right, left, center, right, bottom-left, bottom, or bottom-right?

worlds.title: Nested depth duel
worlds.question: Which colored panel has the deeper nesting? Each panel is a stack of closed colored rings with one shared center; count the rings from the outside inward, and answer red or blue for the panel with more rings.

worlds.title: Unpaired window plate
worlds.question: This page carries five coloured plates - one red, one orange, one green, one blue and one purple - together with many grey plates. Only the five coloured plates decide the answer; grey plates are decoration and never count. Each plate is a solid slab with one or more square windows punched right through it, so that the page shows through each window; a window is fully surrounded by its own plate and never touches the edge of that plate. Count the windows of each coloured plate. Exactly four of the five coloured plates split into two pairs whose two members have equally many windows, and exactly one coloured plate has a window count matching no other coloured plate; call that plate the unpaired plate. Plate size, plate position and total ink are irrelevant. Which colour is the unpaired plate? Answer red, orange, green, blue, or purple.

worlds.title: Trapped area majority
worlds.question: Within the black square, is the total white area completely cut off from the square's border larger than the white area that can reach the border through edge-sharing white space? Corner touching alone does not connect white areas.

worlds.title: Pocket component balance
worlds.question: Ignore pale gray decorations. Does the navy frame enclose the same number of separate white pockets as there are detached navy tiles beside it? A pocket counts only when it is fully surrounded by navy, and touching navy tiles count as one. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Bridge cut terminal
worlds.question: Each disconnected green-to-terminal network has one ringed route segment. Imagine removing the ringed segment from each network. Which terminal—amber or violet—would then be disconnected from its green start? Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Port weave partner
worlds.question: The image shows several opaque light-gray square plates on a plain white background, all the same size and separated from one another by clear background. Each plate carries exactly four small coloured square ports, one flush against the middle of each of its four sides, and two thick dark bands drawn entirely inside that plate. On every plate the two bands join its four ports into two pairs: each band runs from one port to exactly one other port and the two bands never touch or cross. Exactly one plate in the image carries a green port; call it the wired plate, and ignore every other plate entirely. The wired plate's other three ports are one orange, one purple and one blue. Follow the dark band that leaves the green port and see which of those three ports it ends at. Which port does the band from the green port reach? Answer orange, purple or blue.

worlds.title: Turn run presence
worlds.question: Trace the navy centerline from the green start to the red finish. Among every pair of consecutive bends, is there any pair that turns the same way twice in a row (left-left or right-right)? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Second checkpoint trace
worlds.question: Beginning at the blue-ringed end, trace the single dark route. Of the four colored rings centered on it, which one is second along the route: red, gold, green, or purple?

worlds.title: Twin withdrawal equality
worlds.question: Two rows of nine square cells stand on a white card, one above the other; each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Beneath a cell of each row a small dark arrowhead points straight up at that one cell, marking it.  Imagine that marked cell is removed from each row entirely and the remaining cells are slid together to close the gap, keeping their left-to-right order.  Those shortened eight-cell rows are not drawn anywhere; only after withdrawing each marked cell do they exist.  Do the two surviving rows then read the same in dark and pale, cell for cell?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Color residual compare
worlds.question: Match bars by color. For each candidate, add the absolute height difference from REFERENCE across all four colors. Which candidate has the larger total difference: A, B, or tie?

worlds.title: Counterfactual trace divergence
worlds.question: A ball dropped from the black dot falls straight down, and each time it meets a slanted bar it slides to that bar's lower end and keeps falling from there. Four bars are colored and one bar is red. Drop the ball twice: first on the board exactly as drawn, then on the board with only the red bar re-leaned the opposite way. Exactly one colored bar is met on the second drop but not on the first. Which colored bar is it? Answer blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Reciprocal badge crossmatch
worlds.question: Exactly two rows CROSS-MATCH: the LEFT badge of each is identical to the RIGHT badge of the other. Which two keys label those rows? Both directions must match; order does not matter. Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Simultaneous neighbor rewrite
worlds.question: The START row has seven cells. Make four new rows, one step at a time. At every step, update all cells at once: a new cell is dark exactly when exactly one of its three source cells (itself and its two neighbors) was dark in the previous row. Beyond either end counts as light. Which option is the fourth new row? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Count correspondence
worlds.question: The gray cluster at the top contains a certain number of disks. Below it are three colored clusters, each with a different number of disks and a different color. Which colored cluster contains exactly the same number of disks as the gray cluster? Answer with that cluster's color (red, green, or blue).

worlds.title: Colored collinearity signature correspondence
worlds.question: The image shows a REFERENCE panel and candidate panels A and B. Each panel contains six uniquely colored dots. Exactly three dot centers in each panel lie on one shared straight line, and no other triple is collinear. Which candidate has the same set of three colors on the line as the REFERENCE? Panels may be translated, rotated, or reflected; ignore panel position, dot position, dot size, and drawing order. A is the left candidate and B is the right candidate. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Pour area conservation binding
worlds.question: This image is a record of a pouring experiment, drawn as two stacked panels separated by a horizontal rule. Above the rule stand four open vessels. The vessels are deliberately built to different widths, and each one holds a solid slab of liquid resting on its floor: one red slab, one blue slab, one green slab and one orange slab. Below the rule stand four narrow measuring tubes. Every tube was manufactured to one and the same width, and every tube is shaded in one identical gray, so nothing about a tube's shading identifies where its contents came from. Each vessel above was emptied into exactly one tube below and each tube received exactly one vessel. No tube stands underneath the vessel it received, so vertical position is uninformative. Pouring deforms a slab of liquid but destroys none of it, so the shaded area inside a tube is equal to the shaded area of the slab that was poured into it. Since the vessels were built to different widths, a tall narrow slab can carry less liquid than a short wide one, and the tallest slab above need not correspond to the tallest column below. A black triangle is printed above exactly one of the tubes. Which colour was the liquid that was poured into the marked tube? Answer with red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Panel half exchange
worlds.question: Cut the REFERENCE board at the dashed vertical line. Exchange its left and right halves without rotating or flipping either half. Which colored border encloses the exact result? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Turn signature path correspondence
worlds.question: The gray REFERENCE path and the three colored-border paths may be rotated as wholes, and their straight segment lengths may differ. Starting at the yellow dot and traveling to the cyan dot, compare only the ordered sequence of left and right turns at the black bend dots. A mirror reflection does not count. Which candidate border color has exactly the same turn sequence: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Projected reach compare
worlds.question: A gray vertical line marks a reference column on a light panel. Two thick diagonal strokes, one red and one blue, are drawn on either side of it. Slip each stroke straight along its own tilt until its line meets the gray line; the height of that meeting is the stroke's reach. Which colored stroke's best-fit line reaches HIGHER on the panel (closer to the top) at the gray reference line? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Histogram skew compare
worlds.question: Panel A is the left histogram and panel B is the right histogram. Each has seven equal-width bins with visible integer count bars on one shared vertical scale. For each panel, compute the weighted mean bin number using bar counts, then subtract the median bin number, defined as the first bin whose cumulative count reaches at least half the total. Which panel has the larger mean-minus-median value? Choose A or B; ties and near ties are quarantined.

worlds.title: Undershoot gap rank
worlds.question: The picture shows five horizontal LANES stacked one above another. Each lane holds exactly one solid coloured bar -- one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple -- and exactly one solid BLACK upright tick, which is taller than the bar and is that lane's own TARGET. A lane's tick belongs only to that lane: read every bar against the black tick drawn in the same lane and never against any other lane's tick. A bar STOPS SHORT when its right-hand end lies to the LEFT of its own tick, and its SHORTFALL is the horizontal distance from that end rightwards to the tick. Some bars instead run PAST their own tick, so the tick is drawn across them; those bars have no shortfall at all and can never be the answer, however far past the tick they run. The answer is the colour of the bar with the LARGEST SHORTFALL. In every picture at least two bars stop short and at least one bar runs past its tick, and the largest bar-to-tick distance in the picture always belongs to a bar that runs PAST its tick, so unsigned distance is a trap. Where a bar begins, how long it is and how much colour it carries are all uninformative: in every picture the longest bar, the shortest bar, the bar starting furthest left, the bar whose end lies furthest left and the lane whose tick stands furthest right each belong to a colour that is NOT the answer, and the top-to-bottom position of a lane is the answer no more often than chance allows. The pale grey vertical rules, the pale grey lane lines and the grey stubs at the left edge are decoration and mean nothing. Which colour's bar has the largest shortfall? Answer red, green, blue, orange or purple.

worlds.title: Band run leader
worlds.question: Which colored row has the longest consecutive run of circular checkpoints fully inside its gray tolerance band? A checkpoint is inside only when the whole colored circle lies between the band's top and bottom edges. Answer blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Triangle area leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order and share the same scale. Using the centers of the three colored markers as vertices, which panel's triangle has the largest area? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior floor planks
worlds.question: A well-laid floor is often assumed to have planks of one uniform width, but report what is actually drawn here, not a prior. Are all the visible plank widths equal? Answer only yes or no.

worlds.title: Mailbox flag state
worlds.question: Is the mailbox's signal flag raised or lowered? Treat the long colored signal arm and its small pennant as the flag; raised means the arm extends upward from its pivot, and lowered means it extends horizontally toward the mailbox body. Ignore the mailbox, post, and MAILBOX label. Answer raised or lowered.

worlds.title: Shadow sun side
worlds.question: This picture is a simple daytime drawing on white paper: a blue page frame, one or more pale blue clouds, a yellow sun disk in the sky, a dark green ground line, a brown tree trunk with a green crown standing on that line, and one grey shadow shape lying on the ground and touching the foot of the trunk. The frame, the clouds, the crown and the ground line are fixed decoration and never indicate the answer. Compare only horizontal, left-right positions, measured against the trunk: the sun is on the left of the trunk when the yellow disk lies further left than the trunk and on the right otherwise, and the shadow is on the left of the trunk when the grey shape stretches from the foot of the trunk towards the left and on the right otherwise. The height of the sun, its size, the length and thickness of the grey shadow, the size of the tree, the number and placement of the clouds, the position of everything on the page and the exact shades of the colours all change from picture to picture and never indicate the answer. Answer from the shadow that is actually painted in this picture, not from the side a shadow would fall on in the real world. Is the painted grey shadow on the same side of the trunk as the yellow sun, or on the opposite side? Answer with exactly one of the words same or opposite.

worlds.title: Ladder rail gap
worlds.question: Compare the clear gap between the two colored side rails at their top ends and bottom ends. Is the top gap narrower, equal, or wider? Answer narrower, equal, or wider.

worlds.title: Signal red slot conflict
worlds.question: Which position holds the red lamp: top, middle, or bottom? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Panel collate reveal
worlds.question: The image shows nine square panels, each framed by a thin blue border, scattered across the field. Each panel holds one piece of a letter and carries a small blue dot near its lower edge whose left-to-right position marks that piece's place in the reassembly order. Reassemble the panels into a three-by-three grid: put the piece with the leftmost dot in the top-left cell, advancing left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Which letter, A or B, do the reassembled panels form? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Checkerboard polarity reveal
worlds.question: Use the four colored corner marks to locate the grayscale square. Its alternating dark and light pixels are a carrier. Starting from the polarity at the upper-left pixel, invert gray contrast about 128 on every other pixel, then apply a 7x7 mean with edge replication and ignore the marks and border. Which symbol appears: arch, fork, knot, or stair?

worlds.title: Halftone density reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one square panel enclosed by a blue frame. The panel is divided into a grid of 5 rows and 5 columns of equal square cells, and the cell edges are not drawn. Every cell is printed with the same two greys: a fine speckle of tiny dark blocks on a light background, identical in tone everywhere, but packed more densely in some cells than in others. Blur the panel, or step far back from it, until the individual blocks can no longer be told apart and each cell becomes one flat tone; the densely packed cells then read as the darker cells. Exactly 9 of the 25 cells are the darker ones. Ignore the small orange squares printed on top of the speckle: they are decoration and carry no information about the answer. The 9 darker cells of the blurred grid form a shape that most closely matches one of these six symbols: diamond, ell, ex, flag, plus, zee. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Size rank path trace
worlds.question: Draw straight segments connecting the colored dots from smallest to largest. Which path appears: inward spiral, row snake, crossing star, or diagonal weave?

worlds.title: Row seam composite glyph
worlds.question: The upper and lower cyan-framed mosaics use the same 5-by-5 cell coordinates. In each row of the gold middle key, its one gold dot marks the last column to take from the upper mosaic. Build a 5-by-5 result by taking that row's cells through the marked column from the upper mosaic and all cells strictly to its right from the lower mosaic. Keep every cell in its original position; do not rotate or reflect. Which coral reference card matches? Cards A, B, C, and D are in reading order: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

worlds.title: Convex hull vertex count
worlds.question: Black dots form a scattered group. Imagine the tightest convex polygon that wraps around them all so that no dot lies outside it. How many corners (vertices) does that enclosing polygon have? Choose: 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Euler thread network
worlds.question: Three colored link networks share six gray waypoints. Which color labels a network that can be traced in one continuous stroke, using every colored link exactly once and never lifting the stroke? Ignore the gray waypoints as links; choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Illusory corner cycle
worlds.question: The picture shows ten dark discs of the same size on a plain background. Each disc has one pale wedge cut into it, and the tip of every wedge sits exactly at the centre of its own disc, so each wedge has two straight sides that are rays leaving that disc's centre. Some of the discs are the corners of one hidden polygon whose sides are never drawn: for each corner disc, one straight side of its wedge points exactly at the centre of one neighbouring corner disc and the other straight side points exactly at the centre of the other neighbouring corner disc, so the wedge opens toward the inside of the polygon. Exactly one such closed ring of discs exists, and every disc in it has exactly two neighbours in it. All the other discs are decoys: no straight side of a decoy's wedge points at any disc that points back at it. Two discs count as pointing at each other only when both wedge sides line up with the joining direction to within about nine degrees. The hidden polygon has three, four or five corners. The colours, the disc size, the wedge sizes, the total number of discs, the positions of the discs and the amount of ink carry no information. How many discs are corners of the hidden polygon? Answer 3, 4 or 5.

worlds.title: White corridor connectivity
worlds.question: In the maze, can the two colored disks be joined by one continuous path through the white corridors without crossing a dark wall? Corner-only contact does not count. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Constellation scale center
worlds.question: The small solid dark dots and large hollow dark rings are two versions of the same constellation. The hollow constellation is one enlargement of the solid constellation from a fixed center, with no rotation or slide: corresponding marks lie on the same ray and share one scale factor. Which colored ring marks the enlargement center? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Closed contour quadrant
worlds.question: The image is divided by thin lines into four quadrants: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. Each quadrant contains one dark outline contour. Exactly one of the four contours is completely closed: a full ring whose two ends meet with no gap. The other three contours are open arcs that each have a visible gap in the ring. Which quadrant contains the only completely closed contour? Answer with the quadrant name.

worlds.title: Reference attribute conjunction search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only candidate object that matches both the outer outline and the stripe direction shown in the reference box? Treat stripe directions as undirected lines: a candidate matches the reference stripe when their smaller angle difference modulo 180 degrees is at most 14 degrees. Inspect every object and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Chiral match panel
worlds.question: The framed box at the top of this image shows a reference shape. A thick horizontal line separates that box from a row of four panels, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right and separated by thick vertical lines. Each panel holds one solid shape drawn at its own arbitrary rotation. Exactly one panel holds the same shape as the reference, turned in the plane only, so it could be slid and rotated onto the reference without ever being flipped over. Exactly one other panel holds the mirror image of the reference shape, which can only be brought onto the reference by flipping it over; the two remaining panels hold shapes that are neither. The reference is drawn slightly smaller than the panel shapes, so only its form matters, not its size. Every shape in the image has the same colour, and the four panel shapes have the same size, the same area and the same amount of ink, so colour, size, ink and panel position carry no information about the answer. Does the rotated, un-flipped copy of the reference shape lie in the left half of the row (panels 1 and 2) or the right half (panels 3 and 4)? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Color wire match search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has every dark wire joining two circles of the SAME color? At crossings, each wire continues straight. Panels A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: All lines separate search
worlds.question: Each card contains a red dot, a blue dot, and three dark straight lines. Which labeled card has the two dots on opposite sides of every one of its three lines? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State trajectory coverage
worlds.question: Four square panels are stacked vertically and read top to bottom as panel 1, panel 2, panel 3, panel 4. Every panel shows the same static 3x3 grid of cells. One token (a filled red disk) sits in a single cell of each panel. The magenta ring marks the token's starting cell in the top panel. Between each consecutive pair of panels a navy dot declares the token's one-cell move (up, down, left, or right) to the next panel. Following the moves in order from the ringed start cell, how many distinct cells does the token occupy across all four panels? Count the start cell in panel 1 and every cell it lands on. Answer '1', '2', '3', or '4'.

worlds.title: State terminal mode
worlds.question: Read P1 through P6 from left to right. For each label, count how often its P6 state appears in its own six-panel trajectory. Which label has the largest count? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Deflector drop route
worlds.question: The picture shows a board with seven columns, marked by seven faint vertical guide lines and by the seven grey chutes drawn in a row along the bottom. Number the columns and their chutes 1 to 7 from left to right. A blue ball is drawn above the board: the ball starts in the column whose guide line is nearest to the centre of the blue ball. On the board there are five levels of arrows, and the ball falls through the levels from top to bottom, as the grey arrow in the left margin shows. Each arrow is drawn in one column of one level; an orange arrow points right and a purple arrow points left. On each level, only the arrow standing in the ball's own column has any effect: that arrow pushes the ball one column in the direction it points, and the ball then falls on to the next level from its new column. Every other arrow on that level does nothing to this ball. If there is no arrow in the ball's column on a level, the ball falls straight down to the next level. No arrow in the picture would push the ball off the side of the board, and no arrow on a level can push the ball into another arrow of that same level, so at most one arrow acts per level. The arrows never move, and the ball is drawn only once, in its starting column; no later position of the ball is drawn anywhere. After the ball has fallen through all five levels, which numbered chute does it land in? Answer with a single number from 1 to 7, counting chutes from the left.

worlds.title: Grid axis toggle replay
worlds.question: Start with the marked lamp's shown state. Read the five cards from left to right. Each card's colored bar marks one whole row or column to flip; every lamp on that bar changes ON to OFF or OFF to ON. Is the marked lamp ON or OFF after all five flips?

worlds.title: Cube orientation rolls
worlds.question: The diagram is an unfolded cube: the center square is initially TOP; its neighbors above, right, below, and left are the NORTH, EAST, SOUTH, and WEST faces, and the far lower square is BOTTOM. Read the roll cards from left to right: 1 pip means roll north, 2 east, 3 south, and 4 west. A north roll brings the south face to the top; an east roll brings the west face to the top (south and west are the inverse rolls). Which pip count is on TOP after every roll? Answer 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Shared white region
worlds.question: The image shows several closed black rings drawn on a white background. A ring seals off its own white pocket, and the white area outside all the rings is one further white region. Three small colored dots - one red, one green, one blue - are placed in the picture. Two dots are in the SAME white region when they sit in the same continuous white area (the same sealed pocket, or the same connected outside area), reachable from one to the other without crossing any black ring ink. Exactly two of the three dots lie in the same white region; the third lies in a different one. Which two colored dots are in the same white region? Answer with exactly one of red-green, red-blue, or green-blue.

worlds.title: Bridge link selection
worlds.question: Which colored link is the only bridge in the network? A bridge is a link whose removal increases the number of connected node components. Choose red, blue, or green; ignore text, node outlines, and the frame.

worlds.title: Taut cord pick
worlds.question: The picture shows three coloured cords lying on white paper - one red, one green and one blue - together with several solid black pegs. Each cord is a single curve that is pinned to the paper at its own two ends; no cord touches another cord and no cord touches a peg. Now imagine pulling one cord tight, keeping its own two pinned ends exactly where they are: the cord sweeps across the paper and, with nothing in its way, ends up lying along the straight line that joins those same two pinned ends. A peg gets in the way of that pull exactly when the peg lies inside the area shut in between that cord as it is drawn and the straight line joining that same cord's own two pinned ends; that straight line is not drawn in the picture. Pegs outside that shut-in area never get in the way, and the other two cords never get in the way. Exactly one of the three cords can be pulled completely straight with no peg in the way; each of the other two shuts at least one peg inside. Which cord can be pulled completely straight - red, green or blue?

worlds.title: Common enclosure pair
worlds.question: Black outlines are closed loops. A loop jointly encloses a colored pair when both same-colored dots are inside it. Which colored pair is jointly enclosed by exactly two black loops? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Removable gate connectivity
worlds.question: Do the green and purple gates border at least one same enclosed white chamber? A chamber is a side-connected white region completely surrounded by the dark wall network; touching only at a corner does not connect regions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Farthest terminal on path
worlds.question: Walking only along the blue line from the orange ring, which coloured dot -- red or green -- is farther away along the path? Answer red or green.

worlds.title: Junction arm count selection
worlds.question: Follow the dark network from the green source to the red target. Which shape-marked junction on that route has more connected arms: the circle or the square? Answer circle or square.

worlds.title: Route required node
worlds.question: This picture shows a network of round junctions joined by grey wires. A wire runs from one junction to another and may bend on the way, but wires only meet at junctions and the wiring contains no loop, so between any two junctions there is exactly one route through the network. One junction is green and one junction is red. Three junctions are coloured blue, orange and purple; all remaining junctions are dark grey. Travel only along the wires. Where you sit in the picture does not matter, only what the wires connect. Exactly one of the blue, orange and purple junctions is passed through on the route from the green junction to the red junction. Which coloured junction is on that route? Answer blue, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Two speed rendezvous checkpoint
worlds.question: Two walkers start together at the green and red circles and move toward each other on the one dark chain. In each round, green moves two links while red moves one. Which colored checkpoint do they reach at the same time? A link is one dark segment between adjacent circles. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Two route terminal
worlds.question: Each box is a separate network. In which box can green START reach the colored terminal by two routes that share no black link? Links meet only at circles and never cross. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Seam key completion correspondence
worlds.question: The navy workbench contains a reference patch R and candidate patches A and B. Each patch is one connected 3x3 core with four thick seam keys of lengths 1, 2, or 3 grid units, and all three patches have equal total ink. Rotate each candidate patch 90 degrees clockwise. Read the lengths of the up, right, down, and left keys on the transformed patch. Which candidate has exactly the same four-length completion signature as R? Answer with that candidate's marker color.

worlds.title: Bracket cord partner bind
worlds.question: The picture shows one cream board carrying a single thin slate-grey cord. The cord runs as a staircase of straight horizontal and vertical runs from one corner of the board to the opposite corner; it never crosses or touches itself, and one of its two ends is capped by a solid black disc. Twelve small coloured squares, the BEADS, sit on the cord. Each bead is red, orange, green, teal, blue or purple, and colours repeat. Every bead is either SOLID, filled right through with its colour, or HOLLOW, with a small cream window cut out of its middle. Solid and hollow beads have exactly the same outline, size and colour area apart from that window, so only the window tells them apart. Walk along the cord starting from the black capped end and read the beads in the order you meet them. In that order the beads form a properly nested bracket word: a solid bead OPENS a group, a hollow bead CLOSES the group that was opened most recently and is still open, and every group is opened and closed exactly once. The cord is not laid out simply left to right or top to bottom - it contains a run that doubles back - so the order along the cord is not the order of the beads by position, and sorting the beads by row, by column, or by straight-line distance from the black cap gives a different and wrong reading. Exactly one solid bead is surrounded by a magenta square frame. The bead that closes it is always at least five beads further along the cord, so it is never the next hollow bead you meet, and it is never the last bead on the cord. Bead colours are chosen independently of the bracket structure, and the answer colour is always worn by more than one bead, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies the answer on its own. Find the hollow bead that closes the framed solid bead. What is the colour of that hollow bead? Answer red, orange, green, teal, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Window majority seal
worlds.question: The gold-framed 5-by-5 mosaic is the source. Move a 3-by-3 window across every possible position, without wrapping. Each result tile is cyan when at least five of the nine source tiles in its window are cyan; otherwise it is cream. Keep the window positions as a 3-by-3 result. Which red, green, or blue tag marks the exact result?

worlds.title: Affine beacon correspondence
worlds.question: The circle, square, and triangle are matching landmarks. Imagine stretching or skewing the entire left landmark triangle until each shape lands on its matching shape at right; the magenta dot moves with that same whole-triangle warp. Which colored dot is where the magenta dot lands? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Route checkpoint order
worlds.question: Following the arrow from the purple start marker to the gray terminal cap, which checkpoint comes first: orange or teal? Answer orange or teal.

worlds.title: Column stack depth
worlds.question: The picture is a pale instrument sheet carrying exactly six pure-black horizontal bars, arranged as two bars on each of three well-separated levels. No two black bars touch, and the two bars of one level are always separated by blank paper. Every coloured mark - blue, green, orange, purple or grey, whether a bar or a speck - is decoration and carries no information. Only the horizontal extent of each black bar matters: a vertical line crosses a black bar when it passes through the columns that bar covers, and the level a bar sits on is irrelevant. Imagine sliding a single vertical line all the way across the sheet and, at every position, counting how many of the six black bars it crosses. What is the largest count reached at any position? Answer with a single whole number: 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Trace arc length balance
worlds.question: Does more of the cyan trace's arc length lie above or below the dashed gray reference line? Answer above or below.

worlds.title: Strata boundary variation
worlds.question: The filled colored stratum has equal-width steps. Moving left to right, add the absolute heights of every vertical jump along the top edge, and separately along the bottom edge; horizontal runs do not count. Which total is greater: TOP or BOTTOM?

worlds.title: Stop sign side count
worlds.question: How many sides does the visible STOP sign have? Answer with a whole number.

worlds.title: Drop tip bearing
worlds.question: This picture shows one solid coloured blob shaped like a falling drop: a round body with exactly one drawn-out pointed tip, filled in a single colour with no holes. The tip points closer to one of the four edges of the picture -- top, bottom, left or right -- than to any corner. A short grey bar and a few small grey specks are drawn well away from the drop; they are decoration only, and where they lie tells you nothing about which way the drop's tip points. Which edge of the picture does the drop's tip point toward? Answer with exactly one of: top, bottom, left, right.

worlds.title: Anaglyph lens order
worlds.question: Are the two colored lenses in standard anaglyph order: red on the left and cyan on the right? Judge the visible lens colors only. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Butterfly spot order
worlds.question: Reading the four colored spots from top to bottom on each butterfly wing, is the color order the same on both wings? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Serpentine strip reassembly
worlds.question: Start at the green cap, reassemble the four route panels left-to-right onto one baseline, and read the resulting strip. Is it A) a wave or B) a fork? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Tally sort reveal
worlds.question: This picture shows one square panel with a dark border. Inside the border is a seven-row, seven-column field of equal square cells; each cell is either dark or pale, and exactly thirteen cells are dark in every picture. Just to the left of the panel, separated from it and from one another by background, float seven dark tally bars, one beside each panel row and vertically centred on that row. The seven bars all have different lengths. A few small clutter marks - little squares, diamonds and narrow upright rules - lie elsewhere on the background, never beside the panel rows, and carry no evidence. Carry out this operation. Keeping each panel row's seven cells together and in their left-to-right order, reorder the seven rows by the length of the bar beside them: the row whose bar is shortest becomes the top row, the row whose bar is next shortest becomes the second row, and so on down to the row with the longest bar, which becomes the bottom row. The rows are never moved sideways and no cell changes colour. The reordered dark cells always form exactly one of six symbols on the seven-by-seven field. 'cross' is a full centre row crossing a full centre column. 'tee' is a full top row with a full centre column hanging from it. 'zigzag' is a flat bar near the top and a flat bar lower down, joined by a short diagonal that runs from the upper bar down and to the left. 'corners' is four separated two-by-two-style corner elbows, one in each corner, with a single dark cell at the centre. 'stripes' is three separated flat bars, one above another, with two empty rows between neighbouring bars. 'columns' is three separated upright bars of equal height with a single dark cell below the middle one. The symbol is never drawn in the picture as it stands: the panel alone shows the seven rows in a scrambled order and settles nothing, and the bars alone give only an order and carry no cell of the symbol, so the panel and the separated gutter must both be read. Which symbol do the reordered dark cells form? Answer with exactly one of: columns, corners, cross, stripes, tee, zigzag.

worlds.title: Tip to tail resultant
worlds.question: Move the teal arrow without rotating it until its tail touches the amber arrow's tip. Draw one straight arrow from the amber tail to the moved teal tip. Which way does that resulting arrow point: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Antipodal midpoint fold
worlds.question: Start at the red ring and follow the one connected dark thread to the gold triangle. Ignore the pale background dots. Read its eighteen cyan beads in travel order. Pair first with last, second with next-to-last, and so on. Replace each pair by the exact midpoint of its bead centers and connect the nine midpoints in first-half order. Ignoring only position, rotation, and uniform size, which path is closest: chevron, zigzag, or hook? Chevron means four equal diagonal steps to one tip then four away; zigzag means eight advancing diagonal steps alternating sides; hook means six equal straight steps then two equal right-angle steps. Answer ambiguous only if the two closest paths tie.

worlds.title: Paired window clearance
worlds.question: Which colored plaque has the smaller top clearance around its window: amber or teal? Answer amber or teal.

worlds.title: Stripe phase wedge
worlds.question: The picture shows exactly one pale card on a light page, and the card is filled with straight dark bars. Every pale grey blob outside the card is background clutter and must be ignored. All bars have the same dark colour and the same thickness, they all run in the same direction, and they are spaced by one constant pitch, where a pitch means the distance from one bar to the next bar; so colour, thickness, bar count, card position, card size and the total amount of dark ink say nothing about the answer. Somewhere inside the card there is exactly one triangular patch in which the bars are shifted sideways, across the bars, by exactly half a pitch, so that inside the patch the bars sit in the gaps of the bars outside it. Nothing else marks that patch: it has no outline, no colour of its own and no extra ink, and it can be seen only where the bars fail to line up along its border. The patch is a triangle with two equal sides, so it has one straight side, its base, and one opposite corner, its tip, and the tip points straight up, straight down, straight left or straight right on the page. Report the direction in which the tip of the patch points. Answer unclear if the patch is too small to read, that is if either its base or its depth from base to tip spans fewer than about four pitches. Which way does the tip of the shifted patch point: up, down, left, right, or unclear?

worlds.title: Diagonal quadrant balance
worlds.question: The connected island contains exactly 84 equal colored squares. Around the black cross, which opposite quadrant pair contains more colored area: rising (lower-left plus upper-right) or falling (upper-left plus lower-right)? Answer rising or falling.

worlds.title: Convergent ring gaps
worlds.question: Four separate broken rings form a quartet. Do all four open gaps face the common center of the quartet? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Column cover clip search
worlds.question: The picture shows four clips on a plain page, arranged in one tight two-by-two cluster: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left and lower-right of that cluster. A clip is two separate rows of small solid squares, an upper row and a lower row, with a clear empty gap between them and no mark joining them. The squares of both rows of a clip stand on the same eight evenly spaced column positions of that clip, so every square of the lower row sits directly below one column position of the upper row. Each of the eight columns of a clip therefore holds one square, two squares stacked one above the other, or no square at all: a column is covered once when exactly one of the clip's two rows has a square there, covered twice when both rows have a square there, and left bare when neither row has one. Every clip contains exactly eight squares in total, so the four clips carry exactly the same amount of ink and the same number of squares, and counting squares can never name a clip. Exactly one clip has all eight of its columns covered exactly once. Every other clip has at least one doubly covered column and exactly as many bare columns as doubly covered ones. Both rows of a clip must be read together: one row on its own never decides anything, and the leftmost and the rightmost column of every clip, including the losing ones, are always covered exactly once. The ink colours, which row of a clip holds more squares, the small sideways and up-and-down shifts of the clips, where the cluster sits on the page, and the tiny isolated specks dotted about the background all carry no information. Which clip of the cluster has every one of its eight columns covered by exactly one square? Answer with one of: upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, lower-right.

worlds.title: Same turn route search
worlds.question: Start at each cyan dot and follow its black route to the colored dot. Which route turns the same way at every square corner—always left or always right? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Domino cover search
worlds.question: Each color forms one connected island of 16 equal square cells on its own five-by-five lattice. A domino covers exactly two cells that share a full edge. Which color's island can be completely covered by eight non-overlapping dominoes, with no cell left over? Exactly one can. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State split identity
worlds.question: The left panel is the initial snapshot and the right panel is the final snapshot. Matching outer disk colors identify the same token across panels; the ring marks the initial token. In the final panel, badge colors mean gold A, orange B, green C, and blue D. Which state badge does the initially ringed token carry? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Crest watermark trail
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one thin grey trail: a single line of constant width that zigzags along but never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself. One end of the trail carries a solid black round bead and the other end carries a solid black square block. The walk starts at the round bead and follows the trail all the way to the square block. Small coloured triangles sit directly on the trail, each coloured red, green, blue or purple. A triangle whose point aims upwards adds one to a running count, and a triangle whose point aims downwards takes one away from it. The count is zero at the bead, it changes only when the walk meets a triangle, and it is allowed to fall below zero. Exactly one triangle on the trail is the place where the running count reaches its highest value. Only the order of the triangles along the trail matters, not how far apart they are and not where they sit on the canvas. The trail may lie anywhere in the picture, and every pale grey shape lying off the trail is inert decoration. What colour is the triangle at which the running count reaches its highest value? Answer with one of red, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Relay ribbon replay
worlds.question: The bead begins in the color shown at the ribbon's round start. Follow the connected ribbon toward its arrow tip. Each cyan span advances red to green to blue to red; each violet span swaps red and blue while green stays green. What color is the bead at the tip?

worlds.title: Four corner entry ledger
worlds.question: Order the four detached cards by their purple pips (1 to 4). Track cyan, amber, and rose separately. Count one inward crossing for each OUTSIDE-to-INSIDE change between adjacent snapshots; INSIDE-to-OUTSIDE does not count. Which color has the greatest number of inward crossings: cyan, amber, or rose?

worlds.title: Branch path membership
worlds.question: In the one connected dark tree, is the green marker on the unique route joining the red and blue markers? Answer yes or no. Ignore pale corner marks.

worlds.title: Strand break loop match
worlds.question: This page shows two black figures far apart, one on each side, together with grey decorations. Grey never counts. One black figure is a strand that snakes back and forth; a few visible gaps are cut right through it, so it falls into separate pieces, and two parts belong to the same piece only when black ink joins them along the strand. The other black figure is a frame of two long rails crossed by several bars; a bar that reaches both rails closes off a white loop, while a bar that stops short of the far rail closes nothing, so the number of loops is the number of white areas the frame surrounds completely.
