Count the pieces of the strand and the loops of the frame. Which side of the page each figure sits on, figure size, bar count, gap positions and total ink are all irrelevant. Does the strand have exactly as many pieces as the frame has loops? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Double courtyard seam
worlds.question: Which colored wall segment—cyan or orange—shares an edge with two different enclosed white courtyards? A courtyard is white space that cannot reach the image edge through edge-sharing white pixels; corner touching does not connect regions.

worlds.title: Pocket merger patch
worlds.question: The amber patch is solid now. If only that amber patch were erased to white, would two enclosed white pockets merge into one enclosed pocket? A pocket is white space fully surrounded by solid teal or amber; white areas connect through shared edges, not diagonal corners. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cycle rank terminal
worlds.question: Two disconnected route networks are shown. Each has a green start and one terminal, amber or violet. Which terminal is attached to the network with more independent loops? Count enclosed route cycles in each network; answer amber or violet. Use topology, not position, color, or total ink.

worlds.title: Snake side tally
worlds.question: The picture shows one connected teal wire that zigzags between two horizontal levels. A violet ring marks the port at one end of the wire; the wire's other end is bare. Five orange squares and three gray squares sit beside the wire, each separated from it by a visible gap. The gray squares are decoys and mean nothing. Walk along the teal wire starting at the violet ringed port and continue to the bare end, following every bend. Each orange square lies on your left hand or on your right hand as you pass it, judged against the direction you are walking along the piece of wire that that square sits beside. Do you pass more orange squares on your left or more on your right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Checkpoint span comparison
worlds.question: Trace the navy route. Which matching-color checkpoint pair is farther apart when distance is measured along the route: cyan or orange?

worlds.title: Paired bend parity
worlds.question: Two separate navy routes are shown. Starting at each blue circle, follow its route to the orange square. Count only the square 90-degree corners, not the endpoints. Do the two routes have the same bend parity—both even or both odd? Answer yes or no. Ignore pale gray dashes.

worlds.title: Tabbed partner match
worlds.question: Two columns of square slots, left and right.  Every slot carries a small coloured tab: cyan, magenta, or amber.  Each column uses all three tab colours once, but the right column's top-to-bottom order differs from the left.  A left slot and a right slot are PARTNERS when they share the same tab colour.  Every slot also holds a marker that is either a solid dark square or a hollow square.  A pair is TRUE when the two partner slots (same tab colour) hold the same marker kind.  How many true partners are there: zero, one, two, or three?

worlds.title: Dual register branch
worlds.question: Start with the ordered pair in START. The color cycle is amber → cyan → violet → amber. Read the seven COMMAND cards left to right. Each card has a color and a + or − sign. If its color matches the left register, move the right register one step in the signed direction; otherwise move the left register one step in the opposite direction. Carry both registers forward. Which two-letter code is active after command 7? Answer with the code from the key.

worlds.title: Pan balance makeweight
worlds.question: The two rows at the top are equalities: the black shapes left of a double bar are worth exactly the circles to its right, and a circle is worth one. Neither row prices a shape on its own, so use both together to find what a triangle and a square are worth. The two gray pans are not worth the same. Exactly one colored purse holds shapes worth exactly the difference between the pans, so adding it to the lighter pan would balance them. Which purse is it? Answer blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Exclusive chip assignment
worlds.question: Pair all four badges with all four parcels, using each once. A pair is allowed only when its two cards share exactly one colored chip. There is exactly one complete pairing. Which parcel pairs with START: parcel-A, parcel-B, parcel-C, or parcel-D?

worlds.title: Carried pin landing
worlds.question: The green pin travels with the blue cells. First reflect both across the dashed red line. Then rotate only the blue cells 90 degrees clockwise about the pin's new position. Which option's amber cells mark the final blue-cell positions? Answer option-1, option-2, option-3, or option-4.

worlds.title: Arc sweep correspondence
worlds.question: The gray gauge at the top is a pivot hub with a gray arc that sweeps out a certain central angle. Below it are three colored gauges A, B, C: one is red, one green, one blue, and each arc sweeps a different angle. Which colored gauge has an arc that sweeps out exactly the same central angle as the gray gauge? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Delaunay face correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate has the same complete set of color triples that form Delaunay triangles as the reference? Use the six colored point centers; a triangle is included when its circumcircle contains no other point. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Unit rescaled bar value binding
worlds.question: This image has two framed panels, one above the other. In each panel the short black bar at the bottom left is that panel's unit ruler, and the two panels use different unit-ruler lengths. The upper panel contains four horizontal colored bars (red, blue, green, orange). The lower panel contains four horizontal gray bars. Every bar and every unit ruler starts at the same left edge inside its own panel. A bar's value is its length divided by the length of the unit ruler in its own panel. The four values in the lower panel are exactly the four values in the upper panel, so each gray bar has one matching colored bar. The small black square in the left margin of the lower panel marks one gray bar. Which colored bar has the same value as the marked gray bar? Answer with one word: red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Overlap membership match
worlds.question: The top card is the REFERENCE. Every card has one dot of each color and two overlapping regions: a blue circle and a purple rectangle. A dot's pattern is whether its center is inside or outside each region. Which colored border marks the bottom card where all four dot colors have exactly the same circle-and-rectangle membership pattern as the reference? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Rotated mosaic crop correspondence
worlds.question: The 4 by 4 REFERENCE window was copied from somewhere in the 8 by 8 TARGET mosaic, then rotated as a whole by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees. Find its unique match without reflecting it, and map the magenta-ringed REFERENCE cell back through that same rotation. What color ring marks that TARGET cell: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Band containment count
worlds.question: A blue horizontal band is formed by two parallel full-width lines, and several black circular markers lie scattered at various heights. How many of the black markers have their centre strictly between the two blue lines (inside the band)? Answer with only a whole number.

worlds.title: Box whisker asymmetry
worlds.question: Panel A is the left box-and-whisker plot and panel B is the right one. For each plot, divide the absolute difference between the left whisker length (minimum to Q1) and right whisker length (Q3 to maximum) by its full minimum-to-maximum span. Which panel has the larger normalized whisker asymmetry? Choose A or B; quarantine ties, near ties, or unclear box plots.

worlds.title: Slope extension finish
worlds.question: The picture shows four straight coloured segments, one red, one green, one blue and one orange, and a single solid black vertical line near the right-hand edge which is the FINISH LINE. Every coloured segment stops well short of the finish line and never touches it. Continue each segment to the right as a straight line, keeping exactly its own slope, until it meets the finish line; the row where it meets the finish line is that colour's ARRIVAL HEIGHT, and a smaller row, that is a point nearer the top of the picture, counts as HIGHER. All four extensions arrive inside the picture. The four drawn segments never cross and never touch one another, so their drawn top-to-bottom order is the same everywhere they are inked; that drawn order is NOT the answer, because a lower segment that rises more steeply can arrive above a higher one. Segment length, how far right a segment reaches, and which segment is drawn highest are all uninformative. The pale grey dashed horizontal lines and the black horizontal rail along the bottom are decoration and carry no information. Which colour arrives highest on the finish line? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Checkpoint rms deviation
worlds.question: Which color's five circular checkpoints have the largest root-mean-square vertical deviation from the magenta dashed baseline? Square the five vertical distances, average them, and take the square root. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Baseline crossing leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order. Each curve connects seven equally spaced checkpoints. Which curve crosses its dashed baseline the greatest number of times? Count only crossings between adjacent checkpoints; no checkpoint lies on a baseline. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior target rings
worlds.question: This is a scored archery target face. How many concentric rings are painted on it? Count only the visible bands and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Medallion blue count
worlds.question: How many blue planets are visible? Count each large blue planet disk in the catalog once; ignore gray rings, white highlights, colored non-blue planets, card frames, labels, and the header. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Keyboard black group
worlds.question: This image shows a stretch of piano keyboard drawn on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The dark upright rectangles standing on the keyboard are the black keys; the pale keyboard body and its thin grey dividing lines are not black keys. The black keys are painted in groups. Two neighbouring black keys belong to the same group when the strip of pale keyboard between them is narrow; a gap more than twice as wide as the narrowest gap in this image separates one group from the next group. The number of groups, the number of black keys in each group, the width and height of the black keys, the width of the pale keys, the ink colour and the position of the keyboard on the page all change from image to image, and the keyboard drawn here need not follow the two-and-three grouping of a real piano. Read only what is painted in this image and do not answer from what a piano keyboard normally looks like. The leftmost group is the group of black keys nearest the left edge of the page. How many black keys are in the leftmost group? Answer with exactly one of the integers 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Usb plug contact count
worlds.question: How many separate gold contact pads are visible inside the USB plug? Count each disconnected gold rectangle once. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Battery polarity plate conflict
worlds.question: Ignore the pale gray wires. Which polarity sign is directly above the longer of the two dark battery plates? Answer plus or minus.

worlds.title: Binocular consensus reveal
worlds.question: The image shows two 32-by-32 grids of dark and light cells, side by side (panel P on the left, panel Q on the right), and each grid alone looks like pure random noise. A symbol was hidden between the two panels: wherever the symbol is drawn the two panels carry the SAME shade, and everywhere else they carry OPPOSITE shades, so no single panel reveals anything. Undo the declared coding by comparing the two panels cell by cell: a cell belongs to the symbol wherever both panels are the SAME shade (both dark or both light). Those agreeing cells trace a single abstract symbol, either a filled circle (A) or a filled square (B). Which symbol appears, A or B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Transpose overlay symbol
worlds.question: Find the red-marked reference panel and the blue-marked recording panel. Swap the blue panel's rows and columns, average the two aligned grayscale interiors pixel by pixel, and ignore the borders, colored marks, and fine carrier. Which broad symbol appears: arch, loop, fork, or kite?

worlds.title: Panel parity overlay
worlds.question: The image shows three square panels side by side. Each panel is ruled into the same 7 by 7 grid of cells, and some of its cells are filled. Imagine stacking the three panels exactly on top of one another so that their grids line up cell for cell. In the stack, mark a cell when it is filled in an odd number of the three panels (that is, in exactly one or in all three), and leave it blank when it is filled in an even number of them (that is, in none or in exactly two). The marked cells of the stack form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: arrow, chevron, ell, hourglass, ring. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Component size sieve
worlds.question: Inside the four cyan-framed grids, erase every side-connected black component unless it contains exactly three cells. Corner-touching cells are separate. Which symbol remains: flag, hook, bolt, or cup?

worlds.title: Corner pin perspective glyph
worlds.question: Treat the four colored pin centers as the corners of a square: gold is upper-left, orange upper-right, violet lower-right, and cyan lower-left. Rectify the 9-by-9 tiled quadrilateral to that front-on square without reflecting it. Which dark path appears: fork, hook, zigzag, or ladder?

worlds.title: Concyclic consistency
worlds.question: A set of small dark dots is drawn on a white canvas. In one arrangement every dot's centre lies exactly on the perimeter of a single common circle, so together the dots trace one round ring; in the other arrangement the dots are scattered so that no single circle passes through all of their centres. Are all the dots lying on one common circle together? Choose: yes, no.

worlds.title: Unique spacing constellation
worlds.question: Which color's dots have the fewest repeated pairwise center distances? Treat two distances within 3 pixels as the same; compare the whole constellation and answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Even spacing panel
worlds.question: The picture shows three square panels side by side on a plain background. Each panel is outlined by a frame of its own colour - one red frame, one green frame and one blue frame - and the frames are placed left to right in no fixed order. Inside every panel sit small round dots. Every dot in the picture is the same size and the same dark grey, no dot touches another dot, and each of the three panels contains exactly the same number of dots, so the panels use exactly the same amount of ink and differ only in where their dots sit. In exactly one panel the dots are spread evenly: each dot keeps roughly the same distance from its closest neighbour, so that panel shows no tight clump of dots and no wide empty patch. In each of the other two panels the dots are spread unevenly, gathering into crowded groups with bare ground between them. Judge a panel by the typical distance from a dot to its nearest neighbour: the evenly spread panel is the one where that typical nearest-neighbour distance is the largest, because its dots share the panel instead of huddling. The frame colours, the left-to-right order of the panels, the number of dots, the size of the dots and the total amount of ink carry no information about the answer. Which frame colour surrounds the panel whose dots are spread evenly? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: Paired constellation chirality
worlds.question: The black dots form two separated constellations, one on each side of the gray divider. Ignoring position, rotation, and uniform size, is the right constellation a rotated copy or a mirror copy of the left? Answer rotated or mirrored.

worlds.title: Constellation balance point
worlds.question: Treat every dark dot center as one equal weight. Average all horizontal center positions and, separately, all vertical center positions. Which colored ring is centered at that balance point? The rings are candidates, not weights; ring size does not count. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Eccentric dot oddball
worlds.question: The image is divided by thin lines into four quadrants: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. Each quadrant contains one light-gray filled disk with a small dark dot at the disk's center. Exactly one of the four disks has its dark dot displaced clearly away from the center (off-center); the other three disks have their dot exactly at the disk center. Which quadrant contains the disk whose dark dot is off-center? Answer with the quadrant name.

worlds.title: Curvature reversal panel search
worlds.question: The image shows four equal panels labeled A, B, C, and D. Each panel contains one dark open stroke with the same width and endpoint span. Trace each stroke from either endpoint: a curvature reversal is present when the centerline bends consistently one way and then consistently the other way, producing one S-bend. Which labeled panel contains the only stroke with a curvature reversal? Ignore labels, location, color, and stroke length; inspect every panel and answer A, B, C, or D. A unique one-reversal score separates the correct panel from the runner-up.

worlds.title: Occluded rod join panel
worlds.question: Two straight dark gray lines split this image into four equal quadrants. Each quadrant contains one wide vertical gray band and exactly one coloured rod that runs behind that band, so only the rod's left piece and its right piece are visible; the light gray squares are scatter and belong to no rod. In exactly one quadrant the two visible pieces are the two ends of a single straight rod, so the left piece's centre line continues exactly into the right piece. In every other quadrant the right piece is shifted parallel to that continuation or hinged away from it, and its centre line departs from the continuation by at least nine pixels on average. Inside a quadrant both pieces always share one colour and one thickness, so colour and thickness never mark the answer, and rod colour, rod thickness, rod tilt, band width, band position, rod height, the number of gray squares and the amount of ink in a quadrant carry no information about which rod is the straight one. Which quadrant holds the rod whose two pieces continue straight through the band? Answer with exactly one of: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

worlds.title: Dual route terminals search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has two routes from the MAGENTA circle to the AMBER circle that share no gray circle or dark link except the two colored endpoints? A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Equal angular spacing search
worlds.question: Each labeled panel has six colored dots around a smaller colored center. Which panel has all six neighboring angular gaps equal? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State edge latch
worlds.question: A vertical timeline of five panels reads top to bottom. Each panel shows a single horizontal signal bar that is either ON (filled dark) or OFF (empty). A magenta ring beside the first (top) panel marks a bit whose starting state is shown there: a filled interior means the bit starts ON, an empty interior means it starts OFF. The bit's state changes only when the signal makes a rising edge, meaning the signal is OFF in one panel and ON in the next panel; otherwise the bit keeps its current state. Reading the panels in order, what is the final state of the ringed bit at the last (bottom) panel? Answer 'ON' or 'OFF'.

worlds.title: Rarest state occupant
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 left to right. Each panel has five shuffled labels and a LOW/MID/HIGH STATE KEY. Exactly one state occurs once in each panel. Which label occupies that singleton state in the greatest number of panels? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Carry counter replay
worlds.question: The picture shows four counters standing side by side. Each counter is a column of four square cells and a coloured bar at the top; the four top bars are red, blue, green and orange, and the top bar is that counter's colour. A counter's reading is how many of its cells are shaded dark; cells shade from the bottom upwards, so a counter reads 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4. The columns as drawn show every counter's starting reading. Below the counters is a row of white cards, and the grey arrow says to apply them one at a time from left to right. Each card carries a coloured square naming the counter it acts on, which is the counter whose top bar has that same colour, and one, two or three black dots giving how many steps that card applies to that counter. One step works like this: if the named counter is not already full, one more of its cells becomes shaded, so its reading goes up by one; but if the named counter is already full, that is, all four of its cells are shaded, then instead every one of its cells is cleared so it reads 0 and one single step is passed to the counter immediately to its left, and that step then follows this very same rule on that neighbour, which may in turn clear and pass a step further left. A step passed leftwards out of the leftmost counter is simply discarded. Counters keep their colour and their place throughout, and a card affects only the counter it names and any counters reached by passed steps. The magenta ring below the counters marks the queried counter. After all the cards have been applied in order, what is the reading of the queried counter, that is, how many of its cells are shaded? Answer with one of: 0, 1, 2, 3, 4.

worlds.title: Ripple carry replay
worlds.question: The four lamps start as shown. Read the ADVANCE cards left to right. A card flips its dot-numbered lamp. If that lamp flips from ON to OFF, carry one lamp to the right and flip it too; keep carrying rightward after every ON-to-OFF flip, and stop after an OFF-to-ON flip or after lamp 4. Is the ringed lamp ON or OFF at the end?

worlds.title: Alphabetic comparator replay
worlds.question: Four letter tiles start in the shown numbered slots. Read the six cards from left to right. One, two, or three purple dots selects slots 1-2, 2-3, or 3-4. The orange arrow points to the side that must hold the alphabetically later tile. Swap the selected tiles only if needed to satisfy that arrow; otherwise do nothing. Which letter finishes in the red-ringed slot? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Adjacent regions
worlds.question: The image shows three filled colored regions on a white background: one red, one green, and one blue. Each region is a closed area of the same size. A pair of regions is ADJACENT when their boundaries meet, meaning their filled areas touch (the two regions share a boundary). The other two pairs are separated by a clear white gap. Exactly one pair of the three regions is adjacent. Which one pair of regions is adjacent (shares a boundary)? Answer with exactly one of red-blue, red-green, or green-blue.

worlds.title: Red component count
worlds.question: How many separate red regions are visible? Count edge-connected pixels as one region. Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Wall hop nearest
worlds.question: The picture shows white paper with several closed black rings drawn on it. No two rings touch or cross: any two rings are either one completely inside the other or completely apart. Four coloured dots - green, red, blue and orange - are painted flat on the paper, and no dot touches a ring. A journey from one dot to another may run anywhere on the paper, in any shape, and it costs one crossing each time it steps over a black ring; the cost between two dots is the smallest total any journey between them can have. No coloured dot shares a white area with the green dot, so all three costs from the green dot are at least one, and the three costs are all different from each other. Which dot costs the fewest crossings to reach from the green dot: red, blue or orange?

worlds.title: Switchyard color cut
worlds.question: All paths are thick links. Imagine removing every orange link. Which colored station can still reach the black station using only the remaining gray links? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Chamber door cycle
worlds.question: The map contains 16 enclosed white rooms and exactly 12 orange doorways. Each orange doorway links the two rooms on its long sides. Dark walls block travel, and rooms touching only at a corner are not connected. Is there a loop through three or more different rooms that returns to its starting room without revisiting another room? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Count between on path
worlds.question: Starting at the orange ring and walking only along the blue path, how many black dots do you pass between the red dot and the green dot? Answer with the number of black dots only (0, 1, 2, or 3).

worlds.title: Route distance terminal
worlds.question: Trace the dark connected track from the green source. Which terminal color is farthest away along the track, rather than straight across the page? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Transit fewest changes
worlds.question: This picture is a small transit map. Each dark disc is a station, and each coloured stroke is part of a transit line: there are exactly four lines, one blue, one orange, one purple and one teal. A line runs through the stations it touches, and once you board a line you may ride it to any station on that same line for free. You may switch from one line to another only at a station where both of those lines stop. The green disc is the station you start at and the red disc is the station you must reach; both are ordinary stations apart from their colour. Count only the switches from one line to another, not the stations you pass and not the lines you ride. Travelling from the green station to the red station, what is the smallest number of line switches you can manage with? Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Junction hop terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green node, which colored terminal is exactly three links away along the tree? Count one link for each dark stroke between two adjacent circular nodes. Answer red, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Left turn checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green START disk, follow the black route to the purple FINISH disk. At which colored checkpoint do you make the only left turn among the three colored checkpoints? Other bends without colored checkpoints do not count. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Paired silhouette rotation correspondence
worlds.question: The board has three labeled cards: R is the reference and A and B are candidates. Each card contains two separated dark islands. Rotate each candidate card 90 degrees clockwise about its center. Compare the complete two-island silhouette, including both island shapes and their relative placement, with R. Choose the matching candidate and answer with that candidate's badge color.

worlds.title: Socket notch plug fit
worlds.question: The board is scattered with decorative coloured tiles, and exactly one cream panel sits somewhere on it. Only what is drawn on the cream panel decides the answer; every tile off the panel is decoration and means nothing. The panel carries three separate shapes, each built from small square tiles laid on a regular grid with cream showing between the tiles. The upper shape is the gray SOCKET: a 5-by-5 block of tiles with a hole bitten out of it. The hole is a connected group of 3, 4 or 5 missing tiles and it never touches the socket's outer border, so the socket's 5-by-5 outline is always complete. Below the socket are two PLUGS, one on the left and one on the right. Each plug is a single colour, the two plugs have different colours, and both colours come from red, blue, green and purple. Each plug is built from exactly as many tiles as the hole is missing, and both plugs have the same overall width and height in tiles. Exactly one of the two plugs would fill the hole exactly if it were slid straight into it, with no turning and no mirror-flipping; the other plug is the same tiles in a different arrangement and would not fit. What colour is the plug that fits the hole? Answer red, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Counterrotating attributes
worlds.question: Each corner token has a shape and a color. Read corners clockwise as top-left, top-right, bottom-right, bottom-left. From the left group to the right group, every shape moves one corner clockwise while every color moves one corner counterclockwise; tokens stay upright. Is the right group exactly the result? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Crosskey cell correspondence
worlds.question: The magenta query card contains one black shape and one blue dot group. Match the shape to its column in the top key and the dot count to its row in the left key. What color fills the grid cell at that row and column? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Trace variation halves
worlds.question: In the boxed measurement plot, follow the single connected green trace from the filled start dot to the arrowhead. At the amber split marker, is the trace's total upward travel greater before or after the marker? Answer before or after.

worlds.title: Trace dwell stratum
worlds.question: A chart panel is divided from top to bottom into exactly four horizontal bands of plain grey shades of different lightness and different heights; a band boundary is simply the row where the shade changes and is not drawn as a line. One thin near-black trace runs across the whole panel from its left edge to its right edge with exactly one centre height per pixel column, so every column of the panel belongs to exactly one band: the band that contains the trace's centre in that column. Count, over all columns of the panel, how many columns the trace's centre lies in each band. The coloured dashes, coloured horizontal rules and coloured dots are decoration and carry no information; band shade, band height, and the heights of the trace's two endpoints carry no information, and the answer is not the tallest band. Exactly one band has the largest column count. Numbering the bands 1, 2, 3, 4 from the top downwards, which band holds the trace for the largest number of columns? Answer with one digit.

worlds.title: Region balance centroid
worlds.question: Is the center of area of the single filled region above or below the dashed horizontal reference line? Answer above or below.

worlds.title: Checkpoint turn balance
worlds.question: The gold marks identify the middle checkpoint. Following the teal trace from left to right, add the absolute direction changes at the three bends before the checkpoint and separately at the three bends after it; ignore the bend at the checkpoint itself. Which total is greater? Answer BEFORE or AFTER.

worlds.title: Mitten thumb side
worlds.question: Which side of the visible mitten has the thumb? Use the palm's vertical centerline to name the side: answer left if the thumb projects from the left edge of the palm, or right if it projects from the right edge.

worlds.title: Guitar string count
worlds.question: How many complete blue string courses are shown? A complete course has one blue circular marker at the top nut and one aligned blue circular marker at the bottom bridge. Count aligned blue pairs only; ignore unpaired blue markers, gray guide lines, frets, and gold pegs.

worlds.title: Music staff line count
worlds.question: How many long horizontal staff lines run continuously from the left barline to the right end? Ignore notes and short ledger marks. Answer 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Perspective checksum sheet
worlds.question: Apply the perspective rectification defined by the four gold corner marks. Does the complete front-on sheet show A) a lozenge or B) a chevron? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Phase sieve reveal
worlds.question: This picture shows one bordered panel of 21 rows and 21 columns of square cells. Every cell is a flat block of exactly one of two tones, dark or pale, and both tones appear many times inside the panel. Nine different symbols have been interleaved cell by cell across the whole panel, so the panel on its own looks like clutter and no symbol is drawn anywhere in one piece. Two solid triangles are drawn in the margins outside the panel, far apart from each other: one of them lies beyond the left or the right side of the panel and points sideways at a panel row, and the other lies above or below the panel and points at a panel column. Each triangle points at exactly one panel row or one panel column, and the two triangles are always far apart. A few small clutter bars are also scattered on the background; they are plain rectangles, they never taper to a point, and they carry no evidence. Carry out this operation. Take the row the sideways triangle points at, and keep that row together with every third row from it, counting both upwards and downwards - seven rows in all. Take the column the other triangle points at, and keep that column together with every third column from it, counting both leftwards and rightwards - seven columns in all. Discard every other row and column, close up the gaps, and read the 49 surviving cells as a 7-row, 7-column picture in their original order. The dark cells of that picture form exactly one of nine symbols on the 7 by 7 grid. 'plus' is the full middle row together with the full middle column. 'ex' is the two full diagonals. 'ring' is a hollow rectangle outline five cells wide and seven cells tall, set one cell in from the left and right edges. 'tee' is the full top row together with the full middle column. 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. 'zee' is the full top row and the full bottom row joined by a diagonal that climbs from the bottom-left corner to the top-right corner. 'arrow' is the full middle column with a splayed head on the top four rows: one cell out on each side in the second row, two cells out in the third row, three cells out in the fourth row. 'vee' is two thick diagonals that start at the two top corners, step one column inwards every two rows, and meet at the single middle cell of the bottom row. 'corners' is a two-by-two block in each of the four corners together with three side-by-side cells at the very centre. A few cells of the panel are speckle: the surviving picture can differ from its symbol in a small number of cells, so choose the symbol it is closest to, cell by cell. Neither triangle settles the answer on its own, because each of the nine interleaved sub-lattices carries a different one of the nine symbols: the sideways triangle alone leaves three symbols possible and the other triangle alone leaves a different three, so both distant pointers and the whole panel must be used. Which symbol do the surviving cells form? Answer with exactly one of: arrow, corners, ell, ex, plus, ring, tee, vee, zee.

worlds.title: Corner spiral reassembly
worlds.question: The detached violet key shows a red starting corner and an adjacent blue corner to move toward first. Apply those two corners to the 5 by 5 panel. Read its squares along the resulting inward spiral, then write those 25 shades into a new 5 by 5 panel from left to right, top to bottom. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Period smoothed thread
worlds.question: The red-to-gold thread has twelve fine teeth. Average the thread sideways over exactly one full tooth period, so the fine teeth cancel. Which smooth symbol remains: arch, cup, or wave? Ignore the pale background marks; answer ambiguous only for a tie.

worlds.title: Eccentric void direction
worlds.question: The colored plaque has one circular opening. Relative to the center of the plaque's outer circle, is the opening shifted left or right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Meander partition pair
worlds.question: The single dark trail runs unbroken from the top edge to the bottom edge, splitting the pale field. Are the red and blue dots in the same region or in opposite regions? Answer same or opposite.

worlds.title: Wire walk echo search
worlds.question: The picture shows one thin wire folded into a staircase of eight straight runs on a plain background. The runs alternate between horizontal and vertical, so the wire turns a right angle between one run and the next. One end of the wire is marked by a small solid square block; the other end is bare. Walk along the wire starting from the blocked end: the straight run that touches the block is run one, the run after the first turn is run two, and so on up to run eight at the bare end. The length of a run is how far the wire travels along that straight run, and horizontal and vertical travel are measured in the same units, so a horizontal run and a vertical run can have equal length. Exactly one of runs three, four, five and six has exactly the same length as the run immediately before it on this walk. For every other neighbouring pair of runs, the two lengths clearly differ. The wire's colour, its size on the page, its position on the page, which end carries the block, and the isolated specks scattered in the background all carry no information. Which run has exactly the same length as the run just before it on the walk from the block? Answer with one of: third, fourth, fifth, sixth.

worlds.title: Facing apertures search
worlds.question: Which color pair of broken rings has its two gaps facing each other? Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Latin quilt search
worlds.question: The colored quilt is divided into four 4 by 4 patches: A top-left, B top-right, C bottom-left, and D bottom-right. Which patch has each of the four colors exactly once in every row and exactly once in every column? Exactly one qualifies. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State conveyor replay
worlds.question: Starting at the ringed token, follow the one connected dark conveyor from start to finish. The token has four labeled states W, X, Y, and Z. At each station, apply its visible rule in path order: a clockwise arrow rotates the state one step W-X-Y-Z-W; a counterclockwise arrow rotates it one step backward; a fork keeps the state only if it is W or Y and otherwise advances it one step; a bar resets it to X. Which state label is on the token at the finish?

worlds.title: Keyring gate corridor
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small lock: a single thin dark corridor of constant width that bends about but never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself. A solid dark round bead sits at one end of the corridor, and the walk starts at that bead and follows the corridor to its far end. Coloured marks sit directly on the corridor, and each is one of two kinds: a small filled round disk is a key, and a straight narrow bar laid across the corridor is a gate. Keys and gates are coloured red, green, blue or purple. Walking from the bead, every key that is met is picked up and kept for the rest of the walk. A gate can be passed only if a key of that same colour has already been picked up earlier along the corridor; a key of the gate's colour that lies further along the corridor is too late to help. The walk stops at the first gate it cannot pass, and there is always such a gate. Only the order of the marks along the corridor matters, not how far apart they are. The lock may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside the corridor is inert decoration. What colour is the gate where the walk stops? Answer with one of red, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Inkhead tape replay
worlds.question: The gold ring marks the head on START. Dark cells are INK and light cells are BLANK. Read arrows 1, 2, then 3. For each arrow, first flip the cell under the head, then move the head one cell left or right; a move past an end stays at that end. After all three arrows, is the cell under the head INK?

worlds.title: Pendulum sieve chain
worlds.question: The colored beads lie on one chain between the green START cap and red TURN cap. Begin at START and sweep toward TURN. On each sweep, count the first remaining bead as 1, the next as 2, and remove every bead counted 2. At the far end reverse direction, restart the count at 1 from the first remaining bead there, and repeat until one bead remains. Which color remains?

worlds.title: Focal room seal
worlds.question: If the colored wall tile is erased, does it create a new connection between the two white chambers? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Pressed jaw pocket count
worlds.question: This page shows two solid dark jaws facing each other across a white channel, together with a few small coloured marks. Only the dark ink decides the answer; coloured marks are decoration and never count, even when a coloured mark lies inside the channel. Each jaw is one connected dark piece: an upright bar with a row of straight fingers reaching out across the channel toward the other jaw. The fingers come in facing pairs, one left finger exactly opposite one right finger at the same height, and both jaws have the same top edge and the same bottom edge. Now imagine sliding the right jaw straight to the left, without turning it and without moving it up or down, until the two jaws first touch. The pairs that touch are exactly the pairs whose two fingertips are drawn with the smallest white gap between them; every other pair keeps a gap, and the gap it keeps is the amount by which its drawn gap exceeds that smallest drawn gap. A pair that touches becomes a wall right across the channel; a pair that keeps a gap leaves a passage that white can flow through. Count the closed chambers of white inside the channel: a closed chamber is a piece of the channel with a wall directly above it and a wall directly below it, so white cannot escape from it. The part of the channel above the highest wall opens out at the top of the jaws and the part below the lowest wall opens out at the bottom, so neither of those is a closed chamber. Neither jaw alone fixes any gap: a pair's drawn gap is set by how far its left finger reaches together with how far its right finger reaches. How many fingers the jaws carry, how far any one finger reaches, how far apart the two jaws are drawn, which jaw carries the longer fingers, how thick the fingers are, how much dark ink is on the page, where the jaws sit on the page, and how many coloured marks are drawn never decide the answer. There is always at least one closed chamber and never more than three. How many closed chambers form when the two jaws are pressed together? Answer 1, 2 or 3.

worlds.title: Minimal loop break pair
worlds.question: The black-and-yellow railway has exactly two closed loops, joined by a track. Erase both yellow links. Are they a minimal loop-breaking pair: erasing both leaves no closed loop, while erasing either one alone leaves at least one closed loop? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Lagoon centroid island
worlds.question: Ignore the pale gray decorations. The outer teal sheet encloses one courtyard containing a detached teal island. Treat every pixel of the courtyard footprint, white space and island together, as equal weight. Does that footprint's center of area—the average horizontal and vertical position of all its pixels—land on the teal island? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Unmarked spur route
worlds.question: Trace the thick dark network from the green start. Does the path to the amber terminal contain an extra unmarked dead-end spur? Ignore the colored terminal markers; answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Stile arc census
worlds.question: The picture contains one dark blue wire: a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness that wanders inside one boxed area of the picture. The wire never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself; parallel folds of the wire are always separated by clear background. Two square stiles, each a black frame around a white core, are clamped onto the wire. Every stile is wider than the wire, so it covers the wire completely and cuts the ink into exactly three arcs: the arc that runs between the two stiles, and the two outer arcs that run from a stile to a free end of the wire. Eight small orange beads are printed on the wire. Every bead is narrower than the wire, so a bead never cuts it; beads never touch a stile and never touch each other. A bead counts as lying between the stiles only if it sits on the arc you travel when you walk along the wire's own ink from one stile to the other; stepping across background, or onto a neighbouring fold, is never a legal step. The straight line between the two stiles is not a guide: because the wire folds, beads that look enclosed between the stiles can sit on an outer arc, and beads far away from that line can sit between them. The total number of beads is always eight, so counting all the beads never gives the answer. All gray shapes anywhere in the picture are decoration and mean nothing. How many orange beads lie on the arc of wire between the two stiles? Answer 2, 3, 4 or 5.

worlds.title: Route running balance
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green ring to the red ring. Add 1 at each cyan ring and subtract 1 at each orange ring. Does the running total ever go below zero? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Confluence checkpoint
worlds.question: From the blue and cyan starts, follow their dark routes toward the orange finish. Which checkpoint is at the first junction shared by both routes: red or green? Answer red or green.

worlds.title: Segment ratio correspondence
worlds.question: The picture shows a REFERENCE bar and two candidate bars labeled A and B. Every bar is divided by two vertical boundaries into three side-by-side sections: an indigo section on the left, a turquoise section in the middle, and an amber section on the right. The bars have different total lengths, so their section widths differ too. In the REFERENCE bar, the middle section's width divided by the left section's width gives a certain ratio. Exactly one candidate reproduces this same middle-to-left ratio; the other candidate uses a clearly different ratio. Which candidate, A or B, has the same middle-to-left ratio as the REFERENCE? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Paired badge rank join
worlds.question: QUERY has two gold-framed badges, P and Q. In KEY A, match each badge to its ribbon. In KEY B, find each ribbon and read its rank. Which badge has the smaller rank? Answer P or Q.

worlds.title: Deflector flip counterfactual
worlds.question: A ball is released from the black dot at the top and falls straight down. Each time it meets a slanted bar it slides to that bar's lower end and keeps falling in that column; empty cells let it pass straight through. Exactly one bar is red. Suppose only that red bar is replaced by a bar of the opposite slant and nothing else changes. Which colored bin does the ball then land in? Answer blue, green, orange, purple, or yellow.

worlds.title: Shuffled membership registry
worlds.question: Each symbol-tagged row is the same club on both boards, but the rows are shuffled. A filled cell means member. Which letter has exactly the same six club memberships as START: A, B, C, D, E, or F?

worlds.title: Global compatibility matching
worlds.question: The red arrow marks one row. Blue dots are allowed pairings. Match all seven rows to different columns, using every column once. Exactly one complete matching works. Which column matches the red-arrow row? Answer A, B, C, D, E, F, or G.

worlds.title: Correspondence size color
worlds.question: The gray probe circle at the top has a specific size. Below it are three colored circles, each with a different size and a different color. Which colored circle has exactly the same size as the gray probe? Answer with that circle's color (red, green, or blue).

worlds.title: Seam connector correspondence
worlds.question: The center tile is missing from the reference panel. Which candidate tile, A or B, makes every colored line continue across all four seams? A continuation is valid only when a candidate stub has the same color and touches the same side at the same relative position along that side as the reference stub. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Key socket fit assignment
worlds.question: The top of the image shows four gray keys side by side; the bottom shows four colored sockets, one red, one orange, one green and one blue, in random order. Every key and every socket is a stack of four solid bars of equal thickness. Key bars start at the key's left edge and run rightwards; each socket is the same kind of stack drawn rotated by 180 degrees, so its bars end at the socket's right edge and its rows read in reverse order. A socket fits a key when the socket, slid onto the key without rotating it further, interlocks exactly: pairing the socket's bottom bar with the key's top bar, its next bar up with the key's next bar down, and so on, all four pairs must have the same combined bar length, so the two stacks together form a flush block with no gap and no overhang. Every key and every socket has the same total bar length, so size, ink and average bar length cannot identify the fit; only the arrangement of the bars can. Exactly one socket fits the key marked by the black triangle above it. What is the color of the socket that fits the marked key? Answer red, orange, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Contour corner binding
worlds.question: REFERENCE and each tagged option have one cyan, magenta, green, and orange landmark on a closed dark outline. At each landmark the outline makes either an outward pointed tooth or an inward V-shaped notch. Cards may be turned. Which tag color marks the option with exactly the same corner type for every landmark color as REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Pattern relay chain correspondence
worlds.question: The magenta-framed pattern is START. Each relay card maps its left pattern to its right pattern; follow the arrow. Find the card whose left pattern exactly matches START, then keep matching each output to another card's input. Stop when no input matches. What color tag is on the last card: red, green, or blue? Do not rotate or reflect patterns.

worlds.title: Tightest arc
worlds.question: Three concentric colored semicircular arcs are drawn; they share one center and one angular span but have different radii. Which colored arc has the tightest bend, meaning the smallest radius (strongest curvature)? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Bilateral balance compare
worlds.question: Panel A is left and panel B is right. For each colored silhouette, compare the absolute left-versus-right area difference divided by its total colored area about the visible vertical guide. Which panel has the larger normalized imbalance? Answer A or B; quarantine a tie or a gap below 0.08.

worlds.title: Panel scale units
worlds.question: Each panel has its own vertical scale: the short black tick marks beside a panel's axis are exactly one unit apart in that panel, the lowest tick is zero, and the two panels do not share the same tick spacing. Each colored bar rises from its own panel's zero level. Measure each bar in its own panel's units, that is, bar height divided by that panel's tick spacing. Which panel's bar is taller in its own units? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Ternary balance leader
worlds.question: Which colored sample is the most balanced composition? For each dot, measure its perpendicular distance to each of the three sides of the triangular frame, take the smallest of those three distances, and choose the dot with the largest such minimum. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Interval midpoint marker
worlds.question: Which colored estimate marker is closest to the midpoint of its own horizontal uncertainty interval? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior spider legs
worlds.question: This is a spider. A typical spider has eight legs, but report exactly what is drawn here. How many legs does this spider have? Count only the visible legs and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Week planner columns
worlds.question: How many columns are in the WEEK grid? Count each full-height day lane once; ignore the WEEK title, row labels, header tabs, and small appointment marks. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Balance pan low side
worlds.question: This image shows one balance drawn on white paper: a light grey stand, a light grey beam that crosses the top of the stand, and two dark slate PANS hanging from the two ends of the beam on light grey cords. Small coloured blocks rest on the pans. THE LEFT PAN is the dark slate pan whose centre is further to the left of the page and THE RIGHT PAN is the other one. A pan HANGS LOWER than the other when the centre of its dark slate bar is nearer the bottom edge of the page, that is when it is drawn further down the page; compare only the two dark slate bars, not the blocks, the cords or the beam. The blocks are decoration for this question: the number of blocks on a pan, their colour and their size are chosen separately from the way the beam is drawn, so on some pages the pan with more blocks is the lower one and on other pages it is the higher one, and neither is a mistake. No image in this set is a borderline case: the beam is always clearly tilted, never level. Report the picture in front of you, and do not answer from how a balance would settle under the weight of the blocks. Which pan hangs lower? Answer exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Bias rainbow bands
worlds.question: How many continuous colored arc bands are visible in the rainbow? Count each differently colored arc band once. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Envelope flap direction conflict
worlds.question: On the large envelope, which direction does the colored triangular flap point: up, right, down, or left? Judge the flap's sharp apex, ignore the small stamp, and answer with one word.

worlds.title: Polar unwrap reveal
worlds.question: The image shows an annulus (ring) with a symbol written around it in polar space. Unwrap the ring by mapping radius to rows and angle to columns. Which letter, A or B, is revealed? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Phase slip raster reveal
worlds.question: Find the grayscale square immediately inside the four colored corner squares. It was recorded by circularly shifting row r to the right by (3r) pixels, wrapping at 256, where r=0 is the top row. Undo that shift by moving row r left by (3r) pixels, then replace every pixel by the centered 7x7 mean using edge replication. Ignore the marks and frame. Which symbol appears: ring, cross, triangle, or zigzag?

worlds.title: Mirror fold defect reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one framed lattice of 7 rows and 12 columns of short straight bars, all the same length, thickness and colour. Each bar leans either to the left or to the right of vertical, always by the same small angle. A dashed coloured line down the middle gap of the lattice, with a triangular pointer above and below the frame, marks the fold axis: it separates the 6 left columns from the 6 right columns. Fold the right half onto the left half about that axis, so that the bar in row r and column 12 lands on the bar in row r and column 1, column 11 lands on column 2, and so on. Almost everywhere the right-hand bar is the exact mirror image of the bar it lands on, meaning the two bars of a pair lean towards each other or away from each other. In the remaining cells the pair breaks that mirror rule: both bars lean the same way, so they look parallel. Mark exactly those broken cells on the left half. The marked cells form one of these five symbols inside a 5-by-5 block of cells, each symbol using exactly 9 cells: plus (a full centre row crossed by a full centre column), ex (the two full diagonals of the block, crossing at its centre), tee (a full top row with a centre column hanging from it), ell (a full left column with a full bottom row), cee (a full left column with a short bar across the top and a short bar across the bottom, open on the right). Which of the five symbols do the marked cells form? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Tri panel consensus reveal
worlds.question: Align the three cyan-framed grids by row and column. Make an output cell dark exactly when at least two of the three matching cells are dark. Which symbol appears: diamond, plus, X, or square?

worlds.title: Row column color unmask
worlds.question: The top rail gives color-cycle values 0, 1, 2, 3 from left to right. For each mosaic tile, subtract its row bead value and its column bead value, wrapping modulo 4. Keep only result-0 tiles as ink. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Constellation polygon sides
worlds.question: The dark dots together outline a regular polygon through their arrangement. How many sides does that outlined polygon have? Choose: 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Checkerboard weave field
worlds.question: Which color's 6-by-6 field has a checkerboard weave? Every horizontal and vertical neighbor reverses slant; the other fields are row or column stripes. Compare the complete fields and ignore color, panel position, bar size, spacing, and overall tilt.

worlds.title: Negative space reach
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain light background crossed by thick dark walls, and five dots: one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple. A dot can be reached from the red dot when you can travel from the red dot to it over background only, never crossing a wall and never leaving the outer wall frame; gaps in the walls are open passages. Exactly one of the green, blue, orange and purple dots can be reached from the red dot. Which dot can be reached from the red dot? Answer green, blue, orange or purple.

worlds.title: Constellation cut vertex
worlds.question: Treat two dots as linked when the distance between their centers is shorter than the gray scale bar. Removing exactly one of the two colored dots would split the complete constellation into more connected groups. Which colored dot is it? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Oriented dash topology
worlds.question: Forward-slash (/) dashes mark the target cells. Using only horizontal and vertical neighboring cells as connected, what do they form: one island with no hole, one ring enclosing a hole, or two separate islands?

worlds.title: Collinear dot search
worlds.question: The image contains two gray dots that together mark a straight line (the line is the one passing exactly through the centers of the two gray dots). Four dark dots are drawn, one in each quadrant (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). Exactly one dark dot lies exactly ON that reference line; the other three dark dots each lie clearly off it. Which quadrant contains the dark dot that lies on the reference line? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Vertical alignment pair search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel, A, B, C, or D, contains the only pair of markers with the same vertical centerline? Each panel has exactly four identical filled blue markers. Treat a pair as vertically aligned when the two marker centers differ by at most 4 pixels horizontally; inspect every pair, ignore labels and panel location, and choose the unique panel.

worlds.title: Weave cycle panel
worlds.question: This image shows five square framed panels standing side by side; count them 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly three straight opaque bands of the same thickness, each band in its own solid colour, and every band runs the whole way across its own panel. Inside each panel the three bands meet in three separate crossings, one for each pair of bands. At a crossing one band passes in front of the other: the band in front keeps its colour running unbroken through the crossing, and the band behind is interrupted there and reappears on the far side. Solid bands lying flat on a table can only be stacked in one top-to-bottom order, so in a physically possible panel the three crossings agree with a single stacking order: one band is in front at both of its crossings, one band is behind at both of its crossings, and the third is in between. In exactly one panel the three crossings instead run in a cycle, so that the first band is in front of the second, the second is in front of the third, and the third is in front of the first; that panel is woven and no single stacking order can explain it. The four other panels are each consistent with a stacking order. Nothing else marks the answer: the colours of the bands, which colour happens to be in front at any single crossing, the directions of the bands, where in the panel the crossings fall, the number of bands, the amount of ink and the size of every part are the same kind in every panel and carry no information. Only whether the three crossings of a panel can all hold at once decides the answer. Which numbered panel is the woven one whose three crossings cannot be produced by any single stacking order of its three bands? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Concurrent lines search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has all three colored lines meeting at one point? Judge the lines themselves; A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Enclosed cell search
worlds.question: Which labeled mosaic contains exactly one white cell that cannot reach the mosaic edge through side-adjacent white cells? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State motion reversal
worlds.question: Four ordered panels P1, P2, P3 and P4 are shown side by side, read left to right. Each panel shows the same horizontal track divided into six sites by thin tick marks, and a single red marker on one site. The red marker is the same token in every panel and it moves to a different site between each pair of consecutive panels. A reversal occurs when the marker's direction of horizontal travel changes sign: it moves right between two panels and then left between the next two (or left then right). Reading the four panels in order, how many times does the marker reverse its direction of travel across the whole sequence? Answer 0, 1, or 2.

worlds.title: State run persistence
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each panel shows the same labeled tiles, but their rows may be rearranged. Track each label by its visible glyph and state swatch. Which label has the longest uninterrupted run of one unchanged state across the seven panels? Compare the longest contiguous block for A, B, C, and D; answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Push cart replay
worlds.question: The picture shows a track of nine grey square cells in a row. Number the cells 1 to 9 from left to right. Two discs stand on the track, one red and one blue, in two different cells: a disc is in the cell whose centre is nearest to the centre of that disc. Below the track is a row of cream cards, applied one at a time in order from left to right, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries one coloured spot, one green arrow and one or two purple dots. The coloured spot says which disc that card moves, the red disc or the blue disc. The green arrow says which way that disc moves, left or right: the arrow points the way the disc moves. The number of purple dots says how many single-cell steps the card asks for. The steps of a card are taken one at a time. In a step the named disc moves one cell in the card's direction; if the other disc is already standing in the cell the named disc is moving into, the other disc is pushed one further cell in the same direction and the named disc takes its place. A step is refused if it would carry the named disc off the end of the track, or if it would push the other disc off the end of the track: on a refused step nothing moves, the rest of that card is lost, and the next card is then applied from wherever the discs stand. Discs never jump over one another and never share a cell. The track is drawn only once, in the starting layout; no later position of either disc is drawn anywhere. After every card has been applied in order, which cell does the red disc end in? Answer with a single number from 1 to 9, counting cells from the left.

worlds.title: Compass turn replay
worlds.question: The red pointer starts as shown. Read the blue turn cards from left to right; L means a quarter-turn left and R means a quarter-turn right. Which direction does the pointer face after all cards?

worlds.title: Controlled lamp circuit
worlds.question: Four lamps A-D start as shown (filled = ON/1, ring = OFF/0). Read the eight cards from left to right. Purple pips name the control lamp and orange pips name the target lamp; one pip means A, two B, three C, and four D. On each card, if the control is currently ON, toggle the target; if the control is OFF, do nothing. The control itself does not change on that card. What is the final A-D pattern? Answer with four bits in A,B,C,D order, where 1=ON and 0=OFF.

worlds.title: Longest shared boundary
worlds.question: The image shows three filled colored regions on a white background: one red, one green, and one blue. One region is a wide base block; the other two colored regions sit on top of the base, and each of them touches the base along a stretch of shared boundary. A pair of regions SHARES A BOUNDARY when their filled areas touch along a contiguous edge. The two regions that sit on top of the base do not touch each other; there is a clear white gap between them. Which two colored regions run along each other for the greatest distance, that is, which pair has the longest shared touching edge? Reply with exactly one of red-blue, red-green, or green-blue.

worlds.title: Loop multiplicity link
worlds.question: Which highlighted link belongs to exactly two distinct loops: red, green, or blue? Treat every visible node-to-node segment as one undirected link. A loop is a simple closed path that starts and ends at the same node without repeating any other node; the same loop counts once regardless of direction or starting node. Ignore the white canvas.

worlds.title: Common loop pair
worlds.question: The picture shows a network of grey pipes of equal thickness on white paper. Pipes join only inside the round hubs where they end, and pipes that merely pass near each other are not joined. Three hubs are painted red, green and blue; every hub can be reached from every other hub by travelling along pipe, so all three coloured hubs are connected. Two hubs are said to lie on a common loop when you can travel from one to the other and back again along pipe without using any piece of pipe twice. Exactly one pair of the coloured hubs lies on a common loop. Which two coloured hubs lie on a common loop? Answer 'red and green', 'red and blue', or 'green and blue'.

worlds.title: Wall same chamber
worlds.question: Black and colored segments are walls; connected white floor forms a chamber, whether or not it touches the canvas border. Which colored wall has the same chamber on both opposite sides? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Alternating link route
worlds.question: Can the green junction reach the purple junction along a route whose consecutive link colors strictly alternate between blue and orange? Either color may come first. Do not revisit a junction; links meet only at circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Path crossings over guide
worlds.question: A dashed horizontal grey guide line is drawn. A single blue path winds back and forth across it, passing from one side of the line to the other each time it crosses. Count how many times the blue path crosses the grey guide line. Answer 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Route hop depth
worlds.question: Trace the single dark tree from the green source to the red, blue, and gold terminals. Count links, not pixels: each dark segment between neighboring visible nodes counts once, regardless of its length. Which terminal is reached through the greatest number of links? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Hub clockwise wire
worlds.question: The black square in the middle of this picture is a hub. Exactly one grey wire touches each of its four sides - top, right, bottom and left - and each of those four wires runs to one of the four coloured squares near the edge of the picture: green, red, blue and orange. All the wires are drawn in the same grey with the same thickness, and wires often cross one another; where two wires cross, each one carries straight on through the crossing and neither one turns there. A wire turns only where it visibly ends its straight run and bends. First follow the wire that ends at the green square back to the hub and note which side of the hub it touches. Then move one side clockwise around the hub, where clockwise means top side, then right side, then bottom side, then left side, and back to top. Now follow the wire touching that next side out to its coloured square. Which coloured square does that wire end at? Answer red, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Hamiltonian checkpoint terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green circle and travel along dark links. Visit every cyan circle exactly once, never visit any node twice, and stop at a colored square. Which colored square can you reach: orange, purple, or blue?

worlds.title: Two shortest routes terminal
worlds.question: Each box is a separate network. From green START, which colored terminal has exactly two different shortest routes? Count one black link between neighboring circles as one step; longer routes do not count. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Stained graph slab correspondence
worlds.question: After the stated clockwise turn, which candidate reproduces every colored-part contact in R, including compass direction? Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Quilt rotation mark swap
worlds.question: The picture is one square quilt of 6 rows by 6 columns of touching tiles. Columns 1-3 are the LEFT block and columns 4-6 are the RIGHT block. Every tile has one fill colour (red, blue, green or purple) and one white mark. The right block's marks were copied from the left block by rotating that block 180 degrees: the mark of the right-block tile in row r of right-block column c should equal the mark of the left-block tile in row 7-r, left-block column 4-c. The marks themselves were copied without being rotated. Exactly two right-block tiles break this rule, because their two marks were exchanged with each other; every other right-block tile matches its rotated partner exactly. Fill colours follow no rule and say nothing about which tiles those are. Of the two exchanged tiles, take the one that comes first in reading order: the smaller row number, or if the rows are equal the smaller column number. What is the fill colour of that tile? Answer red, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Reciprocal diagonal seal
worlds.question: The small dark seal is a square grid. Ignore the pale background dots. Across the gold diagonal from top-left to bottom-right, every cyan cell must have a cyan partner in the reflected row-and-column position, and blank cells must likewise pair. Is the grid an exact mirror across that diagonal?

worlds.title: Palette rekey carpet correspondence
worlds.question: Across the top two rows, each four-tile-wide vertical band is a key: its top color changes to the color directly beneath it. Apply those four substitutions to every tile in the leftmost six-row mosaic below, without moving tiles. Exactly one of the three mosaics to its right is the result. What color fills the tag row directly beneath that mosaic? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Connected basin half balance
worlds.question: Which half of the single connected filled basin contains more inked area: left or right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Inscribed square band
worlds.question: Compare the largest axis-aligned square that fits inside the plate with the plate's own width, and report which of the three bands it falls in. The plate is the single solid dark slate-grey shape on the sheet; the pale grey body, the grey ticks, the grey rings and the thin border are decoration and are never measured. A fitted square must be axis-aligned, that is not rotated, and must lie entirely inside the plate; touching the plate's edge is allowed. Let S be the side of the largest such square, and let W be the plate's full width, the horizontal distance from its leftmost to its rightmost point. Use exactly these rules: less_than_third if S is smaller than W/3; third_to_half if S is at least W/3 and at most W/2; more_than_half if S is larger than W/2. Answer with one label: less_than_third, third_to_half or more_than_half.

worlds.title: Field gradient axis
worlds.question: Across the gray measurement field, along which direction is the edge-to-edge brightness change larger: horizontal or vertical? Answer horizontal or vertical.

worlds.title: Triplet linearity residual
worlds.question: Each row shows three dot measurements at equally spaced settings. For each row, compare the middle dot's height with the average height of its two outer dots. Which row has the smaller absolute difference? Answer TOP or BOTTOM.

worlds.title: Butterfly wing mirror match
worlds.question: Are the visible butterfly wings mirror-matched? Reflect the left colored wing across the vertical line halfway between the two wing centroids; answer yes only if at least 92% of the two visible wing masks' union overlaps, otherwise answer no.

worlds.title: Cross arm length equality
worlds.question: Do all four arms of the single colored plus sign extend equally far from its center? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Piano key group order
worlds.question: Reading the black keys from left to right, are they arranged as a separated group of two followed by a separated group of three? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Quartet mosaic rectify
worlds.question: Find the four separated cards. Rectify each card from its four gold corners, place the quadrants in their visible compass positions, and read the complete 16x16 mosaic. Is it A) a diamond or B) a cross? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Endfold pairing reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one cord in this picture is teal; any other cord is pale lavender. The teal cord is a single unbranching thin route with exactly two ends, and it carries exactly 50 round beads, one at every corner and one at each end. Each bead is filled with one of just two grays, a darker gray and a lighter gray; the two-square key near one corner of the picture shows those two grays. Exactly one end bead of the teal cord has four small black brackets around it. Carry out this operation: walk the teal cord from that bracketed end bead to its other end and number the beads 1 to 50 in the order you meet them; then fold the cord end to end, so that bead 1 meets bead 50, bead 2 meets bead 49, bead 3 meets bead 48, and so on down to bead 25 meeting bead 26, giving 25 folded pairs; then mark every folded pair whose two beads are filled with the same gray, and leave a pair unmarked when its two beads differ. Then write the 25 verdicts into a 5 by 5 grid, filling the first row left to right with pairs 1 to 5, the second row with pairs 6 to 10, and so on to the fifth row with pairs 21 to 25. Exactly 9 of the 25 positions are marked. The marked positions form one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the full centre row together with the full centre column, 'ex' is the two full diagonals, 'tee' is the full top row together with the centre column below it, and 'ell' is the full left column together with the full bottom row. The shape the cord traces across the picture is not the symbol, the lavender cords and the key are decoration, and only the folded pairing of beads from the two ends of the walk decides which positions are marked. Which symbol do the marked positions form? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tee.

worlds.title: Paircode lookup reveal
worlds.question: Read the 5 by 10 purple source panel in adjacent horizontal pairs, left pair to right pair on each row. In each detached teal key card, the two small top squares show an input pair and the wide lower square shows its output shade. Replace every source pair by the matching key output, preserving row order, to form a 5 by 5 tile. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Keyed column transposition
worlds.question: Starting below the triangular notch, read the seven colored chips on the detached left key from top to bottom. Reorder the seven tagged columns of the right grid so their header chips follow that color order; keep every column upright. Which dark-cell symbol needs the fewest cell changes to match the reordered 7 by 7 grid: arch, fork, or zigzag? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Quilt fold axis
worlds.question: The quilt is one seamless 12 by 12 field of equal colored squares. Along which direction could it be folded in half so every square lands on the same color: left-to-right or top-to-bottom?

worlds.title: Orbit reversal trail
worlds.question: The dark trail is one unbroken route inside the square. Imagine the panel center as a pivot and trace the trail from either end. Does its travel around the panel center keep one direction throughout, or reverse direction once? Answer one direction or reverses.

worlds.title: Orientation census search
worlds.question: The cyan key bar shows the direction to count. Each framed field has nine black bars. Which marker color labels the field with more bars parallel to the key than every other field? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Traced terminal search
worlds.question: Starting at the gold START disk, follow its unbroken dark cable through every bend. Which colored terminal does that same cable reach? The cables never cross or join. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State patch turn replay
worlds.question: The image shows one framed 4x4 patch: rows A-D run top to bottom and columns 1-4 run left to right. Start at the ringed cell. Read the numbered turn markers from top to bottom. A right-pointing marker rotates the token one quarter-turn clockwise around the patch center; a left-pointing marker rotates it one quarter-turn counterclockwise. Apply every turn in order. Which labeled cell contains the token after the last turn?

worlds.title: Swatch rewrite relay
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small notice board made of six separated tiles: three tiles in an upper row and three tiles in a lower row, with plain background between every tile. The leftmost tile of the upper row is the badge: one coloured square drawn inside a thin dark rectangular ring, and its colour is the colour carried at the start. Each of the other five tiles is a card: two coloured squares side by side at the same height with a background gap between them, the left square being that card's guard colour and the right square being that card's result colour. Every square is red, green, blue, purple or orange.
