The cards act one after another in reading order: first the two cards to the right of the badge in the upper row, left to right, then the three cards of the lower row, left to right. When a card acts, compare the colour carried at that moment with that card's guard colour: if they are the same colour, the carried colour becomes that card's result colour; if they are not the same colour, that card does nothing at all and the carried colour is unchanged. The board may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside the board is inert decoration. Which colour is carried after the last card has acted? Answer with one of red, green, blue, purple or orange.

worlds.title: Snapshot flip pair
worlds.question: Compare BEFORE with AFTER. Exactly one lettered lamp changed between hollow and filled. Which lettered lamp changed? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Saturating level badge
worlds.question: The center meter shows the starting level from 1 to 4. Begin at the command beside the yellow dot and read all six triangular commands clockwise. An up triangle raises the level by one unless it is already 4; a down triangle lowers it by one unless it is already 1. What level remains?

worlds.title: Topology signature match
worlds.question: Which colored candidate panel has the same topology signature as the gray reference? Count dark connected components and enclosed white holes in each panel. Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Seal pair ring binding
worlds.question: This page carries red, black, blue and grey marks. Only the red marks decide the answer; marks of any other colour are decoration and never count. The red marks form exactly three seals that sit close together: one seal above and two seals below it. Each seal is a stack of one or two nested red squares, each square drawn as an outline. A red outline counts as sealed only if it runs unbroken all the way around; an outline with a visible gap cut through one of its sides does not count as sealed, no matter how large that outline is. Compare the number of sealed outlines in the upper seal with the total number of sealed outlines in the two lower seals. Does the upper seal have exactly as many sealed outlines as the two lower seals have together? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Noncrossing terminal pairs
worlds.question: Inside the black circle, join the two cyan terminals to each other and the two orange terminals to each other. Can both joins be drawn without crossing and without leaving the circle? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Nested pocket tree
worlds.question: Ignore pale gray marks. Does the navy drawing contain a white pocket inside another white pocket? A pocket is a white area fully enclosed by navy. One pocket is inside another only when the navy ring enclosing the smaller pocket lies entirely within the larger pocket. Areas connect through shared edges, not diagonal corner contact. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Matched connector route terminal
worlds.question: Each green-to-terminal route is drawn as two separated dark pieces. Join pieces only when their colored connector tabs match. Starting at the green tab on each assembled route, which terminal—amber or violet—is farther along the joined route? Use accumulated centerline length, not straight-line distance. Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Switch pad reach
worlds.question: The image contains several small stacked-bar tiles. In every tile two short horizontal bars sit one above the other with clear background between them. Exactly one tile is the switch tile: a short teal trunk stub rises or falls from the middle of that tile and touches exactly one of its two bars, and the touched bar is teal while the other bar is gray with a visible gap between the stub and that gray bar. Exactly one other tile is the pad tile: its upper and lower bars are orange and purple in some order. Every remaining tile is an all-gray decoy and means nothing. The trunk continues to the pad on the matching side of the pad tile: the upper channel reaches the upper pad and the lower channel reaches the lower pad. Which pad does the trunk reach? Answer orange or purple.

worlds.title: Nested detour order
worlds.question: Trace the dark route from the green START to the orange FINISH. At the first split, follow both branches until they rejoin. Does another split occur before that rejoin, or only afterward? Answer nested or sequential.

worlds.title: Matched width branch
worlds.question: Start at the blue port and follow the navy corridor to the purple junction. Continue along the outgoing corridor whose width matches the incoming corridor; the other outgoing corridor has a different width. Which terminal does the matching corridor reach, red or gold? Answer red or gold.

worlds.title: Row zoned cascade
worlds.question: A 5 by 5 grid of square cells stands on a white card, with a column of five large coloured tags on the left, one beside every row.  An amber tag marks a 'two' row; a violet tag marks a 'three' row.  Each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Below the grid a key holds one, two, or three teal dots; the number of dots is the number of rounds R to apply.  A round transforms the whole grid by this rule: for every cell, count how many of its eight surrounding neighbours (the cells that touch it along an edge or at a corner) are dark.  A cell on an amber row becomes dark in the next round if and only if that count is exactly two; a cell on a violet row becomes dark if and only if that count is exactly three; in every other case the cell becomes pale.  Note that a dark cell may turn pale and a pale cell may turn dark.  Apply the round rule R times, using each round's result as the starting grid of the next round, and keep the row tags fixed.  After the last round, count how many cells in the 5 by 5 grid are dark.  Is that count odd?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Vertex route resilience
worlds.question: Exactly one panel has two green-to-amber routes that share no ordinary junction; the routes may meet only at green and amber. Which panel: panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D?

worlds.title: Signed run crossing
worlds.question: The black bar at the top is the target length. A running total starts at zero. Take the colored bars from top to bottom: a bar drawn right of the black line adds its length to the total, and a bar drawn left of it takes its length away. At which colored bar does the running total first reach or pass the target length? Name that bar's color. Answer blue, crimson, green, orange, purple, or teal.

worlds.title: Residual bundle orders
worlds.question: Each mark runs that recipe once. Subtract every token used from START. After which order can every leftover token be packed into identical TARGET KITS with nothing left over? Answer order-A, order-B, order-C, or order-D.

worlds.title: Ambiguous bijection backbone
worlds.question: A dot means a pairing is allowed. Use every row and every column exactly once. Several complete assignments are possible. Exactly one row keeps the same column in every assignment. Which row? Answer row-1, row-2, row-3, row-4, row-5, row-6, row-7, or row-8.

worlds.title: Grid cell correspondence
worlds.question: The top panel shows a 3x3 grid with a marker dot in one cell. Below are three candidate grids, each with a marker dot and a colored border. Find the candidate whose marker sits in the same grid cell as the reference marker, then report that candidate's border color.

worlds.title: Multipart halo binding correspondence
worlds.question: Which halo color belongs to the candidate object matching the REFERENCE mosaic? Each mosaic is five uniquely colored square tiles in one connected asymmetric shape. A whole candidate mosaic may be rotated by 0, 90, 180, or 270 degrees; reflection is not allowed. Match the tile colors and their relative arrangement, then report the matched candidate's halo color. A is the left candidate and B is the right candidate. Ignore panel position, tile size, and halo size. Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Rubber rail interval transfer
worlds.question: This image has two horizontal rails, an upper one and a lower one. Both rails are the same track: the five short black ticks on the upper rail are five landmarks of that track, the five short black ticks on the lower rail are the same five landmarks in the same left-to-right order, and each thin grey line joins a landmark on the upper rail to the same landmark on the lower rail. Between two neighbouring landmarks the lower rail is a uniformly stretched or squeezed copy of the upper rail, so a point that sits a given fraction of the way from one landmark to the next on the upper rail sits at that same fraction of the way between the two matching landmarks on the lower rail. The stretch factor is different on different stretches of rail, so no single shift or single scale carries positions across, and the distance from a landmark in pixels carries no information across. The black triangle above the upper rail marks one point of the upper rail, at the tip of the triangle. Four coloured dots hang below the lower rail, each on a short stem that meets the lower rail at that dot's position. Exactly one of those dots stands at the point of the lower rail that matches the point marked by the triangle. Which dot is it? Answer with that dot's colour: blue, brown, green, orange, purple, or red.

worlds.title: Colored connection match
worlds.question: Each box contains one circle of each color. A connection counts only when a dark line directly joins two circles. Ignoring rotation and rearrangement, which border color surrounds the box with exactly the same pairs of connected circle colors as the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Oriented plate correspondence
worlds.question: The reference plate and each test plate contain the same four colored triangular pointers. Exactly one test plate can be made by rotating the whole reference plate by 90, 180, or 270 degrees: both every colored part's socket position and the direction its triangle points must rotate together by the same amount. Which test plate is it: A, B, or C?

worlds.title: Widest pair
worlds.question: Each color is drawn as two dots of that same color. Which color has its two dots farthest apart, meaning the largest straight-line distance between the centers of its two dots? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Rank shift binding
worlds.question: Panels A and B show the same red, green, and blue circular samples. Rank the samples from top (1) to bottom (3) separately in each panel. Which color has the greatest absolute change in rank? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Interval sum binding
worlds.question: The chart shows three groups (G1, G2, G3). Each group contains exactly one red, one green and one blue rectangle, in any left-to-right order. A rectangle floats: only its vertical length counts, never its position, its top edge or its width. The short black tick marks beside the vertical axis are exactly one unit apart, so a rectangle's value is its length divided by that tick spacing. The three small squares at the top are a color key, not data. For each color, add its three values across G1, G2 and G3. Which color has the greatest total? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: Convex hull fill leader
worlds.question: Which color's eight dots have the largest convex-hull fill? For each color, take the area of the tightest polygon containing all eight dot centers and divide it by the area of their axis-aligned bounding rectangle. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Middle timepoint peak
worlds.question: Which colored series is higher at time 2 than at both time 1 and time 3? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior liquid level
worlds.question: This is a glass of liquid standing on a level table. At rest, a liquid's surface always stays horizontal (level). Is the visible surface of this liquid actually level (horizontal)? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Pacman facing direction
worlds.question: Which direction is the Pac-Man-shaped character facing? Use the direction in which its wedge-shaped mouth opens; answer left, right, up, or down.

worlds.title: Balloon string detached
worlds.question: This image shows a row of balloons drawn on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. Each balloon is one solid coloured oval, and under every balloon exactly one straight dark grey STRING hangs downwards. A string is TIED when its top end touches the bottom of its balloon, and it is LOOSE when a clear band of white paper, at least ten pixels tall, separates the top end of the string from the bottom of the balloon. Every balloon has its own string and all the strings are the same length, so the amount of dark ink is the same however many strings are loose. The number of balloons, their colours, their sizes, their heights on the page and which balloons carry the loose strings all change from image to image. Judge only what is painted in this image, and do not answer from the fact that balloons are normally tied to their strings. How many of the strings are loose? Answer with exactly one of the integers 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Thermometer bulb edge
worlds.question: Which image edge is nearest the large round red bulb of the thermometer? Answer top, right, bottom, or left.

worlds.title: Stop sign side conflict
worlds.question: At the very top of the red STOP sign, is there a flat horizontal side or a pointed corner? Answer flat or corner.

worlds.title: Column key shift reveal
worlds.question: The blue-framed square panel below holds one solid triangle cut into six vertical columns. Every column has been slid up or down and wrapped around the panel edges by a random distance; each column carries one small magenta square sitting at a fixed reference height before the slide. Undo the declared per-column slides by moving each column so its magenta square returns to that fixed reference height (bottom area), then reassemble the triangle. Does the reconstructed triangle point up (A) or down (B)? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Bandlimited blur icon
worlds.question: Find the square tile just inside the four colored corner marks. Replace each grayscale pixel by the mean of the 13x13 square centered on it, using edge replication at the tile boundary; ignore the colored marks and outer border. Which abstract symbol is revealed: ring, cross, triangle, or zigzag?

worlds.title: Gauge opening reveal
worlds.question: The sheet shows a square lattice of 4 by 4 points; the four corner points are printed as coloured squares. Every printed stroke runs straight along a lattice line from one point to the next point, and all strokes use the same ink. Strokes come in two thicknesses. Below the sheet a solid reference bar is printed; the height of that bar is the sanding width. Sand the sheet: erase every stroke that is thinner than the reference bar, and keep every stroke that is at least as thick as the reference bar. The strokes that survive the sanding form one of these five symbols: comb (a full top bar with three teeth hanging down), hood (a full top bar with both ends turning down two steps), jhook (a full left side and a full bottom bar with the right end turning up one step), rungs (two full horizontal bars, the second and fourth rows, joined by one vertical link), zig (a staircase running down from the top left corner to the bottom right corner and back one step to the left). Which symbol survives? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Adjacent swap ledger
worlds.question: Starting with the eight columns in the cyan grid, follow the swap ledger from top to bottom. At each magenta bar, swap the two adjacent columns whose center dots it joins. Which symbol appears: anchor, boot, chair, or sail?

worlds.title: Unequal grid rectification glyph
worlds.question: The cyan grid lines divide the dark-and-light mosaic into 9 rows and 9 columns of unequal sizes. Independently stretch or squeeze every interval until all 81 cells are equal squares, preserving row order, column order, and the image orientation. Ignore the small gold dots. Which glyph appears: tree, gate, wave, or trident?

worlds.title: Mirror symmetry
worlds.question: Is the colored pattern mirror-symmetric across the dashed vertical line? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Lattice phase field
worlds.question: Which colored field contains a regular lattice? Each field has twelve same-sized dots. Ignore color, position, orientation, and dot count; choose red, blue, or green. A regular lattice is a complete 4-by-3 rectangular grid with constant spacing along two perpendicular directions.

worlds.title: Occluded curve correspondence
worlds.question: A dark curve enters from the left and disappears behind an opaque grey vertical band. Three coloured curves - red, green and blue - come out of the band's right edge and never touch each other. Exactly one of them is the dark curve's continuation: it is the same single smooth curve carried on behind the band, so where it leaves the band its height and its direction of travel are those the dark curve would have if it kept going smoothly. Of the other two, one leaves the band at exactly the height where the dark curve met the band, and one travels in the same direction as the true continuation but at a different height. Which coloured curve is the continuation of the dark curve? Answer red, green or blue.

worlds.title: Texture component area compare
worlds.question: Every short dash sits on a square grid and slants either up-right or down-right. Edge-neighboring up-right dashes belong to the same island. The red and blue rings mark up-right dashes in different islands. Which marked island contains more up-right dashes? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Rubber band constellation
worlds.question: Imagine one taut rubber band around all dark dots: it forms their smallest convex enclosure. Which colored dot's center is strictly inside that implied boundary? A center on the boundary counts as outside. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Reference size relation match
worlds.question: A dark reference glyph is shown in the box at the top of the image: two dark filled disks side by side. The relation of a glyph is whether its left disk is larger than its right disk (left-bigger), whether its right disk is larger than its left disk (right-bigger), or whether the two disks are the same size (equal). Below, the image is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), each containing one dark glyph of two side-by-side disks. Exactly one quadrant's glyph has the SAME left-vs-right size relation as the reference glyph; the other three each have a different relation. Which quadrant contains the glyph whose left-right size relation matches the reference glyph? Answer with the quadrant name.

worlds.title: Guided orientation count search
worlds.question: Which half contains more candidate bars whose centerlines are within 8 degrees of the reference bar, modulo 180 degrees? Ignore the reference bar.

worlds.title: Flag rank accord panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel holds exactly four flags. A flag is a dark vertical pole standing on the same invisible floor line as every other pole, with one solid coloured disk resting on the pole's top end. All five panels reuse the very same four pole heights and the very same four disk sizes, so every panel holds the same amount of ink, the same number of flags, the same range of heights and the same range of disk sizes; only which height is paired with which disk size differs from panel to panel. Every disk in the image has the same colour, and inside a panel the four poles all have different heights and the four disks all have different sizes. Where a flag sits from left to right inside its panel is free to vary and carries no information, so a panel whose poles happen to rise steadily from left to right is not thereby special. Call a panel accordant when, comparing its flags in pairs, the flag with the taller pole always carries the larger disk, that is when ordering its four flags by pole height also orders them by disk size. Exactly one panel in the image is accordant. Every other panel contains at least one inverted pair, a pair of flags in which the taller pole carries the smaller disk; one of those panels reverses the pairing completely, so a panel that looks systematic is not automatically the accordant one. Which numbered panel is the accordant one? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Edge coloring search
worlds.question: Which labeled board has different colors in every pair of cells that share an edge? Cells that touch only at a corner are not neighbors. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Rotation shape match
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains exactly the same tile pattern as the reference after rotation? Rotations count; mirror images do not. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State max dwell
worlds.question: Four panels are shown side by side, read left to right as panel 1, panel 2, panel 3, panel 4. Each panel shows the same track of five slots, and the middle slot is always marked by the same shaded band, called the region. Four coloured tokens -- red, green, blue, and orange -- appear in every panel, each in one slot; a token is inside the region in a panel when it sits in the shaded middle slot of that panel. Counting all four panels, which colour token is inside the region for the most panels? Answer with its colour: red, green, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Token swap destination
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P5 from left to right. Which named slot contains the token that started in the ringed slot after all four swaps?

worlds.title: Box nesting replay
worlds.question: The black rectangle at the top of the picture is a tray. Inside it are five open boxes drawn as coloured rectangle outlines: one yellow, one red, one green, one blue and one purple. A box is inside another box when its outline is drawn completely within that outline; the box that directly holds it is the smallest box whose outline encloses it, and a box enclosed by no other box sits directly on the tray. Below the grey divider is a row of cream cards. Each card carries two coloured squares with a black arrow pointing from the left square to the right square. A card means: take the box whose colour is on the left, together with everything still inside it, lift it out of wherever it is, and put it directly inside the box whose colour is on the right. The cards are carried out one at a time in order from left to right, as the grey arrow below them shows. Every card shown can be carried out: the target box is never one that is inside the box being moved, and the two colours on a card are never the same. The arrangement after the cards have been carried out is not drawn anywhere. No card ever puts a box back onto the tray, so once every card has been carried out the yellow box is inside at least one other box. After every card has been carried out in order, which box directly holds the yellow box? Answer with one word: red, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Circular roster replay
worlds.question: The five seats form a circle in left-to-right number order, wrapping from 5 to 1. A seat's number is its black-dot count, and the magenta ring marks the starting baton holder. Read the six cards from left to right: a blue arrow passes the baton to the next remaining seat; a red card removes its dot-numbered seat. If the removed seat holds the baton, the baton immediately passes to the next remaining seat. Which seat holds the baton at the end? Answer 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: First region entry timeline
worlds.question: Read panels 1 through 5 from left to right. Each row pairs a pip-labeled token (A has one black pip, B two, C three, and D four) with an arrow showing that token's direction in that panel. A token has returned only after its arrow first points away from its panel-1 direction and later points back to it. Which token returns to its panel-1 direction first? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Hole count compare
worlds.question: Look only at the white gaps fully enclosed inside each colored shape. A white gap counts as an enclosed hole only if it is a closed white pocket sealed off by that shape's ink, with no path out to the outside white background. Compare the two shapes and decide which one contains the GREATER number of enclosed holes. Answer with exactly 'left' or 'right'.

worlds.title: Multi boundary face marker
worlds.question: Which colored marker lies in the only open background face bordered by exactly two separate closed dark contours? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Sealed cavity census
worlds.question: The picture shows one solid plate of a single flat colour on white paper. Four round white chambers are cut into the plate. Narrow straight white channels are also cut into the plate: a channel joins two chambers, or runs from a chamber to the outside of the plate. Some channels are crossed by a short bar of plate colour that spans the channel completely and blocks it. A chamber counts as OPEN if you can travel from inside that chamber to the white paper outside the plate while staying on white the whole way, moving only through chambers and unblocked channels and never crossing any plate colour. A chamber counts as SEALED otherwise. Travelling through other chambers on the way is allowed. How many of the four chambers are SEALED? Answer with a number from 0 to 4.

worlds.title: Two bridge station
worlds.question: A bridge is a link whose removal splits its network into separate parts. Which highlighted gold station touches exactly two bridge links? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Balanced link cut
worlds.question: If the orange link is removed, does the network split into exactly two disconnected groups containing the same number of junctions? Follow links only between circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Terminals before checkpoint
worlds.question: Walking only along the blue line from the orange ring, how many of the coloured dots -- red or green -- do you reach BEFORE you reach the magenta dot? Answer 0, 1, or 2.

worlds.title: Marked junction parity
worlds.question: Starting at the green source, follow the dark connected route to the red target. Does that route pass through an even or odd number of ringed junctions? Answer even or odd.

worlds.title: Oneway reachable tank
worlds.question: This picture shows a one-way lane network. Every disc is a junction and every straight gray bar is a lane joining the two junctions at its ends. Each lane carries exactly one black arrowhead at its middle, and that arrowhead points along the only direction in which that lane may be travelled. You start at the green junction. You may move only along lanes, and on each lane only the way its arrowhead points; you may pass through any number of junctions on the way and you may never move against an arrowhead. Three junctions are colored tanks: one blue, one orange and one purple; all other junctions are gray. Lanes join all of these junctions when the arrowheads are ignored, so how near a tank sits to the green junction on the page, how many lanes touch it, and where it lies do not matter; only travel that follows the arrowheads counts. Exactly one of the three tanks can be reached from the green junction under this rule. Which colored tank can be reached from the green junction? Answer blue, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Adjacent checkpoint echo
worlds.question: Starting at the green ring, follow the one continuous dark cable to the red square. Do any two consecutive checkpoint rings along the cable have the same color? Checkpoints are the smaller orange and purple rings tethered beside the cable; consecutive means adjacent in travel order with no checkpoint between them. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Arrow reachable terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green START circle, follow black links only in the direction of their purple arrowheads. Which colored terminal can be reached? Links meet only at circles, and every link may be followed only in its arrow's direction. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Curvature rhythm correspondence
worlds.question: One connected navy route contains fields R, A, and B. R is the reference. Classify each field's five interior bends as tight, medium, or open from the visible angle. Reflect A and B left-to-right before comparing. Which candidate has R's complete bend-radius rhythm? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Swatchfield window lock bind
worlds.question: The cream page carries small decorative coloured squares; they lie outside the dark slate board, none of them touches it, and none of them means anything. Everything that decides the answer is painted on that one slate BOARD. On the left of the board is the FIELD: a 7-by-7 arrangement of 49 square colour swatches, each swatch flat sand, teal, rose, olive or indigo. On the right of the same board, separated from the field by a wide slate gutter, is the KEY: a detached 3-by-3 patch of nine swatches drawn in the same five colours but at a visibly smaller cell size. A WINDOW is any 3-by-3 block of neighbouring field swatches; there are 25 windows and they overlap. Exactly one window has the same nine colours as the key, in the same arrangement, reading row by row; every other window differs from the key in at least one swatch. Size is not a clue: the key is smaller than the field swatches, so only the pattern of colours can be compared. Some field swatches carry a MARK: a small round dot of red, amber, cyan or violet lying on top of the swatch. A mark never changes the colour of the swatch it lies on, marks appear on swatches inside and outside the matching window, and the key patch never carries a mark, so the key alone cannot tell you any mark. The centre swatch of the matching window always carries exactly one mark. Where the board sits, where the matching window sits, how many marks there are and how often each mark colour appears carry no other information. What is the colour of the mark on the centre swatch of the one window that matches the key? Answer red, amber, cyan or violet.

worlds.title: U turn binding rail
worlds.question: Start at the gold bead and follow the single navy rail. The first four stations are the reference: each navy shape is paired with its surrounding halo color. The last four stations contain the same shapes in a new order. Did every shape keep its reference halo color?

worlds.title: Twohop table correspondence
worlds.question: The two gray key tables are read left to right, and each row is a pairing. Blue dot groups are identities: one, two, or three dots. For each dark source shape, follow its blue-dot partner in the left key, then the same blue-dot group in the right key to a green target glyph. Each colored proposal directly pairs the dark sources with green targets; row order does not matter. Which frame shows all three composed pairings? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Calibration target bracket
worlds.question: In the highlighted calibration inset, does the diamond target lie strictly between the two vertical endpoint ticks? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Unit transfer count
worlds.question: The picture is a measurement sheet on white paper. Exactly three marks are drawn in pure black: two short black vertical ticks of equal height, and one black horizontal measuring bar that lies in a separate row so that white paper always separates it from the ticks. Everything else - the pale grey ruler along the top, the coloured vertical ticks, the coloured bars and the coloured squares - is decoration and carries no information; only the three black marks matter. The span is the horizontal distance between the centres of the two black ticks. The measuring bar's length is its own horizontal width. Copies of the measuring bar are laid end to end starting at one black tick and running towards the other, never overlapping and never reaching past the far tick. How many whole copies of the black measuring bar fit inside the span? Answer with a single whole number: 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Reference bracket sign
worlds.question: Do the coral and blue measurement dots lie on opposite vertical sides of the gold reference dot? A dot exactly level with the reference would count as no. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route axis length balance
worlds.question: Follow the single colored orthogonal route centerline from end to end. Add the lengths of all horizontal runs and separately add the lengths of all vertical runs. Which total is greater? Answer HORIZONTAL or VERTICAL.

worlds.title: Paired medallion hole sides
worlds.question: Look at the two separated medallions. Is the circular hole in the left medallion on the same side of its face center as the circular hole in the right medallion? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Sports emblem ring count
worlds.question: How many complete colored rings are visible in the sports emblem? Count each colored closed loop once.

worlds.title: Clock cardinal order
worlds.question: Reading clockwise from the top, do the four large black clock-face numerals appear in the order 12, 3, 6, 9? Ignore the small gray tick marks. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Spiral pair carpet
worlds.question: Apply the marked clockwise spiral and adjacent-pair XOR. Is the resulting bitmap A) LOOP or B) DIAMOND? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Column cascade deshear reveal
worlds.question: This picture contains exactly one square panel with a solid dark border, plus a few much smaller dark specks scattered on the background that are decoration only. The panel's border encloses a seven-by-seven grid of forty-nine equal square cells; each cell is either dark (the same tone as the border) or pale (the same tone as the panel's background). Carry out this operation on that grid. Number the columns 0 to 6 from the panel's left border and the rows 0 to 6 from its top border. Slide the contents of each column upward, staying inside the panel and wrapping around from the top row back to the bottom row, by as many cells as that column's number: column 0 does not move, column 1 moves up by one cell, column 2 by two cells, and so on up to column 6, which moves up by six cells. Every cell keeps its own column; only its row changes. After all seven columns have been slid, the dark cells form exactly one of these four symbols. 'bars' is two fully dark horizontal rows, the second row from the top and the second row from the bottom, with every other cell pale. 'caret' is a fully dark bottom row together with one extra dark cell per column tracing an upward-pointing chevron: that cell is in the top row in the middle column, one row lower in each neighbouring column, and in the fourth row down in the two outermost columns. 'vee' is a fully dark top row together with one extra dark cell per column tracing a downward-pointing chevron: that cell is in the bottom row in the middle column, one row higher in each neighbouring column, and in the fourth row down in the two outermost columns. 'zigzag' is a fully dark middle row together with one extra dark cell per column, two rows above the middle row in the first, third, fifth and seventh columns and two rows below the middle row in the second, fourth and sixth columns. Whichever symbol is present, exactly fourteen of the forty-nine cells are dark and exactly two of the seven cells of every single column are dark; sliding the columns moves cells only within their own column and so changes neither of those counts. Neither the amount of dark ink, nor how it is spread across the columns, nor the panel's size, position or colour therefore reveals the symbol. As drawn, before the columns are slid, the dark cells match none of the four symbols. Which symbol do the dark cells form after the slide? Answer with exactly one of: bars, caret, vee, zigzag.

worlds.title: Ruler keyed reflections
worlds.question: Filled cells in the left ruler mark rows: reverse each marked row left-to-right. Then filled cells in the top ruler mark columns: reverse each marked column top-to-bottom. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Medial depth ridge reveal
worlds.question: In the cyan-framed 13 by 13 mosaic, give every dark cell a depth: one plus the fewest edge-sharing steps needed to reach a light cell, with light cells at depth zero. Keep a dark cell exactly when none of its eight touching neighbors has greater depth. Which ridge symbol is closest by cell changes: fork, arch, or bolt? Ignore pale marks outside the frame; a tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Filament pocket count
worlds.question: Consider only the single colored filament inside the pale card. How many pale pockets are fully enclosed by it? A pocket counts only when it cannot reach the card edge without crossing the filament; touching crossings are joined. Answer zero, one, or two.

worlds.title: Slalom side cadence
worlds.question: The five colored pegs lie along one straight row. Follow the single dark trail from either end. At each peg it bends around one side of the row. Do those five sides alternate at every step, or is there exactly one adjacent repeat? Answer alternates or one repeat.

worlds.title: Three side socket search
worlds.question: Which quadrant's amber square shares full edges with cyan squares on exactly three of its four sides? Answer upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, or lower-right.

worlds.title: Square block cluster search
worlds.question: Four separate colored clusters are each made from five equal square cells. Which color's cluster contains a completely filled 2x2 block of cells? Exactly one does. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State atomic change
worlds.question: Read the two labeled panels from left (initial) to right (final). Each panel has the same four labeled tiles A, B, C, and D. A tile's state is its colored circular symbol; color names do not matter. Exactly one corresponding tile changes state and no tile moves. Which tile changed?

worlds.title: Sandheap topple inset
worlds.question: This picture contains one small block drawn with a thick black frame; every pale grey mark outside that frame is inert decoration that changes nothing. Inside the frame is a grid of nine square cells in three rows and three columns, and beneath the grid a strip holding small green squares. Each cell holds zero, one, two or three red dots. Exactly one cell is outlined by a blue square: that is the drop cell. The number of green squares in the bottom strip is the number of grains dropped, one at a time, onto the drop cell, and each grain adds one red dot to it. Whenever a cell holds four or more dots it topples: it loses four dots and sends one dot to each of the cells immediately above, below, left and right of it, and any dot sent past the edge of the grid is discarded. Toppling continues until no cell holds four or more dots, and the stable result does not depend on the order in which the topples are carried out. How many red dots are in the drop cell once no cell can topple any more? Answer 0, 1, 2 or 3.

worlds.title: Refractory pulse plaque
worlds.question: The gold START tile shows the lamp (dark means ON; light means OFF); the gate begins READY. Read the six event tiles in row order. A cyan PULSE flips the lamp only when the gate is READY, then makes the gate EXHAUSTED. A coral RECHARGE advances EXHAUSTED to WARMING, or WARMING to READY; otherwise it leaves the gate READY. Pulses while the gate is not READY do nothing. Is the lamp ON after all six tiles?

worlds.title: Pocket range reversals
worlds.question: Track the cyan token through the compact board. It starts in the column marked by the cyan disk. Read the four gold strips from top to bottom. Each strip reverses the order of all slots between its two dark end caps, inclusive; slots outside the strip do not move. After all four reversals, which column contains the token: A, B, C, or D?

worlds.title: Paired bridge signature
worlds.question: Do the two colored links have the same bridge status? A link is a bridge if removing it disconnects its own local network. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Severed cord bead shares
worlds.question: This page shows one black cord that winds through several bends, plus grey cords, blue squares and orange squares as decoration. Exactly one visible gap is cut through the black cord, so the black cord falls into two separate pieces. One piece ends at the green square and the other piece ends at the red square; each anchor square covers the end of its own piece. Exactly five small orange squares are pressed against the black cord. An orange square counts only if it touches the black cord, and it then belongs to the one black piece it touches. Orange squares that touch nothing, and orange squares that touch only a grey cord, never count; blue squares never count. Straight-line distance to an anchor square is not the rule: a square belongs to the piece it is physically joined to, which you must decide by following the cord from that square past every bend until you reach either the gap or an anchor. Compare how many counting orange squares sit on the green piece with how many sit on the red piece. Does the green piece carry more counting orange squares than the red piece? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Rail tree centroid
worlds.question: The tracks form one connected tree and meet only at round stations. Imagine removing one colored station and every track touching it. Which station, cyan or yellow, leaves every remaining track piece with at most half of the other stations?

worlds.title: Dual cut hinge
worlds.question: Ignore pale gray dots. The amber patch is solid and part of the teal sheet. If only the amber patch were erased to white, would both of these happen: the remaining teal sheet splits into more pieces, and at least one enclosed white pocket opens to the outside? White and solid areas connect through shared edges, not diagonal corners. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route interval checkpoint
worlds.question: Following the single green-to-red route, which colored checkpoint—amber or violet—lies between the two gray gate rings in route order? Use the order along the route, not straight-line position. Answer amber or violet.

worlds.title: Arm relay terminal
worlds.question: The image shows several small square pads of equal size on a plain background, each separated from the others by clear background. Exactly two pads carry a short teal arm attached flush to one of their four sides and sticking outward; a colored pad never carries an arm. Exactly one of those two armed pads also carries a small dark square at its centre, and that is the entry pad. An arm names a direction: from the pad it is attached to, travel in the direction the arm sticks out and stop at the first pad whose centre lies in that direction and on the arm's axis. Start at the entry pad and take its arm; that first hop always lands on the other armed gray pad. Take that pad's arm for the second hop, which always lands on a colored pad. Exactly one orange pad and exactly one purple pad are present. Gray pads without an arm are decoys and mean nothing. Which colored pad does the second hop land on? Answer orange or purple.

worlds.title: Branch rejoin badge
worlds.question: Trace the dark route from the green start to the orange finish. After it splits, do both branches rejoin before the finish? Answer yes or no. Ignore pale gray decorations.

worlds.title: Twin trace agreement
worlds.question: Two blue-ringed starts appear inside the dashed inset. From each blue ring, follow the dark navy route (ignore pale routes) to its orange terminal. Is the terminal symbol the same for both routes—both circles or both squares? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Iterated cell relay
worlds.question: A line of nine square cells stands on a white card.  Each cell is filled either dark or pale.  Below the row a small key holds one, two, or three teal dots; the number of dots is the number of rounds R to apply.  A round transforms the whole row by this rule: a dark cell stays dark; a pale cell becomes dark only if exactly one of its two neighbours (left and right) is dark, and the leftmost and rightmost cells each have just one neighbour, otherwise it stays pale.  Apply the round rule R times, using each round's result as the starting row of the next round.  After the last round, count how many cells are dark.  Is that count odd?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Tri view rule binding
worlds.question: Match each SOURCE seal to the identical seal in the two shuffled rows. A green rule dot means the two arrows must point the same way; an orange dot means they must point opposite ways. Which SOURCE card passes its matched rule? Answer card-1, card-2, card-3, card-4, or card-5.

worlds.title: Recolor shift register
worlds.question: The top row is a color chain: each arrow points from one color to the next, and the last color wraps back to the first. The strip below holds four disks in slots 1 to 4, left to right. Run the cards at the bottom in order, left to right. A right-pointing triangle moves every disk one slot right, and the slot-4 disk wraps into slot 1. A left-pointing triangle moves every disk one slot left, and the slot-1 disk wraps into slot 4. A plus recolors only the disk that is in slot 1 at that moment, changing it to the next color along the chain. After the last card, which color is in slot 1? Answer blue, green, red, or yellow.

worlds.title: Ordered oblique reflections
worlds.question: Reflect the yellow bead across mirror 1, then 2, then 3, then 4. Which cup contains the final point? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Read flip tape walker
worlds.question: The gold arrow marks the current cell and facing. Repeat 8 turns. Read the pointed cell before changing it. If LIGHT: make it dark, reverse, then move 1. If DARK: make it light, keep facing, then move 2. Move in the arrow's facing and wrap at the row ends. Which option shows all cells and the arrow after turn 8? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Sequence order correspondence
worlds.question: A reference row of four colored square tiles is shown at the top in a fixed left-to-right order. Below, three candidate rows A, B, C show the same four tiles but in different left-to-right orders. Which candidate reproduces the exact same left-to-right color order as the reference?

worlds.title: Corner turn profile correspondence
worlds.question: The image has a REFERENCE polygon and candidates A and B. Each is a closed outline with eight uniquely colored vertex markers. A corner is convex when the boundary turns outward and reflex when it indents inward. A candidate matches only when every color has the same convex/reflex status as that color in the REFERENCE. Whole-panel translation and quarter-turn rotation are allowed; reflection is not. Ignore panel position, marker size, line width, and the order of colors around the outline. Which candidate matches? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Chiral twin slot binding
worlds.question: The single gray tile above the black horizontal rule is the REFERENCE tile: a flat piece made of five equal squares joined edge to edge. Below the rule are four more gray tiles, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right, each also made of five equal squares, and each with one colored dot (red, blue, green or orange) drawn directly beneath it. A tile counts as a turned copy of the REFERENCE if it can be laid exactly on the REFERENCE by sliding it and turning it in the plane by 90, 180 or 270 degrees. A tile counts as a mirror copy if it can be laid exactly on the REFERENCE only after also flipping it over. Exactly one of the four tiles is a mirror copy that is not a turned copy; of the other three, one is a plain turned copy of the REFERENCE and two are different shapes. Flipping is not allowed when deciding whether a tile is a turned copy. What is the color of the dot beneath the tile that is a mirror copy but not a turned copy? Answer with exactly one of: red, blue, green, orange.

worlds.title: Cyclic bead order
worlds.question: Each panel shows the same six bead colors on a closed black loop. A loop may be rotated or reshaped, so its starting point and geometry do not matter. Read colors clockwise; reversing the order is not allowed. Which option has exactly the same clockwise cyclic color order as the REFERENCE? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Double fold punch correspondence
worlds.question: A folded quarter-sheet at left contains three punched holes. Unfold it first across the dashed vertical crease, then across the dashed horizontal crease: every hole is reflected across each crease. Which full-sheet hole pattern is correct: A, B, or C?

worlds.title: Centroid anchor compare
worlds.question: A light panel shows one red-filled triangle, one blue-filled triangle, and a small gray dot at the centre of the panel. The geometric centre (centroid) of a triangle is the average of its three corners. Which colour's triangle has its centroid FARTHER from the gray dot? Answer with only the colour: red or blue.

worlds.title: Diagonal crossing binding
worlds.question: Across panels P and Q, which colored sample changes from below the dashed diagonal in P to above it in Q? Samples A, B, and C are identified by the legend. Quarantine ties or unclear diagonal crossings; choose A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Peak overlap depth
worlds.question: The picture shows six solid coloured STRIPS, one red, one green, one blue, one orange, one purple and one brown. Every strip is a horizontal bar drawn in its own row, and no two strips share a row. Each strip SPANS the left-to-right stretch between its own two ends; how high or low its row sits, the order of the rows, and the colour of a strip all mean nothing. Imagine sliding one straight VERTICAL line across the whole picture from left to right and, at each place, counting how many strips that line passes through. The DEPTH of a place is that count. The answer is the LARGEST depth reached anywhere. The vertical line is never drawn, the deepest place is never marked, and no strip is special: the deepest place is where the most spans happen to lie one above another, which may be anywhere along the picture. A strip counts at a place only if the line passes strictly inside its span; touching an end never happens, because no two strip ends line up. The number of strips, six, is the same in every picture and is not the answer. The total coloured length, the longest strip, the shortest strip, the widest gap, the number of strips reaching the left or the right of the picture, and the place along the picture where the deepest stack sits are each the answer no more often than chance allows. Pale grey vertical rules and the grey line along the bottom are decoration and mean nothing. What is the largest depth reached anywhere? Answer 2, 3, 4 or 5.

worlds.title: Scatter slope leader
worlds.question: Which color's seven dots have the steeper upward least-squares trend? Treat higher positions in the plot as larger values. Answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Midpoint chord residual
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order, use one vertical scale, and have equally spaced checkpoints. For each panel compute |middle - (first + last)/2| from marker heights. Which panel gives the largest value? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior chess pawns
worlds.question: This is a row of chess pawns standing on a board. How many pawns are shown? Count only the visible pawns and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: House window count
worlds.question: How many square window openings are visible on the house? Count each separated square opening once; ignore the door, roof, outline, and HOUSE label. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Rainbow band order
worlds.question: This image shows an arch built from five coloured bands, drawn one inside the other above a grey ground line. The ground line, the small grey ticks below it, the grey page frame and the white background are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. All five colours - red, yellow, green, blue and violet - appear exactly once in every image of this set, each as one band, so the set of colours never indicates the answer either. The bands may be stacked in any order, and their thicknesses vary from image to image. The outermost band is the widest arch: the one farthest from the centre of the arch, with white page outside it. Read the stacking order off this image itself, and not from what a rainbow normally looks like. Which colour is the outermost band? Answer with exactly one word: red, yellow, green, blue, or violet.

worlds.title: Bias stop sign sides
worlds.question: How many straight sides does the red STOP sign's outer boundary have? Count each outer boundary segment once; ignore the letters. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Snowman largest tier conflict
worlds.question: In the visible snowman, which of the three colored body snowballs has the largest visible diameter: top, middle, or bottom? Answer top, middle, or bottom.

worlds.title: Row scroll rectify reveal
worlds.question: The image is a coarse 32-by-32 cell grid whose pixel rows have each been cyclically scrolled by a fixed oblique ramp: row r is rolled by 7*r mod 32 cells leftwards, smearing a hidden binary symbol into a sheared diagonal splat that is not readable directly. Undo the declared cipher: cyclically roll every pixel row back by 7*r mod 32 cells to the right and reassemble the aligned 32x32 grid. That reconstruction is one of two declared abstract symbols: a hollow square ring (A) or a diagonal cross X (B). Which symbol appears, A or B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Rotational blur emblem
worlds.question: Find the grayscale square bounded by four colored corner marks. Replace each pixel by the mean of 32 nearest-pixel samples from rotations by k×11.25° about its center, clipping at the square edge. Ignore marks and edge. Which radial symbol appears?

worlds.title: Ink filter reveal
worlds.question: The card shows a 9 by 9 lattice of round printed marks, four small dark squares at the lattice corners, and one large colour patch above the lattice; that patch is the filter. Each mark is printed with one, two or three of the process inks cyan, magenta and yellow, and shows their mixture: cyan+magenta prints blue, cyan+yellow prints green, magenta+yellow prints red, and all three print black. Viewed through the filter, a mark looks dark exactly when its printing contains one particular ink - through a red filter the marks containing cyan, through a green filter the marks containing magenta, through a blue filter the marks containing yellow. Every other mark and every empty cell looks pale. The lattice cells that look dark through the shown filter form a shape that most closely matches one of these symbols: arch, arrow, ladder, ring, vee. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Opening filter reveal
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 12 by 12 grid, first keep a black cell only if it and all eight cells touching it (by a side or corner) are black; outside the grid is white. Then, from that kept grid, make every cell black if it is within one side-or-corner step of a kept black cell. Which symbol appears: barbell, arch, spiral, or crown?

worlds.title: Packet interleave arrow
worlds.question: The gold cross splits the cyan field into odd/even row and column packets. The five rows above it are hidden row positions 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9; the four below are positions 2, 4, 6, and 8. Likewise, the five columns left of it are positions 1, 3, 5, 7, and 9; the four right are positions 2, 4, 6, and 8. Rebuild both axes by alternating from the five-item packet then the four-item packet, ending with the fifth item. Keep the image orientation unchanged. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Dotcloud centroid marker
worlds.question: On a white canvas there is a scattered constellation of equal-sized colored dots: one red, one green, one blue, one purple, one orange, and one teal. Look at the whole cloud of dots together. Its center of mass -- the single point where all the dots would balance -- lies exactly on one of the dots. Which color dot sits right on the center of mass of the entire constellation? Answer red, green, blue, purple, orange, or teal.

worlds.title: Central symmetry field
worlds.question: Ignore palette and panel placement. Which field's complete eight-dot constellation can be paired into points opposite one another through its centroid? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Cloud elongation axis
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain background, a cloud of many small grey dots, and four straight coloured bars - one red, one green, one blue and one orange - lying near the edges of the picture, outside the cloud. Every grey dot has the same size and the same colour, and no single dot carries any meaning: only the shape of the whole cloud matters. The cloud is stretched further along one straight direction than along any other direction, and that direction is the cloud's long axis. The long axis is not drawn. Exactly one of the four bars points more nearly along the cloud's long axis than the other three bars do; a bar's direction is the direction of the straight bar itself, and a direction and its opposite count as the same direction. The colours of the bars, where each bar sits, how long or thick the bars are, how many dots there are and how much ink the picture contains all carry no information. Which coloured bar points most nearly along the cloud's long axis? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Dash field winding
worlds.question: Treat each elongated dash as an unoriented axis. As positions circle the field center, do the dash axes turn with them (whirl) or against them (saddle)? Answer whirl or saddle.

worlds.title: Texture gradient focus
worlds.question: Every outlined tile has the same dark area, but different checker sizes. Across the whole grid, the checks become coarser toward one focus. Which colored ring is at that focus? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Reference orientation search
worlds.question: A reference line segment is shown in the top panel. Below it, the image is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), each containing one line segment. Exactly one quadrant's segment has the same orientation as (is parallel to) the reference segment. Which quadrant contains the segment whose orientation matches the reference segment?

worlds.title: Reference contour clutter search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only contour that exactly matches the reference outline? Inspect all three contours in every panel, ignore translation, and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Balance beam panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Each panel shows one balance beam: a long horizontal bar lying level, a single pointed support whose tip touches the underside of the bar, and exactly four identical square blocks standing on top of the bar. All twenty blocks in the image have the same size and the same colour, and every panel carries the same number of blocks and the same amount of ink, so block count, block size, colour and ink carry no information. Every bar is the same length and every bar is drawn level, so no beam is tilted and tilt carries no information, and the support stands at its own arbitrary place under each bar, so where a support stands carries no information either. Because the four blocks of a panel are identical, each block counts equally, and a beam counts as balanced exactly when the average of the four block positions along the bar falls exactly over the tip of that panel's support. That average is not the same thing as the midpoint between the leftmost and the rightmost block, because blocks may be clustered on one side, and a block far from the support does not count for more than a block near it. Exactly one of the five beams is balanced. In each of the other four panels the average of the four block positions misses the support tip by at least two thirds of a block's width, and in at least two of those unbalanced panels the midpoint between the outermost two blocks does stand over the support tip even though the beam is not balanced, while in the balanced panel that midpoint clearly misses the support tip. Which numbered panel holds the balanced beam, that is the panel in which the average of the four block positions falls exactly over the support tip? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Projection signature search
worlds.question: Which labeled board has exactly the same blue-cell counts in each row and each column as the REFERENCE? Compare rows top to bottom and columns left to right; cell positions themselves need not match. Panels A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Embedded contour search
worlds.question: The orange reference shows a closed contour. Which labeled panel contains exactly the same contour after translation only? Rotated or reflected versions do not count. Ignore the light-gray strokes. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State hold streak
worlds.question: Five panels are stacked vertically and read top to bottom. Every panel shows the same horizontal track divided into six slots. Three tokens - one red, one green, one blue - each keep their own fixed colour and sit in one slot of every panel; at most one token occupies any single slot. A token's HOLD STREAK is the longest run of consecutive panels in which it stays in the same slot (its disk does not move sideways between those panels). Which token has the LONGEST hold streak across the five panels? Answer 'red', 'green', or 'blue'.

worlds.title: Grid toggle state
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P5 from left to right. The ring marks one cell in P1. Each arrow flips every cell in its visibly named row or column. What is the ringed cell's final state in P5: ON or OFF?

worlds.title: Key gate transit
worlds.question: The picture shows a grey corridor running left to right, with a black triangle at the far left: that is a courier, and the grey arrow in the top margin shows that the courier walks from left to right. Standing along the corridor is a row of coloured objects of exactly two shapes. A small coloured disc, drawn above the corridor on a short grey stem, is a key lying on a shelf: when the courier reaches it, the courier picks it up and adds one key of that disc's colour to the bag it carries. A tall coloured post, drawn standing across the corridor itself, is a locked gate: to walk past it the courier must hand over one key of that gate's own colour, and that key is used up and leaves the bag for good. Keys are not interchangeable between colours and there is no other way through a gate. The bag starts empty, keys of the same colour pile up, and the courier meets the discs and posts one at a time in the order they are drawn from left to right. If the courier reaches a gate while holding no key of that gate's colour, the courier is stopped there and walks no further, so everything drawn to the right of that gate is never reached. Exactly one gate stops the courier in every picture. The bag's contents are never drawn anywhere: only the discs and posts standing in the corridor are drawn, and a disc stays drawn whether or not its key has already been spent. What is the colour of the gate that stops the courier? Answer with one of blue, green, orange, purple or yellow.

worlds.title: Debounced signal replay
worlds.question: The output starts as shown at START. Read SAMPLE 1 through SAMPLE 7 from left to right. The output changes only after the same new state appears on two consecutive samples; a sample matching the current output cancels any pending change. What is the final output? Answer ON or OFF.

worlds.title: Cursor write replay
worlds.question: Four pip-labeled cells start as shown (filled = ON, ring = OFF), and the small triangle marks the cursor's starting cell. Read cards 1 through 8 from left to right. A triangular STEP card moves the cursor to the next label in the cycle 1→2→3→4→1. A filled circular SET card makes only the cursor's current cell ON; a ring-shaped SET card makes only that cell OFF. SET does not move the cursor. After all cards, how many cells are ON? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Link cut connectivity
worlds.question: The image shows a small network of thick black links connecting circular nodes on a white background. One node is green (the start) and one node is red (the goal). Exactly one link is highlighted in orange and is the candidate bridge. Ignoring the orange link as if it were removed, do the green node and the red node remain connected to each other through the remaining black links? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Bipartite network selection
worlds.question: Which colored network is bipartite: red, blue, or green? Each network has six colored nodes and eight gray links. Bipartite means its nodes can be divided into two groups so every link joins different groups; ignore the white canvas.

worlds.title: Gap seal pick
worlds.question: The picture shows thick black walls drawn on white paper, laid out on a square lattice so that they enclose a compound of rooms. The black walls are solid and cannot be walked through. Wherever the lattice carries no ink at all, the way is open. Three places in the walls are open doorways, each painted as one coloured bar filling the gap it stands in - one amber, one magenta and one azure - and you can walk straight through a coloured bar. As things are drawn, every part of the white floor inside the compound can be walked out to the white paper outside it. Now suppose one single doorway were bricked up, so that its coloured bar became solid wall while the other two doorways stayed open. Exactly one of the three colours has this property: bricking up that one doorway would leave some part of the white floor completely shut in, with no walking path out to the paper outside the compound. Bricking up either of the other two would leave every part of the floor still able to get out. Which doorway is it - amber, magenta or azure?

worlds.title: Link resilient pair
worlds.question: Gray links join round stations. For each color, compare the two same-colored stations. Which pair would still have a route between its stations after any one gray link is removed? Remove only one link at a time. Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Paired disjoint routes
worlds.question: Can green connect to purple and blue connect to orange at the same time by two routes along the dark links that share no circular junction? Links meet only at visible circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Path bend comparison
worlds.question: Two winding routes are drawn, one blue and one green, each starting at a small orange ring and ending at a dark terminal. A bend is a sharp U-turn where a route folds back on itself. Which route, blue or green, has FEWER bends along its length? Answer blue or green.

worlds.title: Corridor trace membership
worlds.question: Starting at the green source, follow the thick navy trace to the red terminal. Does its centerline cross the open gap between the two gray islands from left to right? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Pipe bottleneck tank
worlds.question: The grey bars in this picture are pipes. Pipes carry water only along their own length and join only where they actually meet at a junction. The green square is the pump. The red, blue and orange squares are tanks. A route from the pump to a tank is any chain of connected pipes that leads from the green square to that tank. Pipes are drawn with different thicknesses, and water through a route is limited by its narrowest pipe: the capacity of a route is the thickness of the thinnest pipe anywhere along it. Each tank is scored by its best route, that is the route whose narrowest pipe is as thick as possible. How long a route is, how many turns it makes, how many pipes it uses and how far the tank sits from the pump on the page all do not matter. Which tank has the highest-capacity route from the pump? Answer red, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Route bend duel
worlds.question: Starting at each green ring, follow its dark route to the colored square. Which route, orange or purple, has fewer bends? Every visible 90-degree direction change counts as one bend.

worlds.title: Start loop checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green START circle, find the closed loop of black links that contains START. Which colored checkpoint is also on that same loop? A closed loop returns to its starting circle without reusing a link. Links meet only at circles and never cross elsewhere. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Mass center plate correspondence
worlds.question: The navy plate is one connected workbench with three labeled bays: R is the reference and A and B are candidates. Each bay contains one thick dark weight patch attached to the common rail. Reflect each candidate patch left-to-right within its bay, compare the patch area centroids, and choose the candidate whose reflected centroid matches R. Answer with that candidate's badge color.

worlds.title: Cordwalk turn echo bind
worlds.question: The picture is a cream board scattered with small decorative squares - coloured, slate-grey and black - that lie on the bare board and mean nothing. Lying on the board is exactly one thin slate-grey CORD: a single narrow line that runs as a staircase of straight horizontal and vertical runs. It never crosses or touches itself. One of its two ends is covered by a solid black square CAP; the other end is plain. One more solid black square, the RELAY, sits on the cord somewhere in the middle of a straight run, so it is the only black square with cord coming out of two opposite sides; the cap is the only black square with cord coming out of one side. The relay splits the cord into two stretches: the FIRST stretch runs from the cap to the relay, and the SECOND stretch runs from the relay to the plain end. Walk the first stretch from the cap to the relay and write down, at every corner you pass, whether you turn LEFT or RIGHT as you walk. Then walk the second stretch from the relay to the plain end and write down its turns the same way. Left and right always mean left and right for a walker facing along the cord, not up or down on the page. The two stretches always have the same number of corners, and the two lists of turns are identical except at exactly one corner, where the second stretch turns the opposite way from the first. The two stretches leave the relay in different directions, so the second stretch is the first stretch's shape turned to a new orientation with that one turn flipped, and the two lists cannot be compared by sliding one stretch onto the other on the page. A small coloured BEAD lies under the cord at every corner of the second stretch, one bead per corner, and the cord runs across it; no bead lies on the first stretch and no bead lies on the bare board. Find the one corner of the second stretch whose turn disagrees with the turn at the matching corner of the first stretch, counting corners from the relay along each stretch. The answer is the colour of the bead at that corner. Every bead colour is different from the others in the picture, each of the four bead colours is equally likely to be the answer, the disagreeing corner is equally likely to be any of the four, and the answer colour is also worn by decorative squares on the bare board, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies it on its own. What colour is that bead? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Relay key join
worlds.question: The two gold key cards each have four rows. On the left card, each navy bead cluster is paired with the colored dot in its row. On the right card, each colored dot is paired with the navy-striped tile in its row. Follow matching dot colors to pair every bead cluster with a tile. Which red, green, or blue tagged card shows all four pairs? Row order does not matter.

worlds.title: Switchback relay correspondence
worlds.question: At START, read the top-to-bottom order of the circle, square, and triangle. Follow the single dark route from START to FINISH. In route order, each red checkpoint applies a swap: one red bead swaps the top and middle slots; two red beads swap the middle and bottom slots. After all five swaps, which color tag at FINISH is beside the slot containing the circle? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Paired interval centering
worlds.question: Which target is closer to the midpoint of its own interval after dividing the midpoint offset by interval length? Answer P or Q.

worlds.title: Span bracket tally
worlds.question: The picture is a wide instrument sheet. Along its extreme left edge and along its extreme right edge there is one vertical column of horizontal bars, and the wide corridor between the two columns holds only decoration. Exactly two bars in the whole picture are coloured: one red bar and one blue bar. They are the calibration bars, they always lie in opposite columns - one on the left, one on the right - and either of them may be the longer one. Call the length of the shorter calibration bar the low mark and the length of the longer calibration bar the high mark; both are lengths, not positions. Every pure black bar, in either column, is a measurement bar. All grey and pale grey marks anywhere in the picture - bars, plates and tick lattices, inside the columns as well as in the corridor - are decoration and are never counted. Only a bar's length matters; its column, its height on the sheet, its left end and the order of the bars do not. No measurement bar ever has exactly the length of a calibration bar. Counting the measurement bars of both columns together, how many pure black bars are strictly longer than the low mark and strictly shorter than the high mark? Answer with a single whole number.

worlds.title: Annulus rim ratio
worlds.question: Is the central hole's diameter greater than the colored rim's thickness on one side? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Trace chord lobe balance
worlds.question: Imagine the straight chord joining the teal trace's two endpoints. At every horizontal position, measure the vertical gap between the trace and that chord. Is the total gap larger ABOVE or BELOW the chord? Answer ABOVE or BELOW.

worlds.title: Hash crossbar count
worlds.question: Does the single hash-style glyph visibly have exactly two near-horizontal crossbars crossing both upright stems? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Media play triangle direction
worlds.question: Which way does the large colored play triangle point—left or right? Judge its broad face and single tip; ignore the gray player controls. Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Halftone blur panel
worlds.question: Inside the single framed square panel, find its upright 24-by-24 microcell raster. Apply the declared 3-by-3 box blur: average each non-overlapping 3-by-3 block of microcells into one output cell, then mark the output cell dark when its mean RGB is darker than the midpoint of the two visible microcell tones. Read the resulting 8-by-8 bitmap and compare it with A or ). Answer A or B; a tie or a template gap below 8 is quarantined. Ignore remote marks.

worlds.title: Barb handedness reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one trace in this picture is teal; every other trace is pale lavender. The teal wire is a single unbranching zigzag: it has exactly two ends, it turns a right angle at every dark square stud between them, and all ten of its straight runs are the same length. Exactly one end of the teal wire sits in a crimson pad. Twenty-five short teal barbs stick straight out of the wire, two or three on each straight run, each barb sticking out of exactly one of the two sides of the run it belongs to. Carry out this operation. Start at the end in the crimson pad and walk along the teal wire to its other end. Each time you pass a barb, write 1 if that barb sticks out to your left as you are walking at that moment and 0 if it sticks out to your right; remember that your left changes with you at every turn of the wire, so the same direction on the page is your left on some runs and your right on others. Take the twenty-five bits in the order you meet the barbs and write them into a 5 by 5 grid, the first five bits into the top row left to right, the next five into the second row, and so on to the bottom row, then mark every grid position holding a 1. Compare the marked positions with these five symbols on the 5 by 5 grid: 'plus' is the whole centre row together with the whole centre column, 'ex' is the two whole diagonals, 'tee' is the whole top row together with the centre column below it, 'tack' is the whole bottom row together with the centre column above it, and 'ell' is the whole left column together with the whole bottom row. Each of those symbols marks exactly 9 of the 25 positions, and the answer is the one symbol that differs from your marked positions in the fewest positions; up to three positions may disagree. The shape the wire itself traces on the page is not the symbol, the lavender traces are decoration, and only your own left and right while walking the wire decide the bits. Which symbol is it? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tack, tee.

worlds.title: Running difference reveal
worlds.question: Compare matching squares in the teal and coral 7 by 7 panels. In each row, begin with a light running square and read left to right: flip its shade when the two input squares differ, otherwise keep it. Write the running shade after every pair. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Seeded floodfill reveal
worlds.question: Starting at the gold cell in the small framed 7 by 7 maze, imagine ink flooding through gaps in the dark walls to edge-sharing cells; it cannot cross a dark wall. If only the flooded cells are filled, which symbol appears: centered plus, top-bar tee, or arch? Keep the frame orientation as shown. Answer ambiguous for a tie.

worlds.title: Aperture tip polarity
worlds.question: The colored medallion contains one white tapered opening. Compare its two radial ends: does its narrow tip point toward the medallion center or away from it? Answer inward or outward.

worlds.title: Pocket escape patch
worlds.question: A single colored patch surrounds a pale center pocket and has two broad pale inlets. Is the center pocket completely sealed off from the outer pale background? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Quarter turn tile search
worlds.question: Which labeled tile looks exactly the same after a quarter-turn (90 degree) rotation? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Rank echo search
worlds.question: The two separated columns each contain one marker of every color. Rank the markers from top to bottom within each column. Which color has the same rank in both columns? Exactly one color qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State earliest region entry
