worlds.question: The image has four separate numbered cards in reading order: card 1 is upper-left, card 2 upper-right, card 3 lower-left, and card 4 lower-right. Read them in number order. Each card shows objects A, B, C, and D in top-to-bottom rows. The unshaded left side is OUTSIDE and the shaded right side is INSIDE. An object makes an entry only when its marker is outside on one card and inside on the next. Consider only objects inside on card 4. Which object makes the earliest entry? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Ladder rung walk
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small ladder: four thin vertical rails of the same length standing side by side, joined by short horizontal rungs. Each rung joins two neighbouring rails, and every rung sits at its own height, so no two rungs are level. A small coloured square is welded under the bottom end of each rail; the four squares are red, green, blue and purple in some order. A solid dark triangular tab sits just above the top end of exactly one rail, and that rail is where the walk begins. The walk moves downwards. Whenever it reaches an end of a rung on the rail it is currently on, it crosses that rung to the neighbouring rail and then carries on downwards from there; rungs are met in top-to-bottom order, and a rung that does not touch the rail the walk is currently on is passed by with no effect. The walk ends at the bottom end of whichever rail it is on then. The ladder may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside the ladder is inert decoration. Which colour is the square under the rail where the walk ends? Answer with one of red, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Torus pilot mosaic
worlds.question: The gold-ringed arrow on the START board shows the pilot's cell and heading. Read the command tiles in row order, left-to-right then top-to-bottom. A cyan curved arrow turns the pilot 90 degrees clockwise without moving. A coral chevron moves the pilot one cell forward; crossing an edge wraps to the opposite edge of the 3 by 3 board. Which lettered cell contains the pilot after every command?

worlds.title: Notched swap ribbon
worlds.question: The green bead's row gives the token's starting lane: A is top, B middle, and C bottom. Follow the blue ribbon from green to red, left to right. Each upward notch swaps A with B; each downward notch swaps B with C. Apply all six notches in order. Which lane holds the token at the end: A, B, or C?

worlds.title: Mandatory route station
worlds.question: The black tracks form one connected network with no loops. Tracks meet only at visible junctions. Which station lies on the unique track route from orange to blue: cyan or yellow?

worlds.title: Nesting rank reversal
worlds.question: Ignore pale gray marks. Across the two separate emblems, does the more deeply enclosed color reverse? A dot's depth is the number of closed navy loops surrounding it. Answer yes if orange is deeper in one emblem and purple is deeper in the other; answer no if the same color is deeper in both. There are no ties.

worlds.title: Tick twin run
worlds.question: The picture contains exactly one dark wire: a single unbranched stroke of constant thickness that winds across the whole picture. The wire never branches, never crosses itself and never touches itself; parallel folds of the wire are always separated by clear background. Eight small square ticks are printed on the wire, four orange and four blue, so the two colours are always four and four and counting colours never gives the answer. Every tick is narrower than the wire, so a tick never cuts the wire and the ink runs past it on both sides. Two ticks are neighbours only if you meet them one straight after the other while walking along the wire's own ink; stepping across background, or onto a neighbouring fold, is never a legal step. Exactly one pair of neighbours along the wire has two ticks of the same colour; every other pair of neighbours has two different colours. Straight-line looks are not a guide: the two ticks of the same-coloured pair always sit far apart on the page, and the two same-coloured ticks that look closest together on the page are never that pair. Gray squares near the border are decoration and mean nothing. Which colour is shared by the one pair of neighbouring ticks along the wire that have the same colour? Answer orange or blue.

worlds.title: Cyclic checkpoint neighbors
worlds.question: Trace the dark closed loop. Are the two cyan checkpoints consecutive around the loop, with no orange checkpoint between them?

worlds.title: Paired checkpoint change compare
worlds.question: Two separate routes are shown, one in each panel. Starting at each blue ring, follow that dark route to its orange finish and read its six red or green checkpoints in travel order. Count one change whenever two consecutive checkpoints have different colors. Which route has more changes: left or right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Division fraction correspondence
worlds.question: Three horizontal bars are shown: the REFERENCE bar at the top, and two candidate bars labeled A and B below. Every bar is split by a vertical boundary into a navy left part and a teal right part, but the bars have different total lengths. In the REFERENCE bar the navy part occupies a certain fraction of that bar's own length. Exactly one candidate bar is split at the same fraction of its own length as the REFERENCE; the other is split at a clearly different fraction. Which candidate, A or B, has the same left/right division as the REFERENCE? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Binary pair correspondence
worlds.question: Which QUERY pair is JOIN? Replace each badge with its KEY A token, then find that unordered pair in PAIR KEY. Answer 1 or 2.

worlds.title: Rung removal replay
worlds.question: A token drops down this ladder from the black arrow: it slides down its vertical line, and at every horizontal rung it meets it crosses to the neighbouring line and keeps going down. The pale yellow band shows the route it takes in the ladder as drawn. The six slots along the bottom are numbered 1 to 6 from left to right. Exactly one rung is red; every other rung is blue. Take the red rung away, leave everything else unchanged, and drop the token again from the same arrow. Which slot does it reach? Answer with exactly one of: slot-1, slot-2, slot-3, slot-4, slot-5, slot-6.

worlds.title: Register match rotation escape
worlds.question: The front badge moves that token. Turn RIGHT on GOLD or LEFT on BLUE and flip. Compare old HERE with old matching LINK. If SAME: card to HERE, old HERE to LINK, old LINK to BACK. If DIFFERENT: card to LINK, old LINK to HERE, old HERE to BACK. Step. Which exits first? Answer token-red or token-violet.

worlds.title: Counterturn rendezvous
worlds.question: In each panel, first reflect both cell groups across the dashed red line. Then turn blue 90 degrees clockwise about the green pin and violet 90 degrees counterclockwise about the orange pin. In which panel do both groups land on exactly the same cells? Answer panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, or panel-4.

worlds.title: Correspondence scatter scope
worlds.question: The gray constellation at the top is a scatter of gray dots that spread out to a certain scope. Below it are three colored constellations A, B, C: one is red, one green, one blue, and each spreads to a different scope. Which colored constellation has dots that spread out to exactly the same scope as the gray constellation? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Fraction denominator correspondence
worlds.question: Which candidate fraction, A or B, has a numerator with the same number of solid marks as the green denominator in the reference fraction? A is the left card and B is the right card; ignore mark color, size, and card decoration. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Share wheel sector binding
worlds.question: The top panel of this image shows four upright bars - one red, one blue, one green and one orange - standing on a common black baseline. The bottom panel shows a gray wheel cut into four sectors by dark spokes running from the center to the rim. The four sectors stand for the four bars: each bar matches exactly one sector, and each bar's share of the total height of all four bars equals its sector's share of the full turn of the wheel. No length unit is drawn, so only these shares can be compared, and the left-to-right order of the bars has nothing to do with where its sector sits on the wheel. Just outside each sector, at the middle of that sector, sits a black glyph tag - a square, a circle, a triangle, or a diamond - and each glyph tags the sector it sits beside. Which glyph tags the sector that matches the red bar? Answer square, circle, triangle, or diamond.

worlds.title: Nearest neighbor map
worlds.question: The top card is the REFERENCE. Each card contains one red, blue, green, and purple dot. For every dot, find the other dot whose center is closest to it. Which colored border encloses the bottom card with exactly the same color-to-closest-color map as the reference? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Slot shuffle correspondence
worlds.question: Match the patterned tiles to learn how the four slots were rearranged. Apply that same rearrangement to the colored tiles. Which candidate result is correct: A, B, or C? Patterns and colors do not rotate or change.

worlds.title: Mean height compare
worlds.question: Colored vertical bars stand on a shared baseline. The red bars and the blue bars each form their own group, and the two groups contain different numbers of bars. Which color's bars have the GREATER average height, meaning the larger mean bar height within that color's group? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Checkpoint range compare
worlds.question: Panels A and B each show one colored piecewise-linear trace through nine marked checkpoints. For each trace, subtract the lowest checkpoint center from the highest checkpoint center. Which panel has the larger vertical dynamic range? Answer A or B; ignore color, stroke width, and panel placement.

worlds.title: Gap fit binding
worlds.question: The picture shows one solid black BAR near the top and four grey rails below it, one above the other. The four rails all start at the same left position and end at the same right position, and each rail is marked at both of its ends by a short downward grey stub. Standing on each rail is a row of solid blocks, all of them in that rail's own colour: one rail carries red blocks, one green, one blue and one orange. An EMPTY STRETCH of a rail is a piece of that rail with no block standing on it; the piece of rail between the left end and the first block, and the piece between the last block and the right end, are empty stretches too, exactly like the pieces between neighbouring blocks. A rail ACCEPTS the bar when at least one single empty stretch of that rail is wider than the black bar, so that the bar could be set down there without overlapping a block; only one empty stretch at a time may be used, and empty stretches on the same rail are never added together. In every picture exactly one of the four rails accepts the bar, and the bar is never the same width as any empty stretch. Only the widest single empty stretch of a rail matters. The rail with the most empty rail in total, the rail with the most blocks, the rail with the fewest blocks, the rail carrying the widest single block and the rail with the least block material are each the answer no more often than chance allows, and so is the topmost rail; the horizontal position of the black bar carries no information and only its width counts. Which rail accepts the bar? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Checkpoint total variation
worlds.question: Which colored series travels the greatest total vertical distance? Order its five circular checkpoints from left to right and add the absolute vertical changes between consecutive checkpoints. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Histogram halfmass crossing
worlds.question: All six colored histogram bars have equal width. Starting at the left, add their visible heights. The gray TOTAL reference marks half of their combined height. Dividers D1-D4 are labeled from left to right. At which divider does the running sum first reach or exceed half the total? Answer D1, D2, D3, or D4.

worlds.title: Prior piano keys
worlds.question: This is a piano keyboard. A conventional piano octave has seven white keys, but report exactly what is drawn here. How many white keys are shown? Count only the visible white keys and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Rainbow middle band color
worlds.question: What color is the middle band of the rainbow? Count the five visible bands from top to bottom and answer with a color.

worlds.title: Paddock gate gap
worlds.question: This image shows a pen drawn on white paper with one animal in it. The FENCE is the large loop of thick straight rails, all painted in the same single dark colour; it is the only barrier in the picture. The ANIMAL is the one solid round blob inside the loop. The pale elongated bars inside the pen are feeding troughs and the four short grey ticks at the corners of the page are fixed decoration: neither is a barrier, neither blocks movement, and both are drawn the same way whatever the answer is. A GAP is a stretch of one rail where no paint has been laid down, so the white paper runs straight through the line of the fence from the inside of the pen to the outside. There is at most one gap; it may sit anywhere along any rail, or there may be no gap at all. The animal counts as able to get out if it can travel from where it stands to the edge of the page without ever crossing painted fence; it may walk over troughs freely, and it does not matter how far it happens to be standing from the fence or from the gap. The shape and size of the pen, the number of rails, the thickness of the rails, the colours, the number of troughs, and where the animal stands all change from image to image and none of them tells you the answer. Judge only the fence you can actually see in this image, and do not assume that a pen drawn round an animal must be closed. Can the animal get out of the pen? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Flag edge stripes
worlds.question: Along the flag's right edge, how many alternating horizontal stripes are visible? Count each color band once.

worlds.title: Magnifier handle side conflict
worlds.question: Which way does the handle extend from the circular lens: down-left or down-right? Answer down-left or down-right.

worlds.title: Lowpass icon reveal
worlds.question: The image is pure high-frequency speckle hiding a large letter. Blur it until the speckle averages away. Which letter, A or B, emerges? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Complementary stencil symbol
worlds.question: Find the two grayscale plates from their same-colored corner marks. Align their interiors, keep the lighter value at each pixel, and choose the revealed symbol: ring, cross, diamond, or zigzag.

worlds.title: Stripe phase moire reveal
worlds.question: The image shows two square plates side by side, each bounded by a printed registration frame. Each plate is ruled into the same 7 by 7 grid of cells, and every cell of both plates is filled edge to edge with fine vertical stripes of the same width and the same spacing; only the position at which a cell's stripes start differs from cell to cell. Pair each cell of the left plate with the cell in the same row and the same column of the right plate, and compare the two stripe patterns of the pair. Mark the cell when the two patterns are out of step, meaning the right plate's dark stripes sit nearer to the middle of the left plate's light gaps than to its dark stripes, so that laying the right plate over the left would close the gaps and fill the cell solid. Leave the cell unmarked when the two patterns are more nearly in step, so that laying one plate over the other would leave the cell striped. The marked cells form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: cross, ring, saltire, tee, wedge. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Cross clue nonogram
worlds.question: The blue bars beside each row and above each column give, in order, the lengths of consecutive black runs; separate bars mean separate runs. Fill the 8 by 8 grid so every row and column matches its bars. Which symbol appears: circle, kite, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Edge coded mosaic reassembly
worlds.question: Arrange the nine square cards as a 3-by-3 mosaic, without reflecting them. Rotate and move cards so every outer bar is on its named side—gold at top, orange at right, violet at bottom, and cyan at left—and every pair of touching inner bars has exactly the same color. Then join the 3-by-3 tile patches. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Constellation trace letter
worlds.question: A set of small dark dots is drawn on a white canvas. The dots are placed all along the strokes of one single capital letter, so together the whole constellation traces that letter's outline. Which capital letter do the dots trace? Choose T, L, V, or X.

worlds.title: Diagonal texture rhythm
worlds.question: Ignore hue, panel placement, dot size, and total ink. The fields contain equal-count continuous mark clouds; which one has a whole-field alternating rhythm when viewed along a diagonal? Choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Similarity grouping axis
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain background and an 8 by 8 square grid of 64 small marks, all painted in the same single dark colour on the same plain background. The 64 marks sit at equally spaced positions, with exactly the same spacing between neighbouring columns as between neighbouring rows, so no mark is closer to its left and right neighbours than to its neighbours above and below. Every mark is one of exactly two kinds and nothing else: a solid dot, whose middle is filled with the dark colour, or a hollow ring, whose middle is left empty in the background colour. Both kinds are drawn with the same amount of dark paint, so the two kinds cannot be told apart by how much ink they use, only by whether the middle is filled or empty. Score the picture as follows. For one horizontal row of 8 marks, its purity is the difference between the number of solid dots and the number of hollow rings in that row, taken as a positive number, divided by 8. The row score of the picture is the average of the purities of its 8 horizontal rows. The column score is defined in exactly the same way over the 8 vertical columns of 8 marks. One score is always strictly larger than the other; they are never equal. Nothing else matters: the background shade, the mark shade, the size of the marks, the spacing of the grid, the position of the grid on the canvas, the total amount of ink, how many solid dots and how many hollow rings the picture holds in total, and which kind sits in any particular corner all carry no information about the answer, and neither does any single row or column on its own, because only the average over all 8 rows and the average over all 8 columns decide it. Which score is larger, the row score or the column score? Answer rows or columns.

worlds.title: Constellation principal axis
worlds.question: Treat every black dot as an equal point. Which colored dashed line through their average center follows the direction in which the complete dot constellation has the greatest spread? Answer orange or blue.

worlds.title: Translation mode constellation
worlds.question: The dark dots contain two copies of one constellation under a single slide, plus unpaired distractors. A slide pairs multiple dots with one equal-length parallel displacement. Which colored undirected guide below is parallel to that repeated slide? Reversing a guide counts as the same direction. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Unique vertex count search
worlds.question: Four dark convex polygons are drawn, one in each quadrant of the image (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right), and they are all the same size. The number of sides of a polygon is how many straight edges bound it. Exactly three of the polygons have the same number of sides, while the fourth polygon has a different number of sides. Which quadrant contains the polygon whose number of sides is different from the other three?

worlds.title: Cyclic color pair search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only six-dot ring in which at least one pair of same-colored dots occupies neighboring positions? Read neighbors in the visible circular order, including the wraparound pair between the last and first dot; ignore the color names and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Spoke degree hub panel
worlds.question: This image shows one small framed box labelled KEY standing alone above a row of five larger framed panels of identical size, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every hub in the image is a filled coloured dot with thin straight spokes radiating outward from it; every spoke is a separate straight line of the same length, and no spoke ever reaches another hub. The KEY box holds exactly one hub and every panel holds exactly three hubs. Hub colour, hub size, spoke length, spoke thickness and hub position are dealt independently of the answer and never carry information. Every one of the five panels holds eleven spokes in total, so hub count, total spoke count and total ink are identical in every panel and can never separate them. A single hub carries between two and six spokes, and the spokes of a hub are always separated by a plainly visible angle, so they can be counted one by one. Neither the direction a spoke points, nor the order of the spokes around a hub, nor the colour of a hub matters: only how many spokes a hub has. Exactly one hub in the five panels carries the same number of spokes as the key hub, and every other hub in the five panels differs from the key hub by at least one spoke. Each of the four panels without that hub still holds at least one hub whose spoke count is within one of the key's, so no panel stands out by holding conspicuously crowded or conspicuously bare hubs. Which numbered panel contains the hub with exactly as many spokes as the key hub? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Shared neighbor terminals search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has exactly one gray circle directly linked to both the MAGENTA circle and the AMBER circle? Count a link only when the dark line meets the circle; A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Noncrossing chords search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has three colored straight strokes with no pair crossing? Colors may blend where strokes cross. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State slot accumulator
worlds.question: Five ordered panels read left to right each show the same five-slot track, whose slots are numbered 0 to 4 from left to right, and a marker token in one slot. The orange ring marks the marker's starting slot in the leftmost panel. Between consecutive panels an operator glyph is shown: a red right-pointing triangle advances the marker one slot and a blue left-pointing triangle retreats it one slot. Applying the operators in order across the panels, which slot does the marker finish in? Answer '0', '1', '2', '3' or '4'.

worlds.title: Checkpoint state delta
worlds.question: Read the visible panels in order P1 then P2. Each labeled object has one categorical state shown by the STATE KEY. Exactly one object's state changes between the panels. Which label changes? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Deal collect shuffle
worlds.question: The top row of the picture is a hand of nine coloured discs, all nine colours different, standing side by side; the grey arrow under them shows that they are dealt one at a time in drawn left-to-right order. A thick black ring is drawn around the hand at one place: the ringed disc is the disc whose centre is nearest the centre of that ring, and the ring is drawn behind the discs, so a disc may cover part of it. In the middle of the picture is a row of coloured bins, all of different colours, and these are the piles: they receive discs in their drawn left-to-right order. Dealing goes round the bins in that order over and over, so the first disc of the hand goes to the leftmost bin, the next disc to the bin to its right, and so on; after the rightmost bin the next disc goes to the leftmost bin again, until all nine discs have been dealt. Each pile keeps its own discs in the order it received them, earliest received first. The bottom row of coloured chips is the pick-up order, read left to right as the grey arrow beneath it shows: each chip has the colour of one bin, every bin appears exactly once, and the piles are picked up in that order. The picked-up piles are then laid down end to end in one final row, each pile keeping its own order, earliest received first, so the first picked-up pile fills the leftmost places of the final row, the next picked-up pile the places just to its right, and so on. The nine places of the final row are numbered one to nine from the left. No pile and no final row is drawn anywhere in the picture; only the starting hand, the bins and the chips are drawn. Disc colours carry no rule and only name the discs. Once every disc has been dealt and every pile has been laid down, which numbered place of the final row holds the ringed disc? Answer with one word: one, two, three, four, five, six, seven, eight or nine.

worlds.title: Prefix flip stack
worlds.question: The four shape tokens start in the stack shown. A solid dot means face-up; a hollow dot means face-down. Read the flip cards from left to right. On each card, the blue prefix shows how many tokens from the top to reverse, then flip every moved token face-up to face-down or face-down to face-up. What shape and face state finishes at the slot marked TARGET?

worlds.title: Deferred toggle pulse
worlds.question: Four pip-labeled lamps start as shown (filled = ON, ring = OFF). Read the eight cards from left to right. A triangular TICKET card adds one pending toggle for the lamp named by its 1-4 pips; it does not change any lamp yet. A circular PULSE card applies every pending toggle, then clears all pending tickets. Two pending toggles for the same lamp cancel. Tickets still pending after card 8 are never applied. After all cards, how many lamps are ON? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Cycle membership
worlds.question: In this picture a network of links joins circular nodes. Precisely three links are tinted: red, green, and blue, while every other link is black. A link is part of a closed loop when, if you mentally cut only that link, its two ends still join up through the rest of the net (it is not a bridge). Exactly one of the three tinted links is part of a closed loop. Which tinted link (red, green, or blue) is the one lying on a loop? Reply with exactly red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Bounded face count
worlds.question: Inside the black frame, how many separate white chambers are enclosed? Treat every black stroke as a wall, ignore the colored dots, and count only white regions that cannot reach outside the frame. Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Hinge node pick
worlds.question: The picture shows a wiring harness on white paper. Grey wires of equal thickness join only where they meet at a junction, and no two wires cross anywhere in the picture, so wires that merely pass near each other are not joined. Three junctions are marked by round coloured patches - one red, one green, one blue - and the grey wires are painted across these patches, so the wiring runs through each patch without a break. Now imagine rubbing out one whole round patch: everything inside that circle disappears, including the pieces of grey wire crossing it, while all ink outside the circle stays exactly as drawn, including the other two patches and their wiring. The remaining grey wiring is in one piece if you can travel between any two bits of grey wire along grey wire the whole way, never jumping a gap. As drawn, before any rubbing out, all the grey wiring is a single piece. Rubbing out exactly one of the three patches breaks the remaining grey wiring into two or more separate pieces; rubbing out either of the other two leaves it in one piece. Which patch is the one that breaks the wiring? Answer 'red', 'green', or 'blue'.

worlds.title: Island in lake marker
worlds.question: Black ink forms land components and white space is water. Which colored dot is on a black land component lying inside a fully enclosed white lake of a different black component? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Marker region partition
worlds.question: The four colored dots lie inside a black-walled box. Two dots occupy the same region only when a path through white space connects them without crossing a black wall; corner-only contact does not connect. Do the dots occupy exactly two regions? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Geodesic nearest terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the orange ring and walking only along the blue path, which coloured terminal -- red, green, or blue -- is the closest to the ring along the path? Answer with the colour only.

worlds.title: Marked bridge survivor
worlds.question: Trace the dark network from the green source. If the purple-ringed bridge is closed, which terminal remains connected: red or blue? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Strand more ends
worlds.question: This picture shows grey strands on a white page. Two ports are marked, one by a blue ring and one by an orange ring, and each ring sits on a strand. Small black squares mark the ends of strands. Grey strand is the only kind of connection: two things are joined only when you can travel from one to the other along grey strand without ever leaving it. The strands attached to the blue ring and the strands attached to the orange ring form two separate systems that never touch and never cross, so every black square is joined to exactly one of the two rings. Being close together on the page does not mean being joined. Which ring is joined to more black squares by its strands, the blue ring or the orange ring? Answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Subtree terminal checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green root, follow the dark tree away from it. Which colored circular checkpoint has exactly three gray square terminals downstream? A terminal is downstream when its unique route from the green root passes through that checkpoint. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Key sequence terminal
worlds.question: The five cyan shapes at the top form a key; read them left to right. Starting at the green disk in each panel, follow the unbranched black chain and read its five purple checkpoint shapes in travel order. Which colored terminal has exactly the same shape sequence as the key? Links meet only at markers and never cross. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Mosaic density correspondence
worlds.question: The compact cassette contains a reference badge R and candidate badges A and B. Each badge is a 4x4 dark-cell mosaic with equal total ink. Reflect each candidate mosaic left-to-right. For each badge, count dark cells in its four 2x2 quadrants in clockwise order starting at upper-left. Choose the candidate whose transformed four-count sequence equals R, then answer with that candidate's seal color.

worlds.title: Foldcord span partner bind
worlds.question: The picture is a cream board scattered with small decorative squares that mean nothing. Lying across the board is exactly one thin CORD: a single narrow route of straight horizontal and vertical runs that never crosses or touches itself. One black square CLAMP, larger than any decorative square, sits on the cord. On one side of the clamp the cord is TEAL and on the other side it is TAN. Sitting on the cord are large coloured BEADS, each a disc of red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple, and exactly one bead on the teal stretch wears a grey COLLAR ring. Only discs sitting on the cord are beads; every small square lying on the bare board away from the cord is decoration and means nothing, including decorative squares in teal, tan, black or any bead colour. The cord is folded at the clamp, and the fold pairs each point of the teal stretch with the point of the tan stretch that lies the same TRAVEL DISTANCE from the clamp, where travel distance means the length of the walk along the cord itself, following every corner and every detour hump, and never a straight-line distance. Measure the travel distance from the clamp to the collared bead along the teal stretch, then find the bead on the tan stretch whose travel distance from the clamp is the same. That bead is the FOLD PARTNER. Because the cord doubles back and its runs carry detour humps, the fold partner is never the tan bead that comes at the same place in bead order from the clamp, never the tan bead nearest the collared bead in a straight line, never the tan bead at the most similar height, never the tan bead in the most similar column, and never the first or the last tan bead along the cord. The partner's colour is worn by at least two beads in the picture and is never the single commonest bead colour, and the collared bead never wears it, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies it on its own. Find the fold partner of the collared bead. What is its colour? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Permutation quilt
worlds.question: The five mosaics are stamps on one continuous navy quilt. The top mosaic is the reference. A matching stamp may rearrange whole rows and rearrange whole columns independently, but may not change any tile. Which colored frame encloses the matching mosaic?

worlds.title: Woven necklace correspondence
worlds.question: Treat the twelve colored tiles after the neutral patch in the top band as a loop. Treat each lower band the same way: the loop may start anywhere and may be read clockwise or counterclockwise. Which lower loop preserves the full order, and what is the color of its first patch? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Unpaired length row
worlds.question: A pale sheet shows two small light grey panels far apart, one on the left and one on the right, with empty sheet between them. The left panel holds four solid dark navy bars and the right panel holds three, all of the same thickness. The bars do not share a common left edge, so measure each bar only by its own length from its own left end to its own right end. Three of the four left bars have exactly one right bar of exactly the same length, and every right bar is used by exactly one of them; exactly one left bar has no right bar of its length. The unpaired left bar is neither the longest nor the shortest bar in the left panel. All four left bars have different lengths. Vertical position, thickness, left edge position, and the pale coloured decoration outside the panels carry no information. Numbering the left-panel bars 1, 2, 3, 4 from the top downwards, which numbered left bar has no equal-length partner in the right panel? Answer with one digit.

worlds.title: Route turn majority
worlds.question: Follow the dark-blue route from the coral start dot to the blue finish dot. Across its five bends, are there more left turns or right turns? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Interval clearance comparison
worlds.question: In each panel, measure the horizontal empty gap between the two colored capped intervals, from the right edge of the left interval to the left edge of the right interval. Which panel has the larger gap? Answer LEFT or RIGHT.

worlds.title: Visible star point count
worlds.question: How many sharp outward points does the single large filled star have? Count only the outer tips, not the inward notches.

worlds.title: Paperclip round turns
worlds.question: How many large rounded end turns does the single colored paperclip wire make? Count a turn only where the wire visibly reverses horizontal direction; follow the whole wire and answer 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Peel layer reveal
worlds.question: This picture contains exactly one large square panel with a solid dark border, plus a few much smaller dark specks scattered on the background outside it that are decoration only. The panel's border encloses an eleven-by-eleven grid of 121 equal square cells; each cell is entirely dark, in the same tone as the border, or entirely pale, in the same tone as the panel's background. The dark cells form one thick solid blob. Carry out this operation on that grid, and only then read the answer. Peel one layer off the blob: delete every dark cell that touches a pale cell or touches the outside of the grid, counting a touch at a shared corner as well as a touch along a shared edge. Equivalently, keep a dark cell only when all eight cells surrounding it are dark cells of the grid, and delete every other dark cell. Delete them all at once, judging every cell against the grid as it is drawn rather than against the partly peeled grid. The cells that survive this single peel form exactly one of these four figures, described with the rows numbered 0 to 10 from the top of the grid and the columns numbered 0 to 10 from its left. 'bars' is two horizontal bars of five cells lying four rows apart: row 2 from column 2 to column 6, and row 6 from column 4 to column 8. 'pipes' is two vertical bars of five cells lying four columns apart: column 3 from row 2 to row 6, and column 7 from row 4 to row 8. 'tee' is a horizontal bar of five cells in row 3 from column 3 to column 7, with a vertical bar of five cells hanging from the middle of it, in column 5 from row 4 to row 8. 'corner' is a horizontal bar of five cells in row 4 from column 4 to column 8, with a vertical bar of five cells descending from its left end, in column 3 from row 4 to row 8, so the two bars meet at a square corner. Each figure is exactly ten cells, and every two of them differ in at least twelve cells. Whichever figure is hidden, the panel as drawn always carries exactly fifty dark cells, and those dark cells always fill the same bounding rectangle, from row 1 to row 9 and from column 1 to column 9, leaving the outermost ring of cells entirely pale. Neither the amount of dark ink, nor the extent of the blob, nor the panel's size, position or colour therefore reveals the figure. The blob as drawn is not any of the four figures and does not contain one that is readable without the peel: only the peel reveals it. Which figure do the surviving cells form? Answer with exactly one of: bars, corner, pipes, tee.

worlds.title: Checkerboard carrier weave
worlds.question: Take every square whose row plus column is even from the one-dot panel (the top-left square is even). Take every other square from the two-dot panel. Keep all squares in their original positions. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Orthogonal ruler projection
worlds.question: Each detached ruler has seven slots. On the circle-marked ruler, each filled tab selects a whole row of an imagined 7 by 7 grid. On the triangle-marked ruler, each filled tab selects a whole column. Fill every selected row and column. Ignoring rotation and reflection, which symbol appears: plus, tee, or corner? Answer ambiguous if two symbols are equally close by cell changes.

worlds.title: Illusory triangle closure
worlds.question: The card has exactly three separate colored notched disks. Treat each notch as an open mouth and imagine continuing its two straight sides into the central blank space. Do all three mouths face inward to outline one closed illusory triangle, or is one mouth turned away so the triangle is broken? Answer closed or broken.

worlds.title: Bend motif echo
worlds.question: Follow the single dark trail from the round cap to the square cap. Small colored beads mark each slant boundary, and the large diamond splits it into eight slants before and eight after. Reading each slant as rising or falling as you move right, is the second eight-slant pattern the same as the first, or its exact up/down opposite? Answer same or opposite.

worlds.title: Rectangle constellation search
worlds.question: Which labeled card has four cyan dots at the corners of a rectangle? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Signed dot delta search
worlds.question: The gray reference pair at the top shows a left-to-right change in dot count. Which colored pair below has the same signed change, including direction? Exactly one matches. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State transition inventory
worlds.question: Start at the ringed badge and trace the one connected route in increasing station-number order. The token has states A, B, and C; red means A, green means B, and blue means C. A filled right triangle advances one step A-B-C-A, a filled left triangle retreats one step, and an outlined square leaves the state unchanged. Include the change from the start to station 1, ignore unchanged steps, and count each directed change in the complete route history. Which directed change occurs most often? Answer AB, BC, CA, AC, CB, or BA.

worlds.title: Slab stack replay
worlds.question: This picture contains one slab: a four-by-four block of sixteen square tiles of the same size, separated by thin dark lines. Every mark outside the slab is inert decoration and changes nothing. Read the sixteen tiles in reading order, that is row by row starting at the top-left tile, each row left to right. The top-left tile is filled edge to edge with one solid colour, and that colour is the single chip already stacked on an imaginary spike. Each of the fifteen remaining tiles is one instruction, applied in reading order. A tile carrying a small coloured disk means put one chip of that colour on top of the stack. A tile carrying a dark cross means take the top chip off the stack and discard it. The removals never empty the stack, and the only chip colours are red, green, blue and purple. After all fifteen instructions have been applied, which colour is the chip on top of the stack? Answer with one of red, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Two pile ferry
worlds.question: The gold START card shows piles A and B from bottom to top. Read transfer cards by their dot counts, 1 through 4. A cyan card moves the top token of A onto B; a coral card moves the top token of B onto A. If the source is empty, nothing moves. Which color is on top of pile A after all four cards?

worlds.title: Emblem flip correspondence
worlds.question: Read the two cards from left to right. Each card contains the same three emblems, possibly rearranged. A vertical black bar means RAISED; a horizontal black bar means FLAT. Exactly one emblem changes state from the left card to the right card. Which emblem changed: circle, triangle, or square?

worlds.title: Threaded terminal trace
worlds.question: Starting at the orange dot, follow the continuous black filament. At a crossing, the white-edged filament passes over without joining the strand beneath. Which colored dot does it reach: blue or green?

worlds.title: Serpentine station order
worlds.question: Begin at the green terminal and follow the single navy trail without jumping. Do you encounter the orange station before the purple station? The trail never branches or crosses. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Fat rover reach
worlds.question: The blue shape is one connected corridor network. The dark disk is a rover. The rover may slide anywhere, in any direction, as long as its entire disk stays on blue; it may not shrink, and it may not leave the blue area. A dot counts as reached when the rover center can arrive exactly on that dot. How many of the three colored dots can the rover reach? Answer 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Paired turn sequence
worlds.question: Trace each separate navy route from its green START to its red FINISH. At every yellow square corner, record whether the route turns left or right. Are the two complete turn sequences the same? Answer same or different.

worlds.title: Paired order agreement
worlds.question: Two separate dark routes are shown. Start at each blue ring and follow its route to the orange end. Each red or green checkpoint ring is attached by a short dark stem; encounter it when you reach that stem. Do the two routes encounter red and green in the same order? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Coupled pair transition
worlds.question: A running state is an ordered pair of two colours: a LEADER colour and a FOLLOWER colour. The KEY table lists nine rows, one for every ordered source pair; each row shows two source squares (the current LEADER, then the current FOLLOWER) and, after the arrow, the two squares of the pair the state turns into under one application of the transition. The pair labelled START shows the initial LEADER and FOLLOWER. A row of STEPS dots gives the number of times to compose the transition: each step reads the current pair's KEY row and moves to the pair shown there. After exactly as many transition steps as there are STEPS dots, what is the final LEADER colour? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Paired motion collision
worlds.question: Each panel shows a blue disk and an orange disk. An arrow starting at each disk shows its movement. Imagine moving each disk by its own arrow vector. Which panel would make the two disks overlap? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Dispatch head shuffle
worlds.question: Seven discs sit in seven slots, numbered 1 to 7 from the left, and the strip is a loop: counting past slot 7 continues at slot 1, and counting back past slot 1 continues at slot 7. The black arrow starts under one slot. The key below gives every colour a direction and a number of slots, drawn as that many grey squares. Do this twelve times: look at the disc in the slot the arrow is under, find that colour in the key, count that many slots from the arrow's slot in the key's direction, swap the disc in the arrow's slot with the disc you land on, then move the arrow one slot to the right. Which slot holds the red disc after the twelfth swap? Answer with the slot number alone: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7.

worlds.title: Register swap queue escape
worlds.question: The front badge moves that token. On its current tile: turn RIGHT on GOLD or LEFT on BLUE, flip the color, swap the front badge with the small tile badge, step, and send the changed card to the queue back. Repeat until one token leaves. Which exits first? Answer token-red or token-violet.

worlds.title: Corner keyed tile cycle
worlds.question: Repeat 7 turns. Read the tile in the gold READER cell. Its cyan corner dot chooses the 2 by 2 block toward that corner. Flip that tile. If it was LIGHT, cycle the four tiles one corner clockwise; if DARK, counterclockwise. Tiles move without turning. Which numbered tile is in READER after turn 7? Answer 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.

worlds.title: Triangle apex angle correspondence
worlds.question: A gray triangle is shown at the top (the reference). Below, three colored isosceles triangles (red, green, blue), each with its point up and a different apex angle. Find the triangle whose apex angle exactly matches the reference triangle's apex angle, then report that triangle's color (red, green, or blue).

worlds.title: Colored endpoint count correspondence
worlds.question: The image has a REFERENCE panel and candidates A and B. Each colored radial glyph has an endpoint count: count its outer arm tips, excluding the central hub. Which candidate has the same color-to-endpoint-count assignment as the REFERENCE? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Polyomino rotation binding
worlds.question: The top row shows four block shapes, each made of four squares and each painted a different color. The bottom row shows the same four shapes in gray: they appear in a different left-to-right order and each one has been turned by a quarter, half, or three-quarter turn, but none of them was mirrored or resized. Exactly one gray shape is enclosed in a black rectangular frame. Which color is the framed shape in the top row? Answer with red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Constellation landmark transfer
worlds.question: The two boxes show the same five-dot constellation after a turn and uniform resizing, never reflection. The ring marks one dot in the right box. Which color marks its matching dot in the left box? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Edge clue assembly correspondence
worlds.question: Place the four upright tiles into the 2 by 2 frame without rotating them. Adjacent tile edges must show the same number of navy squares, and each shown outer clue must match the touching tile edge; blank outer sides impose no clue. Which center-tag color belongs in the magenta-ringed cell? Answer red, green, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Lever torque balance
worlds.question: A horizontal gray beam rests on a small black fulcrum triangle. A red disk sits on the beam to the left of the fulcrum and a blue disk sits on the beam to the right. Treat each disk's weight as proportional to its area (pi times its radius squared), and its side's torque as the weight times the horizontal distance from the disk's center to the fulcrum. Which color's side has the larger torque and therefore tips down? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Heatmap column reversal
worlds.question: Each panel is a heatmap with four labeled rows (A-D) and five equal-width columns. Using the shared cold-to-hot scale, average each row's five cell heats. Which row is greatest in panel P and smallest in panel Q? Choose A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Even split fraction
worlds.question: The picture shows five solid coloured BARS, one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple. Each bar is a horizontal block lying in its own row, and every bar is cut by exactly one short black DIVIDER that stands across it. A bar's LENGTH is the distance from its own left end to its own right end. A bar's MIDDLE is the point half way between those two ends; the middle is never marked. A bar's SPLIT is how far its own divider sits from its own middle, counted as a share of that same bar's own length: the distance from the divider to the middle, divided by the length of that bar. So a divider that sits exactly half way along its bar has a split of zero, and the same gap in millimetres counts for MORE on a short bar than on a long bar. Read every bar against its own two ends only, never against another bar and never against the page. The answer is the colour with the SMALLEST split, that is, the colour whose divider cuts its own bar most nearly into two equal halves. Cheap readings are deliberately steered elsewhere. In every picture the divider that is nearest its own middle measured in plain distance rather than as a share of its bar, the longest bar, the shortest bar, the bar with the largest left-hand piece, the bar with the largest right-hand piece, the divider nearest the middle of the page and the bar in the topmost row each belong to a colour that is NOT the answer. Bars do not all start or end at the same place, and how high or low a bar's row sits means nothing. The grey bar with its own divider is a distractor and carries no information; ignore it completely, as you should the pale grey vertical rules and the grey frame. Which colour has the smallest split? Answer red, green, blue, orange or purple.

worlds.title: Scatter centroid target
worlds.question: Which color's point-cloud centroid is closest to the black crosshair? The centroid is the average horizontal and vertical position of all seven dots of that color. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Trapezoid auc leader
worlds.question: All panels use the same scale and the six checkpoints are equally spaced. Treat each colored line as straight between adjacent markers. Which curve has the largest trapezoidal area above its visible zero line? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior slanting rain
worlds.question: This image shows rain falling in the sky. Rain normally falls straight down, vertically, unless a strong wind slants it -- but report exactly what is visible. Is the rain in this image actually falling straight down (vertical)? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Solar blue planet count
worlds.question: How many blue planets are visible? Count each solid blue planet disk once; ignore orbit strokes, the sun, and labels. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Target band count
worlds.question: This image shows one round target painted on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. A band is one solid area of a single colour inside the target: the filled disc in the very middle is a band, and every complete ring of colour drawn around it is also a band. Neighbouring bands always use two different colours, and those two colours take turns from the middle outwards, so the same two colours reappear again and again no matter how many bands there are. The number of bands, the two colours used, the overall size of the target, the thickness of the individual bands and the position of the target on the page all change from image to image. Count the bands that are actually painted in this image, from the middle disc out to the outer edge of the target, and do not answer from how many rings a target normally has. How many bands does this target have? Answer with exactly one of the integers 3, 4, 5, 6, or 7.

worlds.title: Bias checker columns
worlds.question: How many columns of square cells are visible in the checkerboard? Count the spaces between vertical grid lines; do not count the border as a column.

worlds.title: Power ring gap prior conflict
worlds.question: On the large power-button-like symbol, which side has the gap in the colored outer ring: top, right, bottom, or left? Judge only the ring; ignore the dark center bar and small corner diamonds. Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Gradient flatten reveal
worlds.question: The image is a coarse lattice of bright and dark cells crossed by a strong left-to-right brightness ramp that hides a diagonal band. Flatten the image by subtracting the best-fit linear (planar) brightness gradient, so the ramp is removed. Which diagonal band remains, the rising band A or the falling band B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Polyphase quilt restore
worlds.question: Use the four colored corner marks to locate the even-sided grayscale square. Deinterleave its four parity streams into the four quadrants, apply a 7x7 edge-replicated mean, and choose the broad symbol: arch, bolt, fork, or crown.

worlds.title: Block majority coarsen reveal
worlds.question: The image shows one square lattice of 24 by 24 small cells inside a coloured frame. Heavier coloured rules divide the lattice into an 8 by 8 arrangement of blocks, and each block is 3 cells wide and 3 cells tall. Some small cells are filled dark. Every block contains either four or five dark cells out of its nine. Replace each block by a single square that is dark when at least five of that block's nine cells are dark and light otherwise. The 8 by 8 pattern of dark squares produced by this majority rule matches one of these symbols: plus, chevron, square, ladder, cross. Match by counting how many of the 64 squares disagree with each symbol and take the smallest count. Which symbol does it most closely match? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Bowed mesh rectify
worlds.question: Straighten the bowed magenta-dot mesh into an equal square grid, preserving row and column order from the yellow top-left, orange top-right, purple bottom-right, and green bottom-left corners. Read dark cells as black and pale cells as white. Which symbol appears: plus, X, diamond, or square?

worlds.title: Cable routed strip trace
worlds.question: Follow each colored cable from its round top socket to the plug above a scrambled tile column. Move that whole column to the cable's top-socket position, keeping it upright. Which trace appears: rising staircase, falling staircase, valley, or peak?

worlds.title: Vanishing point selection
worlds.question: On a white canvas, several straight colored line segments are drawn, and when you extend each line in your mind, every one of them passes through a single shared point. A set of colored marker dots is also shown: red, green, blue, and purple. Exactly one marker dot sits on that shared point where all the extended lines meet. Which color marker dot is it? Answer red, green, blue, or purple.

worlds.title: Biconnected dot constellation
worlds.question: For each color, imagine a link between two dot centers when their distance is no more than 1.35 times that color's median nearest-neighbor distance. Which color is the only one whose link graph stays connected after any one dot is removed? Ignore color, lane, dot count, dot size, and overall placement; choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Moire fringe direction
worlds.question: The picture is filled with two overlapping families of straight dark lines on a plain pale background. Inside one family every line is parallel to the others, the lines are evenly spaced and all have the same thickness; the two families differ in tilt and in spacing, and every line of both families is painted in the same dark colour, so no single line is marked out. Where lines of the two families fall on top of one another more pale background stays visible, and where they fall between one another the dark ink packs together, so the picture as a whole is crossed by broad pale and dark bands that are many times wider than the spacing of either family. Those broad bands are parallel to one another and are not drawn as lines anywhere: no painted line runs along them, and neither line family runs within 22 degrees of the band direction. The tilt of either line family, the spacing of the lines, their thickness, the amount of ink and the position of the pattern carry no information about the answer. The broad bands run within 7 degrees of one of four directions: horizontal (left to right), vertical (top to bottom), rising (from the bottom left towards the top right) or falling (from the top left towards the bottom right). In which direction do the broad bands run? Answer horizontal, vertical, rising or falling.

worlds.title: Proximity route parity
worlds.question: Treat each dot as its center. Connect two dots when their center-to-center distance is strictly shorter than the gray scale bar. The red and blue dots have a unique connecting route. Does that route contain an odd or even number of links? Answer odd or even.

worlds.title: Minimum tree junction
worlds.question: Imagine joining all dot centers into the one loop-free network with the smallest total straight-line length. Which colored dot has exactly three connections in that network? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Gap match search
worlds.question: A reference pair of stacked horizontal bars is shown in the top panel. Below it, the image is split into four quadrants, each containing one pair of stacked horizontal bars. The vertical gap is the empty space between the lower edge of the top bar and the upper edge of the bottom bar of a pair. Exactly one quadrant's bar pair has the same vertical gap as the reference pair. Which quadrant contains the bar pair whose gap matches the reference pair?

worlds.title: Network hub panel
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only five-node network with a hub node joined directly to all four other nodes? Each panel has exactly five identical nodes and five straight connection lines; a connection is the visible line between two nodes. Ignore node locations and labels, inspect all four panels, and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Mirror bounce panel
worlds.question: This image shows five square panels of the same size standing side by side in one row, each framed in grey and numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel holds exactly the same three things: an orange dot, a straight green beam that starts at that orange dot and stops where it meets a straight blue bar, and one red disk. The blue bar is a mirror. Within a scene the blue bars all have the same length, the green beams all have the same length and the red disks all have the same size, so length, size, colour, count and the amount of ink carry no information. The green beam does not pass through the mirror: at the point where it meets the blue bar it reflects, leaving on the other side of the point at the same angle to the bar as it arrived, and then travels on in a perfectly straight line. That reflected part of the path is never drawn, so it has to be worked out. Exactly one panel is arranged so that its reflected beam runs into that panel's red disk; in each of the other four panels the reflected beam passes the red disk and misses it by at least 10 pixels of clearance. The undrawn straight continuation of the beam through the mirror, without reflecting, misses the red disk in every panel, so ignoring the mirror never gives the answer. In every panel the beam meets the blue bar well inside the bar's two ends, and the red disk touches neither the beam nor the bar. Where the mirror sits, how it is tilted, which side the beam comes from and where the red disk lies are all free to vary from panel to panel. Which numbered panel is the one whose reflected beam runs into its red disk? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Paired aperture relation
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has the same clockwise angle from the LEFT ring's gap to the RIGHT ring's gap as the REFERENCE? Rotating both gaps together counts as the same; mirror reversal does not. A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Alternating color ring search
worlds.question: Each labeled panel has six dots in a ring, with three dots of each color. Which panel alternates color at every neighboring pair around the full ring, including the last-to-first pair? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State mirror register
worlds.question: A horizontal track of five slot boxes is shown, read left to right as slot 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. A red marker sits in one box and an orange ring surrounds that box; it marks the START slot. Four operator boxes are read left to right; each holds one colored disk. A green disk advances the tracked register one slot to the right (+1), a blue disk retreats it one slot to the left (-1), and a violet disk MIRRORs it: the current slot index is reflected about the track's central axis (slot 1 swaps with slot 5, slot 2 with slot 4, and slot 3 stays fixed). The register is never shown after its start. Replaying the operators in order from the ringed start, what is the FINAL slot of the tracked register? Answer exactly 'slot 1' through 'slot 5'.

worlds.title: State coverage race
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each labeled tile has one state from the STATE KEY. For each state, keep the set of labels that have appeared in that state so far. Which state is the first whose set contains A, B, C, and D? Answer LOW, MID, or HIGH.

worlds.title: Attribute overwrite match
worlds.question: The picture has two rows of cream panels. In the top row, the leftmost panel shows a token: a single coloured shape. Every other panel of the top row is a machine card, and the cards act on the token one at a time in order from left to right, as the arrow under the row shows. A card holding a grey shape sets the token's shape to that shape and leaves the token's colour unchanged. A card holding a wide, flat coloured bar sets the token's colour to that colour and leaves the token's shape unchanged. A later card of the same kind overwrites an earlier one, and a register that no card ever writes keeps the value drawn in the leftmost panel. The bottom row has four panels, numbered one to four from left to right, each holding one coloured shape. Exactly one of those four objects has both the shape and the colour that the token has after every card has acted. The token's final state is not drawn anywhere in the top row. Which of the four bottom panels holds that object? Answer with one word: one, two, three or four.

worlds.title: Stable partition replay
worlds.question: The six tokens start in the shown left-to-right order, and the magenta ring marks one token. Read the five command cards from left to right. On each card, move every token matching the card's color to the arrow's edge. Matching tokens keep their relative order, and all other tokens keep their relative order. Which numbered slot contains the ringed token at the end? Answer 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Synchronous neighbor lamps
worlds.question: Seven lamps start as shown (filled = ON, ring = OFF), and the red triangle marks the lamp to track. Each orange ROUND card performs one update. In each round, every lamp becomes ON exactly when one of its immediate neighbors was ON at the start of that round (one neighbor ON and the other OFF); otherwise it becomes OFF. All seven lamps update simultaneously. A missing neighbor beyond either end counts as OFF. After all ROUND cards, is the marked lamp ON or OFF? Answer ON or OFF.

worlds.title: Independent cycles
worlds.question: Ignoring the outside white background, look only at white pockets that are fully enclosed rings of the node-and-link network (each is a separate closed loop with no path out to the picture edge and no opening). How many enclosed loops does the network form? Answer with exactly 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Outer face junction
worlds.question: Which colored junction is enclosed by the network? Treat every dark link and every uncolored junction as an impassable barrier. A colored junction is enclosed when no blank four-neighbor route from a blank region touching it reaches the canvas edge without crossing a barrier. Exactly one of red, green, and blue is enclosed; answer its color and ignore the canvas border.

worlds.title: Cut curve split pick
worlds.question: The picture shows a grey metal plate lying on white paper. Two white holes are punched right through the plate, so the plate has an outer rim and two hole rims. Three coloured bands are painted across the plate - one red, one green and one blue. Each band is a single unbroken strip that starts on a rim, wanders across the grey and ends on a rim; the bands never touch each other, and away from its two ends a band never touches any rim. Now imagine cutting the plate with scissors along ONE of the coloured bands, all the way from one end of that band to the other, and nowhere else: the grey under that band is removed, and the other two bands are only paint and are not cut along. Two bits of grey belong to the same piece when grey still joins them after the cut. Exactly one of the three bands falls the plate into two separate pieces; cutting along either of the other two leaves the plate in one single piece. Which band falls the plate into two pieces - red, green or blue?

worlds.title: Cycle vertex residue panel
worlds.question: Gray links meet only at cyan round stations; a crossing without a station is not a connection. A station belongs to a loop if it lies on any closed route. Imagine removing every station that belongs to a loop and every link touching those stations. Which panel leaves exactly two nonempty connected groups of stations? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Marked link detour two
worlds.question: If only the orange link is removed, is the new shortest route from the green junction to the purple junction exactly two links longer than the shortest route now? If no route remains, answer no. Links meet only at circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route component count
worlds.question: The drawing is made of some separate blue routes that never touch each other. How many separate (unconnected) blue routes are drawn? Answer with the number only (1, 2, or 3).

worlds.title: Junction branch turn choice
worlds.question: Starting at the green source, follow the solid dark route to the purple-ringed fork. Which labeled terminal, A or B, is attached to the branch that makes the smaller absolute turn from the incoming route? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Wire underpass count
worlds.question: Each gray line in this picture is one straight wire running between two ports on the ring. Where two wires cross, one of them is drawn with a short break on either side of the other wire: the wire with the breaks passes UNDERNEATH, and the unbroken wire passes OVER it. Exactly one port is green, and exactly one wire starts there. Follow the wire that starts at the green port all the way to its other port. How many times does that wire pass underneath another wire? Answer with a single number: 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Route toll sum terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green node, follow the unique dark-line route to each colored terminal. Each cyan diamond beside a link adds one toll to every route using that link. Which terminal has a total toll of exactly 5: orange, purple, or blue?

worlds.title: Relay trace terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green START port, follow the black traces through every panel. At an X crossing, continue straight on the same line; do not turn. Which colored terminal is reached? Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Beacon spacing chain correspondence
worlds.question: One continuous navy route runs through fields R, A, and B. Each field has six identical gold checkpoint flags attached to the route. Read R from left to right and record its five horizontal gaps between successive flag centers. Read each candidate from right to left. Which candidate has exactly the same five-gap rhythm as R? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Switchlane descent bind
worlds.question: The picture shows one cream board carrying a single connected slate-grey ladder. The ladder has five tall thin RAILS standing side by side across the whole board, and a handful of short horizontal SWITCHES, each of which joins one rail to the rail immediately next to it at some height. No two switches sit at the same height. A solid black triangle points down at the top of exactly one rail: that is where the descent starts. Now walk down. You always move downwards along the rail you are on and you may never move upwards or skip past anything: every time you reach a switch that touches your current rail you MUST cross it to the neighbouring rail, and then keep going down that rail. Switches therefore act one after another in order of height, from the highest to the lowest, and a switch that touches neither of your current positions is simply never used. A square coloured BEAD is parked at the foot of each of the five rails; the five beads have five different colours out of red, orange, green, teal, blue and purple. The bead at the foot of the rail where the descent finishes is the answer. The rail you finish on is usually not the rail you started on, so the bead under the black triangle is not the answer unless the crossings bring you back to that rail, and the descent always wanders as far as both the leftmost and the rightmost rail, so no single side of the board settles it. The small scattered coloured squares away from the ladder are decoration and mean nothing. Bead colours are shuffled independently of the route, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies the answer on its own, and every switch in the picture must be accounted for at its own height rather than counted or averaged. Follow the descent to its end. What is the colour of the bead at the foot of the finishing rail? Answer red, orange, green, teal, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Turn trace correspondence
worlds.question: The gold tag starts the reference section. Follow its four straight steps through the three pale bend pegs. For each red, green, and blue tag, follow the next four steps likewise. A candidate matches only if one rigid rotation of the whole section, without reflection or reordering, makes all four steps and bends coincide with the reference. Which candidate tag color marks the match? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Zipper merge correspondence
worlds.question: Read the four tiles in the far-left source strip A and the four tiles in the far-right source strip B from left to right. ZIP them by alternating A1, B1, A2, B2, A3, B3, A4, B4. Exactly one lower strip shows that eight-tile sequence. Which color frames it? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Endtoend reach duel
worlds.question: A pale instrument sheet carries grey ticks and several coloured or grey marks, and exactly three solid pure-black horizontal bars that sit close together in one small group. Ignore every mark that is not pure black. The three black bars have different thicknesses and are not aligned with one another, so measure each black bar only by its own length from its left end to its right end and ignore its thickness, its height on the sheet and where it starts. Is the single longest black bar longer than the other two black bars laid end to end in one straight line? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route peak half
worlds.question: Follow the cyan route from the coral start dot to the blue finish dot. Is the route's highest point reached before or after halfway along the route's visible length? Answer before or after.

worlds.title: Microprofile extrema order
worlds.question: Following the teal mini-profile from left to right, which flat extreme occurs first: its highest plateau (PEAK) or its lowest plateau (TROUGH)? Answer PEAK or TROUGH.

worlds.title: Capital n stroke sequence
worlds.question: On the CAPITAL N practice card, follow the single blue stroke from the red START dot. Are its three long straight runs in this order: up, down-right, up? Answer yes or no from the visible stroke.

worlds.title: Red cable terminal
worlds.question: Follow the single red cable from the plug on the left across the whole image. Which battery terminal does it visibly touch—the green terminal marked + or the blue terminal marked −? Answer plus or minus.

worlds.title: Corner notch rectify reveal
worlds.question: This picture contains four small square tiles, arranged as the four corners of one wide two-by-two block with plenty of empty background between them. Every tile has a solid dark border enclosing a four-by-four grid of sixteen equal square cells, and each cell is either dark (the same tone as the border) or pale (the same tone as the tile's background). Exactly one corner of each tile's border is broken by a pale square notch. Carry out this operation. First turn each tile in place, by a quarter turn at a time, until that tile's notched corner is its top-left corner; the tile's sixteen cells turn with it. Leave each tile in its own corner of the two-by-two block: the tile at the top left of the block stays top left, and so on. Then read the four turned tiles together as one eight-by-eight grid, with each turned tile supplying the four-by-four quadrant that matches its place in the block. The dark cells of that eight-by-eight grid form exactly one symbol: 'plus' is a thick upright cross of two central rows crossing two central columns, 'box' is a hollow square ring one cell in from the outer edge, 'hourglass' is a full top bar and a full bottom bar joined by a narrow waist of two crossing diagonals, and 'diamond' is a tilted outline square through the edge midpoints with its centre filled. Every tile shows exactly five dark cells whichever symbol is present, so no tile and no count of dark cells reveals the symbol on its own, and the symbol is not visible anywhere until all four tiles have been turned. Which symbol do the dark cells form? Answer with exactly one of: plus, box, hourglass, diamond.

worlds.title: Blurred quilt reveal
worlds.question: Inside the violet frame, blur the tiny checker texture until individual checks disappear. Which symbol remains: X, plus, diamond, or ring?

worlds.title: Paired mask intersection
worlds.question: Rotate each of the two nearby square grids until its small corner block is at the upper left. Superimpose the grids and keep only cells filled in both. Which symbol requires the fewest cell changes to match the result: diamond, plus, or X? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Cavity midprofile mode
worlds.question: The colored plaque contains one connected pale opening. From left to right, is the opening's vertical width narrowest near the middle or widest near the middle? Answer waist or belly.

worlds.title: Broad petal pairing
worlds.question: The single colored seal contains one pale rosette with four petals: two broad and two narrow. Around the center, are the two broad petals adjacent or opposite? Answer adjacent or opposite.

worlds.title: Thread terminal search
worlds.question: Begin at the cyan start bead and follow the connected black thread without jumping a gap. Which colored terminal bead does it touch? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Equal stride checkpoint search
worlds.question: Starting at the gold disk, follow the single dark route to the gray disk. Which colored checkpoint is the only one where the two straight route sections meeting there have exactly the same length, measured center to center? Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: State ribbon replay
worlds.question: Starting with the ringed token, follow the numbered arrows from left to right. An up arrow moves one lane upward, a down arrow moves one lane downward, a flat arrow leaves the token in place, and moving past an edge wraps to the opposite lane. Which labeled lane contains the token after the last arrow?

worlds.title: Tessera permute relay
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there are exactly two panels drawn with heavy black frames, standing apart from one another, and every pale grey mark outside those two frames is inert decoration that means nothing. The left panel is the rule table. Its top row holds three dot glyphs, one in each of its three right-hand columns; a dot glyph is one, two or three small black dots, and only the number of dots matters, never their arrangement. Underneath that top row the table has four rows. Each row starts, in its leftmost cell, with a coloured disc, and that disc is the row's own colour; the four rows carry four different colours. The other three cells of a row hold coloured discs as well, one under each dot glyph. The table is used as a lookup: if the colour you are holding is the colour that starts a row, and the glyph you are applying has n dots, then the colour you are holding is replaced by the disc that sits in that row in the column whose top-row glyph also has n dots. The right panel is the program. At the top of it, on its own and encircled by a heavy black ring, sits a single coloured disc: that is the colour you start out holding. Below the ring, separated by thin black lines, are four cells stacked one above another, and each of them holds one dot glyph. Those four glyphs are applied one after another, starting with the glyph in the top cell and working downwards, each one replacing the colour you hold by the colour the table looks up for it. The two panels may sit at slightly different places from picture to picture, and the four colours in play are always red, amber, green and blue. After all four glyphs of the program have been applied, which colour are you holding? Answer with one of red, amber, green or blue.

worlds.title: Seal gate patch
