worlds.question: The gold-rimmed START tile shows the lamp (filled means ON; hollow means OFF). Read the other five tiles in row order, left to right then top to bottom. A double-bar tile flips the lamp only while the gate is open. A solid seal tile closes the gate permanently. A dot tile waits. Is the lamp ON after every tile? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Relay pair register
worlds.question: The two lamps at START show a register from left to right: a dark lamp is on and a white lamp is off. Follow the cord from left to right. At each triangle, flip only the left lamp. At each square, set the right lamp equal to the left lamp. After all four relay beads, which lamps are on?

worlds.title: Edge disjoint terminals
worlds.question: Do the orange and blue terminals have two routes that share no gray track segment? Routes may meet at black junctions, and gray tracks meet only at visible junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cut patch sheet
worlds.question: Treat every teal pixel as equal weight and ignore the pale gray decorations. Does the teal sheet's center of area—the average horizontal and vertical position of all its teal pixels—fall inside its enclosed white pocket? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Gap bridge flag
worlds.question: The picture shows small dark gray squares of one common size (the stones), one larger dark green square (the pad), and three coloured squares: an orange flag, a purple flag and a blue flag. No two squares touch. Two squares are linked when the clear white gap between them is narrower than one stone is wide, and they are not linked when that gap is at least as wide as a stone. Linking chains: the pad reaches a square if you can get from the pad to it through a run of linked squares, hopping only over gaps narrower than a stone. Exactly one of the three flags is cut off from the pad: the run of stones leading to that flag is interrupted by a single gap at least as wide as a stone, so no hopping route reaches it. The other two flags are reachable. Stone count, run length, how far a flag sits from the pad and the direction of a run say nothing about the answer, and stones that are linked to nothing are still ordinary stones. Which flag is cut off from the green pad? Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Paired link parity
worlds.question: Trace both separate navy links between their colored endpoint dots. Is the number of links joining two dots of the same color odd or even? Answer odd or even.

worlds.title: Rail crossing count
worlds.question: Follow the navy centerline between the blue and orange rings. Count each passage through the straight gold rail that takes the centerline from one side to the other. Are there two crossings or four? Answer two or four.

worlds.title: Intervention rule flip
worlds.question: The picture shows two colour rules and a START disc. The ACTUAL RULE legend pairs every source colour with the target colour it turns into under that rule; the colour the ACTUAL RULE would give for the START disc is shown in the NOW disc. The IF RULE is a copy of the ACTUAL RULE in which exactly one entry is changed: the row for the START colour now points at a different target colour. This is a counterfactual: suppose the IF RULE, not the ACTUAL RULE, had produced the outcome for the same START colour. Which colour would the IF RULE have given for the START disc? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Crossview transform check
worlds.question: Match each SOURCE token to its key in both shuffled rows. ACTION gives the operation and RESULT gives its target token. Apply the matched ACTION to the SOURCE token, then select the SOURCE card whose transformed token exactly matches its matched RESULT token. Red CW means a clockwise quarter-turn; green LR means a left-right mirror; purple UD means a top-bottom mirror. Answer card-1, card-2, card-3, card-4, or card-5.

worlds.title: Pivotal vote counterfactual
worlds.question: Bottom disks are black (filled) or white (hollow). Each hollow middle circle takes the majority color of the three disks linked to it, and the hollow top circle takes the majority color of the five middle circles. Three bottom disks are ringed. Flipping exactly one of those three disks to its other color, changing nothing else, would change the top circle's color. Which ring marks that disk? Answer amber, teal, or violet.

worlds.title: Transferred socket clamp
worlds.question: A clamp forces only the socket it covers to the shown CLAMP BIT; other uses of that source are unchanged. Move the clamp from the amber NOW socket to the violet NEXT socket, then recompute every gate. Exactly one displayed current output changes. Which one: output-A, output-B, output-C, or output-D?

worlds.title: Reciprocal route deadline
worlds.question: The six colors have different whole-number speeds from 1 to 9. Every CLUE says its LEFT pair has greater combined speed than its RIGHT pair. A ROUTE performs two 1-unit jobs in sequence, so its time is 1/first speed + 1/second speed. Which route must take less than 3/4 time unit for every speed assignment fitting all clues? Answer route-1, route-2, route-3, or route-4.

worlds.title: Disk spacing correspondence
worlds.question: The gray object at the top is a pair of two gray disks separated by a specific center-to-center distance. Below it are three colored objects A, B, C: one is red, one green, one blue, and each is a pair of two same-colored disks separated by a different center-to-center distance. Which colored object has the two disks of its pair separated by exactly the same center-to-center distance as the gray pair? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Colored divider side correspondence
worlds.question: The image has a REFERENCE panel and candidates A and B. Each panel contains six uniquely colored disks and one vertical divider. A disk is on the LEFT or RIGHT side according to which side of the divider its center occupies. Which candidate has exactly the same color-to-side assignment as the REFERENCE? A is the middle panel and B is the right panel. Ignore panel location, divider position, disk size, and line thickness. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Constellation landmark transfer
worlds.question: The upper panel shows four colored dots. The lower panel shows the same four dots after the whole group was rotated, uniformly rescaled, and moved; the group was never mirrored and the dots keep their relative arrangement. In the lower panel every dot is gray and exactly one dot is circled in black. Which color is that circled dot in the upper panel? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Folded tile pairs
worlds.question: Fold the six-tile strip at the dashed center so positions 1 and 6, 2 and 5, and 3 and 4 meet. In each resulting pair, order does not matter, and the three pair rows may be rearranged. Which colored border contains exactly the three resulting pairs? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Braided cable correspondence
worlds.question: The REFERENCE plug face is marked in magenta. In the CABLE BANK, first find the plug with the identical 3x3 black-square pattern; patterns are not rotated or reflected. Then trace its cable downward through all five bands. At an X, continue straight diagonally across the white bridge gap—never turn onto the crossing cable. Which colored socket does it reach: red, green, blue, or orange?

worlds.title: Taller than reference
worlds.question: Three colored vertical bars (red, blue, green) and one gray reference bar stand on a black baseline. Count how many of the colored bars are TALLER than the gray reference bar, where a colored bar counts if the top of that bar is above the top of the gray bar. Answer with only the number: 0, 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Interval center offset
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Each panel shows a horizontal interval with two endpoints and one sample marker strictly inside it. Divide the marker's absolute distance from that interval's midpoint by that interval's width. Which panel has the larger normalized midpoint offset? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Window overlap total
worlds.question: The picture shows two shaded grey columns that run from the top edge to the bottom edge; these two columns are the WINDOWS. Five horizontal bars lie across the picture: one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one black. The black bar is a distractor and carries no information; ignore it completely. For each coloured bar, its SCORE is the total horizontal length of that bar that lies inside the windows, that is, the length of its part inside the left window plus the length of its part inside the right window. The part of a bar that lies outside both windows counts for nothing. Only horizontal extent counts: a bar's thickness, how high or low it sits, and the top-to-bottom order of the bars carry no information, and no bar starts or ends at a window edge. The longest bar need not be the answer, and neither need the bar with the most of itself inside a single window, because a bar can also score by taking a share of both windows. Which coloured bar has the greatest score? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Paired doubling gap
worlds.question: Rows A-D run from top to bottom on one linear ruler. For each row, measure both marker values from the magenta zero line. Which row makes the orange diamond closest to twice the blue circle? Minimize |orange - 2 x blue|.

worlds.title: Pearson panel leader
worlds.question: Panels A–D are in reading order. Which panel has the largest Pearson correlation coefficient between the plotted x- and y-coordinates? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior checker columns
worlds.question: This is a checkerboard. An ordinary chessboard is 8 squares by 8 squares, so it normally has 8 columns, but report exactly what is drawn here. Count how many columns of squares the checkerboard has and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Clock face time reading
worlds.question: What time is shown on the analog clock face? Read the short hand as the hour and the long hand as minutes at the nearest quarter-hour; answer in H:MM format.

worlds.title: Envelope stamp corner
worlds.question: This image shows one envelope lying at some angle on a page. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks just inside it are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The envelope is the large four-sided patch of paper. The big triangle printed on it is the envelope's flap, and the flap's straight base always runs along the envelope's own top edge, with the flap's point aimed at the middle of the envelope, however the envelope has been turned on the page. The small solid square patch is the stamp. The thin parallel strokes are address lines and never mark the answer. Turn the envelope in your mind, without flipping it over, until its flap base is at the top and its opposite edge is at the bottom; left and right mean your left and right in that upright view, so they are not the left and right of the page. The stamp belongs to the corner that contains the centre of the stamp. The colours, the size and shape of the envelope, where it sits on the page, the angle it is turned through, the size of the stamp and the number and placement of the address lines all change from image to image, and the stamp need not be placed where a stamp is normally placed. Read only what is painted in this image and do not answer from where stamps usually go. In which corner of the envelope is the stamp? Answer with exactly one of: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right.

worlds.title: Bias solar blue planets
worlds.question: How many blue planets are visible in the solar-system diagram? Count each separate blue circular planet once; ignore the yellow Sun and thin gray orbit rings. Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Clock numeral winding conflict
worlds.question: On the visible dial, starting at 12 and taking the shorter arc to 3, which direction do the numerals advance: clockwise or counterclockwise?

worlds.title: Salt pepper median reveal
worlds.question: The image is dense salt-and-pepper black-and-white speckle that hides a diagonal band. Apply a median (majority-vote) filter with a neighborhood so the outlier speckle is removed and only the wide band remains. Which diagonal band is revealed, the rising band A or the falling band B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Rectified quadrilateral emblem
worlds.question: First identify the four colored corner marks. Projectively rectify the quadrilateral they enclose into a square as if viewed straight on; do not use the fine checkerboard as evidence. Select the broad emblem: diamond, hourglass, chevron, or crown.

worlds.title: Annulus unwrap reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one flat ring. The ring is cut into 5 concentric bands and into 7 equal wedge-shaped sectors, so it holds 35 curved cells; each cell is either dark or light. A small coloured tab is printed just outside the ring, next to exactly one sector. Rebuild the ring as a flat rectangle of 5 rows and 7 columns: the innermost band becomes the top row and the outermost band becomes the bottom row, the sector touched by the tab becomes the leftmost column, and the remaining columns follow that sector clockwise around the ring. Copy each cell's dark or light state into its new place. The dark cells of the rebuilt rectangle form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: cross, diamond, flag, goalpost, zigzag. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Run bar decompression
worlds.question: In each cyan lane, read the bars from left to right. A dark bar means black cells and a pale bar means white cells; the bar height in small grid steps is that run's length. Expand the runs into one row per lane, then stack the lanes from top to bottom. Which symbol appears: zigzag, key, anchor, or bell?

worlds.title: Calibrated motion blur symbol
worlds.question: Inside the cyan frame, slide a horizontal window exactly as wide as the gold bar from left to right. Replace each full window with its average and ignore the narrow incomplete edge windows. Which large symbol appears: up arrow, right arrow, down arrow, or left arrow? Keep the image orientation unchanged.

worlds.title: Circumcenter marker selection
worlds.question: On a white canvas, three dots mark the three corners of a triangle (the three dots are the triangle's vertices). The circumcenter of a triangle is the single point that is equally distant from all three corner dots -- the center of the one circle that passes through all three corners. A set of colored marker dots is also shown: red, green, blue, and purple. Exactly one marker dot sits on that circumcenter, equally distant from all three corners. Which color marker dot is it? Answer red, green, blue, or purple.

worlds.title: Mirror axis constellation
worlds.question: Choose the color of the one line that bisects the gray constellation with mirror symmetry; judge all gray dots, not local line appearance.

worlds.title: Spiral chain handedness
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain background with a number of dark round blobs and nothing else. Exactly one blob, the hub, is much larger than the others; all the remaining blobs are dots of one and the same size. Every dot sits at a different distance from the hub, so the dots can be put in one order by walking outward from the hub, from the nearest dot to the farthest dot. Following that outward order, the direction from the hub to the dot keeps turning the same way around the hub, by a similar amount at every step and always by less than a quarter turn, so the dots trace a single chain that winds outward around the hub. Turning as the hands of a clock printed on this picture would turn counts as clockwise. The number of dots, the size of the blobs, the position of the hub in the frame, the direction in which the chain starts, the amount of dark ink and how far apart the dots are all carry no information about the answer. Walking outward from the hub, which way does the chain of dots wind? Answer clockwise or counter-clockwise.

worlds.title: Hull area bisector
worlds.question: Imagine the tightest convex rubber band around all black dot centers and uniformly fill its interior. Which colored dashed line divides that filled region into two equal areas: orange or blue? Answer orange or blue.

worlds.title: Widest empty moat
worlds.question: Four colored rings mark candidate centers. For each ring, its empty-moat radius is the straight-line distance from the ring's center to the nearest dark-dot center. Which ring has the largest empty-moat radius? Ring size does not count. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Bar circle overlap search
worlds.question: The image is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right) by two light-gray crossed divider lines. Inside each quadrant there is one dark filled circle and one dark bar (a thick straight line). In exactly one quadrant the circle and the bar overlap each other, so the two dark shapes touch and merge into a single connected blob. In the other three quadrants the circle sits clearly away from the bar with a visible gap between them. Which quadrant contains the only pair in which the circle and the bar overlap each other? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Inversion parity panel search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has an even number of vertical-order inversions? In each panel, read the four identical dots from left to right, rank their heights from top (1) to bottom (4), and count pairs whose left dot is lower than the right dot. Exactly one panel has an even count; answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Ring depth panel
worlds.question: This image shows five square panels of the same size standing side by side in one row, each framed in grey and numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel holds exactly two rings, drawn as thin closed circular outlines, and exactly one small solid black dot. Within a scene all ten rings use the same two sizes, so ring size, ring colour and the amount of ink carry no information. The two rings of a panel never touch and never cross: they are either nested, with the smaller ring lying completely inside the larger one, or set apart side by side with a clear gap between them. A dot is enclosed by a ring when it lies inside that ring's closed outline. Exactly one panel in the image holds a dot that is enclosed by both of its rings at once, which happens only when the rings are nested and the dot lies inside the smaller of them. In each of the other four panels the dot is enclosed by exactly one of the two rings or by neither of them, and in every panel the edge of the dot clears every ring outline by at least 6 pixels, so no dot ever sits on a ring. Whether a panel's rings are nested or set apart, which ring the dot of a losing panel sits in, and where the pair sits inside its panel are all free to vary. Which numbered panel holds the dot that is enclosed by both of its rings? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Containment hierarchy search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has exactly the same circle-within-circle relationships as the REFERENCE? Colors identify circles; positions and sizes do not need to match. A circle is within another only when its entire outline lies inside the other circle.

worlds.title: Triangle bar search
worlds.question: Which labeled rack has three bars whose visible lengths could form a nondegenerate triangle? The longest bar must be shorter than the other two combined. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State fifo queue
worlds.question: A horizontal timeline of five panels reads left to right. The leftmost panel is the START queue: a row of colored discs (red, green, blue, or orange), read left to right, with the FRONT of the queue at the very left. The four panels to the right are OPERATOR panels, read left to right in order. An operator panel showing a colored disc means ENQUEUE: that disc's color is appended to the BACK (right end) of the queue. An operator panel showing only a dark left-pointing arrow means DEQUEUE: the FRONT (leftmost) disc is removed and every remaining disc shifts left, so a new disc becomes the front. The queue is never drawn again; replay the operators from the START queue. What color is at the FRONT of the final queue? Answer 'red', 'green', 'blue', 'orange', or 'empty'.

worlds.title: State change parity
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each labeled tile shows LOW, MID, or HIGH using the STATE KEY. Count a change whenever a label's state differs between adjacent panels. Which label changes state an odd number of times? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Egocentric turn walk
worlds.question: The picture shows a board of 6 by 6 square cells drawn in grey. Five of the cells hold a coloured pad: one red, one blue, one purple, one teal and one yellow, each colour used once. A black triangle stands in another cell: that is the robot, and the robot stands in the cell whose square contains the triangle. The robot faces the way its apex, the sharp corner opposite its flat back edge, points; that facing is whichever of up, right, down or left the apex points closest to, where up means towards the top edge of the board, down towards the bottom edge, left towards the left edge and right towards the right edge. Below the board is a row of cream cards, carried out one at a time in order from left to right, as the grey arrow beneath the row shows. A card carrying a grey arrow and some black dots is a drive card: the robot moves straight ahead, in the direction it is facing at that moment, one cell for each black dot on that card, and its facing does not change. A card carrying a green bent arrow turns the robot a quarter turn to its own left, and a card carrying an orange bent arrow turns it a quarter turn to its own right; a turn card never moves the robot. The turns are made from the robot's point of view, so a turn card changes the direction every later drive card sends it: after a green card a robot that faced up faces left, and after an orange card a robot that faced up faces right. The grey arrow on a drive card points up on the card only to mark it as a drive card; it does not say which way the robot moves. No card ever takes the robot off the board, pads do not block or divert it, and it may pass over pads on the way. The robot is drawn only once, in its starting cell and starting facing: no later position or facing of the robot is drawn anywhere. After every card has been carried out, the robot stands on one of the five coloured pads. After every card has been carried out in order, which coloured pad is the robot standing on? Answer with one word: red, blue, purple, teal or yellow.

worlds.title: Stack transfer replay
worlds.question: The three stacks start as shown, with each top at the top. Read the five MOVE cards from left to right. Each card moves the top token from its left stack onto its right stack; if the left stack is empty, nothing happens. Which numbered token is on top of the stack marked QUERY at the end? A token's number is its black-dot count. Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Capacity pour replay
worlds.question: Three pip-labeled vessels each hold at most four units and start at the shown levels. Read the seven arrow cards from left to right. On each card, pour from the left vessel into the right vessel until either the left vessel is empty or the right vessel is full. Which level does the red-ringed vessel have at the end? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Bridge cut count
worlds.question: The image shows a network of colored circular nodes connected by thick black links. A black link is called a bridge if removing that one link would break the network into two or more separate parts (so its two endpoint nodes could no longer reach each other using the remaining links). How many of the black links are bridges? Answer with exactly one whole number.

worlds.title: Boundary separator selection
worlds.question: Exactly one colored wall separates the white interior of its black frame into two four-neighbor connected regions. Which wall color is it? Ignore the black frames and answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Loop free panel pick
worlds.question: Three square plates are drawn side by side on white paper: a left plate, a centre plate and a right plate. Each plate is solid black except for the white corridors cut into it, and every plate is surrounded by a closed black rim. Inside one plate you may walk anywhere along the white corridors, but you may never step on black. A plate CONTAINS A ROUND TRIP when you can start somewhere in its white corridors, walk, and come back to your starting point without ever turning around and without walking back along any stretch of corridor you have already used; otherwise the plate is LOOP FREE. Short black spurs stick out from the walls into some corridors; a spur that stops short of the opposite wall leaves a gap you may walk through. Exactly one of the three plates is loop free, and the three plates carry exactly the same amount of black ink. Which plate is the loop-free one - left, centre or right?

worlds.title: Station cut vertex
worlds.question: Routes follow the thick gray links through round stations. Imagine removing one colored station and every link touching it. Which removal leaves no route between the two black square terminals? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Pair link resilience
worlds.question: The network has 11 colored circular junctions and 13 dark links. Would the green and purple junctions remain connected no matter which one dark link is removed? Remove exactly one entire link; links meet only at visible circles. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Path fold count
worlds.question: A single winding blue path is drawn. It doubles back on itself several times, making sharp U-turn folds where the stroke reverses direction. How many U-turn folds does the blue path make? Answer 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Ladder descent terminal
worlds.question: This picture is a ladder puzzle drawn in gray. There are four long vertical rails. Each short horizontal bar is a rung, and every rung joins exactly two rails that stand next to each other. A green dot sits on top of one rail, and one coloured square sits under each of the four rails: one blue, one orange, one purple and one red. Start at the green dot and move down the rail below it. Whenever you arrive at an end of a rung you must cross that rung to the rail at its other end, and then keep moving down that rail. You may never move upwards and you may never skip a rung you arrive at, so the rungs are taken in top-to-bottom order. Stop when you reach the bottom of a rail. Which coloured square do you stop at? Answer blue, orange, purple, or red.

worlds.title: Color keyed junction terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green ring and follow the links. At each gray junction, continue along the outgoing colored link that matches the small colored key inside that junction; never reverse along the link just used. Which colored square do you reach: orange, purple, blue, or red?

worlds.title: Double gate trace
worlds.question: Follow the continuous black route from the green START disk to the purple FINISH disk. Which colored gate ring does that route cross exactly twice? The other black routes are distractors. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Foldnet face opposite bind
worlds.question: The picture is a cream board littered with small decorative squares that mean nothing. Lying on the board are several large SQUARE TILES, all of exactly the same size and all far bigger than any decorative square. Exactly six of these large tiles are joined edge to edge, with no gap between them, into one single connected piece: that piece is the NET. Every other large tile is a LOOSE TILE: it stands clear of the net and clear of every other loose tile, with visible cream board all round it, and loose tiles mean nothing. The six squares of the net all have different colours, one each of red, orange, yellow, green, blue and purple, and exactly one of them carries a white DOT at its centre; loose tiles and decorative squares may repeat any of those colours and never carry a dot. Fold the net along the shared edges of its six squares so that it closes up into a cube, each square becoming one face of that cube. In the folded cube the dotted face lies directly opposite exactly one other face, the face it never touches: that face is the OPPOSITE FACE. Its colour is the answer. Every scene is sampled so that cheap reading fails: the opposite face is never a square that touches the dotted square along an edge on the board, no square of the net lies two straight steps away from the dotted square along a row or a column, the dotted square touches at most two other squares of the net, and the opposite face is never the single square lying farthest from the dotted square in board steps. Tile size, tile count, the six net colours and the total amount of ink are the same whatever the answer is, and the net can sit anywhere on the board, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies the answer on its own. Fold the net into a cube and find the face opposite the dotted face. What is its colour? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Halfturn seam splice
worlds.question: The gold-marked trace is complete. The broken trace below must be the same shape after a half-turn (180 degrees), with no reflection or resizing. Which colored proposed splice supplies the missing middle so every step continues? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Reverse registry correspondence
worlds.question: The gray registry pairs each dark source glyph on the left with a green target glyph on the right. Reverse every pairing by swapping its two ends; row order does not matter. Which colored registry contains exactly the three reversed pairings? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Excursion area balance
worlds.question: A single thin dark trace crosses this sheet from its left end to its right end, and one straight blue reference line runs the whole width of the sheet. The trace has exactly one height at each horizontal position, so it can be followed end to end. Between its two ends the trace makes several separate bulges: each bulge leaves the blue line, swells to one side of it, and comes back to it, and the bulges are spread all the way across the sheet. For every bulge consider the area of paper trapped between the trace and the blue line. Add up the trapped areas of all bulges lying above the blue line, and separately add up the trapped areas of all bulges lying below it. Every bulge counts towards its own side, however wide or however tall it is, and a wide shallow bulge can trap more paper than a narrow deep one. The pale grey edge ticks and the pale coloured decoration are not part of the trace and carry no information. Which side traps more paper in total: above the blue line, or below it? Answer with the single word above or below.

worlds.title: Trimmed row span
worlds.question: Ignore the leftmost and rightmost dot in each row. Which row has the wider horizontal span between its remaining leftmost and rightmost dots? Answer top or bottom.

worlds.title: Panel ratio comparison
worlds.question: In each framed panel, divide the taller colored bar's height by the shorter colored bar's height. Which panel has the larger tall-to-short ratio? Answer LEFT or RIGHT.

worlds.title: Paperclip enclosure count
worlds.question: How many separate white pockets are fully enclosed by the single dark paperclip stroke? Count only white regions completely surrounded by the stroke.

worlds.title: Pretzel enclosed holes
worlds.question: How many white regions are completely enclosed by the single brown pretzel rope? Count only white regions not connected to the outer white background. Answer 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Swatch key sieve reveal
worlds.question: Exactly two blocks in this picture are drawn with a solid black border; every other block or mark is drawn in colour and is decoration. The black-bordered square block is the panel: it is divided into a 5 by 5 grid of 25 equal square cells, and each cell is filled with one flat gray taken from a set of exactly four different grays. The other black-bordered block is the key: it shows two flat gray swatches side by side or one above the other, and each swatch gray is one of the four grays used in the panel. Carry out this operation: mark every panel cell whose gray matches either of the two swatch grays in the key, and leave every other panel cell unmarked. The order of the two swatches does not matter. The marked cells form exactly one symbol on the 5 by 5 grid: 'ring' is the eight cells of the 3 by 3 centre block without its middle cell, 'cross' is the four corner cells together with the four cells diagonally inside them, 'arrow' is a centre column of three cells rising into a three-cell bar with one cell above its middle and one cell out at each side below it, and 'stair' is an eight-cell staircase of horizontal pairs stepping down from the top-left corner to the bottom right. Every symbol marks exactly 8 of the 25 cells. The panel shows two of these symbols superposed and does not by itself say which one is marked; only the key's two grays decide that. Which symbol do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: arrow, cross, ring, stair.

worlds.title: Perspective residual diptych
worlds.question: View both marked trapezoids front-on. For each matching square, mark it dark when the two shades differ and light when they match. Which symbol appears: X, plus, diamond, or U?

worlds.title: Midline ribbon reveal
worlds.question: Starting at the red ring and reading toward the gold triangle, for every image column through the single dark ribbon outline, mark the point halfway between its upper and lower dark edges. Connect those halfway points in order without smoothing, then ignore overall position and tilt. Which path appears: arch, cup, or wave? An arch has a high middle and low ends; a cup has a low middle and high ends; a wave has one low and one high lobe. Answer ambiguous if the two best matches tie.

worlds.title: Channel cycle seal
worlds.question: Inside the small blue seal, the cream channel is one connected thick corridor with four rounded terminals. Does the channel contain a closed cycle, or is it a loop-free branching tree? Answer cycle or tree.

worlds.title: Paired void handedness
worlds.question: Each far-apart dark tile contains a pale cutout made of exactly eight equal square blocks. Ignoring shifts and quarter-turns, is the right cutout the same handed shape as the left, or its mirror image? Answer same or mirrored.

worlds.title: Mirror window search
worlds.question: The connected blue tile has four horizontal strips, each with 12 positions. Which strip's white-window pattern reads the same from left to right and right to left? Answer top, upper-middle, lower-middle, or bottom.

worlds.title: Constant ribbon search
worlds.question: Each colored ribbon has two identical wide end tabs and four equal-length interior sections. Ignore the end tabs. Which ribbon keeps exactly the same thickness through all four interior sections? The ribbons have equal length and equal colored area, and exactly one is constant. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Carry cascade meter
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one meter made of four separated tiles at the corners of a square, with plain background between them; every pale grey mark outside those four tiles is inert decoration. Three tiles are lamp banks: the top-left tile, the top-right tile and the bottom-left tile. Each bank is a dark rectangular frame holding three round sockets in a vertical column; a socket is either lit, drawn as a filled amber disc, or empty, drawn as a pale disc. A bank's count is simply how many of its three sockets are lit, and it never starts above two. The fourth tile, at the bottom right, is the tick patch: a dark frame holding twelve small square slots in three rows of four, of which some are filled solid teal and the rest are pale. Each teal slot is one tick, and the ticks are applied one after another. Applying one tick works like this: the bottom-left bank gains one lit lamp; but if that bank already shows two lit lamps it instead empties to zero lit lamps and one tick is passed to the top-right bank, which gains one lit lamp under the same rule and, if it already shows two, empties to zero and passes one tick to the top-left bank, which likewise gains one lit lamp and empties to zero if it already shows two. Exactly one bank is marked by a thin red rectangle drawn just inside its dark frame. The meter may sit anywhere on the canvas, and the sockets that happen to be lit within a bank carry no meaning beyond their number. After every tick in the patch has been applied, how many lamps are lit in the bank marked by the red rectangle? Answer with one of zero, one or two.

worlds.title: Lamp register mosaic
worlds.question: The START tile shows three lamps from left to right (filled = 1, hollow = 0). Read the other tiles in row order, left-to-right then top-to-bottom. R rotates all three lamp states one place left; F flips only the left lamp. What three-bit pattern remains?

worlds.title: Three chamber itinerary
worlds.question: Read the three snapshot cards from left to right. Each cyan, amber, and rose disk keeps its color identity. A disk's chamber is TOP, MIDDLE, or BOTTOM. Which disk visits TOP in the first card, MIDDLE in the second, and BOTTOM in the third? Answer cyan, amber, or rose.

worlds.title: Shared hole boundary
worlds.question: Does each colored patch—the cyan patch and the orange patch—share an edge with an enclosed white hole? A white bay connected to the outside is not a hole. Edge-sharing counts; corner-touching does not. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Loop color alternation
worlds.question: A single navy closed trail carries two orange and two purple stations. Do the station colors alternate as you go once around the trail? The starting point and direction do not matter. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route transition majority
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START to the red FINISH. Between every adjacent pair of the eight tethered checkpoint dots, count a switch when their colors differ and a repeat when their colors match. Are there more switches or repeats? Answer switches or repeats.

worlds.title: Checkpoint half tally
worlds.question: Starting at the blue ring, follow the single navy route toward the orange ring. Each red or green checkpoint ring sits beside one route station; encounter it at its nearest route point. Which group contains more red checkpoints: the first four or the last four? Answer first or last.

worlds.title: Weighted pan balance
worlds.question: Two boxes, A on the left and B on the right, each hold exactly the same number of coloured disks.  Across the top a key shows three colour swatches; beside each swatch a row of one, two, or three dark dots gives that colour's weight (one dot is weight one, three dots are weight three).  For each box, its total weight is the sum over the box's disks of the weight of each disk's colour.  Which box has the larger total weight: A or B?  Answer with exactly one of: A, B.

worlds.title: Right triangle bar relation
worlds.question: Each panel shows three horizontal bars: red and blue are the two legs of a right triangle, and gold is the hypotenuse. Which panel satisfies red squared + blue squared = gold squared? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Isometry transfer corner
worlds.question: Left of the gray line, the arrow shows one black shape before and after a single move. The move is one of these: a quarter turn clockwise, a quarter turn counter-clockwise, a half turn, or a mirror flip across one of the square's four axes. Work out which move it was. Now apply that same move to the square right of the gray line, which holds four colored dots near its corners; the square lands back on itself and only its contents move. After the move, which color sits in the top-left corner? Answer blue, green, red, or yellow.

worlds.title: Turn flip escape
worlds.question: Follow the red token. On GOLD, turn right; on BLUE, turn left. Then flip that tile's color and move one cell. Repeat until the token leaves the board. Which gate does it leave through: gate-N, gate-E, gate-S, or gate-W?

worlds.title: Permuted lever totals
worlds.question: Each block counts 1. For each hanger, multiply its block count by its numbered distance from the pivot. Add the five products on each side. Which total is larger? Answer left, right, or same.

worlds.title: Orbital count correspondence
worlds.question: A black square points at a disk in the right panel. The same colour appears exactly once in the left panel, where each disk is decorated with orbiting black dots. Using the colour to connect the two panels, report how many dots wrap the left (reference) disk of that same colour. Answer with two, three, or four.

worlds.title: Colored aperture signature
worlds.question: Which candidate, A or B, has the same color-to-aperture pattern as the REFERENCE? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Row column tally binding
worlds.question: The upper part of this image shows an empty 5-by-5 grid. Beside each of its five rows a group of red dots is drawn, and under each of its five columns a group of blue dots is drawn. The number of red dots beside a row is the number of green cells that row must contain, and the number of blue dots under a column is the number of green cells that column must contain. Below are three filled 5-by-5 grids, labeled A, B and C from left to right, in which some cells are painted green. A candidate grid agrees with the tally when, for every one of the five rows, its number of green cells equals the number of red dots beside that row of the upper grid, and, for every one of the five columns, its number of green cells equals the number of blue dots under that column. Exactly one of A, B and C agrees with the tally. Each of the other two matches the red row dots only or the blue column dots only, never both, and all three candidates contain the same total number of green cells, so neither the row dots alone nor the column dots alone nor the total amount of green identifies the answer. Which candidate grid agrees with the tally? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Normalized slider rail
worlds.question: Each card has a horizontal rail with black end stops and four colored sliders. A rail may move and resize, but it is read from its left stop to its right stop. Which colored border encloses the option where every slider color is at the same fraction of the end-to-end rail length as in the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Rhythm gap correspondence
worlds.question: The top strip is the REFERENCE rhythm. Within each strip, compare the four consecutive gaps between the five dots from left to right. Uniform horizontal stretching is allowed; reversing the order is not. Which colored candidate frame has the same gap proportions: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Pie sector fraction
worlds.question: A filled circle (a pie chart) is cut into three colored sectors: red, blue, and green, which together cover the whole disk. Which colored sector has the largest central angle, meaning it is the biggest slice (covers the largest fraction of the pie)? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Hull fill ratio compare
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. For each filled silhouette, divide colored area by the area of its convex hull. Which panel has the larger value of 1 minus that fraction? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Stack relay binding
worlds.question: The picture shows six columns standing on one long black baseline. Each column is a vertical stack of grey squares of the same size, resting on the baseline, and the stacks differ only in how many squares they hold; every stack holds between one and six squares. Directly below the baseline, under each column, sits one round coloured disk, its TAG. The six tags are red, orange, green, blue, purple and brown, one of each, and which tag sits under which column changes from picture to picture. A single black triangle above the row points down at exactly one column: that is the POINTED column, the one whose centre the triangle is nearest to. Read the picture in two steps. First count the grey squares in the pointed column and call that number K. Second, ignore the pointed column and count columns from the LEFT edge of the picture, so that the leftmost column is number 1 and the rightmost is number 6, and go to column number K. The answer is the colour of the tag under that K-th column. K is a position, never a colour and never a height: the pointed column's own tag, the tallest stack, the shortest stack, the leftmost and the rightmost columns are each the answer only as often as chance allows, and the triangle marks where to start reading rather than what to report. The pointed column is sometimes itself the K-th column and usually is not. Which tag colour does this pick out? Answer red, orange, green, blue, purple or brown.

worlds.title: Paired panel rank rise
worlds.question: From left panel A to right panel B, which colored sample rises the most rank positions? Rank 1 is the highest point.

worlds.title: Rank inversion leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order. In each panel, match same-colored dots between BEFORE and AFTER. A pair of colors is reversed when its top-to-bottom order switches. Which panel has the most reversed color pairs? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior octopus arms
worlds.question: This is an octopus. How many arms does it have? Count only the visible arms and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Envelope stamp corner
worlds.question: Which corner of the envelope contains the postage stamp? Answer top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right.

worlds.title: Snowflake arm count
worlds.question: This image shows one snowflake drawn in a single colour on white paper. The grey page frame and the four short grey ticks near the corners are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. An arm is a long straight spoke that starts at the small hub in the middle of the snowflake and runs all the way out to the edge of the shape. The arms are evenly spaced around the hub and are separated from each other by white wedges of page. Each arm carries two short side branches near its outer end; a side branch is attached partway along an arm, does not touch the hub, and is not itself an arm. The number of arms, the length and thickness of the arms, the colour of the ink and the rotation of the whole snowflake all change from image to image. Count the arms that are actually painted in this image, and do not answer from what a snowflake normally looks like. How many arms does this snowflake have? Answer with exactly one of the integers 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.

worlds.title: Stovetop burner count
worlds.question: How many blue circular burner rings are visible on the stovetop? Count each separate blue ring once. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Next track triangle bar conflict
worlds.question: Does the point of the large filled triangle face toward or away from the separate short bar? Ignore the small corner diamonds. Answer toward or away.

worlds.title: Column bend rectify reveal
worlds.question: A solid triangle is drawn inside a magenta-framed panel, but the panel's vertical strips have been bent: each column is shifted vertically by round(6*sin(2*pi*x/32)) pixels. Undo that declared column bend to level the panel, then read the abstract symbol that appears. Is it an upward-pointing triangle (A) or a downward-pointing triangle (B)? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Mosaic tile reassembly
worlds.question: Find the four grayscale panels, each with a matching pair of colored edge marks. The two marks indicate which outside corner the panel belongs to: marks on the top and left mean upper-left, top and right mean upper-right, bottom and left mean lower-left, and bottom and right mean lower-right. Crop each panel's interior, place the four panels into that 2x2 order, average each 9x9 square of the reconstructed raster using edge replication, and read the broad dark symbol. Which appears: spiral, fork, bracket, or petal?

worlds.title: Ternary smear deconvolve
worlds.question: The picture shows one square panel enclosed by a black frame and ruled into a grid of 7 rows and 7 columns of equal square cells. Below the panel a black-framed key strip shows three swatches: the left swatch is the colour that stands for the number 0, the middle swatch stands for 1 and the right swatch stands for 2. The panel is a smeared print of a hidden 7 by 7 pattern of inked and blank cells. Each printed cell shows, in the colour given by the key, the remainder after division by three of the number of inked cells among the hidden cell in the same place and the two hidden cells immediately to its left in the same row; cells beyond the left edge of the panel count as blank. Undo the smear row by row, working from the left edge rightwards, to recover the hidden pattern. Its inked cells form exactly one of these five symbols: bars (three separate horizontal bars stacked one above another), chevron (a wide V narrowing downwards to a single cell), plus (a full horizontal bar crossed by a vertical bar), ring (a closed ring enclosing empty cells), steps (a staircase of pairs running from the upper left down to the lower right). Which symbol do the inked cells form? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Keystone window rectify
worlds.question: Rectify the cyan-outlined window into an upright square, mapping its magenta, yellow, blue, and green corners to top-left, top-right, bottom-right, and bottom-left. Which symbol appears: circle, triangle, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Adjacent transition arrow
worlds.question: The cyan frame contains 9 rows of 10 tiles. Compare each tile with the tile immediately to its right. Make a 9-by-9 result: mark a dark cell when the pair is different and leave it blank when the pair is the same. Keep the rows and image orientation unchanged. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Texture flow orientation
worlds.question: Ignoring the few stray marks, the overall pattern of the small strokes forms one dominant orientation across the whole image. Which one orientation does the whole stroke field lean toward: horizontal, rising, vertical, or falling? Answer with the single direction word.

worlds.title: Thickness peak silhouette
worlds.question: Which colored silhouette has exactly one dominant interior thickness peak? For each filled silhouette, consider every interior pixel's distance to the boundary; a dominant peak is a local maximum at least 22 pixels from any other selected maximum and at least 42% of that silhouette's deepest distance. Compare the complete fields and choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Loop nesting depth
worlds.question: The picture shows four coloured dots - red, green, blue and orange - and several black outlines. Every outline is a closed loop, no two outlines cross or touch, and some outlines enclose no dot at all. The depth of a dot is the number of outlines that enclose it; a dot lying outside every outline has depth 0. Exactly one dot has the greatest depth. Which coloured dot has the greatest depth? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Dash focus count
worlds.question: Extend every black dash as a straight line. Do the complete set of lines converge around one common point or around two separate common points? Answer one or two.

worlds.title: Proximity bridge articulation
worlds.question: The gray bracket below is a distance ruler. Imagine linking every pair of dot centers strictly closer than that ruler's end-to-end length. Which colored dot is the sole bridge whose removal disconnects the resulting network? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Hollow cavity quadrant
worlds.question: The image is divided by thin lines into four quadrants: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. Each quadrant contains one dark filled round shape of the same size. Three of the four shapes are solid disks, filled completely with no opening on the inside. Exactly one shape is a hollow ring: its inside is empty, showing a clearly visible enclosed cavity (a hole of background) at its centre. Which quadrant contains the hollow ring instead of a solid disk? Answer with the quadrant name.

worlds.title: Enclosed hole search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the only dark silhouette that surrounds a white region completely separated from the outside? Inspect all four equal panels, ignore labels and position, and answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Hatch conjunction panel
worlds.question: This image shows one small framed box labelled KEY standing alone above a row of five larger framed panels of identical size, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. The KEY box holds a single figure. Every panel holds exactly four figures. Every figure in the image, including the key, is an outlined silhouette whose inside is filled with straight parallel stripes, and all outlines enclose the same amount of area, so size, figure count and total ink carry no information. Figures are drawn in several colours and colour is never informative: a figure never has to share the key's colour to match it. An outline is never rotated and never mirrored anywhere in the image, so two figures share an outline exactly when one could be slid over the other and cover it. The stripes inside a figure run in one of four directions: flat across, upright, or slanted one way or the other. A figure matches the key only if it satisfies both conditions at once: the same outline as the key and the same stripe direction as the key. In every one of the five panels exactly two of the four figures repeat the key's outline and exactly two of the four figures repeat the key's stripe direction, so counting figures that share only the outline, or only the stripe direction, gives the same answer of two in every panel and never separates them. In exactly one panel a single figure carries both key features together; in the other four panels no figure does, and there every figure that repeats the key's outline has stripes running at least a quarter turn away from the key's stripes, while every figure that repeats the key's stripe direction has a visibly different outline. Which numbered panel contains the figure that matches the key in both outline and stripe direction? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: One visit route search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has a route that visits all nine colored circles exactly once? Start at any circle, follow only dark links, and never revisit a circle. You do not need to use every link. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Proper coloring search
worlds.question: Which labeled network has every dark line joining one red node and one blue node? Inspect every line. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State token parity
worlds.question: A single token is tracked across the four panels read left to right. A filled disk is state 1 and a hollow ring is state 0; the red ring marks the starting token in the leftmost panel. Between each pair of consecutive panels an operator is shown: a red circle means flip the token's state and a blue square means keep the token's state. Applying the operators in order, what is the token's final state in the final panel? Answer 'filled' or 'outline'.

worlds.title: State handoff recipient
worlds.question: Read P1 through P6 from left to right. On each adjacent transition, a label receives one handoff when it changes into the exact state that a different label changes away from on that same transition; count at most one handoff per label per transition. Which label receives the most handoffs? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Macro expansion walk
worlds.question: The picture has three parts on a cream background. At the bottom is a track of seven coloured square cells in a row; each cell is one of red, orange, yellow, green, blue, purple, brown or teal. Exactly one cell carries a black ring, and that is the cell the marker starts on. Directly above the track is one row of coloured circles and no triangles: that row is the programme, read from left to right. Above the programme are three legend rows. Each legend row begins with one coloured circle, called a badge, followed to its right by one, two or three dark triangles. Every circle in the programme has the same colour as exactly one legend badge and stands for that legend row's triangles; a programme circle is never a move by itself. Carry out the programme one circle at a time from left to right: for each programme circle take the triangles of the legend row with the matching badge colour, in left-to-right order, and for each triangle move the marker one cell to the right if that triangle points right and one cell to the left if it points left. The same legend row may be used more than once, the order in which the legend rows are drawn does not matter, the track does not wrap, and the marker never leaves the track. What is the colour of the cell the marker finishes on?

worlds.title: Rising edge counter replay
worlds.question: The signal starts as shown at START. Read the seven signal cards from left to right. Record one pulse only when the signal changes from OFF (hollow) to ON (solid); all other steps record no pulse. How many pulses are recorded? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Saturating level replay
worlds.question: The gauge starts with the shown number of filled steps. Read the eight triangle cards from left to right: an up-pointing triangle adds one step unless the gauge is already full, and a down-pointing triangle removes one step unless it is already empty. What level remains? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Sealed hole select
worlds.question: The image shows two colored loops, one red and one blue, drawn on a white background. Exactly one of the loops is a fully closed ring: the white region enclosed by its band is a sealed white region (a pocket) that has no opening at all to the surrounding white -- you cannot reach it from the outside without crossing the loop. The other loop is an open ring arc that has one wide visible gap, so the white region inside its curvature is open to the surrounding white through that gap. Look at the red loop and the blue loop. One of them is a complete closed ring whose inside is cut off from the surrounding white (a closed pocket); the other is open with a clear gap. Which colored loop is the closed one that walls off its interior from the outside? Answer with exactly red or blue.

worlds.title: Enclosure depth match
worlds.question: The black rings are closed barriers and green is the reference marker. Which of red, blue, or orange is enclosed by the same number of rings? Count a ring when the marker center is strictly inside it; ignore the canvas.

worlds.title: Broken ring reach
worlds.question: The picture shows blue strips of equal thickness on white paper. Some blue strips are interrupted by white gaps, so the blue ink falls apart into separate pieces. Two black dots sit on blue ink. Two dots count as being on the same piece only if you can travel from one dot to the other while staying on blue ink the whole way, never crossing a white gap and never jumping between strips. Are the two black dots on the same piece of blue ink? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Perfect matching panel
worlds.question: Pairing uses drawn links. A perfect pairing selects links so every round station is an endpoint of exactly one selected link. Which network allows a perfect pairing? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Route homotopy islands
worlds.question: The blue and orange routes meet only at the two green endpoints. Can the blue route be continuously slid onto the orange route without crossing a black island or moving either endpoint? Routes may bend and stretch, but cannot pass through an island. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Corridor farther room
worlds.question: This picture is a floor plan drawn in two colours: white is open corridor and black is solid wall. You may move only through white corridor and never through black wall. The corridors form a plan with no loop, so between any two points of white corridor there is exactly one route that never doubles back. There is one green dot, one blue dot and one red dot, each in its own part of the corridor. Measure distance only as the length of corridor you walk along that route, following every turn; straight-line distance across the picture does not count. Walking from the green dot, which dot is farther away, the blue dot or the red dot? Answer blue or red.

worlds.title: Alternating turn terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green ring, follow the dark network. At the first gray junction turn left; at the second gray junction turn right. Which colored square do you reach? At each gray junction there are exactly two outgoing branches, both at right angles to the incoming route.

worlds.title: Longest rising run terminal
worlds.question: Starting at each green START circle, follow its chain to the colored terminal. Which terminal's chain has the longest run of consecutive links where every link is longer than the link immediately before it? Measure each link center-to-center; a run may start anywhere in a chain. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Relaythread step index bind
worlds.question: The picture is a cream board scattered with small decorative squares that mean nothing. Somewhere on the board lies exactly one thin slate-grey THREAD: a single narrow line that runs as a staircase of short straight horizontal and vertical runs. It never crosses or touches itself, and one of its two ends is a thickened square CAP while the other end is plain. Sitting on the thread, each one straddling the thread so that the thread continues out of both of its sides, are several small square MARKS: most are coloured red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple, and exactly one mark on the thread is BLACK. That black mark is the GATE. Only marks that sit on the thread count; every square that lies on the bare board away from the thread is decoration and means nothing, including decorative black and slate-grey squares. Walk along the thread starting at the thickened cap and meet the marks in the order in which you reach them, following every corner of the thread. Let k be the number of coloured marks you meet before you reach the black gate. Then carry on past the gate and count coloured marks again from the gate onwards: the answer is the k-th coloured mark after the gate. So the count taken on one stretch of the thread selects a position on the other stretch. The thread doubles back on itself, so the order along the thread is not the order of the marks by row, by column, or by straight-line distance from the cap, and each of those three sorts gives a different and wrong answer. k is always at least 2, so the answer is never the first coloured mark after the gate; the answer is never the last coloured mark on the thread, never the first coloured mark from the cap, and never the coloured mark just before the gate. The answer colour is always worn by at least two marks on the thread and is never the single commonest colour, so no colour, position, size, count or amount of ink identifies it on its own. Find that k-th coloured mark after the gate. What is its colour? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Run compression rail
worlds.question: The gold dot starts eight square beads. Starting there, replace each maximal consecutive run of the same bead color by one lavender stack containing one square per bead in that run. Which red, green, or blue dot starts the exact four-stack result? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Ribbon link correspondence
worlds.question: The ribbon's upper run shows four black landmark shapes. A magenta bridge marks one neighboring pair. The lower return run contains the same four shapes in a new order; its three bridges are amber, cyan, and violet. Find the lower bridge joining the same two shapes, in either direction. What color is it? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Descent switchback count
worlds.question: The figure shows one survey panel on off-white paper. Exactly one mark is pure black: a single thick black route that descends continuously from its upper end to its lower end and never rises back up, so at every height it has exactly one horizontal position. Follow that black route from its upper end to its lower end. A reversal is a place where the route stops moving to the left and starts moving to the right, or the other way round. Every reversal in this figure is a wide swing: the route travels at least twenty pixels horizontally on each side of it, and the route contains no smaller wiggles, so every direction change counts. Count every reversal along the whole route, including all of the ones in its middle. The thin coloured curves, the grey rectangle, the grey tick marks and the two small grey squares at the route's ends are decoration and carry no information. How many reversals does the black route make? Answer with one number: 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Trace half variation
worlds.question: Which half of the cyan route has more total vertical travel: left or right? Add every upward and downward change within each side of the dashed divider. Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Sparkline runup drawdown
worlds.question: Following the colored mini-trace from left to right, which is larger: its largest rise from an earlier point to a later point, or its largest fall from an earlier point to a later point? Answer RISE or FALL.

worlds.title: Shoelace overpass alternation
worlds.question: From top to bottom, do the visible top strands at the five crossings of the single blue shoelace follow this exact sequence: /, \, /, \, /? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Vinyl center label shape
worlds.question: What is the visible shape of the large colored center label on the record—circle or square? Judge its outer colored boundary, ignore the tiny spindle hole, and answer circle or square.

worlds.title: Rail conjunction reveal
worlds.question: This picture contains two rails of small square pads that lie far apart: one upright rail of nine pads stacked near a left or right margin, and one flat rail of nine pads in a row near the top or bottom margin. Every pad is a square block of exactly one of two tones, dark or pale, and both tones appear inside both rails. A few small clutter marks - narrow bars and diamonds, none of them square pads and none of them on a rail - are scattered on the background and carry no evidence. Exactly three pads of the upright rail are dark and exactly three pads of the flat rail are dark, whatever the answer is. Carry out this operation. Number the upright rail's pads 1 to 9 from top to bottom and the flat rail's pads 1 to 9 from left to right. Now take an empty nine-row, nine-column field and mark every cell whose row number is a dark pad of the upright rail and whose column number is a dark pad of the flat rail; mark no other cell. Exactly nine cells get marked in every picture. The marked cells always form exactly one of four figures. 'solid_block' is one solid three-by-three square of nine touching cells. 'dot_lattice' is nine separated single cells in a widely spaced three-by-three arrangement, no two of them touching. 'upright_bars' is three separated upright bars, each one cell wide and three cells tall. 'flat_bars' is three separated flat bars, each three cells wide and one cell tall. The figure is drawn nowhere in the picture. Neither rail settles the answer on its own: the upright rail alone leaves two figures possible and the flat rail alone leaves the other pairing, so both distant rails must be read and combined. Which figure do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: solid_block, dot_lattice, upright_bars, flat_bars.

worlds.title: Winding filmstrip rectify
worlds.question: Follow the connected blue filmstrip from the triangular START cap to the round END cap. At each framed cell, copy its 7 samples from the green bead toward the orange bead as one top-to-bottom column. Straighten the strip by placing those columns side by side in route order. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Adjacent change reveal
worlds.question: Rotate the single framed mosaic until the cyan corner is upper left and the gold corner is upper right. In each of its ten rows of nine cells, compare every side-by-side neighboring pair from left to right. Make an eight-cell result row: dark exactly when the two compared cells differ, and light when they match. Stack the ten result rows without reordering. Which symbol needs the fewest cell changes to match the 10 by 8 result: diamond, fork, or stair? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Broken curve turn relation
worlds.question: Treat the two blue curve fragments as consecutive pieces of one interrupted path, reading from one fragment to the other across the small gap. Do they bend to the same side, making a C-bend, or to opposite sides, making an S-bend? Answer C or S.

worlds.title: Threaded bead order
worlds.question: Begin at the round cap and follow the single dark trail to the square cap. Do you encounter the colored beads in red-blue-gold order or gold-blue-red order? Answer red-blue-gold or gold-blue-red.

worlds.title: Interval rail search
worlds.question: Which labeled stretch of the continuous rail has four square bumps whose centers are equally spaced from left to right? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Adjacent notch plate search
worlds.question: Each colored square plate has two identical white notches cut into its edges. Which color has its two notches on neighboring edges rather than opposite edges? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Pitsow chain replay
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small block drawn with a thick black frame, and every pale grey mark lying outside that frame is inert decoration that means nothing. Inside the frame are nine equal square pits in three rows of three, each pit filled with its own solid floor colour, and no two pits share a colour. The nine pits are ordered by reading order: left to right along the top row, then left to right along the middle row, then left to right along the bottom row, and after the last pit the order wraps round to the first pit again. Each pit holds nought, one, two or three pips, drawn as equal small black squares standing in a row on that pit's floor; a pit with no black square on it is empty. Exactly one pit carries a thick white ring drawn just inside its own border; the ring is only a marking, it never moves, and the pit it rings holds pips and a floor colour like any other pit. Now sow the pips. Lift every pip out of the ringed pit, leaving that pit empty, and hold them in your hand. Drop them one at a time into the pits that follow in reading order, one single pip into each successive pit, wrapping past the last pit back to the first, until your hand is empty. Then look at the pit that received the very last pip of the handful. If that pit had been empty just before that pip landed, so it now holds exactly one pip, the sowing stops there. Otherwise that pit now holds more than one pip: lift every pip out of it, including the one that just landed, leaving it empty, and sow that new handful onward in exactly the same way, continuing from the pit that follows it. Repeat this until a handful ends in a pit that was empty before the final pip landed, and that pit is where the sowing stops. What is the floor colour of the pit where the sowing finally stops? Answer with one of red, green, blue, yellow, orange, purple, teal, pink or brown.

worlds.title: Checkpoint return tableau
worlds.question: Blue with a dot means ON; gold with a ring means OFF. Each horizontal row is one lamp. Read START, then checkpoints 1, 2, 3 from left to right. Which checkpoint has the most lamps back in their START state? Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Detached emblem chain
worlds.question: The green ring marks the starting emblem. Read the four separate tickets by their purple-dot counts: one dot, then two, three, and four. On each ticket, match the current emblem to one of the two emblems and cross the divider to the other emblem. Only emblems inside tickets take part; free-floating emblems are distractors. After all four tickets, which emblem remains: circle, triangle, or square?

worlds.title: Courtyard fusion shutter
worlds.question: The teal and yellow areas are solid wall. Turn only the yellow shutter white. Do the two enclosed white courtyards merge into one still-enclosed courtyard? White areas connect through shared edges, not corners. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: One stroke return
worlds.question: Treat the six circles as vertices and the seven dark corridors as undirected edges; ignore pale gray decorations and fill colors. Does this connected graph have a closed Euler tour that uses every edge exactly once? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Paired turn agreement
worlds.question: Trace the navy centerline from the green start to the red finish. At the two bends, are the turns the same direction (both left or both right) or opposite directions? Answer same or opposite.

worlds.title: Alternating checkpoint trace
worlds.question: Starting at the blue ring, follow the single dark route to the orange ring and read the six colored checkpoints in travel order. Do red and green alternate at every checkpoint, with no same-color neighbors? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Withdrawn pivot symmetry
worlds.question: A row of ten square cells stands on a white card; each cell is filled either dark or pale.  A small solid arrowhead points up at exactly one cell, marking it.  Imagine that marked cell is removed from the row entirely and the remaining nine cells are slid together to close the gap, keeping their left-to-right order.  That shortened nine-cell row is not drawn anywhere; only after withdrawing the marked cell does it exist.  Is the shortened row a palindrome, reading the same left-to-right as right-to-left in dark and pale?  Answer with exactly one of: yes, no.

worlds.title: Weighted pivot balance
worlds.question: Each red and blue disk weighs in proportion to its visible area. Which panel would balance at the marked pivot? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Unvisited state row
worlds.question: The six discs above the grey rule are the starting row. Below the rule are four more rows, numbered 1 to 4 from the top. Every row holds the same six colours in some order, in six places numbered 1 to 6 from the left. Do this twelve times to the starting row: swap the red disc with the disc in the next place to its right, counting on past place 6 back to place 1; then move the disc in place 6 to place 1 and slide the other five discs one place to the right. Together with the starting row that gives thirteen rows. Three of the four numbered rows are among those thirteen and one of them never is. Which numbered row never appears? Answer with the row number alone: 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Stable disturbance search
worlds.question: Each gate has its own hidden flip bit: its shown result equals the named operation, then XOR the hidden bit. Infer all hidden bits from CURRENT. In TEST they stay unchanged. Try one source card at a time and recompute. Which sole card makes the four TARGET lamps? Answer card-A, card-B, card-C, or card-D.

worlds.title: Twin flip relay
worlds.question: Start at the green arrow, facing the way it points. Repeat 20 moves: on LIGHT turn right; on DARK turn left. A lettered square flips the other square with the same letter; a blank square flips itself. Then move ahead. The path stays on the board. After move 20, which goal badge holds the cursor? Answer goal-A, goal-B, goal-C, or goal-D.

worlds.title: Bow sagitta correspondence
worlds.question: The gray bow at the top is an arc that rises from a straight chord between two dark endpoints, deflecting upward by a certain amount. Below it are three colored bows A, B, C: one is red, one green, one blue, and each deflects a different amount. Which colored bow deflects upward by exactly the same amount as the gray bow? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Colored nearest partner correspondence
worlds.question: The image has a REFERENCE panel and candidates A and B. For every colored disk, find the other disk with the nearest center. Which candidate has the same color-to-partner map as the REFERENCE? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Mirror axis partner binding
worlds.question: A single straight black line crosses this picture; treat that line as a mirror. On one side of the line there are five coloured disks: one red, one blue, one green, one orange and one purple. On the other side of the line there are five gray squares, all exactly the same size and the same shade, so the squares carry no colour information at all. The mirror image of a point is the point at the same perpendicular distance from the line, on the other side, along the perpendicular through it. Exactly four of the five gray squares are centred precisely on the mirror image of the centre of one of the disks, and each of those four squares belongs to a different disk. The remaining gray square is displaced: it is not centred on the mirror image of any disk. So exactly one disk has no gray square at its mirror image. What is the colour of that one disk? Answer red, blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Shape texture transfer
worlds.question: The TARGET and each reference card contain one circle, triangle, square, and diamond. Shapes may move, but each shape keeps its surface pattern. Which tag color belongs to the reference card with exactly the same shape-to-pattern binding as the TARGET? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Similarity constellation correspondence
worlds.question: The reference card shows four colored landmarks. Exactly one test card preserves which color occupies each place in the landmark arrangement after translation, rotation, and uniform resizing of the whole set. A mirror reflection does not count. Ignore the cards' placement and marker size. Which card is it: A, B, or C?

worlds.title: Longest stroke
worlds.question: Three colored line segments are drawn at different angles and positions on a light panel. Which colored segment is longest, meaning it has the largest true straight-line (end-to-end) length? Measure the actual planar length of each stroke. Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Calibration residual extreme
worlds.question: Which model (A, B, or C) departs furthest from the dashed diagonal? At the seven marked checkpoints, compare each model's largest absolute vertical gap; ties or gaps below 0.045 normalized units are quarantined. Choose A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Moment arm balance
