worlds.question: The picture shows a horizontal black rail with a row of evenly spaced black tick marks just below it; the distance between neighbouring ticks is one STEP. The black triangle under the ticks points at exactly one tick: that tick is the PIVOT. Standing on the rail are several columns, each built from square cells stacked one on top of another and outlined in black. Every column stands on exactly one tick and no column stands on the pivot tick. A column's WEIGHT is its number of cells. A column's ARM is the number of steps between the tick it stands on and the pivot tick. A column's MOMENT is its weight multiplied by its arm. Add the moments of all columns left of the pivot to get the left total, and the moments of all columns right of the pivot to get the right total. The cell colours and the pale horizontal guide rows are decorative and carry no information. Which side has the greater total moment? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Standardized interval separation
worlds.question: Which color has the largest standardized center separation? For each color, divide the horizontal distance between the centers of its two capped intervals by the average of those intervals' full widths. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Forest interval exclusion
worlds.question: Which colored horizontal uncertainty interval lies completely to the right of the dashed vertical reference line? Answer with red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior vehicle wheels
worlds.question: This is a vehicle. How many wheels does it have? Count only the visible wheels and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Piano bracketed key count
worlds.question: How many dark keys have a light key immediately to their left and right in the piano keyboard strip? Count only dark keys bracketed by one visible light key on each side; ignore the frame, lower key bed, and PIANO label. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Butterfly spot symmetry
worlds.question: This image shows one butterfly drawn on white paper. The dark bar down the middle is its BODY, and the CENTRE LINE is the straight up-and-down line running through the middle of that body. The two coloured wings are drawn one on each side of the centre line and are exact mirror images of each other in shape. Each wing carries exactly one round SPOT; the two spots are drawn in the same colour as each other and at the same size, and that spot colour is used nowhere else on the page. The DISTANCE of a spot from the centre line means the sideways distance across the page from the centre line to the middle of that spot, and it is measured the same way on both sides. LEFT and RIGHT are the left and right of the page as you look at it. The grey page frame, the grey corner ticks, the grey antennae and the small grey diamonds are decoration and carry no marking. Which spot sits farther out is chosen separately from the wing colour, the spot colour, the spot size, the height of the spots on the wings, the wing shape, the total amount of coloured ink and the position of the butterfly on the page, and on a given page the two distances always add up to the same total whichever spot is the farther one, so on some pages the two spots are exactly the same distance from the centre line and on other pages one spot is drawn clearly farther out than the other, and neither is a mistake. No image in this set is a borderline case: the two distances are either exactly equal or differ by at least 16 pixels. Report the picture in front of you, and do not answer from how a butterfly's wing markings are usually arranged. Which wing's spot is farther from the centre line? Answer exactly one of: left, right, neither.

worlds.title: Bias rotary dial holes
worlds.question: How many separate cyan circular finger holes are visible around the rotary telephone dial? Count only cyan-filled circles on the dial; ignore the center label and gray screws. Answer 8, 10, or 12.

worlds.title: Music staff line conflict
worlds.question: Does the visible staff contain exactly five long, parallel horizontal lines? Ignore the notes and the short vertical barline. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Column integral reveal
worlds.question: The image is a 2D field of random black speckle on a white background. A single 1D glyph is hidden purely in the column of the ink: each column holds an independent vertical scatter of dark pixels whose count traces a smooth profile across the picture (a peak, two humps), but because they are scattered at random heights the raw raster looks like shape-less speckle. Declared transform: add up the black ink in every column to get a 1D profile. If the profile is one central peak, the answer is A; if it is two symmetric peaks, the answer is B. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Polar band unwrap symbol
worlds.question: Use the two same-colour fiducial pairs to find the two radial edges and the shared center of the annular band. Unwrap angle horizontally and radius vertically into a rectangle, ignoring the fine carrier. Which broad symbol appears: wave, ladder, bowtie, or key?

worlds.title: Loop corridor reach reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one lattice of 13 rows and 33 columns of square cells, with a blue square printed at each of its four corners. Every cell is either white (open) or dark (blocked). Three rooms are outlined in green; each room is 9 rows tall and 9 columns wide, and each room is walled in except for the single cell in its bottom wall that may be open. A red dot is printed in one open cell: that is where you start. Now walk: from the cell you are in you may step to the cell directly above, below, to the left or to the right, but only onto white cells, never onto a dark cell and never diagonally. Shade every cell you can reach from the red dot by repeating such steps. Exactly one room contains shaded cells. Inside that room the shaded cells form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: comb, cross, cup, ell, tee. Ignore the shaded corridor cells outside the rooms, and ignore the white cells of rooms you cannot reach. Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Directional shadow fill
worlds.question: Inside the cyan grid, every dark cell casts a solid shadow straight toward the side marked by the magenta bar: make every cell from it through that side dark. Columns or rows with no dark cell stay light. Ignore gray distractors. Then turn the grid so the magenta side is at the bottom. Which skyline appears: crown, bowl, stairs, or wave?

worlds.title: Quadrant card reassembly arrow
worlds.question: Use the four colored circles in the assembly map to place the matching cards. First rotate each card by quarter-turns, without reflecting it, until its gold triangular notch points up; then place it in the matching colored quadrant. In the assembled grid, ignore isolated single dark cells and read the one connected dark shape. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Polygon sharpest corner
worlds.question: On a white canvas, five colored dots are drawn (red, green, blue, purple, and orange). Taken together the five dots outline one irregular five-sided polygon (a pentagon), one colored dot at each corner. One corner is noticeably sharper than all the others: its interior angle is the most acute, most pointed. Which color dot sits at the sharpest corner? Answer red, green, blue, purple, or orange.

worlds.title: Translated motif constellation
worlds.question: Which color's dots contain two translated copies of one four-dot motif? Compare all eight dots and choose red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Mirror versus repeat
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain background, one thin vertical grey rule, and a number of identical solid dots, all the same size and the same colour. Every dot lies either fully to the left of the grey rule or fully to the right of it, and the two sides always hold the same number of dots. The dots on the right side were produced from the dots on the left side by exactly one of two operations, and by nothing else: either every left dot was reflected across the grey rule, as in a mirror, or the whole left group was slid sideways to the right without being flipped, keeping every dot at its own height. Under both operations each dot keeps its vertical position, the two groups hold the same number of dots, cover the same total area of ink, span the same width and height, and have the same average position, so dot colour, dot size, dot count, ink, group width and group centre never indicate which operation was used. Only the arrangement of the right dots relative to one another decides it: under the mirror the left-to-right order of the dots is turned around, and under the slide it is kept. Which operation produced the right group: mirror or copy? Answer with exactly one word, "mirror" or "copy".

worlds.title: Radial scale center
worlds.question: Across all black circles, their sizes increase with distance from one colored marker. Which marker is it: red or blue? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Orientation flow center
worlds.question: Every short dark dash follows one turning flow. From the correct colored ring to every dash, the connecting direction is perpendicular to that dash; the dashes may be at different distances. Which ring is the flow's center? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Fill ratio search
worlds.question: A reference filled gauge is shown in the top panel. Below it, the image is split into four quadrants, each containing one filled gauge. Exactly one quadrant's gauge has the same fill level (its dark fill rises to the same fraction of the track height from the bottom) as the reference gauge. Which quadrant contains the gauge whose fill level matches the reference gauge?

worlds.title: Proportion tick rail
worlds.question: A thin horizontal rule runs across the full width of this image. Above the rule stands a single reference rail: a solid horizontal bar with one small square marker floating just above it. Below the rule stand five candidate rails of the same kind, one per row; count them 1 to 5 from top to bottom. Every rail is a straight bar of the same thickness and the same colour, and every rail carries exactly one marker. The six rails have different lengths and each one begins at its own horizontal position on the page, so the rails are not aligned with one another. For any rail, read its marker's position as the distance from that rail's own left end to the centre of its marker, divided by that same rail's own full length: that is the marker's fraction along its rail, and it does not change if the rail is moved sideways or if the whole rail with its marker is scaled up or down. Exactly one candidate rail places its marker at the same fraction along its own length as the reference rail does along the reference length. In every other candidate rail that fraction differs from the reference fraction by at least ten percent of the rail's length, so no comparison is a close call. Absolute pixel measurements are traps and are not the rule: one of the wrong rails puts its marker exactly the same number of pixels from its own left end as the reference does, in the very same screen column, and another wrong rail has exactly the same total length as the reference rail, while the correct rail has a different length and a different absolute marker offset from the reference. Rail length, rail starting position, the amount of ink, marker size and colour therefore carry no information; only the fraction does. Where in the stack below the rule is the rail whose marker sits at the same fraction of its own length as the reference marker? Answer with exactly one of: topmost, second-from-top, middle, fourth-from-top, bottommost.

worlds.title: Edge connected terminals
worlds.question: Which panel has a continuous dark-tile route connecting the MAGENTA terminal to the AMBER terminal? Tiles connect only when they share an edge; corner touches do not count. Panels A-D are in reading order (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right).

worlds.title: Convex boundary search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has every navy dot on the boundary of the convex hull of all its dots? Dots along a straight hull edge count as on the boundary. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State travel distance
worlds.question: Four panels P1, P2, P3, P4 are shown side by side; read them left to right as time steps. Each panel contains the same three markers -- red on the top lane, green on the middle lane, blue on the bottom lane -- and every lane is divided into nine evenly spaced sites, numbered 1 at the leftmost position to 9 at the rightmost. In each panel every marker sits on exactly one site. A marker's total travel is the sum, measured in sites, of the absolute steps it takes between consecutive panels: |P2-P1| + |P3-P2| + |P4-P3|. Which marker colour accumulates the greatest total travel across the four panels? Answer with its colour: red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: State path length
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each labeled tile shows LOW, MID, or HIGH using the STATE KEY. Treat LOW=0, MID=1, and HIGH=2. For each label, add the absolute changes between consecutive states. Which label has the greatest total state travel? Exactly one wins. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State machine tape run
worlds.question: The picture shows a transition table, a marker and a tape. Down the left of the table are four coloured circles: these are the four states, one per table row, and no two of them share a colour. Along the top of the table are three coloured squares: these are the three input symbols, one per table column, and no two of them share a colour. Every cell of the table holds a square painted in one of the four state colours: that cell says which state you move to if you are currently in the state of that cell's row and you read the symbol of that cell's column. A cell painted in its own row's colour means you stay where you are. To the left of the circles is a black ring: the marker starts in the state whose circle centre is nearest to the centre of that black ring. Below the table is a tape of coloured squares, each painted in one of the three symbol colours. The tape is read one square at a time from left to right, in the direction of the arrow drawn beneath it, and each square is one step: look up the row of the state you are currently in and the column whose header square has that tape square's colour, and move to the state named by that cell. Nothing about the run is drawn: the path of the marker and the state it ends in appear nowhere in the picture. After every tape square has been read in order, which state is the marker in? Answer with the colour of that state: red, blue, green or orange.

worlds.title: Domino roll replay
worlds.question: The two-cell domino starts in the numbered bays shown; the magenta ring marks one end. Read the five arrow cards from left to right. Each arrow tries to roll the domino one bay in that direction. A successful roll shifts the domino one bay and swaps its two ends. An arrow that would cross an edge does nothing, including no end swap. Which bay contains the marked end after all five cards? Answer 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Guarded skip replay
worlds.question: The badge starts in the state shown. Read the eight numbered cards from left to right. A FLIP card changes ON to OFF or OFF to ON. At a GUARD card, if the badge is ON, do not execute the next card and continue with the following card; if the badge is OFF, continue normally. Skipped cards have no effect. What state remains after the program? Answer ON or OFF.

worlds.title: Loop separation
worlds.question: The image shows one closed black loop drawn on a white background, and two small colored dots: one red and one blue. A closed loop splits the plane into two sides: its inside (the white pocket the loop surrounds) and its outside (the rest of the white background). The two dots are on OPPOSITE sides of the loop exactly when one of them lies inside the loop and the other lies outside it. Are the red dot and the blue dot on opposite sides of the closed black loop? Answer with exactly yes or no.

worlds.title: Contour closure selection
worlds.question: Which colored contour is open? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Hub removal piece count
worlds.question: The picture shows one flat network drawn on white paper: straight black struts joining round junctions. Three junctions are painted as large coloured hubs - one red, one green and one blue - and every other junction is a small black dot. The whole drawing is one single connected network: starting from any junction you can reach every other junction by walking along struts, and no two struts cross anywhere. Each coloured hub has exactly three struts touching it. Now imagine rubbing out all three coloured hubs at once, each one together with the three struts that touch it, and leaving every other junction and strut exactly where it is. What is left breaks into a number of separate pieces: two junctions belong to the same piece when a chain of remaining struts still joins them, and to different pieces when no chain of remaining struts joins them. The number of pieces left is four, five or six. How many separate pieces are left - four, five or six?

worlds.title: Crossing free redraw
worlds.question: Gray links join cyan round stations. A crossing without a cyan station is not a connection. Could this same station-to-station network be redrawn so that no links cross except at stations? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Euler components holes
worlds.question: Count side-connected dark pieces and fully enclosed light holes. Are the two counts equal? Corner-only touching does not connect. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Net reaches more pads
worlds.question: This picture shows dark gray wires, one green square, one purple square and eight identical orange pads. Every wire runs only horizontally or vertically, and no wire ever touches or crosses another wire. Some wires contain a visible blank break; a break means the wire is cut there and nothing passes through it. A pad is supplied by a colored square when you can follow dark gray wire from that square to that pad without ever crossing a break or jumping a blank space. Each pad can be supplied by at most one square, and some pads are supplied by neither. How long the wires are, how many breaks each network has, where the pads sit and which side of the picture a square is on do not matter; only the number of pads each square supplies counts. Which colored square supplies more orange pads? Answer green or purple.

worlds.title: Euler trail terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green node and travel along the dark links. Use every dark link exactly once, without reusing a link. Which colored node must be last: red, orange, or purple?

worlds.title: Glyph switch terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green circle and take its solid link. Then move downward from junction to junction. At each purple junction, a circle means keep the incoming link style, while a square means switch style (solid to dashed or dashed to solid). Take the one outgoing link with the required style. Which colored terminal is reached? Links meet only at marked junctions and do not cross. Answer red, blue, orange, or cyan.

worlds.title: Beadring cyclic order bind
worlds.question: The dark board is scattered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly one cream CARD sits somewhere on it. Only what is drawn on the card decides the answer; every square off the card is decoration and means nothing. The card carries three RINGS, each of six small square beads evenly spaced around a circle. Every bead is red, blue, green or purple, and a colour may repeat inside a ring. The single ring at the top of the card is the KEY ring. Below it are two DIAL rings, one on the left and one on the right, and under each dial ring lies one wide coloured BAR. Reading a ring means walking its six beads clockwise, starting at any bead, which gives that ring a closed cyclic colour order. Each dial ring carries exactly the same six bead colours as the key ring. One of the two dials is the key ring turned by some angle, so reading it clockwise gives the key's cyclic order starting somewhere else; the other dial is the key ring flipped over, so reading it clockwise gives the key's cyclic order backwards. Flipping keeps every colour count and keeps every pair of neighbouring beads, so counting colours or checking which colours touch cannot tell the two dials apart - only the clockwise direction of the order can. The two bars have two different colours drawn from red, blue, green and purple, and the bar colours are chosen independently of the beads, so no bead tells you a bar colour. What colour is the bar under the dial ring that is the key ring turned rather than flipped? Answer red, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Xor folded stencil
worlds.question: The wide card is the reference. Fold its left half rightward across the dashed crease. In each aligned square, the folded result is filled exactly when one source square is filled and the other is empty. Which colored rim encloses that result? Answer ruby, green, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Running parity correspondence
worlds.question: The upper-left grid is the SOURCE. In each row, scan left to right. An output cell is dark exactly when the number of dark SOURCE cells seen so far in that row, including the current cell, is odd. Exactly one of the other three grids is the output. Which color fills its tag strip? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Region axis spread
worlds.question: Is the colored specimen's filled area spread more horizontally or vertically about the gold center marker? Count all colored area. Answer horizontal or vertical.

worlds.title: Local well density
worlds.question: Each outlined sampling well contains visible particles. Which well has the greater particle density: particle count divided by the visible interior area of its frame? Answer LEFT or RIGHT.

worlds.title: Visible m arch count
worlds.question: How many high arches are visible in this handwritten lowercase m? Count each distinct crest that rises above the dashed guide.

worlds.title: Bowling ball finger holes
worlds.question: Is the largest dark finger hole visibly below the other two holes on the colored bowling ball? Compare the three holes only; ignore gray lane marks. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Spiral chirality reveal
worlds.question: Exactly one stroke in this picture is a long unbroken wire: it winds inward as a rectangular spiral of straight runs and square corners, and it covers the whole page from the outer border to the middle. One end of the wire carries a small filled round bead just inside its tip; the other end is a bare tip. At twenty-five places along the wire, spread over every part of the spiral, the wire briefly leaves its lane: it steps sideways by a short jog, runs a short distance parallel to the lane it left, and steps back into that same lane. There are exactly twenty-five such detours and nothing else interrupts the wire. Carry out this operation: stand at the beaded end facing along the wire, walk the wire all the way to the bare tip, and for each detour in the order you meet it record whether the wire stepped out to your left hand or to your right hand at that moment, judging left and right from the direction you are walking at that point, not from the page. Write those twenty-five records into a 5 by 5 grid in that same order, filling row 1 left to right, then row 2, and so on to row 5, and mark every grid cell whose detour went to your left. Exactly 9 of the 25 cells are marked. The marked cells form one symbol on the grid: 'tee' is the whole top row together with the centre column below it; 'ell' is the whole left column together with the bottom row; 'plus' is the whole centre row together with the whole centre column; 'ex' is the two full diagonals. The spiral's winding sense, which tip carries the bead, the colours, the wire's position on the page and the small scattered squares elsewhere are decoration; only the left-or-right handedness of the twenty-five detours, taken in walking order from the beaded end, decides the symbol. Which symbol do the marked cells form? Answer with exactly one of: ell, ex, plus, tee.

worlds.title: Double turn stamp
worlds.question: The square tile holds a T-stamp. Apply the quarter-turn shown in the one-dot circle, then the quarter-turn shown in the two-dot circle. Each curved arrow turns the stamp 90 degrees in its arrow direction. Where does the T's full crossbar end up: top, right, bottom, or left?

worlds.title: Alternating vertex reflection
worlds.question: Start at the red ring and follow the single dark trail to the gold triangle. Imagine the straight chord joining their centers. Number the seven cyan beads in travel order. Reflect beads 2, 4, and 6 across that chord; leave beads 1, 3, 5, and 7 fixed, then reconnect the endpoints and beads in order. Which path appears: arch (one bulge on the left-hand side as you travel red to gold), cup (one bulge on the right-hand side), or wave (one bulge on each side)?

worlds.title: Spiral growth handedness
worlds.question: Follow the single blue trail from its tight inner end toward its wide outer end. Does it wind clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Coherent arc triplet
worlds.question: Do all three separated colored curve fragments trace parts of one imaginary circle? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Junction cell search
worlds.question: Which colored patch contains a square joined edge-to-edge to colored squares above, below, left, and right?

worlds.title: Paired stamp search
worlds.question: Each labeled badge contains two detached 2×2 color stamps. Which badge has two identical stamp patterns? Exactly one does. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Medallion swap replay
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one small coloured medallion: a solid central disk wrapped in four concentric rings of equal thickness. Every ring is split down its vertical middle, so it has a left half of one colour and a right half of a different colour. Every coloured part of the medallion is red, green, blue, purple or orange. The colour of the central disk is the colour carried at the start. Each ring is one swap rule between its own two half colours: when the colour carried at that moment is one of that ring's two half colours it becomes the ring's other half colour, and otherwise that ring does nothing at all. The rings act one after another, beginning with the innermost ring, which touches the central disk, and working outwards to the outermost ring, so the order matters. The medallion may sit anywhere on the canvas, and every grey mark outside it is inert decoration that changes nothing. Which colour is carried after the outermost ring has acted? Answer with one of red, green, blue, purple or orange.

worlds.title: Die roll dispatch
worlds.question: The START card shows the die's TOP, FRONT, and RIGHT faces. Opposite faces sum to 7. Read roll cards 1 then 2: each arrow rolls the die one step in that direction on the table (up means away from you; down means toward you). What number is on TOP after both rolls?

worlds.title: Interval clamp cascade
worlds.question: The orange ring marks the starting lane. Read the six highlighted bands from top to bottom. At each band, keep the marker where it is if its lane is highlighted. If it is outside the band, move it to the nearest highlighted end. After all six bands, which lane remains: A, B, C, D, or E?

worlds.title: Railway station precedence
worlds.question: Follow the single black railway from the orange terminal to the blue terminal. Do you reach the cyan station before the yellow station? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Courtyard island separation
worlds.question: Does the enclosed white courtyard wrap all the way around a detached colored island? Answer yes if the inner colored region is separated from the outer colored sheet by white on every side; answer no if it is joined to the outer sheet. White areas connect through shared edges, not diagonal corners.

worlds.title: Wide fork terminal
worlds.question: Trace the dark channel from the green START to the central fork. Follow the wider of the two outgoing dark corridors. Which terminal does it reach: cyan or orange?

worlds.title: Symbol relay trace
worlds.question: First, in the left panel, start at the blue ring and follow its unbroken navy route to the violet symbol (circle or square). Then, in the right panel, start at the matching violet symbol and follow that symbol's separate navy route. Which terminal ring does it reach: red or gold? Ignore pale gray dashes.

worlds.title: Normalized pan average
worlds.question: Two boxes, A on the left and B on the right, hold coloured disks of three colours; the two boxes need not hold the same number of disks. Across the top a key shows three colour swatches; beside each swatch a row of one, two, or three dark dots gives that colour's weight (one dot is weight one, three dots are weight three).  For each box its average weight is the sum of the weights of its disks' colours, divided by the number of disks in that box.  Which box has the larger average weight per disk: A or B?  Answer with exactly one of: A, B.

worlds.title: Keyed grid intersection
worlds.question: For each QUERY pair, use KEY to replace its first badge by a row token and its second badge by a column token. Which pair lands on the gold cell in GRID? Answer 1 or 2.

worlds.title: Handed relay transport
worlds.question: One motion of the plane carries the green tile exactly onto the orange tile; call it A. One motion carries the blue tile exactly onto the cyan tile; call it B. Each of them may be a turn, a slide or a flip. Apply A to the purple dot, then apply B to where it lands. Which black square does the dot end in? The four black squares are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right. Answer with exactly one of: square-1, square-2, square-3, square-4.

worlds.title: Counterfactual patch search
worlds.question: Freeze the bit arriving at blue SAMPLE in the displayed current circuit. Release amber NOW. Then try the four violet PATCH sockets one at a time, forcing the frozen bit at that socket only. Exactly one patch recreates all four displayed outputs. Which one: patch-A, patch-B, patch-C, or patch-D?

worlds.title: Ordinal mass guarantee
worlds.question: Each CLUE says its LEFT pair is heavier than its RIGHT pair. The six colors have different whole-number masses from 1 to 9. Which TEST must also have LEFT heavier for every mass assignment fitting all seven clues? Answer test-1, test-2, test-3, or test-4.

worlds.title: Correspondence partition color
worlds.question: The gray bar at the top is divided by a dark vertical line that sits at a specific fraction of its length. Below it are three colored bars, each divided at a different fraction and shown in a different color with a different width. Which colored bar has its dark partition line at exactly the same fraction of its own length as the gray bar? Answer with that bar's color (red, green, or blue).

worlds.title: Wire bend bead spacing binding
worlds.question: Each panel shows one thin wire carrying four beads. The lower wire is the same wire as the upper one after bending: the bends changed, but the total wire length and the distance of every bead measured along the wire never changed. The wire may have been turned end for end, so the lower wire can run in either direction. The upper beads are coloured, the lower beads are all gray, and exactly one lower bead is circled in black. Which colour is that circled bead in the upper panel? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Mirror fold landmark
worlds.question: The dashed vertical line is a mirror fold. Reflect the center of the magenta diamond straight across that line, keeping the same height and the same perpendicular distance. Which colored dot has the reflected center? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Gear phase correspondence
worlds.question: Turn the left equal eight-slot gear clockwise until its magenta dot reaches the cyan top pointer. Touching gears turn the same number of slots in opposite directions. Which colored dot on the right gear reaches its cyan top pointer: red, green, blue, or orange?

worlds.title: Sum height color compare
worlds.question: Four vertical bars (two red, two blue) stand on a shared baseline. Look at the two red bars: are their heights closer to each other, or are the two blue bars' heights closer to each other? Answer the colour whose two bars are more equal in height, red or blue.

worlds.title: Disk bar clearance
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Which panel has the smaller vertical disk-to-bar clearance? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Spacing evenness lane
worlds.question: The picture shows five horizontal LANES of small upright tick marks: one red lane, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple. A lane is simply all the marks of one colour sitting on one grey rail. Every lane holds exactly the same number of marks, eight, every lane's leftmost mark starts at the same place on the page and every lane's rightmost mark ends at the same place, and every mark is drawn the same size and the same brightness. So the number of marks, the amount of coloured ink, how far a lane reaches, how wide a lane is and the average spacing of a lane are identical for all five colours and mean nothing. Take one lane at a time and look only at the seven GAPS between its neighbouring marks, measured from mark to mark along the page. Find that lane's WIDEST gap and that lane's NARROWEST gap and subtract the narrowest from the widest: that difference is how UNEVEN the lane is, and a lane whose marks are spaced almost equally gives a small difference. The answer is the colour of the lane with the SMALLEST such difference, that is, the most evenly spaced lane. No gap is marked, measured or labelled anywhere in the picture, and vertical height, the top-to-bottom order of the lanes and the left-to-right order of the marks mean nothing. Cheap readings are deliberately steered elsewhere: in every picture the lane holding the single widest gap of all, the lane holding the single narrowest gap of all and the lane with the widest opening gap each belong to a colour that is NOT the answer, and which row a lane occupies is the answer no more often than chance allows. The frame, the pale grey vertical guide lines and the grey rails are decoration and mean nothing. Which colour's lane is the most evenly spaced? Answer red, green, blue, orange or purple.

worlds.title: Pareto bubble area leader
worlds.question: A bubble is on the upper-right frontier if no other bubble is both farther right and higher. Among frontier bubbles, which has the largest visible disk area? Answer blue, orange, green, purple, or red.

worlds.title: Slopegraph rank gain
worlds.question: The legend lists series A-D from top to bottom. In each vertical column, rank the four markers from highest (rank 1) to lowest (rank 4). Subtract the AFTER rank from the BEFORE rank. Which series has the largest result? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior traffic lamps
worlds.question: This is a traffic signal. An ordinary traffic signal has exactly three lamps -- red, yellow, and green -- but report exactly what is drawn here. How many round lamps does this traffic signal actually have? Count the visible lamps and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Planet moon binding
worlds.question: How many blue planets have exactly one visible moon? Count only large blue planet circles with exactly one small moon circle on their nearby orbit; ignore orbit lines, cards, and the title. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Hillside post upright
worlds.question: This image shows one straight coloured post planted on a sloping hillside. The hillside is the large solid coloured area, and the straight line where it meets the white sky is the ground line. The grey page frame and the grey stones lying inside the hillside are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The post is always painted exactly along one of two directions, and only these two are possible. It is UPRIGHT when it is parallel to the left and right edges of the page, so that it makes the same angle with the page's top edge as those side edges do. It is SQUARE when it stands at a right angle to the ground line it is planted on, so that it leans by exactly the slope of the hillside. Which of the two it is, which way the hillside slopes, how steep the slope is, the height of the ground line, the two colours, the position of the post along the slope, and the post's length and thickness all change from image to image. Judge the direction actually painted in this image by comparing the post with the page edges and with the ground line, and do not answer from the direction a post normally has. Is the post upright or square? Answer with exactly one of the words upright or square.

worlds.title: Traffic signal top color
worlds.question: Which color is the top lamp in the traffic signal? Answer red, yellow, or green.

worlds.title: Teapot appendage opposition conflict
worlds.question: On the visible teapot, are the orange triangular spout and green loop handle attached to opposite sides of the blue body? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Texture variance reveal
worlds.question: The image is a 32x32 field of gray-noise blocks; every block has the same mean brightness, but a coarse diagonal band is hidden in the local texture: inside the band each block carries a strong checkerboard modulation, outside it a low-dispersion gray noise. Compute the local luminance VARIANCE of every block so the high-texture blocks light up and the band appears. Which diagonal band is revealed, the rising band A or the falling band B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Median rank filter reveal
worlds.question: Find the gray square just inside four colored 16x16 corner marks, with an 8-pixel gap. Replace each pixel by the median of its centered 7x7 grayscale neighborhood, using edge replication. Ignore the marks and canvas. Which broad symbol appears: fan, gate, orb, or sail? Answer with one listed word.

worlds.title: Stepwise pen trail reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one empty grid of 7 rows and 7 columns of square cells, and above the grid a list of solid triangular arrows. Exactly one cell of the grid carries a small hollow square marker: that cell is where the pen starts. Read the arrows in printed order, taking the top row of arrows first, then each next row down, and inside a row from left to right. Each arrow moves the pen exactly one cell in the direction that arrow points: up, down, left or right. Ink the starting cell and every cell the pen enters; a cell entered more than once is simply inked. The pen never leaves the grid. The inked cells form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: bracket (two horizontal bars, one along the top row and one lower down, joined at their right ends by a short vertical bar), ell (a vertical bar down the left column with a horizontal foot running right along the bottom row), plus (a horizontal bar across the middle row crossing a vertical bar down the middle column), stairs (a staircase of cells climbing from the bottom left corner to the top right corner), tee (a bar along the top row with a vertical stem hanging from its middle). Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Paired luminance decode
worlds.question: Treat each outlined left-right tone pair as one cell. Mark the cell black exactly when its left half is darker than its right half; otherwise leave it white. Which symbol does the resulting 9 by 9 grid show: plus or X?

worlds.title: Runlength strip expansion arrow
worlds.question: Inside the cyan frame, each of the nine lanes is one compressed row; ignore the gray bars outside. Read separated bars left to right: width in gold-bar lengths is run length, dark expands to dark tiles, and pale expands to blank tiles. Expand each lane to nine tiles, keep lanes top to bottom, and do not rotate or reflect. Which arrow is closest: up, right, down, or left? Closest means fewest differing tiles; ties are ambiguous and quarantined.

worlds.title: Texture energy silhouette
worlds.question: A field of random dark dots covers the canvas; inside one central region the dots are packed densely while outside they are scattered sparsely. Which shape does that denser cluster of dots outline? Choose from: circle, square, diamond, triangle.

worlds.title: Fragmented contour closure
worlds.question: Ignore any one stroke or panel location and judge the whole fragmented contour. Which color forms the most globally closed loop? Answer red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Rotation order
worlds.question: The picture shows twelve identical coloured dots and one black cross. Turn the whole picture about the centre of the cross by 360/k degrees, where k is a whole number. For some values of k every dot lands exactly on a dot, so the arrangement looks unchanged; the only values of k to consider are 2, 3, 4 and 6. What is the largest such k? Answer 2, 3, 4 or 6.

worlds.title: Texture region hole
worlds.question: The short black dashes lie on a regular grid and slant either up-right or down-right. Treat edge-neighboring grid cells with up-right dashes as one region. Does that region surround a finite group of down-right dashes, forming a hole? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Fragmented circle center
worlds.question: All four dots are candidates. The disconnected dark arcs are pieces of one circle. Which colored dot is at that circle's center? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Proximity pair oddball
worlds.question: The image is split by thin lines into four quadrants: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. Each quadrant contains two dark dots. In exactly three of the quadrants the two dots are far apart from each other; in the remaining one quadrant the two dots are very close together. Which quadrant contains the pair of dots that are the closest together? Answer with the quadrant name.

worlds.title: Triple concurrence panel
worlds.question: Thin gray lines split this image into four panels of equal size standing side by side, counted from the left. Every panel contains exactly three straight lines, one red, one green and one blue, and each line is drawn all the way across its own panel. Inside a panel every pair of lines crosses exactly once, so each panel shows three crossing points. In exactly one panel the three lines all run through one single common point, so its three crossings coincide and no triangle is visible there. In every other panel the three crossings stay apart and leave a small open triangle of white background between them. The same three colours, the same stroke width and three full-width lines appear in every panel, and the line bearings, the crossing location inside the panel and the size of each triangle are drawn independently of the answer, so colour, ink, line angle, crossing position and panel position carry no information. Judge each panel only by the three lines drawn inside it. Which half of the image contains the panel whose three lines all run through one common point, given that the first two panels form the left half and the last two form the right half? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Directed bead sequence search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has the same bead-color order as the REFERENCE when each route is followed from its teal triangle to its navy square? Route shape and spacing do not matter; A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Dual sequence search
worlds.question: Each lane contains the same four symbols. From left to right, which lane is large-small-large-small and circle-circle-square-square? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State visible swaps
worlds.question: A vertical timeline of four panels reads top to bottom. Each panel shows four slots (slot 1 to slot 4, left to right) and each slot holds one token. Every token has its own fixed color that never changes. A magenta ring in the first (top) panel marks the token you must track. Between consecutive panels, a cyan exchange mark joins two adjacent slots, meaning those two tokens swap positions as you move to the next panel. Reading the panels in order and following the swap marks, which slot does the ringed token occupy in the last (bottom) panel? Answer 'slot 1', 'slot 2', 'slot 3', or 'slot 4'.

worlds.title: Lagged leader state
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 from left to right. The LEADER row gives one state per panel. Which label's state at P2 through P6 exactly matches the LEADER state at the preceding panel P1 through P5? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Count out elimination ring
worlds.question: The picture shows a row of coloured discs standing side by side, all of them a different colour; count them, because how many discs are drawn is part of what decides the answer. The row is counted as a closed ring: counting always moves towards the right, as the grey arrow under the row shows, and after the rightmost disc still standing the count continues at the leftmost disc still standing. A single black triangle is drawn above the row: the marked disc is the disc whose centre is nearest to that triangle. The cream card at the bottom of the picture carries a number of black pips; call that number k, so k is how many pips are drawn on the card. Discs are taken away one at a time by this rule. For the first count, the marked disc is counted as one, the disc to its right is counted as two, and so on, counting k discs in all; the k-th disc counted is taken away. Every later count starts at the disc still standing that comes next to the right of the disc just taken away, counting that disc as one, and again counts k discs and takes the k-th away. Only discs still standing are ever counted: a disc that has been taken away is skipped over and is never counted again, and counting wraps from the right end of the row round to the left end as often as needed. Discs never move sideways and a disc that has been taken away never comes back. This is repeated until only one disc is left standing. The picture shows only the starting row: no disc is drawn as taken away, and neither the later rows nor the last disc is drawn anywhere in the picture. What colour is the one disc still standing at the end? Answer with one word: red, orange, yellow, green, teal, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Line push replay
worlds.question: Crates start in the four numbered bays shown; one bay is empty, and the magenta ring marks the queried crate. Read the six cards from left to right. Each card's color names a crate and its arrow gives a direction. That crate tries to move one bay. If crates are in the way, it pushes the whole touching chain one bay only when there is an empty bay before the edge; otherwise nothing moves. Which bay contains the ringed crate at the end? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Zone coverage race
worlds.question: Read panels 1 through 5 from left to right. Identify each token by its black pip count: A=1, B=2, C=3, and D=4. A token visits a zone when it appears inside that zone's BLUE, AMBER, or GREEN band. Which token is the first to have visited all three different zones at least once? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Gate opens pocket
worlds.question: The image shows a closed black ring loop drawn on a white background, with a small green dot sitting in the white pocket at the center of the ring. Two colored gate markers, one red and one blue, rest on the circular path of the ring. At exactly ONE of the two gates the ring band has a real break, an open gap where the ring is not drawn, so that the sealed central pocket connects to the outside white through that opening. At the other gate the ring is a continuous, unbroken band. If the gate at the opening were removed, the green dot could pass out of the central pocket. Look at the red and blue gates. The ring is broken at exactly one of them. Which colored gate sits at the gap in the ring? Answer with exactly red or blue.

worlds.title: Same room pair
worlds.question: The picture shows white paper with several closed black fences painted on it; fences may cross one another. A room is a piece of white paper you can walk over without ever crossing a painted black fence line; the coloured dots are painted flat on the paper and never block the way, and you may not leave the paper. Every one of the three dots - red, green and blue - lies inside the same number of fences as the other two, and exactly two of them are in one and the same room. Which two dots are in the same room: red and green, red and blue, or green and blue?

worlds.title: Spanning tree count panel
worlds.question: A spanning tree is a selection of drawn links that connects every round station without a loop. Which network has exactly 21 different spanning trees? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Marked wall two rooms
worlds.question: Does the orange wall segment have a different enclosed white room on each of its two long sides? A room is a side-connected white region cut off from the outside; corner-only contact does not join rooms. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cord middle bead
worlds.question: The gray line in this picture is one single continuous cord. It never branches, never touches itself and has exactly two loose ends. Three round beads - one red, one blue and one amber - are threaded on that cord at three different places along it. Walk along the cord itself from one loose end to the other, following every bend, and note the order in which you pass the three beads. Exactly one bead is passed second, that is, it lies between the other two beads along the cord; this middle bead is the same whichever end you start from. Straight-line distance across the picture does not matter, and a bead that looks like it sits between the other two in the picture need not be the middle one along the cord. Which bead is the middle one along the cord? Answer red, blue, or amber.

worlds.title: Crossover continuity terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green ring and follow the dark route. At each cyan crossover ring, leave by the spoke directly opposite the one you entered; do not turn onto a side spoke. Small gray dots are bends, not choices. Which colored square do you reach: orange, purple, or blue?

worlds.title: Alternating link terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green START circle, inspect each route to a colored terminal. Which terminal's five links alternate solid, dashed, solid, dashed, solid in that order? A link is the black stroke between neighboring circles. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Tickrow mirror pip read
worlds.question: The board is a plain sand-coloured surface littered with small coloured decorative marks - dots, bars, rings and squares - that mean nothing. Lying on the board are exactly three white cards with thin dark borders, all close together in one small part of the board; they never touch each other or any decorative mark, and nothing else in the picture is white. One card is clearly larger than the other two: that large card is the SEAL. The two smaller cards are the KEYS. Every one of the three cards carries, near its top, a row of exactly three short black ticks. On every card the ticks sit on the same invisible lattice of seven evenly spaced slots with the same spacing, so a tick row is fully described by the two slot gaps between its first and second tick and between its second and third tick. The seal's two gaps are never equal. Exactly one key repeats the seal's tick row SLID sideways: its two gaps, read left to right, are the seal's two gaps in the same order. The other key repeats the seal's tick row MIRRORED left to right: its two gaps, read left to right, are the seal's two gaps in the opposite order. Both keys are slid to a different starting slot from the seal's row, both carry exactly three ticks, and both carry exactly the same amount of tick ink, so ink, tick count, card size, card colour and card position tell you nothing about which key is the mirrored one. Below its tick row each key also carries a row of PIPS: between one and four small black filled squares, clearly shorter than the ticks. The two keys always carry different pip counts. The seal carries no pips. You must find the seal, compare each key's tick rhythm with the seal's, and decide which key is the mirrored one before reading its pips. How many pips does the MIRRORED key carry? Answer one, two, three or four.

worlds.title: Nested band echo
worlds.question: The gold-tabbed seal is the reference. In each seal, count navy dots in each of the three nested bands: inside the smallest ring, between the small and middle rings, and between the middle and outer ring. Dot angles may change. Which red, green, or blue tab marks the seal with the same three counts? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Bendprint correspondence
worlds.question: The black panel is the reference. One colored panel contains the same connected zigzag after any rotation or mirror flip; the other two rearrange its interior bends. Which color is the matching path? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Paired span overlap
worlds.question: For each color, divide the horizontal length shared by both bars by the full horizontal span from that pair's leftmost to rightmost endpoint. Which color has the larger fraction? Answer coral or blue.

worlds.title: Local pairing cost
worlds.question: In the local four-dot inset, define WITHIN as the center-to-center distance between the two cyan dots plus that between the two orange dots. Define CROSS as the smaller total from the two possible one-to-one cyan-orange pairings. Which total is smaller? Answer WITHIN or CROSS.

worlds.title: Continuous staff row count
worlds.question: How many long horizontal rows are in the visible music staff? Count each long row of the single continuous dark staff stroke once; ignore the short side connectors and the colored noteheads.

worlds.title: Snake staff side alternation
worlds.question: From the snake's head downward, treat each colored bulge that leaves the gray staff and returns to it as one loop. Do all four successive loops alternate left and right of the staff? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Height tab strip sort
worlds.question: Inside the violet badge are seven vertical strips. Reorder whole strips from the shortest amber height tab to the tallest, keeping every strip upright. Which glyph appears: Z, I, H, or U?

worlds.title: Hinge mirror unfold
worlds.question: Reflect the small 7-by-4 cell panel across its red hinge to make a 7-by-7 grid, keeping the hinge-side column only once. Which dark-cell symbol needs the fewest cell changes: X, arrow, or crown? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Area balance mosaic
worlds.question: The colored landmass contains exactly 42 equal square tiles joined edge-to-edge. Treat every colored tile as equal weight. Is the landmass's balance point left or right of the black center line? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Radial cadence medallion
worlds.question: The single colored medallion contains five bright circular ridges. Ignoring ridge width, compare the four center-to-center radial gaps from the center outward. Do the gaps steadily grow or steadily shrink? Answer grow or shrink.

worlds.title: Half turn center search
worlds.question: The cyan mosaic is one connected shape. Which colored pin is the center of half-turn symmetry? Rotating the entire cyan shape 180 degrees around that pin must make it cover itself exactly. Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Route mileage midpoint search
worlds.question: The gold rings mark the ends of one unbroken dark route. Measure travel distance along the route through every bend, not straight-line distance. Which colored checkpoint splits the route into two equal traveled lengths? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Stairpush corridor replay
worlds.question: Somewhere in this picture there is one corridor: a single connected staircase chain of equal square cells, one cell wide everywhere, that runs along, drops down by one cell, doubles back, drops again and runs along once more. Every pale grey mark lying outside that chain is inert decoration that means nothing. One end of the chain is capped by a solid black bar and the other end by a solid grey bar; both bars are walls. Each cell is tinted pale red, pale green, pale blue or pale yellow, and cells of the same tint always sit next to each other along the chain. In the upper half of every cell there is a floor pip: a solid black disc means step one cell away from the black bar, and a hollow black ring means step one cell towards the black bar. In the lower half of the cells there is exactly one red disc, the shover, and three solid brown squares, the crates. The floor pips are painted on the floor and never move. The replay goes like this, over and over: read the pip of the cell the shover is standing on and try to step one cell that way along the chain. If the next cell along is empty the shover moves into it. If the next cell along holds a crate, that crate is shoved one further cell the same way and the shover takes its place, but only if the cell beyond is inside the corridor and empty; otherwise nothing moves and the replay stops there. The replay also stops when the step would leave the corridor through either wall. The corridor may sit anywhere on the canvas. What is the tint of the cell the shover is resting on when the replay stops? Answer with one of red, green, blue or yellow.

worlds.title: Streak summit quilt
worlds.question: Read every tile in row order, left to right then top to bottom. Begin with a streak of 1 on the gold-outlined START tile. Each next tile adds 1 to the streak if its color matches the previous tile; otherwise reset the streak to 1. What is the largest streak reached anywhere: 3, 4, or 5?

worlds.title: Triad bridge replay
worlds.question: The left triangle shows the starting bridges: a vivid bridge is OPEN and a pale bridge is CLOSED. In the right strip, read the four commands from top to bottom: a vivid mark opens the bridge of that color and a pale mark closes it. After all four commands, can the circle vertex reach the square vertex using open bridges?

worlds.title: Removable land patch
worlds.question: Treat black and yellow as one land shape. If the yellow patch is removed, will the remaining black land split into two pieces? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Two colorable trail
worlds.question: The map has ten circular stations joined by eleven navy links. Links meet only at stations. Could you assign one of two labels to every station so that each link joins stations with different labels? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route heading reversal
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START to the red FINISH. After the first straight segment, does any later straight segment run exactly parallel to that first segment but in the opposite travel direction? Slanted segments do not count. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Paired path junction compare
worlds.question: Each panel shows a branching dark tree. Trace the unique route from the blue node to the orange node. Count only the purple junction nodes on that route where three dark corridors meet. Which panel has more—left or right?

worlds.title: Cascade replacement transition
worlds.question: The KEY legend on the left pairs every source colour with the target colour it turns into after one application of a replacement rule. The START disc shows the initial colour of a single running state. Below, the row of STEPS dots tells you how many times to apply the rule in sequence: replace the current colour by its KEY target, once for each dot. Starting from the START colour and applying the replacement rule exactly the number of times shown by the STEPS dots, what is the final colour of the running state? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Conditional permutation tape
worlds.question: The three colored tiles in START are ordered left to right. Each COMMAND card has a color chip and a + or − sign. For each card, compare its color with the current middle tile. If they match, rotate the whole three-tile row one place in the sign direction (+ = right, − = left). If they do not match, swap the adjacent pair on that side (+ swaps middle/right; − swaps left/middle). Carry the new order to the next card. Which three-letter code is active after card 7? Answer the code shown in the key.

worlds.title: State indexed rule table
worlds.question: The grid is a rule table. Each row is labelled on the left by a colored disk, and each column is labelled on top by a black shape. Start on the ringed row's color. Then read the black shapes in the bottom strip left to right: each shape moves you to the color in the cell where your current color's row meets that shape's column. Which color are you on after the last shape? Answer amber, teal, violet, or crimson.

worlds.title: Projective window transfer
worlds.question: The four colored corners match between SOURCE and WARPED VIEW. Transfer the yellow point through that perspective warp. Which cup receives it? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Flip splice tile deck
worlds.question: Repeat 8 turns. Take the left tile and read its center before flipping it. If it was LIGHT, insert it after the 2nd remaining tile. If it was DARK, insert it before the 2nd-from-right remaining tile. Keep every tile's colored identity. Which option is final? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Line weight correspondence
worlds.question: The gray horizontal stroke at the top has a certain stroke weight (its thickness from top to bottom). Below it are three colored horizontal strokes, one red, one green, one blue, each with a different thickness. Which colored stroke is exactly as thick as the gray reference stroke? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Overlay registration slot binding
worlds.question: This image has two framed panels. The upper panel is a board: it shows four dark square outlines, exactly one of which is filled light gray, and one solid black cross. The lower panel is a clear sheet: it shows four solid colored dots (one red, one blue, one green, one orange) and one solid black cross of the same size and shape. The sheet is slid straight onto the board - without rotating it, mirroring it or changing its size - until the sheet's black cross lies exactly on top of the board's black cross. Every dot moves by that same shift and by nothing else. After that shift, which colored dot is closest to the center of the light gray square? Answer with one word: red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Socket partner tag transfer
worlds.question: REFERENCE has four identity-colored sockets joined into two separate pairs by cyan connectors. The magenta ring marks one socket. LOOKUP has the same four identity colors rearranged; each socket has a colored square tag directly below it. Find the reference socket joined to the ringed socket, match its identity color in LOOKUP, and report that socket's tag color. Answer red, blue, gold, or purple.

worlds.title: Containment tree correspondence
worlds.question: REFERENCE and TARGET show the same hierarchy of directly nested boxes, but boxes inside the same parent may be rearranged. Match the magenta-dotted REFERENCE branch by the pattern of boxes it directly contains. What color is the dot on the matching TARGET branch: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Mass offset argmax
worlds.question: Three L-shaped solid regions are drawn, one red, one blue, one green, each inside its own column and all sharing one identical bounding box. A shape's center of mass (the balance point of its filled area) can sit off the center of its own bounding box. Which colored shape has its center of mass FARTHEST from the center of its own bounding box, i.e. is the most lopsided? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Arc sweep compare
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Which open arc sweeps through the larger central angle? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Decade step count
worlds.question: The picture is one chart panel with a LOGARITHMIC vertical scale. The thick dark horizontal rules are the decade rules: each thick rule stands for ten times the value of the thick rule immediately below it, and the spacing between neighbouring thick rules is the same everywhere in the panel. The thin pale horizontal rules are intermediate marks and carry no information. Standing on the bottom thick rule are four GROUPS of bars. Each group holds, from left to right, one grey bar, one coloured bar (red, green, blue or orange) and one narrow black bar. The black bars are distractors and carry no information; ignore them completely. A bar's value is read at its top edge. A group COUNTS when its coloured bar's value is more than one hundred times its own grey bar's value, which on this scale means that the coloured top stands more than two thick-rule spacings above the grey top of the same group. Two thick-rule spacings is measured on the panel itself, so it changes from picture to picture. Compare a coloured bar only with the grey bar of its own group. In every picture each coloured bar is taller than its grey partner, so height order carries no information; the tallest coloured bar need not belong to a group that counts, the bar colours and the left-to-right order of the groups carry no information, and no top sits exactly two thick-rule spacings above its partner. How many of the four groups count? Answer 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4.

worlds.title: Paired range contraction
worlds.question: From panel A to panel B, which colored row has the largest decrease in horizontal range? For a row, range is the distance from its leftmost dot to its rightmost dot. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Vector dot product leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order. Treat each colored segment from the gray origin to its same-colored endpoint dot as a vector. In which panel do the blue and orange vectors have the largest signed dot product? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior pool rack
worlds.question: This is a rack of billiard balls arranged as a pyramid on a pool table. A full billiard rack holds fifteen balls, but report exactly what is drawn here. Count the balls drawn in this rack and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Pencil tip state
worlds.question: Is the visible pencil tip pointed or flat? Treat a pointed tip as one that narrows to a single apex and a flat tip as one that ends in a vertical face. Ignore the eraser and PENCIL label. Answer pointed or flat.

worlds.title: Jar fill conservation
worlds.question: This image shows two open jars standing on the same table line, a left jar and a right jar. The page frame, the table line, the short grey ticks under it, the grey jar walls and the pale grey grid lines are fixed decoration: they never indicate the answer. The liquid in a jar is the solid coloured block that fills it from the bottom; both jars hold liquid of the same colour. Every jar interior is ruled into identical square cells, and the cells are exactly the same size in the left jar and in the right jar, so the amount of liquid in a jar is the number of coloured cells it contains, counted as width in cells times height in cells. The two jars have different widths and their liquid surfaces stand at different heights. Answer from this image alone, not from the usual expectation that whichever liquid stands higher must be the larger amount. Which jar holds more liquid? Answer with exactly one word: left or right.

worlds.title: Recycling arrow circulation
worlds.question: Which way do the three arrows circulate around the white center? Follow the orange arrowheads and answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Compass opposite label conflict
worlds.question: On the visible compass dial, which printed label is closest to directly opposite N across the red center? Answer E, S, or W.

worlds.title: Diagonal transpose reveal
worlds.question: The image is a dense 32-by-32 lattice of bright and dark cells that looks like pure noise, but the noise is exactly symmetric about the main diagonal (subtracting the transposed copy cancels the noise). A coarse diagonal-band glyph was written as an anti-symmetric brightness bias. Take the field and subtract its transpose (reflect across the main diagonal, swapping rows and columns); the surviving field is a clean single diagonal band. Which band is revealed, A or B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Registered difference glyph
worlds.question: Use the colored role marks and green corner fiducials to identify the reference and transform panels. Rotate the transform panel 180 degrees, align its corners to the reference, and take the absolute pixelwise grayscale difference of the interiors, ignoring the green marks and border. Which abstract symbol appears: triangle, ring, cross, or zigzag?

worlds.title: Notch tile derotate
worlds.question: The picture shows one square sheet ruled into a 4 by 4 grid of square tiles, with four small brightly coloured squares sitting exactly on the four corners of the sheet. Each tile is ruled into 3 by 3 equal cells and carries exactly two things: one solid dark block, which fills a two by two square of cells parked in one of the tile's four corners, and one small brightly coloured notch, which sits in the tile's border strip at the middle of exactly one of the tile's four edges. Every tile has already been turned in place about its own centre by some quarter turn, and its notch was carried around by that same turn. Undo it: turn each tile about its own centre, without moving it out of its place in the grid, until that tile's notch is back at the middle of the tile's top edge, which carries the block to a new corner of the tile. When all sixteen tiles have been turned this way, the sixteen blocks show one of these five arrangements: quads (every block sits in the corner of its tile nearest the centre of the sheet, so the blocks meet in fours to make four large solid squares, one in each quarter of the sheet), window (every block sits in the corner of its tile furthest from the centre of the sheet, so all sixteen blocks stay separate and a wide empty cross is left through the middle of the sheet), grid (every block sits at the top left corner of its own tile, making an evenly spaced array of sixteen separate blocks), bars (the blocks meet in vertical pairs, the first and second tile rows joining and the third and fourth tile rows joining, with every block against the left hand edge of its tile, making eight upright bars), dashes (the blocks meet in horizontal pairs, the first and second tile columns joining and the third and fourth tile columns joining, with every block against the top edge of its tile, making eight flat bars). A few tiles may sit on the wrong corner; take the arrangement that the sixteen turned blocks match most closely. Which arrangement do the turned blocks form? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Matched color stitch
worlds.question: Connect each pair of same-colored dots with one straight line. Which stitch symbol appears: ladder, three Xs, starburst, or braid?

worlds.title: Two tap deblur reference
worlds.question: The gold two-cell bracket shows the blur span. The cyan 9-by-9 mosaic is a horizontal two-exposure blur of one coral reference card: each displayed tile is the average of the source tile at that position and the source tile immediately to its left, using blank beyond the left edge. Undo the blur from left to right without rotating or reflecting. Which reference card is the source? Cards A, B, C, and D are arranged left to right.

worlds.title: Occluded continuation
worlds.question: A filled symbol is drawn in the middle of a white canvas, in part hidden behind three horizontal bars. Which whole symbol continues behind the bars? Choose from: circle, square, diamond, triangle.

worlds.title: Rubber band corner
worlds.question: The picture shows eighteen small round dots on a plain background. Every dot has exactly the same size and the same round shape, and no two dots touch or overlap. Fourteen of the dots are grey and four are coloured: one red, one green, one blue and one orange. Imagine stretching a rubber band around the whole group of dots and letting it snap tight, so that it forms one closed outline that encloses every one of the eighteen dots and never bends inwards. The tightened band runs straight from dot to dot and comes to rest touching only a few of them: a dot that the band touches is a corner of that outline, and every other dot lies strictly inside the outline. All eighteen dots count when the band is tightened, grey ones exactly as much as coloured ones. Exactly one of the four coloured dots is a corner of the tightened band, and the other three coloured dots lie strictly inside it. Distance from the middle of the picture does not decide the answer: a dot near the edge of the picture can still lie well inside the band, and the coloured corner dot can be closer to the middle of the picture than a coloured dot that is not a corner. The colours themselves, the dot size, the number of dots, the amount of ink and where the group sits on the page carry no information about the answer. Which coloured dot is a corner of the tightened rubber band? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Interleaved spiral arms
worlds.question: All 24 black dots trace smooth outward paths around the gray center. Group the dots by smooth outward continuation. How many interleaved spiral arms are there? Answer two or three.

worlds.title: Minimum enclosing center
worlds.question: Imagine the smallest possible circle that contains every dark dot center. Which colored ring marks that circle's center? The colored rings are candidates and do not need to be enclosed; ring size does not count. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Curved stroke oddball
worlds.question: The image is split into four quadrants (top-left, top-right, bottom-left, bottom-right). Each quadrant contains one dark stroke. A stroke is bowed when it bulges clearly out of the straight line joining its two ends; it is straight when it follows that line. Exactly three of the four strokes share the SAME form (all bowed or all straight); the fourth stroke has the opposite form. Which quadrant contains the oddly formed stroke (the one that is bowed when the other three are straight, or straight when the other three are bowed)? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Parallel pair panel
worlds.question: Thin gray lines split this image into four panels: top-left, top-right, bottom-left and bottom-right. Every panel contains four identical dark bars that differ only in position and direction. A bar's direction is the direction of its long axis, ignoring which end is which, so directions are compared modulo 180 degrees. In exactly one panel, two of the four bars have the same direction and are therefore exactly parallel. Every other pair of bars in the same panel differs in direction by at least 3 degrees. Bar colour, bar size, bar count and panel position carry no information about the answer. Which vertical half of the image contains the exactly parallel pair? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Opposite color pairs search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has matching colors at all three pairs of bead positions directly opposite each other through the center? A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Connected terminals search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has the red and blue nodes joined by one unbroken dark path? A path may pass through charcoal nodes. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State register reset
worlds.question: A horizontal track of five slot boxes is shown, read left to right as slot 1, 2, 3, 4, 5. A red marker sits in one box and an orange ring surrounds that box; it marks the START slot. Four operator boxes are read left to right; each holds one colored disk. A green disk advances the tracked register one slot to the right (+1), a blue disk retreats it one slot to the left (-1), and a magenta disk RESETs it back to the origin slot 1. The register is never shown after its start. Replaying the operators in order from the ringed start (each RESET jumps the position back to slot 1 before the next step), what is the FINAL slot of the tracked register? Answer exactly 'slot 1' through 'slot 5'.

worlds.title: State histogram signature
worlds.question: Which label shows LOW exactly 3 times, MID exactly 2 times, and HIGH exactly once across P1-P6? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Lru slot replay
worlds.question: At the top of the picture is a rack of four square slots in a row. Each slot holds one coloured disc, and the four discs drawn on the rack all have different colours. A single black triangle is drawn just under the rack: the queried slot is the rack slot whose centre is nearest to that triangle, and the triangle marks a place on the rack, never a particular disc. Below the rack is a row of cream request cards, applied one at a time in drawn left-to-right order, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries one coloured disc: that card asks for that colour. Apply each card by this rule. If the asked-for colour is already standing on the rack, nothing on the rack changes; the card only counts as a use of that colour. If the asked-for colour is not on the rack, it must be loaded onto the rack, and it takes over the slot of exactly one disc already there: the disc whose colour was least recently used, that is, the colour whose own most recent use is older than the most recent use of each of the other three colours then standing on the rack. The disc it takes over is gone from the rack, and the newly loaded colour now sits in that slot. A colour's most recent use is the last card, so far, that asked for it. A colour that no card has yet asked for counts as used before every card, in the drawn left-to-right order of the starting rack, so among such colours the one drawn in the leftmost slot is the least recently used. Loading a colour also counts as a use of it. Discs never move sideways: a slot only ever changes which colour it holds. Colours come from red, orange, blue, green and purple, and a colour that was taken over earlier may be asked for again later and then be loaded again. The rack is drawn only in its starting state: no later rack, and not the final rack, is drawn anywhere in the picture. After every card has acted in order, what colour is the disc in the queried slot? Answer with one word: red, orange, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Cyclic conveyor replay
worlds.question: The ring starts in the large 3 by 3 board. Read the five cards from left to right. Each card highlights one whole row or column; its arrow shifts every item on that highlighted line one cell in the arrow direction, wrapping around at the edge. Where does the ring finish?

worlds.title: Conditional custody relay
worlds.question: The parcel starts at the station shown on the START card. Read the transfer cards from left to right.
