On each card, the left station is the sender and the right station is the receiver. A transfer moves the parcel only when the sender currently holds it; otherwise that card does nothing. Which station holds the parcel at the end? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Contained loop select
worlds.question: The image shows two colored ring loops, one red and one blue, drawn on a white background. Exactly one of the two ring loops lies entirely inside the interior of the other ring loop: that contained ring is fully within the closed boundary of the larger ring, with a visible white gap between the contained ring's outer edge and the container ring's inner edge. The other ring is the outer loop that contains the first one, and is not inside it. Which colored ring, red or blue, is the contained inner loop -- the ring that lies entirely inside the other ring's interior? Answer with exactly red or blue.

worlds.title: Shared neighbor chambers
worlds.question: Round chambers are joined when one gray corridor directly connects them. For each color, compare the two chambers containing dots. A shared neighbor is another chamber directly joined to both. Which colored pair has exactly two shared neighbors? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Contour separator distance
worlds.question: Are the green and purple dots separated by exactly two closed dark contours? A contour separates the dots when it encloses exactly one of them. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Pipe sharpest bend
worlds.question: This picture shows exactly two grey pipes on a white page. Each pipe is one unbroken stroke built from three straight sections joined end to end, so each pipe has exactly two bends and exactly two loose ends. The two pipes never touch and never cross each other, so every stretch of grey belongs to one pipe only and you can follow either pipe from one of its loose ends to the other. A green disc covers one loose end of one of the two pipes; call that pipe the green-ended pipe. The other pipe has no green disc. There are four coloured squares, one red, one blue, one orange and one purple. Each square sits just outside exactly one bend, in the open corner on the outer side of that bend, separated from the grey stroke by a small gap, and each square is far nearer to its own pipe than to the other pipe, so a square belongs to whichever pipe runs beside it. Two of the four squares therefore mark the two bends of the green-ended pipe and the other two mark the two bends of the other pipe. A bend is sharper when the pipe changes direction there by a larger angle, that is, when the corner between its two sections is tighter; a bend is gentler when the pipe carries on more nearly straight. Only the two bends of the green-ended pipe are being compared. How the bends of the other pipe look, how long the sections are, which colours are used, where the pipes sit on the page and which square happens to lie nearest the green disc do not matter. Of the two squares that mark the bends of the green-ended pipe, which one marks the sharper bend? Answer red, blue, orange or purple.

worlds.title: Cable checkpoint order
worlds.question: Starting at the green ring and following only the continuous dark cable through the colored checkpoints, which checkpoint is encountered first: orange or purple?

worlds.title: Shared prefix terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green START circle, which pair of colored terminals shares the most initial black links before their routes split? Count links from START. Links meet only at circles and never cross. Answer red and blue, red and orange, or blue and orange.

worlds.title: Lagoon islet host bind
worlds.question: The cream board is littered with small decorative coloured squares, and exactly one square block of blue WATER sits somewhere on it: that block is the LAGOON. Only what lies inside the lagoon decides the answer; every square on the bare cream board is decoration and means nothing. Inside the lagoon there are exactly three large solid square ISLANDS, each a single colour drawn from red, blue, green and purple, and the three islands have three different colours. Two of the islands each have one LAKE cut into them: a smaller square of the same blue water, completely surrounded by that island's colour. The third island has no lake. The lagoon also carries several small coloured PATCHES, all about the same size as each other. Some patches float directly on the open lagoon water, some are painted on the body of an island, and exactly one patch - the ISLET - lies inside a lake, completely surrounded by water that is itself completely surrounded by an island. So the islet is the only patch you reach by stepping board, lagoon, island, lake, patch. The islet's own colour is always different from the colour of the island that holds its lake, and patch colours, patch sizes, island sizes and island positions carry no other information. What colour is the island whose lake contains the islet? Answer red, blue, green or purple.

worlds.title: Area ledger atlas
worlds.question: The four mosaics belong to one uninterrupted navy atlas; if its central bridge is broken, the ledger is unreadable. The gold-framed mosaic is the reference. Tile positions may be rearranged. A candidate matches only when each of the four fill colors covers exactly the same number of square cells as in the reference. Which red, green, or blue frame marks the match?

worlds.title: Window census correspondence
worlds.question: The 3-by-3 tile board at left is the SOURCE. Its four overlapping 2-by-2 windows are top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. Count the dark tiles in each window. Each colored candidate at right shows four blue pip groups in that same 2-by-2 order. Which color frames the candidate whose four counts are all correct? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Terrace width change
worlds.question: The teal specimen has three horizontal tiers: top, middle, and bottom. Which absolute change in width is larger: top-to-middle or middle-to-bottom? Answer top-to-middle or middle-to-bottom.

worlds.title: Local whisker overlap
worlds.question: Do the vertical spans of the two colored capped uncertainty whiskers overlap or touch? Treat each span as the closed interval from its upper cap to its lower cap. Answer YES or NO.

worlds.title: Clover leaf lobe count
worlds.question: How many large rounded leaf lobes does the single clover have? Count the lobes around the center; do not count the short stem.

worlds.title: Yin yang field area
worlds.question: Inside the large dark circular outline, which visible color covers more total area—teal, amber, or exactly the same? Count the two small opposite-color dots as part of their colors and ignore the small gray marks outside.

worlds.title: Paired leg zigzag
worlds.question: Follow the single navy zigzag from the amber triangle to the teal circle. Its 50 straight legs form 25 consecutive two-leg teeth. For each tooth, make a dark square when its first leg is longer than its second; otherwise make a light square. Write the 25 squares into a 5 by 5 tile, left-to-right and top-to-bottom. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Paired slant agreement
worlds.question: Rotate each framed 6 by 6 stitch card until its magenta corner is upper left. Compare corresponding cells and make a result cell dark exactly when the two short strokes lean the same way. Which result pattern needs the fewest cell changes to match: H, diamond, or box? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Route bend echo
worlds.question: The colored route crosses the small ring at its midpoint. Read the four equal-width large bends from the left end toward the ring, then the four from the ring toward the right end. Compare each bend's distance from the straight baseline through the bend boundaries. Does the right-side sequence repeat the bend sizes in the same order, or in reverse order? Answer same or reverse.

worlds.title: Halfturn landmass
worlds.question: The colored landmass is made from whole cells of the faint 11 by 11 board. After a 180-degree turn about the board center, would exactly the same cells be colored? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Bridge island search
worlds.question: Which panel contains one connected cyan island rather than two separate cyan islands? Answer upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, or lower-right.

worlds.title: Ordered branch rail search
worlds.question: Four colored rails are shown. Read each rail from left to right. Which rail has four short side branches in this exact order: above, below, above, below? Exactly one matches. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Doublet run ribbon
worlds.question: Start with the lamp OFF. Follow the connected ribbon from the round START to the arrow. Group consecutive spans of the same color into runs. Whenever a run ends, flip the lamp exactly when that run contains two spans; include the final run at the arrow. Is the lamp ON? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Orthogonal bloom replay
worlds.question: Colored squares are ON and pale squares are OFF. The orange-framed center is the tracked cell, and the six orange beads mean six rounds. In every round, update all squares simultaneously: a square is ON next exactly when one of its four edge-sharing neighbors was ON; otherwise it is OFF. Beyond the board counts as OFF. After six rounds, is the tracked center ON or OFF?

worlds.title: Contact hub degree
worlds.question: Edge-sharing counts as touching; corner contact does not. Does the yellow hub touch all three separate black islands? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Outside boundary tile
worlds.question: A broad teal sheet contains two solid colored boundary tiles. Exactly one colored tile borders the outside white background; the other borders an enclosed white pocket. Which tile borders the outside: amber or purple? White areas connect through shared edges, not diagonal corners. Answer amber or purple.

worlds.title: Relay trace terminal
worlds.question: Begin at the green START and follow its navy trail to a cyan or orange relay. Then find the other relay of that same color and follow its separate navy trail. Which FINISH does it reach: magenta or yellow?

worlds.title: Route multiplicity compare
worlds.question: Each window has a blue start ring and an orange finish ring. Count the separate unbroken dark routes that connect its blue ring to its orange ring; ignore dark strokes that reach only one ring. Which window has more connecting routes: left or right?

worlds.title: Chimeric code binding
worlds.question: At the top a key has four rows; each row shows a coloured dot on the left and a shape on the right, so the key pairs colours with shapes.  Below are two columns of four slots: every left slot shows one coloured dot, every right slot shows one shape, and every slot has a marker below it that is either a filled dark square or an open square.  Bind each left slot to the right slot whose shape the key pairs with that slot's colour. A pair is TRUE when the two bound slots show the same marker kind.  How many true pairs are there: zero, one, two, three, or four?

worlds.title: Serial axis reflection
worlds.question: Four tiles are labeled A-D. Each tile has a solid token, a violet dashed line, a gold dashed line, and a hollow target. Reflect the token across the violet line, then across the gold line. Which tile's target is the result?

worlds.title: Chain link interlock
worlds.question: Every loop is a stiff wire. Where two wires cross, the wire drawn with a break passes behind the other. Exactly one colored loop is chained through the black loop, so those two cannot be pulled apart without cutting a wire. Which colored loop is it? Answer green, orange, or violet.

worlds.title: Odd link network
worlds.question: Overlay all three maps. A link stays only if it appears on an odd number of maps; a link shown twice cancels. Which terminal is connected to START: A, B, C, or D?

worlds.title: Scale equation inference
worlds.question: The top three rows balance exactly. Each letter has one fixed weight. Use all three balances. In the QUESTION row, which side is heavier? Answer left, right, or same.

worlds.title: Correspondence signed offset
worlds.question: The gray rail at the top has a dark rider dot sitting a fixed perpendicular distance away, either above or below the rail. Below it are three colored rails A, B, C (red, green, blue), each with its own rider dot. Which colored rail's rider dot is offset from its rail by exactly the same signed distance (same side and same amount) as the gray reference rider dot? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Ring cut code transfer
worlds.question: The upper panel shows a row of twelve upright gray bars of unequal height, with a colored square directly under each bar. The lower panel shows the same twelve items as gray spokes sticking out of a ring around a small gray hub, and a black dot sits just beyond the tip of exactly one spoke. The row is the ring cut open at one spoke and laid out flat: reading the ring clockwise starting from that spoke and continuing all the way around gives the bars from left to right. Which spoke the cut starts at is not shown and is not marked. The ring is never read counterclockwise and the pattern is never mirrored. The ring may be drawn at a different overall size than the row, and every spoke is scaled by that same single factor, so only the pattern of relative lengths is shared between the panels, never the absolute lengths, the angles or the positions. Each of the four square colors is used exactly three times, so no color by itself picks out a bar. Work out which bar in the row is the same item as the spoke carrying the black dot. What is the color of the square under that bar? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Colored chord crossing
worlds.question: Each panel has four straight chords, each identified by the matching color of its two endpoint dots. Chord positions may rotate or reflect. Which colored border surrounds the option where exactly the same pairs of chord colors cross as in the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Grid vector transfer correspondence
worlds.question: REFERENCE shows a move from the cyan ring to the yellow dot. Apply exactly the same row change and column change to the magenta-ringed cell in TARGET, without wrapping at an edge. What color dot is at the destination: red, green, blue, or orange?

worlds.title: Bicolored rank reversal
worlds.question: This two-panel plot shows a red and a blue vertical bar in each panel, all resting on one baseline. Exactly one color is the tallest bar in the left panel and the shortest bar in the right panel. Which color flips rank that way? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Threshold span compare
worlds.question: Panel A is the left plot and panel B is the right plot. Each colored trace is piecewise-linear over the same horizontal width, and the dashed horizontal line is the threshold. Which panel has the larger fraction of its width where the trace lies strictly above the threshold? Choose A or B.

worlds.title: Common cover cells
worlds.question: The picture shows one horizontal RAIL near the bottom, drawn as a dark grey line crossed by short dark grey TICKS. The ticks are evenly spaced, the leftmost tick sits at the left end of the rail and the rightmost tick at its right end, and consecutive ticks cut the rail into equal UNIT CELLS. Above the rail stand five solid horizontal BARS, one red, one green, one blue, one orange and one purple, each drawn in its own row. A bar COVERS the stretch of rail lying directly beneath it, from the vertical line through its left end to the vertical line through its right end; how high up its row is drawn means nothing. The COMMON STRETCH is the part of the rail covered by all five bars at once, so it begins at the RIGHTMOST of the five left ends and ends at the LEFTMOST of the five right ends. The common stretch is never drawn and no single bar marks it: one bar fixes its beginning and a DIFFERENT bar fixes its end. A unit cell is counted only if the whole cell lies inside the common stretch, both of its ticks included; a cell that is only partly inside is not counted. No bar end ever lands on a tick. Every bar covers strictly more whole unit cells than the common stretch does, so the shortest bar never gives the answer. Pale grey vertical lines may show between the rows; they are decoration and mean nothing. Which bar begins the common stretch, which bar ends it, the colours of those two bars, how long each bar is, which row each bar occupies, and where along the rail the common stretch lies are each the answer no more often than chance allows. How many unit cells lie completely inside the common stretch? Answer 2, 3, 4 or 5.

worlds.title: Checkpoint median target
worlds.question: Each color has five circular checkpoints. Sort a color's checkpoints by height and use the middle (third) height. Which color's median height is closest to the magenta dashed target line? Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Group centroid separation
worlds.question: In each panel, treat every dot as equal weight. Which panel has the greatest straight-line distance between the centroid (average position) of the blue dots and the centroid of the orange dots? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior pizza whole
worlds.question: A whole pizza is a complete, unbroken round disk of dough and toppings with no slice missing. Look at this pizza. Is it a complete circle (all of it present) or does it have a missing slice (a wedge-shaped gap cut out)? Report exactly what is visible and answer complete or missing.

worlds.title: Star point count
worlds.question: How many outward points does the visible star have? Count each sharp outward tip once; ignore the background. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Face mouth bulge
worlds.question: This picture shows one head drawn as a large solid light-coloured disc on a plain light background. Inside the head there are exactly three dark marks: two small solid round dots, which are the eyes, and one long curved stroke, which is the mouth. The thin grey outline of the head, the thin grey frame near the edge of the picture and any short grey ticks are decoration and never indicate the answer. Now imagine the straight line that joins the two ends of the mouth stroke: the middle of the mouth stroke lies to one side of that straight line, and that is the side it bulges to. The head is drawn at an arbitrary rotation, so the eyes may appear below, beside or above the mouth on the page, and the head's size, position and colours, the size and spacing of the eyes, and the length and thickness of the mouth stroke all change from picture to picture. The face need not be drawn the way faces are usually drawn. Read only what is painted in this picture and do not answer from how faces usually look. Does the middle of the mouth stroke bulge toward the eyes or away from the eyes? Answer with exactly one of: toward, away.

worlds.title: Capital e spine side
worlds.question: On which side of this blue capital E are all three horizontal arms joined by one long vertical spine? Use image directions and answer left or right.

worlds.title: Map pin tip direction conflict
worlds.question: In the large blue map-pin symbol, which direction does its single pointed outer tip face: up or down? Ignore the small colored corner marks and the pale circular hole. Answer up or down.

worlds.title: Centro rotate reveal
worlds.question: The image is a dense 32-by-32 lattice of bright and dark cells that looks like pure noise, but the noise is exactly symmetric about a 180-degree rotation (subtracting the rotated copy cancels the noise). A coarse diagonal-band glyph was written as an anti-symmetric brightness bias. Take the field and subtract its 180-degree-rotated copy; the surviving field is a clean diagonal band. Which glyph is revealed, A (rising /) or B (falling \)? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Fold overlay symbol
worlds.question: Reflect the right marked panel across the visible center fold, average paired pixels, and read the broad symbol. Is it anchor, fork, loop, or bolt?

worlds.title: Corner mark integral reveal
worlds.question: The image shows one square panel enclosed by a thick border and ruled into an 11 by 11 grid of square cells. Exactly one of the four border corners is drawn as a filled thickened block; that is the marked corner, and the cell of the grid touching it is the marked corner cell. A few cells carry a filled round dot. Now build a new 11 by 11 pattern on the same grid with this rule: ink a cell of the new pattern when the rectangular block of cells that runs from the marked corner cell to that cell, taking every row between their two rows and every column between their two columns and including both, contains an odd number of dots; leave that cell blank when the block contains an even number of dots. Apply the rule to all 121 cells, keeping the panel in the orientation shown. The inked cells of the new pattern form a shape that most closely matches one of these five symbols: arch (a bridge: two upright legs joined by a bar along the bottom, open at the top), bars (two separate horizontal bars, one near the top and one near the bottom), ring (a hollow rectangular frame, filled on all four sides), tee (a horizontal bar along the top with a vertical stem hanging from its middle), zed (two offset blocks forming a Z-like step, the upper block shifted to the left and the lower block shifted to the right). Which symbol is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Mirror fold intersection
worlds.question: Fold the right grid left across the magenta hinge without rotating or resizing it. Keep a cell only when it is dark in both layers. Which symbol appears: circle, diamond, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Quincunx parity arrow
worlds.question: The gold key marks the center and four corners of a 3-by-3 stencil. Slide it over every 3-by-3 block of the framed 13-by-13 mosaic, making an 11-by-11 result. Mark a result cell dark exactly when an odd number of the five marked source tiles are dark. Preserve row and column order. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Radial density regime
worlds.question: Across the whole canvas the dark dots are distributed radially. Are the dots packed tightly toward the centre (a solid core), with the rim spread thin? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Grain density bearing
worlds.question: The picture shows a plain light square sprinkled all over with small grey specks. Every speck is a disc of exactly the same size and exactly the same grey, and no speck touches another, so the specks differ only in where they sit. The specks are not spread evenly: their crowding rises steadily along one straight direction across the picture, so the side of the picture that this direction points to carries the most specks per unit of area and the opposite side carries the fewest. There is no drawn line, no shading, no outline and no change of speck size or colour marking this direction; only the changing crowding shows it. Four coloured discs - red, green, blue and orange - are placed at four different places on one circle centred on the middle of the picture, and all four are the same size. Take the direction that runs from the middle of the picture toward the crowded side of the speck field. Exactly one of the four coloured discs lies closer to that direction, measured as an angle seen from the middle of the picture, than any of the other three. The colours of the discs, which disc sits where on the circle, the number of specks, the size of the specks and the total amount of ink carry no information about the answer. Which coloured disc lies closest in direction to the crowded side of the speck field? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Occluded checker phase
worlds.question: The black dots occupy alternating cells of one regular square grid, with a gray screen hiding a middle band of grid cells. Do the visible patterns on the two sides continue as the same checker phase behind the screen, or switch to the opposite phase? Answer same or opposite.

worlds.title: Fragmented side constellation
worlds.question: Exactly 60 separate dark dashes lie along the straight sides of one implied regular polygon. Group collinear dashes across gaps and count the supporting side-lines, not the dashes. How many sides does the polygon have: 3, 4, 5, or 6?

worlds.title: Contour match clutter sector
worlds.question: A dark reference line is drawn inside the grey box at the top of the image. Thin grey lines split the rest of the image into four sectors: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. Every sector contains several small dark line fragments (the clutter). Exactly one sector contains a fragment that is an exact copy of the reference line; the fragments in the other three sectors are all differently shaped. Which sector contains the exact reference line? Answer with one sector name.

worlds.title: Twin glyph panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly four solid flat glyphs, each printed in its own colour, and all twenty glyphs in the image cover exactly the same amount of area, so ink, size, glyph count and colour carry no information. In every panel the four glyphs come from exactly two outline families, two glyphs from each family, so in every panel some outline shape is repeated. A glyph is only ever printed upright or turned by a quarter, a half or three quarters of a full turn, and it is never mirrored. Two glyphs count as twins only if they have the same outline family and the same turn, so that one of them could be slid over the other and cover it exactly; their colours and their places in the panel never have to agree, and the twins are always printed in two different colours. In exactly one panel a pair of twins is present. In each of the other four panels the two glyphs of each family are turned by different amounts, and no pair of glyphs there could be slid into agreement: at least a fifth of the two glyphs' combined area would still fail to overlap. Which numbered panel contains a pair of twin glyphs, that is two glyphs of the same outline family printed at the same turn? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Broken rhythm search
worlds.question: Which panel has an uneven spacing rhythm? Every panel has seven identical vertical dashes with the same first and last dash. In three panels all neighboring gaps are equal; in one panel a wider gap is compensated by a narrower gap. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Even parity grid search
worlds.question: Which labeled grid has an even number of dark squares in every row and every column? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State atomic change
worlds.question: Two panels sit side by side: panel A on the left and panel B on the right. Each panel shows the same four disks -- red, green, blue, and purple -- at the same fixed positions, read left to right. A disk is either hollow (an outline ring) or filled (a solid disk). Exactly one disk changes its fill state between panel A and panel B; all other disks are identical in the two panels. Which colour is the single changed disk? Answer with its colour: red, green, blue, or purple.

worlds.title: State rank inversion
worlds.question: Read panels P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, and P6 from left to right. Each panel contains the same four labeled tokens A, B, C, and D, but their row positions may be shuffled. Each token shows one state from the ordered STATE KEY: LOW < MID < HIGH < PEAK. For each adjacent arrow, compare every pair of labels: a pair is a rank reversal if its state ordering changes from one panel to the next. Which arrow has the most pairwise state-rank reversals? Exactly one arrow wins. Answer P1->P2, P2->P3, P3->P4, P4->P5, or P5->P6.

worlds.title: Recolour rule replay
worlds.question: The upper row of five squares is the starting board. Exactly one board square is drawn inside a heavy black frame; that framed square is the one the question is about. Below the board is a row of white cards, and each card holds two coloured swatches with a small arrow pointing from the left swatch to the right one. Each card is a recolouring rule: every board square whose colour is the card's left colour becomes the card's right colour, and every other board square is left exactly as it is. The cards act on the board one at a time, in the order they are drawn from left to right, as the long arrow under the card row shows. A rule that matches nothing when its turn comes changes nothing, and a square that a rule has already recoloured can be recoloured again by a later rule. Every colour in the picture is one of red, amber, green or blue. The board after the cards have acted is not drawn anywhere in the picture. What colour is the framed square after every card has acted? Answer with one word: red, amber, green or blue.

worlds.title: Conditional skip program
worlds.question: The lamps start as shown. Read the cards from left to right. A green FLIP card toggles the dot-numbered lamp. An orange SKIP card checks the dot-numbered lamp: if it is ON, do not execute the next card; if it is OFF, continue normally. After a skipped card, continue with the following card. Is the magenta-ringed lamp ON or OFF at the end?

worlds.title: Recency access replay
worlds.question: The four tiles start in the recency rack from LEAST RECENT on the left to MOST RECENT on the right. Identify a tile by its black pip count: A=1, B=2, C=3, D=4. Read the eight ACCESS cards from left to right. On each card, the named tile moves exactly one slot toward MOST RECENT by swapping with its right neighbor; if it is already in the rightmost slot, nothing changes. Which tile is LEAST RECENT after all eight cards? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Figure signature match
worlds.question: A reference dark shape is shown near the top, and three dark candidate shapes are shown below (left, centre, right). For each shape count (a) how many separate dark pieces it is made of, and (b) how many sealed white holes are walled off inside it. A candidate matches the reference exactly when both of those counts are the same. Which candidate matches the reference's counts? Answer with exactly one of left, centre, or right.

worlds.title: Paired holes shared component
worlds.question: Each colored dot lies in a separate enclosed white hole. Which same-colored pair of holes is enclosed by the same connected black piece? Black areas connect only when they touch; corner-only contact does not count. Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Room pairing doors
worlds.question: The map contains eight enclosed white rooms and seven orange doorways. Each orange doorway joins the two rooms on its long sides; black walls and corner-only contact do not join rooms. Can all eight rooms be divided into four pairs so that the two rooms in every pair share an orange doorway, with each room used exactly once? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Panel occluded terminal
worlds.question: This picture shows three grey pipes on a white page and three solid grey panels lying on top of them. A panel is opaque, so wherever a pipe runs behind a panel it is hidden. Each pipe runs from a small black dot on the left edge to a coloured square on the right edge; one pipe ends at the blue square, one at the orange square and one at the purple square. A pipe never bends behind a panel: behind a panel it is one straight run that carries on in exactly the direction it had when it went in, and it comes out heading the same way. Pipes cross each other only behind a panel; wherever you can see them they never touch. One black dot is circled by a black ring. How high a pipe starts, how high a square sits and how near the ring a square looks do not matter; only which pipe joins to which square counts. Follow the pipe that starts at the ringed dot. Which coloured square is at its far end? Answer blue, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Directed arrow terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green node, follow dark links only in the direction of their cyan arrowheads. Which colored square can you reach: red, orange, or purple?

worlds.title: Route cut checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green START circle, move from circle to circle along black links until reaching the purple FINISH circle. Which colored checkpoint lies on every possible route? A link counts only when one continuous black stroke touches both circle outlines; links meet only at circles and never cross elsewhere. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Joinboard pip relay bind
worlds.question: The board carries small coloured squares that are decoration and mean nothing. Only three things decide the answer: two white panels with dark borders, and one small square that is drawn inside a thick black frame on the bare board. The framed square is the TOKEN; its own colour is red, blue, green or purple, and no other square on the bare board has a black frame. Each white panel holds exactly four rows. In one panel, called the TAG panel, every row has a coloured block on its left and a group of black dots on its right; its four block colours are red, blue, green and purple in some order. In the other panel, called the SLOT panel, every row has a group of black dots on its left and a coloured block on its right; its four block colours are orange, teal, pink and brown in some order. Inside each panel separately the four dot groups hold one, two, three and four dots, each count appearing exactly once. Read the answer in two steps and in this order. First, in the TAG panel find the row whose coloured block is the same colour as the TOKEN, and note how many dots that row holds. Second, in the SLOT panel find the row holding that same number of dots. That SLOT row is the OUTPUT row. Dot counts are the only link between the two panels: do not pair rows by their position in the panel, by how near they are drawn to each other, or by colour, and the TOKEN's colour never appears inside the SLOT panel. What colour is the coloured block of the OUTPUT row? Answer orange, teal, pink or brown.

worlds.title: Alternating deal badge
worlds.question: Read the six beads in the gray ribbon from left to right. Deal beads 1, 3, and 5 into the top row and beads 2, 4, and 6 into the bottom row, preserving order. Which colored tag marks the exact two-row result?

worlds.title: Rank relay correspondence
worlds.question: The left card and right card each rank the circle, square, and triangle by bar length (shortest = rank 1, longest = rank 3). Exactly one shape has the same rank on both cards. What color tag is beside that shape on the right card? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Specimen bbox occupancy
worlds.question: Does the colored specimen cover more area than the unfilled part of its tight axis-aligned bounding rectangle? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Dual ruler calibration
worlds.question: Each ruler's adjacent ticks are one unit apart. Starting from its bottom tick as zero, interpolate the orange marker's height in local tick intervals. Which ruler shows the larger reading? Answer LEFT or RIGHT.

worlds.title: Ecg largest spike direction
worlds.question: In the single colored ECG trace, does the largest visible excursion from its flat baseline point upward? Follow the connected trace and answer yes or no from the image.

worlds.title: Figure eight crossing count
worlds.question: How many self-crossings are visible in the single colored practice trace? Count only places where four colored arms meet, and answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Detached ruler crop
worlds.question: The top ruler marks exactly two columns to delete from the 7 by 7 board, and the left ruler marks exactly two rows to delete. Delete every row or column aligned with a filled ruler cell, then close the gaps without changing the remaining order. Which 5 by 5 symbol remains: plus, X, T, or L?

worlds.title: Annular cell unfurl
worlds.question: Inside the small cyan annulus, begin at the magenta notch. Read the five wedge sectors clockwise as columns and the five bands from outside inward as rows, flattening each curved cell without changing whether it is dark or light. Which symbol is closest by cell changes: hook, bolt, or fork? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Implied circle arclets
worlds.question: Treat the three blue arc fragments as separate pieces. Allow at most four pixels of radial mismatch: do their midlines continue around one common circle? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Chord side trail
worlds.question: Follow the entire dark trail and imagine the straight chord joining its two visible ends. Does the trail interior stay on one side of that chord, or visit both sides? Answer one side or both sides.

worlds.title: Turn bisector search
worlds.question: Follow the black cord from the cyan start to the magenta end. Which colored checkpoint has the same number of right-angle corners before it as after it? Count only corners of the cord, not the checkpoint circles. Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Turn balance checkpoint search
worlds.question: Starting at the gold START ring, follow the unbranched dark route. Keep separate totals of left and right bends. At each colored checkpoint, include the bend at that checkpoint. Which checkpoint is the unique one where the two totals are equal? Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Binary odometer dispatch
worlds.question: The distant gold START card shows a two-bit counter: the left lamp is the 2s bit and the right lamp is the 1s bit; dark means 1 and hollow means 0. Read the four command cards in row order, left to right then top to bottom. Cyan adds 1 and coral subtracts 1. Carry or borrow between the lamps, wrapping after 11 to 00 and before 00 to 11. What two-bit pattern remains: 00, 01, 10, or 11?

worlds.title: Threaded mod3 register
worlds.question: Begin with remainder 0 at the green ring. Follow the single blue thread to the red ring and read the round beads in thread order. A filled bead is bit 1 and a hollow bead is bit 0. At each bead update the remainder to the remainder of (2 times the current remainder plus the bit) after division by 3. After the last bead, what is the remainder: 0, 1, or 2?

worlds.title: Courtyard boundary match
worlds.question: The teal, yellow, cyan, and orange pixels form one solid sheet. White regions connect only through shared edges; corner touching does not connect them. Which patch—cyan or orange—shares an edge with the same enclosed white courtyard as the yellow patch?

worlds.title: Shared loop pair
worlds.question: Do the green and orange stations lie together on at least one simple closed loop in the navy trail? A loop follows trail links and visits no station twice except its start; links meet only at circular stations. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Paired bend sum parity
worlds.question: Trace both separate navy routes. Across the two routes together, is the total number of bends odd or even?

worlds.title: Route axis tally
worlds.question: Starting at the blue circle, follow the single navy route to the orange square. Add the centerline lengths of all horizontal straight runs, and separately add the centerline lengths of all vertical straight runs. Which total is longer: horizontal or vertical? Count every run once and ignore the endpoint markers and pale gray dashes.

worlds.title: Counterfactual hinge proximity
worlds.question: Turn the teal arm 90 degrees clockwise around the gold pivot. After the turn, which target is closer to the arm tip: red, blue, or tie? Answer one word.

worlds.title: Ledge shade reveal
worlds.question: Light falls straight down this picture from above. Every ledge sticks out to the right from the dark wall; the yellow part of a ledge is the part the light reaches, and a ledge drawn all grey stands wholly in the shadow of the ledges above it. Five ledges carry a black tag, numbered 1 to 5 from the top. Take away exactly one tagged ledge, leave every other ledge where it is, and count the wholly shadowed ledges that then catch some light. Which tagged ledge frees the most shadowed ledges? Answer with the tag number alone: 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Board then token flip
worlds.question: Rotate the whole START board 90 degrees clockwise, so arrows move and turn with it. Then mirror each arrow itself left-to-right inside its current cell; do not move the cells. Which RESULT panel is correct? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Piecewise barycentric relay
worlds.question: On each card, each bead uses the FROM triangle containing its cell. Corners match by color; keep the bead's same fractional weights at those three corners in the matching TO triangle. Apply cards 1 then 2. Which option is final? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Correspondence aspect color
worlds.question: The gray rectangle at the top has a specific aspect ratio (its width divided by its height). Below it are three colored rectangles A, B, C: one is red, one green, one blue, and each has a different aspect ratio. Which colored rectangle has exactly the same aspect ratio as the gray rectangle? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Wire port completion
worlds.question: Each option has two terminals of each color. Trace the three dark wires. Which option has matching colors at both ends of every wire? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Contour patch correspondence
worlds.question: The context card has a square gap crossed by three colored contours. Which patch, A, B, or C, completes the gap so every contour meets the same color at both seams with no jump in position or direction?

worlds.title: More collinear color
worlds.question: A light panel holds exactly three red dots and exactly three blue dots. Each colour's three dots sit near a line, but some bend off it more than others. Which colour's three dots lie most nearly on a single straight line, meaning the smallest deviation from perfect collinearity (the least bend in the three-dot row)? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Middle rank checkpoint
worlds.question: The visible legend names three piecewise-linear traces A, B, and C. At which marked checkpoint T1 through T6 is trace A strictly between traces B and C in height? Use the marker heights at the checkpoints, not crossings between them. Exactly one checkpoint qualifies; choose T1, T2, T3, T4, T5, or T6.

worlds.title: Running total crossing
worlds.question: The chart shows five colored bars standing on one common baseline: red, orange, green, blue and purple, in some left-to-right order. The horizontal gray gridlines are exactly one unit apart, so a bar's value is its height measured in gridline units. Bar widths and bar positions carry no information. Read the bars from left to right and keep a running total of their values. The crossing bar is the first bar at which this running total reaches at least half of the total of all five bars. Which color is the crossing bar? Answer red, orange, green, blue or purple.

worlds.title: Relative uncertainty leader
worlds.question: Which colored estimate has the largest relative uncertainty? For each row, divide the full width of its capped interval by the horizontal distance from the dashed zero line to its circular center marker. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Largest step drop
worlds.question: All four colored step curves have the same total vertical decline. Which curve has the largest single vertical drop between adjacent horizontal plateaus? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior centipede legs
worlds.question: This is a centipede. The word 'centipede' literally means hundred-legged, and ordinary centipedes have many legs, but report exactly what is drawn here. Count the legs actually drawn on this centipede and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Radial fan blade count
worlds.question: How many blades does the visible electric fan have? Count each separate blade once; ignore the hub, cage, and label. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Dial scale direction
worlds.question: This image shows one round gauge dial. The grey page frame, the four short grey corner ticks, the grey rim circle, the grey hub at the centre and the grey pointer are fixed decoration: the pointer's direction is sampled independently of everything else and never indicates the answer. The readings of the dial are the coloured dots printed just inside the rim. They form exactly five separate groups spaced around the rim, and the groups are always the same five sizes: one dot, two dots, three dots, four dots and five dots. A group is a run of dots that are close together, and the blank arc between two neighbouring groups is always wider than the gap between two dots of the same group. The five groups are arranged so that their sizes ascend steadily as you travel around the rim in one rotational direction, and descend as you travel the other way; which rotational direction that is changes from image to image, as do the dot colour, the dot size, the position of the groups around the rim, the dial's centre and radius, and the pointer. Judge the direction as it appears on the page, where clockwise runs from the top of the dial to its right side. Read the groups you can actually see in this image, and do not answer from the direction a dial or a clock face usually runs. Travelling around the rim from the one-dot group to the two-dot group to the three-dot group and on to the five-dot group, which way are you going? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Snowman body sections
worlds.question: How many separate white circular snow sections are visibly stacked between the ground and the hat? Count each large outlined white circle once; ignore the face, buttons, arms, hat, and small snowflakes. Answer 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Eight hole prior conflict
worlds.question: The large dark figure is shaped like an 8. How many completely enclosed light holes are visible inside it? Count only light regions fully surrounded by dark ink. Answer with 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Ensemble average reveal
worlds.question: The image holds four independent, independently-noised exposures of the same faint two-tone symbol, multiplexed into one field at the column level: column j belongs to exposure j mod 4, so no exposure is ever contiguous and the symbol is invisible in direct view. De-interleave the four exposures by their column phase and average them element-wise; the shared symbol bias accumulates while the independent noise averages away. Which symbol is revealed, the filled circle (A) or the filled square (B)? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Delta integrated emblem
worlds.question: Find the grayscale square bounded by four colored corner marks. The square stores each row as left-to-right gray residuals: keep the first gray value, then replace every later value g by the previous restored value plus (g minus mid-gray 128). Apply a 9 by 9 edge-replicated mean to the restored square, ignore the marks and outer edge, and read the broad symbol: loop, spear, wave, or crown?

worlds.title: Column settle reveal
worlds.question: The picture shows one framed panel ruled into 9 columns and 8 rows of square places; a place is either printed dark or left empty. Let every dark square fall straight down inside its own column, keeping its column, until it rests on the floor of the panel or on top of another fallen square, so each column ends as one solid stack resting on the floor and no square ever moves sideways or between columns. The nine stack heights then form an outline that most closely matches one of these five named profiles: comb, whose stacks alternate tall, short, tall, short across the panel; peak, whose stacks rise to a single tall middle column and fall away evenly on both sides; ramp, whose stacks climb steadily from an empty column at the left to a full column at the right; table, which is one flat wide plateau with a single short stack at each outer end; and valley, whose stacks are tall at both outer ends and fall to an empty middle column. Match by the smallest total difference between the nine stack heights and the profile. Which profile is it? Answer with one word.

worlds.title: Cross parity reveal
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 12 by 12 grid, form a new grid. For each cell, count the black cells among itself and its up, down, left, and right side-neighbors; outside the grid counts as white. Make the new cell black when that count is odd, otherwise white. Which symbol appears: flag, hook, bolt, or cup?

worlds.title: Polar annulus reference match
worlds.question: The annulus is an 8-by-8 tile grid wrapped into a ring. Cut at the gold spoke, unwrap clockwise into columns, and read the circular bands from outside to inside as rows. Do not rotate or reflect the result. Which reference card below matches the dark-tile pattern? The cards are A, B, C, and D from left to right.

worlds.title: Constellation interior dot
worlds.question: A set of small dark dots is drawn on a white canvas. Taken together the outermost dots outline a convex figure: the convex hull of the whole set. Is there a dot lying strictly inside the convex outline formed by the outermost dots? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Fragmented ring center
worlds.question: The short black curved dashes are fragments of three hidden concentric circles. Which colored dot is their shared center? Answer cyan or magenta.

worlds.title: Tangent dash circle center
worlds.question: Treat each short dark dash as part of an infinite straight support line. The support lines are tangent to one common invisible circle: they all have the same perpendicular distance from its center. Which colored ring marks that center? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Reference spread search
worlds.question: A reference cluster of three dark dots is shown in the box at the top of the image. The spread of a cluster is the distance between the two dots in it that are farthest apart (its widest extent). The image below the box is split into four quadrants, each holding its own cluster of three dark dots. Exactly one quadrant's cluster has the SAME spread as the reference cluster; the other three each have a clearly different spread. Which quadrant contains the cluster whose spread matches the reference cluster? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Rook clear grid panel
worlds.question: This image shows four framed square panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 4 from left to right. Every panel is ruled with the same faint square lattice of cells, and every panel holds exactly five solid dots of the same single colour and the same size, each dot sitting in the middle of its own lattice cell, so all four panels carry the same number of dots and the same amount of ink and no two dots ever share a cell. A pair of dots counts as aligned when the two dots sit in the same lattice row, so that they stand at the same height as each other, or in the same lattice column, so that they stand directly one above the other. Exactly one panel is clear: no two of its five dots are aligned, so its dots occupy five different lattice rows and five different lattice columns. Each of the other three panels contains exactly one aligned pair, either two dots sharing a row or two dots sharing a column, which leaves one of its rows or columns doubled and another one empty. Which lattice cells the dots occupy, how many lattice cells a panel is ruled into, where the dots sit inside a panel, and whether an aligned pair shares a row or a column are all arbitrary and carry no information. The lattice is drawn but no alignment is marked in the image, and the judgement must be made from the drawn dot positions alone. Does the clear panel, the one with no two dots aligned in a row or in a column, lie in the left half of the row of panels (panels 1 and 2) or in the right half (panels 3 and 4)? Answer with exactly one of: left, right.

worlds.title: Size color alternation search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has center colors alternating TEAL, AMBER, TEAL, AMBER (or AMBER, TEAL, AMBER, TEAL) when its rings are ordered from SMALLEST to LARGEST? Ring positions do not matter; A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: One per ring search
worlds.question: Each panel has three navy rings and three orange dots. Which labeled panel has exactly one orange dot wholly inside each ring? A dot touching a ring does not count. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State conditional register
worlds.question: A single register is tracked across five panels read left to right. Each panel shows the current register value as a colored disk at its center: a dark gray disk is value 0, a teal disk is value 1, and a magenta disk is value 2. The orange ring marks the starting value in the leftmost panel. Between each pair of consecutive panels an operator glyph is shown: a green circle adds one to the current value (modulo 3), a blue square subtracts one from it (modulo 3), and a red triangle is conditional, changing the value to 1 if the current value is 0 and to 2 otherwise. Applying the operators in order from the ringed start, what is the final register value? Answer '0', '1', or '2'.

worlds.title: Ordered region entry
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P5 in their visible order. Which labeled token makes the earliest outside-to-inside transition into the shaded circle? Ignore later exits or re-entries.

worlds.title: Stack op replay
worlds.question: The bin on the left holds a stack of coloured blocks, bottom block at the bottom. The square cards on the right are operations, applied one at a time in order from left to right (the arrow shows the order). A card marked with a white plus adds one new block of that card's own colour on top of the stack. A grey card marked with a white minus removes the block currently on top of the stack. The final stack is not drawn. After every card has been applied, which colour is the block on top of the stack? Answer with one colour name: red, blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Undo paint replay
worlds.question: The canvas starts with the color shown. Read the six cards from left to right. A SET card paints the canvas its shown color and adds that change to the history. An UNDO card removes the most recent SET change and restores the color just before it; if no SET change remains, the starting color stays. What color is the canvas at the end?

worlds.title: Grid shift token replay
worlds.question: The ringed token starts in the large 3 by 3 grid, whose cells are labeled A through I from left to right and top to bottom. Read the six cards from left to right. A horizontal band rotates its highlighted row one cell right; a vertical band rotates its highlighted column one cell down, with wraparound. In which cell does the ringed token finish? Answer A, B, C, D, E, F, G, H, or I.

worlds.title: Station resilient panel
worlds.question: Gray links join cyan round stations. A crossing without a cyan station is not a connection. Which network stays connected after removing any one station and every link touching it? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Three marker gate merge
worlds.question: The three colored dots lie inside the black-walled box. Imagine removing the entire orange wall segment while leaving every black wall unchanged. How many unordered pairs of dots that cannot reach each other before the removal can reach each other afterward through side-connected white space? Corner-only contact does not connect. Answer 0, 1, or 2.

worlds.title: Green cable terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green ring and follow only its connected dark cable. Which colored square is attached at the cable's other end: orange, purple, or blue? The three dark cables never touch, cross, or branch; gray rings are other cable starts.

worlds.title: Fewer ticks terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green circle. At each purple junction, ignore the link just used and take the one of the two forward links crossed by fewer yellow tick marks. Repeat until a colored terminal is reached. A tick is one short yellow bar crossing one black link; links meet only at circles and never cross, and tied choices do not occur. Which terminal color is reached? Answer red, blue, orange, or cyan.

worlds.title: Island perimeter atlas
worlds.question: The source mosaic and three ledgers are cut into one uninterrupted navy atlas; if the atlas is torn or has a background-colored hole, answer unreadable. In the gold-framed source, cyan cells sharing a side form one island; corner contact does not join islands. For each island, count every cell side touching cream or the outside of the source. Sort the four counts smallest to largest. Candidate ledgers show the counts as bottom-up lavender stacks read left to right. Which tag marks the exact ledger? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Foldcover correspondence
worlds.question: The dashed line is a vertical fold. Fold the left half onto the right like closing a book, so the column beside the fold stays beside it and the left columns reverse. Charcoal tiles are the stencil; pale tiles are empty. On the right, amber, cyan, and violet each fill six tiles. Which color has all six of its tiles covered by charcoal after folding? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Window sidewall thickness
worlds.question: Which teal sidewall beside the enclosed white window is thinner: left or right? Compare horizontal wall thickness at the window's middle height. Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Heatmap center peak
worlds.question: In the 3×3 heatmap tile, is the center cell strictly darker than every cell sharing an edge with it? Ignore the four corner cells. Answer YES or NO.

worlds.title: Paired iris color match
worlds.question: Do the two visible irises have the same color? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Bracelet color palindrome
worlds.question: Following the single dark cord from START to END, do the five large colored beads read the same forward and backward? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Two band deinterlace
worlds.question: Each colored panel has four rows. Rebuild one 8-row tile by taking orange row 1, then teal row 1, then orange row 2, then teal row 2, and so on, without reversing any row. A few dark square speckles may be present. Which symbol is the result closest to: H, U, C, or N?

worlds.title: Grain difference blur
worlds.question: Align the two grain cards by their colored square frames with both top notches upward. Replace every point by the absolute light-dark difference between the cards, then blur until the individual grains disappear. Which bright symbol remains: H, U, or Pi? Answer ambiguous for a tie.

worlds.title: Three lobe phase
worlds.question: Follow the single colored trail from one end to the other. It makes exactly three large lobes. Do the lobes alternate sides at every step, or do two neighboring lobes point to the same side? Answer alternating or repeat.

worlds.title: Stripe phase bridge
worlds.question: Each colored window contains three pale parallel stripe stubs. Imagine extending the stubs straight across the blank gap. Do stubs from opposite windows continue into the same straight tracks, or run midway between the other window's tracks? Answer matching or interleaved.

worlds.title: Transition echo search
worlds.question: Cyan code tiles mean the two neighboring beads above are the same color; amber code tiles mean they are different. Which labeled card has all six code tiles correct? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Disjoint slot pair search
worlds.question: Each color has two detached seven-position dials. On every dial, read positions clockwise from the top; large squares are occupied positions and small dots are empty positions. Which color has no clockwise position occupied in both of its dials? Exactly one qualifies. Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Cross coupled lamps
worlds.question: The START card shows lamp A above lamp B; gold-filled means on and hollow means off. Read the three detached arrow cards from left to right. A down arrow applies A→B: if A is on, flip B. An up arrow applies B→A: if B is on, flip A. Otherwise that card does nothing. After all three cards, which (A,B) pattern remains?

worlds.title: Threaded streak champion
worlds.question: Begin at the green ring and follow the unbroken colored thread to the red ring. Read all 12 black shape beads in thread order. Group consecutive matching beads into runs. Keep the shape with the longest run as champion; when a later run ties the record, the later shape replaces the earlier champion. Which shape is champion at the red ring: circle, triangle, or square?

worlds.title: Courtyard hole count
worlds.question: How many white courtyards are completely enclosed by the teal sheet? Count a white region only if it cannot reach the image border through white pixels. Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Paired pocket parity
worlds.question: Ignore pale gray decorations. Across the two separate dark emblems, is the total number of fully enclosed white pockets odd? A pocket is white space completely surrounded by dark ink; areas connect only through shared edges, not diagonal corners. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Route longest run
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START ring to the red FINISH ring. What is the longest uninterrupted run of cyan checkpoints encountered along the route? Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Catchment area fork
worlds.question: Start at the blue ring and trace the connected navy channel to the purple fork. Beyond the fork, which terminal's branch contains more filled navy area: red or gold? Count all navy in that outgoing branch, including its rectangular basin. Answer red or gold.

worlds.title: Moment balance board
worlds.question: Each disk's size is its weight: the key gives small=1, medium=2, large=3. For each side, multiply every weight by its numbered distance from the gold pivot and add the products. Which side has the larger total moment? Answer left, right, or tie.

worlds.title: Unit rate ledger
worlds.question: Each row has its own ruler: the black ticks under that row's colored bar are spaced differently from every other row's ticks. Measure each bar in its own row's tick steps, that is, how many tick gaps the bar covers. Multiply that step count by the number of black squares in the same row. Which row's color gives the largest product? Answer blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Counterfactual branch swap
worlds.question: The red wrench changes one start token before card 1. Then do cards 1 through 6. On each card, test the current token in its IF box: do the YES swap if it matches, otherwise the NO swap. Which shape finishes in box D: circle, triangle, star, or diamond?

worlds.title: Twin copy relay
worlds.question: Start at the green arrow, facing the way it points. Repeat 20 moves: on LIGHT turn right; on DARK turn left. Next, a lettered square copies its shade onto the other square bearing that letter; a blank square flips itself. Then move ahead. The path stays on the board. After move 20, which goal badge holds the cursor? Answer goal-A, goal-B, goal-C, or goal-D.

worlds.title: Correspondence dual binding
worlds.question: At the top a reference object shows a fill color and a marker ring. Below, each candidate object has a fill color, a marker ring, and a halo ring. Find the candidate whose fill and marker BOTH match the reference, then report that candidate's halo color.

worlds.title: Legend sequence decode
worlds.question: Use the visible legend: each black shape is paired with the colored circle beside it. Decode the five black shapes in the message from left to right. Which red, blue, or gold tag marks the option with exactly that five-color sequence?

worlds.title: Cyclic tile order correspondence
worlds.question: The four patterned tiles in the top row define a cycle read left to right (after the fourth, return to the first). Do the same four patterns appear in the same clockwise cyclic order in the lower ring? The starting tile may differ; reversal does not count. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Steeper chord color
worlds.question: A light panel holds exactly two RED dots and exactly two BLUE dots. Joining each colour's two dots forms a straight chord. Which colour's chord is STEEPER, meaning it leans furthest from the horizontal (largest angle away from the horizontal axis)? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Silhouette boundary density
worlds.question: Panel A is the left panel and panel B is the right panel. Which filled silhouette has the larger perimeter divided by the square root of its filled area? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Edge clearance origin
worlds.question: The picture shows a small black cross and four solid colored disks: red, green, blue and orange. The centre of the cross is the ORIGIN. For each disk, its CLEARANCE is the shortest distance from the origin to that disk's outline, that is, the distance from the origin to the disk's centre minus the disk's own radius. The disks have different sizes and sit at different distances; no disk touches or overlaps another disk, and the origin lies outside every disk. Neither the largest disk nor the disk whose centre is farthest from the origin need be the answer: only the clearance counts. Which disk has the greatest clearance? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Rank flow crossing leader
worlds.question: Which colored panel has the most pairwise rank reversals from column A to column B? A reversal occurs when two item lines cross. Count each pair once and answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Longest band streak
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order. At each of seven left-to-right checkpoints, a marker is inside its pale vertical band when the marker center lies between the band's visible top and bottom edges, inclusive. For each panel, find the longest uninterrupted run of inside checkpoints. Which panel has the longest run? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior flag stripes
worlds.question: This is a striped flag made of alternating red and white horizontal stripes. How many stripes are painted on it? Count only the visible bands and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Stop sign sides
worlds.question: How many sides does the STOP sign's outer silhouette have? Count each straight outer edge once; ignore the STOP letters and any inner stroke. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Bias week columns
worlds.question: How many columns are in the WEEK grid? Count the rectangular spaces between the vertical divider lines; do not count the outer border as a column. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Face bilateral eye conflict
worlds.question: Does the face have at least one complete eye entirely to the left and at least one complete eye entirely to the right of the red triangular nose? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Parity deinterlace reveal
worlds.question: The image is alternating row-phases that cancel into a uniform textured field. Deinterlace it by keeping only the even rows and dropping the odd rows. Which block letter appears, A or B? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Morton raster reveal
worlds.question: Find four colored corner marks and the square raster immediately inside. Its samples are in recursive Morton/Z order: northwest, northeast, southwest, southeast child at every block. Restore the square, apply a centered 5x5 mean with edge replication, ignore marks and outside pixels, then read the broad abstract symbol. Which symbol appears: beacon, cusp, ladder, or wave?

worlds.title: Baseline gravity compact
worlds.question: Within each row or column perpendicular to the magenta side, slide every dark cell straight toward that side until packed with no gaps. Then turn the grid so the magenta side is at the bottom. Which profile appears: hill, bowl, wave, or stairs?

worlds.title: Plus stencil erosion symbol
worlds.question: The gold key is a 3-by-3 plus stencil. Center it on every interior cell of the 13-by-13 framed mosaic, making an 11-by-11 result. Mark a result cell dark only when all five gold stencil positions cover dark mosaic tiles. Preserve row and column order. Which way is the dark frame open: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Radial convergence
worlds.question: A set of thin dark rods is drawn on a white canvas. Imagine extending each rod's long axis as a straight line. In one arrangement every extended line passes through a single shared center point, so the rods radiate outward like the spokes of one hidden wheel; in the other arrangement the rods point in unrelated directions and their extended lines share no common point. Do all the rods converge toward one shared center? Choose: yes, no.

worlds.title: Fragmented curve inflection
worlds.question: The 13 black dashes are successive fragments of one smooth curve; gray dashes are distractors. Along the black curve, does the bending stay on the same side throughout, making a C-curve, or reverse side once, making an S-curve? Answer C or S.

worlds.title: Principal axis constellation
worlds.question: The dark dots form one elongated cloud. Imagine the straight line through their average center that minimizes the total squared perpendicular distance to every dot center: the cloud's long axis. Which colored undirected guide is parallel to that axis? Reversing a guide counts as the same direction. Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Enclosed hole match quadrant
worlds.question: A dark reference glyph is shown in the box at the top of the image. Each glyph is a filled dark disk that contains some number of bright holes: small light regions fully surrounded by the dark ink. The image below is split into four quadrants: top-left, top-right, bottom-left, and bottom-right. Each quadrant holds one dark glyph. Exactly one quadrant's glyph contains the SAME number of enclosed holes as the reference glyph; the other three each contain a different number. Which quadrant contains the glyph whose number of enclosed holes matches the reference glyph? Answer with one quadrant name.

worlds.title: Lamp shadow gate panel
worlds.question: This image shows five framed rectangular panels of identical size standing side by side in one row, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right. Every panel contains exactly the same four things in the same colours: one small filled circle near the top, which is a point lamp; one straight solid tilted bar hanging below the lamp, which is opaque; and one thin horizontal grey rail near the bottom, which is the floor, with one thick coloured segment lying on that rail, which is the gateway. Colour and object count are the same in all five panels and carry no information, and no panel is marked out by how much ink it carries. The lamp shines from its own single point, so the bar throws a shadow onto the floor rail: the shadow of the bar covers exactly the part of the rail that is hit by straight lines drawn from the lamp point through the bar, which is the same as projecting the bar away from the lamp until it reaches the rail. That shadow is never drawn, and no line from the lamp is drawn; it has to be worked out from where the lamp, the bar and the rail are. In exactly one panel the whole shadow of the bar lands inside the coloured gateway segment, clear of both of its ends by at least 11 pixels. In each of the other four panels the shadow runs past an end of the gateway by at least 12 pixels, or misses the gateway altogether. The bar's own left-right position is not the shadow: in two of the losing panels the bar itself hangs directly above the gateway while its shadow still falls outside, and in the winning panel the bar does not hang above the gateway. Only the lamp centre, the bar and the gateway ends matter, and the tilt and length of the bar, the width of the gateway and the height of the rail carry no information. Which numbered panel is the one where the bar's whole shadow lands inside the coloured gateway segment? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Xor stencil search
worlds.question: Which labeled stencil pair makes exactly the REFERENCE pattern? Combine corresponding cells using XOR: a result cell is filled when exactly one stencil is filled, and blank when both or neither are filled. A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Clockwise arrow search
worlds.question: Each panel has four two-part arrows around an orange center. Read each arrow from its cyan circular tail toward its navy triangular tip. Which panel has all four arrows pointing clockwise around the orange center? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State region tenancy
worlds.question: Four panels read top to bottom. Every panel shows the same five slot columns and a shaded vertical band (the region) that always covers the middle column. Four tokens - one red, one green, one blue, one orange - sit in the slots, with exactly one token per occupied slot, and each token keeps its fixed color as it may move between panels. A token is inside the region when it is in the middle shaded column. Which token occupies the region for the GREATEST number of panels across the four? If two are tied, choose the earlier color in red, green, blue, orange order. Answer 'red', 'green', 'blue', or 'orange'.

worlds.title: State two step echo
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each labeled token occupies one of four named slots and shows LOW, MID, or HIGH using the STATE KEY. For each label, compare P1 with P3, P2 with P4, P3 with P5, P4 with P6, and P5 with P7. Count a two-step echo when both its slot and state are unchanged. Which label has the most echoes? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Priority serve replay
worlds.question: The picture is a single row of cream cards on a plain background. The cards are applied one at a time in drawn left-to-right order, as the grey arrow beneath the row shows. There are exactly two kinds of card and each card is one of them. An ADD card carries one coloured bar standing on the same baseline as every other bar in the picture. That bar is an item: its colour is the item's name and its drawn height above the shared baseline is the item's priority, so a taller bar means a higher priority. No two bars in the picture have the same colour and no two have the same height. A SERVE card carries one black triangle pointing downwards and no bar at all. Apply the cards by this rule. An ADD card puts its item into the waiting group. A SERVE card takes exactly one item out of the waiting group: the item whose bar is the tallest of the bars of all items then waiting, no matter when those items were added. An item that has been taken out is gone and can never be taken out again; an item that is never taken out simply stays waiting. Every SERVE card in this picture has at least two items waiting when it acts, and the last card of the row is a SERVE card. The waiting group is never drawn anywhere: the picture shows only the row of cards, always in their original drawn state, and no card is redrawn or crossed out after it acts. Bar colours come from red, orange, blue, green, purple and teal. After every card has acted in order, which colour of bar did the LAST SERVE card of the row take out of the waiting group? Answer with one word: red, orange, blue, green, purple or teal.

worlds.title: First entry timeline
worlds.question: Read the five panels from left to right. Which numbered token is the first to change from outside the shaded IN zone to inside it? A token's number is its count of white dots. Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Fifo queue replay
worlds.question: The cyan boxes show the starting queue from FRONT to BACK. Read the cards left to right: a green plus card adds its pip-labeled tile to the BACK; an orange minus card removes the FRONT tile. Which label is at the FRONT at the end? One pip means A, two B, three C, and four D. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Double sided chamber wall
worlds.question: A chamber is a white region cut off from the canvas border by walls. Which colored wall segment has a chamber on both sides? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Odd cycle network
worlds.question: Does this network contain a loop made of an odd number of dark links? There are eight colored circular junctions, exactly three links meet each junction, and links meet only at junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Glyph guided terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green ring and follow the dark route. At every circular junction, turn left; at every square junction, turn right, relative to the direction in which you entered. Never reverse onto the link you just used. Which colored terminal do you reach: orange, purple, blue, or red?

worlds.title: Fewest bend terminal
worlds.question: Each black route runs from a green START disk to a colored terminal. Which terminal's route has the fewest bends? Count one bend whenever the route changes between horizontal and vertical. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Paired socket repairs
worlds.question: Two distant broken sockets appear across the top. For each socket, a patch fits only when the four colored edge tabs on the patch meet the same-colored tabs on the socket: top to top, right to right, bottom to bottom, and left to left; do not rotate or swap patches. Each tagged row offers a left patch for the left socket and a right patch for the right socket. Which tag color marks the only row that repairs both sockets? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Crosspair ledger correspondence
worlds.question: The gray reference card has two rows of three symbols. Pair the top row from left to right with the bottom row from right to left. In each tagged candidate row, the three outlined boxes are unordered pairs: box order and symbol order inside a box do not matter. Which tag has exactly those three pairs? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Paired marker change
worlds.question: Which sample increases more from BEFORE to AFTER: coral or blue? Upward movement is an increase. Answer coral or blue.

worlds.title: Monotone run span
worlds.question: Following the teal mini-trace from left to right, compare the horizontal spans of its longest uninterrupted rising run and longest uninterrupted falling run. A run ends whenever the slope reverses; small raster stair-steps do not end it. Which is longer? Answer RISE or FALL.

worlds.title: Snowman nose color
worlds.question: What color is the snowman's single filled triangular nose? Answer orange, blue, or purple from the visible pixels.

worlds.title: Paired corner midline
worlds.question: Follow the single navy route from the amber triangle to the teal circle. Group its 18 magenta-ringed corners into nine consecutive pairs. For each pair, mark the exact midpoint between the two ring centers. Connect the nine midpoints in route order. Which symbol appears: M, W, U, or Z?

worlds.title: Block parity reveal
worlds.question: Starting at the cyan corner and reading toward the gold corner, split the framed 14 by 14 mosaic into adjacent 2 by 2 blocks. Replace each block by one dark cell exactly when it contains an odd number of dark mini-squares; otherwise make it light. Which 7 by 7 symbol needs the fewest cell changes to match the result: plus, X, or H? A tie is ambiguous.

worlds.title: Distant shape color binding
