worlds.question: Each pale panel contains one circle, one square, and one triangle, and uses each color once. Ignoring position and size, are the colors paired with the same shapes in both panels? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Level crossing rail search
worlds.question: Follow the cyan rail from left to right. Each colored bead begins one excursion that ends at the next bead. Which bead begins the excursion that crosses the horizontal level through that bead exactly three times? Do not count either endpoint touching the level. Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Tide turn ledger
worlds.question: The gold arrow shows the starting direction. Read basin snapshots 1, 2, then 3. After each change, turn the arrow 90 degrees clockwise if the blue flooded area grows, or 90 degrees counterclockwise if it shrinks. What direction does the arrow face after both changes?

worlds.title: Paired gate closure
worlds.question: Treat both bars of one color as solid black wall, leaving the other color unchanged. Which color, cyan or orange, makes the central white courtyard unable to reach the outer white background?

worlds.title: Route prefix count
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green start to the red finish. Before reaching the first orange checkpoint, how many blue checkpoints do you pass? Count along the route, not by straight-line distance. Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Paired tree trip length
worlds.question: Two separate route maps are shown, one above the other. In each map, trace the unique cyan centerline through the navy network from the blue ring to the orange ring, ignoring dead ends. Which trip is longer along the centerline: top or bottom? Answer top or bottom.

worlds.title: Pivot frame motion
worlds.question: The gold dot starts on the 5 by 5 board. Apply motion 1, then motion 2, exactly as shown in the cards. Which sector contains the dot at the end? Answer northwest, northeast, southwest, or southeast.

worlds.title: Moment balance beam
worlds.question: Each of the four bars rests on a red wedge, and blue blocks hang from the bar at its grey notches. A hanging load's turning effect is its number of blocks multiplied by how many notches it hangs away from the wedge. Exactly one bar has the same total turning effect on its left side as on its right side. Notch spacing differs from bar to bar, so count notches, not pixels. Which bar is the balanced one? The bars are numbered 1 to 4 from the top. Answer with exactly one of: beam-1, beam-2, beam-3, beam-4.

worlds.title: Counterfactual event splice
worlds.question: Try the PATCH swap at one colored gap at a time. For that spliced row, rebuild dependencies: each swap depends on the latest earlier swap touching either box. Cancel the red-X card, repeatedly cancel every dependent swap, then restart from START and do the swaps left. Which patch position puts GOAL in TARGET? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Mutual key agreement
worlds.question: Use the queried symbol row in ROW KEY and the queried disk row in COLUMN KEY. Find the only row-color and blue-stamp pair that agree both ways: under that stamp, ROW KEY gives the row color; under that row color, COLUMN KEY gives the stamp. Read their intersection on the ANSWER GRID. Answer amber, cyan, violet, or lime.

worlds.title: Polygon side correspondence
worlds.question: The gray polygon at the top is a convex shape with a certain number of straight sides. Below it are three colored convex polygons labeled A, B, C: one is red, one green, one blue, and each has a different number of sides. Which colored polygon has exactly the same number of sides as the gray polygon? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Exclusive overlay match
worlds.question: Overlay LAYER 1 and LAYER 2 without turning either grid. A result tile is filled exactly when that cell is filled in ONE layer only, not both. Which colored border encloses the exact result? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Latin grid completion correspondence
worlds.question: Each row and column of the large grid originally contained each of the four black-square symbols exactly once. One removed cell is outlined in magenta; the other three gray blocked cells are irrelevant. Which colored candidate shows the symbol missing from the magenta cell: red, green, blue, or orange?

worlds.title: Trace cross pair
worlds.question: A gray horizontal line crosses the panel, and two wavy colored traces (one red, one blue) undulate across the full width. Which color's trace crosses the gray horizontal line MORE times, meaning it goes from above to below (or below to above) the line more often? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Integrated curve area
worlds.question: Panel A is the left plot and panel B is the right plot. Which panel has the larger area under its colored trace and above its visible horizontal baseline? Choose A or B.

worlds.title: Shadow span rank
worlds.question: The picture shows one long black horizontal axis with short ticks along its lower edge, and four bent rods drawn above it: one red, one green, one blue and one orange, each in its own horizontal lane. Every rod is a single bent line made of two straight pieces joined at a corner, and all four rods are drawn with the same thickness. Imagine the light falling straight down the page, so that every point of a rod drops vertically onto the axis. The stretch of axis that a rod darkens in this way is its SHADOW, and the width of that stretch is what has to be compared: it runs from the leftmost point anywhere on the rod to the rightmost point anywhere on the rod. The corner counts as part of the rod, so a rod that doubles back casts a shadow wider than the gap between its two loose ends, and for such a rod the two ends are the wrong things to measure. Nothing else about a rod matters: not how long the bent line itself is, not how much ink it uses, not how steeply it climbs, not how tall its lane is, not which lane it lies in and not how far left or right it sits. The rod that is drawn longest, the rod whose two ends are farthest apart, the topmost rod and the bottom rod are each the answer only as often as chance allows. Which rod casts the widest shadow on the axis? Answer red, green, blue or orange.

worlds.title: Dual threshold shortfall
worlds.question: Which colored point has the smallest combined shortfall from the dashed x-target and y-target? Add its horizontal gap when it is left of the vertical target (otherwise zero) and its vertical gap when it is below the horizontal target (otherwise zero).

worlds.title: Trajectory directness ratio
worlds.question: Each colored trajectory joins five markers from left to right. For each trajectory, divide the straight-line distance from its first marker to its last by the sum of its four segment lengths. Which trajectory has the largest ratio? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior clock marks
worlds.question: This is an analog clock. How many hour marks are drawn on its face? Count only the visible marks and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Bias letter b holes
worlds.question: How many separate white holes are fully enclosed inside the blue capital B? Count only white regions that do not touch the outer background. Answer 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Padlock shackle closure conflict
worlds.question: Does the dark U-shaped shackle visibly contact the colored lock body at both of its two lower ends? Treat a visible background gap as no contact. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Key xor null reveal
worlds.question: The image shows, on the left, a 32-by-32 grid of dark and light cells that looks like pure random noise, and on the right a magenta-framed box that displays the pure-noise KEY (the same 32-by-32 cell pattern, shown small) that was used to hide a symbol. The hidden symbol was XOR-combined into the left field: every field cell where the symbol is on had its shade flipped. The raw left field alone is uniform noise and reveals nothing. Undo the declared cipher by taking the logical XOR of the left field with the key grid (cell by cell, flip a field cell wherever the key cell is different from it); the matching noise cancels and a clean abstract symbol remains: a filled circle (A) or a filled square (B). Which symbol, A or B, is revealed? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Arrow chain reflow
worlds.question: Start at the cell with the magenta dot. Follow the cyan arrow in each cell to the side-sharing next cell, ending at the yellow dot. Read each cell's dark or light center in that order, then write the 64 values row by row into an 8 by 8 square. Which symbol appears: anchor, boot, chair, or sail?

worlds.title: Cyclic row register symbol
worlds.question: Cyclically slide each row until its orange marker is in the leftmost cell beside the gold rail, wrapping at the row ends. Which symbol do the navy tiles form: slash, backslash, left chevron, or right chevron?

worlds.title: Radial spoke count
worlds.question: A set of small dark dots is drawn on a white canvas. The dots are laid out on straight radial spokes that all emanate from one shared center, so together they trace a star-burst of spokes: dots along the same spoke are very close in direction, while consecutive spokes are separated by a much larger empty angular gap. How many radial spokes do the dots trace around the shared center? Choose 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Dotted rail convergence
worlds.question: The black dots form two straight chains outlining an implied corridor. Extend both chains until they meet. Which colored marker is closest to their meeting point? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Radial spiral handedness
worlds.question: Starting at the gray center marker, order the dark dots from nearest to farthest. As distance increases, does the constellation wind clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Exclusive circle membership search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has every teal dot inside exactly ONE of its two colored circles? A dot in the overlap or outside both circles does not qualify. A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Single cycle network search
worlds.question: Which labeled network is one closed loop containing all six colored dots? Every dot must have exactly two dark lines touching it, and crossings without a dot do not join. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State gap extremum
worlds.question: Four panels sit side by side and are read left to right. Each panel shows a horizontal track divided into six slots, slot 0 at the left up to slot 5 at the right, with one red token and one green token sitting on it. The red token and the green token each keep their identity from panel to panel and may move left or right between panels (their positions are drawn in every panel). In a panel, the separation between the two tokens is the absolute difference of their slot indices. Across all four ordered panels, what is the LARGEST separation in slots ever reached between the red token and the green token? Answer with the integer 0, 1, 2, 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: State cohort stability
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each labeled tile shows LOW, MID, or HIGH using the STATE KEY. For each state, write the exact set of labels occupying it in every panel. Count a match when that entire label set is unchanged between adjacent panels. Which state has the most matches? Exactly one state wins; answer LOW, MID, or HIGH.

worlds.title: Rotor switch relay
worlds.question: The picture shows a pin board of ten grey switches arranged in four rows of one, two, three and four, and five coloured bins in a row along the bottom. Each switch is a square grey block with a short grey tongue sticking out of its left side or out of its right side. The dark blue discs on the shelf at the top are the balls to be released: there are as many balls as discs, and they are released one at a time, each one finishing its whole fall before the next one is released. Every ball starts at the single switch of the top row. When a ball reaches a switch it leaves that switch towards the side its tongue is sticking out of at that moment, and it then arrives at the switch of the next row down that lies on that side: a tongue on the right sends the ball to the next lower switch to its lower right, and a tongue on the left sends it to the next lower switch to its lower left. Immediately after a ball has left a switch, that switch throws its tongue over to its other side, so the next ball that reaches the same switch is sent the opposite way, the ball after that is sent the original way again, and so on. Switches that no ball reaches keep the tongue drawn in the picture. Below the bottom row of switches there are five exit slots, and each coloured bin sits directly under one exit slot, as the faint grey guide lines show; a ball that leaves the bottom row falls into the bin under the slot it left from. The tongues are drawn as they stand before any ball is released, and no later position of any ball or tongue is drawn anywhere. Into which coloured bin does the last released ball fall? Answer with one colour word: red, green, yellow, orange or purple.

worlds.title: Vessel pour replay
worlds.question: Each vessel holds 4 units. Start with the shown filled unit cells and read the five POUR cards from left to right. On each card, the left color is the source and the right color is the destination. Transfer as much as possible, stopping when the source is empty or the destination is full. How many units are in the ringed vessel at the end?

worlds.title: Odd cycle free panel
worlds.question: A loop is a closed route that follows links and does not repeat a junction except at the finish; count one link each time it joins two round junctions, and crossings without a round junction are not connections. Which network has no loop with an odd number of links? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Forbidden junction connectivity
worlds.question: Can all three green junctions reach one another along dark links without entering either orange junction? A route may use blue junctions. Links meet only at circular junctions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Checkpoint span route
worlds.question: Each row is one separate dark route from a green circle to a colored square. Which colored square ends the route whose two cyan diamond checkpoints are farthest apart along the route? Measure the dark route between the checkpoint centers, including every bend. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Straightest branch terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green circle. At each purple junction, ignore the link just used and take the remaining link that deviates least from straight ahead. Which colored terminal is reached? Links meet only at circles and never cross; every choice has one clear smallest turn. Answer red, blue, orange, or cyan.

worlds.title: Gravity stack quilt
worlds.question: The gold chamber is the source. Cyan tiles fall straight down within their own columns until there are no gaps; columns never mix. Which colored chamber is the exact result? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Neighbor press correspondence
worlds.question: The charcoal-framed grid is the SOURCE. For each output cell, inspect the four orthogonal neighbors of the matching source cell: up, down, left, and right; beyond the grid counts as light. An output cell is dark exactly when two of those four neighbors are dark. Which colored frame encloses the correct output? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Paired width balance
worlds.question: Which colored pair has the more nearly equal bar widths? Compare the absolute difference between the two bar widths. Answer coral or blue.

worlds.title: Relative interval centering
worlds.question: Each colored vertical interval has a dark estimate notch. For each interval, measure the notch's distance from the interval midpoint as a fraction of that interval's full height. Which interval has the smaller fraction? Answer CYAN or ORANGE.

worlds.title: Butterfly wing count
worlds.question: How many broad wings are visibly attached to the butterfly's central body? Count each distinct side lobe as one wing; do not count the two antennae.

worlds.title: Paired tone comparator
worlds.question: Compare matching squares in the two 7 by 7 panels. Make an output square dark exactly when the left-panel square is darker than the right-panel square. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Paired chamber channel
worlds.question: The colored plaque contains four round pale chambers. Exactly one opposite pair is joined into a single thick opening. Is the joined pair left-right or top-bottom? Answer left-right or top-bottom.

worlds.title: Clutter glyph search
worlds.question: The cyan box at far left contains the reference glyph. Which labeled field contains that exact black glyph with the same orientation and segment lengths? Extra black strokes are clutter; do not rotate or reflect the reference. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Modulo quilt replay
worlds.question: Begin at 0. Read every quilt tile in row order, left-to-right then top-to-bottom. A cool blue tile adds 1 and a warm orange tile adds 2. After each tile, wrap 3 back to 0. What number remains: 0, 1, or 2?

worlds.title: Twin link resilience
worlds.question: Each panel shows one rail network with a yellow link. Imagine removing only the yellow link in each panel. Do the two removals have the same effect: either both disconnect their network, or both leave it connected? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Checkpoint pair nesting
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START to the red FINISH. The two cyan checkpoints and two orange checkpoints either interleave (cyan-orange-cyan-orange, or the reverse) or nest (one matching-color pair encloses the other). Which arrangement is shown? Answer interleaved or nested.

worlds.title: Corridor width palindrome
worlds.question: Starting at the blue ring, follow the single navy corridor to the orange ring. At each station, the two gold gauge dots face each other across the corridor: record FULL if both dots sit on navy, or SPLIT if both sit on white. Does the seven-station word read the same forward and backward? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Finite state lookup automaton
worlds.question: The RULEBOOK is a four-row by three-column transition table. Each row is the current state (amber, cyan, violet, lime); each column is the next input badge (red, blue, teal). The colored disk in a cell is the next state. START shows the initial state. Read the nine input badges from left to right; for each badge, use the current state's row and that badge's column, then replace the state with the cell's color. After badge 9, which state is current? Answer exactly one of: amber, cyan, violet, lime.

worlds.title: Shared circuit pair
worlds.question: This picture is a 6 by 6 block of square rooms. Walls are solid ink, and you may walk between two rooms only through a doorway gap in the wall between them. Four rooms have a coloured floor: orange, green, blue and pink, and every one of the four stands on some round trip, so that on its own tells you nothing. A round trip is a walk that ends where it began and never passes through the same doorway twice. Exactly two of the four coloured rooms lie on one and the same round trip; for every other pair, no single round trip visits both. Which two rooms are they? Answer with exactly one of: orange+green, orange+blue, orange+pink, green+blue, green+pink, blue+pink.

worlds.title: Directional value transfer
worlds.question: Crates are worth the number shown for the depot they are in. Each arrow moves the shown crates. Apply one plan to START. Which plan leaves LEFT and RIGHT with equal total value? Answer plan-A, plan-B, plan-C, or plan-D.

worlds.title: Landmark transform relay
worlds.question: Each card shows where the same three colored pegs went BEFORE to AFTER under one whole-grid rigid move. Infer each move from the colors. Apply moves 1, 2, then 3 to the two-dot START token (navy tail, red head). Which option is final? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Perforation profile match
worlds.question: The top card is the REFERENCE. Each card contains one cyan, magenta, green, and orange tile. Count only fully enclosed white holes inside each tile; the outer white background is not a hole. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same hole count for every tile color as the reference? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Balance substitution correspondence
worlds.question: Each blue balance row says the symbol groups on its two sides have equal total weight. Which colored candidate tray must have the same total weight as the magenta REFERENCE tray? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Rectangle area argmax
worlds.question: Three colored rectangles are drawn on a light panel, each a different color (red, blue, green) with an independently varied width and height. Which colored rectangle has the LARGEST AREA, meaning the greatest width times height? The tallest and the widest may differ, so multiply each one's width by its height. Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Trace crossing band
worlds.question: The plot frame is divided into four vertical bands by three dashed black vertical lines; number the bands 1, 2, 3, 4 from left to right. The red trace and the blue trace cross each other exactly once inside the frame. The green trace is a distractor: ignore it and ignore every crossing that involves it. Which band contains the point where the red and blue traces cross? Answer 1, 2, 3 or 4.

worlds.title: Interval benchmark narrowest
worlds.question: Among the colored intervals that cross the vertical dashed benchmark, which interval is the narrowest?

worlds.title: Median paired shift leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order and share the same vertical scale. At each checkpoint, measure the signed vertical shift from the blue marker to the orange marker, with upward positive. For each panel, take the median of its five shifts. Which panel has the largest median? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior ladybug spots
worlds.question: This is a ladybug. The common seven-spot ladybug has seven black spots, but report exactly what is drawn here. How many black spots are on this ladybug's red body? Count only the visible spots and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Chair floor supports
worlds.question: How many separate blue supports connect the chair seat's bottom edge to the gray floor line? Count only supports that visibly touch both. Answer 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Star tip prior conflict
worlds.question: How many outward-pointing tips does the large star-like silhouette have? Count only the outer tips, not the inward notches. Answer 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Frontal anamorph reveal
worlds.question: The image shows a quadrilateral framed by blue sides with a symbol drawn inside it, viewed at an angle so the shape is foreshortened. View that marked quadrilateral from directly in front (rectify it to a flat rectangle) so the distorted symbol becomes a clear letter. Which letter, A or B, is revealed? Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Serpentine row reflow
worlds.question: Start at the magenta dot. Read the grid rows from top to bottom, alternating left-to-right then right-to-left. Write the 64 cells down the columns of an upright 8 by 8 square, filling columns from left to right. Which symbol appears: anchor, boot, chair, or sail?

worlds.title: Spiral track raster arrow
worlds.question: Starting at the gold dot, follow the cyan spiral clockwise inward and read all 49 tiles. Rewrite that sequence left-to-right across seven rows of seven, keeping dark tiles dark and pale tiles pale. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Star rotational order
worlds.question: A filled dark star sits centered on a white canvas. The star is rotationally symmetric: rotating it about its center by 360/order brings it back to match itself exactly, and ``order`` is how many times a full 360-degree turn divides into identical sectors. What is the star's rotational symmetry order? Choose: 5, 6, or 8.

worlds.title: Fragment loop closure
worlds.question: Treat same-colored dashes separated by a gap no wider than one dash thickness as connected. Which color forms exactly one closed loop: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Color shape balance search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has EACH COLOR shown once in a CIRCLE and once in a SQUARE? Every panel contains two markers of each color and four circles plus four squares; positions do not matter. Panels A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Straight continuation search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has two dark segments that continue along exactly one straight path across the gray gap, with neither a bend nor a sideways shift? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State entry count
worlds.question: A vertical timeline of five panels reads top to bottom. Each panel shows the same six slots (slot 1 to slot 6, left to right), and the two middle slots, slot 3 and slot 4, are shaded as a single band that appears in every panel. A single royal-blue token sits in exactly one slot of each panel, so the token is inside the shaded band when it occupies slot 3 or slot 4 and outside otherwise. Reading the panels in order, an entry occurs each time the token moves from an outside slot to an inside slot between two consecutive panels. How many entries does the blue token make into the shaded band over the whole timeline? Answer '0', '1', or '2'.

worlds.title: State motion lag
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each labeled token occupies one of four slots and shows LOW, MID, or HIGH using the STATE KEY. At each middle panel P2 through P6, count an echo when that token's state changed on the arrow entering the panel and its slot changed on the arrow leaving it. Which label has the most echoes? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Barrier track replay
worlds.question: The picture shows a track of nine grey square cells in a row. Number the cells 1 to 9 from left to right. A blue disc, the token, stands in one cell: the token is in the cell whose centre is nearest to the centre of the blue disc. Two thick red walls are drawn standing in the gaps between cells; each wall blocks the step between the two cells it stands between, in both directions. Below the track is a row of cream cards, applied one at a time in order from left to right, as the grey arrow under the row shows. Each card carries one green arrow and some purple dots. The green arrow gives the direction the token moves, left or right, and the number of purple dots gives how many single-cell steps that card asks for. A card moves the token one cell at a time in its direction, one step per dot, but the token stops for the rest of that card as soon as the next step would cross a red wall or would leave the track past cell 1 or cell 9; the remaining steps of that card are lost and the next card is then applied from wherever the token has stopped. The walls never move and no card removes a wall. The track is drawn only once, in the token's starting position; no later position of the token is drawn anywhere. After every card has been applied in order, which cell does the token end in? Answer with a single number from 1 to 9, counting cells from the left.

worlds.title: State table replay
worlds.question: Start at the shape inside the magenta ring. For each input card from left to right, use the table row for the current shape and the column whose header color matches the card; the shape in that cell becomes the new state. Which shape is the final state?

worlds.title: Hamiltonian cycle panel
worlds.question: A tour is a closed route that visits every round station exactly once before returning to its start. Travel only along drawn links. Which network has such a tour? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Shared hole island
worlds.question: Do the green and purple dots lie in holes bounded by the same side-connected dark island? A hole is an enclosed white region, and dark parts touching only at a corner are separate. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Balanced cut checkpoint
worlds.question: The dark links form a tree with six gray square terminals. Imagine removing one colored checkpoint circle and its two incident link pieces. Which checkpoint—orange, purple, or blue—leaves exactly two disconnected pieces containing three gray square terminals each? Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Corridor reachable terminal
worlds.question: Which colored terminal can be reached from the green START disk by moving only through white corridor space? Black walls cannot be crossed, and regions that touch only at a corner are not connected. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Parity crossweave atlas
worlds.question: All four mosaics are woven into one uninterrupted navy atlas; any background-colored hole makes it unreadable. In the gold-framed 5-by-5 source, count cyan tiles in each whole row and each whole column. A result tile is cyan exactly when both its source row and its source column contain an odd number of cyan tiles; otherwise it is cream. Keep every row and column position. Which red, green, or blue tag marks the exact 5-by-5 result?

worlds.title: Distribution area split
worlds.question: Does the teal distribution contain more visible area to the left or to the right of the dashed divider? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Plateau mean median
worlds.question: Across the 12 equal-width plateaus, treat each plateau once. Which height is greater: the MEAN, or the MEDIAN (the average of the sixth and seventh heights after sorting)?

worlds.title: Piano black key count
worlds.question: How many raised black keys are visible in the pictured piano octave panel? Count each separate black key once. Do not count the long white keys, gray seams, frame, or colored screws.

worlds.title: Remainder tower cards
worlds.question: Order the four violet cards by their one to four amber dots. On each card, replace each tower by a dark square when its height in boxes is a multiple of three, otherwise by a pale square. Use the four results as rows of a 4 by 4 tile. Which symbol appears: hourglass, diamond, falling blocks, or rising blocks?

worlds.title: Empty keystone direction
worlds.question: The three separate blue blocks surround one small white keystone gap. Is that empty gap wider on the left or on the right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Balance pin search
worlds.question: For each red pin, compare the cyan areas on its two sides and keep the smaller area. Which panel has the largest such smaller-side area?

worlds.title: One shot turnstile trace
worlds.question: Start with the lamp OFF and the key EMPTY. Follow the ribbon from its round gold end to the arrow tip. Cyan loads the key. Coral uses it: if the key is FULL, coral flips the lamp and empties the key; if the key is EMPTY, coral does nothing. Is the lamp ON at the tip?

worlds.title: District cut vertex
worlds.question: The colored map is divided into connected districts. Two districts are neighbors when they share a side; meeting only at a corner does not count. If the yellow district is removed from the district-neighbor graph, can every remaining district still reach every other through neighboring districts? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Broad belt midpoint
worlds.question: Which checkpoint is closer to halfway along the navy belt from the green START to the red FINISH: A (magenta) or B (orange)? Measure distance only along the belt. Answer A or B.

worlds.title: Gated motion collision
worlds.question: Each panel shows a blue disk, an orange disk, a cyan activation ring, and an arrow from each disk. First move the blue disk by its arrow. Move the orange disk by its arrow only if the moved blue disk lands inside the cyan ring; otherwise leave orange where it is. Which panel ends with overlapping disks? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Synchronous ring rewrite
worlds.question: The six framed tiles are a key: the two small dots on a tile are a pair of colors, in no particular order, and the big square on that tile is the color that pair produces. Seven colored disks sit in a ring and one is circled in black. In one round every disk is replaced at the same moment: a disk's new color is the square on the tile whose two dots match the colors of the two disks next to it in the ring, and its own color does not matter. Because all seven change together, always read neighbors as they were before the round, never as you have just rewritten them. Carry out five rounds. What color is the circled disk then? Answer amber, crimson, or teal.

worlds.title: Chained exchange ledger
worlds.question: Each top equation shows two groups with equal value. Add token values. Which numbered crate has the same total value as TARGET? Answer crate-1, crate-2, crate-3, or crate-4.

worlds.title: Fold turn landing
worlds.question: In each panel, reflect the blue cells across the dashed red line. Then rotate the result 90 degrees clockwise about the green pin. Which panel's amber cells show where it lands? Answer panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, or panel-4.

worlds.title: Fraction scale tag
worlds.question: REFERENCE is a fraction. Exactly one tagged candidate is made by multiplying both the reference numerator and denominator by the same positive whole number greater than 1. Which tag color marks it? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Skyline matrix correspondence
worlds.question: Each cell in every lower 3 by 3 candidate shows a stack height using 1, 2, or 3 black blocks. In the large clue card above, the three blue stacks across its top give, left to right, the maximum height in each column; the three orange stacks down its left give, top to bottom, the maximum height in each row. Exactly one candidate matches all six maxima. What is its border color: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Diag distance compare
worlds.question: A dark-gray diagonal segment crosses the image. Two solid dots, one red and one blue, sit on the canvas. Which dot is farther from the gray diagonal, measured as the perpendicular distance from the dot's center to the diagonal line? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Paired point displacement
worlds.question: Which colored sample has the greatest straight-line distance between its two same-colored circular measurements? Answer with a color name.

worlds.title: Regression slope leader
worlds.question: Panels are in reading order and share identical x- and y-scales. Fit a least-squares line to the seven colored point centers in each panel. Which color has the largest slope? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior star tips
worlds.question: This is a star drawn on a plain white background. An ordinary five-pointed star has five points, but stars can be drawn with other numbers of points. Report exactly what is drawn here: how many pointed tips does this star actually have? Count only the visible pointed tips and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Playing card center pips
worlds.question: How many large red heart symbols are visible in the white center of the playing card? Ignore the small corner labels. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Yin yang dot contrast conflict
worlds.question: Inside the large dark-and-light yin-yang symbol, do both small teal-outlined dots have a fill color opposite to the lobe immediately surrounding each dot? Judge the fill inside each teal outline, ignore the gray outer border and colored corner diamonds, and answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Diagonal pair fold
worlds.question: Divide the cyan-framed grid into 2 by 2 blocks. In each block, compare the two cells on the top-left to bottom-right diagonal, then the two cells on the other diagonal. Write a dark cell for different and a light cell for same, placing those two results left to right. Join all results without gaps. Which symbol appears: anchor, boot, chair, or sail?

worlds.title: Hinge fold overlap arrow
worlds.question: Fold the right grid leftward along the dashed gold hinge, as the curved arrow shows, so its columns mirror-reverse. Keep a grid position only when a dot on the left is covered by a dot from the folded right. Which arrow appears: up, right, down, or left?

worlds.title: Dot set central symmetry
worlds.question: Do the colored dots form a pattern that is centrally symmetric about their central point (rotating the whole dot pattern 180 degrees about its centroid maps every dot onto another dot)? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Voronoi territory compare
worlds.question: Imagine assigning every location inside the image border to its nearest dot center. Which colored dot gets the larger territory: red or blue? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Constellation match search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains the same four-dot constellation as the REFERENCE? Translation, rotation, and uniform resizing count as the same; a mirror reflection does not. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Ordered checkpoint path search
worlds.question: Starting at the cyan dot and following the single unbroken dark path, which labeled panel encounters the red, then orange, then blue bead in that order? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: State half count
worlds.question: A vertical timeline of four panels reads top to bottom. Each panel shows the same four slots (slot 1 and slot 2 are the LEFT half; slot 3 and slot 4 are the RIGHT half) and each slot holds one token. Every token has a fixed, unique color that never changes as it moves between panels. A magenta ring in the first (top) panel marks the token you must track. Reading the panels top to bottom and following that token's color across every panel, count how many of the four panels have the tracked token sitting in the LEFT half (slot 1 or slot 2). Answer with the count: '0', '1', '2', '3', or '4'.

worlds.title: State palindrome tile
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P7 from left to right. Each labeled tile shows LOW, MID, or HIGH using the visible STATE KEY. Which label's seven-state trajectory is the same when read forward and backward? Exactly one is symmetric. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Compare swap network
worlds.question: The picture shows four lanes side by side. At the top, each lane holds one coloured bar; the four bars are red, blue, green and purple and every bar has its own height. Below the bars a stack of black rungs is drawn. Apply the rungs one at a time in top-to-bottom order, as the grey arrow on the left shows. Each rung joins exactly two lanes: the two lanes its black bar reaches. A small orange square sits just outside one of the two ends of each rung; that end is the marked end. Applying a rung puts the taller of the two bars then standing in those two lanes into the marked end's lane and the shorter of them into the other lane; if they are already arranged that way, applying the rung changes nothing. Bars keep their colour and their height while they move, lanes that a rung does not join are untouched, and only the two lanes a rung reaches are affected. The teal triangle below the lanes marks the queried lane. After all the rungs have been applied in order, which coloured bar stands in the queried lane? Answer with one of: red, blue, green, purple.

worlds.title: Xor register replay
worlds.question: The four registers start with the shown ON/OFF states. Read the five XOR cards from left to right. On each card, the two shapes left of the arrow are the source registers: write ON into the shape right of the arrow exactly when the two current source states differ; otherwise write OFF. The other registers stay unchanged. Is the register shown in the QUERY box ON or OFF at the end?

worlds.title: Directed reversal connectivity
worlds.question: Arrows are one-way links between round stations. Imagine reversing exactly one colored arrow. Which reversal makes every station reachable from every other by following arrowheads? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Single junction loop cut
worlds.question: Can every loop in this network be broken by removing one colored circular junction and all dark links touching it? A loop follows dark links without repeating a junction; links meet only at visible circles. There are twelve junctions and thirteen links. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cycle checkpoint
worlds.question: Which colored checkpoint lies on the network's only loop? A loop is a closed route along dark links that returns to its starting node without reusing a link. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Three route terminal
worlds.question: Each box is a separate network. From green START, which colored terminal can be reached by exactly three different routes? A route follows black links from circle to circle and may not visit any circle more than once. Links meet only at circles and never cross. Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Serpentine spur code
worlds.question: The gold bead marks the reference run. Each colored bead marks the start of another run. Starting at a bead, move along its straight run away from the bead and record whether each of the four short spurs points to your left or right. Which colored bead has the same four-spur sequence as gold? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Normalized target error
worlds.question: Which gauge's cyan reading is closer to its orange target after dividing the vertical reading-to-target distance by that gauge's purple-zero-to-orange-target distance? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Signed arrow resultant
worlds.question: Three colored arrows show signed vertical adjustments. Treat each arrow's visible tip-to-tail length as its magnitude: UP is positive and DOWN is negative. Add the three signed lengths. Is the total UP or DOWN? Answer UP or DOWN.

worlds.title: Opposite die face sum
worlds.question: Do the two outlined OPPOSITE FACES show exactly seven dark pips in total? Count only dark circular pips inside the two outlined face squares. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Peel core reveal
worlds.question: Inside the violet frame is an 11 by 11 tile. Erase every dark square that touches a pale square by a side or corner (outside the tile counts as pale). Which symbol remains: X, plus, ring, or U?

worlds.title: Target ring concurrence
worlds.question: The card contains exactly five separate colored dashes and one target ring. Imagine extending each dash as an infinite straight line. Do all five extended lines pass through the inside of the ring? Answer all or not all.

worlds.title: Cycle bead search
worlds.question: Which colored bead lies on the only closed loop of the cyan rail?

worlds.title: Rising edge trace
worlds.question: Start with the signal LOW and the lamp OFF. Follow the ribbon from its round start to the arrow tip. Cyan sets the signal HIGH; violet sets it LOW. Every change from LOW to HIGH flips the lamp. Does the lamp finish ON? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: District odd cycle
worlds.question: The colored rectangle is divided into seven connected districts. Two districts are neighbors when their pixels share an edge; corner contact does not count. Does the district-neighbor graph contain an odd cycle? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Checkpoint color palindrome
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START ring to the red FINISH ring. There are eight checkpoints. Does their cyan/orange color sequence read the same backward as forward? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Double hinge stamp
worlds.question: Four tiles are labeled A-D. Each has a solid token, a cyan hinge marked 1, an amber hinge marked 2, a curved quarter-turn arrow at each hinge, and a hollow target outline. Turn the token one quarter-turn in the direction shown at hinge 1, then one quarter-turn in the direction shown at hinge 2. Exactly one target is the result. Which tile?

worlds.title: Rewriting tape walk
worlds.question: The grid is a rule table: each row is labelled on the left by a colored disk and each column on top by a black shape. A reading head sits on the strip cell marked by the black bar, and the machine starts on the ringed color. One step has three parts: read the shape in the head's cell; that cell is then rewritten, a square becoming a circle and a circle becoming a square, so the strip changes as you go; and in the table, the arrowhead where your current color's row meets the column of the shape you just read gives your new color and the side the head moves one cell. Take seven steps. Which color are you on then? Answer amber, teal, violet, or crimson.

worlds.title: Transported glide reflection
worlds.question: GLIDE reflects across one row or column, then shifts one cell along it; colored matches show the line and direction. FRAME maps left coordinates to right coordinates. Transport GLIDE through FRAME and apply it to the black stamp. Which border color results: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Coupled transition table
worlds.question: Use the table for 5 rounds. New LEFT is the cell at row old LEFT, column old RIGHT. New RIGHT is the cell at row old RIGHT, column old LEFT. Both change together from the old pair. Which option is final? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Weave overpass match
worlds.question: Each card contains cyan, orange, and purple ribbons. At every crossing, the ribbon with unbroken color passes over the ribbon with the white gap. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same over/under result for every pair of ribbon colors as the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Landmark board correspondence
worlds.question: The upright black symbols identify corresponding cells on the two 4x4 boards. Their cell positions differ by one rotation or mirror flip of the whole grid. Which color fills the TARGET cell corresponding to the magenta-ringed REFERENCE cell: red, green, or blue?

worlds.title: Interval overlap argmax
worlds.question: Three colored horizontal bars (red, blue, green) and one gray reference bar each span a horizontal interval on their own row. Which colored bar shares the longest horizontal overlap with the gray bar, meaning the greatest common horizontal length? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Paired vector dot leader
worlds.question: Rows A-D each show vectors P and Q as three aligned bar lengths on identical scales. Which row has the largest dot product P dot Q? Multiply the aligned lengths, then add the three products. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Heatmap center edge contrast
worlds.question: Each heatmap row has four cells and the same total. For each labeled row, add the two middle cell values and subtract the two edge cell values. Which row has the largest result? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior bicycle spokes
worlds.question: This is a bicycle-style spoked wheel. An ordinary bicycle wheel has many spokes (traditionally about thirty-two), but report exactly what is drawn here. Count the spokes actually drawn on this wheel and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Rainbow outer band color
worlds.question: Which color is the outermost visible arc band of the rainbow—the band farthest from the white center? Answer red, orange, yellow, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Die net opposite prior conflict
worlds.question: The six colored squares joined by gray bars form a cube net. If folded, is the face opposite the one-pip face the six-pip face? Use the visible layout rather than standard-die conventions. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Double unfold reveal
worlds.question: Unfold the cyan quarter-sheet across the magenta hinge, mirroring every black square. Then unfold across the yellow hinge and mirror every black square again. Which pattern appears: ring, plus, X, or four blocks?

worlds.title: Dot loop topology
worlds.question: A set of small, dark, isolated dots sits on a white canvas. None of the dots touch and no line connects them; the dots are spaced closely enough that each dot clearly belongs next to its nearest neighbours. Read the dots as one single continuous contour traced by their proximity. Does that contour close into one closed loop (every dot lies on the unbroken cycle) or stay as one open chain (a single path with exactly two free ends)? Choose from: one closed loop, one open chain.

worlds.title: Lattice phase components
worlds.question: Most dots lie on one square lattice. Some dots are shifted diagonally by the same small amount. Using edge-sharing lattice cells as connected, do the shifted dots form one connected region or two separate regions? Answer one or two.

worlds.title: Monotone bar order search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has its four dark bars arranged from shortest to tallest from LEFT to RIGHT? Every panel contains the same four bar heights; A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: State grid toggles
worlds.question: A 3x3 grid of cells is shown; each cell is either filled (solid dark) or hollow (an outline). The orange ring marks the target cell whose state you must report. To the right, three operator boxes read left to right. Each box holds one colored disk in the left, middle, or right slot, giving a row or column index 1, 2, or 3. A red disk toggles that row and a blue disk toggles that column, flipping every cell in it. Applying the operators in order, what is the final state of the ringed target cell? Answer 'filled' or 'outline'.

worlds.title: State direction turns
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 in order. The state key is ordered LOW < MID < HIGH. For each label, mark every adjacent change as a rise, fall, or stay. Count a reversal whenever a rise is immediately followed by a fall, or a fall is immediately followed by a rise; stays do not make reversals. Which label has the most reversals? Exactly one wins. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Dual frame selector replay
worlds.question: The black pointer and the four-color tray start as shown. Read the six cards left to right. A blue card rotates only the pointer by one quarter-turn; an orange card rotates only the whole tray by one quarter-turn. A magenta dot on a card's right means clockwise, and a dot on its left means counterclockwise. Which color is the pointer aimed at after all six cards?

worlds.title: Paired link cut
worlds.question: Gray and colored links join round stations. For each color, imagine removing both links of that color. Which removal disconnects the two black square terminals, even though removing either of those two links alone would leave them connected? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Balanced turn terminal
worlds.question: Starting at each green ring, follow its cyan-centered dark cable to the colored square. Which cable makes the same number of left and right turns? Every bend is a 90-degree turn. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Largest stepup terminal
worlds.question: Each chain runs from a green START circle through purple circles to a colored terminal. Traveling from START, compare consecutive black links by the distance between the centers of the circles they join. Which terminal's chain has the largest increase from one link to the next? Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Cumulative switch trace
worlds.question: Follow the connected strand from the gold bead along the gold run. Begin in state L. At each of its four teeth, a narrow tooth means hold the current state and a wide tooth means switch L to R or R to L; record the state after every tooth. Then read each colored run from its bead: a spur on traversal-left means L and one on traversal-right means R. Which colored run shows the four recorded states? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Fork route distance
worlds.question: Starting at the fork, which colored endpoint is farther away when distance is measured along the teal trace: coral or blue?

worlds.title: Bubble rank concordance
worlds.question: In the local bubble-plot inset, is the larger teal bubble also the higher bubble? Judge size by visible filled area and height by the bubble centers. Answer YES or NO.

worlds.title: Traffic signal order match
worlds.question: Do the left and right traffic signals show the same complete top-to-bottom order of red, amber, and green lamps? Compare all three lamp colors in each signal. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Gf2 matrix product reveal
worlds.question: Multiply the teal-framed 5 by 5 matrix by the coral-framed 5 by 5 matrix, in that order. For each output square, compare its row from teal with its column from coral: make it dark exactly when an odd number of positions are dark in both. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Hidden pair crossing
worlds.question: Match equal-colored ports across the pale card and imagine straight connections between each pair. Would the two hidden connections cross inside the card? Answer cross or uncrossed.

worlds.title: Split bearing search
worlds.question: The large cyan bar at the far left and the large amber bar at the far right are the two bearing guides. Which labeled badge has both small bars parallel to the guide of the same color? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Pairwise selector patch
worlds.question: The gold START marker shows which column is ACTIVE, and the lamp starts OFF. Read rows 1, 2, and 3 from top to bottom. On each row, first flip the lamp if the bead in the ACTIVE column is dark. Then switch the ACTIVE column exactly when that row's two beads match. Is the lamp ON after row 3? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Paired depth concordance
worlds.question: Each panel contains closed black loops plus one cyan dot and one orange dot. A dot's depth is the number of black loops surrounding its center. In each panel, determine which color is deeper. Is the deeper color the same in both panels? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Marked bridge redundancy
worlds.question: If the yellow segment vanished, could you still travel from the green ring to the red ring using only the navy lines? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Crossview partner agreement
worlds.question: Match each SOURCE key to the identical key in both shuffled map rows. The arrow in each map points from its key to a partner key. Which SOURCE card has the same partner in Map A and Map B? Answer card-1, card-2, card-3, card-4, card-5, or card-6.

worlds.title: Fold quadrant punch probe
worlds.question: The square sheet is ruled into 8 by 8 cells, and the two dashed lines are creases. Fold the sheet in half along the vertical crease, then in half along the horizontal crease, so all four quarters lie exactly on top of one another. The black squares are holes punched straight through the whole folded stack, so every quarter ends up holed. Now open the sheet flat again. Exactly one of the four colored dots sits on a hole of the opened sheet. Which dot? Answer blue, green, red, or yellow.

worlds.title: Cyclic rim splice
worlds.question: Trace the dark tracks. Paired letter holes splice rims with the same color: enter one rim and leave its match, with no turning inside a hole. Which exit is connected to START: A, B, C, or D?

worlds.title: Folded compass binding
worlds.question: In every panel, the amber squares are in the correct landing cells. Reflect each blue arrow across the dashed red fold, then rotate it 90 degrees clockwise about the green pin. Which panel also shows the correct arrow directions? Answer panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, or panel-4.

worlds.title: Swap gate permutation
worlds.question: Start with the three colored beads shown above the tracks. Read the numbered gates from top to bottom. At each gate, the two tracks joined by the horizontal bar swap their beads; the third bead stays on its track. Which option shows the final left-to-right bead order? Answer A, B, or C.

worlds.title: Peak count argmax
worlds.question: Three colored bands are drawn, each a series of equal-height triangular peaks standing on a horizontal baseline. Which colored band has the most peaks (the most mountain tops)? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Scatter correlation leader
worlds.question: Which color's nine circular points have the larger absolute Pearson correlation between horizontal and vertical coordinates? Answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Paired squared gap leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order and share the same scale. At each checkpoint, measure the vertical gap between the blue and orange marker centers. Square the five gaps and add them. Which panel has the largest total? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior segment digits
worlds.question: This is a digital seven-segment display digit. How many of its seven segments are currently lit? Count only the solid (lit) segments and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Notebook spiral side
worlds.question: Which side of the notebook has the spiral binding? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Thermometer bulb label conflict
worlds.question: Which printed temperature label is closest to the red round bulb: 0 or 100? Read the visible label and answer 0 or 100.

worlds.title: Phase lattice decimate
worlds.question: The magenta tabs mark the first kept row and column. Inside the cyan frame, keep that row and every second row after it, and that column and every second column after it; discard the others and close the gaps. Which symbol appears: circle, diamond, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Largest void marker
worlds.question: On a white canvas a field of many small dark dots is scattered. Taken together the dots leave one large empty void -- a clear region with no dots -- that is clearly larger than every other opening in the field. Four small coloured dots (red, green, blue, orange) are placed on the canvas. Exactly one coloured dot sits inside that largest empty void, far away from every dark dot; the other three sit right among the dark dots. Which coloured dot sits in the largest empty void? Choose: red, green, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Illusory quad containment
worlds.question: Among the six black disks, four right-angle white cutouts face one another and their straight edges imply one closed quadrilateral; the other two do not complete it. Which colored dot lies inside the implied quadrilateral? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Ring line bijection search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has every colored line crossing exactly one amber ring, with every ring crossed by exactly one line? A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: State threshold onset
worlds.question: Four panels P1, P2, P3 and P4 are shown left to right in order. Each panel is a horizontal track with a marked half-way line and a left-aligned level bar whose length is the running amount in a tank. The tank starts at a base amount; then for each successive panel one signed step (add or remove) is applied, so panel Pk shows the level after the first k steps -- the bar in each panel grows or shrinks accordingly. Report the panel in which the running level FIRST rises strictly above the marked half-way line. If no panel ever rises above it, answer 'never'. Answer with exactly one of: P1, P2, P3, P4, never.

worlds.title: State change load peak
worlds.question: Read panels P1 through P6 left to right. Count the labeled tiles whose state changes on each adjacent arrow. Which arrow has the largest count? Answer P1->P2, P2->P3, P3->P4, P4->P5, or P5->P6.

worlds.title: Token transposition replay
worlds.question: The ringed token starts in the shown numbered slot. Read the five SWAP cards from left to right. On each card, the dot counts name two slots; exchange the tokens in those two slots. All other tokens stay. Which slot contains the ringed token after all five swaps? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Bounded face station
worlds.question: Black bands are walls and white areas are regions. A white region is enclosed when it does not touch the image border. Which colored round station touches exactly three distinct enclosed white regions? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Route bottleneck capacity
worlds.question: Starting at each green circle, follow its connected dark route to a colored square. A route's capacity is the width of its narrowest dark link between adjacent markers. Which route has the greatest capacity? Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Threaded rhythm match
worlds.question: Follow the single navy thread from its gold square start, through three pale checkpoints, to the gold diamond, and note the four successive gaps. Do the same from each red, green, and blue square to its matching-color diamond. A candidate matches when all four gaps have the same relative short-to-long pattern as the gold reference, allowing the whole pattern to be uniformly scaled. Which square color marks the unique match? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Enclosed window gate
worlds.question: Does the single teal sample enclose a white window that is completely cut off from the surrounding white background? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Trace regression trend
worlds.question: Treat each horizontal column equally and fit a least-squares straight trend through the colored trace. Does that fitted trend RISE or FALL from left to right? Answer RISE or FALL.

worlds.title: Morse sos pulse order
worlds.question: Following the single colored telegraph trace from left to right, do its nine raised pulses spell SOS in Morse code: short, short, short, long, long, long, short, short, short? Judge pulse widths only. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Opposed row shear residual
worlds.question: The teal and coral panels are both 7 by 7. In the teal panel, cyclically slide row 1 by 0 cells right, row 2 by 1 cell right, through row 7 by 6 cells right, wrapping at the edges. In the coral panel, do the same to the left. Align the results and make a dark square exactly where their shades differ. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Progressive excursion trail
worlds.question: Follow the single blue trail from its red end to its green end. Its three alternating side excursions have distances from the endpoint baseline that steadily change. Do they grow or shrink? Answer grow or shrink.

worlds.title: Axis transfer search
worlds.question: Read the two dots in the sample from top to bottom. Which candidate shows those same two colors from left to right? Answer upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, or lower-right.

worlds.title: Affine pip mosaic
worlds.question: The gold START tile shows the starting number as pips. Read the other tiles in row order, left to right then top to bottom. A cyan tile adds 1 and a coral tile doubles the current number; after every tile, wrap by subtracting 5 until the number is 0 through 4. What number remains?

worlds.title: Universal loop station
worlds.question: Tracks meet only at visible junctions. A loop is a closed route that follows tracks without repeating a track segment. Which colored station lies on every possible loop: cyan or orange?

worlds.title: Dense route deadends
worlds.question: Trace the broad navy network from the green START to the red FINISH. How many dead-end branches split from that route: 2 or 3? Count only branch ends that are neither colored endpoint.

worlds.title: Quarter turn target intervention
worlds.question: Each panel has a dark pointer fixed at a cyan hub, a curved arrow showing a clockwise or counterclockwise quarter-turn, and a red bullseye. If you turn that panel's pointer exactly one quarter-turn around its hub as shown, which panel's tip would land inside its bullseye? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Circuit return disk
worlds.question: The white floor is all one room: from the blue star you can walk to every disk without crossing a black wall. For exactly one disk you can walk out to it and back to the star without ever using the same stretch of corridor twice. Reaching either other disk forces you to repeat a stretch. Which disk is it? Answer red, gold, or magenta.

worlds.title: Single junction seam resilience
worlds.question: Gray seams never fail. SAME keeps socket order top-to-bottom; FLIP reverses it. Only pale circles can fail; colored circles and square sockets cannot. Every matching color pair is connected now. If any ONE pale circle disappears with all black links touching it, which pair is guaranteed to stay connected? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Counterfactual reconvergent lattice
worlds.question: The triangle shows the factual run. Dark means ON. Every lower cell uses the two touching cells directly above it; its row badge gives the rule: ALL, ANY, or ONE. Flip only the red-ringed TOP cell and rebuild downward, one whole row at a time. Which option is the new bottom row? Answer option-1, option-2, option-3, or option-4.

worlds.title: Polyomino perimeter profile
worlds.question: The top card is the REFERENCE. Each card has one cyan, magenta, green, and orange figure made from equal square tiles. For each color, count the exposed unit edges: a side shared by two same-color tiles is not exposed. Figures may move or turn. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same four color-to-perimeter counts as the reference? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Threshold red count
worlds.question: A gray straight line crosses a light panel. Colored dots (red, blue, green) are scattered on both sides of the line. How many RED dots lie strictly ABOVE the gray line? Answer with only the number.

worlds.title: Crosshair area leader
worlds.question: Which colored point makes the largest rectangle area with the dashed vertical and horizontal reference lines? Use the product of its horizontal and vertical distances from the dashed lines.

worlds.title: Standardized reference offset
worlds.question: For each colored row, compute |marker center - dashed reference| divided by the row's full colored interval length. Which color has the largest ratio? Answer red, blue, green, or orange.

worlds.title: Prior guitar strings
worlds.question: This is a guitar. How many strings are drawn on it? Count only the visible strings and answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Speaker sound wave side
worlds.question: The orange curved strokes are sound waves. Are they on the left or right side of the blue speaker body? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Qwerty right neighbor conflict
worlds.question: On the visible row of keys, which letter is on the key immediately to the right of F? Read the printed labels, and answer with G, H, J, or K.

worlds.title: Spiral path reflow
worlds.question: Starting at the magenta-marked cell, follow the cyan clockwise spiral inward to the yellow-marked end. Read dark and light cells in that order, then write them row by row, left to right, into a 12 by 12 square. Which symbol appears: arrow, cup, bolt, or key?

worlds.title: Global elongation axis
worlds.question: The dark dots together form one elongated cloud. Looking at the whole cloud, along which single direction is it stretched out: horizontal, rising (uphill to the right), vertical, or falling (downhill to the right)? Answer horizontal, rising, vertical, or falling.

worlds.title: Occluded path terminal
worlds.question: Start at the path marked by the teal ring. At each gray screen, match the black stubs that meet with the same smooth direction behind the screen; paths do not branch. Which colored terminal does the path reach? Answer red, blue, or yellow.

worlds.title: Reference slant tally
worlds.question: Which side contains more dark bars parallel to the bar in the REFERENCE box? Choose LEFT or RIGHT.

worlds.title: State scale register
worlds.question: Read the image left to right. The leftmost panel shows a track of four cells: the cell whose position is the starting value is filled dark and surrounded by an orange ring, so the ringed cell is value 1, 2, 3, or 4 from left to right. To its right are four operator panels read left to right; each holds one colored disk: green doubles the value (capped at 4), blue halves it (flooring, but at least 1), and red replaces it with 5 minus the current value. The final value is never drawn. Replay the four operators in order from the ringed start. What is the final register value? Answer '1', '2', '3', or '4'.

worlds.title: State stability onset
worlds.question: Read the panels in order P1, P2, P3, P4, P5, P6. Each labeled tile keeps its identity and shows one of the three states in the key. For each label, find the first panel from which its state never changes again. Which label becomes permanent earliest? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Priority scheduler replay
worlds.question: The waiting tray starts with the numbered jobs shown. Read the six cards from left to right. A green ADD card inserts its dot-numbered job. A red SERVE card removes one waiting job with the smallest number; if the tray is empty, it does nothing. Which job number is next (the smallest still waiting) after all six cards? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Chamber graph center
worlds.question: Black lines are walls, and connected white areas are chambers. Two chambers are neighbors only when they share a black wall segment; touching at a corner does not count. For counting distance, one step crosses one shared wall into a neighboring chamber. Which colored dot is in the chamber whose farthest chamber is the fewest steps away? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Compulsory route checkpoint
worlds.question: Follow the dark network from the green ring to the blue square. You may choose any branch at a junction. Which checkpoint, orange or purple, must be passed on every possible route?

worlds.title: Transition count loom
worlds.question: The four panels are woven into one uninterrupted navy loom; if its central weave is broken, the pattern is unreadable. Read each row of the gold-framed 5-by-6 source from left to right and count how many times neighboring squares change between cyan and cream. In the result, each row becomes one bottom-up cyan column whose height is that row's change count. Which red, green, or blue frame marks the exact five-column result?

worlds.title: Route extrema order
worlds.question: Follow the cyan route from the coral start dot to the blue finish dot. Does the route reach its highest point before its lowest point? Answer before or after.

worlds.title: Trace band span
worlds.question: The dashed guides divide the plot into TOP, MIDDLE, and BOTTOM bands. Add the lengths of the teal trace's horizontal runs within each band; vertical connectors have zero horizontal length and do not count. Which band has the greatest total horizontal span? Answer TOP, MIDDLE, or BOTTOM.

worlds.title: Rainbow ribbon order
worlds.question: Reading the single colored ribbon from left to right, are its six sections in this exact order: red, orange, yellow, green, blue, violet? Judge only the visible section order. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Twin spoke unroll
worlds.question: Each circular reel has four spokes of eight cells. Starting at its green bead, read spokes clockwise; within each spoke read center to rim to make one top-to-bottom column. The one-dot reel supplies the left four columns and the two-dot reel supplies the right four columns. Which symbol appears: box, D, backward D, or oval?

worlds.title: Woven swatch order
worlds.question: Treat the 6 by 6 colored squares inside the small framed swatch as one woven pattern. Across the whole swatch, do equal colors continue in horizontal stripes or alternate like a checkerboard? Answer stripes or checkerboard.

worlds.title: Route rhythm search
worlds.question: Follow the blue route from left to right. The first section between the two black gates is the sample. Which colored gate begins the later section with exactly the same six-move up/down pattern? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Color countermand patch
worlds.question: The gold outline marks START. Begin holding its tile color with balance 1. Then read the other tiles in row order, left to right and top to bottom. If a tile matches the held color, add 1 to the balance. If it differs, subtract 1; if that makes the balance 0, immediately hold that differing tile color and reset the balance to 1. After all tiles, which color is held?

worlds.title: Cord peg winding
worlds.question: Follow the single black cord from the orange end to the blue end. Across its whole length, does it wind around the yellow peg clockwise or counterclockwise? Answer clockwise or counterclockwise.

worlds.title: Diagonal checkpoint order
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START to the red FINISH. Which comes first: the yellow checkpoint or the route's only diagonal segment? All other segments are horizontal or vertical. Answer checkpoint or diagonal.

worlds.title: Double key badge relay
worlds.question: Find the gold-outlined badge in QUERY. In KEY A, follow its badge to a sigil. In KEY B, find that sigil. Which station color is paired with it? Answer red, blue, green, orange, or violet.

worlds.title: Unit rod ratio match
worlds.question: Every panel holds one upright dark bar and one flat orange rod. A panel's reading is how many times its own rod's length fits into its own bar's height. The magenta-framed panel at the top has a reading too. Exactly one of the five panels along the bottom, numbered 1 to 5 from left to right, has the same reading as the framed panel. Bars and rods are not drawn to any shared scale, so only a panel's own rod measures its own bar. Which numbered panel matches the framed panel's reading? Answer with exactly one of: panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, panel-4, panel-5.

worlds.title: Conjugated frame move
worlds.question: One-bar MOVE is shown in left coordinates. Two-bar FRAME maps left coordinates to right coordinates; match dots by color. Apply the same MOVE to the black stamp already in the right frame. Which bordered grid results: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Balanced bundle equations
worlds.question: The four top cards are balanced: both sides have the same total weight. Identical colored tiles weigh the same everywhere. Which numbered tray has the same total weight as TARGET? Answer tray-1, tray-2, tray-3, or tray-4.

worlds.title: Convex layer match
worlds.question: The top card is the REFERENCE. Each card has one dot of each color. To find layers, imagine a tight convex rubber band around the centers of all remaining dots: every dot touched by the band is the next layer. Remove that layer and repeat until no dots remain. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same dot colors in every layer as the reference? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Cloud trend argmax
worlds.question: Two colored scatter plots (clusters of dots) are drawn, one red and one blue, each in its own horizontal band. Which color's cluster of dots is drawn with the STEEPER overall trend, meaning the larger absolute slope of the straight line that best fits its dots? Answer with only the color: red or blue.

worlds.title: Trend target first
worlds.question: Moving from left to right, which colored solid trend reaches the orange dashed target line first?

worlds.title: Paired bar product
worlds.question: Groups A-D run from left to right. Each group has two bars sharing the gray baseline. Treat each bar's height above the baseline as its value. Which group has the largest product of its two bar heights? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior plate roundness
worlds.question: Set aside prior assumptions about dinner plates and judge only the drawn shape. Is the plate's visible outline a perfect circle? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Sports emblem loop count
worlds.question: Do all five dark loops form one connected group? Treat loops as connected only where their dark strokes visibly touch, with no background gap. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Isolated cell reveal
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 12 by 12 grid, make a result cell dark exactly when that source cell is dark and all eight cells touching it by a side or corner are light; cells outside the grid count as light. Which symbol appears: anchor, boot, chair, or sail?

worlds.title: Enclosed hole count
worlds.question: A single connected blue region fills part of the canvas. Inside it there are one or more separate white holes (enclosed empty white islands that do not touch the outside white background). How many white holes are inside the blue region? Choose 1, 2, or 3.

worlds.title: Constellation distance center
worlds.question: Treat every black dot center equally. Which colored marker has the smaller total straight-line distance to all black dot centers? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: T junction search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has a teal segment that ends on the middle of an amber segment, while the amber segment continues on both sides of the contact? A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: State phase rotation
worlds.question: A single arrow token is tracked across the four panels read left to right. The arrow's colored head points in one of four directions: east, south, west, or north. The red ring marks the starting arrow in the leftmost panel. Between each pair of consecutive panels an operator is shown: a red circle means rotate the arrow one quarter turn clockwise and a blue square means rotate it one quarter turn counterclockwise. Applying the operators in order, what is the arrow's final direction in the final panel? Answer 'east', 'south', 'west', or 'north'.

worlds.title: Pair cancel replay
worlds.question: The tiles in START form a row whose right end is beside the arrow. Read the six ADD cards from left to right; within each card add its left tile, then its right tile. Add each tile to the right end. If it matches the tile currently at the end, those two tiles disappear; otherwise it stays at the end. Which color is at the right end after all six cards? Answer red, green, blue, or yellow.

worlds.title: Graph isomorphism match
worlds.question: Each network has eight round stations and twelve links. Links meet only at round stations; a crossing without a station is not a connection. Which candidate has exactly the same station-to-station connections as the reference after the stations are renamed? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Cable detour ratio
worlds.question: Starting at each green circle, follow its cyan-centered dark cable to the colored square. For each cable, divide its length along the cable by the straight-line distance between its endpoint centers. Which cable has the greatest ratio? Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Bar sum reference
worlds.question: Add the horizontal span between the two coral ticks to the horizontal span between the two blue ticks. Is that total greater than the horizontal span between the two gold ticks? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Visible trident point count
worlds.question: How many separate upward points does the single blue trident have? Count every pointed prong connected to its stem. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Twin stencil overlay
worlds.question: Align the two colored 7x7 tiles. Keep only positions dark in both. Which symbol remains: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Split lattice phase
