worlds.question: The two separated 4 by 4 blue-dot patches each have equal horizontal and vertical spacing. Imagine extending their rows and columns through the blank gap. Do all 32 dots land on one common square lattice? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Constellation twin search
worlds.question: The small plus in each card is only an alignment marker. Which color has exactly the same four-dot pattern in its left and right 3-by-3 cards? Answer red, blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Twin compass rendezvous
worlds.question: Each compass has four states: up, right, down, left. Its gold dot marks the start. Read its three chips from top to bottom: cyan turns one state clockwise; coral mirrors left and right while leaving up and down fixed. After each compass follows its own chips, do the two tokens finish at the same state? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Cooperative patch cut
worlds.question: Teal, cyan, and orange together form one landmass. Remove a patch by turning all of its pixels white. Are cyan and orange a cooperative cut pair: removing both splits the remaining teal land, while removing either one alone leaves it connected? Edge-sharing connects land; corner touching does not. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Channel continuity stamp
worlds.question: Inside the navy stamp, can you trace one unbroken cream channel from the green dot to the orange dot? Answer connected or broken.

worlds.title: Moving frame rebase
worlds.question: The gold point stays fixed. Move the cyan frame by motion 1, then motion 2. In which quadrant does the point lie in the final frame? Answer northwest, northeast, southwest, or southeast.

worlds.title: Pivot merge centre
worlds.question: One single turn about a grid corner carries the green tile exactly onto the orange tile; call it turn A. One single turn about a grid corner carries the blue tile exactly onto the cyan tile; call it turn B. Doing turn A and then turn B has the same overall effect as one single turn about one point. Which black square holds the centre of that single turn? The four black squares are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right. Answer with exactly one of: square-1, square-2, square-3, square-4.

worlds.title: Cut link connected pair
worlds.question: The red X cuts only the link beneath it. After that link is removed, which matching color pair is still connected by black links? Links meet only at pale circles. Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Counterfactual logic override
worlds.question: Dark is 1 and light is 0. Follow arrows downward. XOR is 1 when its inputs differ; AND is 1 only when both are 1; OR is 1 when either is 1. At the red-boxed B node, ignore its incoming arrows and set B to the red-outlined bit shown. Recompute below B. What are P then Q? Answer 00, 01, 10, or 11.

worlds.title: Beacon visibility match
worlds.question: Each card has one beacon of each color and two opaque gray walls. Two beacons can see each other only when the straight line between their centers does not touch a wall. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same complete set of mutually visible beacon-color pairs as the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Steepest rise
worlds.question: Three colored line segments are drawn, each spanning the same horizontal width. Which colored segment is steepest, meaning it has the largest vertical difference between its higher end and its lower end? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Paired segment slope gain
worlds.question: From panel A to panel B, which colored segment has the largest increase in upward steepness? Steepness is vertical rise divided by horizontal run; all segments run from left to right, and higher on the page means a larger value.

worlds.title: Matrix determinant leader
worlds.question: Matrices A-D are in reading order. For each 2-by-2 matrix with top row a, b and bottom row c, d, calculate ad - bc from the visible entries. Which matrix has the largest determinant? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Prior dartboard sectors
worlds.question: This is a dartboard. A regulation dartboard is divided into 20 radial sectors, but this dartboard may show any number of sectors. Do not assume the usual number; count the radial sectors that are actually drawn. How many sectors is this dartboard divided into? Answer with a single number.

worlds.title: Card suit color conflict
worlds.question: Which playing-card suit symbol is red: heart or spade? Answer heart or spade.

worlds.title: Ranked strip reassembly
worlds.question: Sort the twelve strips from the highest magenta tab to the lowest, then join their black-cell columns without gaps. Which symbol appears: flag, hook, stair, or fork?

worlds.title: Center surround
worlds.question: On a white square canvas a scattered set of small dark dots is drawn. Take the exact center point of the square canvas. Looking at all the dots together as one constellation, do they surround that center point -- meaning the center of the canvas lies inside the region enclosed by the dots -- or do all the dots sit to one side of it? Answer yes if the dot constellation encloses the exact center of the square canvas, or no if every dot lies on the same side of that center.

worlds.title: Mosaic void arrow
worlds.question: Treat touching near-white pixels as one empty region and ignore isolated small square holes. The largest enclosed empty region forms an arrow. Does it point left or right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Terminal region separation
worlds.question: Which panel has the MAGENTA and AMBER dots in different white regions? Dark walls block passage. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: State floor counter
worlds.question: A leftmost panel shows a vertical level track with tick marks 0 at the bottom up to 3 at the top, and an orange ring marks the starting level. To the right, three operator panels are read left to right; a green up-arrow raises the level by one and a red down-arrow lowers it by one. The level stays between 0 and 3: if a down-arrow would take it below zero it stays at zero, and if an up-arrow would take it above three it stays at three. The final level is not drawn anywhere; it is found by applying the operators in order, starting from the marked level. What is the final level? Answer '0', '1', '2', or '3'.

worlds.title: Bounded meter replay
worlds.question: The meter starts with the shown number of blue or green cells. Read the operation cards from left to right: + fills one more cell and - empties one cell. A + on a full meter leaves it full, and a - on an empty meter leaves it empty. How many cells are filled after all cards?

worlds.title: Shared loop children
worlds.question: A black loop directly contains a smaller black loop when no other black loop lies between them. For each same-colored pair of dots, find the smallest black loop enclosing both dots. Which pair's smallest shared loop directly contains exactly two smaller black loops? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Bead branch terminal
worlds.question: Start at the green ring and follow the dark lines to the right. At each gray junction, take the outgoing branch with more cyan beads (three rather than one). Which colored square do you reach?

worlds.title: Trace direction span
worlds.question: Follow the blue trace from left to right. Add the horizontal run of every part that rises and separately add the horizontal run of every part that falls. Which total is larger? Answer rising or falling.

worlds.title: Ring route closure
worlds.question: Does the single blue RING ROUTE visibly form one closed loop? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Odd parity punchcards
worlds.question: Orient all four punched cards by putting each magenta corner marker at top-left. Align their 7 by 7 cells and keep a cell dark exactly when an odd number of cards have it dark. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Diagonal texture bias
worlds.question: The square swatch is a 12 by 12 grid of two-colored tiles. Count every diagonally neighboring pair of tiles that has the same color. Are there more same-color pairs along diagonals that rise / from left to right, or along diagonals that fall \ from left to right? Answer rising or falling.

worlds.title: Articulation cell search
worlds.question: Each colored square marks one cell of the connected mosaic. Which colored square is the only marked cell whose whole cell, if removed, would split the remaining mosaic into two disconnected pieces? Cells are connected only when they share an edge, not merely a corner. Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Echo pair trace
worlds.question: The gold token at the round START end shows a circle or triangle. Follow the connected trace to the arrow tip. Beginning with the second colored span, compare each span with the span immediately before it: matching colors flip the token between circle and triangle; different colors leave it unchanged. What face does the token show at the end?

worlds.title: Euler trail stations
worlds.question: The map has exactly eight stations and ten black roads. Can every black road be traced exactly once, starting at the orange station and finishing at the blue station, without lifting or retracing? Roads meet only at visible stations.

worlds.title: Paired arrival relation
worlds.question: Trace each separate navy route from its green START dot to its orange FINISH dot. Are the two final travel segments parallel (including opposite-facing) or perpendicular? Answer parallel or perpendicular.

worlds.title: Critical gate connectivity
worlds.question: The cyan and violet rings mark open gates. Close one marked gate at a time, leaving every other gap open. Which closure cuts the blue marker off from the image edge? Answer cyan or violet.

worlds.title: Content addressed swaps
worlds.question: The top strip holds six discs in six slots, numbered 1 to 6 from the left. The rows below the grey rule are a program: carry them out in order from top to bottom. Each row shows one coloured disc and an arrow. Find the disc of that colour in the strip as it stands at that moment and swap it with the disc in the next slot on the side the arrow points; if that colour is already in the end slot on that side, the row does nothing. Which slot holds the red disc once the whole program has been carried out? Answer with the slot number alone: 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Transported baseline shear
worlds.question: SLANT shifts each row horizontally by its signed distance from the fixed gold row; colored matches show the sign. FRAME maps left coordinates to right. Transport SLANT through FRAME, then apply it to the black stamp already in right coordinates. Which bordered grid results: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Counterfactual rescue lock
worlds.question: The triangle is the factual run; dark means ON. Each lower cell applies its row rule to the touching pair above. First flip the red-ringed TOP cell. Then test one numbered lock: that cell keeps its shown factual value instead of using its rule; rebuild everything below it. Which single lock restores the shown bottom row? Answer lock-1, lock-2, lock-3, or lock-4.

worlds.title: Nested color hierarchy
worlds.question: The single top box is the reference. Each box has one dot of every color. A small black enclosure groups a pair; a large black enclosure groups that pair with one more dot. Ignoring placement and order, which border color marks the bottom box with exactly the same two nested color groups as the reference? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Mean elevation compare
worlds.question: A light panel shows red dots and blue dots scattered across it, interleaved at different heights. Compare the two colours by the average height of their dots. Which colour's dots sit, on average, HIGHER on the panel (closer to the top)? Answer with only the colour: red or blue.

worlds.title: Dotplot iqr leader
worlds.question: Which color's five dots have the larger horizontal interquartile range? For each color, sort its dots from left to right; the interquartile range is the fourth position minus the second position. Answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Trimmed range leader
worlds.question: Panels A-D are in reading order and share the same vertical scale. In each panel, sort the seven colored marker heights, discard the highest and lowest marker, then measure the vertical distance from the remaining highest marker to the remaining lowest marker. Which panel has the greatest distance? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Clover leaf lobes
worlds.question: How many separate green leaf lobes are visible around the clover's gold center? Count each green leaf body once; do not count the brown stem or gold dots. Answer 3, 4, or 5.

worlds.title: Nested ring register
worlds.question: The 11 by 11 grid is split into five concentric square rings plus one center cell. For each ring separately, cyclically rotate all its dark/light cells until its magenta dot reaches that ring's top-center cell; the center cell stays fixed. Which symbol appears: arch, cup, fork, or bolt?

worlds.title: Contour notch direction
worlds.question: On a white canvas a set of dark dots is arranged around a shared center so that together they read as one closed ring-like outline. Exactly one dot is tucked inward, leaving a single concave notch in the ring. Which side of the outline is notched inward: top, bottom, left, or right? Choose one.

worlds.title: Fragmented concave enclosure
worlds.question: The separated black strokes trace one implied closed boundary. Follow them in order around the figure and connect neighboring stroke centers. Which colored dot is inside: red or blue? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Occlusion cycle search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel shows RED over BLUE, BLUE over GREEN, and GREEN over RED? At a crossing, the uninterrupted strip is over the interrupted strip. A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: State carry chain
worlds.question: A 4-bit register is shown: the rightmost cell is the ones place and each cell leftward doubles the place value. A solid dark cell is bit 1 (filled) and a white cell with a dark ring is bit 0 (outline). The orange ring marks the TARGET cell. The green up-triangles below declare successive increment-by-one operations, applied left to right. The register is never drawn again. Replay the increments from the shown start (propagating carries). What is the FINAL state of the ringed target cell? Answer 'filled' or 'outline'.

worlds.title: Queue front replay
worlds.question: The queue begins with the symbols shown from FRONT (left) to BACK (right). Read the six cards from left to right. A green ADD card places its symbol at the back. A red TAKE card removes the front symbol; if the queue is empty, it does nothing. Which symbol is at the FRONT after all six cards? Answer circle, square, triangle, or ring.

worlds.title: Loop pair separation
worlds.question: The image has five black closed wall loops. A loop separates two dots when it encloses exactly one of them. Which colored pair has exactly two separating loops? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Shortest route checkpoint
worlds.question: Starting at the green circle, travel along the dark links to the red square. Route length is the sum of the straight dark-link lengths between node centers. Which colored checkpoint lies on every shortest route: orange, purple, or blue?

worlds.title: Notch depth stem
worlds.question: The teal tile has a rectangular bite from its right edge. Is the bite's horizontal depth greater than the width of the solid teal stem left behind? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Ladybug spot balance
worlds.question: Does the ladybug have the same number of black spots on its left and right red wing covers? Count only separate black circles fully inside a red wing cover. Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Settled column silhouette
worlds.question: Inside the violet frame, let every dark square fall straight down within its own column; squares never move sideways. Which silhouette appears: rising stair, falling stair, central peak, or central notch?

worlds.title: Distant pinwheel parity
worlds.question: Each panel has exactly nine blue arrowheads around a red pin. Relative to the pin, classify each arrowhead as pointing clockwise or counterclockwise, then take the majority in each panel. Do the two panel majorities have the same flow or opposite flow? Answer same or opposite.

worlds.title: Midpoint checkpoint search
worlds.question: Follow the single black route from the cyan start to the magenta end. Which colored checkpoint divides the route into two equal travel lengths? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Balance checkpoint trace
worlds.question: Begin at balance 0 at the round START. Follow the connected trace to the arrow: each cyan span adds 1 and each violet span subtracts 1. At which labeled checkpoint, A, B, or C, is the running balance closest to 0?

worlds.title: Connected overlap split
worlds.question: Cyan is cyan-only area, orange is orange-only area, and yellow is shared overlap. Both cyan-plus-yellow and orange-plus-yellow are edge-connected. Is the yellow overlap split into exactly two edge-connected pieces? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Midroute finish approach
worlds.question: Trace the navy route from the green START ring to the red FINISH ring. At the point exactly halfway along the route, is your travel moving toward the FINISH or away from it? Compare straight-line distance to FINISH just before and just after that point. Answer toward or away.

worlds.title: Edge cut resilience
worlds.question: Each panel shows a dark link network from a green start to an amber finish. A cyan ring marks one link to remove. After removing that link, in which panel does a dark path still connect green to amber? Answer panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D.

worlds.title: Rotor grid exit
worlds.question: A token starts on the cell with the thick black border. One step: the token leaves its cell in the direction that cell's arrow points at that moment, and that arrow then turns a quarter turn clockwise (up to right to down to left to up). The token carries on from the cell it entered under the same rule, and stops as soon as it steps off the grid. The drawn arrows are only the starting arrows, so any cell the token enters again has already turned. The four sides are labelled N, E, S and W. Which side does the token leave from? Answer with exactly one of: N, E, S, W.

worlds.title: Cross field badge splice
worlds.question: START shows two keys. In the table, find both rows. Take the LEFT badge from the first key's row and the RIGHT badge from the second key's row. Which answer shows that ordered pair? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Coupled matching loops
worlds.question: Each card pairs its eight lettered sockets with colored cords. Snap together sockets bearing the same letter, one from each card. How many separate closed cord loops result? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Aligned row pairing
worlds.question: Each card has four colored beads on each of two vertical rails. A left bead and a right bead form a pair only when their centers share the same horizontal guide row. Rows may be rearranged. Which colored border encloses the option with exactly the same complete left-color-to-right-color pairing as the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Widest gap
worlds.question: Each color is drawn as two horizontal filled bars stacked vertically with a gap between them. Which color has the largest vertical gap between its two bars, measured as the distance between the bottom edge of the upper bar and the top edge of the lower bar? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Gauge target alignment
worlds.question: Which colored gauge has its clockwise fill endpoint closest to its magenta target tick, measured by the smaller angular gap around the circle? Every fill starts at 12 o'clock. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Bias blue planet orbit
worlds.question: Counting the thin gray orbit rings outward from the yellow Sun, starting with 1, which numbered orbit contains the blue planet?

worlds.title: Component bbox solidify
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 12 by 12 grid, replace each side-connected black component by its smallest axis-aligned rectangle, filling that entire rectangle black. Corner-touching cells do not join. Which symbol appears: equals, pause, rising pair, or falling pair?

worlds.title: Density gradient direction
worlds.question: Looking at the full field of dots as a whole, in which single direction does the dot texture become denser: left, right, up, or down? Answer left, right, up, or down.

worlds.title: Rubber band enclosure
worlds.question: Imagine the tightest convex rubber band around every black dot. Which colored marker is inside that rubber band? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Rotated rectangle search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has four teal dots at the corners of a rectangle? The rectangle may be rotated. Panels A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Tile paint overwrite
worlds.question: The ringed tile starts with its shown color. Read the paint cards from left to right. Each card's dots identify one tile, and its color bar repaints that tile, replacing its previous color. What color is on the ringed tile after all five cards?

worlds.title: Split boundary pair
worlds.question: Black bands are walls and white areas are chambers. Each same-colored dot pair marks two different chambers. Shared wall sections are separate when they do not touch, even at a corner. Which colored pair's chambers share exactly two separate wall sections? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Link transition terminal
worlds.question: Starting at each green circle, follow its connected route to a colored square. Which route changes link color exactly three times? Count a change whenever two consecutive links have different colors. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Paired midpoint alignment
worlds.question: Which colored pair has its vertical midpoint closer to the gold reference dot: coral or blue? Answer coral or blue.

worlds.title: Laptop fruit emblem
worlds.question: Which single filled fruit silhouette is visible in the circular badge on the laptop lid: apple or pear?

worlds.title: Chromatic rank registration
worlds.question: Inside the violet 7 by 7 mosaic, treat each square's red, green, and blue values as separate grayscale layers. Cyclically slide red one square right and green one square down, wrapping at the edges; leave blue fixed. Mark a registered square dark when its three brightnesses follow red < green < blue, green < blue < red, or blue < red < green. Otherwise mark it light. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Self echo rail search
worlds.question: Follow the cyan rail from left to right. Each colored gate begins eight diagonal moves. Which gate begins the stretch where moves 5–8 repeat moves 1–4 in the same order? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Delayed mailbox dispatch
worlds.question: The START card shows SOURCE, MAIL, and DISPLAY (filled means ON; hollow means OFF). Read cards 1 through 4. FLIP changes SOURCE. SEND copies SOURCE into MAIL. DELIVER copies MAIL into DISPLAY. Is DISPLAY ON after all four cards?

worlds.title: Dual patch role
worlds.question: Erase the yellow patch to white. What happens: the teal land splits into two pieces, or an enclosed white courtyard opens to the outside? Answer land splits or courtyard opens.

worlds.title: Loop shorter arc gate
worlds.question: Trace the wide navy loop from the green START to the red FINISH in both directions. Which route is shorter along the loop: the route through the cyan gate or the route through the orange gate? Answer cyan or orange.

worlds.title: Lifo stack process
worlds.question: START shows a stack; the gold arrow marks TOP. Read cards 1 through 10 left to right. A red-plus card PUSHES its colored token onto the top, a blue-minus card POPS the top token, and a violet circular card ROTATES the top token to the bottom. After all cards, read the stack from top to bottom. Which sequence is shown: amber-cyan-violet, cyan-violet-lime, violet-lime-amber, or lime-amber-cyan?

worlds.title: Doorway region pairing
worlds.question: This picture is a 6 by 6 block of square rooms. Every wall is solid ink except where it is broken by a doorway gap, and you may walk from room to room only through those gaps. Eight dots sit in eight different rooms: two red, two blue, two green and two purple. Exactly one colour has both of its dots in rooms that are joined to each other by doorways. Which colour is it? Answer with exactly one of: red, blue, green, purple.

worlds.title: Rewriting turn queue escape
worlds.question: The front queue card chooses the mover. Read that token's current tile: on GOLD turn right, flip the shared tile, step, then rotate the queue left; on BLUE turn left, flip, step, then reverse the whole queue. Repeat until a token leaves the board. Which exits first? Answer token-red or token-violet.

worlds.title: Local frame transform relay
worlds.question: Each card maps its FROM frame to its TO frame: gold is the origin, cyan points RIGHT, and violet points UP. A dot keeps the same signed right/up offsets within that card. Apply cards 1, 2, then 3 to both dots of START. Which option is final? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Affine triangle transfer
worlds.question: The LEFT and RIGHT triangles have matching cyan, orange, and purple corner anchors. Imagine stretching or shearing the entire LEFT triangle until those three anchors coincide with the matching RIGHT anchors; the ring moves with the triangle. Which colored dot on the RIGHT is where the ring lands? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Fill fraction argmax
worlds.question: Three colored vertical bars (red, blue, green) stand on a black baseline. Each bar is a light-gray full-height skeleton with a solid colored fill rising from the baseline. Which colored bar is filled to the greatest fraction of its own total height, meaning the largest ratio of colored fill height to that same bar's full gray height? Answer with only the color: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Heatmap mean shift leader
worlds.question: From heatmap A to heatmap B, which colored row has the largest increase in its mean cell value? Darker blue means larger, and every row has four equally weighted cells. Answer with the row-label color.

worlds.title: Hourglass sand balance
worlds.question: Which chamber contains more solid blue sand by visible blue area? Answer top or bottom.

worlds.title: Border flood reveal
worlds.question: Starting at the magenta-gated black cell, erase every black grid cell reachable by side-sharing moves (up, down, left, or right; not diagonally). Which symbol remains: diamond, square, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Proximity cluster count
worlds.question: A row of identical dark disks is laid along a horizontal line. Disks close together form a cluster, and a few conspicuously larger gaps split the row into separate clusters (groups of disks). How many clusters of disks are there? Choose: 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Missing lattice site
worlds.question: The black dots occupy a regular rotated rectangular lattice with exactly one interior site missing. Which colored ring is centered on that missing lattice site: red or blue? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Directed turn signature search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has the same LEFT/RIGHT turn sequence as the REFERENCE when each route is followed from its teal triangle to its orange square? Every straight segment has equal length; rotating a whole route does not change its turn sequence. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Hysteresis switch replay
worlds.question: The start lamp is solid when ON and hollow when OFF. Read the level cards from left to right. A level above the HIGH line sets the lamp ON; a level below the LOW line sets it OFF; a level between the lines leaves it unchanged. Is the lamp finally ON or OFF?

worlds.title: Portal region fusion
worlds.question: Each colored square is a closed gate. White is floor and black is wall. Imagine turning just one colored square white. Which gate would join exactly three currently separate white floor regions into one? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Edge disjoint terminal
worlds.question: Each row begins at a green circle and ends at a colored square. Which colored terminal has two routes from its green circle that share no dark link? Routes may share nodes, but not links. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Route chord area
worlds.question: Relative to the imaginary straight line joining its two round endpoints, does more signed area of the cyan route lie above or below the line? Answer above or below.

worlds.title: Stop sign side count
worlds.question: How many straight sides does the red STOP sign face have? Count only the outer edges of the red sign face.

worlds.title: Toggle route reveal
worlds.question: Follow the cyan route from the triangular START cap to the round END cap. The START cap sets the current cell: green means dark and pink means light. Read the 50 instruction beads in route order, two at a time: amber means flip the state and navy means hold it. After each pair, write the current state into the next cell of a 5 by 5 grid, left-to-right and top-to-bottom. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Virtual crossing search
worlds.question: Imagine extending both black dashes as straight lines without changing their directions. Which colored dot is exactly where those two extended lines cross? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Stack card replay
worlds.question: The START card shows a vertical stack, with its top at the top. Read cards 1, 2, and 3 in number order. A colored triangle pushes that color onto the top; a black X removes the current top. What color is on top after all three cards?

worlds.title: Scaled vector dock
worlds.question: The gold point is transformed by the two cards in order. First double its displacement from the cyan hub. Then slide it by the shown grid-vector. Which colored dock is on its final cell? Answer red, blue, green, or violet.

worlds.title: Even split shelf
worlds.question: Each of the four shelves carries six trains, and a train is a run of square cars standing side by side. Deal one shelf's six trains into two groups, each whole train going into one group or the other; a group's load is its total number of cars. Exactly one shelf can be dealt into two groups of equal load, and the two groups need not hold the same number of trains. Which shelf is it? The shelves are numbered 1 to 4 from the top. Answer with exactly one of: shelf-1, shelf-2, shelf-3, shelf-4.

worlds.title: Edge rolling stamp
worlds.question: Roll the triangular stamp through cells 1 to 8 in order. At each move, flip it over the full edge shared by the two cells: the two corners on that edge stay there, while the third corner swings into the next cell. Which colored corner lands on the gold star? Answer red, green, or violet.

worlds.title: Conjunctive pair address
worlds.question: Treat the two QUERY marks as one pair. In PAIR KEY, each mark occurs twice; find the single row containing both. Use that row's color for the grid row and its blue stamp for the grid column. Which color is at their intersection? Answer amber, cyan, violet, or lime.

worlds.title: Shape pip binding
worlds.question: The top card is the reference. Each card has a circle, triangle, and square, each containing pips. Shapes may move and rotate. Which border color marks the bottom card where every shape has the same pip count as its matching reference shape? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Gauge needle nearest
worlds.question: A circular gauge needle points from the centre hub toward the outer track. Three coloured ticks (red, blue, green) sit on that track at fixed angles. Which coloured tick is the needle closest to, meaning it has the smallest angular gap to the needle's pointing direction? Answer with only the colour: red, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Histogram half mass first
worlds.question: Which colored histogram reaches half of its own total bar area in the earlier bin? Starting at bin 1, add bar areas from left to right; the crossing bin is the first where the cumulative area is at least half that histogram's total. Answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Bias musical staff lines
worlds.question: How many long, parallel staff lines run horizontally across the music staff? Count each continuous long line once; ignore notes and other symbols. Answer 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Paired row parity decode
worlds.question: Inside the cyan frame, combine each consecutive pair of grid rows (rows 1 and 2, then 3 and 4, and so on). Compress each pair into one row: make a result cell dark exactly when the two source cells differ, otherwise make it light. Which symbol appears: cup, cap, comb, or gate?

worlds.title: Halfturn constellation center
worlds.question: Rotate every black dot center by 180 degrees about each colored ring. Which ring makes the complete black-dot constellation match itself? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Cyclic palette match
worlds.question: Which labeled tile has its four colored markers in the same clockwise order as the REFERENCE? Rotating the whole pattern counts as the same; mirror reversal does not.

worlds.title: Parcel courier replay
worlds.question: The outlined cross marks the courier's start and the wrapped block marks the parcel's start. Rooms are numbered 1 to 4 from left to right by black-dot count. Read the six cards from left to right. A left or right arrow moves the courier one room, but an arrow beyond the corridor leaves it in place. A solid circle means PICK: the courier picks up the parcel only when they are in the same room and the parcel is not already carried; otherwise nothing happens. A hollow circle means DROP: a carried parcel is left in the courier's current room; otherwise nothing happens. While carried, the parcel moves with the courier. Which room contains the parcel at the end? Answer 1, 2, 3, or 4.

worlds.title: Cycle multiplicity link
worlds.question: The diagram is a network of round junctions joined by links; crossings count as connections only at a round junction. A loop is a simple closed route that never repeats a junction except its start/end. Which colored link belongs to exactly two distinct loops? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Well nested trace
worlds.question: Starting at each green ring, follow its connected dark cable to a colored square. Cyan checkpoints open and magenta checkpoints close. Which cable's checkpoint sequence is well nested? Moving from green, closes must never outnumber opens at any prefix, and their totals must be equal at the terminal. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Trace reference crossings
worlds.question: How many times does the cyan trace cross the dashed reference line? Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Mirrored s bend order
worlds.question: Following the single blue S-shaped stroke from its top endpoint to its bottom endpoint, which bend order is visible: right then left, or left then right?

worlds.title: Crossbar broadcast reveal
worlds.question: The teal vertical strip selects a row and the coral horizontal strip selects a column of an imagined 5 by 5 tile. Fill that whole row and whole column. Where is the revealed T's full crossbar: top, right, bottom, or left?

worlds.title: Centroid pin search
worlds.question: Treat every visible cyan part of the plate as having equal weight. Which colored pin is nearest the plate's center of area? Answer red, gold, violet, or green.

worlds.title: Harbor lock trace
worlds.question: Begin at water level 0 at START. Follow the connected channel toward the arrow. Each cyan lock raises the level by 1; each coral lock lowers it by 1. Which labeled buoy, A, B, or C, is reached at the greatest running water level?

worlds.title: Mirror slide stamp
worlds.question: Four tiles are labeled A-D. Each tile has a solid source token, a dashed mirror axis, a cyan arrow, and a hollow target outline. Reflect the source across its dashed axis, then translate it by the cyan arrow. Exactly one hollow outline is the result. Which tile?

worlds.title: Sealed room shared region
worlds.question: The black walls cut the white field into sealed rooms. Starting on the blue star you may walk anywhere across white space, but you may never cross a black wall. Exactly one colored disk stands in white space you can walk to. Which one? Answer red, gold, or magenta.

worlds.title: Single flip seam resilience
worlds.question: Gray seams connect facing sockets. SAME keeps top-to-bottom order; FLIP reverses it. Every matching color pair is connected now. If either ONE seam toggles (SAME becomes FLIP or FLIP becomes SAME), which pair stays connected in both possible cases? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Counterfactual mode transfer
worlds.question: Dark is 1 and light is 0. Every square shows its ACTUAL value. XOR is 1 when inputs differ; AND is 1 only when both are 1; OR is 1 when either is 1. Each gate has a fixed hidden mode: NORMAL gives the named rule and INVERTED gives its opposite. Infer the modes from ACTUAL. In TEST, force the shown node to the shown bit, ignoring its incoming arrows. Keep the inferred modes at every other gate and recompute. What are P then Q? Answer 00, 01, 10, or 11.

worlds.title: Normalized bar profile
worlds.question: Each card has one cyan, magenta, green, and orange bar rising from a common baseline. A whole card may be uniformly resized, but the four bar proportions stay the same. Which colored border encloses the option whose complete color-to-height profile is a uniform rescaling of the REFERENCE? Answer red, blue, or gold.

worlds.title: Closest color pair
worlds.question: A light panel holds exactly two RED dots and exactly two BLUE dots. Which colour has its two dots CLOSER together (smaller centre-to-centre distance)? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Trace excursion span
worlds.question: Which colored curve stays above its own orange dashed benchmark for the widest horizontal span, measured between the curve's two crossings?

worlds.title: Magnifier handle corner
worlds.question: The magnifying-glass handle is the solid blue bar outside the ring. Which image corner does it point toward? Answer top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right.

worlds.title: Equal cell mosaic
worlds.question: Resize every cyan-outlined row and column so that all grid cells become equal squares, without changing any cell from dark to light or light to dark. Which symbol appears: ring, plus, X, or diamond?

worlds.title: Tangent field center
worlds.question: The black dashes form one global flow: each dash is tangent to an imaginary circle around the same center. Which colored point is that center? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Clear sightline search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has a gray center-to-center guide from the teal circle to the amber circle that is not crossed by any dark rectangle? A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Dynamic link replay
worlds.question: Four dot-numbered stations start with the links shown. Read the six cards from left to right. A green LINK card adds the undirected link between its two dot-numbered stations; a red CUT card removes that link. Adding an existing link or cutting a missing link does nothing. After all six cards, is there a path of links between the two magenta-ringed stations? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Balanced cut station
worlds.question: Delete one colored station together with all links that meet it. Which color leaves two disconnected groups with equal numbers of stations? Answer orange, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Zone crossing terminal
worlds.question: Each row has one dark cable and one cyan inspection zone. Which colored square ends the cable that crosses its cyan zone boundary exactly four times? Count every entry into or exit from the zone as one crossing. Answer orange, purple, or blue.

worlds.title: Reflection axis match
worlds.question: Which reflection makes the colored specimen match itself more closely: left-right or top-bottom? Use the gold center dot as the crossing point of the reflection axes. Answer left-right or top-bottom.

worlds.title: Checkerboard column count
worlds.question: How many columns are in the checkerboard? Count the vertical stacks of alternating colored squares from left to right.

worlds.title: Orthogonal modular loom
worlds.question: Each small ruler has five boxes; its filled-cell count is a number from 0 through 4. For every cell of the faint 5 by 5 loom, add the amber ruler aligned with its row to the teal ruler aligned with its column, wrapping modulo 5. Make the cell dark exactly when the sum is 0. Which wrapped path appears: rising 1, rising 2, falling 2, or falling 1?

worlds.title: Territory split chronicle
worlds.question: Read the panels by their one, two, and three white dots. A paint territory is split when its same-colored paint forms two separate pieces. One color begins split; the other two split later and never rejoin. Which color splits first after panel 1?

worlds.title: Conditional bay latch
worlds.question: START marks one token in one of four colored bays: amber, cyan, violet, or lime. Follow rule cards 1 through 8. On each card, the left badge is FROM and the right badge is TO: if the token currently has the FROM color, move it to TO; otherwise leave it where it is. After card 8, which bay holds the token? Answer exactly one of: amber, cyan, violet, lime.

worlds.title: Rotation center recovery
worlds.question: The two black shapes are the same shape: one is the other after a single turn of the whole picture about one point, and that point does not move. Exactly one of the four colored dots sits on that point. Which dot is it? Answer blue, green, orange, or purple.

worlds.title: Reversing arrow tilewalk
worlds.question: Move both tokens for 7 rounds. Each round, RED uses the red arrow in BLUE's current tile; BLUE uses the blue arrow in RED's current tile. Use the positions and arrows from the start of the round. After both move, reverse the two arrows just used. Which colored goal contains RED at the end: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Counterfactual gate cascade
worlds.question: Dark means ON. Blue gates need both inputs ON; amber gates need at least one; violet gates need exactly one. In every panel, flip only its red-ringed input, then recompute the three gates left to right. Which panel's output changes from the shown lamp? Answer panel-1, panel-2, panel-3, or panel-4.

worlds.title: Satellite angle transfer
worlds.question: Each badge has one octagonal hub and exactly two teal satellites joined by spokes. Badges may move and rotate, but the smaller angle between their two spokes stays the same. The magenta ring marks one TARGET badge. Which colored tag is below the REFERENCE badge with the same spoke angle? Answer red, blue, gold, or purple.

worlds.title: Interval overlap degree
worlds.question: Which colored interval overlaps the greatest number of the other intervals? Endpoint contact alone does not count. Answer with the color name.

worlds.title: Dice opposite pip sum
worlds.question: The two gold-framed squares are declared opposite faces of this die. What is the total number of dark circular pips inside those two gold frames? Answer 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.

worlds.title: Paired midpoint reveal
worlds.question: For each pair of same-colored dots, mark the point exactly halfway between their centers. Ignore the original dots and the gray distractors. Which constellation do the midpoint marks form: plus, X, diamond, or square?

worlds.title: Dotfield equal split
worlds.question: Which colored dashed line divides all black dots into two groups with the same number of dots? Dots on a line would count in neither group, but no dot is on either line. Answer orange or blue.

worlds.title: Quarter turn board search
worlds.question: Which labeled board is unchanged after a quarter-turn (90 degrees) about its center? Filled and empty cells must all match; A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Cyclic sowing replay
worlds.question: The four bins start with the shown colored counters. Read the five SOW cards from left to right. Each card's black-dot count names a bin. On each card, remove all counters from that bin, then place them one at a time into the following bins to the right, wrapping from bin 4 to bin 1, until all removed counters are placed. How many counters are in the magenta-ringed bin at the end? Answer 0 through 8.

worlds.title: Vertex disjoint pair
worlds.question: Gray links join round stations. For each color, compare the two same-colored stations. Routes are independent when they share no station except those two colored endpoints. Which pair has a maximum of exactly two independent routes (two are possible, but three are not)? Answer red, green, or blue.

worlds.title: Longest straight checkpoint
worlds.question: Start at the magenta square and follow the dark cable. Which colored checkpoint is reached immediately after traversing the cable's longest uninterrupted straight section? A straight section ends at every 90-degree bend, and every colored ring marks a section end. Answer orange, blue, or green.

worlds.title: Neck partition area
worlds.question: The colored specimen has two filled lobes joined by one narrow horizontal neck. Split it with a vertical line through the horizontal midpoint of that neck. Which side contains more colored area: left or right? Answer left or right.

worlds.title: Enclosed flood reveal
worlds.question: Inside the violet 11 by 11 badge, begin at the amber cell and flood through pale cells that share a side, never crossing navy cells. Keep only pale cells the flood cannot reach. Which digit is that result closest to: 2, 3, 5, or 6?

worlds.title: Braided token trace
worlds.question: The gold ring marks the token's starting lane. Follow the braid away from the ring: each cyan crossover exchanges the top and middle lanes, and each violet crossover exchanges the middle and bottom lanes. After all six crossovers, which lane holds the marked token: top, middle, or bottom?

worlds.title: Euler trail connectivity
worlds.question: Exactly one panel has a connected dark network that can be traced from green to amber while using every dark link exactly once. Which panel: panel-A, panel-B, panel-C, or panel-D?

worlds.title: Head walk rule tape
worlds.question: The grid is a rule table: every row is labelled on the left by a colored disk and every column on top by a black shape. A reading head sits on the strip cell marked by the black bar, and the machine starts on the ringed color. One step: read the shape in the head's cell, then find the cell where your current color's row meets that shape's column. That arrowhead's color is your new color, and the head moves one strip cell to the side the arrowhead points. Take six steps. Which color are you on then? Answer amber, teal, violet, or crimson.

worlds.title: Mode switch tilewalk
worlds.question: Start on the tile at the black arrow, with its blue or purple badge active. Repeat 10 times: follow the arrow of the active color on your current tile and move one tile. If the tile you land on has a black ring, switch the active color. Which colored goal contains the final tile: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Bivariate mixer network
worlds.question: Each colored mixer computes a × LEFT + b × RIGHT with its own positive whole-number a and b. Its two examples fix them. In BUILD, compute U and V. Then use the ordered U/V inputs in COMPARE. Which final is larger? Answer left, right, or same.

worlds.title: Histogram variance leader
worlds.question: Which colored histogram has the larger frequency-weighted variance in bin position? Treat each bar's area as frequency, use bin positions 1 through 6 from left to right, and answer blue or orange.

worlds.title: Crossbuck board alignment
worlds.question: Do the two colored railroad-crossing boards form an X or a plus sign? Answer X or plus.

worlds.title: Cyclic row unscramble
worlds.question: Cyclically slide each row within the cyan frame until its magenta tab reaches the left edge. Which symbol appears: diamond, square, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Translation constellation vector
worlds.question: Each colored ring-to-square pair defines a shift from the ring center to the square center. Apply each shift to every black dot center. Which color makes more shifted centers land inside another black dot: orange or blue?

worlds.title: Axis mirror search
worlds.question: Which panel is mirror-symmetric across its vertical dashed line? Every dark dot must have a same-size partner on the opposite side at the same height and equal distance from the line. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Move to front replay
worlds.question: The four tokens start in the shown order from FRONT to BACK. Read the five MOVE cards from left to right. Each card moves its pictured token to the FRONT; the other tokens keep their relative order. Which token is in the ringed QUERY position at the end?

worlds.title: Cycle closing proposal
worlds.question: Each panel has cyan stations joined by gray links and one gold proposed link. The gold link is not yet part of the network. In which panel would adding the gold link create a loop? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Palindromic turn terminal
worlds.question: Start at each green circle and follow its dark cable to a colored square. At each cyan bend dot, record L for a left turn or R for a right turn relative to your direction of travel. Which terminal color has a turn sequence that reads the same forward and backward?

worlds.title: Route detour ratio
worlds.question: Is the cyan route's total visible length more than twice the straight-line gap from the coral start dot to the blue finish dot? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Endpoint span reveal
worlds.question: For each row, fill every square from the marked square in one panel through the marked square in the other panel, inclusive. Which symbol appears: T, L, I, or Z?

worlds.title: Debounced signal plaque
worlds.question: The gold START tile shows the output: dark means ON and light means OFF. Read the five signal tiles in row order. Cyan requests ON; coral requests OFF. The output changes only when the same request appears twice in a row. Is the output ON after all five signals?

worlds.title: Reflect turn stamp
worlds.question: Four tiles are labeled A-D. Each has a solid token, a dashed mirror axis, a marked pivot, a quarter-turn arrow, and a hollow target. Reflect the token across the axis, then turn it a quarter-turn around the pivot in the arrow's direction. Which tile's target is the result?

worlds.title: Exclusive fit binding
worlds.question: The five cards on the left are badges, each carrying two coloured pips. The five cards on the right are holders, each carrying three coloured pips; count the holders 1 to 5 from the top. A badge fits a holder only if both of the badge's colours appear on that holder, and the order of the pips means nothing. There is exactly one way to put all five badges into five different holders, one badge in each holder. One badge is marked by a black tag. Which holder does the tagged badge go into? Answer with exactly one of: holder-1, holder-2, holder-3, holder-4, holder-5.

worlds.title: Hidden symmetry composition
worlds.question: Each machine applies one whole-board symmetry, shown only by its example. Infer A and B. Apply A, then B, to START. Which RESULT is correct? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Counterfactual edge clamp
worlds.question: Dark is 1 and light is 0. Every square shows its ACTUAL value. XOR is 1 when inputs differ; AND is 1 only when both are 1; OR is 1 when either is 1. Each gate has a fixed hidden mode: NORMAL gives the named rule and INVERTED gives its opposite. Infer all modes from ACTUAL. In TEST, force only the red arrow to carry the shown bit. Do not force its source node or its other outgoing arrow. Recompute affected descendants with the inferred modes. What are P then Q? Answer 00, 01, 10, or 11.

worlds.title: Vector projection leader
worlds.question: Treat the displacement from the black center to each colored dot as a vector. Which colored dot has the greatest signed projection in the direction from the black center toward the magenta diamond? Compare forward components, not straight-line distances.

worlds.title: Bias page fold corner
worlds.question: Which image corner of the note is folded? Answer top-left, top-right, bottom-left, or bottom-right.

worlds.title: Center tab tile assembly
worlds.question: Rotate each cyan-framed 12 by 12 tile in place until its magenta corner points toward the center gap. Then join the four black-cell grids without gaps, preserving their upper-left, upper-right, lower-left, and lower-right positions. Which symbol appears: circle, diamond, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Braid closure components
worlds.question: The four black strands cross but never branch. At each crossing, follow each smooth diagonal strand through the crossing; the visible outer curves join each bottom end back to the top end in the same column. Does the complete drawing contain one closed strand or three separate closed strands? Answer one or three.

worlds.title: Triple overlap search
worlds.question: Which labeled panel contains a region that is inside all three colored circles at once? Every pair overlaps in every panel, but pairwise overlaps alone do not count. A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Refractory lamp replay
worlds.question: The lamp and its two-cell cooldown start as shown. Read the seven cards from left to right. WAIT lowers the cooldown by one, stopping at zero. PRESS toggles the lamp only when the cooldown is zero, then fills the cooldown to two; a PRESS while cooldown remains does nothing. Is the lamp ON or OFF at the end?

worlds.title: Girth four panel
worlds.question: A loop follows links and repeats no round station except when returning to its start. The shortest-loop length is the fewest links in any loop. Which network has shortest-loop length exactly four? Answer left, center, or right.

worlds.title: Route multiplicity terminal
worlds.question: Starting at the green ring, follow the dark network. Gray dots mark junctions. Which colored square can be reached by exactly two different routes? A route may not revisit a junction or travel any segment more than once, and different routes must differ by at least one segment.

worlds.title: Cross arm thickness
worlds.question: At the shared center of the colored plus-shaped sample, which arm is thicker across its narrow dimension: horizontal or vertical? Ignore how far the arms extend. Answer horizontal or vertical.

worlds.title: Paired block density reveal
worlds.question: Compare each matching outlined 3 by 3 block in the teal and coral panels. Make one output square dark exactly when the teal block contains more dark micro-squares than the coral block. Read the 5 by 5 output. Which symbol appears: X, plus, T, or L?

worlds.title: Rollback bead trace
worlds.question: Start with LAMP OFF and CHECKPOINT OFF. Follow the connected wire from the round START to the arrow. Each cyan bead flips LAMP. Each gold bead saves the current LAMP state into CHECKPOINT. Each coral bead restores LAMP from CHECKPOINT. Is LAMP ON at the arrow? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Two center turn locator
worlds.question: The gold bead is hidden after the moves. Rotate it 90 degrees around P1 using TURN 1, then 90 degrees around P2 using TURN 2. Which colored landing port is on the bead's final cell? Answer red, blue, green, or violet.

worlds.title: Structure twin binding
worlds.question: Both halves of this picture draw the same network: the same nine dots and the same thirteen links between them, but the dots are placed differently in the two halves, so position on the page tells you nothing and only the pattern of links matches. One dot on the left is inside a black ring. That same dot appears on the right, and exactly one of the four coloured dots on the right is it. Which colour is it? Answer with exactly one of: red, blue, green, orange.

worlds.title: Rim glued escape
worlds.question: Overlay the plans: walls shown once stay; walls shown twice vanish. Paired letter holes glue matching rim colors. Enter one rim and leave its match; no turning inside a hole. Which exit can START reach: A, B, C, or D?

worlds.title: Lever arm calibration
worlds.question: Each CLUE beam is level. Matching colors have matching weight. On each side, add weight times numbered arm distance. Which TEST beam would stay level? Answer beam-1, beam-2, beam-3, or beam-4.

worlds.title: Calibration peak residual
worlds.question: Each color has four circular checkpoints. Which color has the largest worst-case calibration error? For each checkpoint, measure the vertical gap to the magenta dashed ideal diagonal; for each color take its largest gap, then choose the color with the largest result. Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Clock hand length conflict
worlds.question: The blue HOUR hand and red MINUTE hand start at the center. Which hand is longer from center to tip? Answer blue or red.

worlds.title: Diagonal grid transpose
worlds.question: Inside the cyan square, swap every cell's row and column across the magenta-to-yellow diagonal (do not rotate the result). Which symbol appears: flag, hook, stair, or fork?

worlds.title: Striped gap contour
worlds.question: The colored horizontal bands break around one central white opening. Taken together, do their aligned inner endpoints outline a circle or a diamond? Answer circle or diamond.

worlds.title: Paired arrow convergence
worlds.question: Which panel contains the pair of arrows pointing toward each other? An arrow points from its rectangular shaft toward its triangular head. Panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Signal copy replay
worlds.question: The three registers start with the shown ON/OFF states. Read the six COPY cards from left to right. On each card, copy the left register's current state into the right register; the left register does not change. Is the register shown in the QUERY box ON or OFF after all six copies?

worlds.title: Route shared prefix
worlds.question: Starting at the green ring, follow the dark network toward the blue diamond. Among the orange, purple, and red squares, which square's route from green shares the greatest length of dark line with the green-to-blue route before the two routes split? Measure only the shared path from green up to the split.

worlds.title: Route midpoint reference
worlds.question: At the point halfway along the cyan route's visible length, is the route above or below the dashed gray reference? Answer above or below.

worlds.title: Revisit lamp wire
worlds.question: Begin at balance 0 with the lamp OFF. Follow the connected wire from the round START to the arrow. A cyan bead adds 1 and a coral bead subtracts 1. After each bead, flip the lamp if the new balance has been visited before, then remember that balance. Is the lamp ON at the arrow? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Wall face connectivity
worlds.question: The dark strokes are walls. Which colored marker is cut off from the outside white space? Answer red, blue, or orange.

worlds.title: Nested loop depth probe
worlds.question: Every black outline is a closed loop, and the loops never touch or cross. A dot can have zero, one, or two loops around it. Exactly one dot has two loops around it. Which dot? Answer orange, teal, or violet.

worlds.title: Conditional handoff escape
worlds.question: Red is active first. The active token reads its current tile: on GOLD, turn right and make the other token next; on BLUE, turn left and make the same token next. The active token then flips that shared tile and steps. Stop at the first exit. Answer token-red or token-violet.

worlds.title: Socket fusion components
worlds.question: Every plate joins its own sockets. Matching sockets (same color and shape) also join across plates. After all matches, which terminal is connected to START? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Histogram entropy leader
worlds.question: Which colored histogram has the largest entropy? For each histogram, divide each of its four bar heights by their total, then compute -sum(p x log2(p)). Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Battery positive terminal edge
worlds.question: Which side of the battery body is the red positive terminal attached to? Use image directions and answer top, right, bottom, or left.

worlds.title: Quarter turn xor
worlds.question: Inside the cyan frame, rotate a copy of the 20 by 20 grid 90 degrees clockwise, then keep a black cell only where exactly one copy is black (XOR). Which symbol appears: circle, diamond, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Reflection residual marker
worlds.question: Reflect every dot across the vertical gray line and pair it with a dot at the reflected position. Exactly one colored dot has no partner. Which color is it? Answer red or blue.

worlds.title: Alternating sides search
worlds.question: Which panel has dots alternating above and below its horizontal line from left to right? Panels A-D are in reading order. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Recency touch wire
worlds.question: The three gold START beads are ordered oldest to newest. Follow the connected wire from START to the arrow. At each later bead, TOUCH that letter: move it to newest while preserving the order of the other two. Which letter is oldest at the arrow: A, B, or C?

worlds.title: State ledger trace
worlds.question: Start at the gold START mode. Read the table: use the current row and next event column to get the next mode, then continue through all seven events left to right. Which mode is active at the end? Answer alpha, beta, gamma, or delta.

worlds.title: Parity wall escape
worlds.question: Overlay the three plans. A wall remains only if it appears on an odd number of plans; a wall shown twice disappears. From START, which exit can be reached without crossing a remaining wall: A, B, C, or D?

worlds.title: Flip turn revisit
worlds.question: Begin on the green arrow, facing the way it points. Repeat 18 moves: on a LIGHT square turn right; on a DARK square turn left. Flip that square, then move ahead one square. The path stays on the board. After move 18, which goal badge marks the cursor's square? Answer goal-A, goal-B, goal-C, or goal-D.

worlds.title: Peak to final drop
worlds.question: Which colored series has the largest vertical drop from its own highest checkpoint to its final checkpoint? A higher point represents a larger value.

worlds.title: Bowling ball finger holes
worlds.question: How many separate dark circular finger holes are visibly enclosed inside the bowling ball? Count each hole once.

worlds.title: Aligned xor cards
worlds.question: Align the cyan crosses without rotating or resizing the cards. Keep black only where exactly one card is black (XOR). Which symbol appears: circle, triangle, plus, or X?

worlds.title: Implied disk union hole
worlds.question: Imagine a disk centered on every black dot, each with radius equal to the length of the gray bar. Does the union of those disks enclose a white hole? Answer yes or no.

worlds.title: Quadrant coverage search
worlds.question: Which panel has exactly one dot in each of the four regions made by its cross? Dots on a line would not count; panels A-D are in reading order.

worlds.title: Mirror turn tapestry
worlds.question: Begin with the white heading on the gold tile. Read the remaining tiles in snake order: top row left-to-right, middle row right-to-left, bottom row left-to-right. A cyan tile turns the heading 90 degrees clockwise; a coral tile reflects it across the vertical axis. Where does the heading point after all eight operations?

worlds.title: Counterfactual branch readout
worlds.question: Move the gold-ringed token along the gold arrow. After the move, use the fuller bank's cyan-framed READOUT. What color is it? Answer red, blue, green, violet, or tie.

worlds.title: Offset fold punch
worlds.question: Fold the left two columns right along crease 1. Then fold the bottom three rows up along crease 2. Punch the folded packet as shown, then unfold in reverse. Which RESULT is correct? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Twin swap relay
worlds.question: Start at the green arrow, facing the way it points. Repeat 20 moves: on LIGHT turn right; on DARK turn left. Next, a lettered square swaps its shade with the other square bearing that letter; a blank square flips itself. Then move ahead. The path stays on the board. After move 20, which goal badge holds the cursor? Answer goal-A, goal-B, goal-C, or goal-D.

worlds.title: Interval pair iou
worlds.question: Which colored row has the largest overlap between its two intervals as a fraction of their combined span? Answer with the color name.

worlds.title: Bias piano black keys
worlds.question: How many separate raised black keys are visible above the seven white keys? Count each disconnected black key once. Answer 4, 5, or 6.

worlds.title: Vector tab scatter
worlds.question: Inside the cyan 12 by 12 grid, move every black-centered cell exactly four cells toward its magenta side tab (up, right, down, or left), wrapping across the opposite edge. Ignore the tabs and gray distractor cells after moving. Which symbol appears: arch, cup, fork, or bolt?

worlds.title: Texture orientation silhouette
worlds.question: The short black dashes use two tilt directions. Group dashes with the same tilt across the whole image: does the bounded central texture region form a triangle or a hexagon? Answer triangle or hexagon.

worlds.title: Strand crossing match
worlds.question: Which labeled panel has exactly the same pairs of colored strands crossing as the REFERENCE? A-D run left to right.

worlds.title: Switchback stamp walk
worlds.question: Start at the gold-ringed square. Follow the connected violet track in its arrow direction. On each move, read the cyan stamp in your current square: one dot advances 1 square and two dots advance 2 squares. After exactly three moves, which numbered square are you on?

worlds.title: Ratio bottleneck compare
worlds.question: Match equal colors to REFERENCE. For each candidate, compute each color's coverage ratio min(candidate height, reference height) / max(candidate height, reference height). Which candidate has the larger worst (smallest) ratio: A, B, or tie?

worlds.title: Flexible stock orders
worlds.question: Each mark runs that recipe once. Every slot uses one token: a solid slot needs that color; a split slot may use either shown color. All runs share START stock. Which order earns the most stars among orders whose slots can all be supplied? Answer order-A, order-B, order-C, or order-D.

worlds.title: Dual key crossindex
worlds.question: Use both keys. Match the queried black stamp in ROW KEY to get a row color, and match the queried colored disk in COLUMN KEY to get a column stamp. On the grid, which color fills that row and column? Answer amber, cyan, violet, or lime.

worlds.title: Normalized midpoint marker
worlds.question: Which colored interval has its black marker closest to the interval's midpoint, measured as a fraction of that interval's full length? Answer with a color name.

worlds.title: Star tip count
worlds.question: How many outward-pointing tips does the filled star have? Count only the sharp outer tips. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Minimal network topology
worlds.question: Connect every black dot with the unique shortest-total-length network that reaches all dots and has no loops. Is that network a chain, or does it branch? Answer chain or branch.

worlds.title: First homecoming chronicle
worlds.question: Read the four frames by their 1, 2, 3, and 4 gold center dots. Each colored bead's HOME is its position in frame 1. No bead is home in frames 2 or 3. Which bead first returns HOME in frame 4?

worlds.title: Counterfactual card patch
worlds.question: Run the six cards twice from the same START. ORIGINAL uses every printed card. PATCHED replaces the YES swap on the red-numbered card with the red patch. On each card, test the current shape, then do one swap. Which three boxes finish with different shapes: A-B-C, A-B-D, A-C-D, or B-C-D?

worlds.title: Counterfactual pair cancellation
worlds.question: Dark is 1 and light is 0. Follow arrows. XOR is 1 when inputs differ; AND is 1 only when both are 1; OR is 1 when either is 1. First compute normal P. On each card, try LEFT alone, RIGHT alone, then BOTH, resetting each time. An override forces its node to the shown bit, ignoring incoming arrows. Which card has this pattern: LEFT flips P; RIGHT flips P; BOTH leave P normal? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Dot gap spread leader
worlds.question: Each colored row has five dots with the same total span. Sort each row's dots from left to right. Which color has the largest difference between its widest and narrowest consecutive gap? Answer blue, orange, or green.

worlds.title: Compass north pointer
worlds.question: Which image edge does the red north pointer aim toward? Answer top, right, bottom, or left.

worlds.title: Enclosing circle support
worlds.question: Imagine the smallest possible circle that contains every black dot center. Is that circle fixed by two dots at opposite ends of a diameter, or by three dots on its boundary? Answer two or three.

worlds.title: Skipped stack transfer
worlds.question: A card moves the top tile from its left stack to its right stack. Do cards 1 through 6, but skip the red-X card. Which shape finishes on top of stack C: circle, triangle, or star?

worlds.title: Socket weave terminal
worlds.question: Inside each plate, each black cord joins two sockets; crossed cords do not join. Matching sockets (same color and shape) join across plates. Which terminal is connected to START: A, B, C, D, or E?

worlds.title: Trace crossing count leader
worlds.question: Which colored trace crosses the orange dashed baseline the most times? Count a crossing only when two consecutive circular checkpoints are on opposite sides of the baseline. Answer blue, green, or purple.

worlds.title: Fork top prongs
worlds.question: How many separate solid prongs are visible at the top of the fork? Count each prong once. Answer with a number.

worlds.title: Released clamp circuit
worlds.question: The amber clamp forces its outlined gate to the value now shown. XOR is 1 when its inputs differ; AND is 1 only when both inputs are 1. If the clamp were removed and every gate recomputed, exactly one output lamp would change. Which one: output-A, output-B, output-C, or output-D?

worlds.title: Keyed access closure
worlds.question: Start at S and move up, down, left, or right through white cells and markers on white cells. Reaching a round key opens every square gate with the same letter, even far away; opened gates become walkable and stay open. Which colored diamond EXIT is eventually reachable? Answer red, blue, orange, or violet.

worlds.title: Paired control badge registry
worlds.question: Each routing row shows a CARRY badge and a CHECK badge. If CHECK is filled at START, send CARRY's own state to the FILLED destination; otherwise use the HOLLOW destination. Which target letter matches the six routed CARRY states: A, B, C, D, E, or F?

worlds.title: Counterfactual swap network
worlds.question: Five labeled tokens move down the black tracks. Every black X crossing swaps the two tokens. Imagine the one crossing inside the red box is replaced by two straight tracks instead. Which token reaches the red target ring? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Counterfactual provenance rewire
worlds.question: For each of a card's two boxes, its dependency is the latest earlier card touching that box. The wrench replaces the red card's OLD boxes with its NEW boxes. Which later card is a descendant of the red card BEFORE but not AFTER the replacement? Answer 5, 6, or 7.

worlds.title: Affine order comparison
worlds.question: Each colored machine multiplies by one positive whole number, then adds one fixed whole-number offset, which may be negative. Its two examples fix the rule. Run the QUESTION number through each route from left to right. Which final number is larger? Answer left, right, or same.

worlds.title: Renamed switchboards
worlds.question: The two boards show the same six switches after renaming. Each row's red square and blue circle mark its two outgoing links. The renaming preserves both link colors. Which right switch is START: A, B, C, D, E, or F?

worlds.title: Coupled ledger invariant
worlds.question: Each board is one possible wiring. On each board, follow a letter to its token, then that token to its number. Which letter reaches the same number on all five boards? Answer letter-A, letter-B, letter-C, letter-D, or letter-E.

worlds.title: Folded flap hole recovery
worlds.question: The 6 x 6 sheet was folded left flap right across the red line, then bottom flap up across the blue line. The two black dots were punched through the folded 4 x 4 packet. Unfold both flaps. Which bordered grid shows every hole: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Crosskey pair consensus
worlds.question: Each board assigns every letter one LEFT badge and one RIGHT badge. Its PAIR KEY lists which badge pairs count. Which letter has a listed pair on all four boards? Answer letter-A, letter-B, letter-C, letter-D, or letter-E.

worlds.title: Control selected donor registry
worlds.question: Each row shows CHECK, two TAKE badges, and PUT. Read CHECK at START: if filled, choose the FILLED TAKE badge; if hollow, choose the HOLLOW TAKE badge. Copy the chosen badge's START state to PUT. Which TARGET letter matches all six states: A, B, C, D, E, or F?

worlds.title: Disjoint portal linkage
worlds.question: Which option pairs the three colored STARTS with exits 1, 2, and 3 so that all three routes can be drawn at once without sharing any corridor or portal cell? Touching white cells connect; equal portal letters jump. Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Crosskey membership registry
worlds.question: The center key pairs each source badge with a target badge. Rows are shuffled; filled means member. Which target letter has exactly START's six translated memberships: A, B, C, D, E, or F?

worlds.title: Two relation alignment
worlds.question: The two maps show the same seven tokens under different names. Blue circles and orange squares mark two kinds of directed relation: read each row as FROM and each column as TO. Which letter names the queried color in the LETTER MAP? Answer A, B, C, D, E, F, or G.

worlds.title: Paired stock orders
worlds.question: Each mark runs its numbered recipe. Choose two orders; together they use one shared START stock. Which pair earns the most stars without their combined token use exceeding stock? Answer pair-AB, pair-AC, pair-AD, pair-AE, pair-BC, pair-BD, pair-BE, pair-CD, pair-CE, or pair-DE.

worlds.title: Affine catchup threshold
worlds.question: Each colored machine multiplies the input by one positive whole number, then adds one fixed whole-number offset. Its two examples fix the rule. Starting at input 0 and checking whole numbers in order, what is the first input where ORANGE output is at least BLUE output? Answer 5, 6, 7, 8, or 9.

worlds.title: Conditional badge membership
worlds.question: For each source badge, use its FILLED destination if START is filled there; otherwise use its HOLLOW destination. Which target letter has the routed six-state pattern: A, B, C, D, E, or F?

worlds.title: Triplet socket closure
worlds.question: Inside each plate, black cords pair sockets; crossed cords do not join. Every matching color-and-shape socket appears three times, and all three join. Which terminal shares START's network: A, B, C, D, or E?

worlds.title: Transported pivot turn
worlds.question: ONE-TURN rotates dots a quarter-turn around the gold anchor in left coordinates. FRAME maps left coordinates to right coordinates; match dots by color. Apply that ONE-TURN to the black stamp already in right coordinates. Which bordered grid results: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Twin read relay
worlds.question: Start at the green arrow, facing its point. Repeat 20 moves. On a blank square, use its own shade: LIGHT turns right and DARK turns left, then flip that square. On a lettered square, instead use the OTHER same-letter square's shade to turn, then flip that other square. Move ahead. The path stays on-board. After move 20, which goal holds the cursor? Answer goal-A, goal-B, goal-C, or goal-D.

worlds.title: Card swap tilewalk
worlds.question: Move both tokens for 8 rounds. Each round, RED uses the red arrow on BLUE's current card; BLUE uses the blue arrow on RED's current card. Use the positions and cards from the start of the round. After both move, exchange the entire arrow cards in the two tiles where the tokens began that round. Which colored goal contains RED at the end: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Counterfactual provenance mosaic
worlds.question: The triangle is the factual run; dark means ON. Each lower cell applies its row rule to the touching pair above. Make a RED run by flipping only the red-ringed TOP cell, and a BLUE run by flipping only the blue-ringed TOP cell. Record each letter's value in both runs. Then restore TOP. Test one card: at each listed letter, install its value from the run named by the card, then continue downward. Which card recreates the bottom made by flipping BOTH ringed TOP cells? Answer card-1, card-2, card-3, or card-4.

worlds.title: Path specific splice
worlds.question: Flip SOURCE X for TEST. Try PATH A, B, C, and D separately: the chosen path's mediator uses its TEST value, while the other three mediators stay at their displayed ACTUAL values. Recompute downstream. Which sole path makes all three TARGET lamps? Answer path-A, path-B, path-C, or path-D.

worlds.title: Bridge cut connectivity
worlds.question: Remove the two bridge-plugs shown in the CUT key. Without crossing any remaining gap, which terminal is still connected to START? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Batch exchange pouch
worlds.question: Visit booths 1, 2, then 3. At each booth, trade every complete LEFT group for its RIGHT group; keep leftovers and all other tokens. Which tray is the final pouch? Answer tray-A, tray-B, tray-C, or tray-D.

worlds.title: Locked pair bijection
worlds.question: A blue dot means that pairing is allowed. Assign all eight rows to different columns. Many complete assignments work. In exactly one bracketed pair, the two rows always occupy the same two columns between them, although they can swap which row gets which. Which pair? Answer pair-A, pair-B, pair-C, or pair-D.

worlds.title: Reciprocal selector braid
worlds.question: START shows row 1 and row 2. Find both in the table. Each selected row's arrow chooses LEFT or RIGHT from the other selected row: row 1's arrow takes badge 1 from row 2, and row 2's arrow takes badge 2 from row 1. Which answer shows badges 1, 2 in order? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Pair rewrite cursor machine
