worlds.question: Use the visible instruction table for 7 turns. At the gold cursor, read the ordered adjacent pair. Its table entry replaces both chips together, then its arrow moves the cursor one gap (wrapping at the ends). Which option is final? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Badge twin rebinding
worlds.question: START names a row and field. Take that badge, then find its identical twin elsewhere in the table. What color dot is paired with the twin? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Counterfactual effect selection
worlds.question: Dark is 1 and light is 0. Follow arrows. XOR is 1 when inputs differ; AND is 1 only when both are 1; OR is 1 when either is 1. First compute normal P and Q. Then try each card separately, resetting the circuit. A card forces its named node to the shown bit, ignoring that node's incoming arrows. Which card flips P but leaves Q unchanged? Answer A, B, C, or D.

worlds.title: Layered link union
worlds.question: Sockets with the same letter are the same socket. Combine every cable on all four cards. Which socket is connected to START: A, B, C, or D?

worlds.title: Hinged chain turns
worlds.question: Follow the 3 FOLD cards left to right. On each card, hold the chain from START through the marked colored pivot fixed; flip the whole END-side remainder across the blue line through that pivot. Use the new positions for later folds. Which option is final? Answer A, B, C, D, or E.

worlds.title: Portal quotient escape
worlds.question: Overlay the three plans: walls shown once stay; walls shown twice vanish. Matching portal letters join their cells. From START, which exit is reachable: A, B, C, or D?

worlds.title: Conditioned probe patch
worlds.question: Release amber NOW. For each letter separately: flip the bit entering its green CHECK socket; read the resulting bit entering blue SAMPLE; reset to the released circuit; then force that bit at the letter's violet PATCH socket. Which letter makes every output equal the displayed TARGET? Answer pair-A, pair-B, pair-C, or pair-D.

worlds.title: Alternating shared escape
worlds.question: Red moves first, then violet, and they alternate. On GOLD turn right; on BLUE turn left; then flip that shared tile and move one cell. Stop when either token leaves the board. Which token exits first? Answer token-red or token-violet.

worlds.title: Balanced symbol weights
worlds.question: Each symbol always has the same weight. The three top rows balance exactly. Which bordered box balances the symbols at bottom: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Single break seam resilience
worlds.question: Gray seams never break. SAME keeps socket order top-to-bottom; FLIP reverses it. Black links join at circles. Every matching color pair is connected now. If any ONE black link breaks, which pair is guaranteed to stay connected? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Counterfactual shield choice
worlds.question: Using the full printed row, each swap depends on the latest earlier swap touching either box. Cancel the red-X card. Try each shield separately: that shielded card stays even if it depends on a canceled card. Repeatedly cancel every other card that depends on a canceled card, then restart from START and do the swaps left. Which shield puts the GOAL shape in TARGET? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Composed frame transfer
worlds.question: The one-bar KEY and two-bar KEY each map left grid to right grid; match dots by color. Apply one-bar, then two-bar, to the black center STAMP. Which bordered grid results: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Twisted rim cover
worlds.question: Overlay the plans: walls shown once stay; walls shown twice vanish. Paired holes join matching rim colors. The visible key says whether each letter KEEPS or SWAPS layer I/II; no turning inside a hole. START is on I. Which labeled exit-side is reachable?

worlds.title: Hinged cube net
worlds.question: Fold the colored net into a cube. Hold the dotted face toward you, with its black arrow pointing up. Which color is the cube's RIGHT face? Answer red, blue, green, amber, violet, or cyan.

worlds.title: Cross coupled tilewalk
worlds.question: Move both tokens for 6 rounds. Each round, RED follows the red arrow in BLUE's current tile, while BLUE follows the blue arrow in RED's current tile. Both use the positions at the start of the round. Which colored goal contains RED at the end: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Simultaneous flip rounds
worlds.question: Start with the four shown lamps. In each round, every arrow whose source lamp was ON at the start of that round flips its target lamp. Apply all three arrows simultaneously, then continue. After round 3, exactly one lamp is ON. Which one: lamp-A, lamp-B, lamp-C, or lamp-D?

worlds.title: Directed inequality consequence
worlds.question: Every top row says its left group is heavier. Which colored bottom row must also have a heavier left group for every set of positive symbol weights that fits all three top rows? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Dual key badge join
worlds.question: The START card shows one shape and one stripe. In SHAPE KEY, find the badge paired with that shape. In STRIPE KEY, find the badge paired with that stripe. Which answer card contains both badges? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Competing rate bounds
worlds.question: Each arrow label p:q means its tail is more than p/q times its head. Multiply the three labels on each colored START-to-FINISH route. Which route gives the strongest guaranteed ratio: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Intervened signal cascade
worlds.question: Filled means 1 and hollow means 0. Gates show AND, OR, or XOR. The wrench forces its node to the opposite value, ignoring that node's incoming gate. Recompute downstream. Which one lamp changes: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Twisted seam components
worlds.question: Gray seams glue facing patch edges. SAME keeps socket order top-to-bottom; FLIP reverses it. Inside a patch, black links join only at circles. Which matching color pair is connected through links and seams? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Transported one side fold
worlds.question: FOLD reflects only dots on one side of its crease; all other dots stay fixed. Colored matches show the crease and moving side. FRAME maps left coordinates to right coordinates. Transport FOLD through FRAME and apply it to the black stamp. Which border color results: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Portal glued connectivity
worlds.question: Matching shape portals join the two boards: entering one continues from the same shape on the other board. Which matching color pair is connected by black links and portals? Each link joins the two marks it touches. Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Snapshot copy tilewalk
worlds.question: Move both tokens for 8 rounds. Each round, RED uses the red arrow on BLUE's current card; BLUE uses the blue arrow on RED's current card. Use the start-of-round board. After moving, each token copies its landing card back onto the tile it left; the landing card stays. Which goal contains RED at the end: amber, cyan, or violet?

worlds.title: Shuffled record swap audit
worlds.question: BEFORE and AFTER contain the same keyed records in shuffled row order. Exactly two RIGHT badges were exchanged; LEFT badges did not move. Which two keys were swapped? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Frozen sample patch
worlds.question: In the displayed current circuit, freeze the bit arriving at blue SAMPLE. Remove the amber NOW clamp, then force violet PATCH to that frozen bit and recompute every gate. Exactly one displayed output changes. Which one: output-A, output-B, output-C, or output-D?

worlds.title: Cross field badge xor
worlds.question: Find the first START key's LEFT badge and the second START key's RIGHT badge. Overlay matching cells: dark only when exactly one source cell is dark. Which answer is the result? Answer amber, cyan, or violet.

worlds.title: Shared stock orders
worlds.question: Each mark on an order runs that numbered recipe once. Recipes consume the shown tokens and earn the shown stars. Which order earns the most stars without using more than START stock? Answer order-A, order-B, order-C, or order-D.
